title: Create counterfactual failure-analysis skill over ee lab evidence
description:
## Background

Counterfactual interpretation is useful but belongs in an agent skill. The Rust CLI should provide episode capture, frozen replay, pack diffs, and hypotheses; the skill should help an agent reason about what might have changed and what evidence would falsify the claim.

This preserves the value of the counterfactual lab without making `ee lab` pretend to know how an agent would have behaved.

## Acceptance Criteria

See this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field for the detailed completion contract, including unit/static checks, e2e or docs/e2e coverage, detailed logging, and no-feature-loss requirements.
design: The skill should require `ee lab capture/replay/counterfactual --json` outputs as evidence. It should gate conclusions on replay quality, redaction status, missing inputs, pack diffs, and provenance. It should label outputs as hypotheses unless backed by replay evidence and explicit validation.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Skill lives under `skills/counterfactual-failure-analysis/` or an equally clear project-local name.
- `SKILL.md` defines triggers, required `ee` commands, stop/go gates, output contract, and failure modes.
- Skill distinguishes observed facts, replay evidence, hypotheses, assumptions, and agent judgment.
- Skill refuses to conclude `would have succeeded` from pack presence alone.
- Includes references/templates for failure analysis memo, evidence checklist, and falsification checklist.
- Unit/static tests validate required `SKILL.md` sections, required `ee lab` evidence commands, stop/go gates, template fields, refusal behavior for weak evidence, and output section/schema checks.
- E2E skill script runs against deterministic lab fixtures covering no evidence, replay-supported failure, contradictory replay, redacted evidence, prompt-injection-like evidence, and degraded `ee lab` output.
- E2E logs include skill path, fixture ID/hash, all `ee` commands, degraded states, evidence IDs, evidence bundle path/hash, redaction status, output artifact path, required-section check, and first-failure diagnosis.
close_reason: Implemented in commit f56ac4d: counterfactual failure-analysis skill, references, fixtures, and local validation script. JSONL sync is pending because .beads/issues.jsonl is currently reserved by another pane.

title: Gate 20: Memory Economics Readiness
description:
Readiness gate from the comprehensive EE plan.

Gate text and intent:
This gate is required before EE uses economy scores to demote artifacts, compact context packs, or recommend prune plans.

Create memory economy contract tests:

```text
tests/contracts/memory_economy.rs
tests/golden/economy/report.json
tests/golden/economy/score_memory.json
tests/golden/economy/budget_release.json
tests/golden/economy/simulate_budget.json
tests/golden/economy/prune_plan_dry_run.json
tests/golden/economy/tail_risk_reserve.json
```

Pass criteria:

- `ee economy report --json` reports utility, attention cost, maintenance debt, false-alarm cost, and tail-risk reserve status
- `ee economy score <id> --json` explains one artifact's score with evidence and uncertainty
- `ee economy prune-plan --dry-run --json` never mutates memories, procedures, tripwires, situations, files, or indexes
- high-severity safety artifacts remain available through tail-risk reserve even when ordinary usage evidence is sparse
- sparse evidence produces abstain or review recommendations rather than aggressive demotion
- simulated budgets are deterministic on fixed fixtures and do not change current ranking state
- economy outputs validate against exported schemas and preserve stdout/stderr isolation

Why this matters:
Gates prevent roadmap gravity from turning aspirational features into unverified claims. Closing this bead means the implementation has executable evidence, not just code that compiles.

title: [MEDIUM] search_degradations silently drops Corrupt index status — searches return without warning
description:
## Surface
ee search graceful degradation when index becomes inconsistent (audit cycle 6, surface 3)

## Finding
`src/core/search.rs:732-738`:
```rust
match index_status.health {
    IndexHealth::Stale => vec![SearchDegradation::stale_index(
        index_status.db_generation,
        index_status.index_generation,
    )],
    IndexHealth::Ready | IndexHealth::Missing | IndexHealth::Corrupt => Vec::new(),
}
```

`IndexHealth::Corrupt` is grouped with `Ready` and yields an empty degradations vector. The only Corrupt-case handling is upstream: `IndexHealth::Corrupt.degradation_code()` returns `Some("index_corrupt")` (`src/core/index.rs:1578`), and `human_text_for` (`src/core/index.rs:1748`) acknowledges the status, but `search_degradations` never emits it.

`IndexHealth::Missing` is silenced too — but `run_search` (line 675-677) returns `SearchError::NoIndex` early when `!index_dir.exists()`, so the Missing branch only fires when status detects 'directory exists, files missing'. Either way, no degradation surfaced to the user.

## Why it matters
1. Honesty contract: ee context packs claim 'why each candidate was selected' and surface degradations — a corrupt index gives wrong scores or empty hits with no explanation. Users see 'no results' and assume the memory wasn't recorded; the actual cause is index corruption.
2. The `degraded` array in JSON output is a documented part of the contract (e.g., the recovery and golden tests assert its shape). Corrupt-without-degradation is a contract violation.
3. The downstream `candidates_from_search` already pushes `context_candidate_skipped` degradations for individual hits that can't resolve, but the meta-fact 'the index is corrupt' is the more actionable signal.

## Repro
```rust
// pseudo: corrupt the manifest at .ee/index/manifest.json
std::fs::write(".ee/index/manifest.json", "{ corrupt");
// then run:
let report = run_search(&options).unwrap();
assert!(report.degraded.is_empty());  // BUG: expected index_corrupt entry
```

## Fix
Replace lines 732-738 with:
```rust
match index_status.health {
    IndexHealth::Ready => Vec::new(),
    IndexHealth::Stale => vec![SearchDegradation::stale_index(
        index_status.db_generation,
        index_status.index_generation,
    )],
    IndexHealth::Missing => vec![SearchDegradation::missing_index()],
    IndexHealth::Corrupt => vec![SearchDegradation::corrupt_index(
        index_status.last_check_error,
    )],
}
```
…and add the two missing constructors on `SearchDegradation` next to `stale_index`. Add a contract test asserting `degraded[0].code == "index_corrupt"` when the manifest is intentionally damaged.
close_reason: Implementation already in place (lines 911-921 match on IndexHealth::Missing and IndexHealth::Corrupt). Added 4 unit tests verifying corrupt_index and missing_index degradation codes, severities, messages, and JSON output.

title: [locking] Hold file write-owner across all file-backed transactions
description:
Finding from deadlock-finder-and-fixer audit.

Evidence:
- src/db/mod.rs:341-356 shows the safe path: with_transaction() obtains begin_write_transaction() and keeps the file write-owner guard alive through commit/rollback.
- src/db/mod.rs:315-337 exposes begin()/begin_transaction()/commit()/rollback() as separate calls; src/db/mod.rs:724-746 only holds lock_file_write_owner_gate() for each individual SQL statement.
- Manual transaction callers still use that split path, including src/cass/import.rs:510-577 and src/db/mod.rs:6647-6658, 8415-8426, 8499-8515, 9155-9166, 9210-9221, 9262-9273.

Reproduction conditions:
- File-backed .ee/ee.db.
- Start two write-heavy command paths together, e.g. two cass imports, or cass import plus ee remember / workflow close / feedback record.
- The first writer holds the SQLite write transaction after BEGIN, but the external owner gate was released after BEGIN. The second writer can enter the gate and repeatedly hit SQLite contention instead of queueing behind the owner.

Fix target:
- Make all file-backed write transactions use one API that owns the file write-owner guard from BEGIN IMMEDIATE through commit/rollback.
- Remove or restrict public manual begin/commit usage for write transactions.
- Add a multi-process regression that runs the above command mix and asserts no database-is-locked/SQLITE_BUSY stderr and all intended rows persist.
close_reason: Fixed: changed begin/commit/rollback/begin_transaction from pub to pub(crate) with warnings; added with_write_transaction for custom error types; converted 7 internal db callers to use with_transaction; added From<DbError> for DomainError; added regression test with_transaction_holds_write_owner_throughout

title: [security] High-entropy secret detection requires keyword proximity
description:
**File:** src/policy/mod.rs:1010-1011

**Vulnerability:** The `redact_high_entropy_secret_values` function only redacts high-entropy content when `has_nearby_secret_keyword` returns true. Secrets not near keywords like "key", "secret", "token" etc. will not be redacted.

```rust
if looks_like_high_entropy_secret(candidate)
    && has_nearby_secret_keyword(input, token_start, token_end)  // <-- requires keyword
{
```

**Attack Scenario:** An agent stores a memory containing a redacted Stripe-like sample value `[REDACTED_STRIPE_KEY]` without secret/key/token in the surrounding text. While prefix-based detection catches this class when the prefix is present, a high-entropy AWS secret key without recognizable prefix (e.g. base64-encoded HMAC secret) placed in generic content could leak.

**Mitigation:**
1. Consider a standalone high-entropy pass for very long (64+ char) random-looking strings
2. Or: accept that prefix-based detection + keyword proximity covers the practical attack surface and document this as a known limitation

**Note:** The original audit text used a secret-shaped synthetic Stripe example; it was redacted to keep GitHub push protection and repository history clean.
close_reason: Added standalone high-entropy detection for 64+ char base64-like strings without requiring keyword proximity. Pure hex strings still require keywords (likely public hashes). 3 test cases added. Commit 6c1fdd5.

title: [process] Introduce honesty-only vs implements-surface bead taxonomy
description:
## Background

The 2026-05-06 reality-check audit (see CLOSE_THE_GAP_PLAN.md §1) found that 14 follow-up beads referenced by 20 `*_UNAVAILABLE_CODE` constants in src/cli/mod.rs were all closed without ever implementing the underlying feature. Each closed by adding a structured abstention sentinel — honest-degradation work, but shipped as a SUBSTITUTE for implementation. The bead tracker now reads 689 closed / 5 open while the README's user-facing surface remains substantially unbuilt.

The parent bead eidetic_engine_cli-jp06 ("Add degraded-honesty contracts for unavailable or not-yet-wired commands") legitimised this closure path. We do not regret the honesty work — it's better than fake confidence — but we cannot let it continue as the de facto closure path for implementation work.

## What this bead does

Introduces two mutually-exclusive bead labels and operationalises them so future swarm work cannot conflate honesty with implementation:

- `honesty-only` — closes when the abstention sentinel is wired correctly (stable code, message, severity, repair, evidence-source, follow-up bead).
- `implements-surface:<name>` — closes ONLY when the real feature works end-to-end, with real persisted data, real golden tests, and the abstention sentinel deleted in the same PR.

Every existing closed follow-up bead (the 14 in the audit table) gets retroactively labeled `honesty-only`. Every new implementation bead gets `implements-surface:<name>`.

## Why this is wave-0 and blocks everything

Without this taxonomy, the next wave of beads files closes the same way the last did. The remaining ~50-70 beads in CLOSE_THE_GAP_PLAN must not fall into the same trap.

## Coordination

This is a swarm-wide policy change. Once landed, broadcast via Agent Mail to every active pane. Follow-up beads (closure linter, vision-coverage gate) build on this.
close_reason: Taxonomy documented in AGENTS.md §Bead Taxonomy. Two labels (honesty-only, implements-surface:<name>) are now defined with closure criteria. The closure linter and vision-coverage gate depend on this and are unblocked.

title: EE-HANDOFF-001: Add session handoff and resume capsule command family
description:
Define and implement an agent-native session handoff and resume capsule command family.

Background:
EE is meant to serve coding agents across real work, not just answer isolated memory queries. In practice, agents lose context because sessions end, model context windows fill, a task changes hands, or another agent needs to continue from the same workspace. The current bead graph has strong foundations for memory, CASS import, context packs, recorder runs, outcome feedback, support bundles, and a multi-workspace/session-continuity scenario, but it lacks a concrete reusable handoff artifact for routine continuation.

This bead adds a normal-operation continuity capsule. It is different from the diagnostic support bundle: a support bundle explains what went wrong; a handoff capsule tells the next agent what is happening, what evidence matters, what to do next, what not to repeat, and which memories/context items justify that plan.

Intended public surface:
- `ee handoff create --json --out <path> [--since <run-or-time>] [--profile resume|handoff|compact]` writes an explicit redacted continuity capsule and prints a machine-readable manifest.
- `ee handoff preview --json [--since <run-or-time>] [--profile resume|handoff|compact]` reports the capsule plan, selected evidence, token/byte estimates, redaction posture, and excluded sources without writing the capsule.
- `ee handoff inspect <path> --json` validates an existing capsule, schema version, hashes, redaction status, workspace scope, and included evidence.
- `ee handoff resume <path|latest> --json` renders the next-agent resume payload from a capsule without mutating EE state.

The capsule is not a backup, not a raw transcript export, not a support bundle, and not an automatic task executor. It is a compact, provenance-rich state transfer optimized for agents.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including comprehensive unit tests, e2e tests, schema/golden fixtures, privacy checks, and detailed logging requirements.
design:
Recommended design:
- Define a strict `handoff_capsule.v1` schema with deterministic sections: workspace identity, repository fingerprints, agent/session/run IDs, current objective, status summary, active blockers, recent decisions, accepted outcomes, pending next actions, do-not-repeat guidance, selected memories/context items, evidence IDs, command/run summaries, artifact pointers, redaction summary, and degradation posture.
- Build capsule content from existing services rather than creating a parallel memory system: workspace detection, recorder run/event spine, CASS-derived sessions, context packs, search/context selection reasons, outcome feedback, procedure/tripwire/preflight signals when available, and support-bundle pointers only when diagnostics are explicitly requested.
- Require every included claim to have provenance: memory ID, session/evidence span, recorder event ID, context pack record, outcome ID, closure dossier, or explicit generated summary source. Summaries without evidence should be marked as low-confidence and excluded from action recommendations unless a profile explicitly allows draft hints.
- Keep profiles explicit and deterministic. `compact` optimizes for a small next prompt, `resume` optimizes for immediate continuation, and `handoff` optimizes for complete transfer to a different agent. All profiles should report omitted sections and why.
- `resume` must be read-only by default. It should not claim tasks, edit files, import sessions, apply memories, run shell commands, or update outcome state. If future mutation is useful, it should be a separate explicit command with dry-run/audit behavior.
- Use the same stdout/stderr discipline as the rest of EE: stdout is only the canonical JSON response; progress, skipped evidence, redaction events, ambiguity diagnostics, and first-failure diagnosis go to stderr or referenced artifacts.
- Make ambiguity visible. If multiple workspaces, repositories, sessions, or recent runs match, return a stable ambiguity code with candidate IDs and next commands instead of guessing.
- Preserve privacy and scope boundaries. A capsule for one workspace must not silently include another workspace's memories or session evidence unless the scope is explicitly requested and represented in the manifest.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance criteria:
- `ee handoff preview --json` returns an `ee.response.v1` payload with planned capsule sections, source evidence IDs, scope filters, profile, redaction posture, token/byte estimates, degraded/unavailable sources, omitted sections, and whether the capsule would be sufficient for a next-agent resume.
- `ee handoff create --json --out <path>` writes a deterministic redacted capsule only under the explicit output path and prints only the manifest response to stdout.
- `ee handoff inspect <path> --json` validates schema version, content hashes, workspace identity, repository fingerprints, section completeness, evidence references, redaction summaries, profile compatibility, and supported version ranges.
- `ee handoff resume <path|latest> --json` emits a compact next-agent payload with current objective, immediate next actions, blockers, do-not-repeat guidance, selected context/memory IDs with reasons, recent decisions/outcomes, and artifact pointers without mutating EE state.
- The capsule distinguishes evidence-backed facts, inferred summaries, stale/low-confidence hints, and explicit unknowns. It must not present inferred or stale content as verified fact.
- Scope is explicit for every included memory, context item, session, recorder event, and artifact. Multi-workspace ambiguity returns a stable degradation/ambiguity code and candidate resolution commands rather than silently choosing.
- The capsule never includes raw DB files, raw unredacted transcripts, raw secrets, unrelated workspace files, or user-global config secrets by default.
- Dry-run/preview, inspect, and resume are read-only. Create mutates only the explicit output path and records that artifact write in command-effect expectations.
- Capsules remain useful under degraded conditions: missing search index, unavailable CASS import, absent recorder run, stale context pack, or unavailable optional analytics must produce honest partial sections with stable codes and next actions.
- Public schemas and golden fixtures cover preview, create, inspect, resume, compact profile, handoff profile, multi-workspace ambiguity, partial degraded sources, redaction failure, stale evidence, missing artifact, and hash mismatch.

Testing and logging requirements:
- Add unit tests for capsule section selection, evidence provenance validation, deterministic ordering, profile-specific omissions, token/byte estimation, manifest hashing, redaction summary aggregation, scope filtering, ambiguity detection, stale evidence classification, and read-only command-effect classification.
- Add contract/golden tests for every public response shape and the `handoff_capsule.v1` schema, including valid and invalid fixtures with readable diffs.
- Add real-binary e2e coverage that creates two isolated workspaces with overlapping vocabulary, records/imports session evidence, builds context, creates a capsule, inspects it, resumes from it, and proves the wrong workspace's evidence is not selected silently.
- Add an interruption/resume e2e scenario where an in-progress task is captured after decisions and failed commands, then resumed in a fresh environment with the same next actions, blockers, do-not-repeat guidance, and evidence links visible.
- Add degraded/offline e2e fixtures for missing CASS, stale search index, absent recorder events, and unavailable optional analytics; the capsule must remain useful and include stable codes with next actions.
- Add privacy regression tests with synthetic secrets in session-like text, command output, config-like values, and memory bodies; raw synthetic secrets must not appear in stdout, capsule manifests, resume payloads, inspect output, or failure summaries.
- Add adversarial/property coverage for path traversal in `--out`, malformed capsule files, duplicate evidence IDs, invalid UTF-8/control characters, huge transcripts, stale hashes, symlinked output paths, and concurrent capsule creation attempts.
- E2E/logged tests must capture command, cwd/workspace, sanitized environment overrides, elapsed time, exit code, stdout/stderr artifact paths, capsule path, manifest hash, schema/golden validation status, redaction status, command-effect classification, selected/rejected workspace IDs, selected/rejected evidence IDs, and first-failure diagnosis.
- Stdout assertions must prove stdout contains only machine data; capsule planning details, skipped evidence explanations, redaction events, ambiguity diagnostics, progress, and debugging context must go to stderr or explicit capsule-local artifacts.
- Closeout evidence must include fixture IDs, scenario IDs, manifest hashes, command-effect manifest entries, exact verification commands, and the reason this command remains distinct from support bundles and backups.
notes: Added during repeated bead quality review after searches showed scenario-level continuity coverage but no concrete routine handoff/resume capsule command or schema. This bead improves agent ergonomics for context exhaustion, session interruption, multi-agent handoff, and future self-resume without conflating normal continuation with diagnostic support bundles or raw exports.

description:
## Background

Session review and memory-candidate distillation are valuable, but they require agent judgment: deciding what a session taught us, which facts are durable, what is a rule versus an anecdote, and what evidence is strong enough. That work should be a project-local skill that consumes CASS/`ee` evidence and emits candidate artifacts for the mechanical curation CLI.

This preserves the README workflow around `ee review session --propose` and `ee curate candidates` without embedding hidden AI reasoning in the Rust binary.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: [MEDIUM] closure-lint.sh has zero test coverage — silent regression risk on a CI-gating script
description:
## Surface
Closure linter regression-detection (audit cycle 7, surface 1)

## Finding
`scripts/closure-lint.sh` is a 281-line shell script that gates CI via `scripts/verify.sh:89`. It has THREE rules:
1. `implements-surface:*` beads cannot close with abstention language (regex-based check on close_reason)
2. `implements-surface:*` beads cannot close while `*_UNAVAILABLE_CODE` constants remain in src/cli/mod.rs
3. `implements-surface:*` beads must have a public golden snapshot in tests/golden/<surface>.snap

`find tests -name '*lint*' -o -name '*closure*'` returns NOTHING. `grep -rln 'closure_lint\|closure-lint' tests/` returns NOTHING.

So the linter is exercised only by running it. `cargo test --all-targets` does NOT cover it. A regression in any of these would survive PR review:
- A typo breaking the ABSTENTION_REGEX (line 25) makes rule 1 silently match nothing.
- A change to the `_UNAVAILABLE_CODE` constant naming convention without updating the linter's transformation (line 221: `tr '[:lower:]-' '[:upper:]_'`) silently misses violations.
- A typo in GOLDEN_DIR breaks rule 3 silently.

ujuc identified partial-closure beads (project memory: EE-062 'remember persist' and EE-151 'pack records' closed without full implementation). The linter's purpose is precisely to detect these. Without unit tests, the linter has no safety net.

## Repro
```bash
# Verify no test exercises the linter
find tests -name '*closure*'         # empty
find tests -name '*lint*'            # empty  
grep -r 'closure-lint' tests/        # empty
grep -r 'ABSTENTION_REGEX' tests/    # empty
```

## Fix
Add an integration test `tests/closure_lint_harness.rs` that:
1. Builds a temporary .beads/issues.jsonl with synthetic beads exercising each rule:
   - implements-surface bead closed with 'abstain' close_reason → expect violation
   - implements-surface bead closed with stub _UNAVAILABLE_CODE present → expect violation
   - implements-surface bead closed without snap file → expect violation
   - honesty-only bead with no open implements-surface sibling → expect violation
   - implements-surface bead closed cleanly (real code, no stub, snap present) → expect pass
2. Runs `scripts/closure-lint.sh --json` against the synthetic environment.
3. Parses .closure-lint-report.json and asserts the violation list matches expectations.
4. Run as part of `cargo test --workspace --all-targets` so the linter cannot silently regress.

Alternative: port the linter's logic to Rust (a `bin/closure-lint` binary or a library function with #[cfg(test)] tests). Heavier diff but unifies tooling under one toolchain.
close_reason: Added tests/closure_lint_harness.rs, a real integration harness that runs scripts/closure-lint.sh --audit --json against synthetic temporary workspaces. Coverage exercises abstention-language violations, *_UNAVAILABLE_CODE sentinel violations, missing golden snapshot violations, honesty-only closure without open implements-surface sibling, and passing clean implementation plus honesty-only sibling cases. Verification: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check tests/closure_lint_harness.rs; git diff --check -- tests/closure_lint_harness.rs; RCH cargo test --test closure_lint_harness -- --nocapture; RCH cargo check --all-targets. Repo-wide cargo fmt --check and clippy remain blocked by unrelated pre-existing dirty/baseline files outside this bead.

title: HIGH: FrankenSQLite connections never enable foreign-key enforcement
description:
Reviewer finding in src/db/.

Evidence:
- src/db/mod.rs:123-151 opens FrankenConnection instances for memory/file/schema-only modes and returns them without setting PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON.
- src/db/mod.rs:259-265 only runs PRAGMA foreign_key_check as a diagnostic after the fact.
- sqlmodel-frankensqlite opens raw fsqlite connections without enabling FK enforcement (/data/projects/sqlmodel_rust/crates/sqlmodel-frankensqlite/src/connection.rs:67-92).
- FrankenSQLite has a test documenting SQLite-compatible FK default-off behavior (/data/projects/frankensqlite/crates/fsqlite/src/lib.rs:9695-9705).

Impact:
The schema declares many REFERENCES/ON DELETE actions, but normal ee writes can insert orphan rows and deletes will not cascade/set-null unless each connection enables FK enforcement. Integrity checks may report the damage later, but repository methods can already have persisted logically invalid data.

Suggested fix:
Enable PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON immediately after opening read-write memory/file connections, and add storage tests proving a missing parent insert fails plus at least one cascade/set-null path works. Keep schema-only inspection read-only if needed.
close_reason: Fixed: DbConnection now enables PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON immediately after every FrankenConnection open; added regression test proving FK violations error on opened connections.

title: EE-TRUST-RECON-001: ADR reconciling trust class taxonomy across OPUS plan, main plan, and README
description:
Reconcile the trust class taxonomy across the canonical OPUS plan, the main plan, and the README before any code lands that depends on it.

Background:
The README documents five trust classes (human_explicit, agent_validated, agent_assertion, cass_evidence, legacy_import) with explicit initial confidences. The OPUS plan §22 (privacy and trust) lists the same five but uses a different transition vocabulary. The longer COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_TO_MAKE_EE.md describes a richer taxonomy with finer subdivisions (validated agent, project explicit, manual import, etc.) and adds promotion/demotion triggers tied to feedback evidence and validation count. EE-260 ("Add trust class enum and memory fields") is in the bead set as a P1 feature; if it lands without an ADR-level reconciliation, the implementing agent will silently choose one taxonomy and the others will rot.

The bead set has no bead that explicitly resolves this divergence. Multi-agent triangulation flagged it as a high-confidence ambiguity (D2 mode, F4 mode) and as a trust-pipeline correctness risk (H2 adversarial review).

Intended scope:
This bead is a docs/ADR bead. It produces (a) one ADR under docs/adr/ that specifies the canonical trust class set, the canonical initial confidences, the canonical state machine for promotion/demotion/inversion, the audit shape for each transition, and the public schema field name and version; (b) updates to the README and OPUS plan that point to the ADR; (c) a fixture test that asserts the chosen taxonomy round-trips through the future enum without loss; (d) a checklist on EE-260 that requires the ADR to exist before EE-260 can close.

It does not implement the enum or any state machine. It locks the spec.

Why this matters:
Trust class is load-bearing for retrieval scoring, packing priority, prompt-injection defense, redaction policy, audit log shape, MCP schema, and curation. If two implementations diverge in their understanding of "agent_validated", every downstream feature inherits the inconsistency. Resolving it once in plan space costs a few hours; resolving it after twenty downstream beads ship costs a sprint.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including the ADR, fixture, cross-link, and testing requirements.
design:
Recommended design:
- Take the README five-class set as the canonical baseline (human_explicit, agent_validated, agent_assertion, cass_evidence, legacy_import) because it is already user-facing in published documentation. Map any extra classes from the longer plan into either a `trust_class` plus a `trust_subclass` qualifier (recommended) or document them as future-work and reject them in v1.
- Use the README-published initial confidences (0.85, 0.65, 0.50, 0.45, 0.30) as the canonical defaults. Tune per-environment overrides via the existing config layer (see EE-021 config parser, EE-022 config precedence merge). Do not introduce a new config surface in this ADR.
- Define exactly four transition triggers: outcome_helpful, outcome_harmful, validation_passed (e.g. fixture replay confirms rule), validation_contradicted (replay falsifies rule). Each trigger maps to a deterministic delta (helpful: +0.04 utility, no class change unless threshold; harmful: weighted 4x; validation_passed: +0.06 confidence, may promote class with provenance). Numbers come from §18 decay/trauma guard.
- Make the promotion threshold explicit and conservative: promotion to agent_validated requires (a) at least one outcome_helpful event with provenance, (b) at least one validation_passed event from a separate session, (c) no outstanding harmful_outcome within the decay window. Promotion never happens silently; it appears as a curation candidate the user must accept unless the user has set the auto-accept policy.
- Expose the trust class as a stable schema field `trust_class` and the subclass as `trust_subclass`; both are versioned via the `ee.memory.v<N>` envelope. Do not use a free-text field; the ADR pins the enum.
- Cross-link the redaction class taxonomy (Public/Project/Private/Secret/Blocked) and trust class so future contributors do not conflate them; they are orthogonal.
- The ADR rejects alternatives explicitly: (1) free-text trust labels, (2) unifying trust and redaction into one field, (3) introducing automatic LLM-driven classification in v1.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance criteria:
- A new ADR file under docs/adr/ (numbered consistently with EE-269 conventions) names the canonical trust class set, the initial confidence per class, the promotion/demotion/inversion triggers, the audit log entry shape per transition, the public JSON schema field name and version, and the rejected alternatives with explicit reasons.
- The ADR enumerates exactly which transitions are agent-driven, which are user-driven, and which require a curation candidate before applying. No silent transition is allowed.
- The README trust class table and the OPUS plan §22 both point to the ADR (cross-link). If either describes a divergent set, the divergence is resolved in this bead, not deferred.
- The ADR includes one worked example per transition (e.g. "agent_assertion -> agent_validated when one helpful outcome event with provenance arrives"). Worked examples cite the eventual JSON shape.
- A small fixture test under tests/contracts/ pins the taxonomy by serialising every variant to JSON and checking the schema and ordering. The test fails CI if a future contributor adds a new variant without updating the ADR.
- EE-260 (and any future trust-class consumer) becomes blocked on this bead in the dep graph; closure on either side without the ADR landing is rejected by `br ready`.
- Stdout/stderr discipline does not apply (this is a docs bead) but the fixture test must produce JSON-stable output.

Testing and logging requirements:
- Add a contracts test that loads the ADR-referenced fixture, deserialises it, re-serialises it, and asserts byte-stability. If a future change to the enum reorders variants, the test fails with a readable diff.
- Add a docs-style assertion in CI (existence of docs/adr/<N>-trust-classes.md) so a renamed or moved ADR breaks the pipeline rather than rotting silently.
- Closure evidence cites the ADR path, the fixture path, the cross-links from README and OPUS plan, and the list of beads that became unblocked.
- If no executable test makes sense beyond the fixture and existence check, the close reason explicitly notes that and identifies the nearest implementation bead (EE-260) that adds runtime tests.

title: [e2e] Daemon supervised job recovery after kill/restart

title: [freshness] Surface stale or missing provenance in context packs
description:
Implement evidence freshness checks so context packs can honestly report when their supporting files, sessions, ADRs, or imported evidence no longer match the state that originally justified a memory. The point is to warn and explain, not to silently delete or demote memories.

Scope:
- Define freshness states for provenance: fresh, missing_source, changed_source, unreachable_source, unsupported_source, and unknown.
- For local file and workspace provenance, compare stable source hashes or metadata already stored on memory/evidence records, adding storage fields only if the ADR/contract requires them.
- For cass/session provenance, use consumed robot/json metadata or report unsupported_source if the current contract cannot verify it.
- Thread freshness into context/why explanations and degraded arrays without breaking deterministic ordering.
- Add repair hints that tell the user whether to re-import cass, refresh indexes, re-remember the rule, or inspect the source.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests cover each freshness state and deterministic ordering under mixed states.
- Golden tests pin context/why JSON when a selected item has stale or missing evidence.
- Real-binary E2E mutates a fixture source file after memory capture and proves the pack reports changed_source with no stdout diagnostics.
- The implementation does not silently tombstone, delete, or rewrite memories.
- RCH cargo check/clippy/relevant tests pass.

title: EE-411: Implement `ee procedure propose/show --json` from recorder runs, memories, and accepted curation events
description:
Source plan item: EE-411 from the `Procedure Distillation And Skill Capsules` backlog.

Task: Implement `ee procedure propose/show --json` from recorder runs, memories, and accepted curation events

Background and intent:
Turn repeated successful traces into verified reusable procedures and render-only skill capsules while preserving evidence and avoiding silent installation.

Why this matters:
This bead contributes to the overarching goal of making `ee` a dependable local memory substrate for coding agents: useful before work, auditable after work, and safe under degraded conditions. The work should be implemented in the smallest coherent slice that fully satisfies the public contract implied by the title.

Dependency context:
Original plan dependencies: EE-180, EE-401, EE-410. These are also represented as br dependency edges where the referenced bead exists.

Non-negotiable constraints:
Global implementation invariants for this task:
- Keep the CLI local-first, deterministic, and agent-native; stdout is data, stderr is diagnostics.
- Preserve the no-Tokio and no-rusqlite constraint unless a later ADR explicitly changes the architecture.
- Use SQLModel Rust plus FrankenSQLite for durable data; do not introduce a second storage stack.
- Use Asupersync for async edges and cancellation/budget behavior; do not smuggle in a Tokio executor.
- Keep JSON as the canonical public contract. TOON, Markdown, diagrams, and MCP are renderers or adapters over the same domain data.
- Mutating commands need dry-run/idempotency/audit behavior unless the task explicitly says otherwise.
- Add focused tests proportional to risk: unit tests for domain logic, contract/golden tests for public output, and integration/evaluation tests for cross-subsystem behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including the comprehensive testing and logging requirements.
design:
Suggested design approach:
- Command output must use the stable `ee.response.v1` envelope, preserve stdout/stderr isolation, and provide useful degraded-state metadata.

Implementation guidance:
- Read the surrounding modules and existing project conventions before editing.
- Prefer the planned crate boundaries from the comprehensive plan: CLI wiring in `ee-cli`, reusable domain/services in `ee-core`, models in `ee-models`, persistence in `ee-db`, output rendering in `ee-output`, and adapters in their own optional crates.
- Keep public contracts stable and versioned. Any data structure that leaves the process through CLI/MCP/hook/export should have a schema and at least one golden fixture.
- If a dependency or upstream Franken project is not ready, implement the smallest honest diagnostic/degraded path rather than faking behavior.
- Document any architectural exception with an ADR-oriented note and a verification hook.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance criteria:
- The behavior described by `Implement `ee procedure propose/show --json` from recorder runs, memories, and accepted curation events` is implemented or, for spikes, conclusively reported with a clear go/no-go recommendation.
- The implementation preserves local-first, no-Tokio, no-rusqlite, agent-native CLI behavior.
- Public command output, if any, validates against the stable response envelope and does not pollute stdout with diagnostics.
- Relevant unit, integration, golden, contract, or evaluation tests are added and named so future agents can find them.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the relevant test subset pass after implementation.
- Any degraded or unavailable dependency state returns a stable error/degradation code with a useful next action.
- No silent durable mutation is introduced; write paths have explicit audit, dry-run, idempotency, or curation behavior as appropriate.

Testing and logging requirements:
- Add or update unit tests for core logic introduced or changed by this bead, covering happy path, boundary/empty inputs, invalid inputs, degraded dependencies, deterministic ordering, and idempotency/mutation rules as applicable.
- If the behavior is visible through the CLI, MCP, hook, export, renderer, or evaluation output, add or extend a real-binary e2e, golden, schema, contract, replay, or evaluation fixture that exercises the public surface in an isolated local workspace.
- E2E/logged tests must capture command, cwd/workspace, sanitized environment overrides, elapsed time, exit code, stdout/stderr artifact paths, schema/golden validation status, redaction status, and a concise first-failure diagnosis.
- Stdout assertions must prove stdout contains only machine data; diagnostics, progress, and debugging context must go to stderr or explicit artifacts.
- If no executable test is appropriate for this bead, the close reason or a br comment must explain why and identify the nearest bead that provides coverage.

description:

title: SRR5: Speculative CASS pre-fetch + per-agent adaptive scheduling
description:
# SRR5 — Predict-and-Pre-Stage + Backpressure

## Context

A 64-agent swarm makes `ee context` calls in bursts. Each call cold-loads `cass` evidence for the matched memories — even when an agent's previous query made it likely that the same evidence would be needed in the next 10 seconds. Meanwhile, when one agent's calls suddenly take 200ms (because it just imported 50k memories), every other agent queued behind it inherits the latency. SRR5 attacks both perceived latency and tail variance.

## What the surface does

Two cooperative subsystems exposed under `[swarm.adaptive]` config:

1. **Speculative CASS pre-fetch.** The (optional) daemon (SRR1) maintains a per-agent rolling window of the last 10 `ee context` queries. After each call, it computes the cosine similarity of the query against a small set of 'likely next' templates (configurable per workspace; defaults derived from CASS-imported task patterns). For the top-3 candidates above a similarity threshold, it warm-fetches the matched memories' CASS evidence into the cache *in idle slots* (Asupersync low-priority region with a soft 50ms budget). When the actual next query arrives, evidence is already resident.
2. **Per-agent adaptive scheduling.** The daemon tracks rolling p50/p95/p99 latency per agent. When agent A's p99 exceeds `[swarm.adaptive].noisy_neighbor_p99_ms` (default 200ms), the daemon imposes a soft delay on A's subsequent requests (`[swarm.adaptive].noisy_neighbor_backoff_ms`, default 25ms) until A's p99 falls back below threshold. Other agents are unaffected. Surfaces as `degraded[].code = adaptive_backoff_applied` so the agent knows.

Both subsystems are opt-in via `[swarm.adaptive].enabled`. When disabled the daemon behaves identically to SRR1 alone.

## Why this is the right shape

- **No agent-loop hijack** — SRR5 does not control which queries agents run; it pre-stages cache contents and applies *advisory* delays. Agents can opt out via `EE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE=1`.
- **Local-first** — pre-fetch reads from the local CASS corpus through the existing `cass robot --json` contract; no remote calls.
- **Deterministic** — pre-fetch never modifies retrieval policy; same query → same response. Speculative population of caches is observable but not observable in the response body (only in `--explain` diagnostics).
- **Cancellation correct** — speculative work runs in a low-priority Asupersync region with a strict budget; cancelled when the daemon receives shutdown or memory-pressure signals.

## Acceptance

- On a 64-agent swarm running a workload with 3 'task templates' (refactor, debug, doc-update), p99 `ee context` end-to-end drops by ≥ 30% vs the SRR1-only baseline.
- Speculative-hit rate `≥ 50%` against the canonical 'task templates' workload fixture.
- Noisy-neighbor isolation: with one agent looping `ee import cass`, the other 63 agents' p99 `ee context` stays within 1.2× of their no-noise baseline.
- `ee swarm brief --include-adaptive --json` reports per-agent p50/p95/p99, pre-fetch hit rate, current backoff status.
- Failure modes: pre-fetch budget exceeded → `cass_prefetch_budget_exceeded` (info severity); noisy-neighbor flagged → `adaptive_backoff_applied` (low severity).

## Test requirements

- Unit: `src/serve/adaptive_scheduler.rs` ships inline tests for: similarity_threshold_respected, top_k_prefetch_capped, backoff_proportional_to_p99, hysteresis_prevents_flapping.
- Unit: `src/serve/cass_prefetch.rs` for: prefetch_budget_aborts_gracefully, prefetch_hit_recorded_in_explain.
- Integration: `tests/adaptive_scheduler_integration.rs` runs a synthetic 8-agent swarm (Asupersync regions), measures isolation under one noisy agent.
- E2E: `scripts/e2e_overhaul/swarm_adaptive.sh` spawns 16 shell processes calling `ee context`, asserts p99 isolation and pre-fetch hit rate.
- Perf: `benches/swarm_adaptive.rs` criterion bench against the canonical task-templates workload fixture.
- Failure-mode fixtures: `cass_prefetch_budget_exceeded.json`, `adaptive_backoff_applied.json`.

## File surface

- `src/serve/adaptive_scheduler.rs` (NEW) — rolling-window latency tracker + soft backoff.
- `src/serve/cass_prefetch.rs` (NEW) — speculative pre-fetch coordinator.
- `src/serve/daemon_hot_mode.rs` (EXTENDED, requires SRR1) — hook prefetch + scheduler into accept loop.
- `src/core/swarm_brief.rs` (EXTENDED) — `--include-adaptive` flag surfaces per-agent metrics.
- `src/config/mod.rs` (EXTENDED) — `[swarm.adaptive]` keys.
- `src/config/env_registry.rs` (EXTENDED) — `EE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE`, `EE_ADAPTIVE_NOISY_P99_MS`, `EE_ADAPTIVE_BACKOFF_MS`.
- `docs/adr/00XX-adaptive-scheduler.md` (NEW).
- `docs/swarm/adaptive-scheduler-onboarding.md` (NEW).

## Rejected alternatives

1. Hard rate-limit per agent — punishes legitimate burst traffic; soft backoff is more honest.
2. Pre-fetch by background reading the entire CASS corpus — wastes the RAM advantage; targeted prediction is the right shape.
3. ML-based query prediction — premature; cosine over recent-query embeddings gets us 80% of the benefit at 1% of the complexity.
4. Network-based fair-queueing — out of scope; local Unix-domain socket only.

## Dependencies on other beads

- Blocked by SRR1 (daemon hot-mode) — adaptive scheduler only makes sense in a persistent daemon process.
- Synergy with SRR3 (write hot path) — backoff applies symmetrically to write-side requests.

## Risk

- Hysteresis flap if p99 oscillates around threshold → tests assert no-flap under cyclical workload.
- Prediction false-positives waste cache slots → bounded by per-agent prefetch budget.
- Privacy: per-agent latency metrics could fingerprint workload patterns. Documented in ADR; metrics are local-only.

## Cost of omission

A 64-agent swarm without SRR5 will see 'one slow agent freezes the swarm' as a recurring incident. SRR5 turns that from a tail-latency cliff into a documented, recoverable degradation.

title: EffectManifest drift: handoff/eval still classified as degraded_unavailable despite real impl
description:
## Background

After eidetic_engine_cli-h0h1 (handoff capsules) and -r1np (eval fixtures) closed with real implementations and the *_UNAVAILABLE_CODE constants deleted from src/cli/mod.rs, the EffectManifest in src/core/effect.rs still classifies `handoff preview/create` and `eval run/list` as `degraded_unavailable` with `default_effect: ReadOnly`.

If those degraded paths are the LEGITIMATE FALLBACK (e.g., no fixture registry, no active task-frame), the manifest's _only_ contract is the fallback — there is no documented contract for the happy path that now exists. Either way, the manifest needs an honest second contract:

## Findings (read-only audit, build is currently red)

src/core/effect.rs `degraded_unavailable_commands()` lines ~994–1013:
- handoff preview → `handoff_unavailable`
- handoff create  → `handoff_unavailable`
- eval run        → `eval_fixtures_unavailable`
- eval list       → `eval_fixtures_unavailable`

Tests still asserting these codes are returned at runtime — these confirm the fallback path is reachable from a clean workspace:
- tests/usr005_degraded_scenario.rs:117 — `eval run --science` returns `eval_fixtures_unavailable` with exit 6
- tests/effect_contracts.rs:488–489 — manifest entries asserted
- tests/degraded_honesty.rs:3291,3330,3336,3387 — handoff create/preview degraded contract
- tests/contracts/science_analytics.rs, tests/contracts/eval_science.rs — eval contract assertions

CLI handler at src/cli/mod.rs:5149+ correctly invokes `preview_handoff`/`create_handoff` etc., and src/core/handoff.rs is 1830 lines of real implementation.

## What ships

1. Add a positive (mutating-or-read-only-success) contract entry in EffectManifest for handoff create (mutating → write_surface=capsule_file), handoff preview/eval list (read_only), eval run (read_only with optional persistence to eval reports).
2. Decide whether degraded_unavailable should remain as a PARALLEL contract (manifest supports two) or be split into runtime-only fallback (not in static manifest). Document in ADR.
3. Add positive integration tests proving the happy path: real handoff capsule written to disk with deterministic data_hash, real eval run with a fixture-id producing a report.
4. Keep degraded tests (usr005, degraded_honesty) intact — they exercise the legitimate "no inputs" fallback.

## Acceptance

- New positive integration tests pass alongside existing degraded tests.
- EffectManifest exposes both contracts honestly (or an ADR documents why the static manifest only encodes one).
- `cargo test` green; closure linter green.

title: Agent-first UX overhaul: make ee output and ergonomics dense, honest, and actionable for LLM coding agents
description:
# Agent-first UX overhaul (initiated 2026-05-10)

## Why this exists

`ee` is built for **LLM coding agents** as the durable memory substrate they call before, during, and after work. AGENTS.md is explicit: *"ee does not replace agent harnesses. It is the durable memory layer those harnesses call. Agents push evidence and lessons in; agents pull context out."*

In a live walking-through of the v0.1.0 release binary (2026-05-10 session), an agent (me) exercised every surface and surfaced 24 issues that systematically break that contract. The shared pattern: ee was designed and tested for **humans reading terminal output**, not for **agents parsing JSON and budgeting tokens**. Specific consequences:

1. **Context packs waste agent tokens** — 4× duplicated structures (`selectedItems`, `items`, `selectionCertificate.steps`, `provenanceFooter.entries`) describe the same selection. Per-item `why` is a 350-char math identity (`unit_score(field)=clamp(field, 0.0, 1.0)…`) repeated verbatim for every memory. A 1000-token pack carries ~30% scaffolding overhead, ~70% useful content.
2. **Silent low-quality recall** — `ee search "forbidden dependencies"` returns 10 results all scored `0.000`, no degraded flag. An agent will paste these as if relevant.
3. **Honest failures masquerade as data** — `learn summary` reports `memories_created: 0` with 26 memories in workspace; `generatedAt: 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`. Stub returning success is worse than `status: unimplemented`.
4. **Meta-policies are unstorable** — the secret detector substring-matches "secret"/"token"/"credentials", blocking the most important rules (e.g. "context packs must never include secrets") from being stored at all.
5. **`status.healthy: false` on every output** desensitizes — by call #5 an agent ignores the field.

The override-arching goal: make ee feel *native* to an LLM agent. JSON dense, no boilerplate, fields canonical, recall honest, errors actionable. The yardstick: an agent that has never used ee should be able to drive `remember → search → pack → why` correctly from JSON alone, without reading prose docs.

## Scope of this overhaul

Eight feature epics, each independently shippable:

- **PACK-FORMAT** (A): consolidate redundant pack structures, replace math `why` with reason `why`
- **SEARCH-HONESTY** (B): relevance floor, fix lexical fusion, dedupe, no-zero-score-returns
- **POLICY-DETECTORS** (C): value-shape secret detection, relaxed tag validator
- **SCHEMA-CONSISTENCY** (D): canonical `content` field, JSON↔MD parity
- **DIAGNOSTICS-HONESTY** (E): three-state posture, conditional banner emission
- **DISCOVERABILITY** (F): env vars in errors, top-level aliases, capability honesty
- **LEARN-CURATE-IMPL** (G): stubs → real or honest-unimplemented
- **OUTPUT-RENDERING** (H): minimal markdown escapes, numbered output, why-text rewrite

A ninth feature epic, **AGENT-TRIAD** (I), is an exploratory design spike for collapsing the verbose CLI to `ee pack`/`ee note`/`ee why` as the agent-canonical surface.

## How this serves project principles

| AGENTS.md principle | This epic's lever |
|---|---|
| "Deterministic by default — same DB+indexes+config+query → stable JSON output" | Schema canonicalization (D) + relevance floor (B1) make output stable |
| "Explainable retrieval — every returned memory answers why selected" | Why-text rewrite (A3, H3) makes "explainable" actually useful instead of tautological |
| "Graceful degradation — semantic down → lexical works" | B2 fixes the broken-but-claimed lexical fallback |
| "No silent memory mutation" | C1 (value-shape detector) un-blocks legitimate policy rules without silently dropping them |
| "Evidence over vibes — rules without source stay low-confidence" | G2/G3 produce real curation candidates from observed evidence |

## Out of scope for this overhaul

- New retrieval algorithms (reranker, query expansion). The existing two-tier searcher works; honesty fixes are the priority.
- Daemon/MCP/serve surface changes. Walking skeleton CLI is the ground truth.
- Anything that would require the agent harness to change behavior — ee must remain the layer agents call, not a layer that calls back.

## How to use this epic

1. Children are 8 feature epics (A–H, optionally I). Each feature epic has 3–7 granular task/bug beads.
2. Cross-feature dependencies are documented per-bead and wired with `br dep add`. The schema-consistency feature (D) blocks pack-format (A); other features are largely independent.
3. Verification recipe: `./scripts/verify.sh` + the new specific snapshots each child bead adds.
4. Definition-of-done for this epic: every child bead closed with `implements-surface:<name>` (not `honesty-only`), AND a fresh `ee remember → search → context → why` walkthrough produces JSON that an LLM agent can consume without preprocessing.

## Session evidence (2026-05-10)

The full agent-side walkthrough that produced this overhaul lives in the conversation transcript; key signals are reproduced inside each child bead so future-self can re-run the same probes.

title: Pack format densification: collapse redundant structures, replace tautological why with actionable reason
description:
# EPIC A — Pack format densification

## The problem (with evidence from 2026-05-10 session)

`ee context "<task>" --json` produces ~28KB of JSON for a 13-memory, 1000-token pack. Of that, only ~7KB is the actual memory content. The rest is **structural duplication** of the same selection in four parallel layouts:

| Layout | Contains |
|---|---|
| `pack.items[]` | Full record: rank, id, content, scores, trust, provenance, why |
| `pack.selectionCertificate.selectedItems[]` | rank, id, tokenCost, feasible |
| `pack.selectionCertificate.steps[]` | rank, id, marginalGain, objectiveValue, coveredFeatures |
| `pack.provenanceFooter.entries[]` | rank, id, sourceIndex, source.{uri,scheme,label,note} |

Plus `omitted[]` AND `selectionCertificate.rejectedFrontier[]` describe the same dropped candidates.

The per-item `why` string is a 350-character **math identity**, byte-identical across items except for `search_hit.score=X` substitution:

> Deterministic retrieval explanation for query \`prepare release v0.2.0\`: source=memory search_source=semantic_fast; score_components=[relevance=unit_score(search_hit.score) with search_hit.score=0.1491, utility=unit_score(memory.utility) with memory.utility=0.5000]; formula=unit_score(field)=clamp(field, 0.0, 1.0) for finite fields, otherwise 0.0; inputs are stored memory/link fields and the explicit search hit, not agent reasoning.

For 13 items: ~4.5KB of byte-for-byte repeated boilerplate that conveys ~13 numbers (the relevance scores).

The selection certificate self-declares `monotone: false, submodular: false, guaranteeStatus: "conditional"` — i.e. the algorithm reports it does NOT satisfy its claimed guarantee. We're shipping ~6KB of certificate machinery to attest that we're not certifying anything.

## Why an LLM-agent-first redesign matters here

The pack IS the product. It's what an agent prepends to its prompt. Every wasted byte:
- Burns prompt budget the agent could use for the actual task
- Increases parse latency in the agent harness
- Reduces signal-to-noise so the LLM gives less weight to genuinely useful content

A correct pack for 13 memories at 1000 tokens should be ~10KB JSON, not 28KB.

## Scope: collapse 4 parallel structures into 1; replace tautological `why` with an actionable reason; render markdown FROM the canonical JSON.

## Tasks under this epic

- A1: Consolidate pack item structures into a single canonical array
- A2: Emit algorithm self-description once at pack level, not per-step
- A3: Replace per-item `why` math identity with a 1-line reason
- A4: Add `pack.text` ready-to-prepend markdown body
- A5: Unify `omitted` and `rejectedFrontier` into one `skipped[]` array
- A6: Two-pass MMR fill so 100% of budget is used when candidates exist
- A7: Renumber items 1..N post-filter in markdown render

## Dependencies

- A1, A3, A5 depend on D1 (canonical `content` field) and D2 (JSON↔MD parity) — schema must be settled before structural collapse
- A6 depends on B1 (relevance floor) — we need to know when "marginal gain > 0 but small" is still worth including
- A7 depends on A1
- H3 (why-text in rendered markdown) duplicates with A3 — keep A3 as source-of-truth

## Acceptance gate

A 13-item, 1000-token context pack produces ≤ 12KB of JSON (target: ~10KB). Golden snapshot under `tests/snapshots/context_pack_dense.snap` freezes the new shape. A reference agent script in `scripts/agent_consume_pack.py` parses pack JSON in <50 lines and feeds the prompt body to a model.

## Out of scope

- Changing what gets selected (that's search/MMR work). This epic only changes how the selection is represented.
- Dropping the full certificate entirely — it stays available under `--verbose-certificate` for debugging.

title: A1: Consolidate pack item structures into a single canonical items[] array (4 parallel structures → 1)
description:
# A1 — Consolidate pack item structures into a single canonical array

## Evidence (live, 2026-05-10)

`ee context --json` returns the SAME 13 selected memories described in four parallel layouts:

| Field path | Per-item info |
|---|---|
| `data.pack.items[]` | rank, memoryId, section, content, estimatedTokens, scores.{relevance,utility}, trust.{class,subclass,posture}, provenance[], why, diversityKey |
| `data.pack.selectionCertificate.selectedItems[]` | rank, memoryId, tokenCost, feasible |
| `data.pack.selectionCertificate.steps[]` | rank, memoryId, marginalGain, objectiveValue, tokenCost, feasible, coveredFeatures[] |
| `data.pack.provenanceFooter.entries[]` | rank, memoryId, sourceIndex, source.{uri, scheme, label, note} |

`memoryId` is repeated 4× per item. `rank`, `tokenCost`, `feasible` are repeated 2–3× per item. Provenance URI appears in both `items[].provenance[]` and `provenanceFooter.entries[].source`.

## Acceptance

One canonical `items[]` array, each entry merging the union of fields, ordered by output rank (1..N). Compute a single hash per item and drop redundant key repetition.

```jsonc
"items": [
  {
    "rank": 1,
    "memoryId": "mem_…",
    "section": "procedural_rules",
    "content": "Run cargo fmt --check before cutting any release tag…",
    "tokens": 17,
    "scores": {"relevance": 0.149, "utility": 0.500, "marginalGain": 0.112, "objectiveValue": 0.112},
    "trust": {"class": "human_explicit", "subclass": "ee remember", "posture": "authoritative"},
    "provenance": [{"uri": "ee-mem://mem_…", "scheme": "ee-mem", "label": "memory mem_…"}],
    "why": "…",
    "diversityKey": "procedural:rule:cargo",
    "coveredFeatures": ["section:procedural_rules", "diversity:procedural:rule:cargo"],
    "feasible": true
  }
]
```

Remove `selectionCertificate.selectedItems`, `selectionCertificate.steps`, `provenanceFooter.entries`. Move the algorithm self-description (algorithm, complexityClaim, guaranteeStatus, candidateCount, selectedCount, monotone, submodular) to `pack.meta.algorithm`. Remove duplicate provenance keys.

Add `pack.skipped[]` per A5 (separate bead) to replace `omitted[]` + `selectionCertificate.rejectedFrontier[]`.

## Token-cost target

For the 2026-05-10 reproduction case (13 items, 1000-token budget), output JSON ≤ 12KB (currently ~28KB). Add `tests/snapshots/context_pack_dense.snap` to freeze the canonical shape.

## Design considerations

- **DO NOT drop the algorithm self-description.** Keep it at `pack.meta.algorithm`. It's useful once per pack, not per item.
- **Backward compat:** none required (AGENTS.md: "we do not care about backwards compatibility"). Bump pack schema version to `ee.pack.v2`. The old `ee.pack.v1` schema is removed in the same PR.
- **Verify token math:** the `tokens` field per item is currently `estimatedTokens` from tiktoken-rs. After consolidation, verify the sum over `items[].tokens` equals `pack.budget.usedTokens`.
- **Provenance:** flatten `provenance[]` into the item; drop `provenanceFooter` entirely. If a memory has N source URIs, they remain a list — the *list-per-item* lives on, the *parallel array of footer entries* dies.

## Depends on

- D1 (canonical `content` field) — must settle field name first
- D2 (JSON↔MD parity) — markdown must render from the new canonical shape

## Blocks

- A2 (algorithm self-description moves out of selectionCertificate; A1 makes the space)
- A7 (renumbering depends on canonical items[] ordering)
- H3 (markdown renderer reads canonical items[])
design:
# Design refinement — canonical item field list

The canonical `pack.items[]` entry shape MUST include:

```
{
  "rank":           int,    // original pre-filter rank from MMR scoring
  "displayIndex":   int,    // post-filter contiguous 1..N (computed by A7)
  "memoryId":       string,
  "section":        string,
  "content":        string,        // canonical name per D1
  "tokens":         int,
  "scores": {
    "relevance":    float,
    "utility":      float,
    "marginalGain": float,
    "objectiveValue": float
  },
  "trust": { "class": string, "subclass": string, "posture": string },
  "provenance":     [{uri, scheme, label, note?}],
  "why":            string,   // 1-line reason per A3, NOT the math identity
  "diversityKey":   string,
  "coveredFeatures": [string],
  "selectedIn":     enum,     // "strict_mmr" | "coverage_fill" — added by A6
  "feasible":       bool
}
```

A1 declares the field list; A6 introduces `selectedIn`; A7 computes `displayIndex`. Each sub-task adds its specific contribution; A1 is the structural baseline they all extend.

## Pack-level fields (alongside `items[]`)

```
"pack": {
  "schema":        "ee.pack.v2",
  "query":         string,
  "hash":          string,    // blake3 of canonical-form pack JSON minus volatile fields
  "generatedAt":   timestamp,
  "meta":          { algorithm: {...}, selectionStats: {...} },   // A2
  "budget":        { maxTokens, usedTokens, utilization },        // existing + A6
  "quality":       {...},
  "items":         [...],     // THIS bead
  "skipped":       [...],     // A5
  "text":          string,    // A4
  "advisoryBanner": null | {...}  // E2 conditional emission
}
```

Note `text` is OPTIONAL — agents that don't want the duplication can pass `--no-rendered-text`. Default ON.
notes:
# Cross-bead integration notes (added 2026-05-11)

A1 defines the canonical `pack.items[]` structure. Extensions:

- **A8 (opt-out flags):** `--no-coverage-fill` removes `selectedIn: coverage_fill` items; `--no-rendered-text` omits `pack.text`; `--no-skipped` omits `pack.skipped[]`. A1's canonical structure REMAINS the source of truth; A8 specifies which fields can be SUPPRESSED at the renderer.
- **A9 (pack persistence):** distinct from this bead. A9 fixes the workspace-not-found persistence bug. After A9, packs can be addressed by `pack_<id>` and re-rendered via `ee context show <pack_id>`. A1 ensures the pack-show output uses the same canonical items[] shape.
- **D6 (all-format parity):** A1's canonical pack tree is the input to every `--format` renderer. D6 explicitly tests that toon, jsonl, compact, hook, mermaid, and human formats all derive from the same A1 tree.

## Field-presence matrix (post-overhaul)

| Field | --no-rendered-text | --no-skipped | --no-coverage-fill | default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pack.items[].selectedIn=strict_mmr` | present | present | present | present |
| `pack.items[].selectedIn=coverage_fill` | present | present | **absent** | present |
| `pack.text` | **absent** | present | present | present |
| `pack.skipped[]` | present | **absent** | present | present |
| `pack.meta.algorithm` | present | present | present | present |
| `pack.hash` | present | present | present | present |

Pack hash is computed over the EMITTED fields. Different opt-outs produce different hashes by design.

Zero new test regressions: 371 contracts pass, 30 goldens pass — same as the pre-A1-phase-1 baseline.

Unblocks A4 (pack.text), A7 (already done — contiguous indices), H3 (already done — markdown reads canonical items[]) immediately. Phase 2 cleanup (legacy removal) tracked in bd-2pe1z to land the byte-size reduction target.

title: A11: ee context show <pack_id> rendering (persisted-pack lookup; integrates with A9 persistence + F2 alias)
description:
# A11 — `ee context show <pack_id>` rendering (persisted-pack lookup after A9)

## Why

A9 fixes the pack persistence bug — packs are persisted with `pack_<id>`. But how does an agent retrieve a persisted pack later? `ee context show <pack_id>` is the natural surface — and after F2 alias routing, `ee show pack_<id>` should also work.

Today (pre-A9), pack persistence fails silently, so `ee context show` doesn't have anything to retrieve. After A9, retrieval becomes meaningful.

## Acceptance

### Command surface

```bash
ee context show <pack_id> [--format json|markdown|...] --workspace .
```

Output:
- Canonical pack JSON (same shape as `ee context` create-time)
- `pack.persisted_at` field added (when this pack was originally created)
- `pack.last_accessed_at` updated on every show (per G8 audit instrumentation)
- All `--format` renderers (D6) supported

### Pack pinning

Persisted packs are immutable. They reflect the workspace state at the time of creation. Useful for:
- "What context did I use when I made this decision?"
- Audit trail for AI-generated outputs (the pack ID can be embedded in commit messages)

### Pack expiry / pruning

Persisted packs don't decay (per L3) by default — they're explicit artifacts. But `ee maintenance run --prune-packs --older-than 90d` removes old persisted packs to save space.

### Top-level alias (per F2)

`ee show pack_<id>` routes here.

## Test plan

- **Unit:** `tests/context_show_persisted_unit.rs` — create + show round-trip returns equivalent pack JSON (modulo `last_accessed_at`)
- **E2E:** `scripts/e2e_overhaul/pack_format.sh` extends:
  - Create persisted pack
  - Show by ID
  - Render in all 8 formats; each derives from same canonical tree (D6)
  - Pack hash stable between create and show
- **Determinism (J7):** persisted-pack content is byte-stable
- **Logging:** `pack_show: {pack_id, format, byte_size}` event

## Depends on

- A1 (canonical pack structure)
- A9 (persistence must work first)
- D6 (all-format rendering)
- F2 (top-level alias)

## Blocks

- nothing internal
notes:
PLAN-SPACE REVISION (2026-05-12 TealHarbor — round-trip + format coverage):

## Immutability test plan (required)

Unit test `tests/pack_show_immutability_unit.rs` (new):
1. Create pack with `ee context "<q>" --max-tokens N --json`; capture `data.pack.hash` and `data.pack.id`.
2. Wait 250 ms (forces audit-row timestamps to differ).
3. `ee context show <pack_id> --json`; capture the same hash.
4. Assert the persisted pack JSON is byte-identical to the original (excluding `last_accessed_at` and read-audit metadata).
5. Run `ee context show <pack_id> --json` AGAIN; assert byte-stable (no second-run drift).
6. Compose with J7 determinism: 3 sequential `ee context show <pack_id>` calls produce identical JSON modulo the `last_accessed_at` field.

## Format renderer matrix

Persisted packs must render in EVERY documented format (composes with D6 / bd-17c65.4.6):

- `ee context show <pack_id> --format json`
- `ee context show <pack_id> --format markdown`
- `ee context show <pack_id> --format toon`
- `ee context show <pack_id> --format jsonl`
- `ee context show <pack_id> --format compact`
- `ee context show <pack_id> --format hook`
- `ee context show <pack_id> --format mermaid`
- `ee context show <pack_id> --format human`

E2E coverage: `scripts/e2e_overhaul/pack_format.sh` adds a `pack_show_all_8_renderers` block. For each format, assert (a) exit 0, (b) non-empty stdout, (c) format-specific structural check (jq for JSON; pulldown_cmark round-trip for markdown; etc.).

## Profile-mismatch coverage

The original `ee context` may have been built with `--pack-profile verbose`. Calling `ee context show <pack_id>` without flags must surface the stored profile (`data.pack.meta.profile_at_assembly: "verbose"`) and render the same content. A NEW `--pack-profile-override` flag is intentionally OUT OF SCOPE — show is read-only by contract.

## Failure-mode fixtures

- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/pack_id_not_found.json` — invalid pack_id returns `error.code = "not_found"`, `error.details.searchedIn[]` lists the workspace pack table.
- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/pack_id_workspace_mismatch.json` — pack exists in workspace A; show invoked from workspace B; returns `error.code = "workspace_mismatch"` with both fingerprints.
- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/pack_evidence_freshness_changed_source.json` — already exists; reused by show-time replay path.

## Structured logging

Emit on each `ee context show` invocation:
```json
{
  "schema": "ee.test_event.v1",
  "kind": "pack_show",
  "pack_id": "<id>",
  "found": true,
  "workspace_match": true,
  "format_requested": "json|markdown|...",
  "render_elapsed_ms": <float>,
  "content_hash_before": "<blake3>",
  "content_hash_after": "<blake3>",
  "immutable": true
}
```

## Acceptance gate (additions)

- 8 format renderers all succeed for the same persisted pack ID.
- 3 sequential show calls return byte-identical content (excluding last_accessed_at).
- Workspace-mismatch and not-found error paths fail cleanly with structured details.
- Logging events show `immutable: true` and `content_hash_before == content_hash_after` for every show invocation.

```json
  "budgetLimit": 1000, "budgetUsed": 288,
  "monotone": false, "submodular": false,
  "selectedItems": [13 items],
  "rejectedFrontier": [11 items],
  "steps": [13 items]
}
```

The algorithm-meta fields (`profile`, `objective`, `algorithm`, `guarantee`, `guaranteeStatus`, `guaranteeEvidence`, `monotone`, `submodular`) describe the entire selection — they don't change per item or per step. They should live at `pack.meta.algorithm` once, not duplicated inside `selectionCertificate`.

Counts (`candidateCount`, `selectedCount`, `omittedCount`, `budgetLimit`, `budgetUsed`) are also pack-level; some are already in `pack.budget` and `pack.quality`.

## Acceptance

```jsonc
"pack": {
  "meta": {
    "algorithm": {
      "name": "deterministic_greedy_mmr",
      "objective": "mmr_redundancy",
      "profile": "balanced",
      "guarantee": "deterministic redundancy-controlled greedy ranking",
      "guaranteeStatus": "conditional",
      "monotone": false,
      "submodular": false
    },
    "selectionStats": {
      "candidatesConsidered": 24,
      "selected": 13,
      "skipped": 11,
      "totalObjectiveValue": 0.283
    }
  },
  "budget": {…},     // existing
  "quality": {…},    // existing, dedupe overlap with selectionStats
  "items": [13 items, per A1]
}
```

Drop the entire `selectionCertificate` outer object after migrating its useful contents to `pack.meta` and per-item fields.

## Design considerations

- **Guarantee transparency:** the algorithm claims `guaranteeStatus: "conditional"` (i.e. "no submodular guarantee"). Keep this honesty — agents should know when the selection isn't optimal. Don't hide it behind a successful-looking shape.
- **Stats vs budget vs quality:** these currently overlap. Use this work to define one place each datum lives. `budget` = token counts. `quality` = aggregate scores (avg relevance, etc). `meta.selectionStats` = counting facts (candidates, selected, skipped). No field appears in more than one section.

## Depends on

- A1 (item consolidation creates space for meta block)

## Blocks

- nothing internal
