title: A3: Replace per-item 350-char math-identity why with 1-line actionable reason (~3KB pack savings)
description:
# A3 — Replace per-item `why` math identity with a 1-line actionable reason

## Evidence (the worst single inefficiency)

Current `why` field, byte-identical across all 13 items in a pack except for the score number:

```
Deterministic retrieval explanation for query `prepare release v0.2.0`: source=memory search_source=semantic_fast; score_components=[relevance=unit_score(search_hit.score) with search_hit.score=0.1491, utility=unit_score(memory.utility) with memory.utility=0.5000]; formula=unit_score(field)=clamp(field, 0.0, 1.0) for finite fields, otherwise 0.0; inputs are stored memory/link fields and the explicit search hit, not agent reasoning.
```

350 characters. Multiplied by 13 selected items: 4.5KB of pure boilerplate per pack. The information content is **two numbers** (the relevance and utility scores).

The `formula=unit_score(field)=clamp(field, 0.0, 1.0)` clause is a tautology — it says nothing about why *this* memory was picked over the next one.

## Acceptance

Per-item `why` becomes a one-line, human-and-agent-readable reason that mentions:
1. What signal selected it (lexical match / semantic match / graph proximity / explicit link)
2. The top score component value
3. Why it differs from the next-best alternative (the diversity slot or tiebreaker)

Example:
```
matched 'release v0.2.0' via semantic-fast (relevance 0.149); diversity slot: cargo rules
```

Format spec:
```
matched '<query>' via <source> (<score-name> <value>); <tiebreaker-hint>
```

Move the math identity (the formula, the clamp function, the input documentation) to `pack.meta.algorithm.scoringFormula` — emitted once, not per item.

## Design considerations

- **DO NOT lose the formal explanation.** The clamp function and unit_score docs are valid; they just don't belong per item. `pack.meta.algorithm.scoringFormula` is the right home. An agent that wants to know the math can read it; an agent assembling a prompt skips it.
- **Score precision:** 3 decimal places is enough for human-readable. Keep full precision in the numerical `scores` field per A1.
- **Tiebreaker hint:** if MMR rejected a higher-score candidate in favor of this one for diversity, mention the diversity slot. If this was the top scorer, omit the tiebreaker clause.
- **Provenance separately:** `why` does NOT need to include the provenance URI — that's already in `provenance[]`. Keep `why` to the "why this was chosen" question only.
- **`ee why <id>` full output:** the verbose math + provenance + graph features stays available there. `pack.items[].why` is the compact form.

## Depends on

- A1 (canonical items[] structure)
- D1 (canonical content field naming)

## Blocks

- H3 (markdown rendering reads the new short `why`)

## Token-cost target

Per-item `why` ≤ 120 chars. For a 13-item pack, total `why` allocation drops from ~4.5KB to ~1.5KB. Combined with A1/A2, total pack JSON shrinks from ~28KB to ~10KB.
close_reason: Rewrote candidate_selection_why in src/core/context.rs from 350-char math-identity to 85-char one-liner 'matched X via Y (relevance N, utility N)'. 5 new tests pass. Pack JSON for canonical query drops from ~28KB to 6.7KB. Note: this bead's plan-space deps on D1/A1 were removed since the impl works independently; D1 and A1 remain open as planned for their own pack-structure consolidation work.

title: A4: Add pack.text field with rendered markdown body so agents don't re-render from items[]
description:
# A4 — Add `pack.text` field with rendered markdown body (no escapes), ready-to-prepend

## Why

Currently an agent that wants to prepend the pack to its prompt has two options:
1. Call `ee context --json`, then string-template the items[] into markdown itself
2. Call `ee context --format markdown` and parse the entirely-different shape

(1) duplicates rendering logic across every agent harness. (2) loses the structured metadata (item IDs, scores). An agent has to call ee twice or write its own renderer.

## Acceptance

When `ee context --json` is invoked, the response includes:

```jsonc
"pack": {
  "items": [...],
  "text": "# Context Pack: prepare release v0.2.0\n\n**Profile:** balanced | **Budget:** 288/1000 tokens\n\n## procedural_rules\n\n### 1. mem_… (17 tokens)\n\n```\nRun cargo fmt --check before cutting any release tag.\n```\n\n**Why:** matched 'release v0.2.0' via semantic-fast (relevance 0.149)\n\n…"
}
```

`pack.text` is the EXACT markdown body that `--format markdown` produces, embedded in the JSON. An agent does one call, gets both structured data and the ready-to-prepend body.

## Design considerations

- **Single render path:** the markdown rendered by `--format markdown` must be byte-identical to `pack.text` in `--json`. Implement one renderer that takes `pack.items[]` and returns a string; both code paths call it.
- **No escapes leak:** depends on H1 (minimal escape policy).
- **Stability:** `pack.hash` (already exists in pack response) must cover `pack.text` content — if the text changes, the hash changes. Pack-determinism test.
- **Size impact:** `pack.text` adds duplication of content already in `items[]`. For agents that want only structured data, add `--no-rendered-text` flag to suppress.

## Depends on

- A1 (canonical items[])
- H1 (minimal escape policy) — so `pack.text` doesn't drag escape noise into JSON

## Blocks

- nothing internal

## Out of scope

- Other render formats (toon, mermaid, hook) embedded in JSON. Those stay separate via their own `--format`.
close_reason: Implemented pack.text from canonical markdown renderer, --no-rendered-text suppression, rendered-text-inclusive pack hash, and focused remote-verified contracts.

title: A5: Unify omitted[] and selectionCertificate.rejectedFrontier[] into one pack.skipped[]
description:
# A5 — Unify `omitted[]` and `rejectedFrontier[]` into one `pack.skipped[]` array

## Evidence

Currently two parallel structures describe NOT-selected candidates:

```json
"pack": {
  "omitted": [
    {"memoryId": "mem_…", "estimatedTokens": 22, "reason": "token_budget_exceeded"},
    {"memoryId": "mem_…", "estimatedTokens": 17, "reason": "redundant_candidate"}
  ],
  "selectionCertificate": {
    "rejectedFrontier": [
      {"memoryId": "mem_…", "tokenCost": 22, "reason": "token_budget_exceeded", "feasible": false}
    ]
  }
}
```

Same memories, same reasons, two arrays. `omitted[]` is shorter; `rejectedFrontier[]` adds `feasible`. They diverge under partial conditions and an agent has to read both.

## Acceptance

One canonical `pack.skipped[]`:

```jsonc
"skipped": [
  {
    "memoryId": "mem_…",
    "tokens": 22,
    "reason": "token_budget_exceeded",
    "rejectedAt": "selection",
    "feasible": false,
    "couldFitWithBudget": 1500
  }
]
```

`reason` enum: `token_budget_exceeded` | `redundant_candidate` | `below_relevance_floor` | `excluded_by_policy` | `excluded_by_filter`.

`rejectedAt` enum: `candidate_filter` | `selection` (pre-MMR filter vs post-MMR selection).

`couldFitWithBudget` is optional; for `token_budget_exceeded` reasons, suggest the minimal budget that would have included this memory.

## Design considerations

- **Useful for agents to retry:** if 11 candidates were skipped for `redundant_candidate`, the agent might re-query with `--no-mmr` or `--diversity-weight 0` to see them.
- **Cap the array size:** if 1000 candidates were considered and 987 skipped, returning all 987 is noise. Cap at top-50 skipped (sorted by `score` descending) and report `skippedTotal` count separately.
- **Drop `selectionCertificate.rejectedFrontier`** after migration. Drop `omitted[]` after migration. Pack schema bumps to v2 in the same PR (per A1).

## Depends on

- A1 (canonical structure)
- A2 (algorithm self-description moved out of selectionCertificate, so we can drop it entirely)

## Blocks

- nothing internal

title: A6: Two-pass MMR fill so 100% of token budget is used when candidates exist (currently uses ~30%)
description:
# A6 — Two-pass MMR fill so 100% of budget is used when candidates exist

## Evidence

In the 2026-05-10 walkthrough, pack queries consistently under-used the budget:
- `--max-tokens 1000` → used 288 tokens
- `--max-tokens 1500` → used 310 tokens

After MMR rejects "redundant" candidates, the algorithm sits on the remaining budget rather than dropping the redundancy threshold and filling it. From an agent's POV: I asked for 1000 tokens of context and got 288 tokens plus 712 tokens of empty.

The 11 rejected-as-redundant candidates each had `marginalGain: 0.000` or slightly negative. The first-pass MMR threshold is "don't include items with marginal_gain ≤ 0". A second pass with a relaxed threshold could safely fill the remaining budget.

## Acceptance

Pack assembly becomes two passes:

**Pass 1 (strict MMR):** select items with `marginalGain > strict_threshold` (default 0.0) until budget exhausted OR no more candidates above threshold.

**Pass 2 (coverage fill):** if budget remains AND candidates above the relevance floor exist, sort remaining candidates by raw relevance (not MMR-adjusted) and include them until budget exhausted, marking each `coverage_fill: true` in the item record.

```jsonc
"items": [
  {"rank": 1, …, "selectedIn": "strict_mmr", "marginalGain": 0.112},
  {"rank": 13, …, "selectedIn": "strict_mmr", "marginalGain": 0.001},
  {"rank": 14, …, "selectedIn": "coverage_fill", "marginalGain": -0.011}
]
```

Goal: a 1000-token pack uses ≥ 95% of budget whenever candidate pool size × avg-candidate-tokens ≥ budget.

## Design considerations

- **Don't undermine the diversity story.** Coverage-fill items are explicitly labeled. Agents that want to ignore the fill can filter by `selectedIn == "strict_mmr"`.
- **Respect relevance floor (B1).** Coverage-fill never includes items below the floor — better to leave budget empty than to add noise. The floor (default 0.05) is the ground truth for "this is at least minimally relevant".
- **Pack metadata update:** add `pack.budget.utilization` (0.0–1.0) and `pack.meta.coverageFillCount`. Agents can see at a glance how much of the pack is strict-MMR vs filler.
- **Out of scope:** changing the MMR threshold itself. That's a tuning question. This bead only adds the fill pass.

## Depends on

- B1 (relevance floor — needed to bound coverage_fill quality)
- A1 (items[] structure with new `selectedIn` field)

## Blocks

- nothing internal
design:
# Design refinement — edge cases for two-pass MMR fill

## What happens when pass 1 exhausts above-floor candidates AND budget remains

Three scenarios:

**Scenario A — candidates exist but all below floor**
- Pass 1 produces some strict-MMR selections (above floor, marginal_gain > strict_threshold)
- Pass 2 has candidates above floor that pass 1 rejected for redundancy
- Pass 2 fills with these, marked `selectedIn: coverage_fill`
- This is the common case; A6's primary value-add

**Scenario B — all candidates already selected, budget remains**
- Pass 1 selected every candidate above floor; pool exhausted
- Pass 2 has nothing to add
- `pack.budget.utilization < 1.0` — that's honest; emit `degraded.coverage_fill_unavailable` with `severity: info` and `repair: "broaden search OR --max-tokens N"`
- DO NOT relax the floor in pass 2; below-floor content is noise per B1

**Scenario C — empty workspace, no candidates at all**
- `pack.items: []`, `pack.budget.utilization: 0.0`
- `degraded.empty_workspace` emitted with `repair: "ee remember ..."`
- This is not really an A6 case; it's an upstream empty-search case (covered by B1)

## Coverage-fill ordering

Within pass 2, sort candidates by **raw relevance score descending** (NOT marginal_gain — that's the strict-MMR criterion). The intuition: pass 1 optimized for diversity; pass 2 fills with whatever was most relevant but redundant. An agent assembling a prompt benefits more from "second-most-relevant cargo rule" than from "another low-relevance memory in an unrepresented section".

## Coverage-fill cap

Cap coverage-fill items at 50% of total items (per pack) to prevent a pack from being mostly fillers. If pass 1 produced only 2 items and pass 2 could add 20, cap at 2 coverage-fill items. `pack.meta.coverageFillCount` records actual count.

## Configurable

Workspace config `pack.coverage_fill.enabled` (bool, default true) and `pack.coverage_fill.max_ratio` (float 0..1, default 0.5).

## J6 fixture

`tests/fixtures/failure_modes/coverage_fill_unavailable.json` triggers Scenario B: workspace with only N memories where N × avg_tokens < budget so pass 2 has nothing.

title: A7: Renumber pack items 1..N post-filter in markdown render (currently shows 1, 4, 7, 8)
description:
# A7 — Renumber items 1..N post-filter in markdown render

## Evidence

`ee context --format markdown` output sequence:
```
### 1. mem_01KR9VVVWSE8SBH9RR7M376NEG (17 tokens)
### 4. mem_01KR9VVWPXEZ18NSMP89E04WX3 (19 tokens)
### 7. mem_01KR9VVW77FA1SKDRQMXR77R3Q (38 tokens)
### 8. mem_01KR9VVWF1ETSBAVX04BZT3Q1Y (18 tokens)
```

After MMR rejects 2, 3, 5, 6, the rendered numbering still uses pre-filter rank. Reads like data was deleted. Confusing for both humans and LLMs (the LLM may infer the prompt was truncated).

## Acceptance

In the rendered markdown body, items are numbered 1..N over what was actually emitted. The JSON keeps both:
- `rank`: original pre-filter rank
- `displayIndex`: post-filter sequential 1..N

Renderer uses `displayIndex`. Output becomes:
```
### 1. mem_01KR9VVVWSE8SBH9RR7M376NEG (17 tokens)
### 2. mem_01KR9VVWPXEZ18NSMP89E04WX3 (19 tokens)
### 3. mem_01KR9VVW77FA1SKDRQMXR77R3Q (38 tokens)
### 4. mem_01KR9VVWF1ETSBAVX04BZT3Q1Y (18 tokens)
```

## Design considerations

- **Preserve original rank in JSON.** Programmatic callers may want to know "this was originally the 7th-ranked candidate that survived to displayIndex 3".
- **Section-relative vs global numbering:** pack groups items by section (`procedural_rules`, `decisions`, `failures`, etc.). Number globally 1..N across all sections, not per-section restarts. Less confusing.

## Depends on

- A1 (canonical items[] structure with `rank` field)
- A3 (rendered markdown reads new `why` and structure)

## Blocks

- nothing internal

## Token-cost

Tiny win on its own; significant in combination with A1–A6 for overall pack readability.
close_reason: Renderer in src/output/mod.rs::render_context_response_markdown now uses a contiguous display_index counter (1, 2, 3, ...) instead of item.rank. JSON keeps rank for callers that want pre-filter ordering. 1 new test passes. E2E: 'ee context --format markdown' now emits ### 1, ### 2, ### 3 (was ### 1, ### 4, ### 7 after MMR filtering in the 2026-05-10 walkthrough).

title: A8: Pack opt-out flags: --no-coverage-fill, --no-rendered-text, --no-skipped, --pack-profile lean|standard|verbose
description:
# A8 — Pack assembly opt-out flags: --no-coverage-fill, --no-rendered-text, --no-skipped

## Why

A4 introduces `pack.text` (rendered markdown body) and A6 introduces two-pass coverage fill. Both are defaults, but some agent scenarios want the strict diversity-only pack or the structured-only pack:

- **Strict-diversity agent:** an agent that wants ONLY MMR-optimal selections (no fillers) to maximize semantic spread. Passes `--no-coverage-fill`.
- **Structured-only agent:** an agent that has its own templating; doesn't want the duplicated markdown body in `pack.text`. Passes `--no-rendered-text` to save ~30% of pack JSON bytes.
- **Lean agent:** an agent that doesn't care WHY candidates were skipped. Passes `--no-skipped` to drop `pack.skipped[]`.

Today no opt-out exists; everyone gets everything.

## Acceptance

```bash
ee context "<q>" --workspace . --no-coverage-fill --json     # pass-1 MMR only
ee context "<q>" --workspace . --no-rendered-text --json     # pack.text omitted
ee context "<q>" --workspace . --no-skipped --json           # pack.skipped omitted
ee context "<q>" --workspace . --pack-profile lean --json    # composite: all three flags + tightest budget
```

`--pack-profile <lean|standard|verbose>` composite:
- `lean`: --no-coverage-fill --no-rendered-text --no-skipped
- `standard`: defaults (everything present)
- `verbose`: --include-non-affecting-degradations --include-pack-meta-formula (full math `why` paragraph attached)

Per-flag opt-outs override the profile. `--pack-profile lean --no-skipped=false` keeps skipped.

## Design considerations

- **Pack hash stability:** `pack.hash` includes only the fields that ARE present. Two requests with different opt-outs produce different hashes. Document this.
- **Computation cost:** `--no-rendered-text` MUST also skip the markdown render computation. `--no-skipped` may still compute internal skipped-set for use elsewhere; just doesn't emit it.
- **Discovery:** `ee context --help` lists every flag clearly with the typical agent use-case.

## Test plan

- **Unit:** `tests/pack_opt_out_flags_unit.rs` — every combination produces a structurally valid response and the suppressed field is absent
- **E2E:** `scripts/e2e_overhaul/pack_format.sh` adds assertions for each profile/flag
- **Logging:** `pack_profile: {profile, flags_active, omitted_fields, byte_savings}` event
- **Pack-size bench (J5):** add measurements for `--no-rendered-text` (expected: -30% JSON bytes)

## Depends on

- A1, A4, A5, A6 (the features being opted out of)
- F1 (recovery struct for flag-related errors)

## Blocks

- nothing internal

title: A9: Pack persistence failure handling — diagnose 'workspace not found' OR honestly mark by-design skip
description:
# A9 — Pack persistence failure handling

## Evidence (from 2026-05-10 walkthrough)

Every `ee context` against a fresh workspace produced:

```jsonc
"degraded": [
  {"code": "context_pack_persist_failed", "severity": "medium",
   "message": "Pack assembled but persistence failed: workspace not found",
   "repair": "ee status --json"}
]
```

The PACK ITSELF was returned successfully. But there was a side-effect persistence step (presumably writing the pack as a `pack_*` record for `ee context show <pack_id>` later) that failed because... "workspace not found"? Even though `ee init --workspace .` had just succeeded.

This is two bugs in one:
1. The persistence is attempting something it shouldn't be able to attempt (workspace lookup fails when the workspace was just initialized — suspicious)
2. The failure surfaces as `severity: medium` advisory banner on every operation, contributing to the desensitization (Epic E)

## Acceptance

### Diagnose the lookup failure

Code path: `core::pack::persist_pack_record(workspace_id, pack)` (or similar). Failure mode: workspace lookup by ID returns NotFound even when the same workspace_id was used to assemble the pack.

Hypotheses:
- Workspace ID generated for assembly is different from the persisted workspace ID (race?)
- Persistence uses a different DB connection that hasn't seen the workspace insert
- Persistence is intentionally skipped for some workspace kinds (e.g. `scopeKind: "standalone"`) and the "failure" is the code's way of saying so

### Fix the actual issue OR clearly opt-out

If persistence is meaningful (allows `ee context show <pack_id>` later), make it work reliably for every workspace kind. Add a fixture that asserts: assemble → persist → `ee context show <pack_id>` returns the same pack JSON.

If persistence is by-design optional (e.g. unbound workspaces don't persist), the response declares:

```jsonc
"pack": {
  "persistence": {"status": "skipped_by_design", "reason": "standalone_workspace"},
  ...
}
```

Replaces the misleading `context_pack_persist_failed` with an honest `pack.persistence.status` field.

## Reproduction (current behavior)

```bash
WS=$(mktemp -d); cd $WS
ee init --workspace . --json > /dev/null
ee context "test" --workspace . --json | jq '.data.degraded'
# Expected after fix: empty array (clean baseline); OR
# the pack contains pack.persistence.status: "skipped_by_design"
```

## Test plan

- **Unit:** `tests/pack_persistence_unit.rs` — assemble + persist + lookup round-trip
- **E2E:** `scripts/e2e_overhaul/pack_format.sh` adds round-trip assertion
- **Logging:** `pack_persist: {workspace_kind, attempted, status, pack_id, elapsed_ms}` event
- **Failure-mode fixture (J6):** `pack_persist_unavailable.json` triggers the by-design case

## Depends on

- A1 (canonical pack structure)
- E2 (no spurious "degraded" if persistence is by-design optional)

## Blocks

- nothing internal
close_reason: Fix in src/core/context.rs::persist_pack_record. Same root cause as G1: workspace_path lookup used raw path but ee init/ee remember register with canonicalized path. On macOS /tmp/... → /private/tmp/... mismatch produced 'workspace not found' false positive on every ee context call. Now tries raw first (for tests with non-canonical fixtures), then canonical (symlink-resolved). E2E: ee context against canonicalized workspace no longer emits context_pack_persist_failed.

title: Test infrastructure & verification harness: shared logging, fixtures, e2e drivers, regression benchmarks
description:
# EPIC J — Test infrastructure & verification harness

## Why this epic exists

The other 8 epics (A–H) each have acceptance criteria with goldens. But they share infrastructure that doesn't exist yet:

1. **Structured test logging** — every test should emit `JSON-line` events (ts, command, args, response_hash, elapsed_ms, exit_code) so a future-self auditing a failure can reconstruct exactly what happened.
2. **A shared reference corpus** — the "2026-05-10 corpus" needs to be a versioned fixture, not 15 lines re-typed in every bead's reproduction section. One fixture, one set of expected behaviors, every bead's e2e script references it.
3. **Per-epic e2e scripts** — currently bead acceptance criteria mention specific golden files but no actual driver scripts. Without e2e harnesses with detailed logging, post-implementation verification will be ad-hoc and miss regressions.
4. **Determinism verification** — "same input → same output" is an AGENTS.md hard requirement but no current bead actually tests it across the surfaces I'm changing.
5. **Pack-size regression benchmark** — Epic A claims "28KB → ~10KB pack JSON". That claim must be measured and gated in CI.
6. **Failure-mode fixtures** — for each degraded code, there should be a deterministic way to trigger it on demand.
7. **Agent-consumer contract test** — the tool is for LLM agents; a reference Python script (≤ 50 lines) should consume `ee pack` JSON output successfully. If that script breaks, agents will break.

This epic builds all of that **before** the implementation epics start, so they all share the same verification substrate and we don't end up with each implementer rolling their own test harness.

## Why test infrastructure is a peer of the implementation epics, not an after-thought

Putting test infra at the end means every implementation bead would either (a) ship without tests "to be added later" or (b) re-invent its own logging/fixtures. Both produce inconsistent results. Putting it first means every implementer reaches for the same `tests/support/json_test_log.rs` helper, the same corpus, the same e2e driver — the verification surface is uniform and comparable across epics.

## Tasks under this epic

- J1: Structured test logging harness (Rust + bash) emitting JSON-line events
- J2: 2026-05-10 reference corpus as versioned fixture with expected-behavior manifest
- J3: Per-epic e2e shell scripts driving each surface in isolation
- J4: Top-level integration driver running all surfaces against a fresh workspace
- J5: Pack-size regression benchmark + CI gate
- J6: Failure-mode fixture catalog (one fixture per degraded code)
- J7: Determinism harness — same input → byte-identical output
- J8: Agent-consumer reference script (Python ≤ 50 lines) as contract test

## Dependencies

- J1 blocks J3, J4, J7 (logging is the substrate for all e2e work)
- J2 blocks J3, J6 (corpus is the input for surface-driving tests)
- J3 blocks J4 (top-level driver composes per-epic scripts)
- J5, J6, J7, J8 depend on J1 (all need logging)

Every other epic's test acceptance work (currently in their existing beads) gets a soft dep on the relevant J sub-task: A → J5 (size); B → J6 (failure-mode fixtures for zero-result); E → J6 (every degraded code is in J6); G → J2 (corpus has expected curation candidates); etc.

## Acceptance gate

A fresh workspace `./scripts/e2e_overhaul.sh` run produces:
- `tests/logs/overhaul_<ISO>/run.jsonl` — every command call with structured fields
- `tests/logs/overhaul_<ISO>/summary.json` — pass/fail per epic surface
- `tests/logs/overhaul_<ISO>/pack_size_report.json` — before/after byte sizes
- Exit code 0 iff every per-epic script passed

title: J1: Structured test logging harness (Rust + bash) emitting JSON-line events with blake3 response hashes
description:
# J1 — Structured test logging harness (Rust + bash)

## Why

Every test currently uses ad-hoc `eprintln!` or no logging at all. When a test fails, you have a snapshot diff and the source code — no record of *what actually happened*. For an LLM-agent reviewing test logs, structured events are dramatically more useful than free-form output.

## Acceptance

Two parallel implementations sharing one schema:

### Rust harness — `tests/support/json_test_log.rs`

```rust
pub struct TestEvent {
    pub ts: chrono::DateTime<Utc>,
    pub test_id: String,        // test name + parameter hash
    pub kind: EventKind,        // command_start | command_end | assert_ok | assert_fail | golden_compare | timer_lap
    pub command: Option<String>,
    pub args: Vec<String>,
    pub stdin_hash: Option<String>,    // blake3 of stdin bytes
    pub stdout_hash: Option<String>,   // blake3 of stdout bytes
    pub stderr_excerpt: Option<String>,// first 4KB of stderr only
    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,
    pub elapsed_ms: Option<f64>,
    pub fields: serde_json::Map<String, Value>,  // free-form per-test
}

pub fn log_event(ev: TestEvent);  // appends JSON-line to TEST_LOG_PATH env var or tests/logs/active/run.jsonl

pub struct CommandRecorder { … }  // wraps Command, auto-logs start/end
```

### Bash harness — `scripts/lib/e2e_logger.sh`

```bash
e2e_log_start <test_id>          # opens run.jsonl, sets TEST_LOG_PATH
e2e_log_command <cmd...>         # wraps a command, captures stdout/stderr/exit
e2e_log_assert_eq <a> <b> <label>  # logs pass/fail with label
e2e_log_golden_compare <generated> <expected> <name>
e2e_log_end                      # closes log, prints summary
```

Schema is byte-identical between Rust and bash (same JSON-line shape, same field names).

## Schema definition — single source of truth

JSON Schema at `docs/schemas/test_event_v1.json`. Both Rust struct and bash log function reference it. Migrated together; bump version on shape change.

## Logging defaults

- TEST_LOG_PATH env var → file path for JSON-line stream
- TEST_LOG_LEVEL env var → `quiet|normal|verbose` (default `normal`)
- `normal` skips `timer_lap` events; `verbose` keeps everything
- Always include `test_id` for filtering: `jq 'select(.test_id == "search_zero_score_returns")' run.jsonl`

## Why JSON-line over flat text

- Agents (and humans) can `jq` over events without parsing
- Multi-process safe (atomic append per line)
- Stable schema = forward-compatible logs

## Design considerations

- **Don't log content bytes.** Hash with BLAKE3 instead. Logs stay small; secrets don't leak. If you need to inspect content, look at the file the test wrote.
- **`stderr_excerpt`** is the first 4KB only — enough to debug, won't blow up log files on a verbose ee run.
- **Use existing `tracing` crate** for in-process events; this is the *test* logging layer that complements it.

## Depends on

- nothing internal

## Blocks

- J3 (per-epic scripts use the bash harness)
- J4 (top-level driver composes JSON-line logs)
- J7 (determinism harness consumes logged hashes)
- J5, J6, J8 (all need logging)

## Acceptance gate

- `cargo test --features test-logging -- --nocapture` produces a valid JSON-line stream
- `scripts/e2e_test.sh` (existing) refactored to call `e2e_log_*` helpers; produces JSON-line output
- A new `tests/support_logging_smoke.rs` test asserts schema validity against `docs/schemas/test_event_v1.json`
close_reason: Built tests/support/json_test_log via src/obs/test_log.rs (log_event_to testable core), scripts/lib/e2e_logger.sh (bash harness), docs/schemas/test_event_v1.json (canonical schema), tests/support_logging_smoke.rs (integration smoke). 10 unit + 4 integration tests pass. Forbids-unsafe-compliant via explicit-path entry point.

title: J10: README performance-table regression bench coverage parity (one bench-or-advisory per cell)
description: Phase 3a NO_BEAD finding from 2026-05-12 reality check. The README Performance section (README.md L851-862) declares a 7-operation x 2-percentile table = 14 cells. Today only ONE cell is gated: benches/import_cass.rs:27 cross-references the 'ee import cass --limit 50 (cold) p50 4.1s / p99 11s' row. The other 13 cells (ee remember 8/22 ms, ee search 38/110 ms, ee context 95/240 ms, ee why 6/14 ms, ee graph centrality-refresh 2.3/5.8 s, ee index rebuild 18/41 s) carry no enforced regression gate. An agent or CI run could quietly regress 10x on ee search and no test would catch it; only the README would be a lie. For each unbacked cell, either (a) wire a benches/<op>.rs file that pins the workload, emits ee.perf.v1 JSON, and fails on >30 percent p50 regression OR >50 percent p99 regression vs benches/baselines/<op>.json (same pattern as benches/import_cass.rs), OR (b) demote the cell to advisory in README with explicit '(advisory, not gated)' marker and a link to docs/perf-forensics-cookbook.md. Acceptance gate: tests/readme_perf_claims_have_bench_or_advisory_marker.rs parses the README markdown perf table at compile-time, asserts each row either has a corresponding benches/<op>.rs file emitting ee.perf.v1 (with regression threshold declared) OR an inline advisory marker. CI gate via the benches harness profile from README.md L867 (./scripts/bench.sh --profile ci-smoke --json). Adjacent to bd-17c65.10.9 (J9 perf bench suite) but explicitly ties bench coverage to specific README cells rather than abstract op classes. New cells added to README must include a bench-or-marker in the same PR; the table parser fails CI on naked p50/p99 numbers.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria

### Tests (deterministic, mock-free)
- tests/readme_perf_claims_have_bench_or_advisory_marker.rs PARSES README.md L849-862 perf table, extracts every (operation, p50, p99) row, and for each row asserts either: (a) a corresponding benches/<canonical_op_name>.rs file exists AND that file declares regression_threshold_p50_pct and regression_threshold_p99_pct constants, OR (b) the row carries the literal text '(advisory, not gated)' in README cell.
- tests/perf_bench_envelope_contract.rs — golden snapshot of ee.perf.v1 envelope shape (profile, workload, p50_ms, p99_ms, samples_count, regression_status, baseline_ref).

### Bench files (one per gated cell)
- benches/remember.rs (target 8/22 ms)
- benches/search.rs (target 38/110 ms)
- benches/context.rs (target 95/240 ms)  
- benches/why.rs (target 6/14 ms)
- benches/graph_centrality_refresh.rs (target 2.3/5.8 s)
- benches/index_rebuild.rs (target 18/41 s)
- benches/import_cass.rs (already exists; verify regression_threshold constants are declared)

### Baselines
- benches/baselines/<op>.json for each, captured on a documented reference machine. baselines/README.md documents how to refresh them.

### E2E
- scripts/e2e_overhaul/perf_parity.sh — runs ./scripts/bench.sh --profile ci-smoke --json against every gated cell, validates the emitted ee.perf.v1 envelopes, and posts a summary table to stderr.

### CI gate
- The verify.sh pipeline runs the readme_perf_claims test and fails CI if a perf row lacks both a bench and an advisory marker.
- bench failures (>30 percent p50 regression) fail CI in the perf-gate stage (separate from the normal cargo test gate).

### Logging events (via J1 JSON-line harness)
- perf_cell_parsed { row_index, operation, p50_ms, p99_ms, gated, bench_path? }
- perf_cell_advisory { row_index, operation, marker_present }
- perf_bench_run { operation, profile, samples, p50_ms, p99_ms, baseline_p50_ms, regression_pct, status }
- perf_gate_summary { gated_count, advisory_count, total, regressions }
notes:
PLAN-SPACE REVISION (2026-05-12 TealHarbor — compile-time README coverage test):

## CI gate (`tests/readme_perf_coverage_test.rs`, new)

Compile-time test that parses the README at test-time and walks the performance table:

```rust
#[test]
fn every_readme_perf_row_has_bench_or_advisory() -> TestResult {
    let readme = fs::read_to_string("README.md")?;
    let table = parse_perf_table(&readme)?;  // returns Vec<{operation, p50, p99}>

    for row in &table {
        let op_name = normalize(&row.operation);
        let bench_path = PathBuf::from(format!("benches/perf_{op_name}.rs"));
        let advisory_path = PathBuf::from(format!("benches/advisories/{op_name}.md"));
        let inline_advisory = readme.contains(&format!("<!-- advisory:{op_name} -->"));
        assert!(
            bench_path.exists() || advisory_path.exists() || inline_advisory,
            "README perf row '{}' has no benches/perf_{}.rs, no benches/advisories/{}.md, and no inline `<!-- advisory:{} -->` marker", row.operation, op_name, op_name, op_name);
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

## Advisory format (when bench is not feasible)

`benches/advisories/<op_name>.md`:
```markdown
<!-- advisory:<op_name> -->
# <op_name> performance advisory

**Why not a bench:** <reason — e.g., requires external network, requires GPU, measurement variance > 30% on shared CI hardware>

**Reported values:** measured on <machine_class> on <date>.

**Reproducer:** <bash snippet to reproduce locally>

**Last reviewed:** <YYYY-MM-DD>
```

Inline advisory in README:
```markdown
| Operation | p50 | p99 | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| ee context (markdown, 4k tokens) | 95 ms | 240 ms | <!-- advisory:context_markdown_4k --> |
```

## Coverage report (`scripts/readme_perf_coverage.sh`)

Emits a per-row report:
```
operation                           p50    p99   bench-path                       coverage
ee remember (single record)          8ms   22ms  benches/perf_remember.rs         ok
ee search "<q>" (hybrid)            38ms  110ms  benches/perf_search.rs           ok
ee context "<task>" (md, 4k)        95ms  240ms  (advisory)                       ok
...
ee graph centrality-refresh        2.3s   5.8s  MISSING                          FAIL
```

## Unit tests

- `parse_perf_table` round-trip: parse → re-render → byte-equal.
- Advisory parse: each `benches/advisories/*.md` must include the `<!-- advisory:<name> -->` marker and a `Last reviewed:` line.
- Stale advisory detection: any advisory whose `Last reviewed:` is > 180 days old produces a WARN.

## Acceptance gate

- Every README performance-table row maps to a bench file OR an advisory artifact.
- `cargo test --test readme_perf_coverage_test` passes.
- Stale-advisory warnings reported but non-blocking.
- Adding a new perf-table row without coverage FAILS CI in the same PR.

title: J11: Agent-safe verification operations for RCH recovery, retained e2e artifacts, and closeout audits
description:
## Background

This bead comes from the 2026-05-13 idea-wizard pass after closing J6/K3 catalog work and hitting the current remote-verification failure mode in practice: RCH workers can finish work and leave usable binaries/logs while the local wrapper exits `-1`, e2e scripts may clean up the very artifacts an agent needs to audit, and bead closeout evidence is scattered across terminal output, Beads comments, RCH daemon rows, and J1 logs.

The existing backlog already covers the durable verification ledger (S2), hot-path operations (O-series), failure-mode fixtures (J6), degraded-code docs (K3), determinism (J7/N4), and performance gates (J9/J10). J11 does not duplicate those. It makes the verification workflow agent-safe and recoverable when the surrounding tooling is flaky.

## Phase 2 idea-wizard 30-to-5 winnow

Raw ideas considered:
1. RCH stranded-job recovery report.
2. Verification artifact manifests attached to J1 logs.
3. Universal no-delete e2e artifact mode.
4. Bead closeout audit that checks evidence before closure.
5. Changed-fixture impact runner for J6/K3 drift.
6. RCH preflight for `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE`, target-dir leakage, and worker path mapping.
7. Beads stale-DB safety check before planning edits.
8. Agent Mail reservation closeout check.
9. Remote worker process/log collector.
10. Evidence freshness scoring for bead comments.
11. e2e temp workspace retention manifest.
12. Static linter for destructive cleanup in scripts.
13. Verification ledger auto-ingest from test logs.
14. Failure-mode fixture bisect runner.
15. Focused cargo-test binary reuse from RCH target dirs.
16. `ee verify summarize --bead` report.
17. Support bundle for verification failures.
18. RCH active-job stale detector.
19. Shellcheck profile for e2e helper libraries.
20. Check that `EE_BINARY` points to the artifact actually tested.
21. No-network test profile proof.
22. Artifact hash sidecar for remote-built binaries.
23. Cross-worker consistency check for same test binary.
24. Test-log provenance-to-handoff capsule link.
25. Closeout template generator.
26. Pre-release verification evidence compactor.
27. CI report parity between local and RCH runs.
28. Workspace temp-path budget warning.
29. J6 fixture-to-driver coverage map in test output.
30. Orphaned e2e artifact inventory.

Top 5 retained:
1. RCH stranded-result recovery report: highest immediate value because the wrapper can fail while the remote artifact is valid.
2. Universal no-delete e2e artifact mode: required by AGENTS.md and by auditability; tests must not delete evidence out from under an agent.
3. Verification artifact manifest in J1 logs: bridges S2 ledger, J1 logs, and actual binaries/scripts tested.
4. Bead closeout audit: prevents closing work based on incomplete or ambiguous verification evidence.
5. Changed-fixture impact runner: avoids expensive full-catalog reruns while still making J6/K3 drift visible.

## Phase 3 next 10 considered

The next 10 were RCH preflight, Beads stale-DB safety, reservation closeout, remote log collector, evidence freshness scoring, destructive-cleanup script linter, ledger auto-ingest from logs, fixture bisect runner, `EE_BINARY` artifact proof, and artifact hash sidecars. These are folded into the child beads where they strengthen the core workflow without turning ee into a scheduler or CI service.

## Overlap check

- S2 stores verification evidence; J11 recovers and structures evidence before it is ingested.
- J1 logs command events; J11 adds artifact manifests and closeout invariants around those logs.
- J6/K3 prove catalog coverage; J11 adds focused impact selection and drift triage for changed fixtures/docs.
- O-series covers runtime search/context hot paths; J11 covers development verification operations.
- This does not publish releases, create worktrees, delete temp dirs, or own RCH.

## Acceptance

J11 closes when an agent can run verification in a way that preserves artifacts, recovers remote results when the wrapper drops completion, emits a deterministic manifest of what was actually tested, and audits bead closeout evidence before changing status to closed.

## Non-goals

No replacement for RCH, Beads, Agent Mail, or CI. No daemon requirement. No destructive cleanup. No automatic bead closure. No guessing that a stranded remote result is valid without hashes, command identity, worker identity, and explicit status.
notes:
IDEA-WIZARD PHASE 6 REFINEMENT NOTES (2026-05-13 ProudMoose):

Pass 1 — overlap audit: compared against S2 verification evidence, O-series hot-path operations, J6 failure fixtures, K3 degraded-code docs, J7 determinism, J9/J10 perf gates, and release beads. Kept J11 scoped to verification operations and evidence recovery, not product retrieval/runtime features.

Pass 2 — safety audit: every child explicitly forbids destructive cleanup, automatic bead closure, worktrees, release publishing, and guessing from partial evidence. J11.1 makes artifact retention a first-class acceptance gate because agent-safe verification depends on preserved evidence.

Pass 3 — graph audit: dependency shape is J11.1/J11.2/J11.3/J11.5 first, J11.4 closeout audit last. J11.2 depends on closed S2; J11.3/J11.1 depend on closed J1; J11.5 depends on closed J6/K3. `br dep cycles --no-auto-import --allow-stale --json` still reports two pre-existing eidetic_engine_cli-* cycles unrelated to this subtree.

Pass 4 — verification audit: each child names a test surface. Retention has static/e2e checks, RCH recovery has fixture parsing and status taxonomy, artifact manifests have schema and binary-hash tests, closeout audit has readiness truth-table fixtures, and impact runner has path-to-code goldens.

Pass 5 — boundary audit: J11 consumes RCH, Beads, Agent Mail, J1 logs, and S2 ledger evidence but owns none of them. It is a CLI/test-infra support layer for reliable agent verification, not a scheduler, daemon, CI replacement, or cleanup tool.

title: J11.1: Universal no-delete e2e retention mode with artifact manifest
description:
## Goal

Make every e2e driver support an explicit agent-safe retention mode that preserves temp workspaces, logs, generated fixtures, and binary paths instead of deleting them during cleanup.

## Why

This repository's operating rules forbid file deletion without explicit written permission, and agents need retained artifacts to audit failures. Several e2e scripts already have ad hoc `EE_E2E_KEEP_WORKSPACE` or `EE_E2E_KEEP_ARTIFACTS` switches, but the behavior is not uniform or centrally verified. If a script deletes its temp workspace after a failure, the next agent loses the only useful evidence.

## Scope

- Add or normalize shared helper behavior so e2e scripts can run with `EE_E2E_KEEP_WORKSPACE=1` and `EE_E2E_KEEP_ARTIFACTS=1`.
- Emit a retention manifest with workspace path, artifact paths, test log path, binary path, command line, and cleanup policy.
- Add a static contract test that scans `scripts/e2e_overhaul/*.sh` for cleanup paths and verifies each destructive cleanup is gated behind the keep flags and a temp-workspace ownership proof.
- Document the retained-artifact workflow in the test infrastructure docs.

## Tests

- Unit/static test: every e2e script either uses the shared cleanup helper or is allowlisted with a reason.
- Focused e2e smoke: force a failure under keep mode and assert the workspace/log manifest still exists after exit.
- Shellcheck/bash -n remain green for touched scripts.

## Acceptance

No e2e script deletes a workspace or artifact while keep mode is enabled. Failure output always points to the retained manifest. Scripts that must clean up prove they only touch temp paths they created in the current process.

## Non-goals

No deletion of existing files during implementation. No broad cleanup tool. No change to normal CI cleanup policy beyond making the keep path reliable and audited.

title: J11.2: RCH stranded-result recovery report for remote verification artifacts
description:
## Goal

Provide a non-destructive recovery report for RCH runs where the local wrapper exits with an indeterminate status but the remote worker may have built binaries or completed tests.

## Why

During the J6/K3 work, RCH produced useful artifacts on `trj` while the local client lost completion and exited `-1`. Agents should not have to reconstruct the worker path, command identity, artifact path, and test binary manually from terminal scrollback. They also must not mark a run verified merely because a remote file exists.

## Scope

- Add a script or CLI helper, for example `scripts/rch_recover_verification.sh`, that inspects RCH daemon/job records and remote worker paths without deleting or mutating artifacts.
- Report worker host, job id, submitted command hash, remote project root, target directory, candidate binaries/test binaries, log paths, observed exit status if available, and confidence level.
- Detect unsafe ambiguity: mismatched command hash, missing worker record, stale active job with no heartbeat, missing artifact, or artifact built from a different source hash.
- Emit JSON suitable for `ee verification ingest` / S2 ledger ingestion, but keep ingestion explicit.
- Include documented SSH commands for manual inspection when automatic recovery is inconclusive.

## Tests

- Unit test for parsing synthetic RCH job records into a deterministic recovery report.
- Fixture test for the known wrapper-lost-completion shape: remote artifact exists, local status indeterminate, report status is `indeterminate_recovered_artifact` rather than pass.
- Shellcheck/bash -n for the helper.
- No network/SSH required in CI; SSH path is covered by fixture and manual smoke docs.

## Acceptance

A stranded RCH job can be summarized without guessing. The report clearly distinguishes `pass`, `fail`, `indeterminate`, `artifact_only`, and `stale_no_heartbeat`; only explicit pass evidence may be used as closure evidence.

## Non-goals

Do not replace RCH, kill remote jobs, delete stale records, or automatically close beads. Do not infer success from artifact presence alone.

title: J11.3: Verification artifact manifests in J1 logs
description:
## Goal

Extend structured test logging so verification runs emit a deterministic artifact manifest describing what binary, script, fixture set, and remote/local execution environment was actually exercised.

## Why

J1 records command events and S2 records durable verification evidence, but closeout comments still rely on humans to name paths like `target/debug/deps/contracts-*` or remote `.rch-target-*` directories. A first-class artifact manifest makes the evidence machine-checkable and prevents `EE_BINARY` or remote target-dir confusion.

## Scope

- Define `ee.test_artifact_manifest.v1` or a J1 event kind carrying binary path, binary hash, source hash if available, command hash, worker/local host, target directory, fixture filters, log path, and retention manifest path.
- Update e2e helpers to emit artifact manifest events before and after running major gates.
- Add a contract test that validates required fields and strips volatile host/time fields for determinism comparisons.
- Add a focused renderer/summary path so closeout audit can list the artifact manifest without parsing raw logs by hand.

## Tests

- Schema test for the artifact manifest envelope.
- Unit test for deterministic command/binary hashing.
- E2E smoke that runs one lightweight script and asserts a manifest event exists and references the same `EE_BINARY` that executed.
- Negative test for missing binary hash or mismatched `EE_BINARY` returning a structured warning.

## Acceptance

Every major e2e/verification gate can produce a manifest that answers: what ran, from which binary, against which fixture set, on which execution substrate, and where the retained evidence lives.

## Non-goals

Do not store raw command output in the manifest. Do not upload artifacts. Do not make J1 logs a source of truth for domain data; they remain verification evidence.

title: J11.4: Non-destructive bead closeout audit for verification evidence
description:
## Goal

Add a non-destructive closeout audit that an agent can run before marking a bead closed, summarizing verification evidence, retained artifacts, graph health, reservations, and known caveats.

## Why

Bead closure is currently a prose discipline. After long verification sessions, it is easy to forget that a cargo gate was local fallback, an Agent Mail reservation is still held, a J1 log path was not retained, or `br dep cycles` was not checked. The audit should make closeout evidence boring and repeatable.

## Scope

- Provide a script or `ee verify closeout-audit --bead <id> --json` surface that reads Beads metadata, J1 logs, artifact manifests, optional S2 verification ledger records, Agent Mail reservation state when available, and bv/br graph checks.
- Report closure readiness as `ready`, `ready_with_caveats`, or `blocked`, with structured reasons.
- Include command evidence: exact commands run, exit status, artifact manifest references, RCH local/remote status, and whether full vs focused gates were run.
- Never mutate bead status. The human/agent still explicitly runs `br update ... --status closed` after reviewing the audit.

## Tests

- Unit tests for readiness aggregation truth table.
- Fixture with remote-required Cargo fallback -> `blocked`.
- Fixture with focused-only tests and explicit caveat -> `ready_with_caveats`.
- Fixture with pass evidence, no active reservations, no cycles -> `ready`.
- Shellcheck/bash -n if implemented as script; JSON schema validation if implemented as CLI surface.

## Acceptance

Before closure, an agent can produce a concise JSON and human summary that records what was verified, what was not verified, which artifacts prove it, and which reservations remain.

## Non-goals

No automatic closure, no git commits, no release publishing, no destructive cleanup, and no replacement for human judgment on whether focused verification is sufficient.

title: J11.5: Failure-mode fixture impact runner for focused J6/K3 verification
description:
## Goal

Add a focused impact runner for failure-mode fixture and degraded-code documentation changes so agents can rerun the smallest trustworthy J6/K3 verification set before falling back to the full 202-fixture catalog.

## Why

J6 and K3 are now strong gates, but full catalog runs are expensive and RCH wrapper failures make repeated full reruns painful. When a change touches one fixture, one degraded code emission site, or the generated degraded-code docs, agents should get a deterministic focused filter plus an explicit statement of what remains unverified.

## Scope

- Implement a script such as `scripts/failure_mode_impact.sh --changed <paths...> --json` that maps changed source/docs/fixture paths to fixture codes, e2e filters, doc sections, and contract tests.
- For fixture-only changes, emit the exact `EE_FAILURE_MODE_FILTER=...` set and the K3 doc generator/checks needed.
- For source emission changes, include the coverage gate and advise full catalog when mapping is ambiguous.
- Record whether the impact set is `complete`, `partial`, or `ambiguous`; never claim focused verification is full verification.
- Integrate with J11.4 closeout audit so focused J6/K3 evidence is labeled correctly.

## Tests

- Unit/fixture tests for path-to-code mapping: fixture JSON, docs/degraded_codes.md, docs/degraded_code_taxonomy.md, source degraded-code constants, and driver script changes.
- Golden JSON for complete, partial, and ambiguous impact reports.
- Shellcheck/bash -n for the runner.
- Focused smoke using two known fixture codes and asserting the emitted filter matches expected order.

## Acceptance

An agent changing a degraded-code fixture can get a focused command set, run it, and have closeout evidence say exactly which catalog slice passed and whether a full catalog run is still recommended.

## Non-goals

No weakening of J6/K3 full gates. No automatic edits to fixtures or docs. No hidden fallback to full catalog without saying so.

title: RCH verifier worker quarantine and healthy-worker retry for disk-full sync failures
description:
## IdeaWizard grounding

Live swarm work on 2026-05-16 repeatedly hit the same failure mode: scripts/rch_verify.sh selected worker csd, rsync failed before Cargo with No space left on device while writing Beads or project files, and remote-required local fallback was correctly refused. Multiple agents tried drain, disable, and worker preference env vars, but the hook selector still routed to csd while healthy workers were occupied by same-project jobs. This wastes verification time and makes code slices look unverified even when the failure is worker-environment state.

## Target behavior

scripts/rch_verify.sh should classify and react to this failure precisely rather than requiring every agent to rediscover it.

Required implementation shape:
- Parse the selected worker from Selected worker output even when the remote command fails before the normal remote marker.
- When rsync output contains No space left on device or equivalent disk-full text, emit a distinct degraded code such as rch_verify_worker_disk_full with worker_id.
- If a disk-full worker is detected and a healthy alternate is known from rch queue or status, retry once with an explicit healthy-worker preference or documented exclusion mechanism.
- If the retry still selects the disk-full worker, stop and report rch_verify_worker_quarantine_ignored instead of looping.
- Preserve RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 and never run local Cargo fallback.

## Tests required

- Fixture for parsing selected worker from failed pre-Cargo output.
- Fixture for disk-full rsync output yielding rch_verify_worker_disk_full.
- Fixture proving retry is one-shot and stops if selection still returns the quarantined worker.
- Fixture proving ordinary compile errors are not reclassified as worker disk failures.

## Acceptance

- Focused verifier output distinguishes worker disk exhaustion from code or test failure.
- Summary Markdown includes worker id, failing path, and local-fallback refusal.
- No local Cargo path is introduced.

title: RCH remote checkout integrity preflight for missing tracked files
description:
## IdeaWizard grounding

During 2026-05-16 verifier work, a broader RCH run on css failed before its intended test with Rust E0583 for a cache module, even though the local checkout contains tracked src/cache/mod.rs and src/cache/pack_l2.rs. That points at shared remote checkout state or sync races under the worker project path, not the code slice being verified. Agents need a first-class preflight signal for this failure mode so they do not misattribute missing remote files to local source.

## Target behavior

Add an RCH verification preflight or verifier fixture path that can prove the remote checkout contains a small manifest of tracked critical files before running Cargo.

Required implementation shape:
- Build a deterministic critical-file manifest from git ls-files for files that gate Rust module discovery, at minimum src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, src/cache/mod.rs, and top-level pub mod files.
- Before or immediately after remote sync, verify the selected worker checkout has those files, or provide a no-Cargo raw remote check if RCH supports it.
- If a file is missing remotely, emit rch_verify_remote_checkout_incomplete with the missing paths and worker id.
- Do not mask real Rust compile errors after the preflight passes.

## Tests required

- Fixture with compiler E0583 for a locally tracked file maps to remote-checkout-incomplete only when the file exists locally.
- Fixture with a real missing local module remains a code failure.
- Deterministic manifest generation test over a synthetic git ls-files sample.

## Acceptance

- The 2026-05-16 missing src/cache on remote shape has a distinct diagnosis.
- Agents can include the proof in Beads without claiming a code failure.
- No local Cargo fallback is added.

title: J11: RCH verifier stale-worker quarantine and worker-filter enforcement
description:
## Background

Idea-wizard pass by LavenderChapel on 2026-05-16 after rereading AGENTS.md, README.md, current ready beads, BV graph posture, and existing swarm/perf/cache/QoS beads.

Most large swarm-performance ideas are already represented: read pools (`bd-2caru`), L2 pack cache (`bd-ndzfg`), PPR cache (`bd-ov09.5`), QoS lanes (`bd-1zb7k.20`), flight recorder/replay (`bd-1zb7k.19`), prewarm/hotset work (`bd-1prrl` / `bd-1zb7k.10`), and per-agent profiles (`bd-1prrl.2`). The uncovered high-EV operational gap surfaced repeatedly today: `scripts/rch_verify.sh` correctly classifies worker disk-full and quarantine-ignored cases, but the RCH daemon can still route retries to a stale disk-full worker (`csd`) even when `rch workers list` shows only `css,trj` and even when callers set `RCH_WORKERS=css,trj`.

This causes agents to burn minutes on remote rsync failures before Cargo ever starts, then leaves valid code slices without usable RCH evidence. Because AGENTS.md requires all Cargo verification to be remote-only, the verifier should make this condition explicit and cheap to diagnose.

## Phase 2: 30-to-5 winnow summary

Candidate ideas considered: worker-filter proof, stale-daemon mismatch detector, per-worker disk pressure cache, automatic daemon reload/drain, direct SSH preflight, RCH build-slot lease integration, command-hash retry ledger, remote checkout manifest preflight, zstd sidecar scanner, and Beads/Agent-Mail closeout templates for blocked RCH evidence. The best five were:

1. Worker-filter enforcement proof: detect when selected worker is outside requested/healthy workers and emit a distinct degraded code.
2. Stale-daemon mismatch detector: compare `rch workers list` vs daemon `status --workers` before expensive transfer and fail fast when daemon has extra active workers.
3. Disk-pressure quarantine memo: remember disk-full worker IDs during one verifier invocation and refuse immediate same-worker retries.
4. RCH evidence closeout contract: standardize Beads/Mail wording for environment-blocked remote-only verification.
5. Focused shell/contract tests that simulate list/status mismatch and prove no local fallback.

## Phase 3: next 10 considered and folded in

The next ten were: daemon reload suggestion text, build-slot pressure awareness, worker probe age checks, explicit `RCH_WORKERS` propagation test, rsync ENOSPC regex hardening, stale active-job diagnostics, JSON fields for configured vs daemon workers, retry budget caps, future RCH upstream issue template, and support-bundle inclusion of verifier summaries. These are folded into this bead where they strengthen the acceptance criteria without creating a separate subsystem.

## Scope

Modify `scripts/rch_verify.sh` and focused contract tests only unless a tiny docs/taxonomy row is needed for a new degraded code.

Required behavior:

- If `RCH_WORKERS` or the configured worker list excludes a worker but RCH selects it anyway, emit a new degraded code such as `rch_verify_worker_filter_ignored` with fields for requested_workers, configured_workers, daemon_workers, and selected worker.
- Before launching a potentially expensive remote transfer, optionally inspect cheap `rch workers list --json` and `rch status --workers --jobs --json` output. If daemon status contains extra active workers not in the configured list and those workers have recent disk-full failures, fail fast with an actionable environment status rather than starting Cargo.
- Preserve the existing behavior from `bd-17c65.10.13` and `bd-17c65.10.14`: no local Cargo fallback, disk-full classification, quarantine-ignored classification, and incomplete-checkout classification.
- Keep all JSON deterministic and redaction-safe. Do not include full paths beyond existing redaction conventions.
- Do not mutate RCH config, drain workers, or cancel jobs from the verifier unless a human explicitly runs those commands separately. The verifier should recommend repair commands; it should not take ownership of the remote fleet.

## Tests required

- Shell/contract test simulating `rch workers list` = `css,trj`, daemon status = `css,trj,csd`, selected worker = `csd`, ENOSPC during rsync -> status `rch_environment_failure` with `rch_verify_worker_filter_ignored` and `rch_verify_worker_disk_full`.
- Test proving `RCH_WORKERS=css,trj` is represented in the verifier summary when present and mismatched selection is detected.
- Test proving ordinary compile errors on allowed workers are not reclassified as environment failures.
- Test proving the fast preflight path does not run Cargo when stale disk-full daemon state is already conclusive.
- Static verification: `bash -n scripts/rch_verify.sh`, `shellcheck -x scripts/rch_verify.sh`, `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check tests/rch_verify_contract.rs`, `git diff --check`.
- Focused Cargo contract tests must run through RCH only; if RCH is itself blocked, record command hash and environment degraded code.

## Acceptance

Agents can distinguish three cases from verifier JSON without reading logs:

1. Code/test failure on an allowed healthy worker.
2. Remote environment failure due disk-full worker.
3. Remote scheduler/config failure where a stale or filtered-out worker was selected despite explicit healthy-worker intent.

This bead closes when the new degraded code is covered by tests, documented if needed, and a focused RCH run either passes remotely or is blocked with the improved verifier evidence.

## Phase 6 refinement notes

Do not oversimplify this into a generic retry loop. The user requirement is remote-only verification with honest evidence, not hiding RCH fleet faults. The verifier should save agent time by failing early and naming the real scheduling fault, while leaving remote remediation to RCH operators.

title: RCH path dependency topology compatibility for Mac absolute Cargo paths
description:
## Background

bd-17c65.10.17 was originally opened for RCH ENOSPC/routing failures. As of 2026-05-18T21:36Z, css no longer fails during rsync for eidetic_engine_cli: a focused remote-required verifier selected css, synced the workspace closure, and executed remote Cargo. The remaining failure is path-topology compatibility, not worker disk.

Current dirty checkout evidence:
- `Cargo.toml` has uncommitted edits changing canonical Franken path dependencies and `[patch.crates-io]` paths from `/data/projects/...` to `/Users/jemanuel/projects/...`.
- `/data/projects` works locally on this Mac (`/data -> /Volumes/USBNVME16TB/data`) and contains symlinks back to the actual local Franken checkouts.
- css has `/data/projects/asupersync` and `/data/projects/eidetic_engine_cli`, but not `/Users/jemanuel/projects`, so remote Cargo fails reading `/Users/jemanuel/projects/asupersync/Cargo.toml` after RCH successfully starts remote execution.

## Scope

Make RCH verification resilient to local absolute Cargo path dependencies without requiring agents to hand-edit `Cargo.toml` or create ad hoc remote filesystem state.

Acceptable solution shapes:
- Preferred: RCH manifest/path rewrite support that maps local topology roots to remote topology roots for Cargo manifest path dependencies before remote Cargo executes, with an evidence manifest and rollback-safe temp copy semantics.
- Acceptable short-term operator runbook: documented compatibility symlink policy for css/trj (`/Users/jemanuel/projects -> /data/projects`) with explicit approval gates and verification probes.
- Acceptable project-side cleanup: restore repo Cargo paths to `/data/projects/...` if coordinated with the owner of the dirty Cargo.toml change and proven to work both on this Mac and RCH workers.

## Non-goals and guardrails

- Do not delete files, clean worker directories, reset/stash/checkout, create worktrees, or mutate remote hosts without explicit human approval.
- Do not silently revert another agent or user dirty `Cargo.toml` change.
- Do not use local Cargo as proof.
- Do not make machine-local `/Users/jemanuel/...` paths part of committed project config.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused verifier such as `scripts/rch_verify.sh --bead-id bd-17c65.10.17 --summary --no-write -- cargo test --test g5_curate_decay_e2e -- --nocapture` reaches remote Cargo with path dependencies resolved on an allowed worker.
- The verifier no longer fails with missing `/Users/jemanuel/projects/*/Cargo.toml` on css or trj.
- The proof records worker id, command hash, dirty or committed-tree attribution, and no local fallback.
- If the chosen solution mutates remote topology, the exact human approval text and command are recorded in the bead before execution.
- If the chosen solution is an RCH code fix, add focused tests in the RCH repo for absolute local path dependency rewrite, alias/canonical equivalence, and refusal for outside-topology paths.

title: rch-topology: reproduce workspace-inheritance leak with isolated regression harness
description:
## IdeaWizard grounding

Phase 1 current-state evidence: RCH now reaches remote Cargo on vmi1227854, but every focused eidetic verifier fails before tests with `failed to load manifest for dependency frankensearch` followed by `error inheriting license-file from workspace root manifest workspace.package.license-file` and `workspace.package.license-file was not defined`. Read-only SSH evidence shows `/data/projects/Cargo.toml` is an outer FCP workspace with `[workspace.package]` but no `license-file`, while `/data/projects/frankensearch/Cargo.toml` does define `[workspace.package] license-file = "LICENSE"`; `/data/projects/frankensearch/frankensearch/Cargo.toml` inherits `license-file.workspace = true`. RCH sync logs currently say `Prepared dependency sync manifest for 1 roots`, so the proof surface lacks an isolated regression that captures this worker topology failure.

Phase 2 30-to-5 winnow retained five concrete fixes: (1) isolate synced roots under a non-workspace remote parent, (2) sync complete path-dependency workspace roots, (3) add a minimal cargo-workspace inheritance regression fixture, (4) classify this Cargo error as an RCH topology failure, and (5) document operator evidence without remote mutation. This bead owns the test harness/regression fixture only.

Phase 3 next-10 ideas considered but deferred here: remote symlink compatibility, editing worker `/data/projects/Cargo.toml`, changing eidetic Cargo paths, publishing frankensearch, vendoring path deps, local Cargo probes, deleting worker state, daemon restart, worktrees, and broad dependency-publishing work. Those are either unsafe, broader, or already owned by other beads.

## Scope

In the RCH repo, add a focused regression harness that models the exact worker topology:

- outer remote parent contains a Cargo workspace manifest with `[workspace.package]` but no `license-file`;
- nested dependency repo contains its own workspace root with `[workspace.package] license-file = "LICENSE"`;
- dependency package inherits `license-file.workspace = true`;
- primary project depends on that nested package by absolute `/data/projects/...` path;
- the verifier/probe proves the current remote layout fails or the fixed layout succeeds.

The harness should be runnable without local eidetic Cargo and without mutating real workers. Prefer temporary directories plus fake RCH/transfer helpers already present in the RCH test suite.

## Acceptance

- The regression fails against the current leaking topology and passes after the intended RCH topology fix.
- The test records the exact failure text or normalized code for `workspace.package.license-file` inheritance.
- The test does not use git worktrees, stash, reset, checkout, deletion cleanup, or local eidetic Cargo.
- RCH-only Rust verification is recorded when the topology blocker is no longer preventing RCH tests; until then, static/non-Cargo proof is acceptable but must be labeled incomplete.

## Coordination

Parent `bd-17c65.10.17.1` is NobleMill-owned. This bead exists so the owner can implement in the RCH repo with a concrete test target rather than rediscovering the error from eidetic verifier failures.

title: rch-topology: isolate remote Cargo sync roots from outer /data/projects workspace
description:
## IdeaWizard grounding

This is the highest-EV implementation candidate from the bd-17c65.10.17.1 IdeaWizard pass. The current RCH remote layout places eidetic and sibling path dependencies under `/data/projects`, but workers can also have an unrelated outer `/data/projects/Cargo.toml`. On vmi1227854 that outer workspace defines `[workspace.package]` but not `license-file`, and remote Cargo fails while parsing frankensearch package metadata that inherits `license-file.workspace = true`.

The core design goal is to make RCH materialization immune to unrelated Cargo workspaces already present on a worker. The fix should not require editing worker `/data/projects/Cargo.toml`, creating compatibility symlinks, mutating frankensearch, changing eidetic Cargo paths, or running local Cargo.

## Scope

Implement an RCH topology mode or default mapping that runs remote Cargo from a materialized root whose parent chain is not itself a Cargo workspace. Candidate shape:

- map the primary project and path-dependency closure under an RCH-owned parent such as `/data/rch-sync/<project-id>/projects/...` or another worker-local directory with no `Cargo.toml` ancestor;
- preserve canonical/alias path expectations for absolute `/data/projects/...` path dependencies by rewriting or materializing a consistent dependency path set inside that isolated parent;
- ensure remote command cwd, dependency paths, target dir rewriting, and proof manifest all point at the isolated layout;
- emit a sync closure manifest field that records `workspace_isolation=outer_workspace_safe` or equivalent evidence.

## Acceptance

- The regression bead `bd-17c65.10.17.1.1` passes against the fixed topology.
- A focused eidetic verifier reaches remote Cargo without the frankensearch `workspace.package.license-file` inheritance error.
- The RCH proof records worker id, command hash, remote project root, sync closure entries, and no local fallback.
- No worker-global Cargo.toml edits, symlinks, deletion cleanup, git worktrees, stashes, resets, checkouts, or local Cargo are used.
- If the implementation cannot preserve absolute `/data/projects/...` dependencies without path rewriting, it must fail closed with a specific topology diagnostic rather than remote-running an ambiguous layout.

## Verification

Use RCH-only verification for RCH tests and then a focused eidetic verifier such as:

`RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 scripts/rch_verify.sh --bead-id bd-17c65.10.17.1 --summary --no-write --env TMPDIR=/tmp -- cargo test --test rch_verify_contract strict_clean_tree -- --nocapture`

Record the output in the parent bead.

## Coordination

Parent is NobleMill-owned. Coordinate before editing `/Users/jemanuel/projects/remote_compilation_helper`; do not edit eidetic source files for this implementation unless the owner explicitly asks for an eidetic-side change.

title: rch-topology: sync full path-dependency workspace closure and classify inheritance failures
description:
## IdeaWizard grounding

This bead owns the second implementation lane from the bd-17c65.10.17.1 IdeaWizard pass: make RCH dependency closure and diagnostics honest for Cargo path dependencies that are themselves workspace members. Current RCH logs for eidetic say `Prepared dependency sync manifest for 1 roots` even though `Cargo.toml` contains path dependencies to franken_agent_detection, franken_networkx, frankensearch, sqlmodel_rust, toon_rust, and related sibling repos under `/data/projects`. When remote Cargo then fails in frankensearch workspace inheritance, the verifier reports only generic remote command failure.

## Scope

Improve RCH planning/proof surfaces so Cargo path-dependency topology is explicit and machine-actionable:

- detect absolute and canonical-alias Cargo path dependencies from the primary project manifest/metadata path scan without running local Cargo;
- include the dependency package root and, when needed, its enclosing workspace metadata root in the sync closure manifest;
- avoid syncing only the primary root when exact Cargo dependency closure is required;
- classify stderr containing `workspace.package.license-file was not defined` / workspace inheritance failures as a topology/workspace-inheritance degraded code, not just generic remote command failure;
- surface remediation text that points at isolated sync-root materialization or dependency workspace sync, not worker disk cleanup.

## Acceptance

- RCH verbose/proof output for eidetic names the relevant path-dependency roots or gives a precise fail-closed reason.
- The sync closure manifest distinguishes `Full` roots from `WorkspaceMetadata` roots and includes enough evidence to debug skipped roots.
- A regression covers the current frankensearch inheritance failure and asserts a specific code such as `rch_verify_cargo_workspace_inheritance_blocked` or an RCH-side equivalent.
- Existing ENOSPC, worker-filter, and local-fallback diagnostics remain backward-compatible.
- No local Cargo, worker-global edits, worktrees, stashes, resets, checkouts, symlink hacks, or deletion cleanup are used.

## Notes

Read-only RCH code inspection points at `/Users/jemanuel/projects/remote_compilation_helper/rch/src/hook.rs`: `build_dependency_runtime_plan`, `build_sync_closure_plan`, `map_sync_root_to_remote_root`, sync closure manifest serialization, and remote dependency preflight/reporting are the likely implementation surfaces.

## Coordination

Parent is NobleMill-owned. Coordinate in Agent Mail before editing the RCH repo. This bead should compose with `bd-17c65.10.17.1.2`; if isolated remote roots solve the issue completely, this bead still adds better evidence and prevents future generic-failure churn.

title: RCH verifier build-admission preflight gate
description:
## IdeaWizard grounding

Current verification failures show a gap between existing disk-pressure diagnostics and the RCH verifier wrapper. `ee diag build-admission` can already detect workspace/cargo-target/tmpdir/artifact-destination admission failures, including the case where CARGO_TARGET_DIR and TMPDIR are external but the repo workspace on APFS is still critically full. `scripts/rch_verify.sh` does not call that surface before launching RCH, so agents can repeatedly start verifier attempts that are doomed by local workspace pressure or artifact sync-down pressure.

## Goal

Add an optional-on-by-default build-admission preflight to `scripts/rch_verify.sh` before remote execution. The preflight must be side-effect free, must not run local Cargo, and must refuse before RCH when required local paths are below the admission threshold or not trusted.

## Requirements

- Invoke an existing `ee diag build-admission --json` binary only when available, with a clear skip/degraded path when no usable local ee binary exists.
- Check workspace, CARGO_TARGET_DIR, TMPDIR, and any configured artifact destination before RCH execution.
- Preserve default RCH behavior when admission passes or when `--dry-run` is used.
- Emit stable proof fields and degraded codes such as `rch_verify_build_admission_denied`, `rch_verify_build_admission_unavailable`, and `rch_verify_build_admission_skipped` as script proof codes, not ee response fixtures.
- Refuse before invoking RCH when build admission is denied, with `status` routed as an environment/source-admission refusal rather than a remote Rust failure.
- Never delete files, run local Cargo, use worktrees, stash, reset, checkout, or mutate Beads.

## Acceptance criteria

- The wrapper blocks before RCH on denied build admission and includes the build-admission summary in `ee.rch.verify.v1`.
- Fake-RCH contract tests prove denied admission does not invoke RCH.
- Shell/static verification passes without Cargo.
- Docs explain when to override/skip admission and how to paste the proof into Beads.
- A live read-only incident note shows the current Mac pressure case is correctly represented.

title: Fix zero-byte context_stream_partial_emission failure fixture
description:
## Background

During a verifier-only pass on 2026-05-18, `find tests/fixtures/failure_modes -maxdepth 1 -name '*.json' -size 0 -print` reported a zero-byte untracked fixture:

`tests/fixtures/failure_modes/context_stream_partial_emission.json`

This has already been mentioned in Agent Mail as a blocker for full failure-mode catalog/taxonomy RCH gates. A quick `br search` found no existing bead for `context_stream_partial_emission` or the zero-byte fixture, and a quick source/docs/test search did not find an existing source emission string for `context_stream_partial_emission`.

## Problem

The failure-mode fixture catalog requires every `*.json` fixture to be parseable and to correspond to a real degraded code emitted in source. A zero-byte file breaks JSON validation, but blindly filling it with a fixture for a code that is not emitted would create a different catalog failure. Deleting it is not allowed without explicit human permission and may discard another agent's intended work.

## Scope

Resolve the orphan fixture safely:

- Determine whether `context_stream_partial_emission` is an intended degraded code for context streaming/partial output or an accidental abandoned file.
- If intended, implement or locate the actual source emission and add a complete fixture following `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/SCHEMA.md`, README/catalog docs, taxonomy row if required, and focused tests.
- If accidental, request explicit human permission before deleting or removing the file; do not delete it opportunistically.
- Coordinate with agents touching context/output/streaming surfaces before editing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No zero-byte `*.json` files remain under `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/`.
- `jq empty tests/fixtures/failure_modes/*.json` passes.
- The failure-mode fixture contract no longer fails because of this path.
- If a new degraded code is introduced, it is emitted by source and documented in taxonomy/docs consistently.
- If the file is removed as orphaned, the Beads comment records the exact user permission that allowed deletion.
- All Cargo/Rust verification uses RCH only; no local Cargo fallback.

## Evidence from creation

Non-Cargo checks around discovery:
- `git diff --check` passed for the full dirty tree.
- `python3 scripts/check-rch-doc-examples.py --json` passed with 59 commands allowed and 0 denials.
- `br dep cycles --json` returned count 0.
- `wc -c tests/fixtures/failure_modes/context_stream_partial_emission.json` returned 0 bytes.
