title: J2: 2026-05-10 reference corpus as versioned fixture with declared expected-behavior manifest
description:
# J2 — 2026-05-10 reference corpus as versioned fixture

## Why

Every overhaul bead's "reproduction" section names a handful of memories ("Forbidden deps: tokio, rusqlite…", "Run cargo fmt --check…", etc.). They're scattered across bead descriptions and would drift if re-typed in each test. A single fixture decouples corpus from test code.

## Acceptance

Three files under `tests/fixtures/corpus/`:

### `corpus_2026_05_10.jsonl` — the corpus (~15+ memories)

JSON-line, one memory per line, mirrors what `ee remember` would persist:

```jsonl
{"content":"Run cargo fmt --check before cutting any release tag; CI rejects unformatted code.","level":"procedural","kind":"rule","tags":["release","cargo"],"confidence":0.9}
{"content":"Forbidden deps: tokio, rusqlite, petgraph, hyper, axum, tower, reqwest, sqlx, diesel, sea-orm — CI greps for them.","level":"procedural","kind":"rule","tags":["release","deps"],"confidence":0.95}
…
```

Include the entire 2026-05-10 seed set PLUS the four originally-rejected ones (decisions with v0.1.0/v0.2.0 tags, the cancellation-token rule, the secret-policy rule) so the corpus also covers C1 (secret detector) and C3 (tag validator) success cases.

### `corpus_2026_05_10_expected.json` — declared expectations

```json
{
  "queries": {
    "forbidden dependencies": {
      "expected_top_docs": ["<canonical id, by content match>"],
      "expected_source": "lexical|hybrid",
      "expected_min_top_score": 0.10,
      "expected_degraded_absent": ["no_relevant_results"],
      "comment": "Literal lexical overlap; BM25 should be at least competitive with semantic"
    },
    "how do I cut a release safely": {
      "expected_top_doc_kinds": ["procedural/rule"],
      "expected_min_top_score": 0.10
    }
  },
  "policy_acceptance": [
    {"content": "Context packs must never include secrets.", "should_accept": true, "reason": "meta-policy mention, not a value"},
    {"content": "API_KEY=sk-abc123def456ghi789", "should_accept": false, "detected_pattern": "openai_sk_prefix"}
  ],
  "policy_tag_acceptance": [
    {"tag": "v0.1.0", "should_accept": true},
    {"tag": "release", "should_accept": true},
    {"tag": "with space", "should_accept": false}
  ],
  "curation_expectations": {
    "min_candidates_after_seed": 1,
    "candidate_should_cover": "cargo rules cluster"
  }
}
```

### `corpus_2026_05_10_seed.sh` — load helper

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Loads corpus into a given workspace. Used by every per-epic e2e script.
set -euo pipefail
WS="${1:?workspace path required}"
EE="${EE_BINARY:-ee}"
LOG_FILE="${TEST_LOG_PATH:-/dev/null}"
…iterates the JSONL, calls $EE remember, logs each via J1 harness…
```

## Why a corpus, not 15 ad-hoc seed scripts

- Schema discipline: every memory has a known kind/level/tags/confidence; tests verify these
- Reproducibility: any agent can `corpus_2026_05_10_seed.sh /tmp/fresh_ws` and have the exact state we're testing against
- Comparability: a future "2026-12-31 corpus" can coexist; tests reference by version

## Memory ID determinism

Memory IDs are ULIDs (time-ordered) — they will differ per seed run. Reference docs by content hash, not by ID:

```bash
content_id() { echo -n "$1" | blake3sum | cut -c1-12; }
```

Expected behavior records use content hashes as keys, not generated IDs.

## Depends on

- nothing internal

## Blocks

- J3 (per-epic scripts load corpus)
- J6 (failure-mode fixtures extend the corpus)
- B5 (embedder synonym blind spots reference these fixtures)
- G3 (curation expectations live in the corpus manifest)

## Acceptance gate

- `corpus_2026_05_10_seed.sh /tmp/test_ws` succeeds; `ee memory list` shows exact count from corpus
- `tests/corpus_integrity.rs` validates JSON-line schema, no duplicate contents, all expectations reference real corpus entries

title: J3: Per-epic e2e shell scripts driving each surface in isolation (scripts/e2e_overhaul/*.sh)
description:
# J3 — Per-epic e2e shell scripts driving each surface in isolation

## Why

Currently no per-surface e2e exists for pack format, search honesty, etc. Without surface-specific drivers, the only place a regression shows up is in `scripts/e2e_advanced.sh` (an existing monolith). Adding per-epic scripts means:

- A bug introduced in pack format is caught by `pack_format.sh` failing, not by a vague e2e timeout
- Each implementation bead has a concrete pre-implementation script to run that fails → after implementation that passes
- CI can parallelize over per-epic scripts

## Acceptance

Eight scripts under `scripts/e2e_overhaul/`, one per implementation epic:

```
scripts/e2e_overhaul/
  ├── pack_format.sh             # Epic A
  ├── search_honesty.sh          # Epic B
  ├── policy_detectors.sh        # Epic C
  ├── schema_consistency.sh      # Epic D
  ├── diagnostics_honesty.sh     # Epic E
  ├── discoverability.sh         # Epic F
  ├── learn_curate.sh            # Epic G
  ├── output_rendering.sh        # Epic H
  └── lib/
      └── shared.sh              # sources e2e_logger.sh (J1) and corpus_seed.sh (J2)
```

### Script structure (every per-epic script follows this template)

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib/shared.sh"

e2e_log_start "epic_A_pack_format"
WS=$(mktemp -d /tmp/ee-e2e-pack.XXXXXX)
trap "e2e_log_end; rm -rf $WS" EXIT

# Setup
e2e_log_command "$EE" init --workspace "$WS" --json
"$(dirname "$0")/../../tests/fixtures/corpus/corpus_2026_05_10_seed.sh" "$WS"

# Surface-specific assertions
PACK_JSON=$(e2e_log_command "$EE" context "prepare release" --workspace "$WS" --max-tokens 1000 --json)
PACK_SIZE=$(echo "$PACK_JSON" | wc -c)
e2e_log_assert_le "$PACK_SIZE" 12000 "pack_size_target"

ITEM_COUNT=$(echo "$PACK_JSON" | jq '.data.pack.items | length')
e2e_log_assert_eq "$ITEM_COUNT" "13" "expected_item_count"

# … many more assertions …

e2e_log_summary
```

Each script writes its summary to `tests/logs/active/epic_<name>_summary.json`.

### Per-script assertion catalog

Each script's description in the bead body lists every assertion (currently shown above as comments). The full assertion catalog is part of the acceptance criteria.

## Design considerations

- **Use `bash`, not `sh`.** We rely on arrays and `local`.
- **Isolate workspaces.** Every script uses `mktemp -d`, cleans up on exit. No shared state.
- **Honor `EE_BINARY` env var.** Default to `target/release/ee`; CI overrides for cross-platform builds.
- **Fail-fast within script** (`set -e`). Aggregate pass/fail at top level (J4).
- **Logging level:** scripts inherit `TEST_LOG_LEVEL` from environment; default `normal`.

## Depends on

- J1 (logging substrate)
- J2 (corpus seed)

## Blocks

- J4 (top-level integration driver composes these)
- Every implementation bead's acceptance gate (each one references the relevant per-epic script)

## Acceptance gate

- `scripts/e2e_overhaul/*.sh` runs against current `target/release/ee`
- Currently expected to FAIL (pre-implementation) — failures are documented and become the "after implementation" target
- After Epic X ships, `scripts/e2e_overhaul/<epic_x>.sh` exits 0
close_reason:
J3 implemented. Eight per-epic e2e shell scripts under scripts/e2e_overhaul/ drive each surface in isolation against a temp workspace, asserting shipped beads with real assertions and recording unshipped beads via todo_assert for an honest progress picture.

Smoke run against the current binary: 37 PASS, 0 FAIL, 36 TODOs covering A1/A2/A4/A5/A6/A8/A11, B2/B6/B7/B8/B10/B11, C2/C4/C5, D2/D3/D4/D5/D6, E2/E3/E5/E6, F3/F5/F6, G3-G9, H2/H4.

The shared helper library (lib/shared.sh) sources J1's e2e_logger.sh and J2's corpus seed, relaxes errexit inside per-script bodies so every assertion runs, and pre-handles workspace setup/teardown via a single epic_setup call. Scripts run cleanly without EE_TEST_LOG_PATH (J1 helpers no-op silently) or capture full event traces when EE_TEST_LOG_PATH is set.

Each script is self-documenting at the top: shipped vs todo beads, what each assertion exercises, how to invoke. Unblocks J4 (top-level integration driver scripts/e2e_overhaul.sh) and every implementation bead's acceptance gate, which now have a concrete per-epic script to run before and after their changes.

### Operating modes

- `./scripts/e2e_overhaul.sh` — full run, all epics
- `./scripts/e2e_overhaul.sh --only A,B` — run only specified epic letters
- `./scripts/e2e_overhaul.sh --skip H` — skip specified epics
- `./scripts/e2e_overhaul.sh --bail-on-first-failure` — stop at first epic failure
- `./scripts/e2e_overhaul.sh --json-summary-to <path>` — output summary to specified file

### CI integration

Added to `scripts/verify.sh` as a new gate after the basic E2E and before advanced E2E:

```
6.5. Overhaul integration (./scripts/e2e_overhaul.sh)
```

Gated behind `VERIFY_OVERHAUL=1` until enough epics ship to make the suite reliably pass; then flipped on by default.

## Design considerations

- **Composability:** the driver doesn't duplicate per-epic logic; it just orchestrates and aggregates.
- **Resilient parsing:** per-epic scripts may panic mid-run; driver detects via exit code + missing summary file, marks epic `error: incomplete_summary`.
- **Cleanup:** even if scripts leave temp workspaces, driver removes them in trap.

## Depends on

- J3 (per-epic scripts must exist)
- J1 (logging substrate)

## Blocks

- nothing internal — this is the top of the J epic

## Acceptance gate

`./scripts/e2e_overhaul.sh --only A,B,C` produces a summary with status per epic and exits with code matching `epics_fail == 0`.

title: J5: Pack-size regression benchmark + CI gate (benches/pack_size.rs + baseline)
description:
# J5 — Pack-size regression benchmark + CI gate

## Why

Epic A claims pack JSON drops from ~28KB to ~10KB. Without a measured gate, the claim drifts. We need a benchmark that:
- Runs against the canonical corpus (J2)
- Produces a stable, comparable byte-size measurement per pack
- Fails CI if pack size grows beyond a threshold

## Acceptance

### Benchmark — `benches/pack_size.rs`

Criterion harness measuring:
- `pack_json_bytes` — `ee context "<query>" --json --max-tokens N` output size for N ∈ {500, 1000, 2000, 4000}
- `pack_text_bytes` — markdown render byte size for same
- `tokens_used_per_pack` — actual tokens (per `pack.budget.usedTokens`)
- `bytes_per_token` — ratio (lower = denser pack)

Outputs go to `target/criterion/pack_size/`. Per existing AGENTS.md convention benchmarks are excluded from normal test gate and run via `./scripts/verify.sh --include-bench` or `./scripts/bench.sh`.

### Regression gate — `scripts/bench_pack_regression.sh`

Runs the benchmark, parses Criterion output, compares against committed baseline at `benches/baselines/pack_size_v0_2.json`. Fails if:

```
pack_json_bytes_for_1000_tokens > baseline * 1.05    # ≤ 5% growth
bytes_per_token > baseline_bpt * 1.10                # ≤ 10% growth
```

After each epic milestone, the baseline gets re-recorded (with explicit commit message).

### Initial baseline (pre-implementation, from 2026-05-10 observations)

```json
{
  "schema": "ee.bench.pack_size.baseline.v1",
  "recorded_at": "2026-05-10",
  "ee_version": "0.1.0",
  "measurements": {
    "pack_json_bytes_for_1000_tokens": {"value": 28000, "stddev": 2000, "n": 5},
    "pack_text_bytes_for_1000_tokens": {"value": 3500, "stddev": 200, "n": 5},
    "tokens_used_per_pack_for_1000_tokens": {"value": 288, "stddev": 30, "n": 5},
    "bytes_per_token": {"value": 97, "stddev": 10, "n": 5}
  },
  "comment": "Pre-overhaul baseline; expect bytes_per_token to drop ~70% post-Epic A"
}
```

### Post-A target

```json
"measurements": {
  "pack_json_bytes_for_1000_tokens": {"value": 12000, "tolerance": "±10%"},
  "tokens_used_per_pack_for_1000_tokens": {"value": 950, "tolerance": "±5%"},
  "bytes_per_token": {"value": 12, "tolerance": "±15%"}
}
```

(Token utilization should approach 100% per A6 two-pass fill.)

## Design considerations

- **Don't conflate raw bytes with usefulness.** Bytes per token is the real metric — bigger pack with more useful content is fine; same content in fewer bytes is the win.
- **Deterministic input:** Criterion seeds the corpus from J2 fixture, identical across runs.
- **Multiple budget sizes** catch budget-utilization regressions (A6).

## Depends on

- J1 (logging during bench runs)
- J2 (corpus is the input)

## Blocks

- nothing internal

## Acceptance gate

- `cargo bench --bench pack_size` runs to completion, populates `target/criterion/pack_size/`
- `./scripts/bench_pack_regression.sh` compares against baseline, exits 0 within tolerance
- Baseline committed at `benches/baselines/pack_size_v0_1.json`

title: J6: Failure-mode fixture catalog — one fixture per degraded code (verifies expected emission)
description:
# J6 — Failure-mode fixture catalog

## Why

Each `degraded[]` code in the response envelope is supposed to fire under specific conditions. Today there's no way to verify "when X happens, code Y is emitted" because we can't reliably trigger X in a test. J6 builds fixtures that intentionally produce each failure mode.

## Acceptance

### Fixture catalog — `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/`

One JSON file per degraded code, describing:
- How to set up a workspace state that triggers the code
- The expected response shape (which `degraded[]` codes should appear)
- The repair action that should resolve it

```jsonc
// tests/fixtures/failure_modes/no_relevant_results.json
{
  "schema": "ee.fixture.failure_mode.v1",
  "degraded_code": "no_relevant_results",
  "epic": "B",
  "trigger": {
    "kind": "search_query_below_floor",
    "setup": [
      {"action": "init_workspace"},
      {"action": "remember", "content": "Apples are red and crunchy.", "level": "semantic", "kind": "fact"}
    ],
    "operation": {"action": "search", "query": "Byzantine consensus algorithms"}
  },
  "expected_response": {
    "results_count": 0,
    "degraded_codes_present": ["no_relevant_results"],
    "degraded_codes_absent": ["weak_query_recall", "search_index_stale"]
  },
  "expected_repair_kinds": ["broaden_query", "lower_relevance_floor"]
}
```

### Drive script — `scripts/e2e_overhaul/failure_modes.sh`

Reads every fixture, applies the trigger, runs the operation, asserts the expected response. Logs via J1 harness.

### Codes that must have fixtures (post-overhaul)

- `no_relevant_results` (B1)
- `weak_query_recall` (B5)
- `lexical_unavailable` (B2 honesty fallback)
- `lexical_fusion_disabled` (B2 honesty fallback)
- `context_profile_budget_capped` (existing)
- `search_index_stale` (E2-recategorized — should rarely fire after E2)
- `coverage_fill_unavailable` (A6 new code)
- `policy_secret_detected` (C1 new code)
- `policy_secret_bypass_used` (C2 new code)
- `tag_normalize_collision` (C3 new code, e.g. NFC collision)
- `cass_binary_not_configured` (E4-recategorized to info, not warning)
- `learn_agenda_unimplemented` (G2 honesty path, if taken)
- `auto_propose_skipped_too_few_neighbors` (G3 expected non-fire)

Each new code introduced by the overhaul comes with its fixture in the same PR.

## Design considerations

- **Coverage gate:** `tests/failure_mode_catalog_coverage.rs` enumerates every `degraded[]` code emitted in `src/` and asserts each has a fixture file. Fails CI on a new code without a fixture.
- **No real secrets in trigger setups.** Use known-fake values; the secret-value detector is tested with synthesized prefixes (sk-FAKE…), not real keys.
- **Fixtures double as docs.** `docs/degraded_codes.md` (K3) is auto-generated from this catalog.

## Depends on

- J1, J2
- All epics that introduce new degraded codes (B1, B5, A6, C1, C2, C3, E4, G2, G3) have soft deps — each one's fixture lands in the implementing PR

## Blocks

- K3 (docs auto-generation)

## Acceptance gate

- `tests/failure_mode_catalog_coverage.rs` passes — every emitted code has a fixture
- `scripts/e2e_overhaul/failure_modes.sh` exercises every fixture, all assertions pass

title: J7: Determinism harness — same input → byte-identical output across 3 runs, every surface
description:
# J7 — Determinism harness

## Why

AGENTS.md non-negotiable: *"Given the same database, indexes, config, and query, JSON output must be stable. Ranking ties must be deterministic. Context pack hashes must be reproducible."*

No existing harness actually tests this end-to-end. We need a script that takes the same input twice (across separate process invocations) and asserts byte-identical output.

## Acceptance

### Harness — `scripts/e2e_overhaul/determinism.sh`

For each surface that emits a hashable response:

```bash
# Seed corpus once
WS=$(mktemp -d)
$EE init --workspace $WS --json > /dev/null
corpus_2026_05_10_seed.sh $WS

# Run the same query 3× and hash each output
for run in 1 2 3; do
  $EE context "prepare release" --workspace $WS --max-tokens 1000 --json | jq -S '.' | blake3sum > /tmp/det_$run.hash
done

# Assert all three are identical
if [ "$(uniq /tmp/det_*.hash | wc -l)" -ne 1 ]; then
  e2e_log_assert_fail "context determinism" "3 runs produced different hashes"
fi
```

### Surfaces tested for determinism

- `ee search "<q>" --json` — same scores, same order, same hash
- `ee context "<q>" --json --max-tokens N` — same `pack.hash`, byte-identical JSON
- `ee why <id> --json` — same audit timeline, same scoring breakdown
- `ee memory list --json` — same order, same IDs
- `ee status --json` — same `posture`, same checks order (note: timestamps will differ; the harness strips known-variable fields)
- `ee export --json` — same `manifestHash`, same `recordsHash`

### Field-stripping for time-varying outputs

Some fields legitimately change between runs (`generatedAt`, `last_accessed`, `audit_ts`). The harness normalizes:

```jsonc
"_strip_fields": [
  "generatedAt", "last_accessed", "audit_ts",
  "elapsedMs", "ts", "started_at", "ended_at",
  "ee_binary_hash"
]
```

After stripping, the remaining output is byte-comparable.

### Tie-breaking checks

A specific failure case: two memories with identical scores must produce a deterministic order. The harness:
1. Seeds a known tie (two memories with same content but different IDs)
2. Runs search 3×
3. Asserts the order is identical across runs
4. Asserts the order is documented (the lower ULID wins — verify both in code and in test)

## Design considerations

- **Run across process boundaries.** Don't just call the same function in-process; spawn `ee` as a child process each time. Catches state leaks and time-based fields you forgot to strip.
- **Compare structurally first, then byte-wise.** If a structural diff exists, surface it; only fall back to byte comparison for the final assertion.
- **Run on macOS and Linux.** Path normalization, locale, etc. — determinism must survive both.

## Depends on

- J1 (logging)
- J2 (corpus)
- A1 (canonical pack structure must exist before we can hash it)

## Blocks

- nothing internal

## Acceptance gate

- `scripts/e2e_overhaul/determinism.sh` runs each test 3× per surface, all hashes match within a surface
- `tests/determinism_unit.rs` asserts in-process determinism for tie-breaking
notes:

2. tests/determinism_unit.rs — in-process tie-breaking test exercising the deterministic memory-id secondary sort on equal-score search hits.
3. Register the script with scripts/e2e_overhaul.sh Epic registry.

title: J8: Agent-consumer reference script (Python ≤50 lines) as contract test for pack consumability
description:
# J8 — Agent-consumer reference script (contract test)

## Why

The whole point of the overhaul is that an LLM agent should consume `ee pack` output easily. We should have a concrete reference script that an LLM agent could plausibly run, producing a ready-to-use prompt fragment. If that script breaks, the agent UX is broken — by definition.

## Acceptance

### Script — `scripts/agent_consume_pack.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Reference agent consumer for `ee pack` output.

Reads `ee context --json` output from stdin (or runs `ee context "<query>" --workspace WS --json`)
and emits the markdown body suitable for prepending to an LLM prompt.

Length target: ≤ 50 lines of meaningful Python.
"""
import json, sys, argparse, subprocess

def consume(pack_response: dict) -> str:
    if not pack_response.get("success"):
        return f"<!-- ee error: {pack_response['error']['code']} -->"
    pack = pack_response["data"]["pack"]
    
    # If pack.text exists (post-A4), use it directly
    if "text" in pack:
        return pack["text"]
    
    # Fallback: render minimally from items[]
    lines = [f"# Context Pack: {pack.get('query', '')}\n"]
    lines.append(f"**Budget:** {pack['budget']['usedTokens']}/{pack['budget']['maxTokens']} tokens\n")
    for item in pack["items"]:
        lines.append(f"\n## {item.get('section','memory')} {item['rank']}. {item['memoryId']}\n")
        lines.append(f"```\n{item['content']}\n```\n")
        lines.append(f"**Why:** {item.get('why','')}\n")
    return "".join(lines)

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--from-stdin", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--workspace", help="if not from stdin, run ee context against this workspace")
    parser.add_argument("--query")
    parser.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=1000)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    
    if args.from_stdin:
        pack_response = json.load(sys.stdin)
    else:
        out = subprocess.check_output([
            "ee", "context", args.query, "--workspace", args.workspace,
            "--max-tokens", str(args.max_tokens), "--json"
        ])
        pack_response = json.loads(out)
    
    print(consume(pack_response))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

### Contract test — `scripts/e2e_overhaul/agent_consumer.sh`

```bash
WS=$(mktemp -d)
$EE init --workspace $WS --json > /dev/null
corpus_2026_05_10_seed.sh $WS

# Pipe pack JSON to the agent consumer
$EE context "prepare release" --workspace $WS --json | scripts/agent_consume_pack.py --from-stdin > /tmp/prompt_fragment.md

# Assertions
e2e_log_assert_command_succeeded scripts/agent_consume_pack.py
e2e_log_assert_file_nonempty /tmp/prompt_fragment.md
e2e_log_assert_file_contains /tmp/prompt_fragment.md "# Context Pack:"
e2e_log_assert_file_max_bytes /tmp/prompt_fragment.md 8000
e2e_log_assert_no_pattern /tmp/prompt_fragment.md '\\.'   # no escape leakage after H1
```

### Why ≤ 50 lines

If consuming ee output requires more than 50 lines of code, the schema is too complex. The line cap is the discipline: the schema serves the consumer, not the other way around.

## Design considerations

- **Pure stdlib.** No `jq`, no `pydantic`. The script must run in any Python 3.8+ environment without `pip install`.
- **Forward-compat:** unknown fields are ignored. The consumer is permissive about new fields, strict about expected fields.
- **Agent-faithful:** writes to stdout exactly what an agent would prepend to its prompt. No "tool call result" wrapping; no metadata noise.

## Depends on

- A1 (canonical pack structure)
- A4 (pack.text field — script preferred path)
- H1 (clean markdown — script asserts no escape leakage)

## Blocks

- nothing internal — but every agent harness consuming ee should use this as the reference

## Acceptance gate

- `scripts/agent_consume_pack.py` ≤ 50 SLoC
- `scripts/e2e_overhaul/agent_consumer.sh` runs against post-overhaul `target/release/ee`, all assertions pass
- Reference repo `eidetic_engine_cli/docs/agent_integration.md` (K-epic) embeds this script as the canonical example

## Why

J5 measures pack JSON size. Other latency/scale concerns went unmeasured:

- Search latency at 1K / 10K / 100K memories
- Index rebuild time
- Workspace init time (target < 100ms)
- Audit log query at 1M rows (G1's learn summary)

- Concurrent writes throughput (L1's 10-writer scenario)

### Benchmark suite — `benches/perf_*.rs` + `benches/baselines/`

- Env vars like `EE_CASS_BINARY` remain undocumented except in source

title: K1: AGENTS.md add 'Agent UX patterns' section reflecting overhaul contract
description:
# K1 — AGENTS.md "Agent UX patterns" section

## Why

AGENTS.md is the first file an agent reads in this repo. The overhaul changes how agents should interact with ee; AGENTS.md must reflect that.

## Acceptance

Add a new top-level section to AGENTS.md after "Product Principles":

```markdown
## Agent UX Patterns (post-2026-05 overhaul)

### How agents consume ee

The canonical agent workflow is:

1. `ee init --workspace . --json`
2. `ee remember "<text>" --workspace . --level X --kind Y --json`
3. `ee search "<query>" --workspace . --json`
4. `ee context "<task>" --workspace . --max-tokens N --json` → use `pack.text` as the prompt fragment
5. `ee why <id> --json` for provenance audits

Output contract:
- Every response wraps in `{"schema": "...", "success": bool, "data": {...}}` or `{"schema": "ee.error.v1", "error": {...}}`
- Memory body text is always under `content`. List views may set `content_truncated: true`.
- Errors include `details.recovery[]` — structured recovery actions, not prose-only.
- `degraded[]` is empty on a clean response. Non-empty means the response was *actually affected*.
- `posture: ok | degraded_recoverable | blocked` replaces `healthy: bool`.

### Failure-mode catalog

See `docs/degraded_codes.md` for every code, when it fires, how to recover.

### Schema versions

- Request envelopes: `ee.<command>.request.v1`
- Response envelopes: `ee.response.v2` (post-overhaul), `ee.error.v1`
- Pack: `ee.pack.v2` (post-overhaul)
- Migration: see `docs/migration_v0.1_to_v0.2.md`

### Env var registry

See `docs/env_vars.md` for every `EE_*` honored.
```

## Depends on

- K2, K3, K4 (cross-links to schemas/codes/env_vars)

## Blocks

- nothing internal
notes:
PLAN-SPACE REVISION (2026-05-13 CopperHarbor — testable docs gate + e2e + logging):

The original bead lists the AGENTS.md content but treats it as a docs-only edit. A "docs bead" still has acceptance tests — that the docs are present, contain the contracted sections, and stay in sync with the surfaces they describe. K1 specifically anchors the overhaul; if AGENTS.md drifts from the actual response shape, every agent reading it gets misled.

## Test surface (named files)

### Unit tests
- tests/agents_md_section_presence_unit.rs — opens AGENTS.md, asserts the "Agent UX Patterns" heading exists at H2 level, contains all 5 numbered workflow steps, contains the schema-envelope contract bullet, contains the failure-mode-catalog cross-link to docs/degraded_codes.md, and the schema-versions block. Catches "section removed by accident" regressions.
- tests/agents_md_cross_link_validity_unit.rs — walks every relative link in the "Agent UX Patterns" section, asserts each target exists on disk (docs/degraded_codes.md, docs/migration_v0.1_to_v0.2.md, docs/env_vars.md, docs/schemas/*.json files). Catches stale cross-references after a K2/K3/K4 rename or move.
- tests/agents_md_response_shape_sync_unit.rs — pulls the "Memory body text is always under `content`" claim from AGENTS.md and cross-checks it against the actual response shape produced by ee context --json on a canonical fixture. Fails if AGENTS.md says one thing and the code does another. This is the anti-drift gate the bead really needs.

### Golden fixtures
- tests/fixtures/golden/agents_md/required_sections.json — JSON list of (heading_level, heading_text, required_bullets[]) the section MUST contain. Editing AGENTS.md to add NEW bullets is fine (additive); removing or renaming REQUIRED ones fails the test, forcing a deliberate goldens update.
- tests/snapshots/agents_md_agent_ux_patterns.snap (insta) — the rendered "Agent UX Patterns" section. Reviewer sees the prose diff in PR.

### E2E
- scripts/e2e_overhaul/discoverability.sh (already exists per J3) — EXTEND with an epic_K1_agents_md_contract block that:
  1. greps AGENTS.md for the H2 "Agent UX Patterns" heading; asserts present.
  2. invokes ee init + ee remember + ee context against a fresh tmp workspace.
  3. Reads the resulting --json output; asserts every claim in the K1 section is observable in the response (success field, schema field, data.pack.text presence when pack.text is documented, content vs content_preview, content_truncated, degraded array, posture string).
  4. Emits J1 events { kind: 'docs_contract_check', section, claim_id, observed, status } per claim — so the test surfaces WHICH claim drifted, not just a generic fail.

## Logging requirements

The discoverability.sh e2e block emits one J1 event per validated claim in the K1 section. No audit_log writes (docs verification is read-side; no state change).

## Composition with K2/K3/K4

K1 cross-links docs/schemas/, docs/degraded_codes.md, docs/env_vars.md. K2 (closed via this revision pass — bd-17c65.11.2), K3, K4 must each land their respective doc files BEFORE K1's cross-link validity test can pass. Adding K1 → K2/K3/K4 hard deps is correct (mirror the cross-links).

## Acceptance gate (FINAL)

- AGENTS.md gains the "Agent UX Patterns" H2 section verbatim from the bead body.
- 3 named unit tests pass.
- 1 golden fixture + 1 insta snapshot committed and accepted.
- discoverability.sh epic_K1_agents_md_contract block passes; J1 events emitted per claim.
- The response-shape-sync test is the linchpin: it MUST fail when ee context output diverges from the documented contract, AND MUST pass on a clean run.

title: K2: Per-envelope JSON Schema files in docs/schemas/ + CI gate validating emitted responses
description:
# K2 — Per-envelope JSON Schema files

## Why

A machine-readable schema makes:
- Test verification trivial (`jsonschema --validate`)
- Agent harness codegen possible (typed clients)
- Drift detection mechanical (CI compares emitted vs schema)

## Acceptance

For every response envelope, a JSON Schema file under `docs/schemas/`:

```
docs/schemas/
  ee.response.v2.json              # general response wrapper
  ee.error.v1.json                 # general error wrapper
  ee.pack.v2.json                  # context pack
  ee.search.v1.json                # search response
  ee.memory.show.v1.json           # memory show
  ee.memory.list.v1.json           # memory list (paged)
  ee.status.v1.json                # ee status
  ee.doctor.v1.json                # ee doctor
  ee.capabilities.v1.json          # ee capabilities
  ee.import.cass.v1.json           # cass import
  ee.export.v1.json                # export
  ee.curate.candidates.v1.json     # curate candidates
  ee.graph.<algorithm>.v1.json     # graph results
  …
```

Each schema declares:
- `$schema`: JSON Schema draft 2020-12
- `$id`: stable URL (e.g. `https://eidetic-engine/schemas/ee.pack.v2.json`)
- All required and optional fields with types and descriptions
- Enums for `degraded[].code`, `posture`, `source`, `recovery[].kind`
- `additionalProperties: false` for strict shapes

### CI gate — `tests/docs_schemas_match_responses.rs`

```rust
#[test]
fn schemas_match_responses() {
    for (command, schema_path) in CANONICAL_SCHEMAS {
        let response = run_command_against_fixture(command);
        let schema: Value = read_json(schema_path);
        validate(&response, &schema).expect_or_fail();
    }
}
```

## Design considerations

- **Keep schemas concise but complete.** Don't ship a 10KB schema for a 1KB response.
- **Versioning policy:** breaking change → bump version, keep old schema for 1 milestone. Per AGENTS.md "no backwards compatibility" we delete old schemas after migration, but during transition both coexist.
- **Don't auto-generate from Rust.** Hand-curate so the schemas are agent-readable docs in their own right. (`schemars`-generated files are noisy; we want clean reference.)

## Depends on

- D4 (canonical field map informs schema)

## Blocks

- K1 (cross-link target)

title: K3: docs/degraded_codes.md catalog auto-generated from J6 fixtures + CI coverage gate
description:
# K3 — docs/degraded_codes.md catalog (auto-generated from J6 fixtures)

## Why

Every `degraded[]` code that fires anywhere in ee needs a human-readable explanation. Currently codes appear in source and tests without a central reference.

## Acceptance

`docs/degraded_codes.md`, one section per code:

```markdown
## `no_relevant_results`

**Severity:** medium
**Category:** workspace_state
**Affects:** search, context

**When emitted:** the search engine returned candidates but none scored above `relevanceFloor`.

**Surface:** the response has `results: []` and `degraded[]` contains:
\`\`\`json
{
  "code": "no_relevant_results",
  "severity": "medium",
  "message": "No memories scored above relevance floor (0.05) for query '<q>'.",
  "repair": "broaden query, lower --relevance-floor, or use --source-mode lexical_only",
  "recovery": [
    {"kind": "broaden_query", "hint": "..."},
    {"kind": "flag", "name": "--relevance-floor", "valueHint": "0.01"},
    {"kind": "flag", "name": "--source-mode", "valueHint": "lexical_only"}
  ]
}
\`\`\`

**Repair commands:**
- Rephrase with concrete words present in stored memories
- Lower the floor: `ee search "<q>" --relevance-floor 0.01`
- Force lexical: `ee search "<q>" --source-mode lexical_only`

**Related codes:** `weak_query_recall` (similar but with results), `empty_workspace` (no memories at all)

**Fixture:** `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/no_relevant_results.json`
```

### Auto-generation

`scripts/build_degraded_codes_doc.sh` reads `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/*.json` and `src/models/degraded.rs` (the canonical enum), produces `docs/degraded_codes.md`. CI fails if the file is stale relative to source.

### CI gate — `tests/degraded_codes_doc_coverage.rs`

For every enum variant in `DegradedCode`:
- Asserts a fixture exists in `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/`
- Asserts the doc file contains a section heading with the code name

## Depends on

- J6 (fixtures are the data source)

## Blocks

- K1 (cross-link)
notes:
PLAN-SPACE REVISION (2026-05-12 TealHarbor — round 2 — staleness gate + generator semantics):

## Auto-generator semantics (canonical)

Script: `scripts/build_degraded_codes_doc.sh` (new)

Algorithm:
1. Walk every `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/*.json` (composes with J6 catalog).
2. For each fixture, extract: code, severity, surfaces[], introduced_by.bead, message_contains[], repair_contains.
3. Render `docs/degraded_codes.md` from a template:
   ```markdown
   # Degraded codes catalog (auto-generated; do not hand-edit)

   Source of truth: `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/*.json`.
   Regenerate: `./scripts/build_degraded_codes_doc.sh`.
   Generator pinned to: `ee.failure_mode_fixture.v1`.

   ## By severity

   ### critical
   - `<code>` (surfaces: search) — message: "..." — repair: "..." — bead: bd-...

   ### high
   ...

   ### medium
   ...

   ## By surface

   ### search
   ...

   ## Index
   - `<code>` → [Section](#bysurface_search)
   ```
4. Write `docs/degraded_codes.md` deterministically (BTreeMap-sorted code listings).

## CI staleness gate

`tests/degraded_codes_doc_freshness.rs` (new):

```rust
#[test]
fn degraded_codes_doc_matches_fixtures() -> TestResult {
    let regenerated = run("scripts/build_degraded_codes_doc.sh", &["--stdout"])?;
    let committed = fs::read_to_string("docs/degraded_codes.md")?;
    if regenerated != committed {
        return Err(format!(
            "docs/degraded_codes.md is stale relative to tests/fixtures/failure_modes/. \
             Run `./scripts/build_degraded_codes_doc.sh` and commit the result.\n\n--- diff ---\n{}",
            diff_strings(&committed, &regenerated)
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

CI runs this test EVERY commit. Staleness → red CI.

## Coverage subtest

A subtest in the same file asserts:
- Every degraded code grep-matched in src/ has a corresponding fixture AND a doc entry.
- No orphan doc entries (every doc entry has a backing fixture).
- No orphan fixtures (every fixture has a backing code in src/) — composes with J6 cross-reference grep.

## Generator idempotency

Running `./scripts/build_degraded_codes_doc.sh` twice produces byte-identical output (the BTreeMap sort + the fixture file mtime exclusion guarantee this).

## E2E (`scripts/e2e_overhaul/discoverability.sh` K3 block)

- Modify a fixture (e.g., change a severity).
- Re-run `./scripts/build_degraded_codes_doc.sh`.
- Verify the diff shows up cleanly.

title: K4: docs/env_vars.md registry + EnvVar enum + lint preventing raw std::env::var('EE_*') outside registry
description:
# K4 — docs/env_vars.md registry

## Why

Today `EE_CASS_BINARY` is the only way to point cass discovery at a non-trusted path. The error message says "set [cass.binary] in config" but doesn't mention the env var. Source code (src/cass/client.rs:108) is the only documentation. This pattern surely repeats: there are likely other `EE_*` env vars only documented in source.

## Acceptance

`docs/env_vars.md`:

```markdown
# `EE_*` environment variables

| Name | Type | Controls | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `EE_CASS_BINARY` | absolute path | cass import binary | — | Required for cass import unless cass is in `/usr/local/bin`, `/usr/bin`, or `/opt/homebrew/bin`. Path is validated for ownership and permissions. |
| `EE_PROFILE` | enum | operating profile | `balanced` | Allowed: `lean`, `balanced`, `extended`. Affects budget caps. |
| `EE_LOG` | tracing-subscriber filter | log filter | — | Standard `RUST_LOG`-style. Honored alongside `RUST_LOG`; `EE_LOG` wins on conflict. |
| `EE_NO_AUTO_LINK` | bool (1/0) | suppress auto-link on remember | `0` | When `1`, equivalent to `ee remember … --no-auto-link`. |
…
```

### CI gate — `tests/env_vars_doc_coverage.rs`

```rust
#[test]
fn env_vars_documented() {
    let env_vars_in_code = grep_env_vars("src/");  // matches std::env::var("EE_*"), env::var_os("EE_*")
    let env_vars_in_doc = parse_env_vars_doc("docs/env_vars.md");
    
    assert_eq!(env_vars_in_code, env_vars_in_doc, "drift detected: code has {:?}, docs have {:?}", …);
}
```

### Companion: `src/config/env_registry.rs`

Single source of truth in code. Every `EE_*` lookup goes through this registry:

```rust
pub fn get_env_var(var: EnvVar) -> Option<String> { … }

pub enum EnvVar {
    CassBinary,
    Profile,
    Log,
    NoAutoLink,
    …
}
```

Linter (clippy custom or grep-based) fails CI if `std::env::var("EE_*")` appears outside this registry.

## Depends on

- F4 (capabilities surface includes env overrides — same registry)

## Blocks

- K1 (cross-link)

title: K5: docs/migration_v0.1_to_v0.2.md guide + test asserting no v1 field names remain in src/

# K5 — Migration guide v0.1 → v0.2

## Why

Schema bumps (`ee.pack.v1` → `v2`, `ee.response.v1` → `v2`) and behavior changes (`healthy: bool` → `posture`, `content_preview` → `content`) need a human-readable migration. Per AGENTS.md no backwards compat, but agents written against v0.1 need to know what to update.

## Acceptance

`docs/migration_v0.1_to_v0.2.md`:

```markdown
# Migrating from ee v0.1 to v0.2

## Schema versions

- Response envelope: `ee.response.v1` → `ee.response.v2`
- Pack: `ee.pack.v1` → `ee.pack.v2`
- All others unchanged

## Breaking changes by surface

### `ee remember`, `ee memory show`, `ee memory list`
- `content_preview` field removed from list view; use `content` + `content_truncated` instead.
- `ee why <id>` now includes `memory.content` inline (was: required separate `memory show` call).

### `ee context`
- Top-level `selectionCertificate`, `provenanceFooter`, `omitted` removed.
- All selected items now live under `pack.items[]` with merged fields.
- Skipped candidates under `pack.skipped[]`.
- Algorithm self-description at `pack.meta.algorithm`.
- New: `pack.text` is the rendered markdown body, ready to prepend.
- Per-item `why` is now a 1-line reason. The math identity moves to `pack.meta.algorithm.scoringFormula`.

### `ee doctor`, `ee status`
- `healthy: bool` → `posture: "ok" | "degraded_recoverable" | "blocked"`.
- Severity rules changed (warning → info for transient/expected states).

### `ee search`
- New: relevance floor. Results below floor excluded; `degraded[].no_relevant_results` may appear.
- `source` field now includes `hybrid` and may show actual lexical_only/semantic_only when applicable.

### Error envelope
- `error.details.recovery[]` added — structured recovery actions. `error.repair` (prose) remains.

### Policy
- Secret detector rebuilt: substring keyword match → value-shape detection. Memories *mentioning* "secret"/"token"/"credentials" in plain English no longer rejected.
- Tag validator: dots, underscores, Unicode now allowed.

## Migration recipes

### Updating an agent harness

\`\`\`python
# OLD (v0.1):
content = response["data"]["memories"][0]["content_preview"]
healthy = response["data"]["healthy"]

# NEW (v0.2):
mem = response["data"]["memories"][0]
content = mem["content"]
if mem.get("content_truncated"):
    # fetch full via ee memory show
    full = subprocess.check_output(["ee", "memory", "show", mem["id"], "--json"])
posture = response["data"]["posture"]
\`\`\`

…etc per surface…

## Env vars

`EE_CASS_BINARY` was already honored in v0.1 but undocumented. Now in `docs/env_vars.md`.
```

### Companion test

`tests/migration_no_v1_references.rs`:

```rust
#[test]
fn no_lingering_v1_references() {
    // Grep src/ for any string literal matching old field names that should be deleted.
    let forbidden = ["content_preview" /* if D1 fully migrated */, "healthy_bool_field", "selectionCertificate"];
    for term in forbidden {
        let hits = grep("src/", term);
        assert!(hits.is_empty(), "v1 leftover: {} appears at {:?}", term, hits);
    }
}
```

## Depends on

- D1 (canonical content field)
- E1 (posture)
- A1, A2, A5 (pack structure changes)
- B1 (relevance floor)
- C1, C3 (policy changes)
- F1 (recovery struct)

## Blocks

- nothing internal — this lands at milestone close
design:
# Design refinement — relationship to L0 (workspace migration implementation)

K5 is the WRITTEN migration guide; L0 is the IMPLEMENTED runner.

```
K5 (this bead)              L0 (implementation)
=================           ====================
docs/migration_v0.1_to_v0.2.md   src/migrate/v0_2_*.rs
                                  ee migrate run --to v0.2
                                  --auto-migrate flag
                                  exit code 8 on first-touch
```

Closure order:
1. L0 lands first (the migration steps exist as Rust code)
2. K5 documents what L0 actually does, with per-step explanation drawn from `migrations/v0_2_*.rs` doc comments

If L0 changes scope mid-implementation, K5 description is updated to match. K5 is NOT prescriptive over L0; it's descriptive.

## Migration test (extends K5's `tests/migration_no_v1_references.rs`)

`tests/migration_runtime.rs` — end-to-end:
1. Build a v0.1 fixture DB (committed as `tests/fixtures/v0_1_workspace.tar.gz`)
2. Open it with v0.2 binary, expect exit code 8
3. Run `ee migrate run --workspace . --to v0.2`
4. Verify all v0.2 invariants
5. Verify no v0.1 field names remain in responses

This test is the gate that v0.1 workspaces are correctly handled — without it, the migration guide is hopeful but unverified.

## Companion: rollback path (deferred)

L0 specifies migration forward only. Rollback (v0.2 → v0.1) is a separate concern, deferred to a future bead if/when needed. K5 mentions this explicitly: "v0.1 → v0.2 is a one-way migration; backup before upgrading."

## What K5 ADDS over L0's per-step docs

- **Agent-harness migration recipes** (Python/JS snippets) — L0's doc comments are Rust-internal; K5 shows external consumers what to update
- **Recovery commands** for users who hit unexpected migration failures
- **`--auto-migrate` UX** — when to use, when not to (CI may want explicit migration step)

title: K6: --redaction <level> documented + tested across export/handoff/context (none/minimal/standard/strict/paranoid)
description:
# K6 — `--redaction <level>` documented + tested across surfaces

## Why

`ee export` has `--redaction <level>` per `--help`. Levels visible in walkthrough: "standard". Other levels? `--redaction strict`? `--redaction none`? Currently undocumented from user-facing perspective.

Multiple surfaces produce content that may need redaction:
- `ee export` (records that could be sensitive)
- `ee handoff create` (capsule that travels between agents)
- `ee context` (pack JSON returned to caller)

Without explicit docs + tests, behavior is opaque and inconsistent.

## Acceptance

### Levels enumeration

`enum RedactionLevel { None, Minimal, Standard, Strict, Paranoid }`:

| Level | What's redacted |
|---|---|
| `none` | nothing — content passed through as-is |
| `minimal` | only obvious secret-value patterns (sk-…, JWT, AWS keys) |
| `standard` | minimal + tagged-as-redacted fields + high-entropy tokens > 32 chars |
| `strict` | standard + content matching workspace PII patterns |
| `paranoid` | strict + truncate content to first 200 chars + hash digests for identifiers |

### Per-surface defaults

- `ee context` default: `minimal`
- `ee handoff create` default: `standard`
- `ee export` default: `standard`
- `--redaction <level>` flag overrides per call

### Per-workspace policy in `.ee/config.toml`:
```toml
[policy.redaction]
default_level = "standard"
strict_pii_patterns = ["SSN-\\d{3}-\\d{2}-\\d{4}"]
```

### Honest fields in response
```jsonc
"redaction": {
  "level_applied": "standard",
  "level_source": "default",
  "fields_redacted": ["items[0].content"],
  "patterns_matched": ["openai_sk_prefix"]
}
```

## Test plan

- **Unit:** `tests/redaction_levels_unit.rs` — fixture content × level → expected redaction
- **E2E:** `scripts/e2e_overhaul/redaction.sh` (NEW under J3) exercises each level across surfaces
- **Logging:** `redaction_apply: {surface, level, level_source, fields_redacted_count, patterns_matched}` event
- **Failure-mode fixture (J6):** `redaction_paranoid_truncation.json`, `redaction_strict_pii.json`

## Depends on

- C1 (secret value detector)
- B10 (output-time redaction)
- K2 (schema for redaction block)
- K4 (env var docs cover EE_REDACTION_LEVEL if added)
notes:
PLAN-SPACE REVISION (2026-05-12 TealHarbor — paranoid level + symmetric round-trip):

## Redaction level matrix (exact behavior per level)

| Level     | Secrets (api_key, jwt, password, etc.) | High-entropy tokens | Memory content body                  | Tags                  | Audit details |
|-----------|----------------------------------------|---------------------|--------------------------------------|-----------------------|---------------|
| none      | passthrough                            | passthrough         | passthrough                          | passthrough           | passthrough   |
| minimal   | redacted with `[REDACTED:<class>]`     | passthrough         | passthrough                          | passthrough           | hash only     |
| standard  | redacted                               | redacted if entropy ≥ 4.0 bits/byte | passthrough             | passthrough           | hash only     |
| strict    | redacted                               | redacted if entropy ≥ 3.5           | truncated to 200 chars + hash | passthrough     | hash only     |
| paranoid  | redacted                               | redacted always     | replaced with content_hash + `[REDACTED]` | hashed             | omitted       |

Default per surface (configurable per workspace):
- `ee export`: default standard (round-trip safe).
- `ee handoff create`: default strict (handoff is bound for another agent).
- `ee context --json`: default minimal (agent-facing, minimal interference).
- `ee support bundle`: default paranoid (third-party-facing, max safety).

## Symmetric round-trip property

`ee export --redaction standard --output-dir <a>` then `ee import jsonl --source <a>` produces a workspace where:
- Non-redacted fields are byte-identical to original.
- Redacted fields are stored with `redaction_markers[]` so a future un-redaction step (with the user's key) could restore them (out of scope for v0.2; just preserve the markers).
- Audit chain shows redaction_apply rows.

Test: `tests/redaction_round_trip_unit.rs` (new) seeds a workspace, exports at each level, re-imports, asserts consistency.

## Unit tests

For each (level, surface) combination — 5 levels × 4 surfaces = 20 cases:

1. Seed a memory carrying one fixture pattern from `tests/fixtures/secrets/pre_redaction.jsonl` (composes with B10).
2. Invoke the surface with `--redaction <level>`.
3. Assert exact output per the matrix above.
4. Assert `data.redaction_manifest.fieldsRedactedCount` matches the count of redactions applied.

20 unit cases minimum.

## E2E (`scripts/e2e_overhaul/policy_detectors.sh` K6 block)

- For each level: run `ee export --redaction <level> --output-dir <dir>`. Inspect contents; assert per-level expectations.
- Verify `ee export --redaction paranoid` followed by `ee import jsonl --source <dir>` produces a workspace with ALL redacted markers preserved AND no plaintext secrets reconstructible.
- Verify the audit chain shows redaction_apply rows for every redaction.

## Failure-mode fixtures (J6)

- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/redaction_pattern_matched.json` (per pattern class).
- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/redaction_level_invalid.json` (rejected with accepted values).
- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/redaction_round_trip_marker_preserved.json` (info severity).

## Logging event

```json
{
  "schema": "ee.test_event.v1",
  "kind": "redaction_apply",
  "level": "none|minimal|standard|strict|paranoid",
  "surface": "export|handoff|context|support_bundle",
  "memory_id": "<id|null>",
  "fields_redacted_count": <usize>,
  "patterns_matched": ["api_key", "stripe_secret", ...],
  "tokens_truncated": <usize>,
  "content_hash_original": "<blake3>",
  "audit_row_id": "<id>"
}
```

## Acceptance gate

- 20 (level × surface) unit cases pass.
- Round-trip symmetry verified for all 5 levels.
- Paranoid + import-from-paranoid produces no plaintext secrets in the resulting workspace.
- All J6 fixtures land.
- Audit chain row written per redaction.

title: K6 follow-up: source-aware redaction response metadata block
description:
Background: K6 now documents and wires the canonical five redaction levels across export, handoff create, context JSON, support bundle, and workspace redaction.defaults. - Update docs/redaction_levels.md once implemented to move the Response metadata status section from remaining acceptance work to live behavior.

Tests required:
- Unit/parser coverage for CLI flag vs workspace config vs built-in default source precedence.
- Contract or integration coverage asserting the redaction block appears on all four surfaces.
- Doc-consistency coverage proving docs/redaction_levels.md and tests agree on the live response fields.
- RCH-only Cargo verification for relevant focused tests. If RCH is environment-blocked, record command hash and degraded evidence; do not run local Cargo.

title: Cross-cutting integrity: workspace schema migration, concurrency, backup round-trip, trust decay
description:
# EPIC L — Cross-cutting integrity (migration, concurrency, persistence, lifecycle)

## Why this epic exists

Some overhaul-relevant work doesn't fit neatly under any single A-K epic because it cuts across them:

- **Workspace DB schema migration** (L0): The overhaul bumps schemas. Existing v0.1 workspaces need an upgrade path. K5 documents the migration; L0 implements it. The implementing work touches every changed surface but isn't owned by any one of them.
- **Concurrent write contention** (L1): Real multi-agent scenarios produce races. Storage-layer concern, but affects every write surface. Tests cross multiple epics.
- **Backup → import round-trip** (L2): Validates that export+import is byte-equivalent. Spans D (canonical fields), C (redaction), B (search index rebuild).
- **Trust decay / forgetting** (L3): AGENTS.md product principle that has no current implementing surface. Spans G (learn), B (search exclusion), E (posture for decay job).

These aren't add-ons; they're integrity guarantees that make the rest of the overhaul honest end-to-end.

## Tasks

- L0: Workspace DB schema migration v0.1 → v0.2 (implements what K5 documents)
- L1: Concurrent write contention test + write-spool back-pressure surface
- L2: Backup → export → import round-trip determinism test
- L3: Trust decay / forgetting as a deterministic maintenance pathway

## Dependencies (cross-epic)

- L0 depends on D1, E1, K5
- L1 depends on E1, F1, J6
- L2 depends on D1, J1, J2
- L3 depends on G1, B8, E1

## Acceptance gate (epic-level)

- L0: `scripts/e2e_overhaul/migration.sh` migrates v0.1 fixture DB → v0.2 schema; all invariants hold
- L1: `scripts/e2e_overhaul/concurrency.sh` 10 concurrent writers all succeed or surface `write_queue_full`
- L2: `scripts/e2e_overhaul/backup_roundtrip.sh` import-after-export workspace state hash equals original
- L3: `scripts/e2e_overhaul/decay.sh` synthesized-old memories demote/tombstone deterministically; ee remember resets last_accessed_at
notes:
ROUND-5 EPIC ACCEPTANCE ROLL-UP (2026-05-12 TealHarbor):

Epic closes when ee survives the things that distinguish toy projects from production substrates: schema migrations don't lose data, concurrent writes don't lose data, backups round-trip byte-identically, and trust decays deterministically.

Children: L0 (ee migrate top-level surface — CLOSED), L1 (concurrent write contention — OPEN, P2), L2 (backup round-trip — referenced; bd-2r19w open), L3 (trust decay — OPEN, P2), L4 (index rebuild in migration — OPEN, P2), L5 (workspace lock + cooperative writes — TBD), L6 (audit-chain tamper detection — TBD).

Closure gate: 64-agent concurrent write test passes (composes with S7 swarm scale); backup records.jsonl byte-deterministic (bd-2r19w closes); migrate is idempotent (running twice produces same result); trust decay reversible via maintenance job replay.

Hidden complexity (now surfaced):
- Audit-table writes bumping DB generation (bd-xzuma root cause) — fix lands as part of L1 or as a separate sub-bead.
- WAL vacuum semantics for lab snapshots (N15.3 reference).

User-visible payoff: ee is safe to use as the durable substrate even in a 64-agent swarm with frequent migrations and backup-restore cycles.

title: L0: Workspace DB schema migration v0.1 → v0.2 implementation (ee migrate run; --auto-migrate; exit code 8)
description:
# L0 — Workspace DB schema migration v0.1 → v0.2

## Why

K5 documents the v0.1 → v0.2 migration. But the documentation describes WHAT changes; no bead implements HOW existing workspaces upgrade. A user with a v0.1 workspace runs the new binary — what happens?

Per AGENTS.md exit codes: `8 | migration required`. So there's an existing migration mechanism. But the overhaul changes need:
- Schema bumps (response envelopes, pack format)
- Field renames (content_preview → content; healthy → posture)
- Database column changes if any (new content_hash column for B3?)

## Acceptance

### Migration runner — `ee migrate run --from v0.1 --to v0.2`

Existing surface (per --help `migrate` is implied by exit code 8). Runner:
1. Detect current schema version from `meta_kv.schema_version` row
2. Apply migration steps in order; each migration is idempotent and atomic
3. Update `meta_kv.schema_version` to new version
4. Verify post-migration invariants (e.g. all memories have content_hash if B3 added the column)

### Migration steps for this overhaul

`migrations/v0_2_<step>.rs`:

1. **`v0_2_001_add_content_hash`** — add `content_hash BLAKE3 GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...)` to memories. Backfill for existing rows.
2. **`v0_2_002_normalize_tag_unicode`** — apply NFC normalization to existing tag rows (C3 change).
3. **`v0_2_003_audit_log_index`** — add index on `audit_log(op, ts)` for `learn summary` performance at scale.
4. **`v0_2_004_meta_pack_versions`** — annotate existing persisted packs with `pack_schema_version: "v1"` so callers can identify them; new packs are `v2`.

Each migration:
- Idempotent (running twice is a no-op)
- Atomic (transaction-wrapped or unambiguous rollback)
- Logged in `migrations_log` table

### Detection on first run

```bash
$ ee context "test" --workspace .
error: migration required

Workspace was last opened by ee v0.1.5; current binary is v0.2.0.

Next:
  ee migrate run --workspace . --to v0.2

Details:
  ee migrate status --workspace . --json
```

Exit code 8.

### `--auto-migrate` opt-in

```bash
ee --auto-migrate context "test" --workspace .  # migrate transparently if needed
```

Off by default. For agent harnesses that want to handle the migration themselves first.

## Design considerations

- **Backwards compat in DB is REAL.** Per AGENTS.md "no backwards compat" applies to APIs, but a v0.1 DB on disk must continue to be openable for ONE migration step at minimum.
- **No silent data loss.** Migration steps that drop columns require explicit confirmation OR a backup is taken first.
- **Migration audit:** every step logs to `audit_log` so an operator can verify what happened.

## Test plan

- **Unit:** `tests/migration_v0_2_unit.rs` — each migration step on a fixture DB
- **E2E:** `scripts/e2e_overhaul/migration.sh` (NEW per-epic script under J3):
  - Seed v0.1 fixture DB
  - Run `ee migrate run`
  - Verify v0.2 invariants hold
  - Test `--auto-migrate` flow
  - Test exit code 8 on first run without migration
- **Logging:** `migration_step: {step_id, applied, elapsed_ms, rows_touched}` event
- **Determinism (J7):** same v0.1 input → same v0.2 output across runs

## Depends on

- D1 (canonical content field — informs whether columns rename)
- E1 (posture — used in migrate status response)
- K5 (documentation of WHAT changes; this bead implements HOW)

## Blocks

- K5 (migration doc can finalize once paths are known)
close_reason:
L0 phase 1 implemented in commits bc7d73b + a2e1175. The existing schema-migration framework (DbConnection::migrate, needs_migration, schema_version, MIGRATIONS registry) is now exposed via a first-class `ee migrate` top-level command:

- `ee migrate status --json` — emits ee.response.v1 with schemaVersion, latestCompiledSchemaVersion, pendingCount, needsMigration, upToDate. Exit code 0 when up-to-date; 8 (MigrationRequired) when pending migrations exist. Storage error envelope when the workspace has no database file.

- `ee migrate run --json` — applies any unapplied migrations idempotently; emits applied[]+skipped[] version-number lists plus the post-migration schemaVersion. Idempotent across reruns.

- `ee migrate run --dry-run --json` — reports wouldApply[] without mutating. Verified by contract test (pre/post schemaVersion identical).

Tests live in tests/contracts/migrate_command_surface.rs — 4 end-to-end tests against the real binary covering up-to-date workspace, dry-run non-mutation, idempotent rerun, missing-database storage error envelope. All 4 pass.

Phase 1 scope per the bead's pragmatic split:

- ✓ Audit log entries (already wired via migration.step in the existing framework)
- ✓ Exit code 8 detection (ee migrate status returns it; other commands already return it via DomainError::MigrationRequired)
- ✓ Dry-run (--dry-run)

Out of scope (deferred to L0 phase 2 / future beads if needed):
- --auto-migrate flag for transparent inline migration during normal commands

title: L1: Concurrent write contention spec + write-queue-full structured error + crash recovery test
description:
# L1 — Concurrent write contention test + write-spool back-pressure

## Why

AGENTS.md non-goal: "No reliance on multi-process concurrent SQLite writers for correctness." So we don't promise full concurrent writes. But two AGENTS in two terminals doing `ee remember` against the same workspace IS a real scenario. What happens?

Hypotheses:
- The second writer blocks until the first finishes (BUSY_TIMEOUT)
- The second writer's `ee remember` returns an error
- The write spool absorbs both into a single batch
- Worst case: DB corruption (extremely unlikely with FrankenSQLite)

The 2026-05-10 walkthrough was single-process. We don't know the current behavior under contention.

Additionally, the write spool (`writeSpool` in `ee status` config) has `queueCap`, `batchCap`, `retryBudget`. What happens at queue capacity? Errors? Block? Drop?

## Acceptance

### Specification

Document and test:
1. **Two-writer happy path:** Two `ee remember` against the same workspace, each completes successfully with no data loss
2. **Heavy contention:** 10 concurrent writers; each succeeds OR returns a structured `degraded.write_queue_full` with a backoff hint
3. **Reader during writes:** `ee search` during heavy writes always succeeds (reads don't block on writes)
4. **Crash mid-write:** if one writer's process is killed mid-write, the DB remains consistent (no partial memory rows)

### Surface changes

When the write spool is at capacity:

```jsonc
{
  "error": {
    "code": "write_queue_full",
    "message": "Workspace write queue at capacity (512/512); retry recommended.",
    "severity": "low",
    "repair": "retry with exponential backoff",
    "details": {
      "queueCap": 512,
      "queueDepth": 512,
      "recovery": [
        {"priority": 1, "kind": "flag", "hint": "Retry with --backoff-ms 100"},
        {"priority": 2, "kind": "config", "key": "writeSpool.queueCap", "valueHint": "increase if memory permits"}
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Exit code: 3 (storage error) per AGENTS.md.

### Crash recovery

After a forced kill, `ee status` reports `posture.workspace.storage.status: "degraded_recoverable", reason: "uncommitted_write_replay_required"` until the next successful `ee remember` (or explicit `ee maintenance run --recover-writes`) flushes the in-flight buffer.

## Test plan

- **Unit:** `tests/concurrent_writes_unit.rs` — spawns 10 LabRuntime tasks; asserts all succeed or surface structured contention errors
- **E2E:** `scripts/e2e_overhaul/concurrency.sh` (NEW under J3):
  - Spawn 10 `ee remember` via xargs -P10 against same workspace

title: L2: Backup → export → import round-trip determinism test (workspace_state_hash invariant)
description:
# L2 — Backup → export → import round-trip determinism test

## Why

`ee export` and `ee backup` and `ee import jsonl` exist. They imply a round-trip contract: a workspace exported and then re-imported into a fresh workspace should be byte-equivalent in DB state. The 2026-05-10 walkthrough showed `ee export` works (101 records, blake3 hashes) but didn't verify the import side.

Round-trip is also the cleanest way to validate K5 migration: a v0.1 workspace, exported then imported into a v0.2 workspace, should produce known-equivalent state.

## Acceptance

### Specification

For a workspace W:
1. `ee export --workspace W --output-dir /tmp/exp` → produces `bk_<id>/manifest.json` + `records.jsonl`
2. `ee import jsonl --workspace W_new --from /tmp/exp/bk_<id>` → loads into fresh workspace
3. Round-trip invariant: `tests/lib/workspace_state_hash.sh W` produces the same hash as `tests/lib/workspace_state_hash.sh W_new`

### Workspace state hash

`tests/lib/workspace_state_hash.sh`:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Computes a deterministic hash of workspace state for round-trip testing.
# Skips volatile fields (timestamps, generated IDs at re-import time, audit IDs).
WS="$1"
$EE memory list --workspace $WS --json --fields full | jq -S '.data.memories | map(del(.id, .created_at, .updated_at, .audit_id) | .content_hash) | sort' | blake3sum
```

### Round-trip with redaction

`ee export --redaction standard` redacts marked fields. Round-trip preserves redaction: re-importing produces records with the same redacted fields.

## Test plan

- **Unit:** `tests/backup_import_roundtrip_unit.rs` — small fixture, in-process
- **E2E:** `scripts/e2e_overhaul/backup_roundtrip.sh` (NEW under J3):
  - Seed J2 reference corpus
  - Export to /tmp
  - Import into fresh workspace
  - Compare workspace state hashes
  - Repeat with `--redaction standard`
- **Determinism (J7):** export of same workspace produces byte-identical archive across runs
- **Logging:** `export_records_count`, `import_records_count`, `roundtrip_hash_match: true|false` events

## Depends on

- D1 (canonical content field — export uses canonical name)
- J1, J2

## Blocks

- nothing internal
close_reason:
L2 implemented in commit d409970. tests/contracts/backup_import_roundtrip.rs covers the workspace → backup → import round-trip determinism contract via an in-process API call (create_backup + import_jsonl_records) and asserts source/dest workspace_state_hash equality. The hash projects each memory to `level;kind;content;sorted_tags`, sorts the projection set, and BLAKE3-hashes the result — volatile fields (timestamps, row IDs, audit IDs, workspace_id) are stripped so the equivalence survives re-import allocating fresh IDs.

Two real findings surfaced during test development; documented as #[ignore]d sibling tests and each tracked as its own follow-up bead:

1. bd-n9w67: RedactionLevel::Standard truncates memory IDs to `mem_...XXXX` which the importer rejects (invalid_memory_id). Fix is either redactor (don't redact opaque ULIDs) or importer (accept + re-generate).

2. bd-2r19w: backup records.jsonl is non-deterministic across two identical exports. records_hash diverges between runs. Likely embedded timestamps / non-deterministic iteration / runtime audit IDs. Belongs under J7's strict byte-equivalence umbrella but the regression test is pre-shipped.

Side fix in src/pack/mod.rs: dropped `Eq` from #[derive] on PackOmission. A concurrent agent added UnitScore fields (UnitScore wraps f32 → can't be Eq) but left the Eq derive, breaking compilation. PartialEq is sufficient.

Test passes (1 PASS, 2 IGNORED documenting findings).

title: L3: Trust decay / forgetting as deterministic maintenance pathway (half-life model; reversible)
description:
# L3 — Trust decay / forgetting as a deterministic process

## Why

AGENTS.md product principle: *"Forgetting and decay are features; do not try to make all memories permanent."*

The existing `memoryHealth` block in `ee status` reports `freshnessScore`. Status has metrics for decay but no observable mechanism that DOES the decay. Currently:
- Memories don't get demoted automatically
- Procedural rules don't lose confidence over time without revalidation
- Tombstoned memories aren't auto-pruned

If "forgetting is a feature", it needs an implementing surface.

## Acceptance

### Decay model

Each memory has:
- `utility` (0..1): observed usefulness from packs/searches
- `confidence` (0..1): per-source trust
- `freshness` (derived): based on `last_accessed_at` and a half-life

Decay function (per-day):

```
freshness(t) = exp(-ln(2) * t / half_life)
where t = days since last access
half_life is per (level, kind), configurable
```

Default half-lives:
- `working/*`: 1 day
- `episodic/event`: 30 days
- `episodic/failure`: 90 days (failures are sticky)
- `semantic/fact`: 180 days
- `procedural/rule`: 365 days (rules persist unless contradicted)

### Decay maintenance job

`ee maintenance run --include-decay --workspace .`:
- Walks memories; updates a derived `current_freshness` column (or recomputes on read)
- Identifies memories with `freshness * confidence * utility < demote_threshold` (default 0.05)
- DEMOTES (not deletes): `level` shifts down (`procedural` → `semantic` → `episodic`), or just lowers `importance`
- Logs every demotion to audit_log with reason

### Forgetting (hard removal)

Memories with `freshness * confidence * utility < forget_threshold` (default 0.01) AND `is_tombstoned: false` get tombstoned with `reason: "auto_forgetting"`. This is reversible — tombstoned memories remain in storage but excluded from retrieval.

### Honest reporting

`ee status` already has `freshnessScore`. After L3, this score is sourced from the actual decay computation, not a stub.

`ee learn summary` reports `memories_demoted_via_decay`, `memories_tombstoned_via_decay`.

### Resetting decay

`ee remember` against an existing memory ID updates `last_accessed_at`. Any `ee why <id>` or pack inclusion also bumps `last_accessed_at`. So "useful" memories naturally stay fresh.

## Design considerations

- **Deterministic.** Decay computation is pure function of (last_accessed_at, half_life, current_time). Same input → same output.
- **Configurable.** Half-lives, thresholds, and the decay function itself are in workspace config under `learn.decay.*`.
- **Reversible.** Auto-forgetting is tombstoning, not deletion. `ee curate untombstone <id>` restores (new command, simple).
- **Opt-out:** `ee maintenance run` without `--include-decay` skips. Heavy workflows that want to control decay manually can disable.

## Test plan

- **Unit:** `tests/decay_compute_unit.rs` — freshness function determinism
- **E2E:** `scripts/e2e_overhaul/decay.sh` (NEW under J3):
  - Seed memories with synthetic `created_at` in the past
  - Run `ee maintenance run --include-decay`
  - Assert memories demoted as expected (table-driven by half-life)
  - Assert tombstoning fires below `forget_threshold`
  - Re-`ee remember` an existing memory; assert decay resets
- **Determinism (J7):** decay deterministic given same fixture timestamps
- **Logging:** `decay_apply: {memory_id, freshness, utility, confidence, action: demote|tombstone|preserve}` event

## Depends on

- G1 (audit log infrastructure — decay writes audit rows)
- B8 (tombstone semantics — decay produces tombstones)
- E1 (posture — decay maintenance job has its own degradation paths)

## Blocks

- K1 (AGENTS.md documents the decay model)
notes:
PLAN-SPACE REVISION (2026-05-13 CopperHarbor — complete the test plan that was cut off):

The original description ends mid-sentence in the "Test plan" section ("Seed memor..."). Filling in the full test plan + logging + e2e details so the implementing agent has a concrete checklist.

## Test surface (named files)

### Unit tests
- tests/decay_compute_unit.rs — pure function tests for freshness(t, half_life): exp decay determinism (same inputs → identical f32 bits), boundary cases (t=0 → 1.0, t=half_life → 0.5, t=∞ → 0.0), and the f32-vs-f64 stability question (pick one; document choice in a comment that this test pins).
- tests/decay_threshold_classification_unit.rs — table-driven: (utility, confidence, freshness, demote_threshold, forget_threshold) -> expected action (keep / demote / tombstone). Covers all 3 thresholds, edge cases (NaN handling), and the explicit "freshness * confidence * utility" multiplication rule.
- tests/decay_level_demotion_unit.rs — table-driven: starting (level, kind) + (freshness * confidence * utility) below demote_threshold -> expected post-demotion (level, kind). Asserts procedural→semantic→episodic transition, and that 'working' is not demoted further (already lowest active level).
- tests/decay_reversibility_unit.rs — proves un-tombstoning works: tombstone a memory via auto_forgetting → ee curate untombstone <id> → memory becomes retrievable again with freshness reset to current_time anchor, NOT to its original capture time (so it doesn't re-tombstone next cycle).
- tests/decay_audit_coverage_unit.rs — every demote/tombstone action produces an audit_log row with action='memory.decay_demote' / 'memory.decay_tombstone' and details={previous_level, new_level, freshness, confidence, utility, threshold, reason}.

### Golden fixtures
- tests/fixtures/golden/decay/demote_procedural_to_semantic.json.golden — deterministic ee learn summary output after a maintenance run with a known-stale procedural rule.
- tests/fixtures/golden/decay/tombstone_via_forgetting.json.golden — same shape, with a memory crossing the forget_threshold.
- tests/snapshots/decay_maintenance_summary.snap (insta) — the ee maintenance run --include-decay --json output for a controlled fixture.

### E2E
- scripts/e2e_overhaul/decay.sh (NEW under J3 conventions; placeholder slot exists per the bead description):
  1. epic_setup; seed_corpus.
  2. Seed 4 memories with known last_accessed_at offsets: procedural at -400d (>365d half-life), semantic at -200d (above 180d half-life), episodic_event at -45d (above 30d), working at -10d (above 1d). All other knobs equal.
  3. ee maintenance run --include-decay --workspace . --json | jq '.data' -> assert demote count=3 (the 3 stale ones), keep count=1 (working at -10d? actually working at -10d is 10x its half-life, so also stale; adjust fixture: working at -0.5d).
  4. ee status --workspace . --json | jq '.data.memoryHealth.freshnessScore' -> assert sourced from real decay computation (NOT a stub; cross-check by running maintenance twice and verifying the score moves monotonically).
  5. ee curate untombstone <id> on the auto-forgotten memory -> assert memory reappears in ee memory list and freshness is anchored to NOW (not original capture).
  6. Re-run maintenance with --dry-run -> assert NO mutations occurred (no audit_log rows, no status field changes).
  7. Re-run maintenance WITHOUT --include-decay -> assert no decay actions, no audit rows.
  Each step emits a J1 event: { kind: 'decay_e2e_step', step_id, expected_count, observed_count, status }.

### Bench (separate from L3 acceptance but called out for J9 to pick up)
- benches/perf_decay.rs — full-corpus maintenance run latency at 1K / 10K / 100K memories. Decay is intended to be cheap; budget < 100ms for 10K.

## Logging requirements

- Every demote and tombstone writes an audit_log row (action, entity_id, details JSON) AND emits a tracing::info! event on the ee::learn::decay target with the same details. Required so an agent investigating "where did my memory go" can trace it back without DB introspection.
- ee maintenance run --include-decay --json output includes a 'decay' sub-object: { memories_demoted, memories_tombstoned, half_lives_applied, threshold_demote, threshold_forget, dry_run } so a downstream auditor sees the parameters in effect.
- The freshnessScore in ee status --json includes a 'sourced_from' field: 'decay_v1' (after L3) vs 'stub' (before L3), so the honesty signal is machine-readable.

## Determinism

- Decay is a pure function of (last_accessed_at, half_life, current_time, thresholds). Two maintenance runs against an identical workspace with current_time pinned (via test seam --as-of) MUST produce byte-identical audit_log diffs and identical 'decay' sub-object.
- The proptest harness from N4.5 should be extended to fuzz decay parameters and assert pure-function determinism.

## Composition

- bd-n22a4 (B2-followup, closed) introduced the per-source relevance floor; not directly related but the same "honesty over silent filtering" pattern applies here — every decay decision must be auditable.
- N7 (Bayesian posteriors) may eventually replace the multiplicative freshness*confidence*utility heuristic with a principled posterior; L3's threshold logic should be implemented behind a small trait so N7 can swap in cleanly.

## Acceptance gate (FINAL — supersedes the cut-off Test plan section)

- All 5 named unit tests pass.
- All 3 golden fixtures committed.
- decay.sh e2e driver runs cleanly, all 7 steps green, J1 events emitted.
- audit_log rows present for every demote and tombstone in the e2e fixture run.
- ee maintenance run --include-decay --json --dry-run produces an honest preview without mutations (verified by re-querying audit_log after dry-run shows zero new rows).
- ee curate untombstone <id> is a new CLI command and is documented in 'ee --help'.
