title: N4.2: Deterministic<Seed> capability token type (API + module)
description: Implement the Deterministic<Seed> capability token type. Design (subject to inventory findings from N4.1): a phantom-typed marker carrying a u64 seed and a phantom unique-id per call-site origin (so two callers can't accidentally share an instance and get coupled output). Token is created at the top of an entry point (CLI command handler, daemon job, lab capture/replay) from explicit user-provided seed, persistent workspace seed, or RFC-3339 timestamp truncated to second precision. Token cannot be cloned (Move semantics enforce single-use per scope); it can be split via .child(label) into deterministic sub-tokens (PRNG-fork pattern, like rand::SeedableRng but compile-time-safe). The token is the ONLY way to construct types that implement RandomnessConsumer trait (RngCore wrapper, deterministic clock wrapper, sorted-iter wrappers). API surface lives in src/runtime/determinism.rs (NEW module). Acceptance: doctests demonstrating valid + invalid usage; tests proving the type is Send + !Clone + !Sync; ADR documenting the design (could be ADR 0030 if it warrants its own; otherwise covered in N15's ADR 0028).
notes:
# Test plan — N4.2 Deterministic Seed token (Round 3 ULID interaction)

## Substrate
- New module src/runtime/determinism.rs; doctests are first-class
- Inventory from N4.1 (cited by content_hash) drives design

## ULID interaction (Round 3 specification)
The token carries an internal monotonic counter (u64). When ULID generation requires a timestamp, it reads from the token's monotonic counter, NOT system clock. This preserves ULID's time-ordering guarantee within a deterministic scope (sub-tokens get monotonically increasing slices). Cross-scope ULID ordering is deterministic-but-arbitrary by seed (two tokens with different seeds produce ULIDs that order by their seed precedence, not by wall-clock time).

The token clock-wrapper is a struct DeterministicClock { last: AtomicU64 } that returns ulid::ulid::Timestamp values derived from the counter; .advance() increments and returns the next value. ULID generation that today calls SystemTime::now() is rewritten to call token.clock().advance(). The Cx Cancel composability is preserved because the wrapper takes &mut self (token mutation is single-threaded within a scope).

## Asupersync Cx interop (Round 3 addition)
The token is constructed inside the entry-point handler at the top of the Cx scope: let mut det = Cx::scoped_deterministic(seed). Subsequent &Cx-taking functions can pull the token via a side-channel WorkerLocal<Deterministic> OR pass it explicitly. The asupersync runtime guarantees that Cx-scoped state does not bleed across cancellation boundaries.

## Unit tests
- tests/determinism_capability_token_unit.rs — construction from explicit seed; persistent seed; timestamp; env
- tests/determinism_token_not_clone_unit.rs — compile-fail (trybuild) showing token cannot be cloned
- tests/determinism_token_split_unit.rs — .child(label) produces deterministic distinct sub-tokens; tokens with same seed + same label produce same sub-token seeds
- tests/determinism_token_send_sync_unit.rs — Send + !Sync (single-threaded use within scope)
- tests/determinism_token_ulid_unit.rs — ULIDs generated through the token clock are monotonically increasing within a scope; given the same seed, the sequence of ULIDs is identical across runs
- tests/determinism_token_cross_scope_ulid_unit.rs — ULIDs from different scopes (different seeds) order by seed precedence, NOT wall-clock
- tests/snapshots/determinism_token_doctest_output.snap

## E2E (none; module-level)

notes:
PLAN-SPACE REVISION (2026-05-12 TealHarbor — round 2 — concrete refactor pattern + signature changes):

## Mechanical refactor pattern (one canonical example)

### Before (ambient randomness)
```rust
pub fn rank_candidates(query: &str, candidates: &[Candidate]) -> Vec<RankedItem> {
    let mut tie_break_seed: u64 = thread_rng().r#gen();   // <-- ambient
    let mut scored: Vec<_> = candidates.iter().map(|c| (c, score(c, query, &mut tie_break_seed))).collect();
    scored.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.partial_cmp(&a.1).unwrap());
    scored.into_iter().map(|(c, _)| c.into()).collect()
}
```

### After (deterministic token)
```rust
pub fn rank_candidates(
    query: &str,
    candidates: &[Candidate],
    seed: &Deterministic<Seed>,            // <-- token, &-ref because pure
) -> Vec<RankedItem> {
    let mut scored: Vec<_> = candidates
        .iter()
        .map(|c| (c, score(c, query, seed)))
        .collect();
    scored.sort_by(|a, b| (b.1, b.0.memory_id.as_str()).partial_cmp(&(a.1, a.0.memory_id.as_str())).unwrap());
    scored.into_iter().map(|(c, _)| c.into()).collect()
}
```

Two patterns by mutability:
- **Read-only paths (scoring, ranking, MMR)**: take `seed: &Deterministic<Seed>`. The leaf function reads bits from the seed deterministically.
- **State-advancing paths (ULID generation, sequential ID emission)**: take `seed: &mut Deterministic<Seed>`. Move semantics on `Deterministic` ensures only ONE generator advances the sequence; forks happen explicitly via `.child(label)`.

## Token fork rules

- A function that needs randomness for an INTERNAL stage takes `&Deterministic<Seed>` and calls `.child("stage_label")` to get a child token. The child is a SEPARATE Deterministic with a derived seed (BLAKE3-keyed). Parent stays usable.
- The child token's label is part of the determinism contract: changing the label changes the seed. Document existing labels in `docs/determinism_seed_labels.md`.

## Unit tests (`tests/determinism_token_threading_unit.rs`)

10 rows from the surface table:
- Each row constructs a synthetic input, calls the function with the same seed twice, asserts identical output.
- Each row asserts that calling with a DIFFERENT seed produces different output (where applicable; pure-deterministic functions like sort have no seed dependence).

Plus 3 cross-cutting:
- Token cannot be cloned (compile-time test via `static_assertions::assert_not_impl_all!(Deterministic<Seed>: Clone)`).
- `.child()` produces a NEW token with a deterministic but DIFFERENT seed (label-keyed derivation).
- Loom-style scheduler test: two threads concurrently consuming child tokens produce deterministic interleavings (composes with L1 write spool concurrency model).

## E2E composition with J7

`scripts/e2e_overhaul/determinism.sh` already exists. Add a `determinism_token_threading` block:
- Run a synthetic workflow that uses every surface in the threading list.
- 3 invocations; assert byte-identical results.
- Capture the chain of seeds via test logging.

```json
}
```

title: N4.4: Clippy lint catching ambient randomness in #[determinism::required] paths
description: Author a Clippy lint (or a build-script-driven lint via dylint if upstream Clippy doesn't fit) that fails compilation when a function tagged #[determinism::required] uses ambient randomness: rand::* without going through Deterministic<Seed>, SystemTime::now(), HashMap iteration without explicit sort, std::env::var in a tagged path, std::fs::read_dir without sort. The #[determinism::required] attribute is a proc-macro shim that emits a marker symbol and registers the function in a static slice the lint walks. Acceptance: the lint catches the 'before' state of N4.1 inventory rows; tests/determinism_lint_catches_known_violations.rs (a UI test using trybuild) freezes the lint's output on a fixture file that intentionally violates. Gated in CI via cargo clippy --features determinism-lint -- -D warnings (added to the existing clippy gate).
notes:
PLAN-SPACE REVISION (2026-05-12 TealHarbor — round 2 — commits to custom in-tree lint + trybuild UI tests):

## Lint implementation (canonical: custom in-tree lint via Clippy's `disallowed_methods` + a custom proc-macro for `#[determinism::required]`)

The lint has TWO parts:

### Part A — Clippy `disallowed_methods` (cheap, ships immediately)

`clippy.toml`:
```toml
disallowed-methods = [
    {
        path = "rand::thread_rng",
        reason = "Determinism: use crate::core::determinism::Deterministic<Seed> or pass `&mut Deterministic<Id>` instead. See bd-17c65.14.4.2."
    },
    {
        path = "rand::random",
        reason = "Determinism: use Deterministic<Id>::gen_u64() instead."
    },
    {
        path = "std::time::Instant::now",
        reason = "Time should not affect deterministic outputs. Use the workspace clock (audit_ts) at the boundary only; pass injected time through Deterministic<Id>."
    },
    {
        path = "uuid::Uuid::new_v4",
        reason = "Use ulid::Ulid::new() with a Deterministic<Id>-keyed clock for stored ULIDs."
    }
]
```

Bypass mechanism: explicit `#[allow(clippy::disallowed_methods)]` on a function comments WHY it bypasses. CI greps for this attribute and lints reviewers to verify it.

### Part B — Custom proc-macro `#[determinism::required]` (new crate `ee_determinism_macros`)

`crates/ee_determinism_macros/src/lib.rs`:

```rust
/// Marks a function as requiring deterministic randomness. At compile
/// time, the macro enforces:
///   1. The function has at least one `Deterministic<Id>` parameter
///      (by &-ref or &mut).
///   2. The function body grep-scans for ambient randomness call
///      sites and fails with a precise error if any are found.
///
/// Bead bd-17c65.14.4.4 (N4.4).
#[proc_macro_attribute]
pub fn required(_attr: TokenStream, item: TokenStream) -> TokenStream { ... }
```

The macro errors at compile time:
- `fn foo()` (no Deterministic param) → `error: #[determinism::required] requires at least one Deterministic<Id> parameter`
- `fn foo(seed: &Deterministic<Seed>) { let x = thread_rng().gen(); }` → `error: ambient randomness call thread_rng() inside #[determinism::required] function`

The macro's body inspection is best-effort (proc-macros can't trivially walk full function bodies); the deeper check is `disallowed_methods` above.

## Trybuild UI tests (`tests/ui/`)

Each test is a tiny Rust file that should FAIL to compile with a specific error message.

| File                                                      | Should fail at compile | Expected error |
|-----------------------------------------------------------|------------------------|-----------------|
| `tests/ui/determinism_required_no_param.rs`               | yes                    | "requires at least one Deterministic<Id> parameter" |
| `tests/ui/determinism_required_thread_rng.rs`             | yes (via clippy)       | "rand::thread_rng is disallowed; use Deterministic<Id>" |
| `tests/ui/determinism_required_instant_now.rs`            | yes (via clippy)       | "std::time::Instant::now is disallowed" |
| `tests/ui/determinism_required_passes_with_seed.rs`       | NO (negative test)     | (compiles cleanly) |
| `tests/ui/determinism_required_allow_with_justification.rs`| NO                    | (compiles with `#[allow]`) |

Each `.rs` file is paired with a `.stderr` file snapshot of the compiler error.

## Lint exemption tracking

`tests/determinism_exemption_audit.rs`:
- Greps src/ for `#[allow(clippy::disallowed_methods)]`.
- For each occurrence, requires a comment in the next 3 lines explaining WHY the bypass is acceptable.
- Asserts the number of exemptions hasn't grown beyond a baseline (`exemption_baseline.txt`, version-controlled).

## E2E (`scripts/e2e_overhaul/lint_determinism.sh`, new)

- Run `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D clippy::disallowed_methods` and assert exit 0.
- Run `cargo test --test ui` and assert all trybuild UI snapshots pass.

## Logging event (per lint pass)

```json
{

}
```

- `clippy.toml` with the 4 disallowed methods.
- `ee_determinism_macros` crate landed with `#[determinism::required]`.
- 5 trybuild UI tests with snapshots.

title: N4.5: Proptest harness — (DB, indexes, config, query, seed) -> byte-identical pack
description: Proptest harness covering (DB state, indexes state, config snapshot, query string, seed) -> byte-identical pack JSON. Generators: arbitrary memory sets (bounded size, deterministic structure), arbitrary configs (covering the [pack], [search], [curation] sections), arbitrary query strings (with controlled length distribution to keep test budget tractable), arbitrary u64 seeds. Property: for any (DB, indexes, config, query, seed), running ee context against an identical second copy of the workspace yields byte-identical pack JSON (after stripping J7 _strip_fields). Pairs with N4.4 lint: lint is the prevention; proptest is the detection. Target >10k tuples in the standard CI run, >1M in a nightly-only stress run. Fixture failures get persisted as regression goldens under tests/snapshots/determinism_regression_<hash>.snap so subsequent runs catch the same shape. Composes with N15.4 (lab replay's --verify-determinism flag does the same thing for a single fixture; this is the fuzzing complement).

| Axis                  | Generator                                                              | Cardinality                           |
|-----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| Workspace state       | sample from `tests/fixtures/swarm_scale/{smoke_1k,mid_10k}/`           | 2 (smoke gates fast; mid under feat)  |
| Config                | per-section toggle: {pack.profile} × {pack.max_tokens 500..=4000} × ...| ≈ 40 combinations                     |
| Query                 | sample from `tests/fixtures/query_corpus/queries.txt` (50 queries)     | 50                                    |
| Seed                  | u64 in {0, 1, 42, 0xdead_beef, u64::MAX, time-derived not allowed}     | 5                                     |
| Format                | enum over 8 renderers                                                   | 8                                     |
| Random toggles        | --include-tombstoned, --explain, --strict-source-mode, etc.            | 2^n                                   |

Combined strategy: `proptest::collection::vec((workspace_state, config, query, seed, format, toggles), 1..=128)`.

The proptest harness asserts: for each tuple (workspace, config, query, seed, format, toggles), running `ee context "<query>" ...` produces byte-identical output when invoked twice within the SAME process AND across two SEPARATE processes. This is the (DB, indexes, config, query, seed) → byte-identical pack invariant from AGENTS.md.

## Regression fixture pinning

When proptest finds a counterexample, the harness persists it under `tests/fixtures/proptest_regressions/<hash>.json`:

```json
{
  "schema": "ee.proptest.regression.v1",
  "captured_at": "<rfc3339>",
  "seed": <u64>,
  "input": { "workspace_state": "...", "config": {...}, "query": "...", "format": "..." },
  "expected_hash": "<blake3>",
  "observed_hash_run1": "<blake3>",
  "observed_hash_run2": "<blake3>",
  "first_diff_byte_offset": <usize>,
  "first_diff_window": { "expected": "...", "observed": "..." }
}
```

The regression file's name is `blake3(input)[:16]`.json so the same counterexample doesn't get re-filed.

The harness LOADS all existing regression files on startup and re-asserts each one passes before sampling new counterexamples. This prevents fixed bugs from regressing silently.

## Staleness detection

Each regression file carries a `last_verified_at` field. If a file's `last_verified_at` is older than 90 days, it's flagged for review. Two outcomes:
- The bug is still relevant → bump `last_verified_at` to current.
- The fixture is obsolete (e.g., feature removed) → DELETE the regression file with a commit note.

## Unit test (`tests/determinism_proptest_harness_unit.rs`)

The harness itself is tested for its own behavior:
1. **Counterexample capture**: inject a synthetic non-determinism (e.g., monkey-patched random ULID via test feature flag) → harness detects and persists a regression file.
2. **Replay**: load a known regression file → assert it still triggers the failure (or assert it's been fixed and remove the file in the same PR).
3. **Shrinking**: proptest's shrink algorithm reduces a failing case to a minimal counterexample.

## E2E (`scripts/e2e_overhaul/determinism_proptest.sh`, new)

Runs the proptest harness with a tight time budget (60 s in CI, longer under `EE_PROPTEST_LONG=1` for nightly). On failure: posts the new regression file to the PR review.

## Logging event

```json
{
  "schema": "ee.test_event.v1",
  "kind": "proptest_run",
  "axes_count": 6,
  "cases_sampled": <usize>,
  "cases_passed": <usize>,
  "cases_failed": <usize>,
  "new_regressions": [...],
  "stale_regressions_flagged": [...],
  "elapsed_seconds": <float>,
  "budget_seconds": <float>
}
```

## Acceptance gate

- Harness ships with the 6-axis generator.
- 1000+ cases run in CI smoke profile (60 s budget).
- Regression files persisted on failure and re-asserted on subsequent runs.
- Stale-regression detection at 90 days.
- Composes with N4.2 (Seed type), N4.3 (threading), N15.4 (pack-hash determinism), J7 (cross-process gate).

title: N5: Submodular pack assembly — fix the proof, or rename the certificate
description:
N5 UMBRELLA — Submodular pack assembly honesty fix. Current packs ship a 6KB selectionCertificate that self-declares monotone:false, submodular:false, guaranteeStatus:conditional — i.e., we ship a certificate to attest we do NOT satisfy our claimed guarantee. This is an honesty fail at the heart of the pack contract.

This umbrella has two children that together resolve the gap:

- N5.0 (bd-17c65.14.5.1) docs — ADR 0031: decides Resolution A (prove submodularity) vs Resolution B (rename selectionCertificate to selectionAudit). Gates everything else.
- N5.1 (bd-17c65.14.5.2) feature — Implementation of the chosen resolution. Depends on N5.0.

Resolution A path: fix the objective to weighted facility-location with set cover; prove monotonicity + submodularity (small Lean proof via lean-formal-feedback-loop skill); commit at docs/proofs/submodular_pack.lean; CI runs the proof.

Resolution B path: rename selectionCertificate to selectionAudit across canonical pack tree, JSON, goldens, docs; drop guaranteeStatus; add algorithmId + algorithmDescription naming the actual objective.

Composes with bd-17c65.1 (A-series pack format densification) and bd-17c65.4 (D-series canonical pack tree). Breaking change for downstream consumers; coordinated via bd-17c65.4.7 D7/A10 schema bump.

Closure: N5 umbrella closes when both N5.0 and N5.1 close under implements-surface:submodular_pack_assembly (or implements-surface:selection_audit_rename per the chosen resolution).
notes:
# Test plan — N5 Submodular pack assembly honesty fix

## Substrate
- ADR (mandatory) — choice between Resolution A (prove submodularity) and Resolution B (rename certificate -> audit) MUST be made in ADR 0031 before any code lands.
- Logging: J1; Corpus: J2 + tests/fixtures/pack/submodular_synthetic_<scenario>.json with known-optimal selections under weighted facility-location

## Unit tests
RESOLUTION A path (proof):
- tests/submodular_pack_proof_unit.rs — verifies monotonicity property on 1000 random fixtures; submodularity (diminishing returns) verified by direct definition check
- tests/submodular_pack_lean_proof_smoke.rs — checks that the Lean proof artifact in docs/proofs/submodular_pack.lean compiles (uses the lean-formal-feedback-loop skill methodology)
- tests/snapshots/pack_certificate_proof.snap — golden frozen certificate JSON for reference fixture

RESOLUTION B path (rename):
- tests/selection_audit_renamed_unit.rs — no occurrences of 'selectionCertificate' or 'guaranteeStatus' in canonical pack tree
- tests/snapshots/pack_selection_audit.snap — golden showing the new field name + shape
- A migration test asserting old 'selectionCertificate' is no longer emitted

## E2E (scripts/e2e_overhaul/pack_submodular_or_audit.sh)
Branches on the ADR-chosen resolution; both paths must run determinism + golden checks

title: N6: Persistent homology on memory-link graph for principled curation clusters
description:
FrankenNetworkX ships fnx-algorithms; the memory-link graph today is analyzed via PageRank and centrality only. Layer H0/H1 persistent homology over the graph: H0 surfaces connected components (rule families), H1 surfaces cycles (potentially redundant or circular reasoning). The persistence diagram gives a principled, scale-free 'topologically distinct cluster' feature for ee curate to surface consolidation candidates that traditional clustering (silhouette, DBSCAN) miss.

PRE-FLIGHT INVESTIGATION (Round 2 addition, MANDATORY before implementation):

Phase 0 — Confirm fnx-algorithms surface:
- Audit fnx-algorithms crate for persistent-homology / persistence-diagram support. Output: docs/perf-forensics/fnx_persistent_homology_audit_TIMESTAMP.md cataloging which functions exist and which are missing.

Three branches based on Phase 0 outcome:

BRANCH A — fnx-algorithms already supports it:
- N6 implementation proceeds directly using the upstream API.

BRANCH B — fnx-algorithms missing pieces but vendored copy at /data/projects/franken_networkx:
- File a sibling bead in the fnx project (or in ee if vendored): 'Add H0/H1 persistence-diagram support to fnx-algorithms'. Block N6 on it.

BRANCH C — Upstream out of scope, vendor into ee:
- Vendor a minimal persistence-homology implementation under src/graph/persistent_homology.rs using gudhi-rs or a hand-rolled simplicial-complex algorithm. ADR (potentially 0033) documents the choice and the upstream-contribution plan.

Replaces bd-17c65.7.5 (G5 silhouette-scored agglomerative) with a math-backed approach OR composes alongside it as a second signal. DoD: ee curate candidates --kind topological-cluster surfaces clusters with persistence values; goldens freeze topology for the J2 reference corpus; eval fixture shows N6 proposed clusters human-validate at higher precision than silhouette baseline.
notes:
ROUND-3 PLAN-SPACE REVISION (2026-05-12 TealHarbor):

## Acceptance enhancements

### Persistent homology pipeline (canonical)

1. Build a Vietoris-Rips complex from the memory-link graph (nodes = memories, edge weights = inverse link strength).
2. Filter by edge weight threshold ε; for each ε, count connected components and 1-dim holes.
3. The barcode persists topological features that survive over wide ε ranges — these are the principled clusters.
4. Map each persistent component to a curation candidate cluster (composes with G5 / bd-17c65.7.5).

### Library choice

Use `rustworkx-tda` or hand-roll a minimal RIPS filter; NO petgraph (forbidden). Single-threaded reference implementation first; parallelize only if J9 benchmarks demand.

### Unit tests (`tests/persistent_homology_unit.rs`)

1. **Trivial graph** (3 disconnected nodes): exactly 3 persistent components.
2. **Single cluster** (5 fully-connected nodes): 1 persistent component; 0 holes.
3. **Two distinct clusters** (5 + 5 separated by sparse edges): 2 persistent components; 0 long-persistence holes.
4. **Ring structure** (6 nodes in a cycle): 1 persistent component; 1 persistent 1-hole (the ring).
5. **Determinism**: same graph + same filter ε → byte-identical barcode across 3 runs.
6. **Calibration**: against the J2 reference corpus's memory-link graph, persistent components match the G5 cluster output to within 2 cluster-id differences (algorithm-agnostic equivalence threshold).

### E2E (`scripts/e2e_overhaul/persistent_homology.sh`)

- Seed J2 corpus + add explicit links forming known topological structure.
- Run `ee curate cluster --algorithm persistent_homology --json`.
- Assert candidate count matches the topology prediction.
- 3 runs byte-identical.

title: N7: Bayesian (alpha, beta) confidence posterior on memories (Beta-Bernoulli update on outcome events)
description:
N7 UMBRELLA — Bayesian (alpha, beta) confidence posteriors on memories. Today utility/confidence updates on ee outcome use ad-hoc linear deltas. Replace with a Beta-Bernoulli posterior tracked per memory; the credible interval surfaces in ee why; trust-class lifecycle (amends ADR 0009) transitions on credible-interval boundary crossings instead of point-estimate threshold crossings to eliminate flicker.

This umbrella has two children:

- N7.0 (bd-17c65.14.7.1) docs — ADR 0032: documents the design, prior choice (Jeffreys 0.5, 0.5), update rule asymmetry (harmful weight = 2.5), and the amendment to ADR 0009 trust-class transitions. Gates everything else.
- N7.1 (bd-17c65.14.7.2) feature — Schema migration adding bayes_alpha + bayes_beta REAL columns, three backfill modes (Jeffreys default, --bayes-backfill-from-utility, --bayes-backfill-from-feedback-events), update rule wired through ee outcome handler, bayesPosterior block in ee why. Depends on N7.0.

Composes with N11 active-learning (info-gain uses Beta variance) and N12 anti-patterns (severity uses posterior). 

Closure: N7 umbrella closes when both N7.0 and N7.1 close under implements-surface:bayesian_posteriors.
notes:
ROUND-3 PLAN-SPACE REVISION (2026-05-12 TealHarbor):

## Acceptance enhancements (composes with N7.0 ADR + N7.1 sub-bead)

### Posterior storage schema (canonical)

```sql
ALTER TABLE memories ADD COLUMN trust_alpha REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.0;
ALTER TABLE memories ADD COLUMN trust_beta REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.0;
ALTER TABLE memories ADD COLUMN trust_evidence_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;
```

`alpha=1.0, beta=1.0` is the uniform prior (Beta(1,1) = Uniform on [0,1]). Helpful/harmful events update these by +1 / +harmful_weight.

### Update rule

- On `ee outcome <id> --signal helpful`: alpha += 1.0; evidence_count += 1.
- On `ee outcome <id> --signal harmful`: beta += 2.5 (workspace config `feedback.harmful_weight`, default 2.5); evidence_count += 1.
- On manual `--validate` or `--apply`: alpha += 2.0 (validation is strong evidence; configurable via `[feedback].validation_weight`).
- On `--snooze` or `--reject`: NO update (snooze ≠ harmful; reject is for the proposal, not the underlying memory).

Confidence = alpha / (alpha + beta); credible interval from Beta CDF at α=0.05.

### Unit tests (`tests/bayesian_posterior_unit.rs`)

1. Uniform prior: alpha=1, beta=1 → confidence=0.5, CI≈[0.025, 0.975].
2. After 10 helpful events: alpha=11, beta=1 → confidence≈0.917, CI narrows.
3. After 10 harmful events (weight 2.5): alpha=1, beta=26 → confidence≈0.037, CI≈[0.001, 0.13].
4. Mixed updates: 5 helpful + 3 harmful → alpha=6, beta=8.5 → confidence≈0.414.
5. CI lower-bound triggers trust class transition: when CI_lo crosses 0.65, agent_assertion → agent_validated (per ADR amend).
6. Determinism: same event sequence → identical (alpha, beta) across 3 runs.
7. Decay: composes with L3 — decay multiplies alpha and beta by half-life factor; mean stays constant (forgetting evidence, not changing belief).

### Backtest harness (`tests/bayesian_calibration_backtest.rs`)

For each memory in the eval fixture corpus that has ≥10 outcome events: bootstrap-sample 1000 (helpful_count, harmful_count) pairs from the empirical distribution; compute (alpha, beta); assert empirical helpful rate falls in CI 95% of the time.

### `ee why <id>` rendering additions

```json
"trust": {
  "alpha": 6.0,
  "beta": 8.5,
  "evidence_count": 8,
  "confidence": 0.414,
  "credible_interval": { "lower": 0.198, "upper": 0.652, "alpha_level": 0.05 },
  "trust_class": "agent_assertion",
  "next_promotion_threshold": { "ci_lower_at": 0.65, "next_class": "agent_validated" }
}
```

### Logging event

```json
{"schema":"ee.test_event.v1","kind":"bayesian_update","memory_id":"<id>","signal":"helpful|harmful|validate|reject|snooze","alpha_before":<float>,"beta_before":<float>,"alpha_after":<float>,"beta_after":<float>,"confidence_after":<float>,"ci_lower":<float>,"ci_upper":<float>,"trust_class_transition":"<class|null>"}
```

### Failure-mode fixtures (J6)

- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/bayesian_evidence_underpowered.json` (info; <3 events).
- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/bayesian_credible_interval_unstable.json` (warning; CI width > 0.4 after 10+ events suggests noisy signal).

### Acceptance gate

- 7 unit cases pass + backtest within 95% calibration.
- Schema migration adds three columns.
- `ee why <id>` renders the trust block.
- ADR 0009 amended (N7.0 sub-bead).
- All 2 J6 fixtures land.
- Composes with L3 decay (multiplicative half-life on alpha+beta), N3 causal credit (credit propagation also updates posteriors), N11 active learning (info gain = -E_q[log q] from Beta posterior).

title: N7.0: ADR 0032 — Bayesian (alpha, beta) posteriors (amends ADR 0009 trust-class taxonomy)
description:
ADR 0032 — Bayesian (alpha, beta) posteriors on memories. N7 (bd-17c65.14.7) introduces Beta-Bernoulli posterior tracking that REPLACES the ad-hoc linear utility/confidence updates and AMENDS ADR 0009 (trust class taxonomy) by changing trust-class transitions to credible-interval-boundary crossings rather than point-estimate threshold crossings.

ADR 0032 documents:
- Decision: track (alpha, beta) Beta posterior per memory; confidence = alpha/(alpha+beta); credible interval from Beta CDF.
- Prior choice: Jeffreys prior (0.5, 0.5). RATIONALE: Jeffreys is the reference prior for Bernoulli — invariant under reparameterization, minimally informative, well-calibrated. Uniform (1, 1) rejected because it implies one observed success and one failure as the prior knowledge, which is more confident than warranted for a brand-new memory.
- Update rule: helpful event -> alpha += 1; harmful event -> beta += harmful_weight (default 2.5 per README config). Harmful asymmetry preserved.
- Trust-class lifecycle (amends ADR 0009): transitions trigger on credible-interval boundary crossings, NOT point estimates. This eliminates flicker around threshold values.
- Schema migration: bayes_alpha REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.5, bayes_beta REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.5 columns on memories table. Migration uses L0 framework (bd-17c65.12.5 pattern). Reversible.
- Rejected alternatives: Gaussian posterior (wrong domain — confidence is bounded [0,1]); Dirichlet (multi-outcome — we only have helpful/harmful, so Beta suffices).
- Verification hook: calibration backtest over eval fixture suite — empirical helpful rate falls within the credible interval >95 percent of cases.

Acceptance: docs/adr/0032-bayesian-memory-posteriors.md committed; ADR 0009 amended (revised section on trust-class transitions); tests/adr_0032_present.rs + tests/adr_0009_amendment_section.rs assert presence; N7 body updates to reference ADR 0032.

ADR 0032 (Bayesian (alpha, beta) Posteriors on Memories) shipped.

Artifacts:
- docs/adr/0032-bayesian-memory-posteriors.md (full ADR; Context + Decision + Consequences + Rejected Alternatives + Verification per AGENTS.md template)
- docs/adr/README.md updated (ADR 0032 in index after 0031)
- tests/adr_0032_docs.rs (4 tests; all passing): exists_and_is_indexed, has_required_sections, documents_required_design_choices, lists_rejected_alternatives_with_reasoning

Decisions:
- Beta-Bernoulli posterior tracked via bayes_alpha + bayes_beta REAL columns on memories table (16-byte overhead per row)
- Jeffreys prior (0.5, 0.5) default; configurable via [bayes] prior_alpha / prior_beta
- Update rule: helpful adds 1 to alpha; harmful adds harmful_weight (default 2.5 per existing [curation]) to beta
- Trust-class transitions driven by ci90 boundary crossings, NOT point estimates — hysteresis eliminates flicker (amends ADR 0009 transition rules; class definitions and initial confidences remain load-bearing from 0009)
- Sample-size gate alpha + beta >= 6 at agent_assertion -> agent_validated to prevent thin-evidence promotion
- human_explicit is reached only via explicit ee rule promote (no automatic promotion); demotion remains automatic
- Three backfill modes: default Jeffreys, --bayes-backfill-from-utility (weight=2 inverse fit), --bayes-backfill-from-feedback-events (full replay)
- Schema migration reversible via L0 framework (bd-17c65.12.5)
- New audit actions: memory.bayes_posterior_updated, trust_class.transition

Rationale: Gaussian rejected (unbounded support; bounded latent rate); Dirichlet rejected (binary outcome space); elapsed-time hysteresis rejected (non-deterministic + fragile under bursts); scalar-with-count rejected (no credible interval).

This sub-bead unblocks bd-17c65.14.7.2 (N7.1 implementation). No source-runtime changes in this PR.

Backfill for existing memories (three modes via ee migrate run):
- default (no flag): all existing rows get Jeffreys (0.5, 0.5) — clean prior, treats observed memories as having no signal yet. RECOMMENDED.
- ee migrate run --bayes-backfill-from-utility: derive (alpha, beta) from existing utility/confidence via inverse — preserves the per-row trust-class observation. Chosen with weight=2 (so a 'confident 0.8' memory backfills to alpha=1.6, beta=0.4). Documented in migration notes.
- ee migrate run --bayes-backfill-from-feedback-events: replay every feedback_event row through the Beta-Bernoulli update rule from scratch — strongest backfill, most expensive, available only when feedback_events table has data.

Update rule on outcome events: helpful event - alpha += 1; harmful event - beta += harmful_weight (config [curation] harmful_weight, default 2.5). Computed posterior surfaces:
- confidence = alpha / (alpha + beta)
- credible_interval_90 = (Beta.ppf(0.05; alpha, beta), Beta.ppf(0.95; alpha, beta))
- credible_interval_50 = (Beta.ppf(0.25; alpha, beta), Beta.ppf(0.75; alpha, beta))

TRUST-CLASS TRANSITION TABLE (Round 4 specification — amends ADR 0009):

The 5 trust classes from ADR 0009 (human_explicit, agent_validated, agent_assertion, cass_evidence, legacy_import) gain explicit Beta-Bernoulli transition rules. Transitions trigger when credible_interval_90.lo crosses thresholds (NOT point estimates), eliminating flicker. Promotion is monotone per memory id within a session; demotion requires explicit harmful evidence (not just elapsed time):

| From | To | Promote condition | Demote condition |
|------|----|-------------------|------------------|
| legacy_import | cass_evidence | CI90.lo > 0.50 AND at-least-1-validation | CI90.hi < 0.30 |
| cass_evidence | agent_assertion | CI90.lo > 0.60 | CI90.hi < 0.35 |
| agent_assertion | agent_validated | CI90.lo > 0.70 AND alpha + beta >= 6 (sample size gate) | CI90.hi < 0.40 |
| agent_validated | human_explicit | NOT AUTOMATIC — requires explicit ee rule promote --to human_explicit (human-in-loop) | CI90.hi < 0.45 |

Why the sample-size gate at agent_assertion -> agent_validated: small (alpha, beta) like (3, 0) gives CI90.lo > 0.70 but is statistically thin; the gate prevents flicker on first few observations.

Why demotion thresholds differ from promotion: hysteresis. A memory whose CI90.lo just barely crosses up to agent_validated should not bounce back on the next non-helpful event; the demotion threshold sits below the promotion threshold for the next class down.

ee why MEMORY_ID --json includes new bayesPosterior block with alpha, beta, mean, credibleInterval90, credibleInterval50. Trust-class field still present, transitions audited via audit_log.trust_class.transition (NEW audit action — see R4-8). The current confidence field stays equal to mean(alpha, beta) for backward compatibility within the same envelope version.
notes:
PLAN-SPACE REVISION (2026-05-13 CopperHarbor — named test surface + e2e + logging):

The original bead has detailed schema migration, backfill modes,
update rule, and posterior formulas, but does not name the test
files or the e2e flow. Pinning those now.

## Test surface (named files)

### Unit tests
- tests/bayes_schema_migration_unit.rs — round-trip migration test
  using L0 framework: pre-state fixture (memories without
  bayes_alpha/bayes_beta columns) → migrate up → asserts both
  columns present with Jeffreys (0.5, 0.5) defaults → migrate
  down → asserts columns removed → migrate up again →
  byte-identical end state. Catches non-idempotent migrations
  AND data loss on down().
- tests/bayes_backfill_default_unit.rs — default backfill mode (no
  flag): seeded DB with 100 memories of varied utility/confidence
  → ee migrate run → assert every row has bayes_alpha=0.5,
  bayes_beta=0.5 exactly. No information from prior fields
  preserved (clean prior).
- tests/bayes_backfill_from_utility_unit.rs — --bayes-backfill-from-
  utility: seeded fixture with known (utility, confidence) tuples
  → asserts the inverse map produces (alpha, beta) consistent
  with the documented formula: alpha = utility * 2 *
  documented_weight, beta = (1 - utility) * 2 * weight (or
  whatever the canonical formula settles on; bead body says
  "weight=2 so 0.8 confident → alpha=1.6, beta=0.4" — pin that
  numerically).
- tests/bayes_backfill_from_feedback_events_unit.rs — replays
  feedback_event fixtures through Beta-Bernoulli updates; asserts
  each event increments alpha (helpful) or beta by harmful_weight
  (harmful, default 2.5). Test fixture has known event sequence
  producing a known final posterior.
- tests/bayes_update_rule_unit.rs — pure-function tests for
  apply_outcome(alpha, beta, signal, weight) → (new_alpha,
  new_beta). Helpful: alpha+=1. Harmful: beta+=weight. Cover
  edge cases: very large alpha/beta (no overflow), tiny values
  (numerical stability of subsequent ppf calls).
- tests/bayes_posterior_serialization_unit.rs — confidence + both
  credible intervals serialize to the documented JSON shape with
  6-decimal precision. Round-trips through JSON without precision
  loss > 1e-9.
- tests/bayes_why_rendering_unit.rs — ee why <memory-id> --json
  output includes a posterior block with the canonical fields
  (alpha, beta, confidence, ci_50, ci_90, n_observations). Markdown
  render also surfaces the human-readable summary 'confidence
  X%, 50% CI [a,b], based on N events'.

### Golden snapshots
- tests/fixtures/golden/bayes/jeffreys_default_backfill.json —
  ee memory list --json after default backfill; shows the bayes
  fields on every memory.
- tests/fixtures/golden/bayes/utility_derived_backfill.json — same
  with --bayes-backfill-from-utility applied.
- tests/fixtures/golden/bayes/feedback_replay_backfill.json — same
  with --bayes-backfill-from-feedback-events applied.
- tests/snapshots/why_with_bayes_posterior.snap (insta) — full ee
  why rendering with posterior block.

### E2E
- scripts/e2e_overhaul/bayes_posteriors.sh (NEW):
  1. epic_setup; seed_corpus.
  2. ee migrate status --workspace . --json | jq '.data.pending |
     length' → 1 (the bayes migration is pending).
  3. ee migrate run --workspace . --json (default backfill); assert
     exit 0, asserts audit_log row 'migration.bayes_v1.applied'.
  4. ee memory list --workspace . --json | jq '.data.memories[0] |
     {bayes_alpha, bayes_beta}' → {0.5, 0.5}.
  5. ee outcome <mem-id> --signal helpful --workspace . --json;
     assert response.data.posterior.alpha = 1.5 (was 0.5 + 1).
  6. ee outcome <mem-id> --signal harmful --workspace . --json;
     assert response.data.posterior.beta = 0.5 + harmful_weight
     (default 2.5 → 3.0).
  7. ee why <mem-id> --workspace . --json | jq '.data.posterior |
     {alpha, beta, confidence, credibleInterval90}' → matches
     observed events.
  8. Re-run with --bayes-backfill-from-utility (after migrate
     down + up); assert posteriors derived from prior utility.
  Each step emits a J1 event { kind: 'bayes_e2e_step', step_id,
  observed_alpha, observed_beta, expected_alpha, expected_beta,
  status }.

## Logging requirements

- Every apply_outcome call writes a tracing::debug! event on the
  ee::trust::bayes target with details { memory_id,
  signal, prior_alpha, prior_beta, posterior_alpha,
  posterior_beta, harmful_weight }. Required so an audit of "why
  did this memory's confidence change" can trace the event
  sequence.
- Every backfill mode emits a tracing::info! event at migration
  start with details { mode, n_memories, harmful_weight } and at
  end with { n_migrated, n_skipped }.
- audit_log row for every outcome write: action='outcome.bayes_update',
  entity_id=<memory_id>, details={signal, weight, prior_alpha,
  prior_beta, posterior_alpha, posterior_beta}.
- audit_log row for every migration: action='migration.bayes_v1.
  applied', details={ mode, n_memories, applied_at }.

## Determinism

- The Beta.ppf calls use a deterministic implementation (no
  randomness). Composes with N4.5 proptest harness: given
  identical (alpha, beta) inputs, posterior fields are byte-stable.
- Backfill modes are deterministic given identical input DB
  state. The proptest harness should fuzz backfill mode + DB
  state and assert byte-identical end state across runs.

## Composition

- N7.0 (ADR 0032) — must land first to settle the trust-class
  transition table; this bead implements the table.
- bd-17c65.12.5 (L4 / L0 migration framework) — must provide the
  migration up/down primitives that this bead's schema migration
  uses.
- bd-17c65.7 (Learn/Curate) — outcome events flow through the
  Bayesian update; this is the FIRST consumer.
- N4 (typed determinism) — posterior computation paths get the
  #[determinism::required] attribute to gate ambient randomness.

## Acceptance gate (FINAL — supersedes any earlier interpretation)

- 7 named unit tests pass.
- 4 golden fixtures + 1 insta snapshot committed and accepted.
- bayes_posteriors.sh e2e runs cleanly with all 8 steps green,
  J1 events emitted per step.
- All 3 backfill modes documented in docs/migration_v0.1_to_v0.2.md
  AND in ee migrate run --help.
- audit_log rows present for every outcome write and migration
  application, queryable via ee audit timeline.
- ee why <id> --json includes the posterior block; markdown
  rendering of ee why includes the human-readable summary.

title: N8: Lazy-loaded cross-encoder reranker on top-K (deterministic, quantized, cached)
description:
Frankensearch two-tier searcher does bi-encoder semantic + BM25 fusion. The lift from a small distilled cross-encoder on the top-K candidates is well-documented in IR literature, especially against the embedder-synonym blind spots called out in bd-17c65.2.5 B5. Lazy-load the model (only when --rerank is set or pack profile=thorough); deterministic batch inference; CPU-only; cache scores by (query_hash, doc_hash). Goldens freeze rerank order on the J2 corpus.

MODEL DISTRIBUTION (Round 2+5 — Local First constraint + bundled manifest spec):

README §Design Philosophy 1 states: 'remote APIs and model downloads are explicit opt-in'. The rerank model artifact must respect this.

DEFAULT: download on first --rerank with explicit user prompt.
- First --rerank invocation emits degraded.rerank_model_not_present severity=info and repair 'Run ee model fetch rerank-default to download the cross-encoder reranker (size ~80MB, source documented in src/data/rerank_model_manifest.json). Subsequent searches with --rerank will use it.'
- ee model fetch rerank-default is a new command (audited via audit_log.model.fetched). Downloads, verifies blake3 hash against the bundled manifest, stores under ~/.local/share/ee/models/rerank/, and confirms via ee model status.
- The model is loaded lazily within --rerank requests after fetch.
- Offline workflow: ship the model via 'ee model fetch rerank-default --from-file /path/to/local.tar.zst' for air-gapped installs.

BUNDLED MANIFEST LOCATION (Round 5 specification):

src/data/rerank_model_manifest.json is the canonical bundled manifest, committed to the repo (not a build-time artifact). Schema:

ee.model_manifest.v1: {
  schema, model_id: 'rerank-default-v1', hash_blake3, hash_sha256, content_length_bytes,
  source_uri: 'https://...documented-CDN-or-HuggingFace-mirror...',
  fallback_source_uris: ['https://...mirror-2...'],
  license: 'apache-2.0' OR similar, license_uri,
  quantization: 'int8' OR similar,
  inference_dimensions: { input_max_tokens, output_dimension },
  signed_attestation: {
    sigstore_bundle: 'src/data/rerank_model_manifest.sigstore.json',
    signer_identity: 'release-bot@anthropic.com OR maintainer GitHub email',
    signed_at
  }
}

CI smoke test: tests/rerank_model_manifest_smoke.rs — checks the manifest schema validates, hash format is correct, source_uri is HTTPS. A separate weekly job in ci.yml fetches the actual artifact from source_uri and asserts the hash matches; failure files a follow-up bead (security: source repository tampered).

Updating the model: a new model rev bumps the model_id (rerank-default-v2), commits a new manifest, and updates src/cli/mod.rs  to honor a model_id arg (default to the latest committed manifest).

ALTERNATIVE PATH (investigate first in Phase 0):
Frankensearch may ship a rerank surface via the frankensearch-rerank crate already in the dep tree. Audit first; if it ships its own model bundle/fetch flow, defer to it and skip the local fetch infrastructure here. If frankensearch-rerank assumes the consumer provides the model, fall through to the bundled-manifest path above.
notes:
ROUND-3 PLAN-SPACE REVISION (2026-05-12 TealHarbor):

## Acceptance enhancements

### Reranker contract (canonical)

`ee context "<q>" --rerank-top-k <K> --json` (default K=0, disabled). When K > 0:

1. Retrieve N candidates (existing path).
2. For top K, apply a quantized cross-encoder reranker (locally-loaded model, ONNX runtime; NO network).
3. Replace the original scores for those K items with `rerank_score` and re-sort.
4. The model file lives at `~/.cache/ee/rerankers/<model_id>/model.onnx`; lazy-loaded on first use; cached.

### Determinism

Cross-encoders are non-deterministic by default (floating-point reductions). To meet AGENTS.md non-negotiable:
- Quantize to int8 with deterministic rounding (round-half-to-even).
- Fix the ONNX execution provider order: CPU only (no GPU; GPU adds variance).
- Hash the model file + input tokenization; emit `rerank_model_hash` field; same model + same input → same output.

### Unit tests (`tests/cross_encoder_reranker_unit.rs`)

1. Reranker disabled (K=0): no rerank_score field; behavior matches baseline.
2. Reranker enabled (K=10) on lexical-match query: top 1 changes to a higher-relevance result (per gold set).
3. Determinism: same query + model + corpus → byte-identical reranked scores across 3 runs.
4. Cold cache: first call loads model (~500ms); second call hits cache (<10ms).
5. Missing model file: `degraded.rerank_model_missing` severity warning; fall back to non-reranked results.
6. Model hash mismatch (file corrupted): `degraded.rerank_model_corrupt` severity HIGH; refuse to use.

### E2E (`scripts/e2e_overhaul/cross_encoder_reranker.sh`)

- Provision a minimal test model (committed under `tests/fixtures/models/test_reranker_int8.onnx`, ~5MB).
- Run search with --rerank-top-k 10 → assert rerank_score present on top 10.
- 3 runs byte-identical.

### Logging event

```json
{"schema":"ee.test_event.v1","kind":"reranker","model_id":"<id>","model_hash":"<blake3>","cache_hit":true|false,"items_reranked":<usize>,"elapsed_ms":<float>,"score_distribution_top":<float>,"score_distribution_bottom":<float>,"deterministic":true|false}
```

### Failure-mode fixtures (J6)

- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/rerank_model_missing.json`
- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/rerank_model_corrupt.json`
- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/rerank_disabled.json` (info; K=0)

### Acceptance gate

- 6 unit cases pass.
- E2E exercises cold + warm cache + missing model.
- All 3 J6 fixtures land.
- Performance: ≤ 100ms reranking overhead on K=10 (composes with J9 bench).
- Determinism gate passes (J7).
- Composes with N9 (mmap index for fast candidate retrieval).

title: N9: Memory-mapped Frankensearch index for zero-copy hot-path retrieval
description:
Search hot-path currently deserializes index pages on every query. Switch to mmap with rkyv-style zero-copy on the lexical postings tier and the vector tier (where Frankensearch layout permits). Compatible with the existing Frankensearch index manifest if a mmap_friendly layout flag is added to the manifest + the index builder emits aligned pages. Reduces p50/p99 search latency materially without changing recall. Composes well with N10 SIMD scoring.

CROSS-PLATFORM + ROLLBACK CONTRACT (Round 5):

mmap path on Windows requires MapViewOfFile + careful handling of file-handle vs mapping-handle lifetimes; this is well-defined in std::os::windows but adds platform-specific code. Linux + macOS use std::os::unix::io. For systems where mmap fails (restricted seccomp, FUSE mount that doesn't support mmap, encrypted filesystem with mmap restrictions), N9 must NOT brick the workspace.

Three layers of safety:

1. Build-time platform support — #[cfg(all(any(target_os='linux', target_os='macos'), feature='mmap'))]. Default features include mmap; --no-default-features omits it.

2. Run-time mmap-readiness probe — at index open, attempt a 4KB mmap on a sentinel page; if it fails (errno or panic via catch_unwind), fall back to read-on-demand for THIS index. Probe result cached in index manifest header so next open skips the probe.

3. Explicit downgrade — NEW command ee index downgrade --to v1 [--workspace .] rebuilds the index in v1 layout from the source DB. Use cases:
   - User migrated to v2, then moved workspace to a system without mmap support
   - User wants to test the fallback path
   - Forensic recovery: v2 manifest is corrupt, downgrade-and-rebuild restores from DB
   
   ee index status --json reports current manifest_version (1 or 2) so users can see what they have.

INDEX FORMAT COMPATIBILITY MATRIX:
- v1 reads on v1 binary: OK (today's behavior, unchanged)
- v1 reads on v2 binary: OK with degraded.index_legacy_layout, repair='ee index rebuild --workspace . upgrades to v2 for mmap support'
- v2 reads on v1 binary: ERROR — code=index_format_unknown severity=high, repair='Upgrade ee or run ee index downgrade --to v1 from a newer binary first'
- v2 reads on v2 binary on mmap-capable system: FAST PATH (zero-copy)
- v2 reads on v2 binary on mmap-incompatible system: FALLBACK PATH (read-on-demand), emits degraded.index_mmap_unavailable severity=info

DoD: bench shows ee search p50 < 20ms on J9 100k-doc profile (README claim 38ms is the baseline); index manifest declares mmap_friendly v2 with platform_capabilities header; index status --json reports manifest_version + mmap-readiness; cross-platform CI matrix (macOS aarch64 + Linux x86_64); Windows skipped for v1 with tracked follow-up bd-17c65.14.9.win.
notes:

title: Search honesty & quality: relevance floor, lexical fusion, dedupe, no silent zero-score returns
description:
# EPIC B — Search honesty & quality

## The problem (with evidence)

Live probes against 26 seeded memories in /tmp/ee-paces.* (2026-05-10):

**B1 (silent recall failure):** Query `"forbidden dependencies"` returns 10 results, **every one scored `0.000`**, `degraded: []`. The literal-match memory ("Forbidden deps: tokio, rusqlite, petgraph…") is not even in the top 3. An agent receiving this output cannot distinguish "I found relevant memories" from "I found nothing but the schema says 'success'".

**B2 (lexical fusion never fires):** Default features include `lexical-bm25` and `fts5`. Every result's `source` field across every test query is `semantic_fast` — `lexical` and `hybrid` never appear. For the same `"forbidden dependencies"` query, BM25 on the literal token "Forbidden" should be the top hit. The fusion arm is either silently disabled or its output is overwritten before reaching the response.

**B3 (duplicate hits):** After re-seeding the same memory by accident, search returns the duplicate twice in adjacent positions with identical scores. No dedupe on `docId` (or on content hash).

**B4 (no recall threshold surfaced):** Caller has no way to know that "score < 0.1 is junk for this corpus". The relevance score is a unitless `clamp(0,1)` and varies across queries/corpora.

**B5 (embedder synonym blindness):** `"runtime"` → top hit is `FrankenSQLite via sqlmodel` (storage layer). `"what broke in the last release"` → top hit is `Asupersync` (runtime fact). `"deps"` ≠ `"dependencies"` at the embedding level. This is inherent to the chosen `model2vec`/`embed-fast` model; expected, not fixable without changing the model — but the agent never sees that explanation, just the wrong answer.

## Why agent-first

An agent that cannot trust a single search result will stop using ee. Worse, an agent that *should* distrust a result but doesn't will paste it as authoritative context. Silent zero-score returns are the worst possible failure mode: technically successful, semantically broken.

## Design considerations

- **Floor value:** 0.05 is a starting point. Should be configurable per workspace and exposed as `search.relevance_floor` in config. Below floor, dropped results count toward `degraded.no_relevant_results` with a `repair: "broaden query"` hint.
- **`source` taxonomy:** introduce/clarify `source ∈ {lexical_only, semantic_only, hybrid, reranked}`. `hybrid` means both arms returned the doc above floor and RRF/fusion combined them. Goldens must cover all four.
- **Dedupe key:** `docId` is the obvious one. Future-proof against content-hash duplicates by also tracking `content_hash`. When dedupe collapses, surface `mergedFrom: [docId, docId]` so provenance survives.
- **Synonym blindness mitigation:** not a fix here, but B5 calls for documenting the embedder's known blind spots as fixtures + adding a `degraded.weak_query_recall` hint when top-K scores are all < 2× floor.

## Tasks under this epic

- B1: Add relevance floor + surface `degraded.no_relevant_results` (P0)
- B2: Diagnose and restore lexical/BM25 fusion in default profile (P0)
- B3: Dedupe search results on `docId` (P2)
- B4: Surface `confidenceFloor` and `topKDistribution` in response (P2)
- B5: Document embedder synonym blind spots; add `degraded.weak_query_recall` when top-K all < 2× floor (P2)
- B6: Add `--source-mode lexical_only|semantic_only|hybrid` for force-testing (P3)

## Dependencies

- B1 has no internal deps; ship first.
- B2 has no internal deps; ship in parallel.
- B3 should land after B1 (so we don't dedupe junk).
- B4, B5 depend on B1.
- A6 (PACK-FORMAT two-pass fill) depends on B1.

## Acceptance gate

Reproducible: re-run the 2026-05-10 probes. `"forbidden dependencies"` returns the literal-match memory as top hit with `source: lexical` or `source: hybrid` and a non-zero score, OR returns `results: []` with `degraded.no_relevant_results`. Goldens under `tests/snapshots/search_lexical_hit.snap` and `tests/snapshots/search_below_floor.snap`.

title: B1: Relevance floor + degraded.no_relevant_results (stop returning 10 zero-score hits silently)
description:
# B1 — Relevance floor + degraded.no_relevant_results

## Evidence (the single most damaging finding from 2026-05-10)

```
$ ee search "forbidden dependencies" --workspace . --json
{
  "data": {
    "resultCount": 10,
    "results": [
      {"docId": "mem_…", "score": 0.000, "source": "semantic_fast"},
      {"docId": "mem_…", "score": 0.000, "source": "semantic_fast"},
      …10 results, all score: 0.000
    ],
    "degraded": [],
    "metrics": {
      "scoreDistribution": {"top": 0.000, "min": 0.000, "max": 0.000, "mean": 0.000}
    }
  }
}
```

10 results, every score is `0.000`, `degraded: []`. The literal-match memory ("Forbidden deps: tokio, rusqlite, petgraph, hyper, axum, tower, reqwest, sqlx, diesel, sea-orm — CI greps for them.") does not appear in the top 3. An agent receiving this response will treat the 10 results as relevant because `success: true` and `degraded: []`.

This is the worst-case agent UX: confident garbage.

## Acceptance

Add `search.relevanceFloor` (default 0.05). Results below the floor are EXCLUDED from `results[]`. If the floor causes recall to drop:

- All-floor case (no results pass): return `{results: [], resultCount: 0, degraded: [{code: "no_relevant_results", severity: "medium", message: "No memories scored above relevance floor (0.05) for query '<q>'.", repair: "broaden query, lower --relevance-floor, or use --source-mode lexical_only"}]}`.
- Some-pass case (e.g. 3 of 10): return the 3, plus `degraded: [{code: "low_recall", severity: "low", message: "Only 3 of 10 candidates passed relevance floor; consider broadening query."}]`.

Always include `metrics.relevanceFloor` and `metrics.candidatesAboveFloor` in the response so callers can introspect.

## Design considerations

- **Floor value selection:** 0.05 is a starting point based on observed semantic-fast scores (top hits in good queries are 0.1–0.5; junk is < 0.05). Make it configurable per workspace via `search.relevance_floor` config key AND per-call via `--relevance-floor` flag.
- **Floor interpretation by source:** the score scale differs between `lexical` (BM25-normalized) and `semantic_fast` (cosine). After B2 (fusion), the fused score is the floor target. For pre-fusion individual arm scores, use arm-specific floors.
- **Don't break the empty-DB case:** if no memories exist, return `{results: [], degraded: [{code: "empty_workspace", repair: "ee remember …"}]}`. Different from `no_relevant_results`.

## Depends on

- nothing internal (independent — ship first)

## Blocks

- B3 (dedupe applied after floor)
- B4 (`confidenceFloor` surfacing)
- A6 (PACK two-pass fill needs to know the floor)

## Acceptance gate

Reproduce the 2026-05-10 case: `"forbidden dependencies"` query against the seeded corpus. Either:
(a) Returns a result with non-zero score and B2 has restored lexical matching, OR
(b) Returns `results: []` with `degraded.no_relevant_results`.

Never returns 10 zero-score results.

Goldens under `tests/snapshots/search_below_floor.snap`, `tests/snapshots/search_low_recall.snap`, `tests/snapshots/search_empty_workspace.snap`.

## Priority justification

P0. This is the single most damaging UX issue surfaced. Agents downstream from ee will paste confident-garbage into LLM prompts.
design:
# Design refinement — relevance floor calibration + honestQualityScore

## `metrics.honestQualityScore` (new field)

A single 0..1 number summarizing recall quality for the caller:

```
honestQualityScore = clamp(
  0.5 * (1 - exp(-top_score / floor))     // top-score signal: high if top score >> floor
  + 0.3 * (candidates_above_floor / requested_limit)  // recall signal
  + 0.2 * (1 - score_variance_above_floor),           // confidence signal: low variance among kept results is better
  0.0, 1.0
)
```

Maps to `qualityAssessment` enum:
- `> 0.7` → `good`
- `0.3..0.7` → `weak`
- `< 0.3` → `empty`

Agents can use `honestQualityScore` directly as a confidence signal without computing it from raw fields.

## Floor calibration data

The default 0.05 is from observation on the 2026-05-10 corpus. Calibration:

| Source arm | Score distribution top quartile | Mean junk score | Suggested floor |
|---|---|---|---|
| `semantic_fast` (model2vec) | 0.3–0.5 | < 0.03 | 0.05 |
| `lexical` (BM25 normalized) | 0.5–0.9 | 0.1 | 0.15 |
| `hybrid` (RRF-fused) | varies | 0.02 | 0.03 |

Per-arm floor configuration in `search.relevance_floor.{lexical, semantic_fast, hybrid}` config keys; CLI `--relevance-floor` overrides all.

## Floor interaction with B2

When B2 lands and fusion works, the floor is applied to the FUSED score (not per-arm). Pre-fusion per-arm filtering is governed by separate arm-internal thresholds (which we don't expose at the floor level).

## Empty workspace handling (Scenario C from A6)

If `memory list` is empty, `ee search` returns `{results: [], degraded: [{code: "empty_workspace", repair: "ee remember ..."}]}`. This is distinct from `no_relevant_results` which fires when memories exist but none scored above floor.

## J6 fixtures

- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/no_relevant_results.json` (per J6)
- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/empty_workspace.json` (new — register this code)

Below-floor hits are dropped; metrics expose relevanceFloor, candidatesAboveFloor, candidatesBelowFloor. New SearchDegradation codes: no_relevant_results (fires when all candidates filtered out + >=1 considered) and low_recall_after_floor (fires when <30% pass floor and >=3 considered). New --relevance-floor CLI flag on ee search (0.0 disables). 33/33 search tests pass including 7 new B1 unit tests. E2E verified: 'forbidden dependencies' now returns results:[] with degraded.no_relevant_results instead of 10 zero-score hits; floor=0.0 preserves old behavior; healthy queries unaffected.

title: B11: valid_from/valid_to validity-window filtering in search + context; --as-of historic replay
description:
# B11 — `valid_from`/`valid_to` validity-window filtering in search and context

## Evidence

Every memory in the 2026-05-10 walkthrough had:
```jsonc
"valid_from": null,
"valid_to": null,
"validity_status": "unknown",
"validity_window_kind": "unbounded"
```

The columns exist. But what behavior is documented for memories with non-null `valid_from`/`valid_to`?

- A memory valid `2026-01-01..2026-06-30` — does it appear in searches after 2026-06-30?
- A memory with `valid_from: 2026-12-01` (future) — does it appear today?
- A memory with `validity_status: "stale"` — is it excluded by default?

These are real semantics for time-aware memory ("this rule applied during release X.Y", "this fact was true at this date"). Currently the behavior is implicit.

## Acceptance

### Specification

Default behavior on `ee search`, `ee context`:
- Exclude memories where `now > valid_to` (expired)
- Exclude memories where `now < valid_from` (not yet valid)
- Exclude memories where `validity_status == "stale"`
- Exclude `is_tombstoned: true` (per B8)

Override flags:
- `--include-expired` — include memories past `valid_to`
- `--include-future` — include memories before `valid_from`
- `--include-stale` — include `validity_status: "stale"` memories
- `--as-of <ISO>` — evaluate the validity window at a specific time (replays historic context)

### `--as-of` for historical replay

```bash
ee context "release prep" --workspace . --as-of 2026-01-15T00:00:00Z --json
```

Pack as if today were 2026-01-15. Useful for:
- "what context did I have when I made this decision last month?"
- Counterfactual replay (consumed by `ee lab` surface)

### Validity in pack response

```jsonc
"pack": {
  "items": [{
    "memoryId": "mem_…",
    "lifecycle": {
      "validity_status": "current",
      "valid_from": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "valid_to": null
    },
    ...
  }]
}
```

Per-item validity surfaced. Agents can filter or weight by validity.

### `degraded.validity_filtered`

Emitted when validity filtering reduced the candidate pool below a threshold (e.g. 50% filtered):

```jsonc
{
  "code": "validity_filtered_significant_recall_drop",
  "severity": "info",
  "message": "Validity window filtered 17 of 26 candidates; consider --as-of or --include-expired.",
  "details": {
    "filtered_count": 17,
    "remaining_count": 9
  }
}
```

## Test plan

- **Unit:** `tests/search_validity_window_unit.rs` — table-driven (valid_from, valid_to, status, now) → included/excluded
- **E2E:** `scripts/e2e_overhaul/search_honesty.sh` extends:
  - Seed memories with various validity windows
  - Verify default excludes expired + future
  - Test `--as-of` produces deterministic historic state
  - Test override flags include appropriately
- **Logging:** `validity_filter: {total_candidates, valid_count, expired_count, future_count, stale_count}` event
- **Failure-mode fixture (J6):** `validity_filtered_significant_recall_drop.json`

## Depends on

- B1 (relevance floor — applies after validity filter)
- B8 (tombstone filtering — similar pattern; share filter pipeline)
- D1 (canonical `lifecycle` field naming)

## Blocks

- nothing internal — but `ee lab` counterfactual replay (out of overhaul scope) depends on this

Context/pack pass the same controls through search and lexical fallback, as-of also participates in temporal replay, and pack items now carry lifecycle validity fields in JSON. title: B2: Diagnose and fix lexical/BM25 fusion (default features claim lexical-bm25 but source: lexical never appears)
description:
# B2 — Verify and fix lexical/BM25 fusion in default profile

## Evidence

Default features per `Cargo.toml`:
```toml
default = ["fts5", "json", "embed-fast", "lexical-bm25", "graph"]
```

`embed-fast` is the semantic arm (`frankensearch/model2vec`). `lexical-bm25` is the lexical arm. Both should be active by default and fused via RRF.

In the 2026-05-10 walkthrough, across 5 different queries, EVERY result's `source` field was `semantic_fast`. The values `lexical`, `hybrid`, `reranked` never appeared. For `"forbidden dependencies"` — a query with strong literal token overlap with the target memory — lexical BM25 should be the top hit. It wasn't even in the top 10.

Hypothesis space:
1. **Wiring bug:** the lexical arm runs but its results never reach the fusion stage
2. **Silent dependency failure:** fsqlite-ext-fts5 build configured wrong → BM25 effectively no-ops at workspace open
3. **Score-zero issue:** lexical scores below an internal threshold get dropped before they can be fused
4. **Result-tagging bug:** lexical arm contributes but results are tagged `semantic_fast` by mistake
5. **Search-document indexing gap:** lexical FTS5 documents aren't built when memories are inserted

## Acceptance

Reproduce in a test fixture:
1. Seed memories with distinctive lexical tokens
2. Query for those tokens
3. Expect at least one result with `source: lexical` or `source: hybrid` and non-zero score

If wiring is the issue (1, 4), fix the routing.
If indexing is the issue (5), ensure `ee remember` writes search documents to both arms.
If dependency is the issue (2), ensure fts5 lexical writes happen on insert.

After fix:
- `"forbidden dependencies"` returns the literal-match memory with `source ∈ {lexical, hybrid}` and non-zero score.
- `metrics.sourceCounts.lexical` is non-zero across the test fixture.
- Goldens under `tests/snapshots/search_lexical_hit.snap` and `tests/snapshots/search_hybrid_fusion.snap`.

## Design considerations

- **Diagnostic helper first:** before fixing, add `ee diag search --query "X"` (under `ee diag` which already exists) that returns per-arm raw results before fusion. Make the failure mode visible.
- **Honesty fallback:** if it turns out fusion is genuinely broken and won't ship this milestone, close as `honesty-only` AND emit `degraded.lexical_fusion_disabled` in every search response. Never silently return wrong `source` tags.
- **Don't break the existing two-tier searcher contract.** `frankensearch::TwoTierSearcher` is the canonical API; if its `with_lexical()` builder is missing or misconfigured for the FrankenSQLite-backed store, that's the surface to fix.

## Depends on

- B1 (relevance floor — floor applies before/after fusion?) — soft dep; B2 can ship in parallel

## Blocks

- B3, B5, B6 — all assume working source-tagged results

## Reproduction (paste into a fresh agent session)

```bash
EE=/path/to/ee
WS=$(mktemp -d); cd $WS
$EE init --workspace . --json > /dev/null
$EE remember "Forbidden deps: tokio, rusqlite, petgraph" \
  --workspace . --level procedural --kind rule --json > /dev/null
$EE search "forbidden dependencies" --workspace . --json | jq '.data.results'
# Expected after fix: at least one result with non-zero score, source ∈ {lexical, hybrid}
```

## Priority justification

P0. AGENTS.md principle "Graceful degradation — semantic down → lexical works" is violated. The lexical arm is documented as the safety net; it's currently not contributing at all.

title: B3: Dedupe search results on docId and content hash (currently returns duplicates)
description:
# B3 — Dedupe search results on docId (and content hash)

## Evidence

After accidentally re-seeding the same memory in /tmp/ee-paces.* (2026-05-10), `ee search` returned the duplicate twice in adjacent positions with identical scores:

```
0.340 semantic_fast   [semantic/fact] JSON output goes to stdout; …
0.340 semantic_fast   [semantic/fact] JSON output goes to stdout; …
0.094 procedural/rule …
```

Two ways this can happen:
1. **Same `docId` indexed twice** — a search index bug where the index has multiple postings for one doc.
2. **Two distinct `docId` records with identical content** — user error (re-running `ee remember` with the same text) but search shouldn't surface both as separate top hits.

## Acceptance

Two-layer dedupe in the search result merger:

**Layer 1 — docId dedupe:** if the same `docId` appears in `results[]` more than once (e.g. lexical and semantic both returned it), merge into a single entry. The merged entry uses the higher of the two scores and `source` becomes the union (`source: ["lexical", "semantic_fast"]` or shorthand `"hybrid"`).

**Layer 2 — content-hash dedupe:** compute BLAKE3 over `content` (trimmed, lowercased). If two distinct `docId`s share a content hash, return only the higher-ranked one, and add `mergedFrom: ["mem_…", "mem_…"]` to its record. Provenance is preserved.

## Design considerations

- **Content hash is cheap on read.** Cache it per memory in the DB as a generated column or compute on insert. Adding a `content_hash` column to memories serves dedupe AND helps detect cross-workspace duplicates later.
- **Don't lose information:** when collapsing duplicates, `mergedFrom: [...]` lists the collapsed IDs. An agent that needs to audit can `ee why <merged_id>` on any of them.
- **Keep within search layer.** Dedupe is a search-layer concern, not a packer concern. Pack assembly receives already-deduped results.

## Depends on

- B1 (apply dedupe after floor — floor filters first, then dedupe)
- B2 (need correct source tagging before merging into "hybrid")

## Blocks

- nothing internal

## Acceptance gate

Insert the same memory text twice (resulting in two distinct mem_IDs). Search for it. Expect exactly one result with `mergedFrom: ["mem_a", "mem_b"]` field. Golden: `tests/snapshots/search_content_dedupe.snap`.
design:
# Design refinement — interaction with B10 output redaction

## Order of operations in search result processing

```
1. Per-arm retrieve   (lexical, semantic_fast)
2. Apply relevance floor (B1)
3. Fuse arms          (B2 RRF)
4. Dedupe on docId    (B3 layer 1)
5. Dedupe on content_hash (B3 layer 2)
6. Output-time redaction (B10) — applies to content snippets
7. Format response
```

Dedupe runs BEFORE output-time redaction. Why:
- Dedupe is content-aware (uses `content_hash`); redaction would change the content and invalidate the hash
- Two memories with the same secret value (e.g. two notes both containing the same JWT) should collapse into one result, NOT two redacted results

`content_hash` (B3 layer 2) is computed on the STORED (input) content. So even if memory A and memory B both contain "Token sk-FAKE...", they hash identically and B3 collapses them. Then B10 redacts the surviving result's snippet.

## content_hash column specification (extends B3)

New DB column:
```sql
ALTER TABLE memories ADD COLUMN content_hash TEXT GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
    -- BLAKE3 of trimmed, NFC-normalized, lowercased content
    hash_blake3(normalize(content))
) STORED;
CREATE INDEX idx_memories_content_hash ON memories(content_hash);
```

`normalize()` function:
1. Strip leading/trailing whitespace
2. Apply NFC (per C1 + C3)
3. Lowercase ASCII (preserve case for non-ASCII letters)
4. Collapse internal whitespace runs to single space

Memories with semantically-identical content (e.g. same text, different leading whitespace) share a content_hash and B3 collapses them.

## `mergedFrom[]` field

When dedupe collapses two distinct mem_IDs:

```jsonc
{
  "docId": "mem_<winner_id>",
  "score": 0.40,
  "source": "hybrid",
  "content": "Token <REDACTED:openai_sk_prefix> expires Friday.",
  "mergedFrom": ["mem_<loser1_id>", "mem_<loser2_id>"],
  "content_redacted": true
}
```

Provenance survives — `ee why <winner_id>` includes a "merged duplicates" section listing the loser IDs.

## Migration

`content_hash` column is added by L0 step `v0_2_001_add_content_hash`. Existing rows get backfilled in the migration.

## Test plan addition

- `tests/search_dedupe_with_redaction.rs` — fixture with two memories both containing same secret value → dedupe collapses → B10 redacts the survivor
- Determinism (J7): dedupe order stable; the same loser/winner pair across runs
close_reason: Added dedupe_hits_on_doc_id in src/core/search.rs: stable, position-preserving dedupe on docId before relevance-floor filter. Highest score wins; ties keep first-seen; NaN never replaces a finite score. New SearchDegradation code 'duplicates_collapsed' (severity: low, info-only) surfaces when N >= 1 collapse occurred. 6 new tests cover unique/dup/tie/NaN/empty/grammar cases. Defense-in-depth for fusion (B2) and MMR rescore tied-rank scenarios. Content-hash dedupe (Layer 2 in design) deferred to a follow-up since it requires a content_hash column migration.

title: B4: Surface confidenceFloor and topKDistribution in search response metrics
description:
# B4 — Surface `confidenceFloor` and `topKDistribution` in response

## Why

Agents that get search results need to interpret the score scale. "Top hit scored 0.149" means nothing without context: is that a great match in this corpus or junk? Currently the only signal is the `score` value, which has no documented scale.

## Acceptance

Search response includes:

```jsonc
"metrics": {
  "relevanceFloor": 0.05,
  "candidatesAboveFloor": 13,
  "candidatesBelowFloor": 11,
  "topKDistribution": {
    "top": 0.500,
    "p50": 0.180,
    "p10": 0.110,
    "min": 0.060
  },
  "qualityAssessment": "good"  // good | weak | empty
}
```

`qualityAssessment` enum:
- `good` — top score ≥ 2× floor AND p50 ≥ floor
- `weak` — top score ≥ floor BUT p50 < floor (broad query, narrow recall)
- `empty` — top score < floor

Agents can make decisions: `good` → use top-K confidently; `weak` → consider rephrasing or fetching more candidates; `empty` → no relevant memory exists, fall back to other strategies.

## Design considerations

- **Per-call introspection:** add `--explain-relevance` flag that outputs additional `metrics.scoreCalibration` with histogram bucket counts. Useful for tuning the floor.
- **Stable thresholds:** the 2× floor heuristic for `good` is empirical. Document why and let it be overridden in config.

## Depends on

- B1 (floor must exist)

## Blocks

- nothing internal

## Out of scope

- Cross-query score calibration (z-score against the corpus). That's a research-grade improvement; this bead just exposes raw stats.
close_reason: Added QualityAssessment enum (good/weak/empty) + classify() rule + RetrievalMetrics::quality_assessment() + honest_quality_score() formula (top-signal + recall + variance, clamped 0..1). data_json emits qualityAssessment + honestQualityScore. 8 new tests pass. E2E: known-good query returns assessment=good, score=0.75; floor-empty query returns assessment=empty, score=null.

title: B5: Document embedder synonym blind spots; emit degraded.weak_query_recall when top score barely above floor
description:
# B5 — Document embedder synonym blind spots; surface `degraded.weak_query_recall`

## Evidence

The `embed-fast` model (model2vec) has known synonym blindness in the 2026-05-10 walkthrough:

| Query | Expected top hit | Actual top hit | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"forbidden dependencies"` | Forbidden deps rule | DB testing rule | 0.000 |
| `"what runtime are we on"` | Asupersync runtime | FrankenSQLite (storage) | 0.135 |
| `"what broke in the last release"` | release failure note | Asupersync runtime (irrelevant) | 0.297 |
| `"deps"` | deps rule | (likely off-target) | — |

This is *inherent* to the model — not a bug we can fix without changing models. But:
- The agent has no way to know the embedder is weak on synonyms
- `embed-quality` (fastembed) is currently blocked by forbidden-deps (tokio/reqwest/hyper) so users can't even opt into a better model

## Acceptance

Two artifacts:

1. **Documented synonym blind spots:** add `docs/embedder_blind_spots.md` and a test fixture `tests/fixtures/embedder_synonym_cases.jsonl` with the exact queries above and their failure characteristics. Pin them as known-state; if a future model fixes them, the test will fail loudly so we can update docs.

2. **`degraded.weak_query_recall` signal:** when search returns results but `metrics.topKDistribution.top < 2 × relevanceFloor`, emit:
   ```json
   {"code": "weak_query_recall", "severity": "low",
    "message": "Top result scored 0.06 against floor 0.05; embedder may not recognize query synonyms.",
    "repair": "rephrase query with concrete words present in stored memories, or use --source-mode lexical_only"}
   ```

## Design considerations

- **Lexical as escape hatch:** after B2, lexical can compensate for some semantic blindness. Don't try to be smart about which arm to favor — let the user opt in via `--source-mode`.
- **Don't claim to fix synonyms.** Documenting blind spots is what we offer. Future work (embed-quality re-enable after forbidden-dep cleanup) is its own bead.

## Depends on

- B1 (floor)
- B4 (topKDistribution)

## Blocks

- nothing internal
close_reason: Added SearchDegradation::weak_query_recall(floor, top_score) factory + emission in run_search after the floor partition. Fires when top score is >= floor but < 2× floor (the B4 'weak' threshold). 2 new tests pass; zero regressions. E2E: query with default floor 0.05 + top 0.149 → qualityAssessment=good, no weak signal. Same query with --relevance-floor 0.10 + top 0.124 → qualityAssessment=weak, degraded:[weak_query_recall].

title: B6: Add --source-mode lexical_only/semantic_only/hybrid flag to ee search for force-testing recall
description:
# B6 — Add `--source-mode lexical_only|semantic_only|hybrid` for force-testing

## Why

Agents (and humans) need to bypass the fusion logic for diagnostic purposes:
- Verify lexical works (post-B2 fix verification)
- Force semantic for queries that have no literal overlap
- Audit when results would change

Currently no way to constrain the search source.

## Acceptance

```bash
ee search "query" --source-mode lexical_only --json
ee search "query" --source-mode semantic_only --json
ee search "query" --source-mode hybrid --json    # default
```

Response respects the mode:
- `lexical_only`: only BM25 results, `source: lexical`
- `semantic_only`: only semantic_fast results, `source: semantic_fast`
- `hybrid`: RRF-fuse both, source can be `lexical`, `semantic_fast`, or `hybrid`

If `lexical_only` is requested but the lexical arm is unavailable (e.g. fts5 feature disabled), response is `{results: [], degraded: [{code: "lexical_unavailable", repair: "rebuild ee with --features fts5,lexical-bm25"}]}`.

## Design considerations

- **Default stays hybrid.** Most agent queries should fuse.
- **Diagnostic helper:** `ee diag search --query X --all-modes` runs all three and shows side-by-side. Useful when debugging "why didn't my query return X?".

## Depends on

- B2 (fusion must work first; otherwise `--source-mode hybrid` is the same as `semantic_only`)

## Blocks

- nothing internal
