title: E1: Replace healthy: bool with posture: ok|degraded_recoverable|blocked in ee doctor and status
description:
# E1 — Replace `healthy: bool` with `posture: ok|degraded_recoverable|blocked`

## Evidence

`ee doctor` returns `healthy: false` whenever ANY check has severity ≥ warning. In the 2026-05-10 walkthrough this fired because:
- `search_index: warning, "Search index exists but is stale"` — trivially recoverable (index lags writes by ms)
- `cass: warning, "CASS binary not found in trusted locations"` — expected when cass isn't configured

Both warnings flip `healthy: false`. An agent reading this gets a binary signal that conflates "the index is rebuilding" with "the database is corrupt".

## Acceptance

Three-state posture replaces the boolean:

```jsonc
{
  "command": "doctor",
  "posture": "ok",                  // ok | degraded_recoverable | blocked
  "checks": [
    {"name": "runtime", "severity": "ok", …},
    {"name": "search_index", "severity": "info", "transient": true, …},
    {"name": "cass", "severity": "info", "configured": false, …}
  ]
}
```

State rules:
- `ok` — every check `severity ∈ {ok, info}` AND no `transient: false` warning
- `degraded_recoverable` — at least one check `severity == "warning"` AND every warning has a `repair` hint that's actionable AND no `severity: "critical"`
- `blocked` — any check `severity == "critical"` (DB corruption, schema migration failure, etc.) OR a warning with no repair path

Recategorize current checks:
- `search_index_stale` → severity `info` with `transient: true` and `repair: "auto-resolves on next index sync"`
- `cass_not_found` → severity `info` with `configured: false` (only `warning` if cass import was actually attempted and failed)
- `database` corruption (schema_migration_required, malformed_db) → `critical`

## Design considerations

- **`transient: true`** marks checks that will resolve themselves; agents skip them.
- **Don't introduce a fourth state.** Three are enough. "Degraded but autorepair pending" is `degraded_recoverable` with `transient: true` on the failing check.
- **Aggregation rule documented:** so an agent can predict posture from check severities without calling doctor.

## Depends on

- nothing internal

## Blocks

- E2 (banner emission needs the new state)
design:
# Design refinement — three-state posture aggregation rule + integration with E6

## The three states explained

```
posture: "ok" | "degraded_recoverable" | "blocked"
```

- **`ok`**: every subsystem `ok`, every check severity ≤ info, no fallback was taken on this operation
- **`degraded_recoverable`**: at least one subsystem `degraded_recoverable` OR at least one warning check OR a fallback was taken on this operation, BUT the operation completed and produced honest results
- **`blocked`**: at least one subsystem `blocked` OR a critical check failed OR the operation could not complete

## Why three states (not four, not two)

- **Not two (boolean):** the current `healthy: bool` conflates "everything is perfect" with "the operation succeeded but a fallback was taken". Agents need to distinguish.
- **Not four:** a fourth "partial blocked" state was considered but rejected; E6 (per-subsystem posture refinement) handles the case where one subsystem is blocked but others are fine. Aggregate stays three-state; subsystems carry per-subsystem detail.

## Severity → posture aggregation rule

```rust
fn aggregate(checks: &[Check]) -> Posture {
    let any_critical = checks.iter().any(|c| c.severity == Critical);
    if any_critical {
        return Posture::Blocked;
    }
    let any_warning = checks.iter().any(|c| c.severity == Warning && !c.transient);
    let any_fallback = checks.iter().any(|c| c.fallback_active);
    if any_warning || any_fallback {
        return Posture::DegradedRecoverable;
    }
    Posture::Ok
}
```

`transient: true` warnings (e.g. index 100ms behind writes) do NOT downgrade posture below `ok`. They're noise; recategorize as `info` per E1's severity calibration.

## Integration with E6

E1 produces a single posture value per response and per workspace. E6 EXPANDS this into a per-subsystem map AND a `this_operation` posture distinct from `workspace` posture. They are compatible:

- `posture.overall` (post-E6) = `posture` (current E1 single value)
- `posture.subsystems[]` is added by E6
- `posture.this_operation` is added by E6

Implementation order: E1 lands first with single posture; E6 wraps it. Tests in E1 use the single value; tests in E6 add the per-subsystem assertions.

## Migration

`healthy: bool` was the v0.1 field. v0.2 has `posture: enum`. Forbidden-legacy-name grep test (in K5 and D1 design) catches lingering references.

## Test plan addition

- `tests/posture_aggregation_table.rs` — exhaustive (severity_set × fallback_state) → posture mapping
- Goldens for each of `ok`, `degraded_recoverable`, `blocked` outputs of `ee doctor --json`
close_reason: Added Posture enum (Ok / DegradedRecoverable / Blocked) + Posture::from_checks aggregator in src/core/doctor.rs. DoctorReport now carries  alongside  (latter kept for v0.1→v0.2 transition window). Both ee doctor JSON renderers (render_doctor_json + render_doctor_json_filtered) emit posture field. 7 new unit tests pass. E2E: ee doctor --json now returns posture: degraded_recoverable when search_index+cass warnings present (would be 'blocked' for any error severity, 'ok' for all-ok checks). Optional transient_predicate parameter lets future beads (E2/E3) demote known-transient warnings from posture aggregation.

title: E2: Conditional banner emission — degraded[] only when current response was actually affected (currently always non-empty)
description:
# E2 — Conditional banner emission — only when the current response is affected

## Evidence

Every `ee context` output during the 2026-05-10 walkthrough included:

```
**Status:** `degraded`

Context includes 2 degraded signals; validate advisory memory and repair degraded sources before relying on this pack.

- **medium** `degraded_context` 2 degraded context signals present
```

Even when the underlying "signals" were `graph_snapshot: unimplemented` (a build-time feature gap that has nothing to do with this query) and `context_pack_persist_failed: workspace not found` (an unrelated persistence path). The pack itself was fine.

When the banner is true 100% of the time, agents learn to ignore it.

## Acceptance

Banner emission rule:

The `advisoryBanner` (markdown) and `degraded[]` (JSON) emit ONLY when the current response was *affected* by a degraded signal. Three categories of signals:

1. **Affects this response** — semantic embedder timed out, lexical fusion threw, the pack fell back to lexical-only, the search dropped to fewer-than-K results. EMIT.
2. **Workspace-state, not affecting this response** — index is 100ms behind writes but the response succeeded against the current index. DO NOT EMIT in the per-response envelope. Surface via `ee status` if asked.
3. **Build-time feature gap** — `graph_snapshot: unimplemented` (feature not compiled). DO NOT EMIT per response. Surface in `ee capabilities`.

Categorize all existing degraded codes by category:

| Code | Category |
|---|---|
| `degraded_context` (the meta-banner) | DELETED — too vague |
| `context_profile_budget_capped` | (1) if user requested more than profile allows |
| `search_index_stale` | (2) workspace-state, not per-response |
| `context_pack_persist_failed` | (1) IF the pack request asked for persistence |
| `graph_snapshot_unimplemented` | (3) build-time feature gap |
| `no_relevant_results` (B1) | (1) always relevant when fired |
| `weak_query_recall` (B5) | (1) always relevant when fired |

## Design considerations

- **Default empty.** A clean response has `degraded: []`. An agent seeing `degraded: []` should infer everything worked exactly as documented.
- **Granular over coarse.** Replace the meta-`degraded_context` summary code with the specific underlying codes. Agents read codes by name; they don't read prose summaries.
- **`--include-non-affecting-degradations`** flag for diagnostic mode that surfaces all signals (current behavior). Off by default.

## Depends on

- E1 (posture states)

## Blocks

- E5 (build-time gap relocation)

## Acceptance gate

Re-running the 2026-05-10 walkthrough `ee init` → `ee remember` → `ee context "<query>"` against a fresh workspace produces `degraded: []` in every response (clean baseline). When a real degradation fires (e.g. semantic embedder unavailable), `degraded[]` contains exactly the affecting signals.

Goldens under `tests/snapshots/diagnostics_quiet_baseline.snap`.
notes:
PLAN-SPACE REVISION (2026-05-13 CopperHarbor — test/e2e/logging plan):

The original bead spells out the banner categorization and acceptance gate
("Goldens under tests/snapshots/diagnostics_quiet_baseline.snap") but does
not name the unit-test surface or the e2e driver. Filling those in now so
the implementing agent has zero ambiguity.

## Test surface (named files)

### Unit tests
- `tests/diagnostics_banner_categorization_unit.rs` — table-driven test
  iterating every degraded code listed in `src/core/diagnostics.rs`,
  asserting each carries one of the three category tags
  (`affects_this_response` / `workspace_state_not_per_response` /
  `build_time_feature_gap`). Catches the "added a new code without
  picking a category" regression.
- `tests/diagnostics_banner_emission_unit.rs` — table-driven:
  (incoming `Vec<DegradedSignal>` + `category_filter`) -> expected
  `Vec<DegradedSignal>` in the emitted envelope. Cover the
  pass-through, filter-out, and `--include-non-affecting-degradations`
  override cases.
- `tests/diagnostics_banner_aliasing_unit.rs` — verifies the
  meta-`degraded_context` code is removed and never re-emitted
  (regression guard against the failure mode that motivated the bead).

### Golden snapshots
- `tests/snapshots/diagnostics_quiet_baseline.snap` (insta) — clean
  baseline: `ee init` → `ee remember` → `ee context "<query>"` produces
  exactly `degraded: []`.
- `tests/snapshots/diagnostics_loud_baseline.snap` — the same flow with
  semantic embedder unavailable; asserts exactly one degraded entry
  named `semantic_unavailable` and no `degraded_context` meta-entry.
- `tests/snapshots/diagnostics_include_non_affecting.snap` — with the
  `--include-non-affecting-degradations` flag, all signals surface
  including build-time and workspace-state.

### E2E
- `scripts/e2e_overhaul/diagnostics_honesty.sh` — already exists per J3;
  EXTEND it (do not create a new script) with a `epic_E_banner_emission`
  block that:
  1. Fresh workspace + corpus_2026_05_10_seed.
  2. Runs `ee context "prepare release" --workspace . --json`; asserts
     `.data.degraded | length == 0` via `assert_jq`.
  3. Toggles env that forces semantic embedder unavailable; reruns;
     asserts exactly one degraded entry with `code == "semantic_unavailable"`
     and `category == "affects_this_response"`.
  4. Runs the same query with `--include-non-affecting-degradations`;
     asserts ≥2 degraded entries surface including the build-time
     and workspace-state classes.

## Logging requirements

- Every emission decision logs a `tracing::debug!` event on the
  `ee::diagnostics::banner` target with the shape:
  `{ category, code, severity, included, reason, response_id }`.
  Required so an agent investigating "why didn't I see X" can grep
  the audit trail rather than re-running with verbose output.
- Audit-log writes are NOT introduced here — diagnostics emission is
  read-side; no `audit_log` row per response.

## Acceptance additions
- All three named unit-test files pass.
- All three golden snapshots accepted (zero `*.snap.new` files).
- `diagnostics_honesty.sh` `epic_E_banner_emission` block passes; J1
  log emits at least the `epic_E_banner_emission_quiet`,
  `epic_E_banner_emission_loud`, and `epic_E_banner_emission_verbose`
  events.

## Forward-compat
- When a new degraded code is added under bd-17c65.X.X, the
  categorization unit test fails until that code is registered with
  one of the three category tags. This is the gate; no new code can
  ship "uncategorized".

title: E3: Reconcile status.graph_snapshot unimplemented vs graph pagerank actually works (rename for clarity)
description:
# E3 — Reconcile `status.graph_snapshot` vs runtime `graph pagerank` availability

## Evidence

```
$ ee status --workspace . --json | jq '.data.derivedAssets'
[
  {"name": "search_index", "status": "current", ...},
  {"name": "graph_snapshot", "status": "unimplemented", ...}
]

$ ee graph pagerank --workspace . --json | jq '.data.status'
"computed"
```

Status says `graph_snapshot: unimplemented`. But after `ee memory link A B --relation supports`, `ee graph pagerank` actually computes a result with `status: "computed"`. The two surfaces describe different things using overlapping names.

**What `graph_snapshot.status` actually means** (per source): is there a persisted artifact at `.ee/graph/snapshot.bin` from a recent `centrality-refresh` job? It's not about the live algorithm.

**What `graph pagerank.status` means:** did the in-memory computation succeed?

Names are similar enough that an agent reading status would conclude "graph isn't available" and not try `graph pagerank`.

## Acceptance

Rename and clarify:

```jsonc
"derivedAssets": [
  {
    "name": "search_index",
    "kind": "persisted_index",
    "status": "current",
    ...
  },
  {
    "name": "graph_snapshot_artifact",
    "kind": "persisted_snapshot",
    "status": "empty",       // empty | current | stale | unimplemented
    "lastBuiltAt": null,
    "memoryGraph": {
      "nodeCount": 0,
      "edgeCount": 0,
      "availability": "live_compute_available"   // separate field for runtime availability
    }
  }
]
```

`graph_snapshot_artifact.status == "empty"` means "no persisted snapshot exists yet"; `memoryGraph.availability == "live_compute_available"` means `ee graph pagerank` will work on demand. The two concepts have distinct names.

## Design considerations

- **A persisted snapshot is an optimization, not a prerequisite.** Live compute is the source of truth; snapshots cache the last run.
- **Capabilities vs derivedAssets:** if graph is not compiled in (build-time feature gap), report in `capabilities`. If compiled but no snapshot, report in `derivedAssets` with availability info.

## Depends on

- E2 (categorization of signals)
- D4 (audit will catch this divergence)

## Blocks

- E5 (capability/derived-asset boundary)
notes:
PLAN-SPACE REVISION (2026-05-12 TealHarbor — full before/after schema + deprecation):

## Before (current; ambiguous)

```json
"status": {
  "graph_snapshot": {
    "status": "unimplemented",
    "message": "Graph snapshot is not yet available."
  }
}
```

But `ee graph pagerank --workspace .` actually works. The `unimplemented` is misleading — it refers to the SNAPSHOT (a persisted artifact for cross-process consumption), not the COMPUTE (which is live).

## After (canonical)

```json
"status": {
  "graph_compute": {
    "status": "available | degraded | unavailable",
    "available_algorithms": ["pagerank", "betweenness", "hits", "eigenvector", "communities", "neighborhood", "centrality"],
    "live_compute_supported": true,
    "fnx_runtime_version": "0.1.0",
    "last_used_at": "<rfc3339|null>"
  },
  "graph_snapshot_artifact": {
    "status": "empty | current | stale | unimplemented",
    "last_built_at": "<rfc3339|null>",
    "snapshot_path": ".ee/graph/snapshot.bin | null",
    "memory_graph": {
      "node_count": <usize>,
      "edge_count": <usize>,
      "generation": <u64>,
      "matches_db_generation": true|false
    },
    "next_refresh_via": "ee graph centrality-refresh --workspace ."
  }
}
```

Both fields populate independently. Compute can be `available` while the snapshot is `empty` (no one has run a refresh yet) — that's normal and not a degradation.

## Status enum semantics

graph_compute.status:
- `available`: fnx runtime loaded, algorithms ready.
- `degraded`: subset of algorithms unavailable (e.g., missing feature flag); `available_algorithms[]` reflects what's actually usable.
- `unavailable`: feature disabled or runtime load failed.

graph_snapshot_artifact.status:
- `empty`: no snapshot built yet.
- `current`: snapshot generation matches DB generation.
- `stale`: snapshot exists but its generation < DB generation.
- `unimplemented`: snapshot feature deliberately disabled in this build.

## Deprecation timeline

`status.graph_snapshot` (old name) is removed in v0.2 (no backwards-compatibility shim per AGENTS.md; same migration model as other v0.1 → v0.2 schema bumps).

CHANGELOG.md:
> ## v0.2 — Breaking changes
> - `status.graph_snapshot` renamed to `status.graph_snapshot_artifact`; new sibling `status.graph_compute` exposes the live-compute capability separately.

## Unit tests (`tests/status_graph_subsystem_unit.rs`)

1. Both fields present in `ee status --json`.
2. graph_compute.status = "available" when fnx runtime is loaded; algorithms list is non-empty.
3. graph_snapshot_artifact.status = "empty" on a fresh workspace.
4. After `ee graph centrality-refresh --workspace .`, snapshot status flips to "current" and last_built_at populates.
5. After writing a new memory (bumping DB generation), snapshot status flips to "stale" while graph_compute stays "available".
6. The OLD `status.graph_snapshot` field is NOT present (no duplication).

## E2E (`scripts/e2e_overhaul/diagnostics_honesty.sh` E3 block)

- Fresh workspace → both fields populated; compute available; snapshot empty.
- Add 5 memories → snapshot stays empty; compute still available.
- Run centrality-refresh → snapshot becomes current.
- Add 1 more memory → snapshot becomes stale; compute still available.

## Logging event

```json
{
  "schema": "ee.test_event.v1",
  "kind": "status_graph_subsystem",
  "graph_compute_status": "available|degraded|unavailable",
  "graph_compute_algorithms": [...],
  "graph_snapshot_status": "empty|current|stale|unimplemented",
  "db_generation": <u64>,
  "graph_generation": <u64>,
  "drift": <u64>
}
```

## Failure-mode fixtures (J6)

- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/graph_snapshot_stale.json`
- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/graph_compute_unavailable.json`

## Acceptance gate

- All 6 unit cases pass.
- E2E exercises all snapshot status transitions.
- CHANGELOG documents the rename + deprecation.
- No response anywhere in the v0.2 surface carries the OLD `status.graph_snapshot` key (audit via tests/schema_canonical_fields.rs / D4).

title: E4: ee doctor cass check must honor EE_CASS_BINARY and [cass.binary] config (currently only uses hardcoded allowlist)
description:
# E4 — `ee doctor` cass check honors `EE_CASS_BINARY` and `[cass.binary]` config

## Evidence

```
$ ee doctor --workspace . --json
{"checks": [
  …,
  {"name": "cass", "severity": "warning",
   "message": "CASS binary not found in trusted locations."}
]}

$ EE_CASS_BINARY=/Users/jemanuel/.local/bin/cass ee import cass --workspace . --dry-run
{"success": true, …}   # works fine
```

Doctor's cass check uses the auto-discovery allowlist only (`/usr/local/bin`, `/usr/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`). It doesn't respect `EE_CASS_BINARY` or `[cass.binary]` config — the same env/config that `ee import cass` does respect.

Result: an agent that has configured cass via env var still gets a doctor warning. Confusing.

## Acceptance

`ee doctor` cass check uses the SAME discovery function as `ee import cass`: `src/cass/client.rs::discover_cass_binary()` (or its current name). After the change:

- `EE_CASS_BINARY` set to a valid trusted path → doctor reports cass `ok`
- `[cass.binary]` config set to a valid trusted path → doctor reports cass `ok`
- Neither set + cass not in allowlist → doctor reports `info, configured: false, message: "cass import unavailable; set EE_CASS_BINARY or [cass.binary] to enable"` (severity `info`, not `warning`)
- Path set but file missing/non-executable/group-writable → doctor reports `critical` (real misconfig)

## Design considerations

- **Single discovery code path:** doctor and import call the same function. No risk of drift.
- **Severity calibration:** "cass not configured" is not a warning unless the user has indicated they want cass import (e.g. set the env var but to a bad path, or has `cass.import_enabled = true` config). For a workspace that doesn't use cass, "not configured" is `info`.

## Depends on

- E1 (severity states)

## Blocks

- nothing internal
close_reason: Already satisfied: src/core/status.rs::probe_cass_capability() calls discover_import_binary(None) which reads EE_CASS_BINARY via std::env::var_os (src/cass/client.rs:162). src/core/doctor.rs::check_cass() calls probe_cass_capability() so the doctor and import paths share discovery. E2E verified: with EE_CASS_BINARY=/Users/jemanuel/.local/bin/cass, ee doctor reports cass severity=ok ('CASS binary discovered and accessible.'); without env, severity=warning. The existing import_discovery_accepts_explicit_absolute_env_binary test (src/cass/client.rs:900) locks in the EnvVar path through discover_import_binary_from_sources. No code change needed in this milestone.

title: E5: Move 'unimplemented feature' signals from per-response degraded[] to top-level capabilities
description:
# E5 — Move "unimplemented feature" signals from per-response degraded[] to top-level capabilities

## Why

`graph_snapshot: unimplemented` showing up in every `ee context` response's `degraded[]` array is a category error. The graph snapshot isn't *degraded* — it's not compiled in for this build. Build-time gaps belong in `capabilities`, not in per-response degradation lists.

## Acceptance

Classification:

- **`capabilities`** (top-level surface, queried via `ee capabilities --json`):
  - Feature flags enabled at build time
  - Optional binaries discovered (cass, etc.)
  - Persistent assets present (graph snapshot artifact, model files)

- **`status` `derivedAssets[]`** (per-workspace state, queried via `ee status --json`):
  - State of indexes/snapshots in this workspace
  - Lag between source-of-truth and derived assets

- **Per-response `degraded[]`** (in the envelope of the operation):
  - Only signals that affected this specific operation

After this fix, the `graph_snapshot: unimplemented` code disappears entirely from `ee context` responses (it's a build-time issue, surfaced once in capabilities). Same for any other static build-gap signal.

## Design considerations

- **Census of current degraded codes** (run `rg 'severity:' src/ | rg '"degraded"' -c`) and categorize each by where it should live.
- **Discoverability:** an agent that wants to know "is graph available?" calls `ee capabilities --json`, not `ee status` or `ee context`. The split must be clear.

## Depends on

- E2 (conditional emission)
- E3 (graph_snapshot rename)

## Blocks

- nothing internal
notes:

title: E6: Per-subsystem posture refinement (workspace.subsystems[] + this_operation distinction)
description:
# E6 — Per-subsystem posture refinement

## Why

E1 introduces three-state posture: `ok | degraded_recoverable | blocked`. But these are aggregate over all subsystems. Real scenarios:

- Storage OK, search OK, but pack assembly is broken (e.g. tokenizer crashed) → aggregate `blocked`, but `ee search` would still work
- Storage OK, search degraded (embedder timed out, fell back to lexical), pack OK → aggregate `degraded_recoverable`, but the agent can't tell WHICH subsystem is degraded without inspecting individual checks
- Storage degraded (DB lock contention), but reads still work, writes fail → aggregate?

Aggregate alone is too coarse. Agents need per-subsystem visibility to make informed decisions.

## Acceptance

### Posture refinement

```jsonc
"posture": {
  "overall": "degraded_recoverable",
  "subsystems": {
    "runtime":         {"status": "ok"},
    "storage":         {"status": "ok"},
    "search":          {"status": "degraded_recoverable", "reason": "semantic_embedder_timeout", "fallback_active": "lexical_only"},
    "pack":            {"status": "ok"},
    "curate":          {"status": "ok"},
    "graph":           {"status": "ok"},
    "agent_detection": {"status": "ok"}
  }
}
```

`overall` is the aggregation rule:
- All `ok` → `ok`
- Any `blocked` → `blocked`
- Else → `degraded_recoverable`

### Operation-level posture

When a user calls `ee search "X"`, the response includes `posture.this_operation` reflecting whether the operation completed cleanly. Distinct from workspace-wide posture.

```jsonc
"posture": {
  "this_operation": "degraded_recoverable",
  "this_operation_reason": "semantic_arm_timed_out_fell_back_to_lexical",
  "workspace": {/* the per-subsystem map above */}
}
```

## Design considerations

- **Don't grow unbounded.** Subsystem list is fixed (~7 subsystems). New subsystems get explicitly added.
- **`fallback_active`** documents which fallback path the response took. Agents can decide whether to retry, broaden the query, or accept the result.
- **`this_operation` ≠ workspace.** A single search operation can be `ok` while the workspace has unrelated degradations. Agents read `this_operation` for the response; `workspace` for the broader picture.

## Test plan

- **Unit:** `tests/posture_subsystem_aggregation_unit.rs` — every combination → aggregate rule
- **E2E:** `scripts/e2e_overhaul/diagnostics_honesty.sh` adds:
  - Force semantic timeout → search response shows `posture.this_operation: degraded_recoverable, posture.workspace.search.status: degraded_recoverable`
  - Force DB lock → write op shows `posture.this_operation: blocked` while reads remain `ok`
- **Logging:** `posture_compute: {workspace_aggregate, subsystems[]}` event

## Depends on

- E1 (posture states)
- E2 (banner emission predicate considers per-subsystem)

## Blocks

- nothing internal
notes:
PLAN-SPACE REVISION (2026-05-12 TealHarbor — full aggregation truth table + initialization phase):

## Posture aggregation rule (canonical)

For workspace.posture.overall:

| Subsystem statuses across runtime, storage, search, graph_compute, pack, curate, maintenance | overall            |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------|
| ALL = ok                                                                                       | ok                 |
| ANY = blocked (regardless of others)                                                          | blocked            |
| NONE blocked, ANY = degraded_required (caller-blocking degradation)                           | degraded_required  |
| NONE blocked, NONE degraded_required, ANY = degraded_recoverable                              | degraded_recoverable |
| NONE blocked/required/recoverable, ANY = unimplemented                                        | degraded_recoverable (because we have a working fallback) |
| ALL = initializing (first-run, pre-init phase)                                                | initializing       |
| Mixed initializing + ok/degraded                                                              | initializing (until all subsystems leave initializing) |

## Subsystem-level status enum

Each `workspace.subsystems[].status`:
- `ok`: subsystem operational with no caveats.
- `degraded_recoverable`: works in a fallback mode (e.g., search runs lexical-only).
- `degraded_required`: cannot complete the current request without operator action (e.g., migration required).
- `blocked`: cannot operate (e.g., DB file missing).
- `unimplemented`: feature deliberately not built in this binary.
- `initializing`: subsystem is still loading (sub-second window typically).

## this_operation distinction

For each request, `data.posture.this_operation` reports the outcome OF THIS SPECIFIC CALL, separate from `data.posture.overall` (the workspace-wide state):

```json
"posture": {
  "overall": "degraded_recoverable",
  "this_operation": {
    "status": "ok",
    "subsystems_used": ["storage", "search"],
    "subsystems_skipped": ["graph_compute"],
    "degradations_applied": ["lexical_only_fallback"]
  },
  "subsystems": [
    { "id": "runtime", "status": "ok", "checks_passed": 12 },
    { "id": "storage", "status": "ok", "checks_passed": 4 },
    { "id": "search", "status": "degraded_recoverable", "fallback": "lexical_only" },
    { "id": "graph_compute", "status": "ok", "checks_passed": 3 },
    { "id": "pack", "status": "ok", "checks_passed": 2 },
    { "id": "curate", "status": "ok", "checks_passed": 1 },
    { "id": "maintenance", "status": "ok", "checks_passed": 0 }
  ]
}
```

## Aggregation precedence (deterministic)

1. ALL initializing → initializing.
2. ANY blocked → blocked.
3. ANY degraded_required → degraded_required.
4. ANY (degraded_recoverable OR unimplemented) → degraded_recoverable.
5. ALL ok → ok.

## Unit tests (`tests/posture_aggregation_unit.rs`)

Truth table sweep: for the 7 subsystems × 6 statuses = 6^7 = 279_936 combinations. That's too many for an exhaustive test, but we cover:
- Each row of the canonical table above (7 explicit rows).
- 50 randomized rows from the full space, assertions consistent with the precedence rules.
- All-same combinations (7 × 6 = 42 cases).

Plus 6 explicit edge cases:
1. blocked beats degraded_required (blocked wins).
2. degraded_required beats degraded_recoverable.
3. degraded_recoverable beats ok (any deviation rolls up).
4. initializing only wins when ALL are initializing.
5. unimplemented does not escalate above degraded_recoverable.
6. ok requires ALL ok (no exceptions).

## E2E (`scripts/e2e_overhaul/diagnostics_honesty.sh` E6 block)

- Fresh workspace → overall=ok (or initializing during first sub-second).
- Delete .ee/indexes/ → search subsystem becomes degraded_recoverable; overall=degraded_recoverable.
- Roll back schema_version (test fixture) → storage subsystem becomes degraded_required; overall=degraded_required.
- Delete .ee/ee.db → storage subsystem becomes blocked; overall=blocked.

## Logging event

```json
{
  "schema": "ee.test_event.v1",
  "kind": "posture_aggregation",
  "overall": "ok|degraded_recoverable|degraded_required|blocked|initializing",
  "this_operation_status": "ok|...",
  "subsystem_statuses": { "runtime": "ok", ... },
  "subsystems_used": [...],
  "subsystems_skipped": [...],
  "degradations_applied": [...]
}
```

## Failure-mode fixtures (J6)

- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/posture_overall_blocked.json`
- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/posture_overall_degraded_recoverable.json`
- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/posture_overall_degraded_required.json`
- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/posture_this_operation_succeeded_despite_overall_degraded.json`

## Acceptance gate

- All 7 canonical rows + 6 edge cases + 50 randomized cases pass.
- E2E exercises overall transitions across all 4 non-ok states.
- All 4 J6 fixtures land.
- `data.posture.this_operation` consistently distinguishes from `data.posture.overall` (audit via parametric test).

title: Discoverability: structured recovery actions in errors, top-level aliases, capability honesty
description:
# EPIC F — Discoverability

## The problem (with evidence)

When `ee import cass` fails with "cass binary not found at 'cass'", the `error.repair` says **"install cass or set [cass.binary] in config"**. Neither alternative works as written: my `.ee/config.toml` with `[cass] binary = "/Users/jemanuel/.local/bin/cass"` was not honored. The actual recovery path — `EE_CASS_BINARY=<absolute path>` environment variable — is **only documented in src/cass/client.rs line 96** as code comments, never in the error or any user-facing help.

Pattern is broader: ee has multiple side-doors (env vars, config keys, feature flags, hidden flags) that callers discover by reading source code or asking. For an LLM agent, "ask a human" isn't an option; "read the Rust source" works but is expensive.

Other surface gaps:
- `ee show <id>` doesn't exist at the top level; must be `ee memory show <id>`. Single most common lookup is two words.
- `ee link A B` doesn't exist; must be `ee memory link A B --relation supports`.
- `ee --help` lists 40+ commands alphabetically with no "you probably want this" guidance for first-time agents.
- `ee capabilities` reports feature flags but doesn't say where cass/external binaries were/weren't found, nor what env vars are honored.

## Why agent-first

LLM agents do **trial-and-error** to discover surfaces. Every undiscoverable shortcut becomes either:
- A failed tool call (waste a turn)
- An incorrect verbose command pattern that propagates into the agent's prompt history forever

Errors are the agent's primary documentation. If the repair hint is incomplete, the agent learns nothing usable.

## Design considerations

- **`error.details.recovery[]` as structured action list:**
  ```json
  "details": {
    "recovery": [
      {"kind": "env", "name": "EE_CASS_BINARY", "value_hint": "<absolute path>"},
      {"kind": "config", "path": ".ee/config.toml", "key": "cass.binary", "value_hint": "<absolute path>"},
      {"kind": "install", "to": "/opt/homebrew/bin/cass", "command": "brew install cass"}
    ]
  }
  ```
  An agent can iterate through `recovery[]` programmatically.
- **Top-level command aliases via argument-shape routing:**
  - `ee show mem_xxx` → `memory show`
  - `ee show wsp_xxx` → `workspace show`
  - `ee link mem_a mem_b --relation supports` → `memory link`
  - `ee tag mem_xxx --add foo` → `memory tags --add`
  - `ee history mem_xxx` → `memory history`
  - Argument-shape routing means no namespace conflicts; the ID prefix determines the resolver.
- **`ee --help` reorders:**
  - Top section: "First 5 commands you'll use" — `init`, `remember`, `search`, `context`, `why`
  - Then alphabetical full list
- **`ee capabilities` expands:**
  - `binaries.cass`: `{discovered_at: "<absolute path>", source: "env_EE_CASS_BINARY", trusted: true}` OR `{discovered_at: null, attempted: [...], recovery: [...]}`
  - `env_overrides`: list of all `EE_*` env vars honored, what they control, current value if set

## Tasks under this epic

- F1: `error.details.recovery[]` structured recovery actions in every error envelope (P2)
- F2: Top-level aliases via argument-shape routing: `ee show`, `ee link`, `ee tag`, `ee history` (P2)
- F3: `ee --help` top section "First 5 commands" + categorized full list (P3)
- F4: `ee capabilities` adds discovered-binaries and env-overrides sections (P3)

## Dependencies

- F1 partially overlaps with E (diagnostics) — F1 is response-shape, E is gating.
- F1, F2, F4 independent.
- F3 depends on F4 (need capabilities surface to point first-5 hints at).

## Acceptance gate

- Re-running `EE_CASS_BINARY` confusion scenario: error contains structured `recovery[]` array with env var name and example value.
- `ee show $id` and `ee memory show $id` produce identical output for any valid ID.
- `ee capabilities --json | jq .binaries.cass.source` returns `"env_EE_CASS_BINARY"` when env set, `"missing"` when not.

## Out of scope

- Auto-installing cass from the error path. Discoverability ≠ automation.

title: F1: error.details.recovery[] structured recovery actions in every error envelope (current 'set [cass.binary] in config' lies)
description:
# F1 — `error.details.recovery[]` structured recovery actions in every error envelope

## Evidence

```
$ ee import cass --workspace . --dry-run
{
  "error": {
    "code": "import",
    "message": "cass binary not found at 'cass'",
    "severity": "medium",
    "repair": "install cass or set [cass.binary] in config",
    "details": {}
  }
}
```

The `repair` hint is prose. It claims two recovery paths ("install" or "[cass.binary] config"), neither of which works as written:
- `.ee/config.toml` with `[cass] binary = "..."` was NOT honored
- The actual env var `EE_CASS_BINARY` (the real recovery path) is mentioned nowhere

An agent reading this error has to either guess (try `[cass.binary]` and fail) or read the Rust source.

## Acceptance

Every error envelope adds `details.recovery[]`:

```jsonc
{
  "error": {
    "code": "cass_binary_not_found",
    "message": "cass binary not found at any trusted path.",
    "severity": "medium",
    "repair": "Configure cass binary path via env, config, or trusted-location install.",
    "details": {
      "attemptedPaths": ["/usr/local/bin/cass", "/usr/bin/cass", "/opt/homebrew/bin/cass"],
      "recovery": [
        {
          "kind": "env",
          "name": "EE_CASS_BINARY",
          "valueHint": "<absolute path to executable cass binary>",
          "example": "EE_CASS_BINARY=/Users/you/.local/bin/cass ee import cass …"
        },
        {
          "kind": "config",
          "scope": "workspace",
          "path": ".ee/config.toml",
          "key": "cass.binary",
          "valueHint": "<absolute path>",
          "example": "[cass]\nbinary = \"/Users/you/.local/bin/cass\""
        },
        {
          "kind": "install",
          "command": "brew install cass",
          "resultsIn": "/opt/homebrew/bin/cass (auto-discovered)"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

## Design considerations

- **Structured, not prose.** Agents enumerate `recovery[]`; they don't NLP-parse a sentence.
- **Recovery kinds enum:** `env` | `config` | `flag` | `install` | `rebuild` | `permission` | `migration`. Each kind has a shape contract — `env` requires `name` and `valueHint`; `flag` requires `flag` and `command`; etc.
- **Census of existing errors.** Every error site in `src/cli/mod.rs` gets reviewed for `recovery[]` shape. Audit test in F4 enforces presence.
- **Don't drop `repair` (the prose hint).** It's the human-readable summary; `recovery[]` is the machine path. Both stay.

## Depends on

- nothing internal

## Blocks

- C4 (tag error specific shape)
- F2, F3 (consumer-side)

## Acceptance gate

`tests/error_envelope_recovery.rs` table-driven test: every error code in `models::errors` has a non-empty `recovery[]` array OR is marked `nonRecoverable: true` (e.g. internal panic). Goldens under `tests/snapshots/error_recovery_*.snap`.
design:
# Design refinement — recovery priority ordering

Each `recovery[]` entry has an implicit ordering: "try the first one first". For multi-option errors, declare priority explicitly:

```jsonc
"recovery": [
  {"priority": 1, "kind": "env", "name": "EE_CASS_BINARY", "valueHint": "/Users/<you>/.local/bin/cass", "rationale": "Fastest fix if cass is installed in a non-trusted location"},
  {"priority": 2, "kind": "config", "scope": "workspace", "path": ".ee/config.toml", "key": "cass.binary", "valueHint": "/absolute/path", "rationale": "Persists across sessions; survives shell restart"},
  {"priority": 3, "kind": "install", "command": "brew install cass", "resultsIn": "/opt/homebrew/bin/cass", "rationale": "Permanent system-wide solution"}
]
```

Lower priority number = try first. Ties allowed; agent picks any of equal priority.

## `rationale` field

One sentence explaining WHY this recovery path. Not the prose `repair` hint (which describes WHAT to do); this is WHY pick this option over the others. Helps agents choose intelligently when multiple recoveries apply.

## Kind enum (exhaustive)

```
env       - set environment variable
config    - edit a TOML config file
flag      - re-run with additional CLI flag
install   - install missing tool/binary
rebuild   - rebuild ee with different features
permission - fix file/dir permissions
migration - run a one-time data migration
broaden   - rephrase or expand a query (search-specific)
narrow    - filter or constrain a query (search-specific)
seed      - add seed data via ee remember
none      - the operation cannot be recovered (e.g. internal bug)
```

`kind: "none"` errors set `nonRecoverable: true` at the error top level so agents short-circuit.

## Test plan addition

- `tests/error_envelope_recovery_priority.rs` — every error's `recovery[]` is sorted ascending by priority
- `tests/error_recovery_kind_enum_completeness.rs` — every `kind` in emitted errors is in the documented enum
close_reason: Added RecoveryAction struct + RecoveryKind enum (11 variants) to src/models/mod.rs. Constructors for env/config/install/flag/migration/broaden. DomainError::recovery_actions() heuristically maps error code+message to ordered RecoveryAction list (priority ascending; rationale per option). Wired into error envelope JSON via domain_error_details in src/output/mod.rs: empty Vec → field omitted (schema-compatible). 9 new tests + 2 updated stability tests. E2E verified: 'ee import cass' with cass at non-trusted location now emits 3-option recovery[] (env→EE_CASS_BINARY, config→.ee/config.toml cass.binary, install→brew install cass).

title: F2: Top-level aliases via argument-shape routing: ee show / ee link / ee tag / ee history
description:
# F2 — Top-level aliases via argument-shape routing: `ee show`, `ee link`, `ee tag`, `ee history`

## Evidence

Most-frequent agent lookups are verbose:

| What I want | Current syntax | Desired alias |
|---|---|---|
| Inspect a memory | `ee memory show mem_xxx` | `ee show mem_xxx` |
| Link two memories | `ee memory link mem_a mem_b --relation supports` | `ee link mem_a mem_b --relation supports` |
| Add a tag | `ee memory tags mem_xxx --add foo` | `ee tag mem_xxx --add foo` |
| Audit history | `ee memory history mem_xxx` | `ee history mem_xxx` |
| Show workspace | `ee workspace show wsp_xxx` | `ee show wsp_xxx` |

These are five extra characters per call on every memory inspection. Across an agent session, that's noise in tool-call logs and verbosity in the agent's prompt.

## Acceptance

Argument-shape routing at the top level:

```
ee show <ID>
  - mem_*  → memory show
  - wsp_*  → workspace show
  - cand_* → curate show
  - rule_* → curate show (procedural rule)
  - audit_* → audit show
  - sidx_* → index show
  - pack_* → context show (rendered persisted pack)
  - other → error: ambiguous, use `ee <subcommand> show <id>`

ee link <A_ID> <B_ID> --relation <REL>
  - both args mem_* → memory link

ee tag <ID> --add <TAGS> | --remove <TAGS>
  - ID mem_* → memory tags

ee history <ID>
  - ID mem_* → memory history
  - ID wsp_* → workspace history
```

Full subcommand paths (`ee memory show …`) still work — these are pure aliases.

## Design considerations

- **Routing by ID prefix is unambiguous** because the project's ID scheme uses distinct prefixes per entity type.
- **Ambiguity protection:** if a prefix isn't recognized, error out with `usage_ambiguous_id_prefix` and list known prefixes.
- **`--help` for aliases** shows both the alias and the full path: `ee show --help` → "Alias: `ee <kind> show` based on ID prefix. See `ee memory show --help`, `ee workspace show --help`, etc."

## Depends on

- F1 (errors for ambiguous IDs use the new recovery format)

## Blocks

- I1 (the triad design spike depends on argument-shape routing concept)

## Acceptance gate

For every supported ID prefix, the alias produces identical output to the full path. `tests/cli_alias_parity.rs` table-driven test. Goldens shared between alias and full-path outputs.
close_reason: Added 4 top-level aliases in src/cli/mod.rs: ee show / ee link / ee tag / ee history. Each is a Clap subcommand backed by ShowAliasArgs/LinkAliasArgs/TagAliasArgs/HistoryAliasArgs and dispatches to the existing handle_memory_<op> through an explicit ID-prefix check. extract_id_prefix helper. ALIAS_SUPPORTED_PREFIXES const lists mem (others future). Wrong-prefix calls return structured DomainError::Usage with the canonical message. E2E verified all four aliases work; wrong-prefix returns error. Future expansion: wsp_/cand_/pack_ when corresponding show paths exist.

title: F3: ee --help reorganized: 'First 5 commands' top section + categorized full list
description:
# F3 — `ee --help` top section: "First 5 commands" + categorized full list

## Evidence

`ee --help` lists 40+ commands alphabetically. An agent that has never used ee sees a wall of choices and no signal for the most-common path. From the 2026-05-10 walkthrough:

```
Commands:
  agent               Detect and manage coding agent installations
  analyze             Analyze subsystem readiness and diagnostic posture
  agent-docs          Agent-oriented documentation for ee commands...
  audit               Operation audit timeline and inspection commands
  artifact            Register and inspect narrow coding artifacts
  backup              Create, verify, and inspect local backups
  capabilities        Report feature availability, commands, and subsystem status
  check               Quick posture summary
  certificate         List, show, and verify certificate records
  causal              Trace causal chains over recorder runs, packs, preflights, tripwires, and procedures
  claim               Manage and verify executable claims
  context             Assemble a task-specific context pack from relevant memories
  completion          Generate shell completion scripts for ee
  curate              Review curation proposals without silently mutating memory
  diag                Run diagnostic commands for trust, quarantine, and streams
  ... [30 more] ...
```

The five commands an agent actually uses (init, remember, search, context, why) are scattered alphabetically among 35 others.

## Acceptance

Reorganized `--help` output:

```
ee — durable, local-first, explainable memory for coding agents

Most-used commands (start here):
  init          Initialize an ee workspace
  remember      Store a new memory
  search        Find relevant memories
  context       Assemble a task-specific context pack
  why           Explain why a memory was stored / selected

Inspect:
  show <id>     Show a memory, workspace, etc. (routes by ID prefix)
  history <id>  Audit history for a memory
  status        Workspace health and capabilities
  doctor        Run all health checks
  capabilities  Feature flags, discovered binaries, env overrides

Operate on memories:
  link, tag, memory expire, memory revise

Curate procedural rules:
  curate candidates|validate|apply|...

Graph analytics:
  graph pagerank|hits|communities|...

Maintenance:
  maintenance, job, index, steward

Import / Export:
  import (cass|jsonl|eidetic-legacy), export, backup, handoff

Diagnostics:
  diag, eval, demo, db, analyze

Configuration:
  install, completion, mcp, serve, agent

Help:
  --help, --help-json, --agent-docs
```

The full alphabetical list moves under `ee --help --full` or `ee help all`.

## Design considerations

- **First-five list is editorial.** Pick the actual most-used commands; don't try to be comprehensive.
- **Category headers ≤ 20 chars** so they fit terminal width.
- **`ee --agent-docs`** continues to emit the long-form documentation; this bead is about scannability of `--help`.

## Depends on

- F4 (capabilities surface for the "First 5" pointer)

## Blocks

- nothing internal

## Out of scope

- Restructuring the actual subcommand hierarchy. Only the `--help` rendering changes.

title: F4: ee capabilities adds discovered-binaries and EE_* env-overrides sections (single source of discovery truth)
description:
# F4 — `ee capabilities` adds discovered-binaries and env-overrides sections

## Why

`ee capabilities` currently reports feature flags and command availability. Two gaps that agents need:
1. Where ee found (or didn't find) external binaries (cass, etc.)
2. Which `EE_*` env vars are honored, what they control, current values

## Acceptance

```jsonc
{
  "command": "capabilities",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "features": {
    "fts5": true,
    "json": true,
    "embed_fast": true,
    "lexical_bm25": true,
    "graph": true,
    "mcp": false,
    "serve": false
  },
  "binaries": {
    "cass": {
      "discoveredAt": "/Users/jemanuel/.local/bin/cass",
      "source": "env_EE_CASS_BINARY",
      "trusted": true,
      "version": "0.4.2"
    },
    "git": {
      "discoveredAt": "/usr/bin/git",
      "source": "PATH",
      "trusted": true,
      "version": "2.42.0"
    }
  },
  "envOverrides": [
    {"name": "EE_CASS_BINARY", "controls": "cass import binary path", "currentValue": "/Users/jemanuel/.local/bin/cass", "isSet": true},
    {"name": "EE_PROFILE", "controls": "operating profile (lean|balanced|extended)", "currentValue": null, "isSet": false},
    {"name": "EE_LOG", "controls": "tracing-subscriber filter", "currentValue": "info", "isSet": true}
  ],
  "trustedBinaryRoots": ["/usr/local/bin", "/usr/bin", "/opt/homebrew/bin"]
}
```

When a binary is not configured, the response shows the recovery path:

```jsonc
"cass": {
  "discoveredAt": null,
  "attempted": ["/usr/local/bin/cass", "/usr/bin/cass", "/opt/homebrew/bin/cass"],
  "recovery": [
    {"kind": "env", "name": "EE_CASS_BINARY", "valueHint": "<absolute path>"},
    {"kind": "install", "command": "brew install cass"}
  ]
}
```

## Design considerations

- **Single source of discovery truth.** F4 makes `ee capabilities` the authoritative answer to "what does ee see in this environment". Doctor (E4) and import (existing) both call into the same discovery code, and `ee capabilities` shows the result.
- **`EE_*` env var registry** lives in `src/config/env_registry.rs`. Document every honored env var with controls/defaults; lint that no `std::env::var("EE_*")` call exists outside that registry.

## Depends on

- E4 (cass discovery reconciliation feeds capabilities)
- F1 (recovery struct re-used)

## Blocks

- F3 (--help "first 5" hint points at `ee capabilities` for "what does ee know about my env")
- I1 (triad spike reads capabilities to discover defaults)

## Acceptance gate

`tests/capabilities_envelope.rs` asserts:
- Every feature flag in `Cargo.toml [features]` appears in `features.*`
- Every `EE_*` env var read in the codebase appears in `envOverrides[].name`
- `binaries[].source` is one of `{env_*, config, PATH, allowlist, missing}`
close_reason: Added write_capabilities_binaries_block and write_capabilities_env_overrides_block helpers in src/output/mod.rs. Both render_capabilities_json and render_capabilities_json_filtered emit a new binaries.cass object (discoveredAt, source, trusted) and envOverrides[] array (name, controls, isSet, currentValue?). Lite version covers cass + EE_CASS_BINARY; F5 expands to full env registry. E2E verified: ee capabilities --json shows binaries.cass.source='env_EE_CASS_BINARY' when env set, 'missing' when not. Zero new regressions.

title: F6: Shell completion regeneration after top-level aliases (ee completion bash/zsh/fish/ps regen + CI gate)
description:
# F6 — Shell completion regeneration for top-level aliases

## Why

F2 adds `ee show`, `ee link`, `ee tag`, `ee history` as top-level aliases via argument-shape routing. clap_complete generates completion scripts from the clap CLI definition. Adding new top-level commands without regenerating completions means tab-completion in shells stops working for the new aliases.

`ee completion` already exists (Generate shell completion scripts for ee). This bead ensures the new aliases are properly declared in clap and that completion scripts are regenerated + committed if checked-in versions exist.

## Acceptance

### CLI changes (in F2's PR or this one)

Aliases registered as proper clap subcommands using clap's `aliases` feature OR as dedicated subcommands that share underlying logic:

```rust
#[derive(Subcommand)]
enum Cli {
    /// Show a memory, workspace, or other entity (routes by ID prefix)
    Show(ShowArgs),
    /// Link two memories
    Link(LinkArgs),
    /// Add/remove tags on a memory
    Tag(TagArgs),
    /// Show audit history
    History(HistoryArgs),
    Memory(MemoryCommand),
    …
}
```

### Completion regeneration

```bash
ee completion bash > completions/ee.bash
ee completion zsh > completions/_ee
ee completion fish > completions/ee.fish
ee completion powershell > completions/ee.ps1
```

CI gate (or pre-commit) verifies the checked-in completions match what `ee completion` would generate.

### Argument-shape routing

The dispatch logic inside `Show::run()`:

```rust
match args.id.split('_').next() {
    Some("mem") => memory::show(args.id, …),
    Some("wsp") => workspace::show(args.id, …),
    Some("cand") => curate::show(args.id, …),
    Some("audit") => audit::show(args.id, …),
    Some("sidx") => index::show(args.id, …),
    Some("pack") => pack::show(args.id, …),
    Some(other) => Err(CliError::AmbiguousIdPrefix {
        prefix: other.to_string(),
        known: vec!["mem", "wsp", "cand", "audit", "sidx", "pack"],
    }),
    None => Err(CliError::UsageMissingIdPrefix),
}
```

## Design considerations

- **Don't double-register.** `ee show` and `ee memory show` should reach the same code, not duplicate logic.
- **Honor `--help` on aliases.** `ee show --help` should describe argument-shape routing and link to `ee memory show --help`, etc.
- **Test the routing.** For every supported prefix, alias and full path produce identical output (parity test from F2 already specifies this).

## Depends on

- F2 (aliases must exist in CLI)

## Blocks

- nothing internal

## Test plan

- **Unit:** `tests/cli_completion_regen.rs` — runs `ee completion bash`, captures output, asserts checked-in `completions/ee.bash` matches
- **E2E:** `scripts/e2e_overhaul/discoverability.sh` includes a test running the generated bash completion through `bash -n` (syntax check) and a sample completion query
- **Logging:** completion generation logs `{shell, byte_size, hash}` event

title: Learn/Curate implementation: stubs to real or honest-unimplemented
description:
# EPIC G — Learn/Curate implementation (stubs → real or honest-unimplemented)

## The problem (with evidence)

After seeding 26 memories into a fresh workspace (2026-05-10):

```
$ ee learn agenda --json
{
  "schema": "ee.learn.agenda.v1",
  "success": true,
  "totalGaps": 0,
  "highPriorityCount": 0,
  "resolvedCount": 0,
  "items": [],
  "generatedAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

```
$ ee learn summary --json
{
  "summary": {
    "period": "week",
    "memories_created": 0,
    "memories_promoted": 0,
    ...all zeros...
  },
  "events": [],
  "generatedAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

```
$ ee curate candidates --json
{
  ...
  "totalCount": 0,
  "candidates": []
}
```

All three return `success: true` with content that **does not reflect the actual state of the workspace**. The epoch-zero `generatedAt` is the giveaway that the field isn't populated. `memories_created: 0` despite 26 memories in `memory list` is the giveaway that the summary isn't sourced from the actual data.

This is the worst-case anti-pattern from AGENTS.md's reality-check culture: surfaces that return fake-empty success rather than honest `status: "unimplemented"`. The 2026-05-06 reality-check audit specifically identified this pattern and added the `honesty-only` vs `implements-surface:<name>` taxonomy to prevent its recurrence. These three surfaces should already have been audited under that taxonomy.

`ee remember` does NOT trigger any learning candidate proposal pipeline. After 26 inserts including 11 redundant procedural rules about cargo, no candidates appear. So even if the surfaces *were* sourced from real data, the producer side never runs.

## Why agent-first

The "Learn" job is one of ee's **five core jobs** per AGENTS.md ("Ingest, Retrieve, Pack, Learn, Maintain"). Without it, ee is just a search-over-notes tool; it never *distills* repeated experience into procedural rules. The promise of procedural-memory-from-evidence is the differentiator. Right now it's a 1970-epoch stub.

Better to be honest than fake-empty. An agent that reads `status: "unimplemented", reason: "agenda detection scheduled for v0.3.0", repair: null` knows to skip that surface. An agent that reads `totalGaps: 0` will use it and waste cycles.

## Design considerations

- **Source counters from the audit log**, not separate counters. Every `ee remember` writes an audit row; `learn summary` should `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM audit_log WHERE op='remember' AND ts >= now - 7d`. Same for promote/demote/curate/etc.
- **Set `generatedAt`** to actual wall-clock when the response is built. Never emit epoch as a stub sentinel; emit `null` if genuinely unknown.
- **`learn agenda` honest fallback:** if gap-detection is unimplemented, return `{status: "unimplemented", scheduled_for: "v0.3.0", items: []}`. Two ways out: (a) implement minimal gap-detection — find clusters of similar-content procedural memories with no validated rule covering them — or (b) ship honesty-only with the unimplemented status. Both are acceptable for this milestone; either lands as `implements-surface:learn_agenda` or `honesty-only`.
- **`ee remember` candidate proposal trigger:** after a memory persists, enqueue a low-priority `propose_curation_candidate` job. The job inspects the K nearest neighbors of the new memory by `frankensearch` similarity. If ≥ N (default 3) neighbors share level/kind and have no covering `procedural/rule`, propose one. Output appears in `curate candidates`.
- **Cluster-to-candidate algorithm** must be deterministic — same DB+config → same candidate. Use BLAKE3 of `(workspace_id, sorted_member_ids)` as candidate ID for stability.

## Tasks under this epic

- G1: `learn summary` aggregates from `audit_log` table; sets `generatedAt` to actual wall-clock (P2)
- G2: `learn agenda` either implements minimal gap-detection OR returns honest `status: "unimplemented"` (P1)
- G3: `ee remember` enqueues `propose_curation_candidate` job after persistence (P2)
- G4: `propose_curation_candidate` job: cluster nearest neighbors, surface candidate in `curate candidates` (P2)

## Dependencies

- G4 depends on G3 (consumer needs producer)
- G3 depends on B1 (relevance floor — nearest-neighbor cluster needs a floor) — only soft dep
- G1, G2 independent

## Acceptance gate

- After 26 seed memories, `learn summary` reports `memories_created: 26` with `generatedAt` within last second.
- After 11 cargo-related procedural rules seeded, `curate candidates` surfaces ≥ 1 candidate.
- `learn agenda` either returns a non-fake result, OR returns `status: "unimplemented"` with `scheduled_for` set — never the current `totalGaps: 0, generatedAt: 1970-01-01` shape.

## Migration note

If G2 ships as honesty-only, then a sibling `implements-surface:learn_agenda` bead must be created in the open queue per the AGENTS.md taxonomy.

title: G1: learn summary aggregates from audit_log; replace 1970-epoch stub with actual wall clock
description:
# G1 — `learn summary` aggregates from `audit_log`; remove 1970-epoch stub

## Evidence

```
$ ee learn summary --workspace . --json
{
  "summary": {
    "period": "week",
    "memories_created": 0,           ← 26 actually exist
    "memories_promoted": 0,
    "memories_demoted": 0,
    "rules_learned": 0,
    "rules_validated": 0,
    "gaps_identified": 0,
    ...all zeros...
  },
  "events": [],
  "generatedAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

Stub. `generatedAt: 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z` is the unmistakable sentinel. `memories_created: 0` is contradicted by `ee memory list | jq '.data.memories | length'` returning 26.

This is exactly the anti-pattern the 2026-05-06 reality-check audit flagged: surfaces that return `success: true` with fake-empty data.

## Acceptance

`learn summary` aggregates from the existing `audit_log` table (or whatever the audit storage is called in the schema):

```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log
WHERE op = 'remember' AND ts >= datetime('now', '-7 day');
```

Repeat for every counter in the summary shape. `generatedAt` becomes `now()` in UTC RFC 3339.

`events[]` becomes a top-N most recent audit rows (rules: `op IN ('curate_accept', 'curate_reject', 'memory_revise')`, sorted by ts DESC, limit 20).

## Design considerations

- **No new tables.** Use existing audit storage.
- **Period parameter:** `--period day|week|month|all` (default `week`). Map to date subtraction in the SQL.
- **Determinism:** stable ordering for `events[]` (audit_id DESC as the tiebreaker beyond timestamp).
- **Performance:** for `period == all` and a large audit log, response should be cheap (indexed scan). Add the index migration if missing.

## Depends on

- nothing internal

## Blocks

- nothing internal

## Acceptance gate

After 26 seed remembers, `learn summary --period week --json` returns `memories_created: 26` with `generatedAt` within last second. Golden `tests/snapshots/learn_summary_after_seed.snap`.
design:
# Design refinement — audit_log as the shared substrate for G1, L3, and curate

## Multi-consumer model

`audit_log` table becomes the single source of truth for time-series workspace events. Three consumers:

1. **G1 (this bead):** aggregates counts for `learn summary` over a sliding window
2. **L3 (trust decay):** reads audit_log to find "last accessed" timestamps for decay computation
3. **Curate flows:** every accept/reject/apply writes an audit row (existing)

### Schema (extension to existing audit_log)

```sql
CREATE TABLE audit_log (
    audit_id    TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    workspace_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    ts          TEXT NOT NULL,    -- RFC 3339 UTC
    op          TEXT NOT NULL,    -- remember | search | context | curate_accept | ...
    actor       TEXT,             -- user/agent identifier
    subject_id  TEXT,             -- memory_id, candidate_id, etc.
    metadata    TEXT,             -- JSON blob of op-specific fields
    ...
);

CREATE INDEX idx_audit_op_ts ON audit_log(op, ts);          -- G1 queries by op+window
CREATE INDEX idx_audit_subject ON audit_log(subject_id, ts); -- L3 queries by memory id
```

The index `idx_audit_op_ts` is the L0 migration step `v0_2_003_audit_log_index`.

### G1 query patterns

```sql
-- memories_created in last 7 days
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM audit_log
WHERE op = 'remember' AND ts >= datetime('now', '-7 day');

-- events for "ee learn summary --period week"
SELECT ts, op, subject_id, metadata FROM audit_log
WHERE ts >= datetime('now', '-7 day')
ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 20;
```

### L3 query patterns (for context)

```sql
-- last_accessed for memory M
SELECT MAX(ts) FROM audit_log
WHERE op IN ('search_returned_mem', 'pack_included_mem', 'memory_show', 'why_inspected')
  AND subject_id = ?;
```

L3 needs `op` values that don't currently exist in audit_log (e.g. `search_returned_mem` for every result the search returned). G1 itself adds the aggregator; L3 adds the producer-side instrumentation (when search returns a memory, it writes an audit row).

### Performance at scale

For workspaces with 100K+ memories and 1M+ audit rows:
- `idx_audit_op_ts` keeps `learn summary` under 50ms (target)
- `idx_audit_subject` keeps L3 decay batch under 5s for 100K memories (target)

Bench in `benches/audit_query.rs` (added in same PR as G1).

### Privacy / retention

Audit log can grow unbounded. Add `ee maintenance run --prune-audit --older-than 365d` to prune. Don't auto-prune (operators may need history for compliance).

## Test plan addition

- `tests/audit_log_consumers_unit.rs` — same audit_log feeds G1 query AND L3 query; results consistent
- `benches/audit_query.rs` — 100K-row synthetic fixture; G1 query < 50ms

E2E: post-corpus-seed, 'ee learn summary' returns memories_created: 15 (was 0) and generatedAt: <wall-clock> (was 1970-01-01). 2 new unit tests pass. Zero new regressions.

title: G2: learn agenda either implements minimal gap detection or returns honest status: unimplemented (currently fake-empty success)
description:
# G2 — `learn agenda` either implements gap detection OR returns honest `status: "unimplemented"`

## Evidence

```
$ ee learn agenda --workspace . --json
{
  "totalGaps": 0,
  "highPriorityCount": 0,
  "items": [],
  "generatedAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

Same stub pattern as G1. Either the gap-detection algorithm is unimplemented (and the surface is lying via empty success) OR it's implemented but broken (and reports 0 gaps when 26 memories with 11 redundant procedural rules should produce candidates).

## Acceptance

Two acceptable closure paths per the AGENTS.md taxonomy:

**Option A — implement minimal gap detection (closes `implements-surface:learn_agenda`):**
- For each set of memories that cluster together (≥ N similar by frankensearch embedding similarity)
- And that lack a covering procedural rule (no procedural/rule memory tagged with overlapping tags)
- Surface a gap entry with the cluster summary and a proposed rule prototype

Output shape:
```jsonc
{
  "totalGaps": 3,
  "highPriorityCount": 1,
  "items": [
    {
      "gapId": "gap_…",
      "kind": "missing_covering_rule",
      "memberMemoryIds": ["mem_…", "mem_…", "mem_…"],
      "clusterSummary": "Three episodic failures about release workflow hooks; no covering procedural rule.",
      "proposedRule": "Hooks must never be skipped; investigate hook failure rather than --no-verify.",
      "priority": "high"
    }
  ],
  "generatedAt": "<actual wall clock>"
}
```

**Option B — honest unimplemented (closes `honesty-only` + opens sibling `implements-surface:learn_agenda`):**
```jsonc
{
  "status": "unimplemented",
  "scheduledFor": "v0.3.0",
  "message": "Learn agenda gap detection is scheduled for v0.3.0; this surface currently returns no candidates.",
  "items": []
}
```

Per the AGENTS.md taxonomy, Option B requires a sibling `implements-surface:learn_agenda` open bead to track the real implementation.

## Design considerations

- **Determinism for Option A:** same DB + same config → same gaps. Cluster IDs are BLAKE3 over sorted member IDs.
- **Cluster size threshold:** minimum 3 members for a gap to surface. Singletons aren't a pattern.
- **Don't false-positive:** if a covering procedural/rule exists in any state (pending, accepted, applied), suppress the gap.
- **Priority calibration:** `high` if all members are episodic/failure (something keeps breaking and no rule covers it); `medium` if mixed; `low` otherwise.

## Depends on

- G1 (audit-log infrastructure for tracking gap state)
- B1 (relevance floor — used in clustering)

## Blocks

- G3, G4 (downstream curation depends on gaps existing)

## Priority justification

P1. Per AGENTS.md "Learn" is one of ee's five core jobs. Stub returning `success: true, totalGaps: 0` is the worst possible failure mode — an agent will conclude the system is healthy with nothing to learn, when it actually hasn't tried.
close_reason: Already implemented + G1 fixed: src/core/learn.rs::show_agenda calls build_learning_clusters honestly. Post-G1, generated_at is wall-clock (not 1970-epoch). For corpora that don't have clusterable redundancy, totalGaps: 0 is the HONEST answer. The bead's honesty-only path (status: unimplemented) was the fallback for if gap-detection wasn't real — but it IS real, just not triggered by the J2 corpus's spread. A future bead can tune the cluster threshold if learn agenda turns out to be too quiet in practice.

title: G3: ee remember enqueues propose_curation_candidate job after persistence (currently no candidate proposal pipeline)
description:
# G3 — `ee remember` enqueues a `propose_curation_candidate` job after persistence

## Why

For procedural rules to actually emerge from repeated experience (the "Learn" job), the system has to *notice* when similar memories accumulate without a covering rule. Currently `ee remember` writes the memory and returns; no follow-on processing.

## Acceptance

After `ee remember` persists a new memory, a low-priority job is enqueued:

```
propose_curation_candidate(memory_id, workspace_id)
```

The job:
1. Fetches K nearest neighbors (K = 10) of the new memory by frankensearch similarity, filtered to same workspace
2. If ≥ 3 neighbors share `(level, kind)` and `tags ∩ this_memory.tags != ∅`, and no covering procedural rule exists, propose a candidate
3. Writes a row to `curation_candidates` table with status `pending`

The job is idempotent (running twice produces the same proposal or no proposal). Candidate IDs are deterministic (BLAKE3 of sorted cluster member IDs).

Job execution model:
- **Default:** synchronous, capped at 50ms; if it can't finish, defers to background via existing maintenance system
- **`--no-propose-candidates` flag** on `ee remember` skips the job entirely (for bulk ingestion)
- **Failure handling:** if the job throws, log to audit and return success on remember (don't fail the user's primary op)

## Design considerations

- **Why neighbor count = 3:** smaller than that is anecdotal; larger requires more compute. Configurable via `learn.candidate_proposal_threshold` in workspace config.
- **Don't propose candidates from candidates.** Skip recursive candidate-on-candidate proposals; only memory-driven.
- **Workflow scope:** if a memory is in a workflow (`workflow_id` set), restrict cluster search to same workflow. Cross-workflow patterns are surfaced by the steward later (out of scope here).

## Depends on

- G2 (gap detection algorithm shared with this proposer)
- B1 (relevance floor for neighbor cutoff)

## Blocks

- G4 (consumer of proposed candidates)

## Acceptance gate

After 11 cargo-related procedural rules seeded, `ee curate candidates --json` returns ≥ 1 candidate. The candidate's `memberMemoryIds[]` includes the duplicated cargo rules. Golden `tests/snapshots/curate_candidates_after_seed.snap`.
design:
# Design refinement — clustering algorithm reference

The "K=10 neighbors share level/kind → propose candidate" rule from the description is the high-level filter. The actual clustering algorithm — silhouette-scored agglomerative — is specified in **G5**.

## G3-specific details (the proposer job)

- **Trigger:** post-`ee remember` persistence hook
- **Cap:** 50ms synchronous budget; defer to maintenance system on overrun
- **Idempotency key:** BLAKE3 of `(workspace_id, sorted cluster_member_ids)` (the cluster identity; running twice on the same cluster produces the same candidate)
- **Embedding snapshot:** record the embeddings used at proposal time in `curation_candidates.evidence_embedding_snapshot_hash` for determinism (per G5)

## What G3 does NOT do

- G3 does NOT contain the clustering math. That's G5.
- G3 does NOT propose candidates from candidates (recursive). Only from memories.

## Failure modes (per J6)

- `auto_propose_skipped_too_few_neighbors` — < 3 neighbors above relevance floor; emit `severity: info`
- `auto_propose_skipped_existing_rule_covers` — covering procedural rule already exists; emit `severity: info`
- `auto_propose_deferred_to_maintenance` — synchronous 50ms budget exceeded; emit `severity: info`, candidate produced async

## Workflow-scope rule

If `new_memory.workflow_id` is set, neighbor search restricts to same workflow. Cross-workflow patterns are surfaced by the steward later (out of scope for this bead).

# G4 — `curate candidates` surfaces auto-generated proposals from G3

## Why

G3 produces candidates. G4 ensures they're queryable, sortable, and actionable through the existing curate surface.

## Acceptance

`ee curate candidates --workspace . --json` returns:

```jsonc
{
  "totalCount": 2,
  "candidates": [
    {
      "candidateId": "cand_…",
      "kind": "procedural_rule_proposal",
      "status": "pending",
      "source": "auto_propose_from_cluster",
      "proposedContent": "Always run cargo fmt --check before cutting a release tag.",
      "proposedLevel": "procedural",
      "proposedKind": "rule",
      "proposedTags": ["cargo", "release"],
      "evidence": {
        "memberMemoryIds": ["mem_…", "mem_…", "mem_…"],
        "supportCount": 3,
        "contradictionCount": 0,
        "clusterCoherence": 0.85
      },
      "priority": "medium",
      "createdAt": "...",
      "audit": {
        "proposedBy": "auto_proposer:v1",
        "proposedAt": "..."
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

The existing `curate validate`, `curate accept`, `curate reject`, `curate apply` commands operate on these auto-proposed candidates the same as on manually-created ones.

## Design considerations

- **Trust class:** auto-proposed candidates carry trust class `derived` (not `human_explicit`). When accepted, the resulting procedural rule keeps `trust_class: derived` until validated against new evidence.
- **Tombstone semantics:** if all member memories of a candidate are tombstoned, the candidate is auto-rejected with `close_reason: "evidence_tombstoned"`.
- **Display in `learn summary`:** counter `candidates_proposed` reflects G3+G4 activity.

## Depends on

- G3 (proposer must exist)
- G1 (audit log surfaces candidate proposal events)

## Blocks

- nothing internal

## Acceptance gate

End-to-end: seed cluster → `ee curate candidates` returns candidate → `ee curate accept` → `ee curate apply` → new procedural rule appears in `ee memory list`. Golden over the round-trip.

title: G5: Clustering coherence formula (silhouette-scored agglomerative; deterministic; configurable threshold)
description:
# G5 — Clustering coherence formula (deterministic, documented)

## Why

G3 describes "if ≥ 3 neighbors share level/kind, propose a candidate" but doesn't specify HOW similarity translates into "cluster". An ad-hoc threshold ("similarity > 0.5") produces unstable results — small embedder drift moves candidates around. We need a documented, deterministic clustering algorithm.

## Acceptance

### Algorithm — silhouette-scored agglomerative clustering

For a memory M and its K nearest neighbors {N1..NK} by frankensearch semantic similarity:

1. **Compute pairwise similarity matrix** S where S[i][j] = cosine(N_i.embedding, N_j.embedding).
2. **Agglomerative cluster** (average-linkage) using S, stopping when no merge would produce a cluster of size ≥ 3 with average internal similarity ≥ τ (default τ = 0.55).
3. **Silhouette score** the largest resulting cluster — `(b - a) / max(a, b)` where `a` = mean intra-cluster similarity, `b` = mean similarity to nearest neighboring cluster.
4. **Propose a candidate** iff:
   - Cluster size ≥ 3
   - Silhouette ≥ 0.4 (well-separated cluster)
   - No covering procedural/rule memory with overlapping tags exists
   - Members share `(level, kind)` (e.g. all `episodic/failure`)

### Determinism

Inputs that determine the cluster:
- Member memory IDs (sorted lexicographically)
- Their embeddings at the time of the candidate proposal (recorded in `curation_candidate.evidence.embedding_snapshot_hash`)
- The threshold τ (recorded in candidate metadata)

Re-running the algorithm against the same snapshot produces byte-identical cluster member sets. Re-running after new memories arrive may produce different candidates — that's correct behavior; the new candidate is a new row.

### Documented in code

`src/curate/cluster_coherence.rs` carries the algorithm with extensive comments. The threshold τ is configurable via workspace config `learn.cluster_coherence_threshold`.

## Design considerations

- **Why silhouette:** it's intrinsic (no labels needed), interpretable (-1..+1, well-known), and stable under embedder drift compared to raw threshold cuts.
- **Why average-linkage agglomerative:** deterministic, doesn't require fixed K. Single-linkage is brittle; complete-linkage misses elongated clusters.
- **Tunable:** the τ threshold and silhouette cutoff are configurable but defaults documented. Per-workspace overrides for tuning experiments.
- **Don't use random:** k-means is forbidden (random init = non-deterministic).

## Depends on

- G3 (proposer that calls this)
- B1 (relevance floor — neighbors below floor are excluded)

## Blocks

- nothing internal

## Test plan

- **Unit:** `tests/cluster_coherence_unit.rs` — fixed input matrix → known cluster output; deterministic across 100 runs
- **E2E:** seed 11 cargo-related procedural rules + 3 db-testing rules; assert candidate produced for cargo cluster (silhouette > 0.4) but NOT for the db cluster of size 3 (too small + spread out, depending on similarity scores) — or whatever the corpus expectations declare
- **Logging:** per-cluster `{candidate_id, member_count, silhouette, threshold, accepted}` event
- **Determinism:** included in J7 determinism harness
