title: [HIGH] tracing-subscriber never initialized — tracing::warn!/debug! calls are silent no-ops
description:
## Surface
ee process startup / observability (audit cycle 6, surface 7)

## Finding
`tracing-subscriber` is NOT a dependency of ee:
```bash
$ grep -E 'tracing.subscriber' Cargo.toml Cargo.lock   # no matches
```

`AGENTS.md` 'Key Dependencies (Phase 0)' table claims:
> `tracing` + `tracing-subscriber` | Structured logging and diagnostics

Only `tracing = { version = "0.1.44" }` is declared. `src/main.rs:97-106` does NOT call any subscriber init function:
```rust
fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let mut args: Vec<OsString> = std::env::args_os().collect();
    if should_inject_json_flag(&args) {
        args.insert(1, OsString::from("--json"));
    }
    let mut stdout = io::stdout();
    let mut stderr = io::stderr();
    write_start_log(&args, &mut stderr);
    ee::cli::run(args, &mut stdout, &mut stderr).into()
}
```

ee uses `tracing` macros at:
- `src/cass/session.rs:247` — `tracing::debug!("unknown_top_level_field", ...)`
- `src/graph/mod.rs:1494` — `tracing::warn!(...)`
- `src/db/mod.rs:10480, 10492` — `tracing::warn!(...)`

Without a global subscriber, `tracing`'s default Dispatch is the no-op dispatch — every event silently drops on the floor. A user who runs `RUST_LOG=debug ee context ...` expecting structured logs gets nothing.

ee has its own `LogEnvelope` JSON logger (`src/main.rs:87-95`) that writes to stderr when `json_log_enabled()`, but that path completely bypasses `tracing`. The two systems don't share schema, level filtering, or destinations.

## Why it matters
1. Diagnostic features documented in AGENTS.md don't work. A user investigating a production bug can't enable any tracing output.
2. `tracing::warn!` calls in `src/db/mod.rs` for SQLite contention or unexpected pragma states are invisible — the worst time for telemetry to vanish.
3. Question 7 from the audit ("tracing-subscriber init: double-init crash?") cannot occur because there's no init at all. Different bug, different shape.

## Repro
```bash
RUST_LOG=trace cargo run -- context 'foo' 2>&1 | grep -i tracing
# silence
```

## Fix options
A) Add `tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3", features = ["env-filter", "json"] }` to Cargo.toml. In `main.rs` call `tracing_subscriber::fmt().with_env_filter(EnvFilter::from_default_env()).json().with_writer(io::stderr).try_init().ok();` (note: `try_init` swallows the AlreadyInit error so library callers can also init).
B) Replace the `tracing::warn!`/`debug!` call sites with `LogEnvelope` writes for consistency with the existing JSON log channel; remove `tracing` from Cargo.toml.

(Option A keeps the structured-logging promise; option B simplifies but reduces ergonomics for adding new instrumentation.)
close_reason: Completed: initialized tracing subscriber at process startup, added JSON/env-filter tracing dependency and coverage, and removed an existing recorder clippy lint exposed by verification.

title: M3 follow-up: capsule body must reflect workspace memory state for canonical hash to be a true state fingerprint
description:
Discovered while writing M3 capsule roundtrip determinism test (bd-17c65.13.4 / tests/contracts/handoff_capsule_roundtrip_determinism.rs).

The v1 capsule body synthesizes Resume-profile sections from templated placeholder strings (workspace identity, objective placeholder, next-actions placeholder, decisions placeholder, swarm brief if any). It does NOT enumerate the underlying memory set. Adding a new memory to the workspace leaves the canonical_content_hash unchanged because no part of the capsule body references the new memory.

For canonical_content_hash to become a real workspace-state fingerprint (useful for cache validation, export/import roundtrip verification, and the M2 fingerprint reconciliation), the capsule producer needs to include either:

(a) A deterministic workspace_state_hash field computed from the memory set (e.g. blake3 over the sorted list of memory IDs + content hashes), OR
(b) A top_memories[] block summarizing the most-relevant memories at handoff time, OR
(c) Both.

The L2 test already computes a workspace_state_hash (level/kind/content/tags projection sorted then hashed) for backup roundtrip verification — that same primitive could be embedded in the capsule.

The regression test is in place but #[ignore]d: tests/contracts/handoff_capsule_roundtrip_determinism.rs::canonical_hash_changes_when_workspace_state_changes — un-ignore once the capsule body reflects memory state.
close_reason:
Implemented in commit b9c283a (auto-bundled with the ADR-0028 commit by a parallel agent's auto-flush). The capsule body now embeds a deterministic workspace_state_hash computed from the underlying memory set, making canonical_content_hash a true workspace-state fingerprint.

Implementation:
- src/core/handoff.rs::compute_workspace_state_hash(database_path) — BLAKE3 over the sorted projection set {level;kind;content;sorted_tags} of every non-tombstoned memory across every workspace in the DB. Same primitive L2 uses for backup round-trip determinism, so a capsule embedding this hash and an L2 backup of the same workspace land on the same fingerprint.
- create_handoff embeds the result at capsule_content.workspace_state_hash, which then flows into canonical_content_hash via the existing M3 hashing pipeline (compute_canonical_capsule_hash strips volatile fields but keeps workspace_state_hash).
- Returns None when the DB can't be opened (preview-on-empty-workspace path); producers fall back to identity fingerprint only.

The previously-ignored M3 test (canonical_hash_changes_when_workspace_state_changes) is now un-ignored and passing:
- Build workspace with seeds → create capsule (capture canonical hash)
- Add a new memory
- Create capsule again
- Canonical hash differs from the first one

cargo test --test contracts handoff_capsule_roundtrip_determinism: 4 PASS, 0 IGNORED. cargo test --test contracts: 435 PASS / 7 baseline FAIL. Zero new regressions.

This closes the M3 follow-up loop: M3 added the canonical_content_hash hashing logic; bd-1xkxi made the capsule body actually reflect the workspace state so the hash means something.

title: HIGH: FrankenSQLite connections never enable foreign-key enforcement
description:
Reviewer finding in src/db/.

Evidence:
- src/db/mod.rs:123-151 opens FrankenConnection instances for memory/file/schema-only modes and returns them without setting PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON.
- src/db/mod.rs:259-265 only runs PRAGMA foreign_key_check as a diagnostic after the fact.
- sqlmodel-frankensqlite opens raw fsqlite connections without enabling FK enforcement (/data/projects/sqlmodel_rust/crates/sqlmodel-frankensqlite/src/connection.rs:67-92).
- FrankenSQLite has a test documenting SQLite-compatible FK default-off behavior (/data/projects/frankensqlite/crates/fsqlite/src/lib.rs:9695-9705).

Impact:
The schema declares many REFERENCES/ON DELETE actions, but normal ee writes can insert orphan rows and deletes will not cascade/set-null unless each connection enables FK enforcement. Integrity checks may report the damage later, but repository methods can already have persisted logically invalid data.

Suggested fix:
Enable PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON immediately after opening read-write memory/file connections, and add storage tests proving a missing parent insert fails plus at least one cascade/set-null path works. Keep schema-only inspection read-only if needed.
close_reason: Fixed: DbConnection now enables PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON immediately after every FrankenConnection open; added regression test proving FK violations error on opened connections.

title: EE-285: Spike deterministic prompt-injection detection
description:
Source plan item: EE-285 from the `Spikes` backlog.

Task: Spike deterministic prompt-injection detection

Background and intent:
Answer dependency and design unknowns with bounded proof tasks before committing to user-visible surfaces or heavy implementation.

Why this matters:
This bead contributes to the overarching goal of making `ee` a dependable local memory substrate for coding agents: useful before work, auditable after work, and safe under degraded conditions. The work should be implemented in the smallest coherent slice that fully satisfies the public contract implied by the title.

Dependency context:
Original plan dependencies: EE-260. These are also represented as br dependency edges where the referenced bead exists.

Non-negotiable constraints:
Global implementation invariants for this task:
- Keep the CLI local-first, deterministic, and agent-native; stdout is data, stderr is diagnostics.
- Preserve the no-Tokio and no-rusqlite constraint unless a later ADR explicitly changes the architecture.
- Use SQLModel Rust plus FrankenSQLite for durable data; do not introduce a second storage stack.
- Use Asupersync for async edges and cancellation/budget behavior; do not smuggle in a Tokio executor.
- Keep JSON as the canonical public contract. TOON, Markdown, diagrams, and MCP are renderers or adapters over the same domain data.
- Mutating commands need dry-run/idempotency/audit behavior unless the task explicitly says otherwise.
- Add focused tests proportional to risk: unit tests for domain logic, contract/golden tests for public output, and integration/evaluation tests for cross-subsystem behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including the comprehensive testing and logging requirements.
design:
Suggested design approach:
- Keep scope narrow but complete: implement the named behavior, wire it into the relevant command/schema/test surfaces, and avoid unrelated refactors.

Implementation guidance:
- Read the surrounding modules and existing project conventions before editing.
- Prefer the planned crate boundaries from the comprehensive plan: CLI wiring in `ee-cli`, reusable domain/services in `ee-core`, models in `ee-models`, persistence in `ee-db`, output rendering in `ee-output`, and adapters in their own optional crates.
- Keep public contracts stable and versioned. Any data structure that leaves the process through CLI/MCP/hook/export should have a schema and at least one golden fixture.
- If a dependency or upstream Franken project is not ready, implement the smallest honest diagnostic/degraded path rather than faking behavior.
- Document any architectural exception with an ADR-oriented note and a verification hook.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance criteria:
- The behavior described by `Spike deterministic prompt-injection detection` is implemented or, for spikes, conclusively reported with a clear go/no-go recommendation.
- The implementation preserves local-first, no-Tokio, no-rusqlite, agent-native CLI behavior.
- Public command output, if any, validates against the stable response envelope and does not pollute stdout with diagnostics.

title: IdeaWizard: source-drift sentinel for memory provenance revalidation
description:
## IdeaWizard phase summary

Phase 1 grounding: AGENTS.md and README.md define ee as a local-first durable memory layer for agents. Live Beads and BV show heavy existing investment in RCH proof, swarm next-action planning, QoS lanes, support bundles, cache and plan economy, graph features, and calibration. The missing non-duplicative gap is that memories can remain syntactically valid while their source code evidence has drifted. Agents then keep retrieving stale procedural rules or implementation facts after the files, tests, APIs, or feature flags they describe have changed.

Phase 2 generated 30 candidate improvements across swarm-scale reliability, latency, memory quality, verification evidence, and operator ergonomics. The best 5 after winnowing were: source-drift sentinel for memory provenance, provenance snapshot hashing, affected-memory scoring, agent-visible revalidation queues, and no-mock drift replay tests.

Phase 3 next 10 considered: CRDT memory merge, reservation heatmaps, semantic drift dashboards, recall calibration, prompt-budget governors, hotset prewarm, live perf streams, RCH evidence normalization, hook-chain readiness, and QoS backpressure. Most overlap existing beads. The retained net-new cluster is source drift because no existing search result owned stale memories caused by codebase evolution.

Phase 4 overlap guard: this complements validity windows, revision dominance frontiers, conformal calibration, next-action planning, support bundles, and completion audit. It does not replace those surfaces. It answers a different question: does the source evidence behind this memory still match the current workspace tree.

Goal: add a deterministic, local-first drift sentinel that compares stored memory provenance against current source snapshots and emits bounded revalidation advice before stale memories are selected into search or context packs.

Non-goals: no automatic deletion, no silent tombstoning, no LLM API, no daemon requirement, no local Cargo, no git checkout or reset or stash or worktree, and no automatic Beads or Agent Mail mutation. The surface recommends and records evidence; humans or agents decide.

Phase 6 refinement: every child must include unit coverage, golden or e2e fixtures with detailed ee.test_event.v1 logging, deterministic output, redaction-safe evidence, and RCH-only Rust verification when executable.

title: drift-sentinel: affected-memory scoring and revalidation queue
description:
## Scope

Compute which memories are affected when source evidence drifts and rank them for explicit revalidation. This child owns the deterministic scoring layer, not the user-facing command.

Acceptance:
- Agents can see which memories need revalidation and why.
- The scoring remains deterministic and side-effect free.
- RCH-only Rust verification is recorded when RCH topology is healthy; otherwise static checks and the remote-required command are documented.

title: [MEDIUM] graph: snapshot source links are read outside the snapshot write lock
description: src/graph/mod.rs:1216 computes centrality and captures source links before persist_graph_snapshot acquires the advisory write lock at src/graph/mod.rs:1290 and starts the repeatable-read transaction at src/graph/mod.rs:1292. The link query itself happens at src/graph/mod.rs:1439-1441. A concurrent memory-link writer can change graph topology between that read and the snapshot insert, leaving a versioned snapshot whose content hash/source_generation describe stale data without being tied to a DB generation. Fix by acquiring the snapshot/source lock before reading links, or move source query, version allocation, content hash, and insert into one transaction tied to a durable source generation.

title: EE-CONTEXT-PERSIST-001: Wire `ee context` command path to persist pack records
description:
Follow-up/regression bead for the walking skeleton: `ee context` currently assembles a `ContextResponse` but the command path does not insert a durable `pack_records` row or item/omission rows. EE-151 closed the database/repository layer and explicitly noted that command wiring was blocked. That means `ee why` and pack-hash inspection can only explain packs seeded by tests or other paths, not normal user-visible context packs.

This bead wires the real command path so every successful non-dry-run `ee context` invocation persists its pack record, selected items, omissions, profile, query, token counts, degradation metadata, deterministic pack hash, and creator/audit context.
design: Use the existing pack record repository APIs rather than inventing a second persistence path. title: Swarm-scale operations: agent namespaces, verification provenance, and resource-aware context at 64+ core scale
description:
## Background

ee is meant to be the durable memory layer for coding agents, not an agent harness. The current backlog already covers agent-first JSON, handoff capsules, search honesty, degraded-code fixtures, and deterministic context packs. The next accretive layer for massive agent swarms is to make ee explicitly understand multi-agent workspaces without becoming the orchestrator.

This epic came from the 2026-05-12 idea-wizard pass after reviewing AGENTS.md, README.md, open beads, and bv graph health. It intentionally complements, rather than duplicates, the existing agent-UX overhaul.

## Goals

- Preserve per-agent provenance for memories, packs, handoffs, verification runs, and curation candidates.
- Let agents request context scoped to self, team, workspace, or trusted lanes without losing provenance.
- Record verification evidence as first-class memory-adjacent facts, including whether Cargo gates were truly RCH-offloaded and fail-closed.
- Add resource-aware pack assembly targets for large workspaces and many concurrent agents: predictable latency, bounded memory, deterministic output, and graceful degradation.
- Surface active coordination state, such as beads, file reservations, and handoff conflicts, as optional context evidence instead of relying on chat history.

## Non-goals

- Do not turn ee into a scheduler, autonomous worker, chat shell, or central service.
- Do not replace MCP Agent Mail, Beads, RCH, or the agent harness. ee consumes/export evidence; it does not own those systems.
- Do not require cloud services, paid LLM APIs, or a daemon for core CLI operation.

## Success criteria

A large multi-agent workspace can ask ee for a context pack and get a compact, explainable answer that says which agent produced each fact, whether the evidence is verified, what coordination state may conflict, and what resource budget was used to assemble the pack. All JSON remains deterministic and all generated text includes provenance.
notes:

## Epic acceptance — swarm-scale operations

When this epic closes, ee performs correctly under 64+ concurrent agents

that an orchestrator can read to make routing decisions.

## Children + status

| S0 (`bd-1zb7k.1`) | Agent identity provenance schema (producer metadata on every persisted artifact) | OPEN |

## Closure criteria

1. All 9 child beads closed.
2. **Concurrency invariants** (composes with L1 / bd-17c65.12.2):
   - 64 concurrent `ee remember` calls on the same workspace: no lost writes; audit chain shows all 64 events; one final memory count = 64.
   - Concurrent reads during heavy writes: read-consistency holds (snapshot isolation).
3. **Producer attribution** (S0):
   - Every memory, pack, candidate, verification event carries `producer.{agent_name, harness, model, run_id, session_id}`.
   - `ee why <id>` renders the producer chain.
4. **Trust-lane filtering** (S1):
   - `ee context --memory-scope team` actually filters to the team list; `scope_stats` block reports candidates_excluded_by_scope.
5. **Coordination snapshot** (S3):
   - `ee context "<task>" --coordination snapshot --json` includes Beads-ready entries + file reservations + Agent Mail threads with staleness markers.
6. **Resource SLOs** (S4):
   - Each profile carries documented budgets; pack assembly emits SLO posture; concurrent_pack_max enforced.
7. **Swarm fixtures** (S5):
   - `tests/fixtures/swarm_scale/{smoke_1k,mid_10k,large_100k}/` generated deterministically; CI smokes 1K.
8. **Schemas + drift gate** (S6):
   - 11 schemas in `docs/schemas/swarm/`; drift test red on divergence.
9. **Scale gates** (S7):
   - 1K + 10K (under feat) bench pass: budget table + determinism gates green.
10. **Consensus + conflicts** (S8):
    - Synthetic 3-agent-conflict fixture produces correct consensus + conflict entries.

## Cross-cutting integrations

- **bd-1ao9a** (volatile field registry): swarm fixtures must reproduce byte-identically across 3 captures.
- **N4** (Deterministic<Seed>): swarm bench must be deterministic AT SCALE; tie-break order stable under 10K-memory concurrent reads.
- **K2** (per-envelope JSON schemas): every swarm response shape has a schema file.
- **M5** (HMAC capsule): handoff between swarm agents uses integrity-verified capsules.

## User-visible payoff

A 64-agent swarm can share one workspace; an orchestrator reads `ee status` + `ee context --coordination snapshot` to understand who's doing what; producer attribution makes accountability concrete; resource profiles let large-scale agents bring their own SLO budgets.

## What's out of scope (intentional)

- Distributed multi-workspace federation (different epic, post-v0.2).
- Cross-machine capsule sync beyond a single shared filesystem.
- Real-time push notifications between agents — coordination is poll-based via the snapshot.

title: S0: Agent identity provenance schema for memories, packs, curation candidates, and verification events
description:
## What

Define the domain model and JSON contract for agent identity provenance across the memory lifecycle. Every memory-like or evidence-like record that can be produced by an agent should be able to say who produced it, from which harness, in which workspace, and under which run/session identity.

## Why

In a swarm, two agents can discover contradictory facts, run different verification gates, or operate against different branches/workspaces. Without explicit agent provenance, ee can only rank evidence by content-level features and timestamps. Agent-aware provenance lets downstream trust, handoff, and curation logic reason about source reliability without relying on chat transcripts.

## How

- Add domain types for `agent_identity`, `agent_run`, and `producer` metadata in `models` rather than CLI structs.
- Store enough stable fields for deterministic JSON: agent name when known, harness/program, model if supplied, workspace fingerprint, session/run id, source system, and observed timestamp.
- Preserve backwards migration semantics through the workspace schema migration path rather than compatibility shims.
- Keep this as metadata on durable facts; do not add agent scheduling or orchestration behavior.

## Risks

- Overfitting to MCP Agent Mail naming would make ee less harness-agnostic. Store source-system metadata, but keep names generic.
- Adding nullable fields without migration tests can create schema drift. Tie this to JSON schema and migration coverage.

## Acceptance

- JSON surfaces that emit memory/provenance evidence include deterministic producer metadata when available.
- Missing identity is explicit (`unknown`/`unobserved`) and never inferred silently.
- Unit tests cover known agent, unknown agent, imported CASS evidence, and manually remembered notes.
- A golden JSON fixture freezes the new producer metadata shape.

title: Swarm hot-path operations: latency explanations, cache prewarm, and burst admission
description:
## Background

This bead comes from a follow-up idea-wizard pass after reviewing AGENTS.md, README.md, current open beads, bv insights, and the existing bd-1zb7k swarm-scale epic. The backlog already covers producer provenance, trust lanes, coordination snapshots, resource profiles, swarm fixtures, JSON schemas, and scale gates. The remaining user-visible gap is operational: when 64+ agents hammer `ee search` and `ee context`, agents need to know why a request was slow, whether hot data can be warmed safely, and whether burst pressure should return structured backoff rather than silently degrading or fighting over local resources.

## Phase 2 30-to-5 winnow

Top 5 ideas retained: (1) explain-latency JSON for search/context stage timings; (2) redaction-safe cache hotset recorder and prewarm command; (3) burst admission/backoff posture for concurrent context pack assembly; (4) swarm hot-path e2e with p95/p99 budgets and J1 logs; (5) profile-aware cache budget conformance in status/doctor so agents can see when a host profile is under-provisioned.

Rejected or merged ideas included full daemon scheduling, replacing RCH, distributed cache federation, direct Agent Mail ownership, and autonomous orchestration because those violate the CLI-first memory-substrate boundary. Ideas already covered by existing beads were merged instead of duplicated: N9 mmap indexes, N10 SIMD BM25, N13 CUSUM scheduling, S4 resource profiles, and S7 10k/100k scale gates.

## Phase 3 next 10 considered

The next ten were: per-agent cache quotas, NUMA-aware pack shards, latency regression bisection, hotset export/import, cold-start wizard, cache shadow-mode comparison, read/write interference probes, query-plan fingerprints, pack renderer streaming, and support-bundle cache diagnostics. They were folded into the children here where they improve the operational surface without making ee the orchestrator.

## Acceptance

This epic closes when search/context hot paths expose deterministic latency explanations, redaction-safe hotset prewarm is available as an explicit CLI command, burst pressure returns structured backoff/admission posture, and a no-mock swarm e2e proves p95/p99 behavior with detailed J1 logging.

## Non-goals

No daemon requirement for core commands, no cross-machine cache federation, no deletion of cache files without explicit permission, no opaque adaptive mutation of source-of-truth data, and no replacement of Beads, RCH, Agent Mail, or the agent harness.

title: O1: ee perf explain-latency for search/context stage timing and cache posture
description:
## Goal

Add a deterministic read-only command such as `ee perf explain-latency --surface search|context --workspace . --json` that explains where time went for recent or replayed `ee search` and `ee context` requests.

## Why

Large swarms need to distinguish slow lexical retrieval, index status probes, pack scoring, redaction, rendering, cache misses, and artifact-lock contention. Today agents mostly see success/failure and coarse elapsed time. That makes performance incidents hard to route and encourages blind reruns.

## Scope

- Emit an `ee.perf.explain_latency.v1` envelope with stable fields: surface, query_shape_hash, workspace_generation, index_generation, profile, stage_timings, cache_status, degraded_codes, and recommended next probe.
- Use existing timing/J1 event data where available; otherwise compute a bounded synthetic replay over fixtures.
- Strip or hash volatile fields through the volatile-field registry.
- Keep the command read-only and deterministic for the same captured evidence.

## Tests

- Unit tests for stage aggregation and volatile-field stripping.
- JSON contract snapshot for search and context surfaces.
- E2E block that runs search/context, captures J1 logs, then explains latency with no mocks.
- Negative test for missing evidence returning a structured recovery action, not fake success.

## Non-goals

No profiler daemon, no sampling agent process, no automatic tuning, and no source-of-truth mutation.

title: O2: Redaction-safe hotset recorder for search/context cache prewarm
description:
## Goal

Persist a redaction-safe hotset record that captures frequent query shapes, memory IDs, index generations, profile tier, and hit counts without storing raw query text or memory content.

## Why

The code already has search-side hotset/prewarm primitives, but swarm operators need a durable and auditable source for what should be warmed before a read-heavy burst. Hotsets must be provenance-rich and safe to put in support bundles.

## Scope

- Add a small DB-backed or artifact-backed hotset manifest schema, for example `ee.cache.hotset.v1`.
- Record query_shape_hash and memory_id/content_hash references, not plaintext snippets.
- Track workspace_generation/index_generation so stale hotsets are rejected rather than silently used.
- Add status output showing candidate count, admitted count, rejected stale entries, memory budget, and redaction safety evidence.

## Tests

- Unit tests proving no raw secret values, raw query text, or memory content enter the hotset manifest.
- Determinism test: same captured search/context traffic yields byte-identical hotset JSON after volatile stripping.
- Contract snapshot for `ee.cache.hotset.v1`.
- Fixture with stale index generation returning structured stale-hotset degradation.

## Non-goals

No cross-machine cache federation, no cache file deletion, and no prewarming from untrusted plaintext logs.

title: O3: Explicit ee cache prewarm command with profile budgets and stale-hotset repair
description:
## Goal

Expose an explicit CLI surface such as `ee cache prewarm --workspace . --from-hotset <path|latest> --profile lean|standard|swarm_heavy --json` that warms derived search/context cache entries within configured memory budgets.

## Why

Prewarm should be opt-in and explainable. Agents preparing a large swarm run need a safe command that says what was warmed, what was skipped, why, and how much memory budget was consumed. This is especially useful on high-RAM hosts without making cache mutation implicit in ordinary reads.

## Scope

- Wire existing cache/hotset prewarm primitives into a CLI command.
- Require generation matching unless `--allow-stale-hotset` is explicitly supplied; stale use emits a high-visibility degraded entry.
- Emit `ee.cache.prewarm.v1` with requested/admitted/rejected counts, budget source, memory pressure, latency estimate, and redaction-safety summary.
- Keep cache writes derived and rebuildable; no source-of-truth data mutation.

## Tests

- Unit tests for budget admission, stale generation rejection, and critical memory pressure bypass.
- CLI contract snapshot for successful prewarm and stale-hotset error.
- E2E script creates a hotset, prewarms it, runs a read burst, and logs before/after latency evidence.
- Support-bundle test includes manifest hashes without raw content.

## Non-goals

No daemon requirement, no automatic background warming, no deleting cache files, and no warming from plaintext secrets.

title: O4: Context burst admission governor with queue-depth posture and structured backoff
description:
## Goal

Make concurrent `ee context` pack assembly expose explicit admission posture under burst pressure: current queue depth, configured cap, retry-after hint, and whether the command waited, succeeded, or returned a structured backoff error.

## Why

On a 64-agent host, context assembly can be CPU and memory heavy even when reads are safe. Agents need a deterministic way to back off instead of stampeding the same workspace, and orchestrators need posture fields they can read without parsing stderr.

## Scope

- Extend the existing pack slot/process gate behavior into a documented status block and error shape.
- Emit queue-depth/cap/retry_after_ms in JSON success and error envelopes when admission was relevant.
- Add profile hooks so lean/standard/swarm_heavy can set different concurrent pack caps.
- Add recovery actions: retry with backoff, lower pack profile, or run prewarm first.

## Tests

- Unit tests for cap=1 contention, retry-after determinism, and recovery action shape.
- E2E with concurrent context requests using J1 logs; all requests must either succeed or fail with the structured admission code.
- Determinism test that repeated contention fixture emits byte-identical scrubbed JSON.
- Doctor/status contract showing current admission profile.

## Non-goals

No central scheduler, no daemon requirement, no killing other agents, and no hidden global process cleanup.

title: O5: No-mock swarm hot-path e2e with prewarm, burst admission, and p95/p99 logging
description:
## Goal

Add a no-mock e2e script, for example `scripts/e2e_overhaul/swarm_hot_path.sh`, that drives a realistic read-heavy swarm burst and proves the hot-path operational surfaces work together.

## Scenario

1. Seed a deterministic workspace with enough memories to exercise search, pack selection, provenance rendering, redaction checks, and cache admission.
2. Capture or synthesize a redaction-safe hotset.
3. Run cache prewarm under a selected resource profile.
4. Launch concurrent `ee search` and `ee context` readers at a bounded fanout.
5. Assert every request either succeeds or returns the structured burst-admission backoff shape.
6. Emit J1 JSONL events with p50/p95/p99 latency, cache admission counts, queue depth, degraded code counts, and response hashes.

## Acceptance

- Script runs without mocks against the real binary and a temp workspace.
- Summary JSON uses a stable schema such as `ee.e2e.swarm_hot_path.v1`.
- Determinism mode runs the same fixture three times and compares scrubbed response hashes.
- CI can run a small tier by default and a larger 10k-memory tier behind an opt-in env var.
- Failures point to O1/O2/O3/O4 surfaces rather than opaque shell output.

## Non-goals

No destructive cleanup beyond temp workspaces created by the script, no daemon dependency, and no benchmarking claims beyond the declared fixture budgets.

title: P: Disk-pressure and artifact retention governance for agent swarms
description: Idea-wizard Phase 2/3 result from 2026-05-13 disk-pressure incident. During active multi-agent work, the internal macOS data volume reached 100% capacity; br began returning SQLite disk I/O errors, Agent Mail was already unavailable, and RCH/build/test coordination became fragile. AGENTS.md already documents that Cargo output should go to external NVMe, but the broader swarm still generates local target trees, e2e artifacts, Agent Mail forensics/backups, Codex logs, support bundles, and verification debris. Goal: make disk pressure a first-class, agent-readable posture before it blocks Beads, Agent Mail, RCH, or ee itself. Phase 2 generated 30 ideas and winnowed to five best: (1) disk-pressure posture and repair planner, (2) non-destructive artifact relocation manifests, (3) verification artifact retention budgets, (4) RCH/build admission disk guard, (5) Agent Mail archive/offload policy. Phase 3 next-best additions added: cache hotset size accounting, support-bundle size budgets, per-agent scratch quotas, cleanup dry-run JSON, and no-deletion e2e harnesses. This epic operationalizes the non-overlapping pieces not already covered by O1-O5 hot-path latency/cache beads or J11 verification provenance beads. Non-negotiable: no automatic deletion. Every repair action must be explicit, auditable, reversible where possible, and safe under the AGENTS.md no-file-deletion rule.

title: P7: Agent-harness runaway log pressure detection and tail-preserving repair plans
description:
Idea-wizard Phase 2/3/4 result from the 2026-05-18 local disk-pressure incident. The existing disk-pressure epic already detects Codex roots and artifact budgets, but the live blocker showed a sharper failure mode: an active agent harness log can grow to hundreds of GB, keep the internal APFS volume at 100%, and make Beads, Agent Mail, and RCH brittle even when Cargo output is correctly routed to the external USB-NVMe drive.

Scope:
- Extend ee diag disk-pressure --json to classify active agent-harness log pressure separately from ordinary artifact pressure.
- Detect known harness log roots such as ~/.codex/log and report oversized current logs with role=agent_harness_log, open-handle status when discoverable, byte size, owning process summary, and whether the path is on the workspace filesystem.
- Emit only preservation-oriented repair actions: ask_human, preserve_tail_copy, rotate_with_manifest, move_preserve, or noop. No automatic deletion, truncation, or unlinking.
- The recommended remediation must be explicit-command text for a human to approve, not an action ee performs silently. It should preserve a configurable tail before suggesting truncation/rotation of an active log.
- Include guidance that CARGO_TARGET_DIR/TMPDIR can be correct while the host is still blocked by harness logs on the internal disk.

Acceptance criteria:
- JSON remains schema-versioned and sideEffectFree=true.
- Active-log recovery actions include enough evidence for a human to approve or reject: path, size, filesystem, process ids or unavailable reason, tail byte count, manifest destination, and exact mutation category.
- Secret redaction rules apply to command text and paths where needed; no log contents are read except an optional size-bounded tail checksum in test fixtures.
- Unit tests cover active open log, closed oversized log, missing lsof capability, external-volume log, and no-pressure cases.
- Static docs explain the no-file-deletion policy and why active log truncation requires explicit human approval.
- RCH/Cargo proofs are remote-only; if RCH is unavailable, record static checks and leave verifier status honest.

title: Host calibration and topology-aware resource profiles for 256GB+ agent swarms
description:
## Background

This bead comes from a follow-up idea-wizard pass after reading AGENTS.md/README.md earlier in this active goal, inspecting the current Beads backlog, and checking bv robot insights. Existing work already covers swarm producer provenance, trust lanes, coordination snapshots, cache prewarm, burst admission, disk-pressure repair planning, support bundles, graph features, and static resource profiles. The remaining gap is calibration: ee should be able to describe the actual host and RCH topology it is running on, then recommend deterministic resource budgets instead of relying only on static labels.

## Phase 2 30-to-5 winnow

Top ideas retained: (1) a read-only host-profile schema and command that records CPU/RAM/disk/build-target/RCH topology without leaking sensitive paths in default output; (2) an explicit calibration harness for search/context/pack/index hot paths with deterministic fixture sizes; (3) a profile recommender that maps observed capacity to existing resource profiles and explains budget deltas; (4) status/doctor integration that reports calibrated vs configured posture without mutating config; (5) golden and e2e fixtures that prove deterministic output using synthetic host manifests.

Rejected or merged ideas: daemon scheduling, NUMA worker pinning, cross-machine cache federation, automatic cleanup, and direct RCH replacement are out of scope. RCH disk admission is already covered by the P-series; hot-path admission/prewarm is already covered by O-series. This epic should consume those signals where useful rather than recreate them.

## Phase 3 next 10 considered

The next ten were: per-agent CPU lane quotas, cold-start recommendations, remote-worker capability fingerprints, target-dir/scratch-dir drift detection, host-class labels for support bundles, calibration artifact retention, microbench regression bisection, cache-size what-if reports, profile override audit events, and large-machine documentation examples. These are folded into the children where they strengthen the calibrated-profile contract without making ee an orchestrator.

## Acceptance

This epic closes when ee can emit a deterministic host-calibration response, recommend an effective resource profile with explainable reasons, surface calibrated posture in status/doctor, and validate the surface through synthetic host fixtures plus a no-mock e2e path.

## Non-goals

No daemon requirement, no autonomous scheduling, no file deletion or cleanup, no mutation of source-of-truth memories, no replacement for RCH/Beads/Agent Mail, and no CPU-heavy calibration in normal commands.

## Goal

Define the machine-facing contract for the calibrated resource-profile recommender before implementation touches status, doctor, or support-bundle surfaces.

## Scope

- Specify the additive report shape that H3 exposes to H4: configuredProfile, recommendedProfile, effectiveProfile, budgetDeltas[], reasonCodes[], calibrationFreshness, topologyWarnings[], and degraded[].

- Decide whether the schema is a standalone ee.host_calibration.recommendation.v1 document or an embedded block under an existing profile/status schema, and document that choice in the bead.

## Acceptance

Future implementers can add the recommender without guessing field names, status semantics, or reason-code spelling. The schema plan is deterministic, redaction-safe by default, and explicitly says that the recommender never mutates config.

title: H3.2: deterministic host-class classifier from host profile and calibration evidence
description:
## Goal

Implement or specify the pure classifier that maps ee.host_profile.v1 plus optional calibration evidence into a stable host class used by the recommender.

## Scope

- Consume redacted host-profile inputs from H1 and synthetic calibration fixture summaries from H2.
- Classify at least portable, laptop, workstation, 256gb-local, and rch-only topology classes.
- Treat missing, stale, or partial calibration as explicit conservative posture, not as a silent default.
- Preserve deterministic ordering and stable tie-breaking when multiple class signals apply.
- Keep the classifier pure and side-effect free; it must not probe live hardware during unit tests.

## Acceptance

Given the same host-profile fixture and calibration evidence, the classifier returns byte-identical hostClass, confidence, and reasonCodes. Missing or stale calibration produces a conservative class plus a repair action instead of a misleading high-resource recommendation.

title: H3.3: budget delta recommender for context, cache, graph, index, and burst admission
description:
## Goal

Map the classified host posture into concrete recommended budgets for the surfaces named by H3 without mutating configuration.

## Scope

- Recommend context-pack budget, cache sizing posture, graph snapshot memory posture, index rebuild concurrency, and burst-admission limits.
- Emit budgetDeltas[] comparing configuredProfile, recommendedProfile, and effectiveProfile with stable numeric units and reason codes.
- Be conservative when target-dir, tmpdir, disk, or RCH topology signals are degraded.
- Include large-host behavior for 256GB+/64-core swarms without making that path the default on smaller machines.
- Keep output explainable enough for ee status, doctor, and support bundles to display compactly in H4.

## Acceptance

The recommender returns deterministic deltas and clear reasons for each changed or unchanged budget. It can say no change is recommended, and it never implies that ee has already applied a recommended profile.

title: H3.4: calibration freshness, degradation, and repair-action contract
description:
## Goal

Define and implement the conservative degraded posture for stale, missing, partial, or contradictory calibration evidence.

## Scope

- Specify freshness thresholds and stable statuses for fresh, stale, missing, synthetic-only, and contradictory calibration evidence.
- Decide which conditions belong in degraded[] versus ordinary reasonCodes, following the AGENTS.md degraded-code taxonomy rules.
- Add repairActions[] that point to explicit calibration commands or RCH/status probes without proposing deletion, cleanup, or config mutation.
- Ensure RCH topology blockers are reported as blockers for calibration confidence, not as proof that the local host is weak.
- Add failure-mode fixtures and taxonomy rows if new degraded codes are emitted.

## Acceptance

Agents can distinguish a real high-resource recommendation from a conservative fallback caused by stale or unavailable evidence. The repair text is actionable and non-destructive, and repeated runs produce stable degraded/reason ordering.

title: Coordination substrate resilience: diagnose unavailable Agent Mail, stale Beads, and worker-specific RCH topology
description:
## Background

This bead comes from the continuation idea-wizard pass on 2026-05-14 after rereading AGENTS.md/README.md, inspecting the current swarm-scale backlog, checking bv robot insights, and observing live coordination failures in this session: MCP Agent Mail health checks fail with a transport error, Beads reports JSONL newer than the DB, and RCH can be healthy overall while a specific worker/path topology fails remote Cargo verification. Existing S3 coordination snapshots model imported Beads/Agent Mail state, S2 records verification evidence, P-series covers disk pressure, and H-series covers host calibration. The remaining gap is coordination substrate resilience: an agent-readable diagnosis and fallback evidence story when the coordination channels themselves are degraded.

## Phase 2 30-to-5 winnow

Top ideas retained: (1) a read-only coordination-substrate diagnostic that probes Agent Mail, Beads freshness, file-reservation availability, and RCH remote viability without mutating state; (2) a fallback coordination evidence ledger for incidents agents otherwise only remember in chat; (3) explicit Beads stale-state guardrails so stale DB/JSONL situations are surfaced before issue mutation or context packing; (4) RCH worker-topology diagnostics that distinguish fleet health from worker/path-specific E327 failures; (5) deterministic fixtures/e2e coverage for unavailable Agent Mail, stale Beads, and remote-required Cargo blocked by topology.

## Phase 3 next 10 considered

The next ten were: stable agent identity recovery, contact-handshake replay, fallback outbox files, inbox ack debt reporting, reservation conflict aging, Beads import/flush repair actions, RCH worker affinity hints, support-bundle redaction for coordination logs, coordination degraded-code taxonomy, and no-live-service e2e fixtures. These are folded into the child beads where they strengthen the diagnostic/fallback contract without turning ee into an orchestrator.

## Non-goals

Do not replace Agent Mail, Beads, RCH, or the agent harness. Do not create a daemon requirement. Do not send messages, acquire reservations, mutate Beads, run Cargo, delete files, or perform cleanup as part of normal diagnostics. All repair suggestions must be explicit commands or structured recovery actions for the agent/human to run intentionally.

## Acceptance

This epic closes when ee can emit deterministic JSON explaining coordination substrate health, persist or import fallback coordination evidence with provenance, warn about stale Beads state before agents trust it, distinguish RCH fleet-ready from worker/path-topology-blocked verification, and validate these surfaces through unit, golden, and no-live-service e2e tests with detailed logging.

title: C1: Extend ee swarm brief with coordination-substrate resilience posture
description:
## What

Extend the existing read-only `ee swarm brief --json` surface so it reports coordination-substrate resilience, not just source availability. The extension should cover Agent Mail MCP health/snapshot posture, Beads DB-vs-JSONL freshness, Beads dependency-cycle summary, and RCH remote verification posture. If a separate `ee diag coordination-substrate` alias is added later, it should delegate to this same domain model rather than creating a parallel report.

## Why

ADR 0027 and `src/core/swarm_brief.rs` already define the right product boundary: one-shot, read-only, advisory coordination preflight. During swarm work an agent can be blocked by coordination failures even when `ee` itself is healthy. Today those failures live in chat: Agent Mail transport errors, stale Beads warnings, or RCH fleet-ready-but-worker-blocked behavior. A stronger swarm brief lets agents and orchestrators decide whether to trust live coordination state, use imported snapshots, or record fallback evidence.

## Existing anchors

- `src/core/swarm_brief.rs` owns `SwarmBriefReport`, source collection, degraded source codes, and deterministic finalization.
- `src/cli/mod.rs` already exposes `ee swarm brief` with source selection, Agent Mail snapshot input, RCH opt-in, timeout, and `--require-sources`.
- ADR 0027 documents the read-only boundary and source list.
- Existing failure-mode fixtures include `agent_mail_unavailable`, `beads_unavailable`, `bv_unavailable`, and `rch_unavailable` for `swarm brief`.

## Implementation notes

- Keep the surface read-only: no message sends, no reservations, no Beads imports/flushes, no RCH jobs that compile code.
- Prefer bounded probes and cached/tool-reported status; every live probe must have a timeout and a degraded fallback.
- Redact absolute home paths by default; expose full paths only under an explicit diagnostic verbosity flag if the existing support-bundle policy allows it.
- Output must keep the response envelope and stable field order.
- Model new states as extensions of existing source snapshots/degraded records where possible.

## Acceptance

- `ee swarm brief --json --include-rch` distinguishes basic source unavailable from substrate-specific postures such as Beads stale DB/JSONL and RCH worker-topology blocked.
- Agent Mail transport failure produces a structured degraded code instead of command failure.
- Beads JSONL-newer-than-DB state is visible with recovery actions.
- RCH fleet-ready/worker-topology-blocked are distinct states.
- Unit tests cover all posture combinations and golden tests lock the JSON contract.

title: C2: Coordination fallback evidence ledger for unavailable or stale substrates
description:
## What

Add a coordination fallback evidence model and import path for incidents that agents otherwise lose when Agent Mail is unavailable: failed health checks, skipped acknowledgements, stale Beads warnings, file-reservation uncertainty, and remote verification coordination blockers.

## Why

When Agent Mail is down, agents still need a durable way to tell future agents: "I tried to coordinate, this substrate was unavailable, here is the evidence, and here is what I did instead." This should not mutate memories silently or pretend to be a successful coordination event. It should be explicit evidence that can appear in `ee why`, support bundles, and coordination context.

## Implementation notes

- Reuse the existing provenance/audit style from verification evidence where possible.
- Store summaries and hashes, not full raw inboxes or secret-bearing logs.
- Represent status as `available | unavailable | stale | blocked | unknown` with a reason code and source kind.
- Link optional Beads IDs and agent identity metadata, but keep the model independent of Beads and Agent Mail runtime availability.

## Acceptance

- `ee coordination evidence ingest --file/--stdin --json` or an equivalent agreed CLI exists and is idempotent by content hash.
- `ee why` and support-bundle surfaces can include linked coordination fallback evidence.
- Missing live Agent Mail never prevents ingesting fallback evidence.
- Tests cover unavailable, stale, blocked, unknown, idempotent replay, and redaction behavior.

title: C3: Beads freshness guardrails for coordination snapshots and diagnostics
description:
## What

Make Beads freshness a first-class coordination signal inside `ee` diagnostics and coordination snapshots. Detect JSONL-newer-than-DB, DB-newer-than-JSONL, dependency cycles, and tracker read errors, then surface them as structured degraded codes with recovery actions.

## Why

This session repeatedly saw `br` warnings that JSONL was newer than the DB. Agents can accidentally make planning decisions from stale tracker state or flush a stale DB over newer JSONL if they are careless. `ee` should not own Beads, but when it consumes Beads snapshots it must say whether the tracker evidence is fresh enough to trust.

## Implementation notes

- Consume `br sync --status --json`/snapshot metadata where available; do not run mutating Beads commands.
- Treat known pre-existing dependency cycles as warnings with IDs, not fatal errors for unrelated context queries.
- Include structured recovery actions such as import-only, inspect cycles, or retry with explicit snapshot file.
- Coordinate with the volatile-field registry so timestamps and local paths do not break determinism tests.

## Acceptance

- New degraded codes are documented with failure-mode fixtures.
- Coordination snapshot JSON includes Beads freshness posture and issue-count provenance.
- Unit tests cover fresh, jsonl_newer, db_newer, unreadable tracker, and cycles-present states.
- E2E uses synthetic `.beads` fixtures and never deletes real tracker files.

title: C4: RCH worker-topology blocked verification diagnostics and fixtures
description:
## What

Add a diagnostic surface and fixture suite for RCH worker topology failures that block remote-required Cargo verification even when the overall RCH fleet reports ready. The key case is worker/path-specific topology preflight failure such as RCH-E327.

## Why

The current objective requires all Cargo builds/tests to be offloaded. In practice RCH can select a worker whose project-root topology is invalid for this checkout, then fail closed because `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1` is set. Agents need to record and explain that as `remote_required_but_worker_topology_blocked`, not as a generic compile failure or a successful verification.

## Implementation notes

- Do not run Cargo as part of the diagnostic. Use RCH status/diagnose metadata, captured failure logs, or synthetic fixtures.
- Distinguish fleet status, selected worker, requested worker hints, canonical/alias root mapping, and fail-closed behavior.
- Feed the result into verification evidence closure guidance where applicable.
- Include recovery actions that point to worker root setup or worker selection config, without auto-draining/disabling workers.

## Acceptance

- JSON distinguishes `remote_ready`, `no_remote_workers`, `worker_unreachable`, `worker_topology_blocked`, and `fallback_prevented`.
- RCH-E327 fixture maps to a blocked verification posture with worker identity and redacted root metadata.
- Closure guidance rejects bead closure when remote-required Cargo evidence is topology-blocked unless an alternate remote pass exists.
- Unit, golden, and no-Cargo e2e fixtures cover the matrix.

title: Swarm incident drills: deterministic outage and recovery rehearsal
description:
## Background

Idea-wizard planning pass by RubyWolf on 2026-05-15 after reviewing AGENTS.md/README.md context, live Agent Mail, bv triage, and the open Beads graph. Existing plans already cover hot-path latency/prewarm (bd-1zb7k.10), disk-pressure governance (bd-1zb7k.11), host calibration (bd-1zb7k.12), coordination-substrate resilience (bd-1zb7k.13), graph insights, and the N-series ambition portfolio. The remaining gap is rehearsal: agents need deterministic incident fixtures that prove the recovery guidance still works when multiple substrates degrade together.

## Phase 2 30-to-5 winnow

The strongest five ideas after scoring robustness, reliability, performance, ergonomics, usefulness, accretion, and pragmatism were: (1) a swarm incident scenario catalog with synthetic Agent Mail, Beads, RCH, disk, and hot-path pressure fixtures; (2) a read-only replay command that feeds those fixtures through existing diagnostic/reporting surfaces; (3) a recovery-action verifier that asserts every emitted repair command is explicit, non-destructive, ordered, and tied to evidence; (4) a no-live-service e2e drill harness with J1-style logs and p95/p99 timing for diagnosis; (5) support-bundle and handoff integration so agents can carry incident context across compaction or handoff without copying chat transcripts.

## Phase 3 next 10 considered

The next ten were: ack-debt drills, stale reservation aging drills, disk-full Beads write-denial drills, RCH fleet-ready-but-worker-blocked drills, context burst backoff drills, redaction failure drills, support-bundle size-budget drills, host-profile mismatch drills, synthetic multi-agent conflict drills, and incident replay diffing across ee versions. These are folded into the child beads rather than filed as separate low-signal work.

## Overlap decisions

This epic deliberately does not duplicate bd-1zb7k.10/11/12/13. Those epics define the underlying signals and recovery surfaces. This epic verifies cross-substrate behavior from fixtures and drills, with no live service dependency and no automatic cleanup or orchestration.

## Non-goals

Do not replace Agent Mail, Beads, RCH, or the agent harness. Do not mutate live coordination state during replay. Do not run local Cargo. Do not delete files. Do not introduce a daemon requirement. Do not make ee an autonomous incident responder; it remains a local-first diagnostic and memory substrate.

## Acceptance

This epic closes when synthetic incident fixtures can be replayed deterministically, emitted recovery actions are mechanically checked for safety and evidence, the drill harness produces detailed logs without live services, and support bundles/handoff capsules can include redacted incident summaries with stable schema coverage.

This epic stays focused on cross-substrate incident drills, not duplicating the underlying diagnostics.

Pass 2 boundary: kept ee CLI-first and read-only for replay. No daemon requirement, no live Agent Mail messaging, no Beads mutation, no RCH job, no cleanup, no deletion, no local Cargo fallback.

Pass 3 dependency sanity: I1 defines the schema/fixtures; I2 replays them; I3 verifies recovery-action safety; I4 is the integrated no-live-service drill; I5 carries compact evidence into support bundles/handoff. Cross-links intentionally wait for existing C/O/P/M surfaces where needed.

Pass 4 test coverage: every child has explicit unit/contract/golden/e2e expectations and detailed logging. Unsafe recovery commands get negative fixtures, not just prose policy.

Pass 5 user value: the result gives future agents a rehearsal suite for the exact failure shape seen in this swarm: Agent Mail degraded, Beads freshness hazards, RCH topology blocked, disk pressure, and bursty context traffic. This should reduce chat-only incident memory and make recovery evidence portable across compaction and handoff.

## What

Create a recovery-action verifier for incident replay outputs. It should validate that repair guidance is explicit, ordered, evidence-linked, non-destructive by default, and does not claim live remediation happened during replay.

## Why

AGENTS.md forbids deletion and dangerous cleanup without explicit human approval. Incident diagnostics are only useful if their recovery guidance is safe enough for agents to trust under pressure.

## Requirements

- Contract test helper checks every recovery action for stable fields: priority, kind, summary, command or manualStep, evidence, destructive flag, and preconditions.
- Commands that contain deletion, reset, clean, stash, checkout, rebase, or local Cargo fallback are rejected unless marked manual_human_approval_required and never emitted as an automatic next step.
- Verifier checks action order: observe first, repair/refresh second, retry verification last.
- Include negative fixtures proving unsafe recovery plans fail the verifier.

## Acceptance

All incident fixtures pass the verifier; deliberately unsafe fixture examples fail with clear diagnostics and line-level fixture pointers.

title: Swarm verification reuse: advisory ledger for RCH/test evidence dedupe
description:
## Background

Continuation idea-wizard pass by RubyWolf on 2026-05-15 after refreshing AGENTS.md constraints, current Agent Mail, br ready/in-progress state, bv graph health, and existing idea-wizard epics. Existing beads already cover hot-path latency/cache/admission (bd-1zb7k.10), disk-pressure governance (bd-1zb7k.11), host calibration/resource profiles (bd-1zb7k.12), and coordination substrate resilience including RCH topology diagnostics (bd-1zb7k.13). The non-overlapping gap observed in the live swarm is verification reuse: several agents independently launch focused RCH cargo tests, broad contract tests, or closure probes because they cannot tell whether an equivalent run is already in flight or just passed against the same source/command fingerprint.

## Phase 2 30-to-5 winnow

Top retained ideas: (1) a verification-run ledger built from J1 test-event artifact manifests and explicit agent closeout evidence; (2) command/source fingerprinting that can prove when a focused RCH result is reusable; (3) duplicate-run advisory that says wait/reuse/rerun without killing another agent's process; (4) compact closeout capsules for Beads comments and support bundles; (5) a no-mock multi-agent verification e2e that demonstrates dedupe and reuse under concurrent focused-test pressure.

Rejected or merged ideas: a central scheduler, daemon-owned worker queue, automatic process termination, RCH replacement, and hidden Cargo fallback all violate the CLI-first memory substrate boundary or AGENTS.md RCH-only rule. Disk admission stays with bd-1zb7k.11, worker topology stays with bd-1zb7k.13, and latency/cache work stays with bd-1zb7k.10.

## Phase 3 next 10 considered

The next ten were worker affinity hints, per-agent verification quotas, stale-artifact quarantine, source-diff bisection, CI parity import, Beads auto-comment drafting, failure clustering, compile-cache reuse explanations, artifact retention policy, and verification debt dashboards. They are folded into this subtree only where they strengthen advisory evidence reuse without making ee an orchestrator.

## Acceptance

This epic closes when ee can ingest or read verification evidence, compute stable command/source/artifact fingerprints, report equivalent in-flight or recent RCH-focused runs, emit a deterministic reuse advisory, and prove the behavior with unit/golden/no-mock e2e coverage. It must never run local Cargo, kill processes, delete artifacts, mutate source-of-truth memories, or replace Agent Mail/Beads/RCH.

## Phase 6 refinement constraints

Keep the surface advisory and read-mostly. All heavy Cargo verification still goes through RCH. All JSON output strips volatile fields and includes provenance. Tests must include detailed J1 logging and failure-mode fixtures for stale source hash, mismatched command hash, missing artifact manifest, and remote-required run unavailable.

title: V1: Verification evidence ledger schema and artifact-manifest importer
description:
## Goal

Define an ee.verification.run.v1 record that can be built from existing J1 ee.test_event.v1 command/artifact_manifest events, explicit retained artifact manifests, and agent-provided closeout snippets. The ledger is evidence, not execution: it records what ran, where, with what source and command fingerprints, and what outcome was observed.

## Why

Agents currently repeat focused RCH Cargo tests because proof is trapped in chat, Beads comments, or raw logs. A small normalized record lets later agents ask whether an equivalent remote run already exists without trusting prose.

## Scope

- Stable fields: schema, run_id, bead_id, agent_name, source_hash, command_hash, command_argv_hash, cargo_target_dir_hash_or_class, execution_substrate, worker_host, started_at, finished_at, exit_code, stdout_hash, stderr_excerpt_hash, artifact_manifest_hash, retained_log_path_hash, and provenance.
- Import from J1 JSONL logs and scripts/lib/e2e_logger.sh artifact_manifest fields where present.
- Reject records with raw stdout/stderr/content bytes; keep hashes and bounded excerpts only.
- Strip or classify local paths through the volatile-field registry so deterministic tests can compare scrubbed output.

## Tests

Unit tests for fingerprint construction, volatile stripping, missing manifest errors, and raw-secret/raw-output rejection. JSON schema/golden contract for one RCH run and one shell/static verifier. No local Cargo in tests except through RCH when a Rust gate is required.

## Non-goals

No process spawning, no RCH replacement, no Beads mutation, and no claim that a run is reusable until V2 computes equivalence.

title: V2: Equivalent RCH run fingerprinting and reuse advisory
description:
## Goal

Given a requested verification command, report whether an equivalent RCH or shell/static run is already in flight, recently passed, recently failed, or stale against the current source and command fingerprint.

## Why

The live swarm repeatedly launched overlapping focused cargo tests and broad contract tests because agents could not inspect reusable evidence. A deterministic advisory lets an agent wait for an in-flight equivalent run, cite a recent green run, or rerun only when the source hash, command hash, feature flags, or target profile changed.

## Scope

- Compute equivalence from source_hash, command_hash, feature/profile hash, workspace generation where relevant, execution substrate, and explicit strictness flags.
- Emit ee.verification.reuse_advisory.v1 with status: reusable_pass, reusable_fail, in_flight, stale_source, mismatched_command, missing_evidence, or rerun_required.
- Include repair actions: wait for agent/thread, rerun with RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1, broaden/narrow command, or import retained J1 log.
- Never kill, pause, throttle, or mutate another agent's process. The output is advisory only.

## Tests

Unit tests for each advisory status; golden snapshots for reusable_pass and stale_source; fixture for command hash mismatch; deterministic scrubbed output across three runs.

## Dependencies

Depends on V1 ledger schema/importer.

description:
## Goal

Add a no-mock e2e harness that exercises verification reuse under realistic multi-agent pressure without launching uncontrolled local Cargo or deleting artifacts.

## Scenario

1. Seed a temp workspace and synthetic J1 verification logs with two equivalent focused RCH test runs, one stale source hash, one command mismatch, and one in-flight placeholder.
2. Run the ledger importer.
3. Ask for reuse advisory for a matching focused cargo test command and for a mismatched broad test command.
4. Assert the matching command returns reusable_pass or in_flight as appropriate, while mismatches return structured rerun_required reasons.
5. Render a closeout capsule and verify it contains hashes, worker/substrate metadata, and caveats without raw stdout/stderr/content.

- The harness runs against the real ee binary and temp files; no mocks for JSON parsing, schema validation, or capsule rendering.

Depends on V1, V2, V3, and V4.

title: Swarm ownership posture: reservation-aware compile blockers and dirty-tree risk map
description:
# Idea-wizard Phase 5 operationalization: swarm ownership posture

## Background

Large shared-agent sessions repeatedly waste RCH slots when one agent runs focused tests that fail at crate compile because another agent currently owns the first failing file. The current process relies on humans reading Agent Mail threads and manually correlating the compiler path with file reservations, Beads assignees, and dirty-tree state. This creates duplicate blocked verification lanes and noisy coordination updates.

This feature makes that correlation explicit and machine-readable: `ee` should be able to report, without mutating anything, which agent/bead appears to own the first compile blocker or dirty file risk, what evidence supports that attribution, and what a safe next action is. It complements, but does not replace, RCH, Beads, or Agent Mail.

## Product intent

A coding agent should be able to run a read-only preflight after an RCH failure or before claiming work and see a concise advisory such as: first compile error is in `src/graph/algorithms.rs`; Agent Mail reservation holder is StormyCove; related bead is bd-igvt.7; recommended action is message holder or wait, not launch another RCH run.

## Non-goals

- Do not run Cargo or RCH from this feature. Consume explicit evidence inputs or existing metadata only.
- Do not claim, close, reopen, or reserve files automatically. Suggested commands are advisory.
- Do not expose raw Agent Mail bodies or raw compiler logs in support bundles. Keep hashes, paths, subjects/counts, and concise excerpts only.
- Do not make `ee` an agent orchestrator. This is diagnostic posture for agents that already use Beads and Agent Mail.

## Success criteria

- Read-only JSON surfaces attribute compile blockers and dirty-tree risks to active reservations/beads where possible.
- Output is deterministic, redaction-safe, and includes provenance for each attribution.
- No-mock tests cover Agent Mail reservation snapshots, Beads assignments, git dirty files, and RCH/test-event evidence.
- The feature improves swarm throughput by steering agents away from duplicate blocked verification attempts.

title: O-P3: Dirty-tree ownership map in ee swarm brief and support-bundle summaries
description:
## Goal

Extend the read-only coordination posture surface so agents can see which dirty files are likely theirs, reserved by another agent, unowned, or tracker-only. This should appear in `ee swarm brief` full output and the redacted support-bundle summary without exposing file contents or mail bodies.

## Requirements

- Add a `fileOwnershipRisks[]` or equivalent block with path pattern, git status bucket, reservation holder, related bead hint, risk factors, severity, and suggested commands.
- Keep summary mode compact: counts by owner/risk plus top few high-severity risks.
- Keep full mode useful: every dirty file or path pattern with deterministic ordering and provenance hashes.
- Support stale or missing Agent Mail/Beads sources by emitting degraded entries instead of failing the whole brief.
- Preserve the existing read-only contract: no reservations, no Beads updates, no git mutation.

## Tests

- Unit/golden tests for dirty-only, reservation-only, and combined dirty+reservation fixtures.
- Support-bundle redaction test proving no raw mail body, raw file content, or full env dump appears.
- Snapshot test for deterministic severity ordering.

## Acceptance

Before claiming work in a crowded checkout, an agent can run `ee swarm brief --fields full --json` and identify high-risk dirty/reserved paths without manually correlating `git status`, Agent Mail, and Beads output.

title: O-P5: No-mock multi-agent ownership posture e2e with RCH-blocker replay
description:
## Goal

Prove the ownership-posture feature works in a realistic multi-agent scenario without mocks: a focused RCH verification attempt fails at compile time, another agent owns the first failing file, and `ee` produces the correct advisory without running another build.

## Scenario

- Seed a temporary Beads database with at least two in-progress beads and one open unclaimed bead.
- Seed a redacted Agent Mail reservation snapshot with one active holder, one expired holder, and one overlapping path pattern.
- Seed a git-status fixture with dirty files across owned, reserved-by-other, and unowned buckets.
- Feed a captured/synthetic test-event or RCH failure artifact whose first source path is reserved by another agent.
- Run the diagnostic surface and assert deterministic JSON, correct owner attribution, degraded-source handling, and no raw mail/log/file content leakage.

## Logging

The e2e script should emit `ee.test_event.v1` lines for fixture setup, command start/end, artifact paths, and assertion summary. Failures must identify the mismatched owner candidate and relevant provenance hash.

## Acceptance

A future agent can run the e2e through RCH-only verification and get a clear pass/fail signal that ownership attribution works across Beads, Agent Mail snapshots, dirty-tree state, and verification failure evidence.

title: IdeaWizard: remote-only verification and swarm-resource intelligence follow-ons
description:
## Idea-wizard pass by NobleBasin (2026-05-15)

This epic captures the best non-duplicative ideas from an idea-wizard pass grounded in AGENTS.md, README.md, live Agent Mail, `br ready --json`, `bv --robot-next`, current tracing/RCH incidents, and source inspection of context-pack, swarm-brief, verification-evidence, and pack-SLO modules.

## Phase 2: 30 ideas considered, best 5 retained

The 30 raw ideas were: RCH/Codex remote-only capability reconciliation; swarm brief delta capsules; active Beads/Mail duplicate-work detector; context hotset prewarm; pack-quality outcome feedback loop; RCH queue admission hints; support-bundle diff viewer; stale reservation aging; agent mail outage evidence ingest; worker topology contradiction detector; install-surface smoke ledger; graph cache memory governor; context burst backoff tuning; pack slot dashboard; RCH failure taxonomy expansion; post-compaction handoff validator; audit-row chain visualizer; memory hot/cold tiering; deterministic session replay for high-value tasks; pack SLO regression fingerprints; index mmap readiness advisor; evidence redaction fuzzing; Beads priority drift detector; high-RAM host profile auto-tuner; context-pack A/B evaluation harness; duplicate Cargo run suppressor; release readiness command router; snapshot lifecycle footprint estimator; CASS risk-memory promoter; and large-swarm no-mock rehearsal fixtures.

The best five are the child beads in this epic:
1. RCH/Codex remote-only capability reconciler.
2. Swarm brief delta capsules for compaction/handoff.
3. Context hotset prewarm from Beads/BV/Agent Mail signals.
4. Duplicate-work detector joining verification evidence, Beads, Agent Mail, and reservations.
5. Outcome-driven pack-quality feedback loop.

They score highest because they address observed live pain in this repo: repeated remote-verification ambiguity, compaction handoff cost, 64-agent context stampedes, duplicated build/test work, and difficulty knowing whether graph/PPR/pack changes actually helped agents.

## Phase 3: next 10 ideas and why they were not filed separately

The next ten were: stale reservation aging, RCH queue admission hints, support-bundle diff viewer, agent mail outage evidence ingest, worker topology contradiction detector, graph cache memory governor, post-compaction handoff validator, index mmap readiness advisor, redaction fuzzing, and high-RAM host auto-tuner. These are folded into child acceptance criteria or existing beads instead of filed separately. Existing overlap is strong with `bd-1zb7k.13`, `bd-1zb7k.10`, `bd-1zb7k.12`, `bd-6boyo`, and GraphAccretion; the goal here is to add missing operator surfaces, not duplicate the substrate work.

## Overlap decisions

- Do not replace `bd-1zb7k.13.4`; extend it to cover local RCH client/hook capability contradictions seen in Codex.
- Do not replace `bd-6boyo`; child IW4 consumes broker views and adds duplicate-work guidance.
- Do not replace `bd-1zb7k.10.4`; child IW3 adds hotset prewarm inputs and tests around the existing admission profile.
- Do not create a new agent scheduler or daemon. All surfaces are read-only/advisory unless explicitly stated.
- Do not require live Agent Mail/RCH in tests; fixtures and redacted evidence must be enough.

## Acceptance

This epic closes when all five child beads ship with unit/contract/golden/no-mock e2e coverage, structured J1-style logs, failure-mode fixtures where new degraded codes are emitted, and docs that tell agents how to use the surfaces without rereading implementation code.

title: IW1: RCH/Codex remote-only capability reconciler
description:
## Goal

Add a read-only diagnostic surface that reconciles local RCH client capabilities, Codex hook status, daemon/socket state, dry-run offload classification, and worker probes into one remote-only safety verdict.

## Why

In the live 2026-05-15 swarm, agents repeatedly hit an ambiguity: `rch check/status` reports healthy workers, `rch workers probe --all --json` reports SSH failures, the installed `rch 0.1.3` has no `exec` subcommand, and `rch agents install-hook codex-cli` exits 0 while `rch agents status codex-cli` still says the hook is not installed. Under AGENTS.md, local Cargo fallback is forbidden. Agents need an explicit JSON answer: is this Codex shell safe for remote-only Cargo verification, and if not, what exact condition blocks it?

## Surface

Preferred: extend `ee swarm brief --include-rch --json` and/or add `ee diag rch --json` with an `rchLocalCapability` block:
- cliVersion
- directExecAvailable
- hook.codex.installed
- hook.codex.installAttemptStatus when known
- daemonStatusSocket and statusSocketConsistent
- dryRunWouldOffload for a sample cargo command
- workerProbeSummary
- remoteOnlySafe: true|false
- degraded[] using existing C4 codes where possible, plus a new code only if no existing code fits

## Tests

- Unit parser tests over captured `rch --help-json`, `rch agents status codex-cli`, `rch status --json`, and `rch workers probe --all --json` fixtures.
- Golden fixture for the exact contradictory state observed on 2026-05-15.
- No-Cargo e2e fixture that proves the command never invokes `cargo` and never depends on live RCH.
- Failure-mode fixture for Codex hook missing while remote execution is required.

## Acceptance

Agents can tell from one JSON response whether they may run Cargo in the current shell, whether a different harness with a hook is required, or whether RCH infrastructure must be repaired first. The output must fail closed: uncertainty means `remoteOnlySafe=false` with actionable recovery steps.
