title: EE-035: Build `EE-Exxx` error-code registry with remediation commands
description:
Source plan item: EE-035 from the `Agent-Native UX` backlog.

Task: Build `EE-Exxx` error-code registry with remediation commands

Background and intent:
Make ee discoverable and safe for coding agents by default: deterministic command metadata, stable envelopes, explicit errors, schema discovery, compact field profiles, and non-interactive behavior.

Why this matters:
This bead contributes to the overarching goal of making `ee` a dependable local memory substrate for coding agents: useful before work, auditable after work, and safe under degraded conditions. The work should be implemented in the smallest coherent slice that fully satisfies the public contract implied by the title.

Dependency context:
Original plan dependencies: EE-006, EE-015. These are also represented as br dependency edges where the referenced bead exists.

Non-negotiable constraints:
Global implementation invariants for this task:
- Keep the CLI local-first, deterministic, and agent-native; stdout is data, stderr is diagnostics.
- Preserve the no-Tokio and no-rusqlite constraint unless a later ADR explicitly changes the architecture.
- Use SQLModel Rust plus FrankenSQLite for durable data; do not introduce a second storage stack.
- Use Asupersync for async edges and cancellation/budget behavior; do not smuggle in a Tokio executor.
- Keep JSON as the canonical public contract. TOON, Markdown, diagrams, and MCP are renderers or adapters over the same domain data.
- Mutating commands need dry-run/idempotency/audit behavior unless the task explicitly says otherwise.
- Add focused tests proportional to risk: unit tests for domain logic, contract/golden tests for public output, and integration/evaluation tests for cross-subsystem behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including the comprehensive testing and logging requirements.
design:
Suggested design approach:
- Command output must use the stable `ee.response.v1` envelope, preserve stdout/stderr isolation, and provide useful degraded-state metadata.

Implementation guidance:
- Read the surrounding modules and existing project conventions before editing.
- Prefer the planned crate boundaries from the comprehensive plan: CLI wiring in `ee-cli`, reusable domain/services in `ee-core`, models in `ee-models`, persistence in `ee-db`, output rendering in `ee-output`, and adapters in their own optional crates.
- Keep public contracts stable and versioned. Any data structure that leaves the process through CLI/MCP/hook/export should have a schema and at least one golden fixture.

title: [LOW] ee init writes AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md non-atomically — last writer wins on concurrent runs
description:
## Surface
ee init idempotency under concurrent invocation (audit cycle 6, surface 1)

## Finding
src/core/init.rs:373-427 writes AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md boilerplate via std::fs::write after a non-atomic existence check:

```rust
if !agents_path.exists() {
    match std::fs::write(&agents_path, AGENTS_MD_BOILERPLATE) { ... }
}
```

Two concurrent ee init processes both observe !agents_path.exists(), both call std::fs::write. The second open clobbers the first. Same for CLAUDE.md.

## Idempotency status — mostly clean
The rest of init_workspace IS race-safe:
- fs::create_dir_all is idempotent — both processes succeed.
- initialize_database (src/core/init.rs:449-456) opens the DB and calls migrate(). Migrations re-check inside a transaction (src/db/mod.rs:3329-3331) so concurrent migrators don't double-apply.
- The needs_migration / migrate machinery uses ee_schema_migrations as the canary.

So ee init is functionally idempotent for the data plane. The only race is on the boilerplate markdown files, where it's also benign because the content is identical const &str.

## Why it matters
This is LOW because:
1. AGENTS_MD_BOILERPLATE / CLAUDE_MD_BOILERPLATE are byte-identical literals — the clobber produces the same output.
2. The race window is short (between exists() and write).
3. std::fs::write itself is roughly atomic on POSIX for small buffers (one write() syscall).

But:
- If a future change makes the boilerplate dynamic (e.g., embed the workspace name), the race becomes visible.
- A user who hand-edited AGENTS.md between two concurrent init --force calls could lose the edit. (Today --force only triggers the Revalidated status, doesn't actually rewrite — so safe.)

## Fix
Use atomic write-via-tempfile-rename:
```rust
let tmp = agents_path.with_extension("md.tmp");
std::fs::write(&tmp, AGENTS_MD_BOILERPLATE)?;
std::fs::rename(&tmp, &agents_path)?;  // atomic on POSIX
```
Or skip when exists() and accept the small race window as acceptable for static boilerplate. Status: documented for future maintainers.
close_reason: Implemented exclusive boilerplate creation for AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md; verified core::init tests

title: swarmx.perf-live: ee perf live --json long-running surface for swarm storm observability
description:
IDEA-WIZARD ROUND 2026-05-18 (ScarletHare): during a swarm storm, an operator (human or automation) needs a single source of truth for surface latency, lock waits, RCH posture, read-pool active pins, audit lane backpressure, and L2 cache hit rate. Today this requires correlating ee status, rch status, br stats, and the various tracing logs. On a 256GB+/64+-core host with 64 agents in flight, that correlation is slow and error-prone.

PROPOSAL
Add ee perf live --json (foreground long-running) emitting one snapshot per second (configurable interval) to stdout:

ee.perf.live.v1 snapshot per line:
{
  schema: ee.perf.live.v1,
  ts: 2026-05-18T04:50:00.000Z,
  intervalMs: 1000,
  surfaces: {
    context: { p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, p999_ms, qps, inflight, qos_class_counts },
    search:  { same fields },
    remember:{ same fields },
    why:     { same fields },
    pack_build: { same fields }
  },
  readPool: { active_pins, expired_pins, release_failures, queue_depth },
  auditLane: { batch_count, batch_size_p50, batch_size_p99, backpressure_events, channel_depth },
  l2Cache: { hits, misses, hit_rate, byte_size, evictions },
  rch: { workers_healthy, slots_available, queue_depth, head_of_line_age_ms },
  graphSnapshot: { age_ms, refreshed_count, refresh_lock_wait_ms_p99 },
  hostPressure: { cpu_user_pct, cpu_iowait_pct, memory_rss_mb, page_cache_mb, fsync_latency_p99_ms },
  beadActivity: { active_agents, ready_beads, in_progress_beads, blocked_beads },
  degraded: [ ... ]
}

DATA SOURCE
- Surfaces: instrumented around the existing tracing spans (already in place for most surfaces).
- readPool: already exposed via ee status; reuse the same source.
- auditLane: from bd-wp5ac counters.
- l2Cache: from bd-ndzfg counters.
- rch: from rch status JSON (subprocess every interval).
- graphSnapshot: from existing graph_telemetry events (bd-2inbn).
- hostPressure: /proc/loadavg, /proc/meminfo, getrusage; macOS path uses sysctl wrappers in src/os/host.rs (NEW).
- beadActivity: br stats --json (subprocess every interval) cached for intervalMs.

PERFORMANCE INVARIANTS
- The command itself must consume <=1% CPU on a 64-core host (deterministic latency budget).
- All data sources are read-only; no DB lock acquisition; no writes; no Cargo.

CLI MODES
1. ee perf live --json: continuous, foreground, one line per intervalMs.
2. ee perf snapshot --json: one-shot single snapshot, returns and exits 0.
3. ee perf live --window 30s --json: rolling window aggregates instead of last-interval-only.

WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT FROM EXISTING BEADS
- bd-1zb7k.20 (QoS lanes) makes decisions; this surface lets operators see them.
- bd-1zb7k.12 (host calibration) is one-shot profiling; perf live is continuous observability.
- bd-bife.16 (cross-feature perf bench) is a benchmark; perf live is production telemetry.
- ee status is one-shot posture; perf live is streaming.

FILE SURFACE
- src/cli/mod.rs: ee perf {live,snapshot} parser + emit loop.
- src/core/perf_live.rs (NEW): aggregator, source readers, interval ticker (asupersync).
- src/os/host.rs (NEW or extend existing): cross-platform host-pressure helpers.
- docs/schemas/ee.perf.live.v1.json: schema.
- tests/perf_live_unit.rs: aggregator math, percentile compute, source-degraded fallback.
- tests/perf_live_e2e.rs: real ee binary; ee perf live emits N snapshots in N seconds; one degraded source returns a degraded code but does not fail the command; cancellation (SIGINT) drains and exits 0.
- tests/snapshots/perf_live_one.snap: insta golden of a deterministic single snapshot in a fixture environment.

ACCEPTANCE
- Snapshots are byte-stable in the fixture environment (deterministic clock + deterministic counters).
- One degraded source -> one degraded entry; the rest of the snapshot still emits.
- Cancellation: Cx cancellation drains in-flight aggregation in <=intervalMs and exits 0.
- Performance: <=1% CPU at intervalMs=1000 on a 64-core fixture host.

TESTING WITH LOGGING (no mocks)
- e2e exercises real ee binary, real DB, real read-pool, real audit log.
- Asserts the snapshot stream is monotonically increasing in ts and that every snapshot validates against docs/schemas/ee.perf.live.v1.json.
- Property test: any subset of degraded sources still produces a usable snapshot (none of the readers panic or block forever).

DEPENDENCIES
- Composes with bd-wp5ac (audit lane counters source), bd-ndzfg (L2 counters), bd-2caru (read pool counters), bd-1zb7k.20 (QoS counters), bd-2inbn (graph telemetry counters).
- Parent epic: bd-1prrl Swarm-X.

NON-GOALS
- Not a webserver. CLI stdout only.
- Not Prometheus exposition format in v1 (could be a follow-up child if needed).
- Not a replacement for ee status; that stays the one-shot posture surface.

TRACING: surface=perf_live; required fields bead_id (of THIS bead), workspace_id, request_id (the long-running run), elapsed_ms_per_snapshot, degraded_codes (perf_live_source_degraded, perf_live_interval_overrun).

title: [PERF] pack::assemble_facility_location_draft: submodular profile recomputes universe coverage

title: swarmx.spec-pack: speculative context pre-assembly during steward idle ticks
description:
IDEA-WIZARD ROUND 2026-05-18 (ScarletHare): on a 256GB+/64+-core swarm host, foreground p50 for ee context is 95ms p50/240ms p99 (canonical mac-m3-pro figures; Linux server numbers will land higher under contention). Most of that latency is retrieval + score + pack assembly, all of which can be done speculatively while the agent is editing files. Today the steward only fires for maintenance jobs; it does not warm packs.

PROPOSAL
Add a speculative pack pre-assembler driven by recent query/bead signals:
1. After each ee context, ee search, ee remember, or ee outcome call by an agent, the optional ee daemon (or a one-shot ee steward prewarm tick) records the query, bead_id (if present), agent_name, workspace_id, and tokens-used into a per-workspace recent_query_ring (bounded LRU, capacity configurable, default 64).
2. When the daemon is idle (or the one-shot tick is invoked), it selects top-K recent_query_ring entries for which no fresh L2 pack cache row exists (gates: bd-ndzfg) and runs ee context speculatively with the same flags, writing the resulting pack into L2 with a SHORT TTL (default 30s, configurable as EE_SPEC_PACK_TTL_SECONDS).
3. On real foreground ee context, if the L2 cache has a fresh speculative entry whose query_hash + bead_id + workspace_id match, return it (the L2 layer already supports this; we just produce more cache hits).
4. Speculative work is QoS-gated by bd-1zb7k.20 lanes: it runs in maintenance lane, yields immediately on foreground pressure.

WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT FROM EXISTING BEADS
- bd-ndzfg (L2 pack cache) is a passive cache; this is an active producer.
- bd-1zb7k.17.3 (hotset prewarm) prewarms hot memory IDs into the page cache; this prewarms entire packs.
- bd-gni47 (single-flight) coalesces concurrent identical queries; speculative pre-assembly attacks the next, not-yet-issued query.
The three compose: speculative producer fills L2 cache; single-flight ensures only one producer fires per (workspace, query_hash, bead_id) tuple; hotset prewarm keeps cold memories out of the foreground path.

ADMISSION CONTROL (CRITICAL)
- Hard QoS gate: speculative ticks check rch and read-pool active counts before each candidate; abort if foreground lane shows ANY pressure (read_pool active_pins > 0 with foreground request_id, or qos.foreground_active > 0).
- Cooperative cancellation: a foreground ee context Cx becomes a back-pressure signal that immediately kills in-flight speculative work via the existing Cx tree.
- Per-workspace concurrent-speculation cap (default 4, configurable as EE_SPEC_PACK_CONCURRENCY).

FILE SURFACE
- src/steward/spec_pack.rs (NEW): recent_query_ring, selection logic, QoS check, speculative driver.
- src/core/recent_queries.rs (NEW): per-workspace bounded LRU with token-based eviction.
- src/cli/mod.rs: ee steward prewarm-packs subcommand (one-shot mode).
- src/config/env_registry.rs: EE_SPEC_PACK_TTL_SECONDS, EE_SPEC_PACK_CONCURRENCY, EE_SPEC_PACK_RING_CAPACITY.
- docs/configuration/storage.md: section on speculative pack TTL.
- docs/schemas/ee.spec_pack.v1.json: telemetry schema.
- tests/spec_pack_unit.rs: ring eviction; selection sorting; QoS gate happy path.
- tests/spec_pack_e2e.rs: real ee context produces an entry; a subsequent ee context call resolves from L2 within the TTL; speculative work is aborted by a concurrent foreground call.

ACCEPTANCE
- Speculative work emits ee.spec_pack.v1 events with phase=admission|prepare|run|abort|store and surface_pack_id.
- p50 of repeated ee context for top-K recent queries drops by >=30% on the canonical bench (256GB host) when speculative prewarm is enabled vs disabled.
- Foreground p99 never degrades (admission gate property-tested).
- Determinism preserved: cache key includes (workspace_id, query, bead_id, max_tokens, profile, agent_name when bias active).

TESTING WITH LOGGING (no mocks)
- e2e exercises the real ee binary, real DB, real index, real L2 cache.
- Asserts ee.spec_pack.v1 events emit in the right order and that foreground request_id never appears in maintenance lane logs.
- Property test (proptest): admission gate never fires speculative work when foreground_active > 0.

DEPENDENCIES
- Requires bd-ndzfg (L2 pack cache producer hook).
- Composes with bd-1zb7k.20 (QoS lanes).
- Parent epic: bd-1prrl Swarm-X.

NON-GOALS
- Not an LLM-based query predictor; the ring is purely observed recent queries.
- Not a daemon-only feature; the one-shot ee steward prewarm-packs command must work without ee daemon running.

TRACING: surface=spec_pack; required fields bead_id (of THIS bead), workspace_id, request_id (speculative), elapsed_ms, degraded_codes (qos_back_pressure, ring_empty, cache_admission_denied).

title: [guard] Add no-silent-fallback conformance test for production data paths
description:
## Background
One-off fixes are not enough. `6xkn`, `kr0m`, and this epic all point to a reusable contract: production paths that feed machine data must not erase failure evidence by defaulting to empty values. A conformance guard should make that policy executable without banning every harmless default.

## What to do
- Add a focused test or script-backed contract that scans production Rust files for high-risk silent-fallback patterns.
- Maintain a small allowlist with file, pattern, reason, and test evidence for intentional defaults.
- Fail when a new unallowlisted `unwrap_or_default`, ignored read, ignored rollback, or serialization fallback appears in an agent-facing data path.
- Keep the guard narrow enough to avoid noisy false positives in test modules, purely human-only formatting, or safe optional-display defaults.

## Acceptance
- The guard fails on at least one synthetic fixture containing `serde_json::to_string(...).unwrap_or_default()` in a machine JSON renderer.
- The guard passes on the final repo state and reports the allowlisted count.
- The guard is documented in its test failure message with the repair pattern: return a contextual error/degradation or add a justified allowlist entry with coverage.
- Verification includes the guard test, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --all-targets`, and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` through RCH.

title: SECURITY: CASS-reported paths are reused as cass view arguments without a separator or confinement
description: CASS import parses each session path directly from the external cass sessions JSON contract (src/cass/import.rs:386, src/cass/import.rs:402). When spans are included, that path is passed back into cass view as the first positional argument (src/cass/import.rs:273, src/cass/import.rs:275, src/cass/import.rs:358, src/cass/import.rs:362). CassClient::view_invocation emits ["view", source_path, "-n", ...] with no -- separator and no workspace/canonical-path confinement (src/cass/client.rs:344, src/cass/client.rs:346, src/cass/client.rs:348). A compromised or contract-drifting CASS binary can return a path beginning with - or an out-of-workspace path and make ee invoke cass view with attacker-chosen options or read/import unintended session content. Expected fix: validate CASS paths against the requested workspace and expected session-file shape, reject option-looking paths, pass -- before path if CASS supports it, and add contract tests for hyphen-prefixed and outside-workspace paths.

title: Lexical index RAM-tier pinning with hugepages on 256GB+ hosts (idea-wizard MagentaPanther 2026-05-18)
description: EVIDENCE: bd-1prrl.3 NUMA-mmap covers graph snapshots only. Frankensearch lexical posting-list files in indexes/combined/ are not RAM-tier pinned. On 256GB+ hosts this leaves tens of GB of pinnable hot data on disk where it pays page-fault cost on each search. DISTINGUISHABILITY: distinct from bd-1prrl.3 (graph snapshot mmap), bd-ndzfg (L2 pack result cache), bd-168gm (embedding LRU). This is page-cache pinning + optional hugepages for Frankensearch lexical-index files. See follow-up comment for full design.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
FULL SPEC (MagentaPanther idea-wizard 2026-05-18)

DESIGN:
1. At ee daemon start (or first ee search), mmap the lexical index files under indexes/combined/ with MAP_POPULATE so kernel proactively populates page cache.
2. On Linux, optionally request MADV_HUGEPAGE on the mmap region (transparent huge pages reduce TLB pressure for the 100MB+ posting-list files).
3. Honor EE_LEXICAL_INDEX_PIN_RAM (default off — explicit opt-in; on by default for daemon mode after measurement validates safety).
4. Honor EE_LEXICAL_INDEX_HUGEPAGES (default off — only effective when EE_LEXICAL_INDEX_PIN_RAM=1 AND kernel supports THP).
5. Graceful degrade: on platforms without MADV_HUGEPAGE or mlock unavailable, emit info-severity degraded code lexical_hugepages_unavailable; functionality unchanged, RAM tier still benefits from page cache.
6. Resource accounting in ee status: report pinned RAM bytes and page-fault delta.

FILE SURFACE:
- src/search/mod.rs (mmap + madvise wiring)
- src/config/env_registry.rs: EE_LEXICAL_INDEX_PIN_RAM, EE_LEXICAL_INDEX_HUGEPAGES
- docs/architecture/lexical-ram-tier.md (NEW)
- tests/lexical_ram_tier_e2e.rs (NEW)
- tests/fixtures/failure_modes/lexical_hugepages_unavailable.json (NEW)

ACCEPTANCE:
1. With EE_LEXICAL_INDEX_PIN_RAM=1, first search after ee daemon start touches only mmapd RAM. Proven by absence of disk I/O in strace/iotop trace.
2. p99 hot-path search latency drops by >= 30% vs unpinned baseline on a fixture workspace (>= 10MB lexical index).
3. Graceful degrade when hugepages unavailable: info-severity lexical_hugepages_unavailable degraded code with fixture; ee status reports the degradation.
4. ee status --json surfaces pinned RAM bytes under data.search.lexicalRamTier (new optional field, schema-versioned).
5. All Cargo verification through RCH only.

TRACING: surface=lexical_ram_tier; required fields workspace_id, index_path, bytes_mmapped, hugepages_requested, hugepages_granted, page_faults_pre, page_faults_post, elapsed_ms_first_search, degraded_codes (lexical_hugepages_unavailable, mmap_failed, mlock_failed).

DISTINGUISHABILITY:
- bd-1prrl.3 NUMA mmap: graph snapshots only. Lexical index has different access patterns + different cost profile.
- bd-ndzfg L2 pack cache: caches assembled pack results. Plan cache hits use this; this bead reduces cost of cache misses.
- bd-168gm embedding LRU: caches embedding vectors. Lexical posting lists are a different dataset.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES:
- Always pin all lexical files: tens of GB on large workspaces could pressure other memory consumers. Hence opt-in default.
- Use tmpfs for indexes/combined/: complicates startup + backup; mmap+MAP_POPULATE achieves same effect more flexibly.

title: [HIGH] Curation TTL stores invalid non-RFC3339 expiration strings
description:
Reviewer finding from mixed-swarm pass.

Location: src/curate/mod.rs:1842-1847 creates ttl_expires_at with format!("{now_rfc3339}+{secs}s"). src/core/curate.rs:2742-2748 later parses ttl_expires_at with DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339.

title: [process] Vision-coverage gate in scripts/verify.sh
description:
## Background

`scripts/verify.sh` enforces 5 readiness gates today (forbidden deps, tests, e2e basic, e2e advanced, e2e boundary). It does not check whether the README + COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_TO_MAKE_EE__OPUS.md vision is actually delivered. The 689-closed/5-open optic hides the gap.

## What this bead does

Adds a new `vision-coverage` stage to verify.sh that:

1. Parses README.md's command reference table (every `ee <subcommand>` mentioned).
2. Parses COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_TO_MAKE_EE__OPUS.md walking-skeleton acceptance gate (§29) and CLI surface (§20).
3. Greps src/cli/mod.rs for every `*_UNAVAILABLE_CODE` constant.
4. Cross-references against `br list -s open --json` and `br list -s in_progress --json`.
5. Emits a JSON report at `.vision-coverage-report.json`:

```json
{
  "schema": "ee.vision_coverage.v1",
  "generated_at": "<rfc3339>",
  "surfaces": {
    "total_documented": <n>,
    "implemented": <n>,
    "stubbed": <n>,
    "missing": <n>,
    "with_open_implements_bead": <n>
  },
  "gap_percentage": <0-100>,
  "missing_surfaces": ["..."],
  "stubbed_surfaces": [{"name": "...", "stub_constant": "...", "implements_bead": "..." | null}]
}
```

6. Exits non-zero if `gap_percentage > 0` AND we are on a release-tag commit. Otherwise warns.
7. CI annotates PRs with a delta vs. `main` (`gap improved by 2.3%` / `gap regressed by 0.4%`).

## Why this is wave-0

The user's reality-check insight: tactical bead-burning velocity is not the same as strategic delivery. This gate makes the strategic gap visible on every commit, so the swarm cannot drift back into closing-without-implementing.

## Non-goals

Does NOT block PRs that don't change the vision-coverage status. Only blocks release tagging.
close_reason: Implemented: vision-coverage gate with delta annotation. Core script emits JSON report, blocks release-tag commits if gap>0, compares vs main branch. Commits: scripts/vision-coverage.sh, tests/vision_coverage_gate.rs, CI wiring in ci.yml.

title: HIGH: JSON error envelope omits required severity/details fields
description:

title: [no-silent-fallback] Inventory production defaults and define allowlist contract
description:
## Background
The repo has multiple legitimate uses of defaults, especially in tests and display helpers, but recent bugs show that production decode and render paths can hide corruption or failed I/O when they use `unwrap_or_default`, ignored reads, or ad hoc empty fallback values. Before broad edits, future agents need a precise map of which defaults are dangerous and which are intentional.

## What to do
- Search production code under `src/` for `unwrap_or_default`, ignored `Result`s around I/O, `serde_json::to_string(...).unwrap_or_default`, builder fields that default machine-facing IDs/timestamps/content to empty strings, and subprocess pipe reads that ignore errors.
- Classify every finding into: must-fix now, safe intentional default, test-only/non-production, or needs a separate follow-up.
- Add a small machine-readable allowlist or a conformance test table that records the safe intentional defaults with reason strings.
- Use the existing `kr0m` and `6xkn` fixes as examples of the policy: machine data failure must become a stable error or degradation, not empty data.

## Acceptance
- The inventory is committed as code/test data or as a self-contained test fixture, not only as a transient comment.
- Each must-fix finding has a linked child bead or is fixed in the same slice if trivial.
- The inventory explicitly covers `src/cass/process.rs`, `src/output/mod.rs`, `src/hooks/installer.rs`, `src/models/jsonl.rs`, and any additional production modules found by the scan.
- Verification includes the focused guard/inventory test and `ubs` on changed files.

title: [HIGH] db: unsafe i64→u32/u64 casts in row decoders can corrupt or hide errors

title: review(preflight-hook): baked block severities create staleness in generated shell hooks
description: In src/hooks/installer.rs, the generated bash/zsh preflight snippets embed a static EE_PREFLIGHT_HOOK_BLOCK_SEVERITIES list at generation time (currently 'high critical'). The live  is always called, but the decision to prompt/block is filtered client-side against the baked list. When the central destructive command policy (commands.json) or severity thresholds are updated, already-installed hooks on machines will not reflect the new policy until the hook is re-generated. This is the same staleness pattern seen in several other recent diagnostic/hook surfaces. Recommendation: either remove the client-side filter (always prompt on high/critical returned by the live check) or make the hook fetch current block severities from ee at runtime. Found during deep review of e43bf0d (preflight shell hook helper). Links to bd-1um33.
close_reason: resolved by the CalmBridge refactor of the bd-3usjw.7 hook snippets following bd-26vu5's design rationale. Verification: grep -n EE_PREFLIGHT_HOOK_BLOCK_SEVERITIES src/hooks/installer.rs returns nothing — the baked client-side severity allowlist is gone from both bash_preflight_snippet and zsh_preflight_snippet templates. The snippet now: (1) calls 'ee preflight check --cmd <cmd> --json' on every interactive command, (2) trusts exit code 7 as the authoritative deny signal, (3) extracts severity from the JSON for the prompt-message display only ('(severity=%s)'), (4) prompts the user unconditionally on exit 7 and blocks/aborts on N. The contract goldens at tests/golden/hook_preflight_{bash,zsh}.snap document this explicitly: 'live ee preflight check exit code 7 is authoritative; the snippet does not embed a stale client-side severity allowlist'. Policy updates to commands.json and central severity thresholds now take effect on the NEXT preflight check call rather than requiring hook regeneration. The PreflightHookShellReport.severity_block JSON field is still emitted for callers who want trust-posture metadata, but it does not gate snippet behavior anymore. RCH-verified through bd-3usjw.7 closure (DarkCardinal: preflight_hook_bash 5/5 + preflight_hook_zsh 5/5 on css). Cross-link: docs/rch_runbook.md (bd-1h8ji.7) cites this design as one of the live preflight policy guarantees.

title: SRR6.11: Eager metadata cache + policy-gated lazy body fetch
description:
Implement eager metadata caching and lazy body fetch. Metadata should be small, policy-filtered, and indexed locally when permitted. Full bodies should be fetched only when policy allows and a query/context/why path actually needs them, then cached with provenance and freshness metadata.

Be careful with embeddings: embeddings can leak content and can drift by model/version. Treat them as policy-governed search surrogates, not harmless metadata. Support metadata-only peers, redacted previews, local recomputation of embeddings from fetched bodies, and body cache invalidation by content hash.

Acceptance: body fetch repository/cache; metadata-only and body-allowed modes; content-hash verification; no body leak under denied policy; search/index jobs reflect local cached state; why/provenance shows whether body is local, cached remote, or fetchable remote.

title: [LOW] ADR-0018 references V033 plan_recipes migration but actual migration is V035 (post-renumber drift)
description:
Repro:
  1. Read docs/adr/0018-plan-recommend-ranking.md (committed in d0e0224
     2026-05-06 14:55 UTC).
  2. Search line 83: "Requires plan_recipes table migration (V033)".
  3. Read src/db/mod.rs and find:
        V031_CERTIFICATES_AND_TRUST_QUARANTINE
        V032_AUDIT_HASH_CHAIN
        V033_LEARNING_OBSERVATIONS  (NOT plan_recipes)
        V034_PROCEDURE_STORE
        V035_PLAN_RECIPES           (the actual table migration)

  The plan_recipes migration is V035, not V033. V033 is learning
  observations, which has nothing to do with plan recommendation.

Expected: ADR-0018 references the correct migration version
(V035_PLAN_RECIPES, file:src/db/mod.rs).

Actual: ADR-0018:83 says "V033", which is wrong by two versions and
points at a different feature.

Aggravating: the V031 → V033 renumber that mis-anchored the ADR is
itself a separate violation tracked in eidetic_engine_cli-4j7v
(migration-version-reuse). The ADR was probably written against the
intermediate state where V031 was learning_observations and a future
V032 would be plan_recipes; the wave-3 renumber and the subsequent
V034/V035 additions left the ADR stale.

Evidence-line:
  docs/adr/0018-plan-recommend-ranking.md:83 (says V033)
  src/db/mod.rs (V035_PLAN_RECIPES is the actual migration)

Suggested fix: edit ADR-0018 to say V035, and add a one-line
"Migration version" cross-reference at the top of the ADR so future
renumbers cannot silently invalidate the doc.

Severity: LOW. Doc-only drift, no behavioural impact, but it leads
the next agent reading the ADR to grep the wrong migration when
implementing the recommender.
close_reason: Fixed V033→V035 reference in ADR-0018. Added explicit Migration field in frontmatter to link ADR to actual migration line in code.

title: [MEDIUM] closure-lint.sh has zero test coverage — silent regression risk on a CI-gating script
description:
## Surface
Closure linter regression-detection (audit cycle 7, surface 1)

## Finding
`scripts/closure-lint.sh` is a 281-line shell script that gates CI via `scripts/verify.sh:89`. It has THREE rules:
1. `implements-surface:*` beads cannot close with abstention language (regex-based check on close_reason)
2. `implements-surface:*` beads cannot close while `*_UNAVAILABLE_CODE` constants remain in src/cli/mod.rs
3. `implements-surface:*` beads must have a public golden snapshot in tests/golden/<surface>.snap

`find tests -name '*lint*' -o -name '*closure*'` returns NOTHING. `grep -rln 'closure_lint\|closure-lint' tests/` returns NOTHING.

So the linter is exercised only by running it. `cargo test --all-targets` does NOT cover it. A regression in any of these would survive PR review:
- A typo breaking the ABSTENTION_REGEX (line 25) makes rule 1 silently match nothing.
- A change to the `_UNAVAILABLE_CODE` constant naming convention without updating the linter's transformation (line 221: `tr '[:lower:]-' '[:upper:]_'`) silently misses violations.
- A typo in GOLDEN_DIR breaks rule 3 silently.

ujuc identified partial-closure beads (project memory: EE-062 'remember persist' and EE-151 'pack records' closed without full implementation). The linter's purpose is precisely to detect these. Without unit tests, the linter has no safety net.

## Repro
```bash
# Verify no test exercises the linter
find tests -name '*closure*'         # empty
find tests -name '*lint*'            # empty  
grep -r 'closure-lint' tests/        # empty
grep -r 'ABSTENTION_REGEX' tests/    # empty
```

## Fix
Add an integration test `tests/closure_lint_harness.rs` that:
1. Builds a temporary .beads/issues.jsonl with synthetic beads exercising each rule:
   - implements-surface bead closed with 'abstain' close_reason → expect violation
   - implements-surface bead closed with stub _UNAVAILABLE_CODE present → expect violation
   - implements-surface bead closed without snap file → expect violation
   - honesty-only bead with no open implements-surface sibling → expect violation
   - implements-surface bead closed cleanly (real code, no stub, snap present) → expect pass
2. Runs `scripts/closure-lint.sh --json` against the synthetic environment.
3. Parses .closure-lint-report.json and asserts the violation list matches expectations.
4. Run as part of `cargo test --workspace --all-targets` so the linter cannot silently regress.

Alternative: port the linter's logic to Rust (a `bin/closure-lint` binary or a library function with #[cfg(test)] tests). Heavier diff but unifies tooling under one toolchain.
close_reason: Added tests/closure_lint_harness.rs, a real integration harness that runs scripts/closure-lint.sh --audit --json against synthetic temporary workspaces. Coverage exercises abstention-language violations, *_UNAVAILABLE_CODE sentinel violations, missing golden snapshot violations, honesty-only closure without open implements-surface sibling, and passing clean implementation plus honesty-only sibling cases. Verification: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check tests/closure_lint_harness.rs; git diff --check -- tests/closure_lint_harness.rs; RCH cargo test --test closure_lint_harness -- --nocapture; RCH cargo check --all-targets. Repo-wide cargo fmt --check and clippy remain blocked by unrelated pre-existing dirty/baseline files outside this bead.

title: [PERF] core::focus::read_active_focus_state: sync JSON file read on every context request
description:
Path: ee context -> src/core/context.rs:377 read_active_focus_state -> src/core/focus.rs:639 read_active_focus_state -> src/core/focus.rs:708 read_focus_state.
Code evidence: src/core/context.rs:377 calls read_active_focus_state on every context request after search; src/core/focus.rs:642 checks storage_path.exists synchronously; src/core/focus.rs:709 performs fs::read_to_string and src/core/focus.rs:713 parses JSON on the request path.

Verification plan: benchmark context with absent, small, and large `.ee/focus/state.json` under warm/cold cache, asserting identical context output and lower p95 after caching/batching.

title: Wire graph_audit payload builders into F1 snapshot lifecycle + F2 cache + algorithm wrappers (bd-bife.15 follow-up to commit adb03fc)
description:
Audit-action constants and payload builders for bd-bife.15 landed in commit `adb03fc` "feat(core): add graph audit-action payload builders" — `src/core/graph_audit.rs` exposes five canonical action names plus typed builders returning a deterministic `GraphAuditPayload`.

This child captures the remaining call-site wiring to actually emit audit rows from F1 snapshot lifecycle, F2 cache, and the algorithm wrappers.

## Files to touch (call sites)

- `src/steward/` or wherever F1 snapshot refresh writes a row to `graph_snapshots`: after a successful insert, build a `SnapshotRefreshedInputs` payload and write it through the existing `audit_log` writer.
- The snapshot archival path (search anchor: `archived_at`, `graph_snapshots`): build a `SnapshotArchivedInputs { reason: NewerSnapshot | Manual }` payload.
- `src/db/mod.rs` (or wherever the algorithm-result cache lives, `graph_algorithm_results`): on insert, build a `ResultCachedInputs` payload; on eviction (TTL or snapshot-archived), build a `ResultEvictedInputs { reason: SnapshotInvalidated | TtlExpired }`.
- Algorithm wrappers in `src/graph/algorithms.rs` / `src/graph/*.rs`: on degraded emission (search anchor: `DegradationReport`, `degraded` fields on result types), build an `AlgorithmDegradedInputs` payload. Pair this with the existing `tracing` emission so the audit row and the tracing event share field values.

## Tests

- `tests/contracts/graph_audit.rs` (NEW): drive a fixture workspace through a sequence that hits all five trigger paths (snapshot refresh, snapshot archive, algorithm compute with cache miss → cache insert, snapshot archive → cache eviction, algorithm with stale snapshot → degraded emit) and assert each canonical action appears in `audit_log` with the documented `target_type` and `details` keys.
- The bead acceptance is "Contract test verifies each fires." The test should walk `ALL_GRAPH_AUDIT_ACTIONS` from `src/core/graph_audit.rs` and assert one row per action, so adding a sixth action automatically gains test coverage.
- Also verify `ee audit query filter --action graph.* --json` surfaces the entries (this works through the existing audit query path; only the new actions need to be findable, no new query plumbing).

## Cross-refs

- Algorithm core: commit `adb03fc`
- Action constants (use these exact strings, do not retype): `SNAPSHOT_REFRESHED_ACTION`, `SNAPSHOT_ARCHIVED_ACTION`, `RESULT_CACHED_ACTION`, `RESULT_EVICTED_ACTION`, `ALGORITHM_DEGRADED_ACTION`
- Builders: `build_snapshot_refreshed_payload`, `build_snapshot_archived_payload`, `build_result_cached_payload`, `build_result_evicted_payload`, `build_algorithm_degraded_payload`
- Reason enums: `SnapshotArchivedReason`, `ResultEvictedReason` with stable `as_str` wire strings
- Sweep slice for tests/docs: `ALL_GRAPH_AUDIT_ACTIONS`

## Why filed as a separate child

`src/steward/`, `src/graph/algorithms.rs`, and `src/db/mod.rs` are all currently hot. The algorithm core in `adb03fc` lives in a brand-new file with zero contention; the wiring touches the hot paths and benefits from a coordinated quieter window.

title: [pack-replay] Benchmark ledger overhead and large-fixture freshness scans
description:
Quantify the cost of replay ledgers and freshness validation before either becomes default-on in hot paths. The goal is to keep ee useful for large agent swarms on 64-core/256GB-class hosts while preserving deterministic CLI behavior.

Scope:
- Add deterministic scale fixtures that exercise many memories, provenance records, redaction classes, and pack candidates without depending on paid APIs.
- Measure pack creation with and without ledger persistence, replay command latency, diff latency, and freshness scan latency.
- Emit stable JSON artifacts with profile name, fixture size, command, elapsed time, memory/resource fields where available, and regression status.
- Define advisory budgets first; release-blocking thresholds can come later once variance is understood.

Acceptance criteria:
- Benchmark/smoke profile runs via RCH and avoids repo-local target contention.

title: [HIGH] pack output (ee context) does not call redact_secret_like_content — defense-in-depth gap against AGENTS.md "no secrets in context packs"
description:
Repro:
  `ee context <task> --json` emits memory content verbatim through
  `core::context::compute_pack_hash` and the JSON renderer in
  `src/output/mod.rs`. The redaction policy in `src/policy/mod.rs::
  redact_secret_like_content` is called at WRITE TIME (memory.rs:749,
  jsonl_import.rs:764, curate.rs:2408/2446, cass/import.rs:852) but
  NEVER at pack-output time.

  Construction:
    1. Bypass `ee remember` and write a memory whose content contains
       a secret directly into the SQLite store (e.g., via an
       integration test, an admin tool, or a pre-V032-redaction-rule
       backup that imported through a path predating the redaction
       upgrade).
    2. Run `ee context <query> --json` whose retrieval surfaces that
       memory.
    3. Observe the secret in the pack output.

Expected: pack output should re-apply `redact_secret_like_content` to
each item.content before emitting, as a defense-in-depth so that any
hole in the write-time redaction (or any historical write that
predated a redaction-rule update) does not leak through `ee context`.

Actual: pack output trusts the storage layer. Greppable confirmation:

      $ grep -rn 'redact_secret_like_content' src/ | grep -v test
        src/core/jsonl_import.rs:764  (write path)
        src/core/memory.rs:749        (write path)
        src/core/curate.rs:2408       (write path)
        src/core/curate.rs:2446       (write path)
        src/cass/import.rs:852        (write path)
        src/policy/mod.rs:465         (definition)

  No call site in `src/core/context.rs`, `src/pack/mod.rs`, or
  `src/output/mod.rs`.

Aggravating: AGENTS.md "Non-Goals For V1" pillar reads "No secrets in
context packs." The repo's code-level enforcement of that pillar lives
entirely on the write side, with no audit gate at the read side.
Adding a redaction pass to the pack output is cheap (the function is
already deterministic and well-tested in
`src/policy/mod.rs::tests::redact_secret_like_content_*`).

Evidence-line:
  src/policy/mod.rs:465 (redact_secret_like_content definition)
  src/core/context.rs:513-559 (compute_pack_hash — does not redact)
  src/core/context.rs (no call to redact_secret_like_content)
  src/pack/mod.rs (no call to redact_secret_like_content)

Suggested fix:
  - Apply `redact_secret_like_content` to `item.content` in the pack
    builder right before the content is hashed and emitted. Capture
    the redaction report into a per-item `redactions: Vec<...>` field
    so the JSON contract is honest.
  - Add a determinism test (`tests/pack_redacts_secrets_at_render.rs`)
    that seeds a memory with a known secret pattern via the raw DB,
    runs `ee context --json`, and asserts the secret is replaced with
    the redaction placeholder.
  - The pack hash currently includes raw content. Once redaction is
    applied at render, the hash should include the redacted content
    so that the same workspace state produces the same hash —
    redaction strings are deterministic so this is straightforward.

Severity: HIGH. The defense-in-depth gap means any future write-path
regression silently leaks secrets through the most-used surface (`ee
context` is the walking-skeleton command). Today the gap is latent
because every known write path redacts, but the architectural rule
should be enforced at every layer that crosses a trust boundary.
close_reason: Completed: context pack selected items are redacted before emission, redaction metadata is exposed in JSON output, pack hashes include redaction metadata, and focused pack/output tests pass.

title: swarmx.barp: bead-aware retrieval prioritization for ee context and ee search
description:
IDEA-WIZARD ROUND 2026-05-18 (ScarletHare): swarm-scale responsiveness on 256GB+/64+-core hosts. When multiple agents are claiming different beads in a swarm, today every agent contends for the same hot memory subset because retrieval scoring is identical across agents. If retrieval knew the current bead context, agents working on different beads would naturally cluster onto disjoint hot subsets, sharding the effective workload and increasing aggregate cache hit rates without explicit partitioning.

PROPOSAL
Add an opt-in --bead-id BEAD argument to ee context, ee search, ee why, and ee pack build. When supplied, retrieval scoring adds a small additive bonus to memories whose:
  - tags overlap with the beads labels
  - content_hash or content matches any token in the beads title or description
  - links[] include any peer bead memory whose source_uri references that bead family (parent/child or label sibling)
The bonus is capped (clamped to +/-0.05 like the swarmx.5 agent_bias, default cap configurable) and shows up in the existing ee why retrieval block as scoreComponents.beadAffinity with the same fields as agentProfile.

WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT FROM EXISTING BEADS
- bd-1prrl.2 (swarmx.5 per-agent context profile) biases by agent identity; this biases by current bead.
- bd-gni47 single-flight coalesces identical queries; this differentiates queries that look the same textually but are semantically scoped to different beads.
- bd-3vwx0 next-action planner picks the bead; this uses the picked bead to shape retrieval.
The three compose: next-action -> bead picked -> bead-aware retrieval focuses pack on bead-relevant memory -> agent profile applies its own bias.

DATA SOURCE
Beads context comes from the local .beads/beads.jsonl plus a thin in-process beads loader. No new dependency; the same parser path swarm brief uses.

FILE SURFACE
- src/core/context.rs: bead_affinity score component, --bead-id wiring.
- src/core/search.rs: same.
- src/core/why.rs: beadAffinity rendering with explain text.
- src/cli/mod.rs: --bead-id flag on the relevant commands (parser only; no logic).
- docs/schemas/ee.context.bead_affinity.v1.json: schema for the new explanation block.
- tests/bead_affinity_unit.rs: cap, sign, sort stability.
- tests/bead_affinity_e2e.rs: two agents on different beads see distinguishable rank orderings for the same query; a third agent without --bead-id sees the unbiased ranking.
- tests/snapshots/bead_affinity.snap: insta golden.

ACCEPTANCE
- |bead_affinity_score| <= 0.05 for any (memory, bead) pair (unit-tested over a property fixture).
- Same DB + indexes + config + query + --bead-id -> byte-identical pack hash (determinism preserved).
- E2E: two contrived beads produce visibly different rankings on the same query.
- Cold-start: bead with no matching tags/labels yields bead_affinity == 0 and emits a degraded code bead_affinity_cold_start in the explain block (no error).
- Bench: bead_affinity adds <=2ms p50 on the 1k-memory fixture (cap is in-process bead lookup + per-candidate token match).

TESTING WITH LOGGING (no mocks)
- All tests emit ee.test_event.v1 with bead_id=this beads id and surface=bead_affinity. Logged fields: query_id, bead_id, applied_count, max_abs_bias, cold_start, elapsed_ms.
- e2e harness asserts log lines for two agents differ in the applied memory ids.

DEPENDENCIES
- Composes with bd-1prrl.2 (agent profile), bd-3vwx0 (next-action), bd-ov09 (PPR).
- Parent epic: bd-1prrl Swarm-X.

NON-GOALS
- Not a replacement for tags or links; bead affinity is a soft prior, not a hard filter.
- Not destructive: existing scoring stays untouched when --bead-id is absent.

TRACING: surface=bead_affinity; required fields bead_id (of THIS bead), workspace_id, request_id, elapsed_ms, degraded_codes.

title: [models] Audit machine-facing builders that default required fields to blanks
description:
## Background
The scan found model/builders that use `unwrap_or_default()` for fields such as export IDs, timestamps, memory IDs, workspace IDs, levels, kinds, and content. Some builder defaults are intentionally ergonomic, but a required machine-facing identity or timestamp becoming an empty string can produce records that look valid until a later command fails or misranks evidence.

## What to do
- Audit builders and record constructors under `src/models/`, `src/curate/`, and JSONL/export code for required machine-facing fields defaulted to empty strings.
- Separate optional display fields from contract-required IDs, timestamps, schema names, content, source URIs, and provenance references.
- For required fields, prefer fallible builders, typed constructors, or validation errors over empty defaults.
- Keep ergonomic builder APIs only where tests prove the default is safe and documented.

## Acceptance
- Any remaining empty default for a machine-facing required field has a test-backed reason in the allowlist/inventory from `sos5.1`.
- At least one regression covers a previously empty-defaulted required field and proves malformed/incomplete output is rejected or reported.
- JSONL export/import and curation risk certificate contracts remain stable for valid records.
- Verification includes focused model/JSONL tests plus the standard cargo gates through RCH.
close_reason: Converted ExportTagRecord::new() to fallible builder with required_string validation. All 9 JSONL export record types now reject missing/blank required fields via ExportRecordBuildError. Added test cases for tag builder. Also fixed DomainError missing Display impl.

title: SRR6.5: Peer trust, authorization, and redaction policy
description:
Design and implement peer trust, app-level authorization, and redaction policy for mesh sharing. Tailscale identity may identify transport peers, but `ee` still needs its own allowlist/capability model and per-peer sharing rules.

Scope includes: peer allowlist records; trust lanes such as local-human, peer-human-via-peer, peer-agent, peer-derived, and untrusted; redaction classes for metadata, preview, embedding, and body; body fetch authorization; policy checks before export and import; and provenance rendering in context packs.

Acceptance: no peer-imported memory can appear as local `human_explicit`; private bodies and disallowed embeddings cannot leave the node; policy failures produce structured errors/degraded codes; tests cover allowed, denied, redacted, and metadata-only peer modes.

title: [sqlite] Add contention retry for file-backed read queries
description:
Finding from deadlock-finder-and-fixer audit.

Evidence:
- src/db/mod.rs:767-781 configures file-backed read/write connections with PRAGMA busy_timeout = 0.
- src/db/mod.rs:754-758 sends all query_for() reads straight to FrankenConnection::query_sync() with no retry wrapper.
- Read-heavy command paths open the same file DB and issue queries during swarm work, e.g. src/core/context.rs:389-423 and src/core/status.rs:533.

Reproduction conditions:
- File-backed .ee/ee.db.
- Hold a writer open with BEGIN EXCLUSIVE or any long with_transaction() path.
- In another process run ee status --json, ee context "..." --json, or another read path that uses query_for(). With busy_timeout set to zero and no read retry, transient SQLite contention can surface directly to the CLI.

Fix target:
- Add bounded retry/backoff around file-backed query_for() for transient SQLite lock errors, or use a nonzero busy_timeout plus outer retry for reads.
- Keep deterministic error shape when retries exhaust.
- Add a regression that holds a writer and proves read commands wait or report a structured retry-exhausted error rather than raw lock contention.
close_reason: File-backed database reads retry transient SQLite contention with bounded backoff and preserve query operation context

title: [LOW] stored_recorder_event_from_row coerces NULL sequence/event_count to 0 silently — masks data corruption
description:
Cycle-4 reviewer audit (REVIEWER pane). Surface: integer coercion in recorder row decoding (boundary-adjacent to scoring math audit).

src/db/mod.rs:11527-11533 (stored_recorder_run_from_row) and 11542-11546 (stored_recorder_event_from_row) decode INTEGER columns with the pattern:
  row.get(N).and_then(|v| v.as_i64()).unwrap_or(0) as u64

Concrete instances:
  - sequence (events): CHECK (sequence > 0) at schema; decoder gives 0 on NULL → silently violates invariant downstream.
  - event_count, redacted_count, payload_bytes (runs): CHECK >= 0; decoder gives 0 on NULL → looks like an empty run, not a decode failure.

If the row is well-formed these branches never fire — but if a future migration reorders columns, drops a NOT NULL, or someone runs raw SQL that nulls a value, the decoder masks it as 'zero'. No degraded-honesty marker; no warning logged.

ALSO — 'as u64' on i64: if a corrupt row stored a negative number (CHECK can be bypassed with PRAGMA ignore_check_constraints=OFF flips, or older DBs from before the constraint), the cast wraps to a huge u64 (~9.2e18). All scoring/budgeting that consumes event_count/payload_bytes would silently misbehave.

INTEGER OVERFLOW SCAN (the broader audit task):
  - src/core/economy.rs scoring math is f64 throughout; saturating_add used at 700-702 for token sums; f64::from(u32) with .max(1) for divisors; no overflow risk found.
  - src/pack/mod.rs:2417 slack() uses saturating_sub correctly; utilization_percent guards quota_tokens > 0.
  - No raw arithmetic on u32/u64 found in scoring paths that could overflow.

So the only integer hazard found is this silent NULL→0 / wrapping-cast pattern in db row decoders.

FIX:
  (1) Change unwrap_or(0) as u64 → ok_or_else(... DbError::Integrity { column: 'sequence' }).
  (2) Use u64::try_from(i64) and surface the error rather than 'as u64' wrapping.
  (3) Add a test that injects a NULL into recorder_events.sequence (via PRAGMA writable_schema, or by mocking row) and asserts decode returns Err.

PRIORITY LOW: requires upstream corruption to fire. File for hardening sweep.
close_reason: Fixed silent data corruption. stored_recorder_run_from_row and stored_recorder_event_from_row now use required_u64/optional_u32 helpers that return DbError on NULL or negative values instead of silently coercing to 0 or wrapping.

title: Read-side connection pool with WAL snapshot pinning for ee context multi-call workflows
description:
## Why this matters (correctness + concurrency)

`ee context` issues 4-7 internal queries against FrankenSQLite during a single pack assembly: workspace resolve, retrieval, candidate scoring, graph snapshot lookup, audit append, and pack record write. Today these all use a single shared connection per process, with no transactional boundary linking them. Two correctness + perf consequences:

1. **Read-after-read inconsistency**: Between the candidate scoring and the graph snapshot lookup, another agent (in a separate process on the same host) can land a memory revise. The pack assembly then sees a candidate set from generation N but graph features from generation N+1. The resulting pack is internally inconsistent — its provenance points at row IDs that may already be tombstoned, and its determinism contract becomes 'same start state' rather than 'same DB state', which is weaker than what AGENTS.md promises.

2. **No read concurrency**: FrankenSQLite WAL supports many concurrent readers + one writer per database file. Today ee uses a single connection per process even for read-heavy workflows like `ee context`. With 4-8 agents on a host all running `ee context` concurrently, they serialize through the single per-process connection (and contend across processes for the WAL header). A read pool exposes the WAL's actual concurrency.

This bead introduces a per-workspace ReadConnectionPool (default size = min(8, num_cpus/2), configurable) plus a SnapshotPin guard that pins a transaction snapshot for the duration of a multi-call workflow.

## Architecture

ReadConnectionPool: lock-free LIFO of N read-only DbConnection handles per workspace, lazily grown up to a cap, idle connections evict after `idle_timeout` (default 30s). Acquire returns a guarded handle that auto-returns to the pool on Drop. Pool is process-scoped; cross-process concurrency relies on the WAL itself (already correct).

SnapshotPin: at the start of `ee context`, acquire a connection AND issue `BEGIN TRANSACTION READ ONLY` (or FrankenSQLite's equivalent isolation primitive — sqlmodel's read-snapshot helper if exposed, otherwise a deferred BEGIN). All subsequent reads in that workflow use the same connection within that transaction. On Drop, the SnapshotPin commits-or-rollbacks (a read-only transaction is safe to commit; FrankenSQLite WAL releases the snapshot reference). The pin gives RC isolation across the workflow without blocking writers.

Multi-workflow contract: each ee context invocation gets its own pin. Two concurrent context invocations on the same workspace each get separate snapshots and never deadlock. Writes from `ee remember` / `ee outcome` continue through the existing single write-owner path; readers see a stable snapshot from before the write started.

## Hard constraints

- Determinism preserved: a context invocation against state S MUST produce the same pack hash regardless of pool size (1, 4, 8) or whether snapshot pinning is on. New tests pin this.
- Backwards compat: pool defaults to size=1 with pinning enabled to match current single-conn behavior in observable JSON output. Operators opt into larger pools via config.
- AGENTS.md no-tokio: pool implementation uses asupersync `Cx` for any background eviction; never blocks acquire.
- Pool teardown on workspace close MUST drain all snapshots cleanly (no leaked WAL reader frames).
- Audit + write paths continue to use the existing single-writer connection — this bead is read-only.

## File surface

- src/db/read_pool.rs (NEW): ReadConnectionPool, SnapshotPin, PoolConfig. Inline #[cfg(test)] units.
- src/db/mod.rs (MODIFY): expose acquire_read_pool(workspace_id) -> &Pool; expose pin_snapshot(workflow_id) -> SnapshotPin guard. Existing single-conn helpers stay (used by writes).
- src/core/context.rs (MODIFY): top of handle_context acquires SnapshotPin from the workspace pool and threads it through retrieval/scoring/graph-lookup/audit-write boundary.
- src/config/mod.rs (MODIFY): `[storage.read_pool]` section: `size` (default min(8, ncpu/2)), `idle_timeout_seconds` (default 30), `pin_snapshot` (default true).
- src/config/env_registry.rs (MODIFY): EE_READ_POOL_SIZE, EE_READ_POOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S, EE_READ_POOL_DISABLE_PIN.

## UNIT TESTS REQUIRED

Inline #[cfg(test)] in src/db/read_pool.rs, minimum:
- happy_path__pool_acquire_returns_distinct_connections_up_to_cap
- happy_path__pool_release_returns_connection_to_lifo
- happy_path__snapshot_pin_holds_state_across_multiple_reads
- empty_or_boundary__pool_size_zero_falls_back_to_size_one_with_warning
- empty_or_boundary__idle_eviction_drops_unused_connections_after_timeout
- error_or_invalid__pool_acquire_when_db_is_locked_returns_error_not_panic
- error_or_invalid__snapshot_pin_drop_after_db_close_does_not_corrupt
- determinism__same_workflow_against_same_state_produces_same_pack_with_or_without_pin

## E2E TESTS REQUIRED

tests/read_pool_concurrency_e2e.rs (NEW): scripts/e2e_overhaul/read_pool_concurrency.sh (NEW). Spawns 8 concurrent `ee context` processes against the same workspace; while running, in a loop spawns `ee remember` writes. After 30 seconds:
- All 8 context calls returned successfully (no deadlocks, no broken pipes)
- All 8 returned packs internally consistent (every memory in the pack present in the DB at any single snapshot, verified by re-querying with snapshot N retrieved from each pack record)
- p50 latency with pool_size=8 ≤ 60% of p50 with pool_size=1 (concurrency win)

Structured logging per AGENTS.md: tracing events read_pool.acquire, read_pool.release, read_pool.evict, snapshot_pin.acquired, snapshot_pin.released. workspace_id, request_id, surface=read_pool|context, phase, elapsed_ms.

## Acceptance

- Pool implementation lands with 8+ unit tests passing.
- Concurrency e2e demonstrates ≥ 40% p50 latency improvement at pool_size=8 vs 1 under 4-writer concurrent load.
- Determinism gate (tests/determinism_unit.rs) extended with pool_size and pin_snapshot dimensions; all variants produce byte-identical pack hashes.
- ee status --json reports pool stats (active, idle, max_seen, drops) per workspace under `[data.read_pool]`.
- Configuration documented in docs/configuration/storage.md.
- AGENTS.md 'Limitations' note about single-process MVCC WAL updated to mention the read pool exposes WAL's actual concurrency under one process.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: nothing. Pool implementation is isolated from existing write path. Determinism gate already exists.

Related: bd-bife.7 (perf gate framework — pool changes go through it), bd-3gutc (alien-artifact swarm responsiveness umbrella).

## Tracing

surface=read_pool; phase=acquire|release|grow|evict|pin|unpin; required fields workspace_id, request_id, bead_id=THIS, surface, phase, elapsed_ms, degraded_codes, plus pool_size_current, pool_size_max.

comments.author: PearlPlateau
comments.text:
Phase 6 refinement pass (PearlPlateau).

Re-read AGENTS.md, particularly the "No reliance on multi-process concurrent SQLite writers" non-goal and the "Cancellation correct" performance principle. Found 8 gaps/optimizations.

### Refined hard constraints

1. SNAPSHOT PIN MAX AGE + WATCHDOG: long-held read snapshots prevent FrankenSQLite WAL checkpoint, which causes the WAL file to grow unbounded → eventually causes write-side latency spikes and disk pressure. Pool implementation MUST:
   - Honor `max_pin_duration` (default 30s, config `[storage.read_pool.max_pin_seconds]`, env `EE_READ_POOL_MAX_PIN_SECONDS`).
   - Run a watchdog in an asupersync background scope that scans active pins every 1s.
   - On expiry: emit `degraded.snapshot_pin_expired` (severity=medium, response_time), log a warning with workflow_id + acquired_at, force-release (rollback the transaction), mark the pin as poisoned so the workflow's next read returns an error rather than silently giving stale data.
   - Add unit test `watchdog__pin_held_beyond_max_duration_is_force_released_and_marked_poisoned`.

2. WAL CHECKPOINT INTERPLAY: a busy read pool effectively pins the WAL. Need explicit coordination:
   - If `ee daemon` is running, daemon owns checkpoint cadence (every 60s).
   - If no daemon, the write-owner thread runs `wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)` opportunistically and `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` when WAL > `EE_WAL_CHECKPOINT_BYTES_THRESHOLD` (default 64 MiB).
   - Document the relationship in `docs/configuration/storage.md` under a new section "Read pool ↔ WAL checkpoint".
   - Add `degraded.wal_growth_exceeds_threshold` (severity=warning, response_time) emitted from `ee status --json` when WAL > threshold.

3. POOL TEARDOWN ORDERING: workspace close MUST drain readers BEFORE shutting down the write owner. Otherwise the writer might block waiting for snapshot release while the readers are waiting for the writer's coordination. Explicit shutdown sequence documented in source + tested via `workspace_close__drains_readers_before_writer_shutdown`.

4. DROP UNDER PANIC + INFALLIBLE RELEASE: SnapshotPin::Drop MUST release the transaction even when the workflow panics. Implementation rules:
   - Use an atomic flag (`released: AtomicBool`) to make Drop idempotent.
   - The release path inside Drop MUST be infallible from the caller's perspective: if rollback returns an error, log via tracing + emit `degraded.snapshot_release_failed` (severity=high, response_time) + abandon the connection (do NOT return it to the pool). Do NOT panic in Drop.
   - Add unit test `drop__on_panic_path_releases_pin_idempotently` using `std::panic::catch_unwind`.

5. ACQUIRE WAIT HISTOGRAM: for tuning, ee status must report not just current { active, idle, max_seen, drops } but also `acquire_wait_ns_p50` and `acquire_wait_ns_p99` over the last N=1024 acquires (sliding window). Add to schema `ee.status.v1` under `data.read_pool.<workspace_id>.acquire_wait`.

6. ASUPERSYNC COOPERATIVE YIELD: when pool is at cap and a new acquire comes in, the acquirer MUST yield via `Cx::yield_now()` rather than busy-wait. Implementation must document the cooperative-yield contract in source comments and verify via test `acquire_under_contention_yields_cooperatively_not_busy_loops` (uses asupersync LabRuntime to assert no busy spin counted).

7. CANCELLATION PROPAGATION: if `ee context` is cancelled while a SnapshotPin is held, the pin MUST release immediately (transaction rollback). Add `tests/cancellation_read_pool.rs` mirroring the pattern in `tests/cancellation_graph.rs`:
   - `read_pool_acquire_exits_promptly_after_budget_cancellation`
   - `snapshot_pin_release_runs_on_cancellation_drop`

8. FRANKENSQLITE PRIMITIVE VERIFICATION: the original bead says "BEGIN TRANSACTION READ ONLY". FrankenSQLite-via-sqlmodel may expose this as `sqlmodel::Session::begin_read()` or equivalent. Implementer MUST:
   - Verify the FrankenSQLite/sqlmodel primitive that gives true RC isolation (snapshot pin until commit/rollback).
   - If the primitive is NOT exposed: fall back to "best effort — re-read on each call" (current behavior), expose this via `degraded.snapshot_pin_not_supported` (severity=low, response_time), and file a follow-up bead against the franken-stack.
   - Do NOT silently degrade — the degraded code MUST appear in `ee context --json` responses when the pin is best-effort, so agents know whether the determinism contract is upheld or downgraded.

### Refined unit-test obligation (extends original)

Original 8 tests stay. Add:
- watchdog__pin_held_beyond_max_duration_is_force_released_and_marked_poisoned
- watchdog__pin_within_max_duration_is_not_disturbed
- workspace_close__drains_readers_before_writer_shutdown
- drop__on_panic_path_releases_pin_idempotently
- drop__double_drop_does_not_double_release
- acquire_under_contention_yields_cooperatively_not_busy_loops
- snapshot_primitive__falls_back_with_degraded_code_when_unsupported
- metrics__acquire_wait_histogram_records_p50_and_p99_correctly

### Refined e2e obligation (extends original)

Original 8-concurrent + 4-writer scenario stays. Add:
- Scenario B (NEW): Long-pin scenario — single `ee context` instrumented to hold a snapshot for 35 seconds (exceeds max_pin_seconds=30). Assert: watchdog fires within 1s of expiry, emits `degraded.snapshot_pin_expired`, the workflow's next read fails with a clean error (not a panic). WAL file size does NOT grow unbounded (asserted via `wc -c .ee/ee.db-wal` before/after — bounded growth, exact bytes depends on writers active).
- Scenario C (NEW): Daemon-interplay — start `ee daemon`, run 4-writer load with `pool_size=8`, monitor WAL size for 5 minutes. Assert WAL stays below 128 MiB (with default 64 MiB checkpoint threshold). Verify checkpoint events appear in tracing logs.
- Scenario D (NEW): Cancellation — start `ee context`, SIGTERM the process mid-flight, assert via DB inspection that no transaction is left orphaned (sqlite_master row count + WAL frame count return to baseline).

`tests/cancellation_read_pool.rs` (NEW): mirrors `tests/cancellation_graph.rs` shape.

### Refined dependency edges (must be added)

- bd-2caru `related to` bd-3usjw.57 (e2e_multi_agent_write_contention) — read pool changes write contention dynamics; SF7's e2e contract must observe the new pool behavior.
- bd-2caru `related to` bd-gni47 (single-flight) — both work to reduce duplicate read work; complementary not duplicative.
- bd-2caru `related to` bd-bife.24 (memory-budget) — WAL growth is a memory/disk budget concern.

### Refined acceptance (extends)

Original 6 items stay. Add:
- Watchdog fires per Scenario B; `degraded.snapshot_pin_expired` lands in failure-modes catalog at `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/snapshot_pin_expired.json` (severity=medium, response_time) per AGENTS.md J6 contract.
- `degraded.snapshot_release_failed`, `degraded.snapshot_pin_not_supported`, `degraded.wal_growth_exceeds_threshold` fixtures added.
- AGENTS.md "Limitations" section update is a docs change touching a load-bearing top-level file — requires explicit user approval before merge per the spirit of RULE 1. Implementer MUST request approval in the bead comment thread before editing AGENTS.md.
- `ee status --json` includes `data.read_pool.<workspace_id>.acquire_wait.{p50,p99}` and `data.wal.bytes`.
- Pool-size guidance section added to `docs/configuration/storage.md`: "Set pool size to expected concurrent in-process workflows × 1.2. For typical agent loops (1 workflow at a time per process), 1-2 is sufficient. For agent harnesses that fan out (one process driving multiple parallel beads), set to fan-out count × 1.2."

### Tracing fields extended

`surface=read_pool`; `phase=acquire|release|grow|evict|pin|unpin|watchdog_fire|force_release|wal_checkpoint`; fields workspace_id, request_id, bead_id, surface, phase, elapsed_ms, degraded_codes, pool_size_current, pool_size_max, pin_age_ms, acquire_wait_ns.

### Open question (decide before implementation starts)

If asupersync exposes a structured-concurrency `Scope` primitive that already enforces resource lifetime bounds (drop-on-scope-exit), should SnapshotPin BE a Scope guard rather than a plain RAII type? Investigate before implementing. The asupersync source is at `/dp/asupersync` per AGENTS.md "Third-Party Library Usage".
