title: SRR3a: write-hot-path ordering and audit invariant spec/proptest
description:
Scope: create the executable correctness harness that must exist before implementing bd-2lsxf write_hot_path_v2 production routing. This bead is intentionally narrower than SRR3: model and test ordering, cancellation, batch commit, audit-chain continuity, and snapshot publication invariants without changing the default write path.

Why: bd-2lsxf has the largest write-path payoff but also the largest correctness risk. A 64-agent wait-free/group-commit path is only acceptable if the total-order and audit-chain properties are pinned before code starts mutating DB/effect routing.

Required artifact shape:
- A pure model of write requests with producer id, per-producer sequence, enqueue order, cancellation point, and batch boundary.
- Invariants: FIFO per producer; deterministic cross-producer tie-break; every committed row has exactly one audit-chain predecessor/successor relation; cancelled-before-commit rows produce an explicit cancellation outcome and never create chain holes; snapshot generation increments only after a committed batch; published snapshots are monotone by generation.
- Property/proptest harness over N producers and M writes with random cancellation/batch-size schedules, comparing the modeled group-commit result to the sequential interpretation.
- Unit tests for single_writer_happy, multi_writer_ordering, cancellation_mid_batch, fsync_failure_propagation_model, snapshot_generation_monotone.
- No default behavior change and no new daemon/write routing.

Implementation guidance:
- Prefer a new isolated test/model surface only if existing files cannot house it cleanly; reserve files first.
- Keep the model deterministic and independent from wall-clock time. Use explicit seed/schedule inputs, not Instant/thread_rng/std::env direct reads.
- Any Cargo verification must run through RCH only.

title: SRR3.spec: executable write-hot-path ordering and audit invariants before implementation
description:
## IdeaWizard grounding

Phase 1 reality check: the backlog already contains broad swarm-response work (`bd-3gutc`), Swarm-X (`bd-1prrl`), workload replay (`bd-1zb7k.19`), read snapshots (`bd-2seqp` / `bd-2caru`), and the actual write-hot-path optimization (`bd-2lsxf`). What is missing is a separate, executable safety spec for SRR3 before agents touch the high-risk queue/group-commit/audit-chain implementation.

Phase 2 30-to-5 winnow: the best idea was not another cache or daemon surface; it was to turn SRR3's correctness requirements into a deterministic model and property harness first. Other considered ideas included adaptive cache admission, latency SLO dashboards, NUMA policy proofs, write-owner chaos tests, queue fairness tuning, audit-chain bisection, and recovery playbooks. Most overlap existing beads or are implementation details.

Phase 3 next-10 disposition: cancellation injection, fsync failure modeling, cross-producer FIFO proofs, epoch reclamation safety, batch-size fairness, audit-chain continuity, degraded-code fixtures, RCH fake-runner integration, TLA+/state-machine sketching, and CI drift gates are folded into the children here.

Phase 4 overlap check: this does not duplicate `bd-2lsxf`; it blocks/derisks it by producing acceptance artifacts before the production queue exists. It does not duplicate `bd-1zb7k.19` workload playback; that replays real command traces, while this enumerates abstract write schedules and failure interleavings. It does not duplicate `bd-nnfq4`; that focuses pack determinism and Agent Mail coordination, while this focuses write-order/audit invariants.

## Goal

Before SRR3 implementation begins, define an executable model of the write-hot-path contract: multi-producer enqueue order, group commit batching, cancellation before commit, fsync failure, audit-chain continuity, and snapshot publication. The model should be small, pure, deterministic, and usable by property tests and future TLA+/Lean proof work.

## Acceptance

- A documented invariant set exists for SRR3, with every invariant mapped to at least one unit/property/e2e or model-check test.
- Property generators cover concurrent producer schedules, cancellation points, fsync failures, and batch boundaries.
- The sequential reference interpreter and modeled group-commit interpreter produce byte-identical durable rows and audit-chain hashes for accepted writes.
- Failure-mode fixtures exist for cancelled-before-commit and fsync-failure paths.
- CI can run a lightweight fake/simulated harness without requiring a live RCH worker, while full Cargo verification remains RCH-only.

## Non-goals

No production queue implementation, no new runtime dependency, no Tokio, no DB schema migration, no daemon-first behavior, no file deletion or cleanup automation. This is plan/proof/test substrate for SRR3, not SRR3 itself.

## Refinement notes

Phase 6 review pass 1: keep the surface deliberately pre-implementation; otherwise agents may mix proof work with production queue churn.
Phase 6 pass 2: include failure fixtures now so degraded-code taxonomy does not lag implementation.
Phase 6 pass 3: require a fake runner so CI can catch model regressions even when RCH workers are saturated.
Phase 6 pass 4: keep audit-chain continuity as load-bearing; throughput wins are invalid if chain order is ambiguous.
Phase 6 pass 5: no oversimplification: cancellation, fsync, and snapshot publication are all required because they are exactly where swarm-scale write paths fail.

title: SRR3.spec.1: sequential reference model and invariant manifest
description:
## Goal

Create the pure reference model for SRR3 before production write-hot-path code exists. The model defines producers, enqueue events, cancellation events, group-commit batch boundaries, accepted durable rows, rejected rows, snapshot publication points, and audit-chain hash transitions.

## Required behavior

- Model input is a deterministic schedule, not wall-clock time.
- Cross-producer ordering uses explicit sequence numbers; per-producer FIFO is preserved.
- Cancelled-before-commit writes are excluded from durable rows but represented as modeled audit outcomes.
- Fsync failure stops publication and returns a structured modeled error without inventing rows.
- The invariant manifest maps each invariant to the child test that proves it.

## Acceptance

- A small module or test-only model exists with inline happy/edge/error unit coverage.
- A checked-in invariant manifest documents ordering, cancellation, fsync, audit-chain, and snapshot-publication invariants.
- No production queue, DB mutation, daemon behavior, or new runtime dependency is introduced.
- RCH-only Cargo verification is used for Rust tests; non-Cargo static checks are acceptable while RCH is saturated.

title: SRR3.spec.4: ADR and implementation gate for write-hot-path v2
description:
## Goal

Write the architecture decision and implementation gate that future SRR3 production patches must satisfy before modifying the write queue, group commit, or snapshot publication paths.

## ADR content

- Why group commit must preserve audit-chain order.
- Why per-table parallel writers are rejected.
- How cancellation before commit is represented.
- How fsync failure prevents snapshot publication.
- How the executable model maps to production APIs.
- Which metrics are correctness gates versus performance gates.

## Implementation gate

- Any production SRR3 patch must cite the invariant manifest.
- Any new write-hot-path degraded code must include a fixture.
- Any queue/batch API must show a property test that compares against the sequential interpreter.
- Any performance benchmark must be secondary to the correctness properties.

## Acceptance

- ADR exists and is linked from `bd-2lsxf` or the SRR3 docs.
- A clear checklist lets agents decide whether a future SRR3 patch is allowed to proceed.
- No source behavior changes are made by this docs/gate bead beyond references needed for discoverability.

title: EQL query plan cache: memoize parse/bind/index-selection across identical queries (idea-wizard MagentaPanther 2026-05-18)
description: EVIDENCE: src/core/search.rs:2412 run_search_inner calls :2476-2483 search_sync() which re-parses the EQL on every invocation. src/models/query.rs:872 parse_eql_query() is the parse entry. No memoization layer. Under swarm load, ee context and ee search re-parse identical EQL queries thousands of times per minute. Memoize the resolved plan tree (parse + bind + index selection + join strategy) keyed on (eql_hash, index_manifest_version, search_config_hash). DISTINGUISHABILITY: distinct from L2 pack cache (bd-ndzfg) which caches RESULTS; plan cache caches the COMPILED PLAN that's the dominant cost on result-cache misses. See follow-up comment for full design.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
FULL SPEC (MagentaPanther idea-wizard + reality-check 2026-05-18)

DESIGN:
1. New module src/search/plan_cache.rs holds a bounded LRU keyed on (eql_hash:u64, index_manifest_version:u64, search_config_hash:u64) -> CompiledPlan.
2. Cache lookup at the top of search_sync() (src/core/search.rs:2476). On hit, skip parse/bind/index-choice and dispatch directly. On miss, run the existing path and insert the resolved plan.
3. Invalidation: bumping index_manifest_version OR search_config_hash naturally invalidates entries since they form part of the key. No active eviction needed beyond LRU bound.
4. Bounded memory: default 1024 entries, ~5MB cap. Configurable via EE_QUERY_PLAN_CACHE_ENTRIES.

FILE SURFACE:
- src/search/plan_cache.rs (NEW)
- src/core/search.rs (hook at :2476 search_sync entry)
- src/config/env_registry.rs: EE_QUERY_PLAN_CACHE_ENTRIES (default 1024)
- tests/plan_cache_unit.rs (NEW)
- tests/plan_cache_e2e.rs (NEW)
- docs/search/plan-cache.md (NEW)

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Identical EQL -> identical plan-tree hash on cache hit (unit test).
2. Plan-cache invalidated on index_manifest_version bump (golden test).
3. Plan-cache invalidated on search_config_hash change.
4. p50 EQL plan resolution drops from baseline (~50us) to <2us on cache hit.
5. Cache miss path identical to baseline (no regression for cold queries).
6. ee diag plan-cache --json exposes hit rate, eviction count, top patterns.
7. Bounded memory (default 1024 entries, ~5MB cap).
8. All Cargo verification through RCH only.

TRACING: surface=plan_cache; required fields workspace_id, eql_hash, manifest_version, decision (hit|miss|invalidated), elapsed_ms, degraded_codes (plan_cache_disabled, plan_cache_full).

DISTINGUISHABILITY:
- bd-ndzfg (L2 pack cache): caches RESULTS keyed on (query, workspace, manifest). Plan cache caches the COMPILED PLAN. On L2 miss (e.g., DB advanced), L2 still pays parse/bind cost which plan cache avoids.
- bd-gni47 (single-flight): coalesces in-flight duplicate calls. Plan cache helps even after the in-flight wave ends.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES:
- Cache resolved plans across DB generations: would re-emit results from a stale plan; rejected for correctness.
- Cache only parse output (not bind/index-choice): the dominant cost is bind+index-choice, not parse. Half-measure.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Per epic constraint: src/core/write_owner.rs implements an actor that queues write requests and dequeues them in order. Today only the advisory_lock primitive (db/mod.rs:8231 acquire_advisory_lock + retry loop) exists — multiple processes coordinate but they do NOT share an in-process queue.

Fix scope:

title: SRR6.44: Peer outcome feedback, trust decay, and quality recalibration
description:
Design peer outcome feedback, trust decay, and quality recalibration without promoting remote feedback into local truth automatically. Nodes should be able to share that a memory helped, misled, became stale, contradicted later evidence, or was withdrawn, while preserving provenance and local policy control.

Scope includes: feedback event kinds; trust-decay inputs from peer outcomes; per-peer weighting; opt-out from receiving or using peer feedback; learn/curate integration; context/why explanation of peer feedback; and safeguards against one bad peer poisoning rankings. Feedback should influence candidate scoring only through explicit, deterministic, auditable rules.

Acceptance: unit tests for feedback weighting, trust caps, decay, and bad-peer isolation; e2e script where one peer reports a memory as misleading and another reports it as useful, then local search/context shows both feedback signals without silently deleting or promoting the memory; structured logs for peer_feedback_received, trust_delta_applied, feedback_ignored_by_policy, ranking_adjustment_reason.

title: [MEDIUM] list_recorder_events_filtered with limit=0 returns ZERO rows (LIMIT 0), not all rows
description:
Cycle-4 reviewer audit (REVIEWER pane). Surface: recorder pagination.

src/db/mod.rs:11469 list_recorder_events_filtered(run_id, since, source, limit: u32) unconditionally appends ' LIMIT ?N' (line 11507-11509) using the supplied limit. SQLite treats LIMIT 0 as 'return zero rows'.

CALLER FOOTGUN:
  src/core/recorder.rs:2259 RecorderEventsListOptions derives Default, so RecorderEventsListOptions { run_id: Some(...), ..Default::default() } yields limit=0. The CLI surface for 'ee recorder events list' must explicitly default the limit; if any future caller forgets, the surface returns an empty list and reports count=0 with no error and no degraded-honesty marker — the operator sees 'no events recorded' when in reality the query was malformed.

CONTRAST with tail_recording_from_events (recorder.rs:1340) which converts limit=0 → usize::try_from(0).unwrap_or(usize::MAX) … wait, that converts 0 to 0, not MAX. So tail_recording with limit=0 also returns zero events but has the additional sort+truncate path. Either way, behavior is silent.

FIX:
  In list_recorder_events_filtered, treat limit==0 as 'no limit' (skip the LIMIT clause), OR enforce limit >= 1 at the API boundary with a typed NonZeroU32. The CLI should also reject --limit 0 with an EE-level usage error.

  Add unit tests:
    - list_recorder_events_filtered(..., 0) returns same count as without LIMIT (after fix)
    - tail_recording_from_events with limit=0 either errors or returns all (decide contract)

PRIORITY: MEDIUM — production callers currently pass non-zero limits, but the silent-failure mode is exactly the kind of regression that goes unnoticed until an operator reports a missing run.
close_reason: fixed

description:
## Background
README promises concrete p50/p99 budgets and the project requires CPU-heavy verification through `rch`. Swarm-scale work needs a benchmark harness that is explicit about where it runs, what it measures, and which results are release-blocking versus exploratory.

## What ships

4. JSON and human summaries suitable for CI annotations and support bundles.
5. Budget config that starts advisory and can become release-blocking once fixtures stabilize.

## Implementation notes
Build on the existing performance harness bead rather than creating a second benchmark universe. Use deterministic fixtures from the scale workload bead. Do not hardcode `/tmp`; follow the `rch` skill requirement to use `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}`.

## Tests and logging

- A no-mock smoke benchmark runs the smallest fixture and writes artifact paths to stderr/logs.
- CI output must make regressions actionable without opening flamegraphs first.

## Closure evidence
Close only after benchmark commands are documented, smallest-profile smoke passes through `rch`, and reports are stable enough for golden/schema tests.

title: [cass] Propagate subprocess pipe read and join failures
description:
## Background
`src/cass/process.rs` currently reads child stdout/stderr on helper threads, ignores `read_to_end` errors, and uses `join().unwrap_or_default()`. If a pipe reader fails or a helper thread panics, the CASS adapter can report an apparently valid command outcome with empty stdout/stderr, which is exactly the kind of silent evidence loss this track is meant to eliminate.

## What to do
- Replace the helper thread return type with a result that preserves whether stdout or stderr failed to read.
- Convert read failures and thread join panics into contextual `CassError` values or a stable degraded outcome if the surrounding CASS contract requires an outcome object.
- Preserve timeout behavior: killing the child on timeout should still wait/reap the process and report timeout truthfully, but it must not hide reader failures behind empty buffers.
- Add focused unit coverage with a testable reader helper where possible; avoid relying on nondeterministic OS pipe failures if a pure helper test can cover the join/read error mapping.

## Acceptance
- No `join().unwrap_or_default()` or ignored `read_to_end` result remains in the CASS subprocess output path.
- Tests cover normal stdout/stderr capture and at least one reader failure or join-failure mapping.
- Machine-facing import/search callers still get stable JSON errors or degradations, not raw panics.
- Verification: focused CASS process tests, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `ubs src/cass/process.rs` through RCH for cargo-heavy gates.
close_reason: Fix merged in e2a40542: join_pipe_reader returns Result and converts read errors/panics to CassError::Io; tests cover success, read error, and thread panic paths; no_silent_fallback_inventory now expects 0 occurrences

title: [cache] Hotset prewarm and cache-governor for context/search
description:
## Background
Large agent swarms repeatedly ask similar before-work questions. The system should make repeated `ee context` and `ee search` calls fast without making indexes authoritative, bypassing policy, or requiring a daemon for correctness.

## What ships
1. A hotset model for frequently used memories, query shapes, search documents, graph neighborhoods, and pack sections.
2. A prewarm command/job that can materialize safe derived caches from FrankenSQLite + Frankensearch state and discard them when generations change.
3. Cache-governor policy that uses explicit memory budgets, generation checks, and graceful degradation when memory pressure is high.
4. Status/reporting fields that explain cache hit rate, stale generation, memory footprint, and fallback reason.

## Implementation notes
Derived caches must be safe to delete and rebuild. They must not store secrets outside the existing redaction policy. Use existing `cache/`, `search/`, `pack/`, and status/capability reporting patterns. Do not add a custom vector store or custom BM25/RRF logic.

## Tests and logging
- Unit tests cover generation invalidation, budget enforcement, stale-cache fallback, and redaction-safe cache entries.
- Integration tests run repeated `context`/`search` calls against a deterministic fixture and assert stable output with and without cache.
- Logged benchmark evidence must show latency improvement or document why the cache was intentionally bypassed.

## Closure evidence
Close only after behavior is deterministic, cache status is visible in JSON, and rch-offloaded tests/benchmarks cover cache-on, cache-off, and pressure-fallback paths.
close_reason: Implemented hotset prewarm with cache-governor; cache-on/cache-off equivalence verified

title: L2 follow-up: backup records.jsonl is non-deterministic across identical exports (J7)
description:
Discovered while writing L2 backup roundtrip determinism test (bd-17c65.12.3 / tests/contracts/backup_import_roundtrip.rs).

Exporting the same workspace twice with the same redaction level produces records.jsonl files whose records_hash diverges. Likely causes: timestamp embedded in record rows, non-deterministic iteration order over memories/tags, or audit_id allocated at export time.

L2's round-trip determinism gate passes because it normalizes via a workspace_state_hash that strips volatile fields. But J7 wants strict byte-equivalence across identical exports — that test is in place but #[ignore]d: tests/contracts/backup_import_roundtrip.rs::backup_records_jsonl_is_deterministic_across_two_exports — un-ignore when fix lands.

Tracking under the J7 umbrella (bd-17c65.10.7) but pre-shipping the regression test.
notes:
PLAN-SPACE REVISION (2026-05-12 TealHarbor — fix path + verification gate):

## Fix candidates (test all three; ship the simplest that works)

The bead identifies non-determinism in backup records.jsonl exports. Three plausible sources:

1. **Wall-clock timestamps embedded in records** — if records carry `exported_at` or any per-export timestamp, scrub it (move to a separate manifest field that is excluded from the records.jsonl hash).
2. **Iteration order over a HashMap-backed structure** — sort by canonical key (memory_id ascending, then revision_number ascending) before serialization. AGENTS.md "determinism is non-negotiable" applies here.
3. **JSON key ordering** — use a BTreeMap-backed serializer or canonical key order to avoid serde_json's default-allocation insertion order.

Implementation order: do #2 first (highest impact, lowest risk). Verify with the existing `#[ignore]'d` test. If still non-deterministic, do #3. #1 is a separate cleanup.

## Verification gate

`tests/contracts/backup_import_roundtrip.rs::backup_records_jsonl_is_deterministic_across_two_exports` (already ignored) un-ignored after the fix lands:

```rust
#[test]
fn backup_records_jsonl_is_deterministic_across_two_exports() -> TestResult {
    let ws = make_workspace_with_seed()?;
    let export_a = export_backup(&ws, "label_a")?;
    let export_b = export_backup(&ws, "label_b")?;
    let bytes_a = fs::read(&export_a.records_jsonl)?;
    let bytes_b = fs::read(&export_b.records_jsonl)?;
    let hash_a = blake3::hash(&bytes_a);
    let hash_b = blake3::hash(&bytes_b);
    assert_eq!(hash_a, hash_b, "backup records.jsonl must be byte-deterministic across exports of the same workspace");
    Ok(())
}
```

## Composes with J7

Add to `scripts/e2e_overhaul/determinism.sh`:

```bash
# bd-2r19w: backup records.jsonl is byte-deterministic across exports
$EE backup create --workspace $WS --label run_1 --json > /dev/null
$EE backup create --workspace $WS --label run_2 --json > /dev/null
HASH_1=$(find $WS/.ee/backups -name 'records.jsonl' -path '*run_1*' | xargs blake3sum | awk '{print $1}')
HASH_2=$(find $WS/.ee/backups -name 'records.jsonl' -path '*run_2*' | xargs blake3sum | awk '{print $1}')
[ "$HASH_1" = "$HASH_2" ] && e2e_log_assert_eq "true" "true" "backup_records_jsonl_deterministic" \
   || e2e_log_assert_eq "h1=$HASH_1 h2=$HASH_2" "all_equal" "backup_records_jsonl_deterministic"
```

## Logging event (per backup create)

```json
{
  "schema": "ee.test_event.v1",
  "kind": "backup_create",
  "label": "<label>",
  "memories_exported": <usize>,
  "records_jsonl_bytes": <usize>,
  "records_jsonl_hash": "<blake3>",
  "manifest_hash": "<blake3>",
  "iteration_order_strategy": "btreemap_memory_id_then_revision",
  "elapsed_ms": <float>
}
```

## Failure-mode fixture (J6)

- `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/backup_records_jsonl_nondeterministic.json` (severity HIGH while bug is open; flipped to closed-fixture once fix lands; serves as a "this used to fail" regression marker).

## Acceptance gate

- The previously-ignored unit test passes without `#[ignore]`.
- determinism.sh `backup_records_jsonl_deterministic` assertion passes across 3 sequential backup creates.
- Logging events show the same `records_jsonl_hash` across exports of identical workspace state.
- The fix's commit message identifies which of fix-candidates #1/#2/#3 was applied (no silent change).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
src/db/mod.rs:8408-8430 is_lock_held does:
```
SELECT ... FROM ee_advisory_locks
WHERE resource_type = ?1 AND resource_id = ?2
ORDER BY acquired_at DESC LIMIT 1
```
The bdab856 commit message says this lookup style supports 'a stale row with a slightly different canonical key still exists (e.g. after a key-format migration)'. But acquire_advisory_lock_in_transaction (8310-8320) only consults WHERE resource_key = ?1, and release_advisory_lock (8390-8402) deletes WHERE resource_key = ? AND holder_id = ?. There is no code path that prunes stale (resource_type, resource_id) rows whose resource_key differs from the current canonical encoding.

Concrete failure: holder A acquires v1-encoded resource_key, code is upgraded to v2 encoding, holder A attempts release with v2 key — DELETE finds nothing, function returns false. Holder B then acquires v2 key successfully. is_lock_held now returns the row with the most recent acquired_at, which depends on row ordering — possibly the stale v1 row, which falsely advertises a held lock to a third party.

Fix: either (a) acquire_advisory_lock_in_transaction also clears stale rows for the same (resource_type, resource_id), or (b) cleanup_expired_locks scans by (resource_type, resource_id) and reaps duplicates. Add a regression test that multi-encoded rows for the same logical resource resolve consistently.

title: [HIGH] Pack item redaction happens post-budget — usedTokens / estimatedTokens over-report rendered content
description:
## Surface
`src/pack/mod.rs` MMR / facility-location selection + emit (audit cycle 5)

## Finding
The new `PackDraftItem::from_selected_candidate` (`src/pack/mod.rs:1252-1284`, added in HEAD's working diff) calls `redact_pack_item_content` AFTER the candidate has already been weighed against the token budget:

```rust
fn from_selected_candidate(rank: u32, candidate: PackCandidate) -> Self {
    let PackCandidate { content, estimated_tokens, ... } = candidate;
    let (content, redactions) = redact_pack_item_content(content);
    Self { content, estimated_tokens, redactions, ... }
}
```

`estimated_tokens` is preserved unchanged. But `content` may now be substantially shorter (every redacted secret becomes `[REDACTED:scanner_name]`).

Effects:
1. `response.data.pack.budget.usedTokens` (sum of items' `estimated_tokens`) over-reports the actual size of rendered content.
2. `item.estimatedTokens` in JSON no longer matches `item.content` for redacted items.
3. `compute_pack_hash` (`src/core/context.rs:524-548`) hashes the redacted content AND the un-redacted estimated_tokens — internally consistent, so determinism is fine, but the hash certifies a number that is wrong.
4. Pack underutilizes its budget: secret-heavy content gets penalized 'as if' it was full size, leaving room unused.

## Determinism: not broken
Redaction is deterministic (`SECRET_REDACTION_PLACEHOLDER` is a literal const, reasons sorted+deduped). Same input → byte-identical JSON. `tests/e2e_pack_determinism.rs` still passes.

## Honesty: broken
The JSON contract advertises `usedTokens` / `estimatedTokens` as 'cost of the rendered content'. Post-emit redaction breaks that claim.

## Fix options
A) Recompute `estimated_tokens` after redaction inside `from_selected_candidate` (and revisit `used_tokens` accumulation if the algorithm wants to backfill the saved budget into the next omitted candidate).
B) Redact at candidate-construction time so the budget sees the post-redaction size from the start. Cleaner, but coupling between candidates_from_search and policy::redact_secret_like_content.
C) Keep current behavior but add an explicit field `item.preRedactionEstimatedTokens` and document the over-counting in the contract.

## Repro
```bash
# look at git diff HEAD -- src/pack/mod.rs lines 1252-1284 and 1298-1310
```
close_reason: Fixed in 053917e: pack candidates are redacted before selection token accounting, so rendered item estimates, usedTokens, and selection-certificate costs align.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
src/db/mod.rs:1152-1183 Migration::new docstring says:
```
/// Construct a migration. Checksum is `blake3:<hex>` of the SQL text.
```
But the body just stashes the caller-supplied &'static str. Every site (V001-V028) supplies a label like "blake3:v028_advisory_locks_2026_05_05" — these are not blake3 hashes; they are date-stamped tags. A contributor can edit the SQL body of an existing migration and forget to bump the checksum string, and validate_applied_migration_records (line 2425+) will not catch it because the stored checksum still matches the (non-)hash in code.

Fix options ranked: (1) compute blake3 lazily on first use with std::sync::OnceLock and fail Migration registration if SQL doesn't hash to the supplied checksum — turns 'forgot to update' into a startup error. (2) drop the misleading 'blake3:' prefix and rename the field to migration_tag — at least the doc no longer lies. (3) generate a build.rs file that emits the actual blake3 of each SQL alongside, and assert at startup that runtime hashes match.

title: [MEDIUM] V036 trigger lacks regression test for direct DELETE FROM recorder_events — design trade-off untested at boundary
description:
## Surface
Effect of recent swarm fixes — V036 / is96 (audit cycle 8, surface 1)

## Finding
The V036 migration (src/db/mod.rs:3141-3186) installs three triggers:
- `recorder_events_no_update` — blocks UPDATE on recorder_events ✓ tested at src/core/recorder.rs:3394
- `audit_log_no_update` — blocks UPDATE on audit_log (with workspaces SET NULL carve-out) ✓ tested at src/core/audit.rs:806
- `audit_log_no_delete` — blocks DELETE on audit_log ✓ tested at src/core/audit.rs:829

NOTABLE OMISSION: there is NO `recorder_events_no_delete` trigger. The migration comment states:
> "recorder_events: append-only at the engine. DELETE is permitted so the existing recorder_runs ON DELETE CASCADE can run; UPDATE is never legitimate."

This is a deliberate design trade-off — SQLite triggers cannot easily distinguish 'a cascade delete fires' from 'a direct DELETE statement'. The fix chose to leave DELETE on recorder_events open.

The accompanying test `deleting_recorder_run_still_cascades_to_events` (src/core/recorder.rs:3432) verifies the cascade WORKS. But there is NO test covering the OTHER half of the trade-off: a direct `DELETE FROM recorder_events WHERE event_id = X` succeeds without going through the parent run row. That's the open hole the design accepts.

The is96 bead's close_reason acknowledges this:
> "An attacker with raw-SQL access can still DROP TRIGGER first ... but the chain hash check still catches the underlying tamper."

But it doesn't address direct DELETE. A raw `DELETE FROM recorder_events WHERE event_id = 'evt_X'` succeeds silently. No DROP TRIGGER required. The chain hash catches that the chain has a gap (sequence N+1 follows N-1) but doesn't surface 'a row was deleted' — it surfaces 'the chain looks broken' which the operator might attribute to a partial import.

## Why it matters
1. The append-only contract for recorder_events is weaker than for audit_log. Documentation should make this explicit.
2. There's no test pinning the 'direct DELETE succeeds' behavior — a future migration could accidentally ADD a recorder_events_no_delete trigger that breaks the cascade, and only a runtime cascade test would notice.
3. ee's chain-verification command surface should explicitly report 'sequence gap' as a separate degradation from 'hash mismatch' so a tamper-via-DELETE is detectable.

## Fix
Either:
A) Add a test `direct_delete_on_recorder_events_succeeds` next to deleting_recorder_run_still_cascades_to_events that asserts the design intent — DELETE FROM recorder_events succeeds and cascades from the run-table delete are unaffected.
B) Replace the missing trigger with a smarter version using SQLite's `raise_when_safe` pattern: install a `recorder_events_no_direct_delete` trigger that aborts unless OLD.run_id NOT IN (SELECT run_id FROM recorder_runs). This blocks direct DELETE but lets the cascade fire because the parent row is already gone when the cascade trigger evaluates. (Verification needed — SQLite's exact trigger ordering for cascades is subtle.)
C) Surface a 'sequence gap' degradation in ee recorder verify so the chain-verifier reports tampered-via-DELETE distinctly from tampered-via-hash-mismatch.

## Severity
MEDIUM because:
- The design choice was made deliberately (per is96 close_reason).
- The trade-off is not catastrophic — chain integrity is still detectable post-hoc.
- But it is a documented gap with no test or degradation surface, which is the same pattern that landed the original is96.
close_reason: Added recorder regression coverage for the accepted direct recorder_events DELETE trade-off. The new test proves direct DELETE removes only the targeted event while preserving the parent run, then proves deleting the parent run still cascade-deletes remaining events. Also removed the adjacent recorder test's expect_err strict-clippy violation. Verification: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check src/core/recorder.rs; git diff --check -- src/core/recorder.rs; RCH cargo test --lib direct_delete_on_recorder_events_succeeds_and_cascade_still_works; RCH cargo test --lib deleting_recorder_run_still_cascades_to_events; RCH cargo test --lib append_only_trigger_blocks_recorder_events_update; RCH cargo check --all-targets; UBS src/core/recorder.rs. Repo-wide cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings were attempted and remain blocked by unrelated pre-existing dirty/baseline issues outside this bead.

title: Idea: Read-only fork-on-context-pack — MVCC snapshot per ee context call to remove read-path contention
description:
## Origin

/idea-wizard pass 2026-05-15T22:36Z, top-ranked feature for 256GB+/64-core swarm hosts. Companion idea-set: bd-1o99v (HITS snapshot persistence), bd-gni47 (single-flight read coalescing — overlapping but read-side only, not connection-side).

## Why this matters

Today every `ee context "<task>"` invocation opens a DbConnection from a pool that contends with writers (curate apply, remember, learn, decay, steward jobs). On a 64-core host with ~16 agents doing context packs concurrently, the writer-induced WAL checkpoint pauses are the dominant tail-latency contributor. README L928-936 reports p99 context = 240ms; profiling shows ~120ms of that is connection-acquisition + WAL-fsync wait under load. The architecture intent (README L1083 'no silent memory mutation', AGENTS.md L494 'CLI first, deterministic by default') is reader/writer separation; the current implementation collapses both into a single ee process and one-pool-fits-all.

## Surface

`ee context` (and `ee why`, `ee search`, `ee pack replay`, `ee insights`, `ee status` — every read_only-classified command per src/core/effect.rs) acquires a *forked* read connection that:

1. Snapshots the current WAL generation via FrankenSQLite's MVCC primitive (or its existing snapshot_id metadata).
2. Holds a read lease against that generation so concurrent writers cannot vacuum it out from under the reader.
3. Releases the lease at the end of the call (drop guard).
4. Never blocks on writer-side fsync.

## Architecture sketch

- New `src/core/read_path.rs` introduces `ReadSnapshot { generation: u64, conn: DbConnection, lease_handle: ReadLeaseGuard }`.
- `ReadSnapshot::open(database_path, options) -> Result<Self, DomainError>` is the new entry point.
- All read_only effect handlers in src/cli/mod.rs take a `ReadSnapshot` rather than a `DbConnection` directly.
- Steward / curate / writer paths continue to use the existing connection_pool.
- The read snapshot has its own page cache sized via `EE_READ_SNAPSHOT_CACHE_MB` (default = min(host_RAM/64, 4096), honoring AGENTS.md per-machine config principle — no committed absolute paths).

## Determinism implications

A read snapshot pinned to generation N produces the same JSON output as any other reader at generation N. The pack hash MUST include the generation so `ee pack replay` against an evolving DB still finds the right ledger row. `ee.context.v2` already carries snapshotVersion; this is just promoting it from advisory to enforcing.

## Acceptance

- `ReadSnapshot` API + `ReadLeaseGuard` Drop impl.
- src/core/effect.rs gains a `#[must_use] read_snapshot()` classifier; CI lint asserts every read_only handler accepts a `ReadSnapshot`.
- Determinism test: pin two readers to the same generation under concurrent writer load (proptest), assert byte-identical JSON output.
- Perf bench: criterion harness in benches/context_swarm_read.rs simulates 16 concurrent agents issuing `ee context` against a 14k-memory fixture; p99 must drop ≥40% vs the current shared-pool baseline.
- E2E: tests/e2e_read_path_isolation.sh seeds a workspace, fires 16 parallel readers + 4 parallel writers, asserts no reader returns partial mutation state.
- Tracing per bd-3usjw.58: surface=read_snapshot, fields { snapshot_generation, lease_held_ms, page_cache_hit_ratio, fork_cost_us }.

## Risk register

- FrankenSQLite MVCC primitive surface area: read-the-source verification needed. If absent, fall back to a coarser snapshot-by-copy.
- Memory pressure: a stale reader holding generation N while writers advance to N+100 keeps the WAL from vacuuming. Mitigation: bounded lease TTL + soft-reject new leases when WAL backlog > threshold.
- Lock-free path: ReadLeaseGuard must not require a global mutex on drop; use atomic refcount.

## Cost of omission

Swarm hosts stall on the read path during bursty writer load. README's stated p99 numbers degrade by 3-5x under realistic 16-agent swarms. The graph-feature work landed this week (PPR, HITS, dominance, pack DNA) compounds the contention because each new feature reads more rows per context call.

## File surface

- src/core/read_path.rs (NEW)
- src/core/effect.rs (read_only classifier)
- src/cli/mod.rs read_only handlers (audit pass)
- benches/context_swarm_read.rs (NEW)
- tests/e2e_read_path_isolation.sh (NEW)
- tests/snapshot_lease_proptest.rs (NEW)
- src/config/env_registry.rs (EE_READ_SNAPSHOT_CACHE_MB)
- docs/env_vars.md (entry)

title: Swarm-X: extreme swarm responsiveness on 256GB+ / 64+-core hosts
description:
# Swarm-X — Extreme swarm responsiveness epic

Goal: take `ee context` and the swarm-write path from "fast" to "world-class" on hosts with 256GB+ RAM and 64+ cores, where dozens of agents fan out the same query within seconds and need byte-stable, low-latency responses.

This epic was filed via the `/idea-wizard` skill on 2026-05-15 by StormyCove against the explicit user goal: "taking full advantage of 256gb+ of RAM and 64+ cpu cores".

## Top 5 (P1 children, each child gets its own bead under this epic)

1. **stream-pack** (swarmx.1): chunked `ee context` output. First usable item ≤10ms via SSE/NDJSON; pack hash committed on stream close so the determinism contract still holds. `--stream` flag on `ee context`; falls back to batch when stdout is not a TTY. Surface: `src/cli/mod.rs`, `src/core/context.rs`, `src/output/mod.rs`. Output contract bumped to `ee.pack.v2.streaming` with one frame per memory + a trailing frame containing the final pack hash and selection ledger.
2. **xagent-pack-singleflight** (swarmx.2): extend `ee.singleflight.key.v1` (already shipped) with a workspace-scoped RAM cache. Same `(query, profile, snapshot_gen, max_tokens)` digest on two panes within ~5s shares one assembled pack. LRU + content-hash invalidation on memory writes. 256GB host holds ~10⁵ cached packs hot.
3. **prewarm-from-beads** (swarmx.3): opt-in steward job that runs `ee context "<bead-title>\n\n<bead-description>"` in background for the top-N `br ready` beads and stages results in the singleflight cache. Bounded by `--prewarm-budget-ms` per bead.
4. **numa-mmap-graph-snapshot** (swarmx.4): pin graph snapshot blobs in RAM via `mmap+MAP_POPULATE+mbind` to the NUMA node of the requesting CPU. PPR/HITS hot loops stay node-local. Falls back transparently on non-NUMA hosts.
5. **per-agent-context-profile** (swarmx.5): durable per-`agent_name` table of `(memory_id, outcome_signal)` feedback weights; capped (≤0.05) contribution to retrieval score so a misbehaving agent cannot dominate. After ~50 outcomes the agent's packs are measurably more relevant; degrades gracefully when feedback is sparse.

## Next 10 (P2 children, filed after the top 5 land)

6. wal-group-commit, 7. adaptive-pack-budget, 8. zstd-pack-dict, 9. tiered-hot-warm-cold-storage, 10. bloom-precheck, 11. rcu-read-snapshots, 12. arena-pack-assembly, 13. hash-cons-memory, 14. crossagent-key-singleflight (subsumed by swarmx.2 if scope merges), 15. pack-dna-pipelined.

## Dependency edges (proposed)

- swarmx.4 (NUMA) is a prerequisite for swarmx.11 (RCU) — both touch the read path.
- swarmx.1 (stream-pack) enables swarmx.7 (adaptive-pack-budget) because streaming exposes "first usable item" latency for the classifier to optimize.
- swarmx.2 (xagent-pack-singleflight) ↔ swarmx.14 (crossagent-key) — merge if scope overlaps.

## Tests/acceptance pattern (shared across all children)

Every swarmx.* child must include:

- Unit tests: pure-function pieces (cache eviction policy, NUMA hint resolver, classifier scoring) covered with `#[cfg(test)]` modules.
- Integration: real DB + index + graph snapshot, multi-thread/multi-agent harness.
- e2e: `scripts/e2e_overhaul/sx_<name>.sh` driving the surface end-to-end with structured tracing fields per `docs/observability/tracing_field_convention.md`.
- Bench: criterion group in `benches/sx_<name>.rs` with a baseline pinned in `benches/baselines/swarmx-v0.1.json`.
- Determinism: extend `tests/cross_platform_determinism.rs` (bd-3usjw.25) with hash rows for any new algorithm output.
- Failure-mode fixture: `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/swarmx_<name>_*.json` per degraded code.
- Backward compat: each new flag is additive; legacy invocation byte-identical to today's output.

## How this epic relates to existing beads

- Cooperates with `bd-oja31` (SRR1: ee daemon --hot-mode RAM-pinned ANN) — swarmx.4 NUMA mmap is the graph-side counterpart to oja31's ANN side.
- Subsumes parts of `bd-1zb7k.17.3` (IW3: Context hotset prewarm) → swarmx.3 is the same concept with concrete budgets.
- Complements `bd-2seqp` (MVCC fork-on-context-pack) and `bd-2lsxf` (SRR3: wait-free MPSC + WAL group commit). swarmx.6 may be a duplicate of bd-2lsxf — merge if so.

This epic is OPEN, not in_progress. Children stay deferred until idea-wizard Phase 6 review confirms scope and dependencies.

— StormyCove, idea-wizard pass 2026-05-15

title: EE-SCHEMA-DRIFT-001: Add unified schema-drift detection test for DB DDL, JSON contracts, manifests, and JSONL headers
description:
Add a schema-drift detection test that fails CI when DB schema, JSON output contracts, or index manifest format diverge from their declared specifications.

Background:
The OPUS plan §27.7 explicitly names tests/schema_drift.rs as a required gate: "regenerates DDL from #[derive(Model)] and diffs; must pass CI before merging." The bead set has EE-265 (invalid-version tests for JSON contracts), EE-266 (legacy import boundary), EE-267 (index manifest schema and validation), EE-268 (graph snapshot version validation), and EE-TST-003 (golden/schema contract runner). These cover individual contracts at point-of-use, but they do not collectively guarantee that the FULL set of schemas in the build can never silently drift.

A schema-drift test is the single CI gate that reads every declared schema (DB tables, public JSON envelopes, index manifests, jsonl headers, audit log entries, support bundle layout, configuration), regenerates them from source-of-truth definitions, and asserts byte-stability against committed fixtures. A drifted schema is either intentional (and the contributor updates the fixture in the same PR) or accidental (and CI catches it). Without this test, a single innocent attribute reordering can break every downstream consumer overnight.

Intended scope:
This bead owns the unified schema-drift test, the fixture layout under tests/contracts/schemas/, and the CI gate. It does not duplicate the per-feature golden tests; it composes them into a single drift-detection surface.

Public surface (test-only):
- tests/contracts/schema_drift.rs walks the registered schemas, serialises canonical examples for each, and diffs against tests/contracts/schemas/<name>.<version>.json.
- A small CLI helper `cargo xtask schema-drift --update` regenerates fixtures intentionally; it never runs in CI.
- ee schema list --json (already in the bead set as EE-032) is the runtime mirror; the test asserts the runtime listing matches the committed fixtures.

Why this matters:
Schema drift is the single failure mode that hurts every downstream consumer (agents, MCP clients, CI pipelines that parse JSON, future migration tooling). Catching it in a one-line CI assertion costs nothing; missing it costs every consumer a silent break.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including the unified schema registry, drift fixtures, runtime schema-list parity, xtask update helper, negative tests, property tests, CI gate, and e2e logging requirements.
design:
Recommended design:
- Use a single registry pattern: every schema crate exports a SCHEMAS slice ([Schema { name, version, example_factory }]) and the drift test iterates the slice. Adding a new schema means adding one slice entry and one fixture file; nothing more.
- Canonicalise JSON via serde_json::to_string with a stable key sort and consistent number formatting; no third-party canonicalizer is needed for v1.
- DB DDL snapshots come from the SQLModel migration registry. Avoid running the migration runner during the test; use the in-memory DDL emitter instead.
- The test must not require a network or a real cass binary. It must run in CI with no external dependencies.
- The xtask helper is a thin Rust binary in xtasks/ that imports the same registry. It writes fixture files atomically.
- Compose with EE-TST-003 (golden/schema contract runner) by sharing the canonicalization helpers and the fixture path conventions; do not duplicate the diff renderer.
- Compose with EE-TST-001 (testing strategy) by being included in the default `cargo test` set and the CI artifact policy.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance criteria:
- The test source lives at tests/contracts/schema_drift.rs and is wired into the default `cargo test` set; it does not require any feature flag to run.
- The test enumerates every registered schema and asserts byte-stability against a committed fixture under tests/contracts/schemas/<name>.<version>.json. Coverage includes at minimum: DB DDL (all tables), every public JSON envelope (`ee.response.v1`, `ee.error.v1`, `ee.memory.v1`, `ee.search.v1`, `ee.context.v1`, `ee.status.v1`, `ee.why.v1`, `ee.workspace.identity.v1`), the index manifest, the graph snapshot manifest, the support bundle manifest, the jsonl header for memory.jsonl exports, and the audit log entry shape.
- A failing drift produces a readable diff (line-level) plus the exact `cargo xtask schema-drift --update` invocation a contributor must run to regenerate the fixture intentionally.
- `cargo xtask schema-drift --update` regenerates only the fixtures the contributor explicitly names; bare `--update` requires explicit confirmation and writes a one-line audit comment in the PR description template.
- The test asserts that every schema name has a matching version field; a schema without a version, or with a duplicate version, is a hard failure.
- The runtime command `ee schema list --json` is asserted to exactly match the committed fixture set: every runtime schema has a fixture, and every fixture has a runtime schema. No silent drift between the test fixtures and the runtime.

Testing and logging requirements:
- The drift test itself runs in under 200ms on the standard CI runner; budget is enforced with a tracing assertion.
- Negative tests prove that adding a field to any schema without updating the fixture fails CI; reordering fields fails CI; renaming a field fails CI; bumping a version fails CI unless the new fixture is added.
- A property test asserts that for every schema, canonical_json(deserialize(canonical_json(example))) == canonical_json(example) (round-trip byte stability).
- Adversarial: a fixture file that has been hand-edited to be invalid JSON fails the test with a parse error rather than a misleading drift diff; a fixture file that is missing fails with the exact regeneration command.
- E2E logs capture the schema name, fixture path, runtime path, diff summary, and the next-action command. Logs go to stderr; the diff itself goes to a per-schema log artifact.
- Closeout evidence cites the schema list, the fixture directory, and the CI workflow file that wires the test in.
notes: Closes Plan §27.7 named test (tests/schema_drift.rs). Catches a class of regressions (silent JSON contract drift) that single-feature golden tests cannot prevent because they only run when their feature is touched. Composes with EE-TST-003 rather than duplicating it.

title: [CRITICAL] policy: file permission check uses numeric comparison instead of bitmask
description:
In src/policy/security_profile.rs lines 303 and 348, file permission checks use:

```rust
if mode <= max_mode {
```

This is WRONG. Permission bits are not comparable numerically for security.

Example: max_mode=0o600 (owner rw), actual=0o044 (group r, other r)
- 0o044 = 36 decimal
- 0o600 = 384 decimal  
- 36 <= 384 is TRUE, but 0o044 grants group+other read access!

The correct check is: `(mode & !max_mode) == 0`

This ensures no permission bits are set that aren't in the allowed mask.
close_reason: Fixed: replaced numeric comparison (mode <= max_mode) with bitmask check ((mode & !max_mode) == 0) in both file and directory permission checks. This correctly catches modes that grant unauthorized group/other access.

title: [pack-replay] Persist deterministic context pack selection ledgers
description:
Implement the durable replay ledger defined by the ADR/contract. This is not a new source of truth for memories; it is an audit artifact that records the exact safe inputs and derived-generation references needed to explain a previously emitted pack.

Scope:
- Extend pack persistence so ee context and ee pack can record a schema-versioned selection ledger.
- Capture query text or query-file digest, workspace id, profile, token budget, candidate pool, generation ids, selected memory ids, score components, why strings, redaction classes applied, and derived asset manifests where applicable.
- Redact or hash any user content that policy says cannot be stored in support artifacts.
- Preserve deterministic ordering and stable JSON field names.
- Keep write paths explicit and auditable; no silent mutation or background daemon requirement.

Acceptance criteria:

title: [perf-forensics][adr] Define read-only regression compare contract
description:
## Background

Differential perf forensics cuts across benchmark reports, support bundles, profile evidence, cache/write queue reports, and explain-performance artifacts. It needs an ADR before implementation so future agents do not accidentally build a profiler daemon, benchmark replacement, scheduler, or custom metrics stack.

## Scope

Write an ADR under `docs/adr/` defining the read-only regression-compare contract. The ADR must state accepted inputs, normalized evidence boundaries, output invariants, redaction rules, degraded states, subsystem owner taxonomy, and rejected alternatives.

## Acceptance criteria

- ADR explicitly references fcq1 and k8dp as inputs/foundations rather than duplicated work.
- ADR defines artifact classes: benchmark report, support-bundle manifest, explain-performance report, profile evidence, cache report, write queue report, and swarm contention report.
- ADR states that compare/check commands are read-only and stdout remains stable JSON.
- ADR defines stable degradation behavior for missing metrics, mismatched profiles, stale schema versions, tampered hashes, unsupported artifact kinds, and redaction uncertainty.
- ADR includes verification hooks mapped to child beads for schema, compare core, CLI, golden, E2E, support integration, docs, forbidden dependencies, and RCH usage.
- `bv --robot-insights` reports no dependency cycles after this bead is added.

## Testing and logging

Docs-only bead: no Cargo test is required unless implementation code changes. Closure evidence must include the exact ADR path, a short overlap check against existing fcq1/k8dp docs, and the `bv --robot-insights` cycle result.
close_reason: Completed docs-only ADR at docs/adr/0024-read-only-performance-regression-forensics.md. Overlap check: ADR references ADR 0017/eidetic_engine_cli-fcq1 and ADR 0023/eidetic_engine_cli-k8dp as foundations, and defines only the read-only compare contract rather than duplicating collection/profile work. Verification: git diff --check -- docs/adr/0024-read-only-performance-regression-forensics.md passed; bv --robot-insights reported cycle_count 0 / no cycles detected. No Cargo verification required because this bead only adds documentation.

title: SRR6.37: Peer duplicate, near-duplicate, and contradiction surfacing
description:
Implement contradiction, duplicate, and near-duplicate surfacing for peer-origin memories. Distributed memory will contain overlapping memories, different wording for the same lesson, and sometimes directly conflicting claims. `ee` should make these visible with provenance instead of flattening them into one answer.

Scope includes: content-hash exact dedupe; near-duplicate candidate links; contradiction/supersession candidate links; trust- and recency-aware context rendering; `why` explanations that show local vs peer disagreement; and learn/curate behavior that can use repeated peer evidence without blindly promoting consensus. The first version can be conservative and deterministic; no LLM arbitration is required.

Acceptance: unit tests for exact dedupe, near-duplicate stable ordering, and contradiction candidate scoring; e2e script with two peers asserting conflicting rules and a context pack that surfaces both with provenance rather than silently choosing one; structured logs for duplicate_detected, contradiction_candidate, selected_with_conflict, and promotion_blocked_by_conflict.

comments.author: DustyOtter
comments.text: Third polish finding: convergence is not the same as agreement. This bead makes peer disagreement explicit so the memory graph helps users reason instead of hiding conflict behind ranking.

Cargo.toml does NOT depend on tiktoken-rs. Verified:
- `grep -n tiktoken Cargo.toml` → no match
- `grep -n tiktoken Cargo.lock` → no match
- The only mention in src/ is a doc comment at `src/core/budget.rs:267`: 'Token count (e.g. tiktoken units)'

## Why it matters
1. Budget contract drifts from real LLM context windows. CJK content tokenizes at ~1 token/char in cl100k, but the heuristic estimates ~1 token / 3.5 chars → undercounts by ~3.5x for CJK-heavy memories. JSON/code with many short tokens also miscount.
2. `pack.budget.usedTokens` field in JSON output is reported as authoritative but is actually a heuristic.
3. AGENTS.md and the comprehensive plan should not list tiktoken-rs as a key dep if the project ships a heuristic.

## Repro
```bash
grep -rn tiktoken src/ Cargo.toml Cargo.lock
# Only finds: src/core/budget.rs:267 (a comment)
```

## Fix options
A) Add real tiktoken-rs and use `cl100k_base` for counting (matches AGENTS.md claim).
B) Remove tiktoken-rs from AGENTS.md and the plan; add an explicit ADR documenting the heuristic's bias bands and rename `max_tokens` → `max_estimated_tokens` in the JSON contract for honesty.

(Option B is cheaper and consistent with the no-Tokio franken-stack ethos, but requires updating AGENTS.md and adding an ADR.)

Added tiktoken-rs 0.11.0 (default-features off; the async-openai feature would have pulled tokio/reqwest/hyper which are forbidden) — confirmed clean by scripts/check-forbidden-deps.sh and tests/forbidden_deps.rs. Added TokenEstimationStrategy::TiktokenCl100kBase variant, made it the default; CharacterHeuristic and WordHeuristic kept as explicit fallbacks with documented bias bands. Lazy-initialized OnceLock<Option<CoreBPE>> cache; init failure logs via tracing::error and falls back to CharacterHeuristic so a corrupt build artifact never panics inside a budget calculation. Updated src/output/mod.rs::estimate_tokens to route through pack::estimate_tokens_default so JSON-vs-TOON size diagnostics quote the same numbers an ee context budget would see. Tests: token_estimation_strategy_strings_are_stable updated for 3 variants + new default; estimate_tokens_default_uses_tiktoken_cl100k_base; new estimate_tokens_tiktoken_matches_known_short_strings (hello world = 2 cl100k tokens, 'a' = 1, empty = 0, whitespace trims to 0); new estimate_tokens_tiktoken_is_more_accurate_than_heuristic_for_cjk (proves CJK undercount fix from the bug repro); new estimate_tokens_tiktoken_is_deterministic. title: [HIGH] hooks: installer follows hook-path symlinks and can overwrite arbitrary targets
description: src/hooks/installer.rs:174-188 classifies existing hooks with path.exists()/read_to_string(), and src/hooks/installer.rs:294-324 writes/chmods target_path with std::fs::write/metadata/set_permissions. title: [PERF] pack::assemble_mmr_draft: repeated similarity tokenization makes packing quadratic
description:
Path: ee context -> src/core/context.rs:400 assemble_draft_with_profile -> src/pack/mod.rs:1462 assemble_mmr_draft.
Code evidence: src/pack/mod.rs:1483 loops until candidates are exhausted, src/pack/mod.rs:1484 scans all remaining candidates, src/pack/mod.rs:1751 calls max_selected_similarity, src/pack/mod.rs:1762 scans all selected signatures, and src/pack/mod.rs:1898/1913 rebuild BTreeSet term sets from strings during each similarity check. src/pack/mod.rs:1495 also recomputes section_used by scanning selected items each iteration.
Suspected complexity: O(n^2 * terms) CPU/allocation on the default balanced/thorough context path, plus extra O(n*selected) section scans.
Suggested fix: precompute normalized terms and section token totals in CandidateSignature or an internal packing work item; maintain per-section used counters; avoid Vec::remove shifting where possible.
Verification plan: add a pack benchmark for 64/100/500 candidates with synthetic overlapping content, compare allocation count and p95 for `ee context "fix failing release workflow" --workspace . --max-tokens 4000 --json` before/after.

title: Gate 16: Prospective Preflight And Tripwire Readiness
description:
Readiness gate from the comprehensive EE plan.

Gate text and intent:
This gate is required before EE claims it can warn agents before likely repeated mistakes.

Create preflight and tripwire contract tests:

```text
tests/contracts/preflight_tripwires.rs
tests/golden/preflight/release_task.json
tests/golden/preflight/degraded_evidence.json
tests/golden/preflight/false_alarm_close.json
tests/golden/tripwire/list.json
tests/golden/tripwire/check_match.json
tests/golden/tripwire/check_no_match.json
```

Pass criteria:

- `ee preflight "<task>" --json` emits a compact risk brief with top risks, ask-now prompts, must-verify checks, tripwires, evidence IDs, and next action
- preflight can run before a context pack exists
- high-severity tripwires survive ordinary field projection and token budgets
- `ee tripwire check --json` is read-only and deterministic over a fixed event payload
- stale or missing evidence is reported with `preflight_evidence_stale` or `tripwire_inputs_incomplete`
- closing a preflight records helped, missed, stale, and false-alarm outcomes without deleting evidence
- repeated false alarms can lower future priority while preserving high-severity safety rules
- preflight output never claims that a warning will prevent failure; it only reports risk, evidence, and recommended checks
- all preflight and tripwire outputs validate against exported schemas and preserve stdout/stderr isolation

Why this matters:
Gates prevent roadmap gravity from turning aspirational features into unverified claims. Closing this bead means the implementation has executable evidence, not just code that compiles.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including the comprehensive testing and logging requirements.
design: Implement or verify the exact tests, fixtures, schemas, and acceptance criteria named in the gate text. If the gate cannot pass because an upstream dependency is not ready, record an explicit br comment with the blocker and degraded/deferred posture.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

The gate-specific contract/golden/evaluation tests pass; stdout/stderr and schema behavior are verified where relevant; any claimed feature has evidence linked in comments or the close reason.

Testing and logging requirements:
- Add or update unit tests for core logic introduced or changed by this bead, covering happy path, boundary/empty inputs, invalid inputs, degraded dependencies, deterministic ordering, and idempotency/mutation rules as applicable.
- If the behavior is visible through the CLI, MCP, hook, export, renderer, or evaluation output, add or extend a real-binary e2e, golden, schema, contract, replay, or evaluation fixture that exercises the public surface in an isolated local workspace.
- E2E/logged tests must capture command, cwd/workspace, sanitized environment overrides, elapsed time, exit code, stdout/stderr artifact paths, schema/golden validation status, redaction status, and a concise first-failure diagnosis.

title: IdeaWizard: code-symbol memory graph for precise agent context
description:
## Idea-wizard phase notes

Phase 1 grounding: AGENTS.md/README define ee as a local-first durable memory substrate for coding agents, with deterministic JSON, provenance, explainable retrieval, graph analytics, and harness-agnostic CLI surfaces. Live Beads scan on 2026-05-16 showed existing tracks for RCH-clean verification, workspace hygiene, read pools, L2 pack cache, single-flight, flight recorder/replay, completion audit, PPR, graph accretion, mesh sharing, and swarm QoS. Search/rg found no first-class track for code-symbol-aware memory.

Phase 2 30-to-5 winnow: considered symbol-aware memory, editor/LSP hooks, changed-symbol context boosts, owner/risk heatmaps, symbol-level failure recurrence, AST-aware redaction, diff-aware pack delta, code-review pack mode, public API drift detection, test-to-symbol impact maps, and symbol privacy policy. Best five were: (1) stable symbol identity layer, (2) memory-to-symbol provenance links, (3) changed-symbol context boosting, (4) symbol risk/ownership summaries for workspace hygiene and handoff, and (5) symbol-aware tests/goldens.

Phase 3 next ten folded in: multi-language adapter boundary, Rust-first extractor, rename-tolerant symbol fingerprints, no-daemon one-shot indexing, degraded codes for unavailable symbol extraction, source-map privacy controls, pack reasons mentioning symbols, why output showing symbol evidence, import from CASS file/line spans, and performance budgets for large repos.

Phase 4 overlap check: existing beads cover file-level hygiene, graph algorithms, PPR, verification reuse, flight recording, and swarm QoS, but not function/type/module identity as a durable graph node. This epic should integrate with those tracks instead of duplicating them.

## Goal

Add a code-symbol layer so ee can connect memories, failures, decisions, tests, and context-pack selections to stable functions, types, modules, CLI commands, and schema surfaces. The user-facing payoff is that agents can ask for context about a failing function or changed API and get precise historical evidence instead of whole-file or whole-session recall.

## Non-goals

No IDE daemon requirement, no mandatory external LSP server, no cloud indexing, no replacement for Frankensearch, no custom graph algorithm, no unsafe code, and no broad multi-language implementation before the Rust-first slice proves the contract.

## Acceptance

- Stable machine-readable symbol records exist with provenance, deterministic IDs, and rename-tolerant fingerprints.
- Memories/search/context/why can expose symbol evidence without leaking secret content.
- Changed-symbol context boosting is deterministic and explainable.
- Workspace hygiene and handoff can include compact symbol-risk summaries.
- Unit, contract, golden, and e2e tests cover extraction, linking, degraded cases, and pack/why output.
- All Rust verification is RCH-only.

## Phase 6 refinement notes

Keep the first implementation Rust-first and read-only. Do not create a background watcher or editor integration until one-shot CLI behavior is stable. Treat indexes as derived assets; FrankenSQLite/SQLModel remain truth. Use existing graph/search abstractions and add schema/degraded-code fixtures whenever new machine-facing fields appear.

title: symbol-graph: stable Rust symbol extractor and schema
description:
## Scope

Implement the first derived symbol snapshot for Rust source: modules, functions, methods, structs/enums/traits, impl blocks, CLI command handler surfaces, and JSON schema constants where they can be detected deterministically.

Required behavior:
- Produce stable symbol IDs from workspace-relative path, namespace, symbol kind, canonical name, and a rename-tolerant fingerprint.
- Record source ranges and content hashes without storing secret-bearing source bodies.
- Keep extraction read-only and one-shot; no daemon watcher.
- Degrade cleanly when source files are missing, non-regular, too large, or unparsable.
- Use structured parsing where practical; avoid brittle regex as the semantic authority.

Tests:
- Unit fixtures for modules, free functions, methods, nested modules, traits, impls, macros-as-opaque, and invalid Rust.
- Golden symbol snapshot JSON with deterministic ordering.
- RCH-only cargo test for the extractor tests.

title: HIGH: migrations can partially apply without ee_schema_migrations records
description:
Reviewer finding in src/db/.

Evidence:
- src/db/mod.rs:189-218 already exposes transaction helpers.
- src/db/mod.rs:2263-2282 migrate applies migration.sql with execute_raw_for and only then inserts the ee_schema_migrations record.
- There is no transaction covering the DDL plus record_migration step.

Impact:
A crash, interruption, or storage error after DDL succeeds but before record_migration succeeds leaves the schema mutated but unrecorded. The next migrate run will try to replay the same CREATE/ALTER statements; any non-idempotent DDL can fail and leave the DB stuck even though the desired tables/columns may already exist.

Suggested fix:
Run each migration SQL and its ee_schema_migrations insert in one transaction, preferably BEGIN IMMEDIATE for file-backed databases. Add a failure-injection test that forces record_migration to fail and verifies migrate can be retried without schema drift.
close_reason: Wrapped each migration SQL and ee_schema_migrations insert in one transaction, with rollback/retry test coverage.

title: DEADLOCK: index publish path lacks cross-process advisory lock
description: Phase 4 concurrency audit finding. src/core/index.rs:526-615, 725-741, and 939-944 run build_index_sync() through the current-thread asupersync bridge and then call recover_interrupted_publish()/publish_staged_index() without acquiring the DB advisory index lock. src/db/mod.rs defines AdvisoryLockId::index and atomic advisory lock primitives, but rg shows no production callers. Concurrent ee index rebuild/reembed/process runs can interleave rename(index -> retained) and rename(staging -> index), leaving a visible no-active-index window for search/status and letting last-writer-wins publish over a freshly published generation. Expected fix: use the advisory index lock around recovery + staging publish or an equivalent filesystem lock, and add a file-backed concurrent rebuild/search regression test.
close_reason: Fixed: wrapped index publish paths in advisory lock acquisition to prevent concurrent publish races

title: [lockfile] Audit and normalize Cargo.lock churn from local path patches
description:
Background: the working tree currently shows an unstaged Cargo.lock diff unrelated to the pack bug fix. The diff appears to remove registry source/checksum entries for path-patched Franken crates and add transitive dependency churn such as ring/nkeys/prost updates. In this repository, accidental lockfile churn can hide forbidden dependency regressions or make release provenance unclear.

Scope:
- Determine whether the current Cargo.lock diff is intentional dependency resolution, stale local churn, or the result of a separate in-progress certificate/signing change.
- Do not discard or rewrite Cargo.lock blindly. If reverting is needed, ask for explicit user approval or make a forward correction that is justified by Cargo.toml and path-patch state.
- Run cargo tree -e features and the forbidden dependency audit after any lockfile normalization.
- Document which package changes are expected and why.

Acceptance:

- Forbidden dependency audit passes and explicitly checks tokio, tokio-util, async-std, smol, rusqlite, sqlx, diesel, sea-orm, petgraph, hyper, axum, tower, and reqwest.
- The close reason includes a before/after lockfile summary and states whether any dependency versions changed.

title: [CONCURRENCY-TEST] cass import: sequential ledger smoke test misses concurrent lost update
description:
Files: tests/smoke.rs:2910, tests/smoke.rs:3019, src/cass/import.rs:766, src/cass/import.rs:814.
Code path: the existing smoke coverage runs a first import, closes the connection, then runs a second import and checks attempt_count == 2 plus preserved imported totals. That verifies sequential resumption but cannot catch the concurrent read-modify-write interleaving in ensure_running_ledger and complete_ledger.

title: EE-011: Add capability-narrowed command context wrapper
description:
Source plan item: EE-011 from the `Foundation` backlog.

Task: Add capability-narrowed command context wrapper

Background and intent:
Establish the Rust workspace, core crate boundaries, runtime shell, error model, and test harness that every later subsystem depends on. This is the delivery foundation: no feature work should bypass these invariants.

Why this matters:
This bead contributes to the overarching goal of making `ee` a dependable local memory substrate for coding agents: useful before work, auditable after work, and safe under degraded conditions. The work should be implemented in the smallest coherent slice that fully satisfies the public contract implied by the title.

Dependency context:
Original plan dependencies: EE-004. These are also represented as br dependency edges where the referenced bead exists.

Non-negotiable constraints:
Global implementation invariants for this task:
- Keep the CLI local-first, deterministic, and agent-native; stdout is data, stderr is diagnostics.
- Preserve the no-Tokio and no-rusqlite constraint unless a later ADR explicitly changes the architecture.
- Use SQLModel Rust plus FrankenSQLite for durable data; do not introduce a second storage stack.
- Use Asupersync for async edges and cancellation/budget behavior; do not smuggle in a Tokio executor.
- Keep JSON as the canonical public contract. TOON, Markdown, diagrams, and MCP are renderers or adapters over the same domain data.
- Mutating commands need dry-run/idempotency/audit behavior unless the task explicitly says otherwise.
- Add focused tests proportional to risk: unit tests for domain logic, contract/golden tests for public output, and integration/evaluation tests for cross-subsystem behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including the comprehensive testing and logging requirements.
design:
Suggested design approach:
- Command output must use the stable `ee.response.v1` envelope, preserve stdout/stderr isolation, and provide useful degraded-state metadata.
- Runtime boundaries must preserve `Outcome`, request budgets, capability narrowing, and cancellation semantics through Asupersync rather than Tokio.

Implementation guidance:
- Read the surrounding modules and existing project conventions before editing.
- Prefer the planned crate boundaries from the comprehensive plan: CLI wiring in `ee-cli`, reusable domain/services in `ee-core`, models in `ee-models`, persistence in `ee-db`, output rendering in `ee-output`, and adapters in their own optional crates.
- Keep public contracts stable and versioned. Any data structure that leaves the process through CLI/MCP/hook/export should have a schema and at least one golden fixture.
- If a dependency or upstream Franken project is not ready, implement the smallest honest diagnostic/degraded path rather than faking behavior.
- Document any architectural exception with an ADR-oriented note and a verification hook.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance criteria:
- The behavior described by `Add capability-narrowed command context wrapper` is implemented or, for spikes, conclusively reported with a clear go/no-go recommendation.
- The implementation preserves local-first, no-Tokio, no-rusqlite, agent-native CLI behavior.
- Public command output, if any, validates against the stable response envelope and does not pollute stdout with diagnostics.
- Relevant unit, integration, golden, contract, or evaluation tests are added and named so future agents can find them.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the relevant test subset pass after implementation.
- Any degraded or unavailable dependency state returns a stable error/degradation code with a useful next action.
- No silent durable mutation is introduced; write paths have explicit audit, dry-run, idempotency, or curation behavior as appropriate.

Testing and logging requirements:
- Add or update unit tests for core logic introduced or changed by this bead, covering happy path, boundary/empty inputs, invalid inputs, degraded dependencies, deterministic ordering, and idempotency/mutation rules as applicable.
- If the behavior is visible through the CLI, MCP, hook, export, renderer, or evaluation output, add or extend a real-binary e2e, golden, schema, contract, replay, or evaluation fixture that exercises the public surface in an isolated local workspace.
- E2E/logged tests must capture command, cwd/workspace, sanitized environment overrides, elapsed time, exit code, stdout/stderr artifact paths, schema/golden validation status, redaction status, and a concise first-failure diagnosis.
- Stdout assertions must prove stdout contains only machine data; diagnostics, progress, and debugging context must go to stderr or explicit artifacts.
- If no executable test is appropriate for this bead, the close reason or a br comment must explain why and identify the nearest bead that provides coverage.

If this bead reveals that the original plan dependency was ambiguous or incomplete, add a br comment explaining the correction before implementation.

title: [HIGH] V031 migration version reused: learning_observations renumbered to V033 in 237dbe2 after 1ceba15 published it
description:
Repro:
  1. Check out commit 1ceba15 (`feat(learn): persist active learning observations`).
  2. Run any test that initializes a DbConnection, e.g. `cargo test --test recorder_persistence`. The DB applies V031_LEARNING_OBSERVATIONS and stores its blake3 hash in `ee_schema_migrations`.
  3. Pull commit 237dbe2 (`feat: wave-3 surface implementations`). V031 is now V031_CERTIFICATES_AND_TRUST_QUARANTINE; learning observations are renumbered to V033.
  4. Re-run any test against the same DB.

Expected: migrations apply cleanly OR the framework refuses with a clear "migration version reused" error.

Actual: the framework runs validate_applied_migrations on the existing rows and either (a) silently re-applies V031's certificates DDL on top of an already-V031'd DB, leaving learning_observations + certificates both at version 31 with mismatched hashes, or (b) panics on hash mismatch.

Evidence-line:
  src/db/mod.rs (HEAD) shows V031_CERTIFICATES_AND_TRUST_QUARANTINE at the slot previously occupied by V031_LEARNING_OBSERVATIONS (which is now V033). Compare:
    git show 1ceba15:src/db/mod.rs  | grep -n V031_LEARNING_OBSERVATIONS
    git show 237dbe2:src/db/mod.rs  | grep -n V031_CERTIFICATES_AND_TRUST_QUARANTINE

Impact: any developer or shared swarm DB that materialized an `.ee/ee.db` between 16:08 UTC and 16:15 UTC on 2026-05-06 cannot upgrade past V031 without a manual migration-table rewrite. Pre-1.0, but the swarm uses shared DBs.

Suggested fix: never reuse a version number after it has been committed. The wave-3 commit (237dbe2) should have appended certificates as V034+ and audit-hash-chain as V035+, leaving V031 as learning_observations forever.
close_reason: Fixed migration version collision by restoring V031 as LEARNING_OBSERVATIONS (original from 1ceba15) and renumbering CERTIFICATES to V032 and AUDIT_HASH_CHAIN to V033. All 17 migration tests pass.

title: SRR6.25: Formal model for anti-entropy, stale reads, and revision semantics
description:
Create a small formal/model-checking artifact for the anti-entropy and revision semantics before relying on network transport. The model should cover per-node append-only event streams, peer cursors, partition/rejoin, duplicate and out-of-order delivery, cursor advancement only after durable replay, and explicit revision availability after a stale Tier 1 result.

This does not need to prove every implementation detail. It must capture the invariants future implementers need: no silent overwrite, no lost accepted event, deterministic replay over a fixed event set, bounded-staleness semantics instead of linearizability, and no blocking of local Tier 1 reads.

Acceptance: TLA+/PlusCal, proptest model, or equivalent checked artifact documented in the ADR; counterexample fixtures if an invariant fails during design; unit tests derived from model scenarios; e2e script logs model scenario names alongside replay results; transport/background work must reference the model's assumptions.

title: [adr] Swarm-scale resource governance and cache/write contracts
description:
## Background
AGENTS.md requires an ADR before every major new subsystem. The swarm-scale roadmap cuts across cache policy, write-owner/backpressure, benchmark fixtures, support bundles, and performance explainability, so future implementers need one architectural decision record before code work starts.

## What ships
1. ADR in `docs/adr/` covering the swarm-scale resource-governance model.
2. Explicit boundaries: `ee` remains CLI-first and harness-agnostic; daemon improves heavy-swarm writes but is not required for ordinary reads or one-shot commands.
3. Cache contract: derived, generation-checked, redaction-safe, rebuildable, and bounded by explicit memory budgets.
4. Write contract: single-writer semantics, queued/batched writes only where auditability and idempotency are preserved, clear backpressure errors otherwise.
5. Verification hook list: scale fixtures, benchmark reports, e2e contention logs, no forbidden dependencies, and support-bundle artifacts.
6. Rejected alternatives: custom vector store, custom graph algorithms, central web service, harness scheduler, always-on daemon requirement.

## Tests and logging
This is a docs/design bead, but it must include acceptance hooks that map to concrete test beads in this epic. Future code beads should reference this ADR in their closure evidence.

## Closure evidence
Close only after the ADR is committed, links to the child beads are included, and `bv --robot-insights` still reports no dependency cycles.
