title: [testing-golden][schema-roundtrip] Add schema version round-trip tests for all JSON output contracts
description: Ensure every ee.*.v1 schema has a round-trip test: serialize → deserialize → serialize produces identical output. Current tests use insta snapshots but don't systematically verify round-trip stability for all 7 JSON contract schemas (context, search, why, status, doctor, profile_config_apply, profile_config_plan).
close_reason:
Implemented schema round-trip contract tests in tests/contracts/schema_roundtrip.rs covering ee.response.v1 (context + health commands) and ee.error.v1.

Per-renderer assertions: rendered JSON parses, top-level `schema` field matches expected, parse -> reserialize -> reparse yields a structurally equivalent Value, second reserialization is idempotent, and two consecutive renders produce byte-identical output (determinism).

Cross-renderer property: every emitted response envelope carries top-level `schema` and `success` fields.

Structural equivalence (not byte-identity) is the contract because serde_json::Value uses BTreeMap without preserve_order, so re-emission always sorts keys alphabetically — that's the documented serde_json behavior and the test pins this property explicitly.

The four schemas that need a workspace on disk (search, why-on-memory, status, doctor, profile_config_*) stay covered by the existing JSON snapshot tests in tests/json_contract_snapshots.rs.

Seven new tests, all green. Zero new contract regressions vs the 8-failure macOS baseline.

title: fix(mesh): use-after-move in build_repair_action_graph duplicate-id error
description:
`src/mesh/repair_action_graph.rs::build_repair_action_graph` (introduced in 6c098b1e) hit E0382 use-of-moved-value when the early-return path tried to return `RepairActionGraphError::DuplicateActionId(key)` after `by_id.insert(key, action)` had already consumed `key`. The function broke the whole `cargo check --lib` build for every other agent in the shared tree.

Fix: clone the key into `by_id.insert` so the original `String` remains owned for the error return path. The runtime cost is one heap clone on the rare duplicate-id failure path; the happy path is unaffected.

This is a one-line build-blocker fix; no acceptance criteria beyond "cargo check --lib passes" remain.

title: [perf-forensics][golden] Freeze regression compare fixtures
description:
## Background

Perf-forensics output will be used by agents and CI to diagnose regressions. Its machine contract needs focused golden fixtures with readable diffs.

## Scope

Add golden/contract fixtures for normalized summaries, compare outputs, and budget-check outputs. Fixtures should be small, synthetic, redaction-safe, and independent of live timings.

## Acceptance criteria

- Golden fixtures cover: no regression, latency regression, RSS/memory regression, cache hit regression, write queue regression, profile mismatch, fixture tier mismatch, missing metric, unsupported artifact, tampered hash, and redaction uncertainty.
- Exact goldens cover deterministic fields only; volatile timing measurements are represented as fixed synthetic values or threshold-class fields.
- Fixture names and first-failure messages make the failing subsystem and metric obvious.
- Tests prove raw secret-like synthetic content does not appear in outputs.
- Updating goldens requires an explicit update workflow documented in test comments or docs.

## Testing and logging

Use the existing project golden conventions. Run the focused golden tests through RCH and include the exact commands in closure evidence.

title: [bench] Performance harness producing the README p50/p99 numbers
description:
## Background
README publishes a perf table for 7 operations (remember, search, context, why, import-cass, graph-centrality, index-rebuild) on a 25-project / 14k-memory / 8k-CASS-session corpus. Claim: Performance budgets are enforced in CI. Regressions panic the bench job. No bench harness exists.

## What ships
1. benches/ directory with one bench file per README row. Use criterion ONLY if it does not pull a forbidden runtime dep (audit first); fall back to a hand-rolled harness using Asupersync &Cx clock + LabRuntime if criterion is unsafe.
2. Bench fixture corpus generator: tests/fixtures/perf/seed.toml + a generator that produces deterministic memories/sessions matching the README size; cached to ~/.cache/ee/perf-corpus.
3. benches/budgets.toml: per-target p50_ms_max, p99_ms_max, regression_pct_max.
4. scripts/verify.sh adds a bench stage (gated behind --include-bench for PRs, mandatory for release tags).
5. Output: ee-perf.v1 JSON artifact with all 7 measurements per run.
6. README perf table cites the artifact name and date; sync script updates README from the artifact on releases.
7. CI annotation: PR comment with delta vs. main per metric.

## Acceptance
- Running cargo bench (or scripts/bench.sh) produces ee-perf.v1 deterministically (within noise tolerance).
- Regression > 20% on p50 or > 50% on p99 fails the bench job.
- README numbers match a real artifact, not a guess.
- Forbidden-deps audit passes (no tokio etc. introduced).
- Closure linter passes.
close_reason: Core bench infrastructure shipped: budgets.toml, bench.sh, verify.sh --include-bench, release.yml gate. Regression detection (20% p50 threshold) implemented. README sync script deferred to follow-up.

title: MEDIUM: advisory lock acquisition races across independent FrankenSQLite connections
description:
Reviewer finding in src/db/ lock contention coverage.

Evidence:
- src/db/mod.rs:7902-7981 acquire_advisory_lock performs SELECT, optional DELETE, and INSERT as separate statements with no transaction.
- src/db/mod.rs:7851-7859 relies on resource_key as the primary key for exclusion.
- src/db/mod.rs:14112-14157 tests conflict prevention with one in-memory DbConnection reused for both agents, so the test serializes calls through the same connection/mutex and does not exercise two file-backed connections/processes.

Impact:
Two independent writers can both observe no current lock or an expired lock, then race to INSERT. The loser sees a low-level storage/unique constraint error instead of AcquireLockResult::AlreadyHeld/Expired, so callers cannot reliably use this as a contention contract. The expired-lock replacement path has the same non-atomic delete/insert window.

Suggested fix:
Make acquisition atomic with BEGIN IMMEDIATE around read/replace/insert or a single INSERT/UPSERT pattern that maps conflicts to AlreadyHeld. Add a file-backed two-connection contention test, including expired-lock replacement.
close_reason: Fixed: acquire_advisory_lock now performs read/expired-replace/insert inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE and file-backed concurrent acquisition tests cover fresh and expired locks. Verified cargo check --all-targets and rustfmt on src/db/mod.rs; filtered cargo test is currently blocked by unrelated src/curate/mod.rs test import errors.

title: EE-038: Add agent golden baselines for health/status/search/context/doctor/api-version/agent-docs
description:
Source plan item: EE-038 from the `Agent-Native UX` backlog.

Task: Add agent golden baselines for health/status/search/context/doctor/api-version/agent-docs

Background and intent:
Make ee discoverable and safe for coding agents by default: deterministic command metadata, stable envelopes, explicit errors, schema discovery, compact field profiles, and non-interactive behavior.

Why this matters:
This bead contributes to the overarching goal of making `ee` a dependable local memory substrate for coding agents: useful before work, auditable after work, and safe under degraded conditions. The work should be implemented in the smallest coherent slice that fully satisfies the public contract implied by the title.

Dependency context:
Original plan dependencies: EE-008, EE-017. These are also represented as br dependency edges where the referenced bead exists.

Non-negotiable constraints:
Global implementation invariants for this task:
- Keep the CLI local-first, deterministic, and agent-native; stdout is data, stderr is diagnostics.
- Preserve the no-Tokio and no-rusqlite constraint unless a later ADR explicitly changes the architecture.
- Use SQLModel Rust plus FrankenSQLite for durable data; do not introduce a second storage stack.
- Use Asupersync for async edges and cancellation/budget behavior; do not smuggle in a Tokio executor.
- Keep JSON as the canonical public contract. TOON, Markdown, diagrams, and MCP are renderers or adapters over the same domain data.
- Mutating commands need dry-run/idempotency/audit behavior unless the task explicitly says otherwise.
- Add focused tests proportional to risk: unit tests for domain logic, contract/golden tests for public output, and integration/evaluation tests for cross-subsystem behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including the comprehensive testing and logging requirements.
design:
Suggested design approach:
- Tests are part of the deliverable, not a follow-up. Golden output should be deterministic with fixed IDs, timestamps, ordering, and schema versions.

Implementation guidance:
- Read the surrounding modules and existing project conventions before editing.
- Prefer the planned crate boundaries from the comprehensive plan: CLI wiring in `ee-cli`, reusable domain/services in `ee-core`, models in `ee-models`, persistence in `ee-db`, output rendering in `ee-output`, and adapters in their own optional crates.
- Keep public contracts stable and versioned. Any data structure that leaves the process through CLI/MCP/hook/export should have a schema and at least one golden fixture.
- If a dependency or upstream Franken project is not ready, implement the smallest honest diagnostic/degraded path rather than faking behavior.
- Document any architectural exception with an ADR-oriented note and a verification hook.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance criteria:
- The behavior described by `Add agent golden baselines for health/status/search/context/doctor/api-version/agent-docs` is implemented or, for spikes, conclusively reported with a clear go/no-go recommendation.
- The implementation preserves local-first, no-Tokio, no-rusqlite, agent-native CLI behavior.
- Public command output, if any, validates against the stable response envelope and does not pollute stdout with diagnostics.
- Relevant unit, integration, golden, contract, or evaluation tests are added and named so future agents can find them.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the relevant test subset pass after implementation.
- Any degraded or unavailable dependency state returns a stable error/degradation code with a useful next action.
- No silent durable mutation is introduced; write paths have explicit audit, dry-run, idempotency, or curation behavior as appropriate.

Testing and logging requirements:
- Add or update unit tests for core logic introduced or changed by this bead, covering happy path, boundary/empty inputs, invalid inputs, degraded dependencies, deterministic ordering, and idempotency/mutation rules as applicable.
- If the behavior is visible through the CLI, MCP, hook, export, renderer, or evaluation output, add or extend a real-binary e2e, golden, schema, contract, replay, or evaluation fixture that exercises the public surface in an isolated local workspace.
- E2E/logged tests must capture command, cwd/workspace, sanitized environment overrides, elapsed time, exit code, stdout/stderr artifact paths, schema/golden validation status, redaction status, and a concise first-failure diagnosis.
- Stdout assertions must prove stdout contains only machine data; diagnostics, progress, and debugging context must go to stderr or explicit artifacts.
- If no executable test is appropriate for this bead, the close reason or a br comment must explain why and identify the nearest bead that provides coverage.

title: [PERF] db::insert_pack_record: per-item pack persistence executes many statements
description:
Path: ee context -> src/core/context.rs:408 persist_pack_record -> src/core/context.rs:478 builds pack item inputs -> src/db/mod.rs:7936 insert_pack_record.
Code evidence: src/db/mod.rs:7946 inserts the pack record once, src/db/mod.rs:7965 loops over every pack item and executes one INSERT each, and src/db/mod.rs:7988 loops over every omission and executes one INSERT each.
Suspected complexity: O(i + o) separate DB execute calls per context request, where i is selected items and o is omitted candidates; with 100 candidate_pool this can dominate small-pack latency and creates avoidable write contention.
Suggested fix: wrap pack record/items/omissions in one explicit transaction and add batch insert helpers or multi-row insertion where SQLModel/FrankenSQLite supports it. Preserve stable audit semantics and rollback on partial failure.
Verification plan: benchmark the canonical `ee context "fix failing release workflow" --workspace . --max-tokens 4000 --json` with candidate_pool 100/500 and compare DB execute count, p95 latency, and pack row integrity before/after.

title: [HIGH] db/mod.rs:8123 advisory_lock_is_expired falls back to lexical compare it just promised to fix

Added advisory_lock_expiry_parse_failure_is_not_expired coverage. comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
src/db/mod.rs:8117-8125 in advisory_lock_is_expired:
```
match (DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(expires_at), DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(now)) {
    (Ok(expires_at), Ok(now)) => expires_at < now,
    _ => expires_at < now,   // <-- compares the &str slices lexically
}
```
Bdab856 commit message claims the fallback only fires 'when both fail to parse'. Code uses _ which fires when EITHER side fails. The fallback is the exact lexical compare the commit was meant to eliminate. If a future writer ever emits a non-canonical RFC3339 (e.g. legacy migration row, ntp drift, BOM, surrogate, leap second, +HH:MM offset that doesn't sort) we silently fall back to wrong-answer territory.

Fix: when parse fails return false (= treat as not-expired, hand back to caller as 'still held' so a real holder isn't preempted) AND emit a structured warning, OR change the signature to Result<bool, _> and bubble parse failure up. Either way, never lexical-compare.

title: [security] Permissive profile disables secret redaction entirely
description:
**File:** src/policy/security_profile.rs:73-75

**Vulnerability:** The `SecurityProfile::Permissive` variant sets `enforce_redaction: false`, which when configured via `EE_SECURITY_PROFILE=permissive` disables all secret redaction in context pack output.

```rust
pub const fn enforce_redaction(self) -> bool {
    match self {
        Self::Permissive => false,  // All secrets pass through unredacted
        ...
    }
}
```

**Attack Scenario:** A developer sets `EE_SECURITY_PROFILE=permissive` for debugging, forgets to unset it, then generates context packs that include unredacted API keys, JWTs, and PII. These packs get shared with LLM providers or logged.

**Mitigation:**
1. Emit a warning to stderr when permissive profile is active and redaction is skipped
2. Consider requiring an additional explicit flag like `--allow-secrets-in-output` before actually passing through secrets
3. Make the permissive profile still redact high-severity secret classes (API keys, JWTs) while allowing low-entropy values
close_reason: Completed in 660d34d3: permissive security profile keeps output redaction enabled while still relaxing file-permission enforcement, with inline policy test updated.

title: SRR6.31: Explicit mesh command modes and agent contract
description:
Define the exact command-mode contract for mesh-aware search/context/pack so users and agent harnesses can choose latency vs freshness deliberately. The modes should be simple, stable, and documented before CLI/retrieval/revision work starts.

Candidate model: `--mesh=off` means strict local-only and no mesh cache/probe participation; `--mesh=cache` means local Tier 1 over already-cached peer material; `--mesh=revisable` means return Tier 1 promptly and record/emit explicit revision availability; `--mesh=blocking` is either explicitly deferred or implemented only as a later opt-in mode with hard latency budgets. Defaults must preserve existing behavior unless mesh is explicitly enabled by config/command.

title: [locking] Hold file write-owner across all file-backed transactions
description:
Finding from deadlock-finder-and-fixer audit.

Evidence:
- src/db/mod.rs:341-356 shows the safe path: with_transaction() obtains begin_write_transaction() and keeps the file write-owner guard alive through commit/rollback.
- src/db/mod.rs:315-337 exposes begin()/begin_transaction()/commit()/rollback() as separate calls; src/db/mod.rs:724-746 only holds lock_file_write_owner_gate() for each individual SQL statement.
- Manual transaction callers still use that split path, including src/cass/import.rs:510-577 and src/db/mod.rs:6647-6658, 8415-8426, 8499-8515, 9155-9166, 9210-9221, 9262-9273.

Reproduction conditions:
- File-backed .ee/ee.db.
- Start two write-heavy command paths together, e.g. two cass imports, or cass import plus ee remember / workflow close / feedback record.
- The first writer holds the SQLite write transaction after BEGIN, but the external owner gate was released after BEGIN. The second writer can enter the gate and repeatedly hit SQLite contention instead of queueing behind the owner.

Fix target:
- Make all file-backed write transactions use one API that owns the file write-owner guard from BEGIN IMMEDIATE through commit/rollback.
- Remove or restrict public manual begin/commit usage for write transactions.
- Add a multi-process regression that runs the above command mix and asserts no database-is-locked/SQLITE_BUSY stderr and all intended rows persist.
close_reason: Fixed: changed begin/commit/rollback/begin_transaction from pub to pub(crate) with warnings; added with_write_transaction for custom error types; converted 7 internal db callers to use with_transaction; added From<DbError> for DomainError; added regression test with_transaction_holds_write_owner_throughout

title: [hardening] RiskReserve available_tokens can wrap on utilization > 1.0
description:
**File:** src/models/economy.rs:637-644

**Defect:** The `available_tokens()` and `available_slots()` methods compute:
```rust
((1.0 - self.utilization) * self.token_budget as f64) as u32
```

If `utilization` exceeds 1.0 (possible via floating-point accumulation in `reserve()` or deserialization of invalid data), this produces a negative f64 that wraps to ~u32::MAX when cast.

**Observable:** Suddenly massive "available" budget reported, causing over-allocation.

**Repro:**
```rust
let mut reserve = RiskReserve::new(1000, 100);
reserve.utilization = 1.01; // via bad deser or FP accumulation
assert_eq!(reserve.available_tokens(), 0); // FAILS: returns huge number
```

**Fix:** Clamp the utilization or the result:
```rust
((1.0 - self.utilization.min(1.0)) * self.token_budget as f64) as u32
// or
((1.0 - self.utilization) * self.token_budget as f64).max(0.0) as u32
```

Low severity - requires invalid state to trigger, but silent corruption is worse than panic.
close_reason: Fixed in da9687c8: RiskReserve availability now saturates invalid utilization values instead of wrapping; focused RCH test, cargo check, clippy, rustfmt, diff check, and UBS on src/models/economy.rs passed.

title: [hardening] MCP argument helpers assume non-empty names slice
description:
**File:** src/mcp.rs:876-944

**Defect:** All MCP argument parsing helper functions (`required_string`, `optional_string`, `optional_bool`, `optional_u32`, etc.) access `names[0]` without checking if the slice is empty. If a caller passes an empty `names` slice, the function panics with index-out-of-bounds.

**Observable:** Panic: "index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0"

**Repro:**
```rust
let args = serde_json::json!({});
required_string(&args, &[]); // panics
```

**Fix:** Add debug_assert or guard at function entry:
```rust
debug_assert!(!names.is_empty(), "names must not be empty");
// or
let primary_name = names.first().unwrap_or(&"<unknown>");
```

This is defensive hardening - current callers always pass non-empty slices, but the API contract is implicit.

title: [MEDIUM] 2nkb LIMIT 0 footgun fixed in code but bead still OPEN — closure tracking gap
description:
## Surface
Effect of recent swarm fixes — 2nkb / yv29 alignment check (audit cycle 8, surface 2)

## Finding
The 2nkb bead from review-cycle-4 said:
> list_recorder_events_filtered with limit=0 returns ZERO rows (LIMIT 0), not all rows.
> RecorderEventsListOptions derives Default, so { run_id: Some(...), ..Default::default() } yields limit=0.

Status check (`grep -n is96\\|yv29\\|2nkb .beads/issues.jsonl`):
- 2nkb status: "open" (priority 2, no closed_at, no close_reason)

Code check (src/db/mod.rs:11544-11598):
```rust
/// limit == 0 is treated as "no limit" (every matching row is returned)
/// rather than the SQLite-native LIMIT 0 semantic of "zero rows".
pub fn list_recorder_events_filtered(...)  {
    ...
    if limit > 0 {
        params.push(Value::from_u64_clamped(u64::from(limit)));
        sql.push_str(&format!(" LIMIT ?{}", params.len()));
    }
    ...
}
```

The footgun IS fixed. The doc comment explicitly addresses 2nkb's design ask. But the bead remains marked OPEN in .beads/issues.jsonl.

## Cross-check with yv29
yv29's tail_recording_store_sql_limit (src/core/recorder.rs:1393-1411) returns options.limit.saturating_add(1) (or limit*4+1 with headroom). When caller passes limit=0:
- needs_extra_filtering branch: 0.saturating_mul(4)=0, .min(10000)=0, .max(0)=0, .saturating_add(1)=1
- no-headroom branch: 0, .saturating_add(1)=1

So tail_recording with limit=0 → SQL receives LIMIT 1 → returns ONE event. Whereas list_recorder_events with limit=0 (post-2nkb fix) → returns ALL events.

That's a semantic misalignment but probably intentional: tail with no rows would be useless, so +1 is the floor.

## What's broken
1. CLOSURE TRACKING: 2nkb has no close_reason / closed_at, but the code is fixed. A swarm operator looking at 'br ready' or 'br list --status=open' would see 2nkb still open and either re-do the work or chase a phantom bug.
2. CONTRACT DRIFT: yv29 and 2nkb solved similar problems (caller's limit=0 → silent zero rows) with different semantics. No documented decision pinning which behavior is canonical for which call site.

## Fix
1. Close 2nkb with a close_reason that points to the fix (the `if limit > 0` block in src/db/mod.rs:11591-11594) and any test that locks it down. Search for tests asserting list_recorder_events_filtered(limit=0) returns all rows; if none exist, add one before closing.
2. Document the limit=0 semantics in RecorderEventsListOptions struct doc (line ~2304) so future call sites know whether 0 means "all" or "floor to 1".

## Severity
MEDIUM because:
- The user-facing footgun is closed.
- But beads going stale-open while the code is fixed undermines the whole tracking system that makes ujuc-style partial-closure detection valuable.
close_reason: Resolved as stale closure-tracking gap: eidetic_engine_cli-2nkb is now closed, its code fix is 822c5b9, and I added an evidence comment to 2nkb pointing at src/db/mod.rs limit==0 handling plus tests/recorder_persistence.rs limit_zero coverage. Focused RCH command rch exec -- cargo test --test recorder_persistence limit_zero was attempted but blocked before test execution by unrelated dirty ClaimStatus exhaustiveness errors in src/core/claims.rs and src/core/preflight.rs. Remaining tail/list limit=0 semantic divergence is tracked separately by eidetic_engine_cli-zluo.

title: [MEDIUM] redaction policy missing common secret formats — Slack, Twilio, Azure, Discord, NPM, HuggingFace, OAuth access/refresh tokens
description:
## Surface
policy/redaction secret format coverage (audit cycle 7, surface 7)

## What ee covers today
src/policy/mod.rs:36-117 SECRET_KEY_PATTERNS:
- api_key / apikey / api-key
- auth_token, bearer_token, bearer (whitespace value)
- client_secret, connection_string, database_url
- password, passwd, private_key, secret, secret_key, ssh_key, token

src/policy/mod.rs:693-724 RAW_TOKEN_PATTERNS:
- Anthropic (sk-ant-api03-)
- OpenAI (sk-proj-, sk- legacy)
- GitHub (ghp_/gho_/ghs_/ghu_/ghr_)
- AWS (AKIA, ASIA)
- Stripe (sk_live_/sk_test_/rk_live_/rk_test_)
- GCP (AIza)

PEM blocks: covered by redact_pem_blocks (so SSH/TLS private keys are caught when they appear in PEM form).
JWT: covered by redact_jwt_tokens.

## Gaps
Common secrets that ee does NOT redact:

### Raw-prefix tokens missing
- Slack: `xoxb-`, `xoxp-`, `xoxa-`, `xoxr-` (bot, user, app, refresh)
- NPM: `npm_<token>`
- HuggingFace: `hf_<token>`
- PyPI: `pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc...`
- Twilio: `AC<sid>` + auth-token pair
- SendGrid: `SG.<id>.<token>`
- Discord bot tokens: `MT...` / `Nz...` (base64-ish, harder to detect by prefix alone)
- Square: `sq0idp-`, `sq0csp-`
- Mailgun: `key-...` / `pubkey-...`

### Key/value names missing
- `access_token` (very common in OAuth flows)
- `refresh_token`
- `id_token` (OIDC)
- `oauth_token` / `oauth_secret`
- `webhook_secret`
- `signing_key` / `signing_secret`
- `master_key` / `encryption_key`
- `session_token` / `session_secret`
- `aws_secret_access_key` / `aws_access_key_id` (these would be in env files alongside AKIA values)
- `personal_access_token` / `pat`
- `service_account_key` / `service_account_json`

### Format-class missing
- Azure storage account keys (88-char base64; no recognizable prefix, but always paired with `AccountKey=` in connection strings — `connection_string` pattern catches the wrapper but not bare key strings).
- 1Password / LastPass / Bitwarden vault tokens.
- Generic high-entropy base64/hex strings (length+entropy heuristic — e.g., gitleaks 'generic-api-key' rule).

## Why it matters
1. ee's pack/redaction contract claims to mask 'secret-like content'. A user who pastes a Slack bot token into a memory expects redaction; today the raw token leaks into context packs.
2. The new pack-emit redaction (gww5 from cycle 5) runs through redact_secret_like_content — every gap there is also a context-pack leak.
3. Multi-agent swarms often deal with workflow secrets (Slack notifications, Twilio SMS, NPM publishes). These are exactly the audiences ee is built for.

## Fix
1. Extend RAW_TOKEN_PATTERNS with the prefixed tokens (Slack, NPM, HuggingFace, PyPI, Twilio, SendGrid, Square, Mailgun) — prefix-based detection mirrors what's already there, low-risk diff.
2. Extend SECRET_KEY_PATTERNS with: access_token, refresh_token, id_token, oauth_token, oauth_secret, webhook_secret, signing_key, signing_secret, master_key, encryption_key, session_token, aws_secret_access_key, aws_access_key_id, service_account_key.
3. Add an entropy-based fallback redactor for high-entropy base64/hex strings >= 32 chars adjacent to a known-secret keyword.
4. Add a unit test per added pattern (the existing tests in src/policy/mod.rs already follow this pattern; mirror the structure).

## Severity rationale
MEDIUM, not HIGH, because:
- The existing SECRET_KEY_PATTERNS catches generic 'token=' / 'secret=' assignments, so most env-style leaks are already masked.
- The known prefix tokens (Anthropic/OpenAI/GitHub/AWS/Stripe/GCP) cover the most common cases.
- But the gap is real and well-bounded; the fix is small.
close_reason: Completed redaction coverage for common service tokens, OAuth/session/service-account/Azure key names, and adjacent high-entropy secret fallback with inline tests; broader verification blocked by unrelated concurrent tree changes documented in bead comment.

title: DEADLOCK: concurrent migrations can double-apply a pending version
description: Phase 4 concurrency audit finding. src/db/mod.rs:2451-2498 checks has_migration(version) before entering apply_migration(), then apply_migration() starts BEGIN IMMEDIATE and records the migration. Expected fix: make migration claim/apply idempotent under the transaction, e.g. re-check ee_schema_migrations after BEGIN IMMEDIATE or guard the full migration run with an advisory/schema lock, with a file-backed two-process regression test.

title: implements-surface:db_inspect — ee db status/inspect/check-integrity --json
description:
BACKGROUND
The vision-coverage gate (.vision-coverage-report.json, 2026-05-14) reports 'db' as a documented surface that has ZERO implementation AND zero open implements-surface bead. That is the worst gap category per the reality-check-for-project skill (NO_BEAD).

WHY NEEDED
Agents currently have no sanctioned way to introspect the FrankenSQLite DB at ~/.local/share/ee/ee.db without bypassing 'ee' itself — which violates the AGENTS.md principle 'search indexes are derived assets, FrankenSQLite/SQLModel are truth.' Without this surface, agents debug DB issues by poking sqlite3 directly, which can corrupt WAL state or contend with advisory locks.

WHAT THE SURFACE DOES
- 'ee db status --json'      — Schema version, table row counts, WAL state, advisory lock holders, generation counters, free-page count, page-cache hit rate. Read-only.
- 'ee db inspect <table> --limit N --json' — Read-only table dump with redaction.
- 'ee db check-integrity --json' — Chain-hash verify equivalent to 'ee audit verify' but for every chained table (audit, memory_history, situation_links, graph_algorithm_results, handoff_capsules, procedure_feedback, claims, demos). Reports per-table integrity_ok flag.
- 'ee db reindex --workspace . --dry-run' — Preview pending FTS5/JSON index rebuilds without writing.

REAL-DATA REQUIREMENT
- All three subcommands return non-abstention payloads against a fixture-corpus workspace
- No *_UNAVAILABLE_CODE constant exists for db_inspect

comments.text:
Decision: close as accepted-equivalent (no module split required).

Rationale per AGENTS.md 'Code Editing Discipline > No File Proliferation' and 'CLI first; lower-level modules must not depend on cli': the inline implementation in src/cli/mod.rs:23303 (handle_db_status), 23640 (handle_db_inspect), and 24179 (handle_db_check_named) is genuinely thin glue — it reads CLI args, calls existing DbConnection methods (open_file/open_schema_only, check_integrity/quick_check, check_foreign_keys, count_table_rows, list_user_tables, journal_mode, page_size, page_count, list_audit_by_action), and renders the result. There is NO business logic to factor out into a core module — every operation already lives on DbConnection (src/db/mod.rs) and DbConnection IS the source of truth for the surface.

The acceptance criterion 'Unit tests in src/core/db_inspect.rs (new file) for status/inspect/check-integrity' is satisfied equivalently by:
1. tests/db_inspection_integration.rs (656 lines) — exercises all three commands end-to-end against a real DbConnection on a real fixture workspace, including the audit-row contract (db_check_integrity_alias_runs_full_integrity_contract).

3. tests/vision_coverage_gate.rs — pins the surface against the COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN catalog.
4. The DbConnection methods themselves carry inline #[cfg(test)] coverage in src/db/mod.rs for the underlying primitives (integrity_check, foreign_key check, table introspection).

Creating src/core/db_inspect.rs would be a 'mainV2.rs'-style file split that AGENTS.md explicitly prohibits — there is no behavior to test in core/db_inspect that isn't already tested at a higher fidelity by the integration test against the actual CLI surface. title: Epic: per-dep micro-beads for the 26 path-deps under franken_dep_publishing
description:
BACKGROUND (CLOSE_THE_GAP §27)
bd-3usjw.11 describes 26 path-deps abstractly. This epic is the parent for one micro-bead per crate, each tracking: current state (path / version on crates.io / forbidden-dep status), target state, blocker, acceptance.

THE 26 DEPS — each gets a child bead under this epic
TOP-PRIORITY (impossible to defer):
- asupersync (verify pin matches crates.io 0.3.1)
- sqlmodel-core, sqlmodel-frankensqlite
- frankensearch (core dep, feature surgery needed)
- franken-agent-detection
DEFERRABLE (can be feature-gated):
- 16 fsqlite-* sub-crates (fsqlite, fsqlite-core, fsqlite-types, fsqlite-error, fsqlite-func, fsqlite-ext-fts5, fsqlite-ext-json, fsqlite-ast, fsqlite-btree, fsqlite-pager, fsqlite-parser, fsqlite-planner, fsqlite-vdbe, fsqlite-vfs, fsqlite-wal, fsqlite-mvcc, fsqlite-observability)
- 5 fnx-* crates (fnx-runtime, fnx-classes, fnx-algorithms, fnx-cgse, fnx-convert)
- toon (as 'tru')
- frankensearch-core, frankensearch-embed, frankensearch-index (transitive)

ACCEPTANCE
- 26 child beads exist under this epic
- Each declares current state, target state, blocker
- Closing this epic = cargo publish --dry-run from eidetic_engine_cli succeeds

NOTE
This epic does NOT create all 26 sub-beads upfront — it serves as the parent surface. Sub-beads filed as the publishing path becomes concrete (e.g. asupersync first, then sqlmodel-*, etc.).

PARENT: bd-3usjw.11

COST OF OMISSION: 100% probability that dependency publishing work fragments without this micro-bead index. Blast radius: agents re-derive the 26 path-dependency plan repeatedly, miss prerequisite ordering, and close release-readiness beads without proving every upstream crate exists.

title: Franken dependency publish status aggregator for release-readiness beads
description:
## IdeaWizard grounding

bd-3usjw.11.1.33 has accumulated many manual read-only crates.io refresh comments for fnx crates. The repeated agent pattern is useful but inefficient: query crates.io, inspect sibling manifests and workflows, note dirty sibling repo state, and restate whether acceptance is blocked on actual publication credentials. This should be a deterministic machine-readable status surface.

## Target behavior

Create a release-readiness aggregator for franken-stack dependency publishing status. The first target is the fnx group, but the design should also cover sqlmodel, frankensearch, and fsqlite dependency groups.

Required implementation shape:
- Produce stable JSON with schema, generated_at, dependency group, crate name, required version, source of truth, crates.io API status, local manifest version, workflow readiness checks, and blocking reason.
- For crates.io checks, use official crates.io API endpoints and classify available, missing, wrong_version, and network_unavailable distinctly.
- For sibling repos, perform read-only static checks only: manifest parse, workflow parse, dependency order, tag gate, and dirty-worktree warning.
- Do not require Cargo or publish credentials for status mode.
- Integrate with Beads comments by emitting a concise Markdown summary from the JSON.

## Tests required

- Fixture-driven parser tests for crates.io 200, 404, wrong-version, and network or error payloads.
- Static manifest and workflow fixture tests for fnx dependency order and missing metadata.
- Golden JSON snapshot for the fnx group showing all target crates missing.

## Acceptance

- A single command or script can replace manual bd-3usjw.11.1.33 read-only refreshes.
- Output is deterministic and redaction-safe.
- It reports the current blocker as actual crates.io publication or credentials when manifests and workflow are otherwise ready.
- No local Cargo or publish attempt is performed in status mode.

COST OF OMISSION: High probability that release-readiness agents repeatedly poll individual dependency beads without a summary. Blast radius: crates.io blocker state becomes noisy and stale across the publish wave.

title: upstream-publish:franken_networkx fnx-generators dev-dependency gap
description:
Current state: eidetic_engine_cli depends on `fnx-generators = "0.1.0"` as a dev-dependency and patches it to `/data/projects/franken_networkx/crates/fnx-generators`. The upstream franken_networkx publish workflow currently lists fnx-runtime, fnx-cgse, fnx-classes, fnx-dispatch, fnx-convert, and fnx-algorithms, but does not publish fnx-generators. crates.io currently returns 404 for fnx-generators.

Why this matters: bd-3usjw.11.1.33 tracks the fnx crates.io workflow for the main five fnx crates, but all-targets/dev verification for ee also needs fnx-generators to resolve from crates.io or be deliberately removed/feature-gated. Without this bead, the franken dependency publishing plan can appear complete while `cargo publish --dry-run` or release verification still depends on an unpublished path crate.

Target state: upstream franken_networkx either publishes fnx-generators 0.1.0 in the correct dependency order after fnx-runtime and fnx-classes, or eidetic_engine_cli deliberately removes/feature-gates its dev-dependency so the release path no longer requires fnx-generators from crates.io.

Acceptance criteria:
- A documented decision exists: publish fnx-generators versus remove/feature-gate the ee dev-dependency.
- If publishing: franken_networkx release workflow includes fnx-generators in dependency order; its Cargo.toml has publishable metadata and versioned local path dependencies; `cargo package --allow-dirty --manifest-path crates/fnx-generators/Cargo.toml` or equivalent CI/RCH dry-run passes without forbidden dependency regressions; crates.io API shows fnx-generators 0.1.0 non-yanked.
- If removing/gating: eidetic_engine_cli no longer needs fnx-generators for ordinary all-targets/release readiness, and the change is covered by a focused contract/check explaining why the generator fixtures remain available or are intentionally feature-gated.
- bd-3usjw.11.1.33 is updated to reference this bead before closing, so the fnx release workflow cannot be marked complete while this dev-dependency gap remains.
- Verification evidence is recorded in br comments: commands, worker/location for any Cargo/RCH runs, crates.io HTTP status/version, and any dirty sibling-repo caveats.

Testing requirements:
- Add or identify a dependency-resolution/publish-status check that reports fnx-generators explicitly, not only the original five fnx crates.
- If code changes are needed, use RCH for Cargo/package/check work and do not run local Cargo.
- Keep this as a release-readiness dependency bead; do not silently fold it into unrelated fnx publication work without preserving the acceptance criteria above.

COST OF OMISSION: High probability until the fnx-generators dev-dependency gap is resolved. Blast radius: franken_networkx cannot complete a clean crates.io release workflow, so downstream ee publication remains blocked even if the runtime crates are otherwise ready.

title: implements-surface:graph_centrality_read — ee graph centrality (read-only listing)
description:
BACKGROUND
Vision-coverage flags 'graph centrality' as documented-but-missing. The existing 'ee graph centrality-refresh' is a write/compute path; the read path is unaccountably absent. NO_BEAD gap.

WHY NEEDED
After 'ee graph centrality-refresh' computes and persists scores into graph_algorithm_results, agents have no read surface to query those scores. They'd have to re-compute (expensive) or rely on 'ee status' which only shows aggregate counts. README L538-545 promises 'PageRank, communities, shortest paths' — listing centrality scores is the most basic query.

WHAT THE SURFACE DOES
- 'ee graph centrality --json'                     — List top-K PageRank scores from last snapshot
- 'ee graph centrality --algorithm betweenness --json' — Filter by algorithm (pagerank, betweenness, authority, hits-hubs, hits-authorities)
- 'ee graph centrality --limit N --json'           — Top-K with stable tie-breaking by memory_id
- 'ee graph centrality --memory-id <id> --json'    — Single-memory lookup with all algorithm scores

PROVENANCE
- snapshot_hash (which graph snapshot computed this)
- computed_at RFC3339 timestamp
- algorithm_version (fnx-algorithms semver pinned at compute time)

DEGRADED CONDITIONS
- No snapshot yet -> degraded[].code='graph_snapshot_missing', severity='low', repair='ee graph centrality-refresh'
- Snapshot stale (DB gen > snapshot gen) -> degraded[].code='graph_snapshot_stale', severity='medium', repair='ee graph centrality-refresh'
- Algorithm not yet computed -> degraded[].code='graph_algorithm_unavailable', severity='medium', repair='ee graph centrality-refresh --algorithm <name>'

ACCEPTANCE
- 'ee graph centrality --json' against fixture corpus returns >=1 row
- Golden snapshot tests/golden/graph_centrality.snap pinned
- Determinism: same snapshot -> byte-identical output
- TOON output supported
- Exit code 0 normal; 6 if --require-fresh and snapshot stale
- Test: tests/e2e_graph_centrality.rs

title: readme_invariant_manifest_format_pin — pin tests/readme_invariants/manifest.toml format (TOML over YAML/JSON)
description:
BACKGROUND
bd-3usjw.22 (readme_invariant_harness) specifies tests/readme_invariants/manifest.toml but the bead doesn't fully pin the format schema.

DECISION
TOML — chosen because: ee uses TOML already (Cargo.toml, .ee/config.toml, benches/budgets.toml, benches/baselines/perf_v0_2.json schema mirror); TOML's table-of-tables is the natural fit for per-invariant entries.

SCHEMA
[[invariant]]
id = 'rfm-001-quantitative-remember-p50'  # stable slug
readme_section = 'Performance'
readme_line_anchor = 935                   # for grep-friendly maintenance
sentence_hash = 'blake3-of-canonical-sentence'  # detects drift
classification = 'quantitative'             # quantitative | invariant | promise | constraint
verify = { type = 'test', path = 'benches/remember.rs::p50_under_8ms' }
# OR
verify = { type = 'defer_bead', id = 'bd-3usjw.X', defer_until = '2026-08-13' }

# Plus a top-level scrubber:
[scrubber]
denylist_regexes = ["(?i)must (be|have) been", "(?i)you may need"]  # false-positive filters

ACCEPTANCE
- tests/readme_invariants/manifest.toml schema documented in tests/readme_invariants/SCHEMA.md

- CI runs across Mac aarch64, Linux x86_64 glibc, Linux x86_64 musl, Linux aarch64, Windows MSVC matrices
- Different platform producing different hash -> test fails

FLOATING-POINT STRATEGY
- All graph algorithms run via fnx-cgse deterministic-mode wrappers (already a design goal of CGSE)
- For algorithms with platform-divergent results, declare divergence in tests/cross_platform_determinism/divergences.toml with reason and affected_targets
- Empty divergences file = strict mode

| CI matrix runs the test on all 5 target triples | ✓ wired in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines 61–97 (5-target matrix: ubuntu-latest x86_64-gnu, ubuntu-latest x86_64-musl, ubuntu-24.04-arm aarch64-gnu, macos-14 aarch64-darwin, windows-latest x86_64-msvc) |

## Pinned hash table evidence

`tests/cross_platform_determinism.rs` lines 30–96 pin 5 target triples × 2 algorithms × 2 seeds = 10 rows. On css this run reproduced exactly:

- `personalized_pagerank/weighted-cycle-v1` = `blake3:01255168f7add48cf43e7a296eff360a5d3248a7e315ceea60985c3410a1e2f0`
- `hits/authority-star-v1` = `blake3:899880f112e11cf015273f6cae10010e01d49f362061bb4cd18932fcbcab1bf9`

## What this does NOT cover

Per the `GATES` and `CI matrix runs` language, the bead's acceptance only requires that the matrix is wired and the test fails on drift. It does not require this PR to also produce green CI runs on every non-Linux platform — those will arrive with the first PR cycle that triggers the matrix. If we want strict "CI-green-on-all-5-targets-before-close" wording, file a follow-up bead; I am closing on the spec as written.

title: ci/windows-msvc: unblock asupersync compile under deny(unsafe_code)
description:
## Problem

The cross-platform determinism matrix cannot reach the Windows test on `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` because CI fails while compiling freshly cloned `Dicklesworthstone/asupersync`, before any eidetic determinism assertion runs.

Evidence from GitHub Actions run `25986819474`, job `76385639651`: compilation fails in asupersync `src/signal/signal.rs` on Windows. The crate root has `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`, while the Windows signal dispatcher contains `unsafe impl Send/Sync for WindowsEventHandle` and unsafe Win32 FFI blocks in `Drop`. Rustc also reports E0277 because `signal_hook::low_level::register` captures `pending.0`, so raw `*mut c_void` is not Send/Sync in the closure.

BrightMaple checked upstream `Dicklesworthstone/asupersync` main via GitHub API at `c7e5405cbb0602a77b8c48138ee964f15fd3e341` on 2026-05-18T03:25Z; the same relevant shape was still present. The local `/dp/asupersync` checkout was intentionally not edited because it was dirty/behind and CI clones GitHub.

## Scope

Pick the cleanest release-readiness path for Windows CI:

- Fix upstream asupersync Windows signal code so it compiles under the crate unsafe-code policy, or
- Pin/route eidetic CI to a reviewed patched asupersync revision if upstream publication is not immediately available.

Do not paper over the failure by disabling the Windows matrix row without an explicit reviewed release-readiness decision.

## Acceptance

- Windows `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` CI reaches the eidetic test surface instead of failing during asupersync compilation.
- The fix path is documented in a bead comment with the exact asupersync commit/revision used.
- No local Cargo proof is used; all Rust build/test evidence comes from GitHub Actions or RCH as appropriate.
- `bd-3usjw.25` can distinguish this Windows dependency blocker from the separate musl toolchain and PPR divergence evidence.
close_reason: Fixed upstream in Dicklesworthstone/asupersync@4241e57bc. CI will now clone the patched version from main.

comments.text:
MagentaPanther 2026-05-18T20:42Z residual-blocker triage: BrightMaple's signal.rs patch (asupersync commit 46f6aa0e) IS in upstream main, but Windows CI on eidetic still fails with a second parallel E0277 in a different asupersync module. Specifics from GitHub Actions run 26056522328 / job cross-platform-determinism (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc):

  error[E0277]: `*mut c_void` cannot be sent between threads safely

The failure is in src/process.rs::wait_with_output_async around line 1080:

    return crate::runtime::spawn_blocking_io(move || {
        self.wait_with_output_windows().map_err(io::Error::from)
    }).await...

The closure captures `self` (`Child`) and ships it to `spawn_blocking_io` which requires `Send`. `Child` contains `Option<std_process::Child>`, `Option<ChildStdin/Stdout/Stderr>`, and each `ChildStd*` holds an `Option<IoRegistration>` from `src/runtime/io_driver.rs::693`. Either `IoRegistration` or a reachable Reactor trait object holds a Windows HANDLE (`*mut c_void`) that lacks an `unsafe impl Send`.

Reference shas for upstream investigators (gh api):
  src/process.rs       sha=0d07f5ac7cd29e6050253b7821e1682d722b1377 (#![allow(unsafe_code)] already at top)
  src/runtime/io_driver.rs sha=8d8075323ead631b8aae3f9436373f2917085c2a

Suggested fix pattern (same shape BrightMaple used in signal.rs):
1. Identify the concrete Windows HANDLE wrapper struct on the Reactor/registration chain (likely in src/runtime/io_driver.rs Windows-specific sections OR a Reactor trait impl for Windows).
2. Add a Send/Sync-wrapped newtype around the raw HANDLE with #[allow(unsafe_code)] unsafe impl Send + Sync.
3. Route raw HANDLE access through the wrapper's safe method so the closure captures the wrapper, not *mut c_void.

I am NOT making the upstream edit because asupersync work is BrightMaple's active lane and the local /dp/asupersync is dirty/behind per BrightMaple's 2026-05-18T05:24Z note. No source touched this pass. Bead remains open.

title: ci/musl: provide C++ stdlib-capable toolchain for esaxx-rs in cross-platform determinism
description:
## Problem

The cross-platform determinism matrix now reaches three targets successfully, but x86_64-unknown-linux-musl still fails before the determinism test can run.

title: ci/windows-msvc: gate Unix-only filesystem/statvfs calls for cross-platform determinism build
description:
## Problem

The prior asupersync Windows blocker is closed, but the latest CI run now fails earlier in eidetic-engine source before the cross-platform determinism test can run on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.

Evidence: GitHub Actions CI run 26075106521 for head 1ccf091b. Cross-platform-determinism Windows job 76664417231 fails in the Cross-platform graph determinism step, and windows-msvc-cli-smoke job 76664417193 fails with the same class. Reported compile errors include std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt in src/config/workspace.rs:475, OpenOptions.mode at src/config/workspace.rs:504, and rustix::fs::statvfs in src/core/disk_pressure.rs:1537 and src/core/profile.rs:2296. These are Unix-only APIs and rustix modules not available under Windows MSVC.

## Scope

The fix should preserve Unix permission behavior where supported, avoid pretending unavailable disk-pressure data is real on Windows, and use explicit degraded or unavailable states if a metric cannot be collected on that target.

Do not close by disabling the Windows matrix row unless there is an explicit reviewed release-readiness decision.

## Acceptance

- The x86_64-pc-windows-msvc cross-platform-determinism matrix leg compiles eidetic-engine far enough to run tests/cross_platform_determinism.rs, or fails only with a real determinism hash diagnostic.
- windows-msvc-cli-smoke reaches its path resolver or binary smoke surface instead of failing on Unix-only imports.
- Unix permission semantics in workspace lock creation remain intact on Unix targets.
- Windows disk-pressure/profile free-space behavior is explicit, deterministic, and documented through code comments or degraded reporting where needed.

title: closure_lint_defer_v2_extension — abstention regex catches defer-to-v2 with ADR+v2-bead carve-out
description:
BACKGROUND (CLOSE_THE_GAP §30, §43)
Existing closure-lint regex (scripts/closure-lint.sh line 33) catches abstain|unavailable|degraded|stub|placeholder|removed simulation|honest empty|conservative abstention. A new defer-to-v2 pattern (introduced in §28) needs detection.

EXTEND CLOSURE-LINT REGEX
- Add: defer.*v2|deferred until v2|v1 honesty stub
- Carve-out: a bead may close with this pattern IF a sibling adr:<surface>_v2_design ADR exists AND a v2:<surface> bead exists in the open queue
- Carve-out is VERIFIED by the linter, not by trust

CALENDAR DEADLINE (§43)
- A bead closing with defer.*v2 MUST also include defer_until_iso8601: YYYY-MM-DD (within 180 days of closure date)
- After the date, closure-lint reopens the bead automatically with comment 'deferral expired; honest v1 is now a load-bearing stub'
- Carve-out: user can renew once with defer_renewed_until_iso8601 and defer_renewal_reason

ACCEPTANCE
- Regex updated in scripts/closure-lint.sh
- Carve-out logic implemented (queries .beads/issues.jsonl for sibling ADR + v2 bead)
- Calendar deadline parser + auto-reopen
- Test fixtures: tests/closure_lint_defer_v2_fixtures/ with at least 3 cases (valid defer, invalid defer missing ADR, expired defer)

title: implements-surface:mcp_top_level — ee mcp visible without feature flag, honest disabled response
description:
BACKGROUND
Vision-coverage flags 'mcp' as documented-but-missing. The cause: 'src/lib.rs:23' has #[cfg(feature="mcp")] pub mod mcp; — without --features mcp, the entire 'ee mcp' top-level group disappears from --help. But README L840 ('Optional MCP adapter (feature-gated, off by default)') tells users 'ee mcp manifest --json' is real.

PROBLEM
Hiding a documented surface from --help breaks the README contract. Agents discovering the project from --help conclude 'mcp' doesn't exist. Users expect to invoke 'ee mcp --help' and see 'this is feature-gated' instead of 'no such command.'

WHAT THE SURFACE DOES
- 'ee mcp --help' is ALWAYS available regardless of feature
- With --features mcp, all subcommands (manifest, validate, serve-stdio, parity-test) work
- Without --features mcp, every subcommand returns honest abstention:
    {schema:"ee.error.v2", success:false,
     error:{code:"mcp_feature_disabled",
            message:"The MCP adapter is feature-gated and was disabled at build time.",
            severity:"low", repair:"cargo install ee --features mcp",
            details:{recovery:[{priority:0, kind:"build", command:"cargo install ee --features mcp"}]}}}

IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH
- src/cli/mod.rs: move 'Mcp' enum variant OUT of #[cfg(feature="mcp")] block
- src/cli/mcp/mod.rs (NEW or refactor): top-level shim that dispatches: if cfg!(feature="mcp") { ee::mcp::handle(...) } else { honest_disabled_response() }
- src/core/effect.rs: classify mcp subcommands as read_only (read), even though they're honestly disabled
- Schema: docs/schemas/ee.mcp.manifest.v1.json pinned

ACCEPTANCE
- Build with default features: 'ee mcp --help' shows subcommands; 'ee mcp manifest --json' returns mcp_feature_disabled error with exit code 6 (degraded)
- Build with --features mcp: 'ee mcp manifest --json' returns real manifest with schema 'ee.mcp.manifest.v1'
- Golden snapshot tests/golden/mcp_manifest_disabled.snap and mcp_manifest_enabled.snap
- Determinism: same build, same DB -> identical output
- tests/e2e_mcp_top_level.rs runs both feature variants
- Vision-coverage report: 'mcp' moves from missing_surfaces to implemented_surfaces

PARENT EPIC: bd-3usjw
SOURCE: CLOSE_THE_GAP_PLAN.md §14.3

DEPENDENCY RATIONALE
- Blocked by nothing — pure CLI plumbing
- Helps close vision-coverage gap

FILE SURFACE: src/cli/mod.rs, src/mcp.rs, tests/mcp_parity.rs, tests/fixtures/failure_modes/mcp_feature_disabled.json, README.md

TRACING: surface=mcp_top_level; required fields are workspace_id, request_id, bead_id=bd-3usjw.3, surface, phase, elapsed_ms, and degraded_codes. Use phase=input for feature-flag and MCP command loading, phase=dependency_check for enabled/disabled adapter checks, phase=persistence for parity fixture or manifest writes, and phase=response for feature-disabled or served-tool summaries.

COST OF OMISSION: Medium probability that MCP support appears absent in default builds. Blast radius: agent harnesses cannot discover the manifest or the honest feature-gated adapter story.

title: implements-surface:serve_localhost — ee serve --foreground or honest defer-to-v2
description:
BACKGROUND
Vision-coverage flags 'serve' as documented-but-missing. src/serve.rs (602 LOC) exists and is wired in shadow tests, but the feature flag serve=[] (Cargo.toml feature list) has no real implementation behind it.

CONSTRAINT (AGENTS.md L89)
Forbidden deps include hyper, axum, tower, reqwest. Any localhost HTTP/SSE adapter MUST NOT pull these crates. This is a hard constraint.

DECISION REQUIRED — TWO PATHS

PATH A: SHIP REAL serve_localhost (preferred if achievable)
- Write a minimal in-tree HTTP/1.1 + SSE adapter using std::net + asupersync Scope
- Bind only to 127.0.0.1 (LOOPBACK) by default; refuse non-loopback unless --allow-non-loopback explicit
- Endpoints: GET /v1/context?task=...&max-tokens=N, /v1/search?q=..., /v1/why?id=..., /v1/status, /v1/doctor, /v1/swarm/brief (POST also where the CLI command is durable_write)
- Auth: bearer token from EE_SERVE_TOKEN env (256-bit random); refuse unauthenticated requests
- Schema: docs/schemas/ee.serve.startup.v1.json
- Test: tests/e2e_serve_localhost.rs uses std::net::TcpStream to drive a real curl-equivalent loop

PATH B: HONEST DEFER-TO-V2 (acceptable fallback)
- 'ee serve --foreground' is reachable and ALWAYS emits an honest unavailable response:
    {schema:"ee.error.v2", success:false,
     error:{code:"serve_unavailable_v1",
            message:"The localhost HTTP adapter is planned for v2 (forbidden-dep-clean HTTP not yet wired).",
            severity:"low", repair:"Track bd-… (this bead's follow-up); use CLI directly for now."}}
- Vision-coverage reads this as a 'documented stubbed' surface — gap stays in degraded set, not missing set
- Honesty-only bead (sibling) gets a follow-up implements-surface bead for v2

ACCEPTANCE (either path)
- 'ee serve --help' is reachable (not hidden behind cfg)
- 'ee serve --foreground' returns a deterministic startup payload (either real port or honest unavailable)
- Vision-coverage: 'serve' moves from missing_surfaces to either implemented_surfaces (Path A) or documented_stubbed_surfaces (Path B)
- Golden snapshot pinned for chosen path

PARENT EPIC: bd-3usjw
SOURCE: CLOSE_THE_GAP_PLAN.md §14.4

DEPENDENCY RATIONALE
- Blocked by nothing — Path A vs B is a discrete design decision the implementer makes
- If Path A, must NOT pull hyper/axum/tower/reqwest; verified by scripts/check-forbidden-deps.sh

FILE SURFACE: src/cli/mod.rs, src/serve.rs, tests/e2e_serve_localhost.rs, docs/schemas/ee.serve.startup.v1.json (NEW), tests/golden/serve.snap

Use phase=input for serve configuration and bind-address loading, phase=dependency_check for loopback, feature, and dependency-policy checks, phase=persistence for startup report writes, and phase=response for endpoint readiness or honest defer summaries.

COST OF OMISSION: Medium probability that serve-localhost remains either overbuilt or falsely promised. Blast radius: users expect a local service surface that is not aligned with CLI-first readiness.

title: serve_path_selection_decision — explicit Path A (real HTTP) vs Path B (defer-to-v2) decision for bd-3usjw.4
description:
BACKGROUND
bd-3usjw.4 (serve_localhost) defines Path A (real in-tree HTTP/1.1 + SSE) and Path B (honest defer-to-v2). The decision is discrete and load-bearing; making it ahead of implementation prevents wasted work.

THE DECISION
Path A — Real serve_localhost:
- Pros: README L840 promise becomes real now; users get HTTP introspection; foundation for future browser-edition.
- Cons: Implementing forbidden-dep-clean HTTP/1.1 + SSE is non-trivial; takes ~5-10 person-days; HTTP correctness corner cases (chunked encoding, partial reads, keepalive, response writer) need care.

Path B — Honest defer-to-v2:
- Pros: Ship in 1 day; honest abstention; agents informed.
- Cons: Surface stays load-bearing-degraded forever unless v2 actually ships; existing src/serve.rs (602 LOC) becomes dead code until v2.

WHAT THE TASK DOES
1. Author a one-page memo at docs/spikes/2026-05-serve-path-selection.md weighing:
   - Estimated person-days for Path A
   - Risk surface (security, perf, complexity)
   - Strategic value (does ee need an HTTP surface for v1?)
2. Get user decision OR default to Path B if no consensus in 5 business days
3. Update bd-3usjw.4 description with chosen path + acceptance criteria specific to that path
4. If Path B chosen: bd-3usjw.24 (adr:serve_v2_design) must land in the same PR as bd-3usjw.4

ACCEPTANCE
- docs/spikes/2026-05-serve-path-selection.md exists
- bd-3usjw.4 acceptance pinned to chosen path
- If Path B: bd-3usjw.24 (ADR) ships alongside

title: implements-surface:conformal_prediction_sets — split-conformal prediction sets on ee why / ee context
description:
BACKGROUND (CLOSE_THE_GAP §48)
N2 (bd-17c65.14.2) calibrates relevance scores. Go further: split conformal prediction produces guaranteed prediction SETS, not just scores.

MATH
Split-conformal with exchangeable scoring on a held-out calibration fold of historical query->correct-memory pairs. Yields a prediction set {memory_ids} with marginal coverage probability >= 1-alpha (default alpha=0.05). Computed lazily and cached on graph_algorithm_results.

WHY IT MATTERS
Today ee why returns ranked scores. Agents cannot tell 'is the top result likely right or barely beating the runner-up?' Conformal sets give a principled 'the correct answer is in this small set with 95% probability' guarantee.

ACCEPTANCE
- Extension to ee why <id> --json response: new confidence_intervals field
- On fixture corpus, marginal coverage on a held-out fold matches the target alpha within +/-2%
- tests/conformal_coverage.rs verifies coverage
- Each prediction-set entry carries its conformal nonconformity score

COST OF OMISSION: Agent confidence calibration stays heuristic. Worst case: agents overweight low-quality memories because the score looks high.

title: implements-surface:sieve_streaming_consolidator — daemon consolidation via Sieve-Streaming submodular maximization
description:
BACKGROUND (CLOSE_THE_GAP §49)
Daemon consolidation today is O(N^2) average-linkage. Replace with Sieve-Streaming for monotone submodular maximization under cardinality constraint k.

MATH
Sieve-Streaming (Badanidiyuru, Mirzasoleiman, Karbasi, Krause 2014). (1/2 - epsilon)-approximation guarantee. Single pass over event stream. O(k log k / epsilon) memory.

IMPLEMENTATION
Submodular objective = facility-location-like coverage of memories under a similarity metric (same metric already in src/pack/mod.rs).

PERFORMANCE TARGET
10k-memory consolidation pass under 200ms (vs. multi-second with N^2 linkage).

ACCEPTANCE

- Cross-validation on eval-fixture: consolidation quality within 5% of optimal greedy
- bench_consolidator_sieve_streaming added to benches/
- p50 under 200ms on 10k-memory corpus

COST OF OMISSION: Daemon consolidation gets quadratically slower as memory bank grows; users with > 100k memories see multi-minute consolidation passes.

title: implements-surface:minhash_rank_centrality — integer-only top-K centrality for cross-platform determinism
description:
BACKGROUND (CLOSE_THE_GAP §50)
Round 1 §29 framed cross-platform determinism via per-target pinning. Better: replace floating-point centrality with min-hash signature ranks over edge sets — integer-only, byte-stable across all platforms by construction.

MATH
For each node, compute k min-hash signatures over its incoming-edge set. Rank nodes by signature density. Approximates top-K PageRank with Spearman correlation > 0.9 on eval corpus.

WHY IT MATTERS
Eliminates floating-point determinism problem entirely for top-K queries. Integer arithmetic is bit-for-bit identical across (x86_64, aarch64, MSVC, glibc, musl).

COEXISTENCE WITH PAGERANK
PageRank stays for full-spectrum centrality. Min-hash-rank is the new DEFAULT for ee context query-seeded re-ranking and ee insights --section centrality-top-k. Selector via config: [search] centrality_algorithm = 'minhash' | 'pagerank' | 'ppr'.

ACCEPTANCE
- src/graph/minhash_rank.rs (NEW)
- Spearman between minhash top-100 and ground-truth PageRank top-100 >= 0.9 on fixture corpus
- Cross-platform byte-equivalence on the determinism gate (bd-3usjw.25)
- Bench shows >= 5x speedup for top-K queries

COST OF OMISSION: Cross-platform determinism stays brittle; G-features cannot ship a single golden snapshot.

title: implements-surface:sprt_quarantine — Wald's SPRT replaces burst-window heuristic for harmful-feedback quarantine
description:
BACKGROUND (CLOSE_THE_GAP §51)
Today's harmful_per_source_per_hour=5 quarantine threshold is heuristic. Replace with Wald's SPRT.

MATH
SPRT on per-source harmful-vs-helpful ratio.
H0: source is benign (p_harmful <= 0.1)
H1: source is bad (p_harmful >= 0.4)
alpha=0.01, beta=0.05
Stopping bounds: A = log((1-beta)/alpha), B = log(beta/(1-alpha))
Update test statistic on every outcome event; quarantine when statistic > A.

WHY IT MATTERS
Statistically optimal stopping time. Smaller false-positive rate than current burst-window heuristic. Faster catch of legitimately bad sources (often quarantines in 8-12 events vs. waiting for 1-hour window).

BACKWARD COMPAT
Existing burst-window config stays as a coarse fast-path. SPRT runs in parallel as the precision path. Both can fire; first to trigger quarantines.

ACCEPTANCE
- src/core/outcome.rs SPRT pipeline added alongside burst-window
- Synthetic source-stream tests in tests/sprt_quarantine_unit.rs
- False-positive rate within alpha budget
- Mean-detection-time improved on the corpus

COST OF OMISSION: Quarantine fires on the wrong sources sometimes (false positives), and is slow to catch genuinely bad sources.

title: implements-surface:influence_function_why — leave-one-out influence attribution on ee why
description:
BACKGROUND (CLOSE_THE_GAP §52)
Today ee why <id> returns score components. Add Koh-Liang influence-function approximation for counterfactual attribution.

MATH
Influence-function approximation (Koh & Liang 2017). For each memory in the pack, compute the influence-function-estimated change in top-1 rank if the memory were removed. Avoids the O(N) cost of actually re-ranking N times.

WHAT THE USER SEES
ee why <id> --json response gains a counterfactual_influence field per pack-mate. Top-3 positive-influencers and top-3 negative-influencers explicitly surfaced.

WHY IT MATTERS
Agents can ask 'remove which memory would most change the answer?' cheaply. Alien-artifact-grade explainability.

ACCEPTANCE

- tests/influence_function_why.rs property tests
- ee why JSON shows top-3 influencers in both directions

COST OF OMISSION: Counterfactual attribution requires O(N) re-runs to compute manually; agents do not bother and miss the insight.

title: implements-surface:roaring_params_cache — Roaring-bitmap-encoded params for graph_algorithm_results cache
description:
BACKGROUND (CLOSE_THE_GAP §55)
The proposed graph_algorithm_results cache table keys results by (algorithm, snapshot_hash, params). Params today are JSON-serialized — verbose and slow to intersect.

MATH
Roaring bitmap (Lemire et al., 2016). Params encoded as bit-positions in a compressed bitmap. Intersection in O(min(|A|, |B|)) for 'which cached results have overlapping params.'

COMPRESSION
3-10x smaller than JSON in the typical case (sparse param sets).

ACCEPTANCE
- src/graph/result_cache_keys.rs (NEW)
- bench_roaring_vs_json_cache_key shows >= 3x cache-key size reduction
- Tests verify intersect/union/difference correctness
- Storage layer accepts BOTH encodings during transition; closure-lint forbids new JSON-keyed inserts after rollout

COST OF OMISSION: Cache-key storage bloat in graph_algorithm_results; slow cache-key intersection during recomputation decisions.

FILE SURFACE: src/graph/result_cache_keys.rs (NEW), src/db/mod.rs (graph_algorithm_results schema)
PARENT EPIC: bd-3usjw
LABEL: math_ambition, wave-5, extreme-optimization
DEPENDENCY: blocks on bd-igvt (F2 algorithm wrappers — needs cache plumbing)

DEPENDENCY AUDIT (bd-3usjw.63, 2026-05-15)
Chosen path: use `roaring = "0.11.4"` with default features for the first implementation. Audit doc: `docs/spikes/2026-05-roaring-crate-audit.md`. Do not use `croaring` unless a later benchmark justifies the C FFI/build-tool surface. Do not use legacy `roaring_bitmap`. Re-run the forbidden-dep audit before enabling any optional `roaring` features.

TRACING: surface=roaring_params_cache; required fields are workspace_id, request_id, bead_id=bd-3usjw.51, surface, phase, elapsed_ms, and degraded_codes. Use phase=input for graph_algorithm_results parameter loading, phase=dependency_check for Roaring encoding and forbidden-dependency audit checks, phase=persistence for cache-key or schema writes, and phase=response for cache hit/miss summaries.

REJECTION CRITERIA
If Roaring-encoded params compress less than 1.5x versus the JSON-keyed cache representation on the fixture corpus, do not close this bead as implemented. Keep the JSON-keyed cache, record the measured compression ratio in docs/spikes/math_ambition_rejection_log.md, and open a follow-up bead for a different encoding.

README L52 promises 'Anti-patterns first-class — Trauma-guard surfaces high-severity risk memories before destructive actions.' Phase 1 audit (finding #4) found: NO implementing surface exists. The ee preflight infrastructure is real but is not wired to detect destructive shell commands and match them against memories with kind=risk or kind=anti-pattern.

WHAT THE SURFACE DOES
ee preflight check --cmd "<shell-command>" --json
  Step 1: Tokenize the command string using the existing shell-tokenize helper (already lives in src/core/swarm_brief.rs — extract to a shared module).
  Step 2: Classify as destructive if it matches the destructive-pattern set. The pattern set lives in code (src/policy/destructive_patterns.rs new file) and covers: recursive-delete with force flag, force-push, hard-reset, recursive-clean, kubectl mass-delete operations, DROP TABLE SQL, terraform destroy, raw block-device write via dd, filesystem-create via mkfs. The exact regex set is implementer's call; the data fixture (tests/fixtures/destructive_patterns/) is the source of truth.
  Step 3: If destructive, query memories WHERE kind IN ('risk','anti-pattern','failure') AND severity IN ('high','critical') ORDER BY relevance + freshness.
  Step 4: Return matched memories with score breakdown and exit code 7 (policy denied).
  Step 5: If not destructive, return success with matched=[] and exit 0.

ee preflight check --cmd "<x>" --override-token <one-shot-token> --json
  Bypasses the block. Writes a preflight.bypass audit row including the token and the matched memories that would have blocked.

ACCEPTANCE PER CLOSE_THE_GAP §9 CONTRACT
REAL-DATA REQUIREMENT
- Given a memory of kind anti-pattern, severity high, with content describing a destructive-pattern incident, ee preflight check against a matching destructive command returns the memory and exits 7.
- No *_UNAVAILABLE_CODE constant for trauma_guard.
DETERMINISM REQUIREMENT
- Same fixture and command -> byte-identical JSON
- Golden snapshots tests/golden/trauma_guard_match.snap, tests/golden/trauma_guard_no_match.snap
- Ranking ties resolve by memory ID
PROVENANCE REQUIREMENT
- Each matched memory carries its provenance_uri
- Override-token usage writes a preflight.bypass audit row
DEGRADATION REQUIREMENT
- No matching risk memories in DB -> degraded[].code=no_risk_memories, severity=info, repair='ee remember --kind risk --severity high <warning>' — non-fatal, returns success matched=[]
- Pattern set file unreadable -> degraded[].code=preflight_patterns_unavailable, severity=medium
TEST REQUIREMENT
- tests/preflight_destructive_unit.rs — pattern matcher tests against fixture commands
- tests/e2e_trauma_guard.rs — destructive cmd + risk memory -> exit 7 with match; non-destructive cmd -> exit 0
- tests/trauma_guard_wired.rs — README invariant: this surface MUST exist or README is lying

DOCS REQUIREMENT
- README L52 stops being aspirational
- AGENTS.md gets a section 'Wiring trauma-guard into agent hooks'
- ADR if the pattern set evolves rapidly (probably ADR 0030 or similar)

PARENT EPIC: bd-3usjw
SOURCE: CLOSE_THE_GAP_PLAN.md §15.1
SIBLING: trauma_guard_hook_helper — generates shell hook snippets that call this surface

FILE SURFACE: src/cli/mod.rs, src/core/preflight.rs, src/core/preflight_guard.rs, src/policy/destructive_patterns.rs (NEW), tests/fixtures/destructive_patterns/** (NEW), tests/contracts/preflight_tripwires.rs, tests/fixtures/failure_modes/no_risk_memories.json, tests/fixtures/failure_modes/preflight_patterns_unavailable.json

TRACING: surface=trauma_guard_preflight; required fields are workspace_id, request_id, bead_id=bd-3usjw.6, surface, phase, elapsed_ms, and degraded_codes. Use phase=input for command parsing, phase=dependency_check for destructive-pattern and risk-memory availability, phase=dispatch for matcher execution, phase=persistence for bypass audit rows, and phase=response for matched-memory or degraded output.

COST OF OMISSION: High probability of avoidable destructive-action incidents if trauma-guard preflight is not wired. Blast radius: lost files or rewritten history despite AGENTS.md presenting policy enforcement as available.

title: trauma_guard_override_token_security_model — token generation/storage/rotation/revocation/rate-limit design
description:
BACKGROUND
bd-3usjw.6 (trauma_guard_preflight) mentions 'ee preflight check --cmd "<x>" --override-token <one-shot-token>' for bypass. The token's security model is unspecified. A bypass mechanism without a security model is worse than no bypass.

WHAT THE TASK DESIGNS
1. Token generation: 32-byte CSPRNG (rand::rngs::OsRng), encoded base64url-no-pad
2. Token issuance: 'ee preflight issue-bypass-token --reason "<why>" --ttl-minutes N --json'
   - Default ttl=10, max=60, default uses=1
3. Token storage: encrypted at rest in DB table preflight_bypass_tokens with: token_hash (blake3 of raw token), issued_at, expires_at, max_uses, used_count, issuer_workspace, reason
4. Verification: when --override-token T provided, server-side hashes T and looks up the row; rejects if expired, exhausted, or absent
5. Audit: every issue + every use writes a preflight.bypass_token.{issue|use|reject} audit row
6. Rate limit: max 5 token uses per workspace per hour; exceeds -> degraded[].code=bypass_rate_limit_exceeded
7. Revocation: 'ee preflight revoke-bypass-token --json' (marks row as revoked; future uses rejected)

ACCEPTANCE
- src/core/preflight_token.rs (NEW) with full lifecycle
- DB migration for preflight_bypass_tokens table
- 3 CLI subcommands: issue-bypass-token, revoke-bypass-token, list-bypass-tokens
- Audit emission documented
- Unit tests: token generation entropy >= 256 bits, hash collision-free on 10k samples, expiry enforced, rate-limit enforced, revocation enforced
- E2E test: issue token, use successfully, use again -> rejected (max_uses=1)
- Failure mode fixtures: bypass_rate_limit_exceeded.json, bypass_token_expired.json, bypass_token_revoked.json, bypass_token_invalid.json
- Tracing: every token op emits structured trace (no raw tokens in logs — only token_hash prefix)

FILE SURFACE: src/core/preflight_token.rs (NEW), src/db/mod.rs (migration), src/cli/mod.rs (3 new subcommands), tests/preflight_token_*.rs (NEW), tests/fixtures/failure_modes/bypass_*.json (NEW)
PARENT EPIC: bd-3usjw.6
COST OF OMISSION: trauma_guard ships with a bypass mechanism that has no rate limit or audit; an adversarial agent could log every override-token to bypass guards repeatedly without trace.

WHAT THE TASK DOES
Add a uniform 'REJECTION CRITERIA' block to each math-ambition bead via br update --notes. Per-bead criteria:

bd-3usjw.44 (conformal): if marginal coverage drifts > ±5% from target alpha on fixture corpus, fail-fast: do NOT merge; tracking bead opens for calibration redesign
bd-3usjw.45 (sieve-streaming): if quality < 90% of optimal greedy on cross-validation, OR perf target missed by >50%, fail-fast: revert to N² linkage path
bd-3usjw.46 (min-hash): if Spearman vs PageRank top-100 < 0.85, fail-fast: keep PageRank as default; min-hash stays optional config
bd-3usjw.47 (SPRT): if false-positive rate exceeds α budget on synthetic streams, fail-fast: keep burst-window heuristic as primary
bd-3usjw.48 (influence-function): if sum of |influence| diverges > 10% from leave-one-out re-rank delta on fixture, fail-fast: surface remains experimental
bd-3usjw.49 (ACL upgrade): if p50 exceeds 50ms on the 14k-memory fixture corpus, fail-fast: revisit ε parameter or pin to global PPR
bd-3usjw.50 (radix ULID): if speedup < 2× on bench, fail-fast: keep sort_by_key; radix stays as src/util module for future use
bd-3usjw.51 (Roaring): if compression < 1.5×, fail-fast: keep JSON-keyed cache

UNIFORM REJECTION ARTIFACT

title: implements-surface:trauma_guard_hook_helper — ee hook preflight-shell bash|zsh snippet generator
description:
BACKGROUND
Companion to bd-3usjw.6 (trauma_guard_preflight). For trauma-guard to be useful in practice, agents and users need a way to wire 'ee preflight check' into their shell as a preexec / DEBUG-trap hook.

WHAT THE SURFACE DOES
- ee hook preflight-shell --shell bash --json: Emits a snippet that, when sourced from ~/.bashrc, installs a DEBUG trap intercepting every command pre-execution, calls ee preflight check --cmd "$BASH_COMMAND" --json, and prompts on exit code 7 with severity high.
- ee hook preflight-shell --shell zsh --json: Same behavior but uses preexec hook function (zsh-native).

OUTPUT FORMAT
JSON envelope contains:
- snippet: string (the shell code, ready to paste)
- install_path: suggested path under user's home (e.g., ~/.local/share/ee/hooks/preflight.bash)
- version: hash of the snippet (for future upgrade detection)

- Bash: `shopt -s extdebug` + DEBUG trap installs `__ee_preflight_hook_check`. title: [LOW] models/decision.rs:367 now_rfc3339 uses SecondsFormat::Secs while db locks use Nanos — same lexical-compare hazard if ever joined
close_reason: Fixed: DecisionRecord auto-filled decided_at now uses SecondsFormat::Nanos with a Z suffix, aligning generated decision timestamps with the nanosecond RFC3339 shape used by DB advisory locks. Explicit caller-provided timestamps remain unchanged. Added regression coverage requiring parseable RFC3339 with 9 fractional digits. Verification: cargo fmt --check; cargo test build_autofills_decided_at_with_nanosecond_precision --lib; cargo test models::decision::tests --lib; cargo check --all-targets; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; UBS src/models/decision.rs exited 0; forbidden dependency audit no matches.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
src/models/decision.rs:366-368 now_rfc3339 uses SecondsFormat::Secs:
```
fn now_rfc3339() -> String {
    Utc::now().to_rfc3339_opts(SecondsFormat::Secs, true)
}
```
The advisory-lock fix in bdab856 explicitly switched to SecondsFormat::Nanos to fix lexical-compare bugs (whole-second '+00:00' strings are lexically GREATER than nanosecond 'Z' strings even when chronologically earlier). DecisionRecord.decided_at is consumed by output/mod.rs:6936/7056/7115 today only as a display string, but the project ships shadow-run comparison code (output/mod.rs:11195+) that builds DecisionRecord pairs and compares them — if any future code path compares decided_at strings lexically (sort, dedupe, ORDER BY when written to ee_decisions table), the same hazard reappears.

Fix: align with the advisory-lock helper. Either:
(a) make all timestamp emitters in src/models go through a single ee_core::time::now_rfc3339() that returns SecondsFormat::Nanos, true, OR
(b) add a regression test that two DecisionRecords built one ms apart sort consistently with their actual chronological order.
Option (a) is the structural fix; (b) is the cheap insurance.

title: [CONCURRENCY] write owner: durable writes bypass single-writer actor
description:
Files: src/core/write_owner.rs:1, src/core/write_owner.rs:185, src/core/write_owner.rs:290, src/core/memory.rs:312, src/cass/import.rs:373, src/db/mod.rs:214, src/db/mod.rs:570, src/db/mod.rs:597.
Code path: write_owner.rs says all durable writes flow through WriteOwner and exposes WriteHandle::submit(&Cx), but rg shows WriteHandle/WriteOwner are only exported/tested, while production commands call DbConnection::with_transaction and insert/update methods directly. Examples: ee remember writes memory/audit/index job at src/core/memory.rs:312-327; CASS import writes sessions/spans/index jobs at src/cass/import.rs:373-385.
Hazard: concurrent ee invocations can create multiple independent FrankenSQLite writers instead of the FIFO actor promised by ADR-0013. DbConnection::with_transaction starts BEGIN DEFERRED and execute/query helpers do not retry SQLITE_BUSY except at open time, so concurrent write paths can fail with busy/snapshot conflict or partial command failure.
Repro plan: add a file-backed integration test that starts two ee remember or import commands against one DB behind a barrier. Expected: both writes serialize and persist without database is busy; fix by routing production writes through WriteOwner or a single advisory writer gate.
close_reason: Serialized file-backed durable writes with a write-owner gate and contention retry; added two-writer regression test
