## Problem

Agents currently use `br ready --json`, `bv --robot-triage`, Agent Mail reservations, inbox state, `rch status`, and `git status` manually. That creates two recurring failure modes: communication purgatory, where agents keep refreshing state but do not start work, and collision churn, where two agents discover the same ready bead or dirty surface late.

## Goal

Add a deterministic, read-only planning surface, tentatively `ee swarm next-action --json` or `ee work next --json`, that produces a ranked set of concrete slices an agent can safely take next, with explicit reasons, blocked-by-coordination evidence, stale-work proposals, RCH capacity posture, dirty-file conflicts, and suggested file reservations.

This must remain a helper surface. It must not create branches, worktrees, commits, stashes, resets, automatic tracker reopens, automatic mail blasts, or automatic file edits. It recommends; agents or humans act.

## Non-goals

No replacement for Beads, BV, Agent Mail, RCH, or the agent harness. No autonomous assignment daemon. No automatic cleanup. No destructive file operations. No local Cargo. No hidden durable mutation except optional explicit audit records behind a dry-run/apply split if a later child bead introduces that mode.

## Acceptance

The epic closes when its children provide a versioned JSON schema, deterministic ordering, stale-work proposal logic, RCH/dirty-state lane hints, Agent Mail reservation overlays, duplicate-work suppression hooks, docs, and no-mock logged e2e coverage showing at least three agents can independently receive non-overlapping next-action recommendations in a dirty shared checkout.

title: SWA1: next-action input snapshot and ee.swarm_next_action.v1 schema
description:
## Background

This is the foundation for the swarm work allocator epic. Before ranking work, ee needs a deterministic snapshot model that captures the inputs agents already inspect manually: Beads ready/in-progress/blocked state, BV scores when available, Agent Mail active identities and reservations, git dirty paths, RCH capacity, and local environment posture.

## Scope

Define `ee.swarm_next_action.v1` and an internal snapshot builder. The first public surface may be `ee swarm next-action --json` or `ee work next --json`; naming should follow existing CLI conventions after inspection. The command is read-only by default and must not update Beads, send mail, reserve files, run Cargo, stage files, or change source state.

## Required behavior

- Gather Beads issue state from the local tracker with deterministic ordering and clear degraded codes when Beads is unavailable or parse-invalid.
- Import BV ranking evidence when available, preserving score, action hint, and blocked-by fields without depending on the BV TUI.
- Include Agent Mail active-agent and reservation summaries when available, with no message bodies in the output.
- Include git dirty path summaries by bucket, but do not read secret file contents.
- Include RCH posture: workers healthy, slots available, queue depth, stale/failing-worker warnings, and remote-required policy hints.
- Include local environment facts relevant to safe work, including external Cargo target/TMPDIR posture and disk-pressure signals.

## Acceptance

- Versioned JSON schema and golden fixture exist for clean, dirty, degraded-Beads, degraded-Mail, and saturated-RCH snapshots.
- Deterministic ordering is covered by a unit or contract test.
- Public output uses the normal response envelope and stdout remains machine data only.
- Degraded codes have fixture catalog entries.
- No local Cargo verification; Rust checks/tests are RCH-only.

title: SWA2: conflict-free slice ranking with suggested reservations
description:
## Background

The allocator is valuable only if it turns raw state into concrete non-conflicting slices. Today agents manually infer which file lanes are dirty, recently mailed, or reserved. This child defines the ranking model that produces actionable recommendations without taking action automatically.

## Scope

Given the SWA1 snapshot, rank candidate beads and produce recommended work slices with reason codes, confidence, suggested file reservations, and conflict explanations.

## Required behavior

- Prefer unblocked, unclaimed, high-impact beads from `br ready --json` and BV robot evidence.
- Penalize candidates with dirty files, active exclusive reservations, recent active assignee work, or RCH needs when RCH is saturated.
- Emit `suggestedReservations[]` as path globs plus reasons, but never call Agent Mail reservation APIs.
- Emit `doNotTakeBecause[]` with concrete blockers for candidates that look attractive but are unsafe.
- Keep ordering deterministic: score, priority, issue id, then title as final tiebreakers.
- Include a no-action recommendation when all safe work is blocked, with explicit unblock suggestions.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests cover clean candidate, reserved-file penalty, dirty-path penalty, active-agent penalty, RCH-saturated penalty, and deterministic ties.
- Golden output covers a three-agent dirty checkout where recommendations are non-overlapping.
- The ranking model is documented in comments or docs with enough detail for future agents to audit score changes.
- No mutation: tests prove the command does not create reservations, comments, Beads updates, Git index changes, or files.

title: SWA3: stale in-progress classifier and reopen proposal evidence
description:
## Background

The user explicitly asked agents to find beads that are marked in-progress by long-dead agents with no recent work and reopen them. Doing that safely requires evidence, not guesswork. This child defines a read-only stale-work classifier and proposal format.

## Scope

Detect stale in-progress beads and emit proposals such as `reopenSuggested`, `contactSuggested`, or `leaveAloneActive`, with evidence fields. The first version must not reopen anything automatically.

## Evidence inputs

- Bead status, assignee, updated_at, comments, and dependency state.
- Agent Mail profile last_active timestamps and recent thread messages when available.
- File reservations still active for the bead or known file surface.
- Git commits/comments referencing the bead when cheaply available.

## Required behavior

- Treat recent activity, active reservations, or recent mail as active work.
- Treat missing Agent Mail as degraded, not as evidence an agent is dead.
- Require multiple stale signals before `reopenSuggested`.
- Produce exact suggested `br reopen`/`br update` commands as strings, but do not execute them.
- Include caveats when tracker timestamps are stale because JSONL/DB sync is degraded.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests cover active assignee, stale assignee, missing mail, active reservation, recent comment, and blocked-parent cases.
- Golden output shows at least three stale-work classifications with evidence.
- Logged e2e uses synthetic Beads/Mail fixtures and proves no tracker mutation occurs.
- Degraded fixtures cover Agent Mail unavailable and Beads parse-invalid cases.

title: SWA4: RCH and dirty-checkout lane planner for remote-only verification
description:
## Background

In this repo, heavy Rust verification must use RCH, while shared checkouts often have dirty peer files and saturated workers. Agents need a planner that separates source-edit slices, static-only slices, dry-run proof slices, and RCH-heavy verifier slices before they collide.

## Scope

Extend the next-action output with verification lane advice derived from RCH posture, dirty tracked paths, file reservations, and bead requirements.

## Required behavior

- Classify recommendations into lanes such as `source_only_static_checks`, `docs_or_tracker_only`, `rch_required_wait_or_queue`, `blocked_by_dirty_checkout`, and `environment_remediation`.
- Surface when RCH is saturated, when workers are unhealthy, when requested-worker routing appears ignored, and when remote ENOSPC is a blocker.
- Explain why local Cargo is forbidden in the recommendation when remote-only policy applies.
- Suggest safe non-Cargo checks for narrow slices: rustfmt check, git diff --check, shellcheck/bash -n, schema validation, or dry-run wrappers.
- Link to existing RCH-clean/verification broker beads instead of duplicating their implementation.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests cover healthy slots, saturated slots, worker ENOSPC, dirty tracked source, scratch-only dirty checkout, and RCH unavailable.
- Golden output includes a saturated-RCH shared checkout and shows useful non-Cargo work instead of stalling.
- No command launched by the surface runs Cargo, RCH, Git staging, Git reset, stash, checkout, clean, or worktree operations.
- Degraded-code fixtures cover RCH unavailable, RCH saturated, and dirty-checkout attribution uncertainty.

title: SWA4.a: RCH head-of-line convoy posture for next-action planning
description:
## IdeaWizard grounding

Phase 1 read-through and Phase 4 overlap check found the broad SWA4 lane-planner bead already covers saturated RCH, unhealthy workers, ENOSPC, dirty checkouts, and non-Cargo fallback advice. This child is intentionally narrower: the live May 18, 2026 blocker is a queue convoy where RCH has a healthy worker and some available slots, but the queue head requires more slots than are currently free because an old active build is holding slots.

## Problem

Current RCH posture can be misleading if agents only see workers_healthy > 0 or slots_available > 0. In the observed case, trj was healthy with 2/4 slots available, while an active 22h-old build held 2 slots and queued jobs needed 4 slots each. Additional remote bench attempts would only pile onto the queue and duplicate verifier work.

## Scope

Extend the swarm next-action RCH/verification lane planner so it can identify and explain head-of-line queue convoy conditions without mutating RCH state.

Required behavior:

- Derive queue_head_slots_needed, slots_available, active_remote_build_count, active_build_max_age_seconds, queued_build_count, and a boolean/evidence-backed head_of_line_blocked state from RCH posture when available.
- Distinguish normal saturation (0 free slots) from convoy blocking (some free slots, but not enough for the queue head) and from unhealthy-worker or ENOSPC cases.
- Recommend source-only/static-check work or wait/coordinate when convoy-blocked; do not recommend launching another heavy RCH job unless it can fit available slots and is not duplicative.
- Surface stale-active-build evidence as a proposal-only remediation hint. The command must never cancel, drain, restart, or delete anything.
- Preserve deterministic ordering and stable JSON field names in ee.swarm_next_action.v1 or the next schema version if the field addition requires one.

## Acceptance

- Unit/golden fixtures cover healthy idle RCH, fully saturated slots, convoy-blocked queue head, old active build with free-but-insufficient slots, and no RCH data.
- Output includes enough evidence for an agent to explain why it did not queue another remote bench.
- No command launched by this surface runs Cargo, RCH jobs, git staging/reset/stash/checkout/clean/worktree, or destructive cleanup.
- Rust verification, if run, uses RCH only; otherwise record the RCH blocker and rely on non-Cargo static checks.

title: SWA4.b: orphaned RCH queued-verifier detection and cleanup guidance
description:
## IdeaWizard grounding

This follow-up comes from the same live May 18, 2026 RCH convoy evidence as bd-3vwx0.4.1, but covers a distinct operator gap. After a remote-required verifier wrapper was killed to prevent local fallback, the daemon-side queued job remained visible in `rch status` as job 120. The public `rch cancel 120 --dry-run` command reported no active cancelable build, so agents had no safe way to remove their own queued verifier entry.

## Problem

In crowded shared checkouts, agents sometimes stop local verifier wrappers when RCH queues or stalls. If the daemon keeps a queued copy, the queue can accumulate stale verifier work. Current next-action and RCH-proof surfaces do not clearly identify whether a queued job is still attached to a live wrapper, who owns it, or what safe cleanup guidance exists.

## Scope

Extend the swarm next-action / RCH lane-planner diagnostics so orphaned queued verifier entries are visible and actionable without mutating RCH state.

Required behavior:

- Detect queued RCH jobs whose command/bead attribution appears to match the current agent or current bead, while no corresponding local wrapper process is running.

## Acceptance

- Unit/golden fixtures cover active build, queued live-wrapper build, queued orphaned build, and no RCH queue.

title: SWA4.c: queueing-theoretic RCH admission certificates for next-action
description:
## Alien-artifact grounding

The live May 18, 2026 RCH incident gives a clear failure signature: agents can see a healthy worker and an open queue, but repeated remote-required verifier launches become harmful when a long-running active build holds slots, queue heads need more slots than are free, and stale queued verifier copies remain after local wrappers stop.

Using the alien-artifact-coding discipline, this bead does not propose another implementation optimization. It compiles queueing theory and control-policy rigor into an auditable recommendation certificate for the existing SWA4 RCH lane planner.

## Goal

Extend the swarm next-action RCH lane advice with a deterministic admission-control certificate that explains whether an agent should queue a verifier, wait/coordinate, or take source-only/static work.

## Scope

- Define a finite-capacity queue model over RCH posture: active slots, queued jobs, queue-head slots needed, job age, estimated service class, duplicate command/bead attribution, and stale-orphan evidence.
- Emit a compact certificate in the next-action JSON, for example action = queue | wait | static_work | coordinate, with evidence fields, assumptions, and rule ids.
- Prove monotonic safety properties in tests: adding queue pressure cannot make the recommendation more aggressive; duplicate same-bead verifier evidence suppresses another queue recommendation; missing RCH data degrades to conservative static/coordinate advice.
- Include fairness/starvation assumptions explicitly. Old active builds may trigger remediation hints, but the surface must remain proposal-only and must not cancel, kill, drain, restart, delete, or mutate RCH state.
- Keep the certificate advisory and redaction-safe; command text may be summarized or hashed when needed.

## Acceptance

- Unit fixtures cover idle capacity, full saturation, head-of-line convoy, duplicate queued verifier, orphaned queued verifier, missing RCH data, and stale active build evidence.
- Golden output demonstrates the certificate for the live-style convoy: healthy worker, zero or insufficient free slots, long-running active job, queued verifier copies, and recommendation to avoid launching another duplicate verifier.
- Property-style or table-driven tests cover monotonicity, duplicate suppression, deterministic ordering, and conservative behavior under unknown data.
- Docs or schema comments define the assumptions ledger, proof obligations, and fallback policy in agent-readable terms.
- No command launched by this surface runs Cargo, RCH jobs, git staging/reset/stash/checkout/clean/worktree, or destructive cleanup.
- Rust verification, if run, uses RCH only; if RCH is blocked, record that blocker and use non-Cargo static/schema checks.

## Non-goals

No production RCH scheduler, no daemon mutation, no queue cancellation, no OS process control, no local Cargo fallback, and no replacement for Beads/BV/Agent Mail/RCH.

title: SWA4.d: robust RCH service-time estimator for admission certificates
description:
## Alien-graveyard grounding

This comes from the alien-graveyard workflow applied to the live RCH queue/verification bottleneck. The matched primitives are §0.8 runtime decision core, §0.10/0.15 statistical benchmarking and tail-latency decomposition, §10.3 learning-augmented online algorithms with robust fallback, and §12.1 conformal calibration.

The point is not to make `ee` schedule RCH jobs. The point is to give the existing SWA4 next-action planner a calibrated service-time/queue-risk estimate that can feed the admission certificate from bd-3vwx0.4.3.

## Goal

Add a testable design and implementation path for estimating RCH verifier service time and queue-risk classes from historical evidence, with a classical conservative fallback when predictions are absent, stale, or miscalibrated.

## Scope

- Define evidence features from RCH posture and prior verifier records: command family, test target, requested slots, observed duration, failure class, queue wait, worker id/class, dirty-checkout attribution, and duplicate/bead attribution.
- Define output fields for the next-action snapshot/admission certificate: serviceTimeClass, serviceTimeIntervalMs, queueRiskClass, predictorCoverage, predictorMode = learned | calibrated | fallback, and conservativeReason when applicable.
- Use a robust baseline first: static command-family buckets plus empirical quantiles. Only use learned estimates when calibration coverage is healthy.
- Add conformal or split-calibration coverage checks for duration intervals, plus an anytime/regret-style harm monitor that falls back to the static policy if prediction error or regret drifts.
- Ensure missing, sparse, or privacy-redacted evidence produces conservative wait/static_work/coordinate advice, not optimistic queue advice.

## Acceptance

- Unit fixtures cover enough-history, sparse-history, missing-history, stale-history, heavy-tailed duration, miscalibrated predictor, and duplicate queued verifier scenarios.
- Golden output shows serviceTimeIntervalMs and queueRiskClass feeding the bd-3vwx0.4.3 admission certificate without changing the no-mutation contract.
- Property/table tests prove monotonic fallback: worse calibration, wider tails, or more queue pressure cannot make recommendations more aggressive.
- A benchmark/profiling note records that estimator overhead is bounded and separately attributed from Beads/BV/Mail/git/RCH collection time.
- Docs/schema comments include the assumptions ledger, coverage ledger, fallback triggers, and rejection criteria for enabling learned mode.
- No command launched by this surface runs Cargo, RCH jobs, git staging/reset/stash/checkout/clean/worktree, or destructive cleanup.
- Rust verification, if run, uses RCH only; if RCH is unavailable, record blocker and rely on non-Cargo schema/static checks.

## Non-goals

No autonomous RCH scheduling, no queue cancellation, no daemon mutation, no ML dependency requirement, no cloud service, and no learned-mode default before calibration evidence exists.

title: SWA5: duplicate-work and verification-reuse hooks in next-action output
description:
## Background

The backlog already includes verification reuse and duplicate-work detector ideas. The allocator should not reimplement those systems, but it should expose enough hooks that agents can avoid re-running tests, taking duplicate beads, or re-auditing evidence that another agent just produced.

## Scope

Add optional evidence fields to next-action recommendations that point to recent equivalent verification, active queued RCH jobs, recent closeout mail, related Beads comments, and duplicate-work warnings.

## Required behavior

- Detect recent RCH commands with matching command hash or same focused test target when available.
- Detect recent Agent Mail closeouts for the same bead or file surface without including message bodies unless explicitly requested by a future command.
- Detect open beads with overlapping title/labels/file-surface hints and recommend coordination before duplicate implementation.
- Link to `bd-1zb7k.15`, `bd-6boyo`, and `bd-1zb7k.17.4` as upstream/downstream integration points instead of duplicating their ledgers.
- Keep all evidence best-effort and degraded when data is unavailable.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests cover exact command-hash reuse, same test target but different env, recent mail closeout, overlapping bead label/title, and unavailable evidence providers.
- Golden output shows a recommendation changed from `run_test` to `reuse_recent_evidence` when a matching remote pass exists.
- Public schema documents evidence freshness and uncertainty.
- No automatic Beads closure or verification claim is made from proxy evidence alone.

title: SWA6: no-mock multi-agent next-action e2e, docs, and release gate
description:
## Background

A work allocator is dangerous if it looks plausible but silently misses conflicts. The final child must prove the public surface works in a realistic shared-checkout scenario and that docs teach agents how to consume it without handing control of the agent loop to ee.

## Scope

Add no-mock logged e2e coverage, golden fixtures, schema drift checks, docs, and help text for the swarm next-action surface.

## Required e2e scenario

Create an isolated fixture with at least three synthetic agents, overlapping Beads candidates, active file reservations, dirty tracked files, scratch-only files, saturated RCH posture, and at least one stale in-progress bead. Run the public command for each synthetic agent identity and assert:

- each receives a deterministic recommendation list;
- top recommendations do not overlap on exclusive file surfaces;
- stale-work proposals include evidence and do not mutate tracker state;
- RCH-heavy work is lane-classified appropriately when workers are saturated;
- stdout is schema-valid machine JSON and diagnostics go to stderr/log artifacts.

## Docs

Document the command in agent-facing docs with examples for: normal next action, all work blocked, stale-work proposal, RCH saturated, Agent Mail unavailable, Beads parse-invalid, and dirty shared checkout.

## Acceptance

- Logged e2e script records command, cwd, sanitized env, synthetic agent, input fixture hashes, stdout/stderr artifacts, elapsed time, exit code, schema validation, recommendation IDs, overlap checks, mutation checks, and first-failure diagnosis.
- Golden fixtures pin clean and dirty output shapes.

- Docs and `--help` examples are updated.

title: SWA7: profile-first next-action latency and isomorphism harness
description:
## Extreme-software-optimization grounding

The optimization rule is profile first, prove behavior unchanged, one lever at a time. The live RCH queue is currently saturated, so this bead does not propose an implementation optimization. It creates the measurement and proof harness future optimizers need before changing the swarm next-action hot path.

## Problem

The SWA planner will combine Beads, BV, Agent Mail reservations, git dirty state, RCH posture, stale-work evidence, and duplicate-work signals. That is exactly the kind of operator surface that can become slow under a 2k+ bead graph and dozens of agents. Existing SWA6 no-mock e2e proves correctness and mutation safety, but it does not require profile attribution, p50/p95/p99 latency budgets, or isomorphism proofs for future optimization changes.

## Scope

Add a profile-first performance harness for the swarm next-action surface after the SWA1 schema/snapshot exists. This is a test/measurement bead, not an optimization implementation bead.

Required behavior:

- Define canonical benchmark fixtures for clean, dirty shared checkout, saturated RCH, queue-convoy, unavailable Agent Mail, and large Beads graph scenarios.
- Capture baseline latency distributions with p50/p95/p99 and input fixture hashes. Prefer lightweight command timing for normal CI and an opt-in heavier profiling mode for flamegraph/allocation evidence.
- Preserve behavior with isomorphism proofs: recommendation ordering, tie-breaking, degraded[] entries, redaction, and mutation-free guarantees must match golden checksums before and after any optimization.
- Produce an opportunity matrix for any proposed hot-path change: hotspot, impact, confidence, effort, score, and proof plan. No implementation should proceed unless score >= 2.0 and behavior proof is available.
- Keep all Cargo/build/profiling work remote-only through RCH or an explicitly documented remote profiler path. Do not run local Cargo, local flamegraph, or heavy CPU profiling on this Mac.
- Do not duplicate SWA6 e2e assertions; reuse or reference its fixtures where possible and add performance/profiling artifacts on top.

## Acceptance

- A benchmark/profile script or contract test records command, cwd, sanitized env, fixture hashes, elapsed p50/p95/p99, stdout/stderr artifact paths, schema validation result, output hash, and first-failure diagnosis.
- Golden/isomorphism checks prove byte-stable JSON for each fixture before and after a no-op run.
- A documented latency budget exists for the initial surface and separately attributes Beads/BV/Mail/git/RCH phases where the implementation can expose timings.
- An opt-in profile mode records enough evidence to identify top-5 hotspots without changing stdout machine data.
- Docs explain that this bead authorizes measurement only; optimization implementation requires a separate bead naming the single lever and behavior proof.
- All Rust/Cargo verification uses RCH only; if RCH is blocked, record the blocker and rely on non-Cargo static/schema checks.

title: SWA8: compile-blocker preflight for shared-checkout RCH proofs
description:
## IdeaWizard grounding

Phase 1 reality check: the live checkout on 2026-05-18 shows a repeated swarm failure mode that is not fully covered by the existing clean-tree verifier (`bd-9ygik`), workspace hygiene (`bd-1eq3l`), verification broker (`bd-6boyo`), or next-action planner (`bd-3vwx0`). Several agents had useful narrow source slices ready, but their RCH-only Cargo proofs failed before their own tests because another active lane had compile-breaking edits in a shared Rust module. Concrete current example: `bd-wp5ac.5` audit-lane property proof and `bd-ov09.5` PPR proof both reached `trj` but failed on SapphireElk's reserved WAL checkpoint work in `src/db/mod.rs` (`WalCheckpointMode` / DB execute errors). The existing verifier honestly reports `live_dirty_checkout`, but it still spends a remote slot and minutes discovering a peer-lane compiler error.

Phase 2 30-to-5 winnow summary: considered (1) compile-blocker preflight for shared checkout proofs, (2) Cargo target-specific dependency closure prediction, (3) per-agent compile-health broadcast, (4) automatic owner ping for first-error reserved files, and (5) RCH queue admission based on dirty compile-critical paths. The best idea is a read-only compile-blocker preflight because it directly saves scarce RCH capacity without adding mutation or scheduler complexity.

Phase 3 next-best-10 overlap check: verification reuse, clean-tree proof, workspace hygiene, stale-work classification, RCH worker health, and duplicate-work detection already exist as beads. This bead is intentionally narrow: it composes those surfaces to answer one question before a remote Cargo launch: "Will this verifier likely fail because a dirty/reserved compile-critical file outside my slice currently breaks the crate?"

## Problem

In the single canonical checkout, any Rust compile error in `src/db/mod.rs`, `src/cli/mod.rs`, `src/core/status.rs`, or another shared module can make unrelated focused tests fail before they reach their target assertions. Agents then burn RCH slots, record noisy proof comments, and cannot distinguish "my code failed" from "peer lane has an active compiler blocker" until after the remote run.

## Goal

Add a read-only planning/check surface inside the `bd-3vwx0` next-action family that can be called before RCH-heavy verification. Tentative surface: `ee swarm next-action --include-compile-blockers --json` or a helper used by that command. It should inspect git dirty state, active Agent Mail reservations, recent Beads/Mail proof failures, and first-error file paths from recent verifier JSON, then emit a deterministic recommendation:

- safeToLaunchRch: true/false/unknown
- compileBlockers[] with file path, owning reservation/agent, recent first_error evidence, affected command kinds, and suggested next action
- recommendedAlternativeWork[] such as static checks, docs checks, fake-RCH tests, or waiting for the owning agent
- mailTemplate for a concise owner ping when the blocker is active and reserved

## Non-goals and guardrails

No automatic cancellation, staging, unstaging, file edits, Beads mutation, worker disabling, branch/worktree/stash/reset/checkout, or local Cargo fallback. The surface recommends and explains only. It must not read or expose secret contents. It must degrade cleanly when Agent Mail or recent verifier evidence is unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- Deterministic JSON schema, e.g. `ee.swarm_compile_blockers.v1`, with stable ordering by severity, reserved-owner recency, and path.
- Unit tests cover clean checkout, dirty unreserved Rust file, dirty reserved Rust file, stale expired reservation, first-error file matching current dirty path, first-error file unrelated to requested command, and unavailable Agent Mail.
- Contract/golden tests prove the current style of failure is represented: audit-lane/PPR verifier command blocked by reserved `src/db/mod.rs` first-error evidence should recommend deferring RCH and messaging the owner rather than launching another remote Cargo run.
- No-mock e2e uses fake verifier JSON and a temporary git repo; it emits `ee.test_event.v1` logs and proves no files are mutated.
- Integration with `bd-3vwx0` next-action output marks affected work items as `blockedByCompileHealth` and proposes non-overlapping alternatives instead of returning no actionable item.
- RCH-only focused Cargo proof is required for any Rust implementation tests; if RCH is blocked by the very condition being detected, record the improved preflight proof and keep closure caveated.

## Phase 6 refinement notes

Do not build a second workspace hygiene classifier or a second RCH verifier. Reuse the hygiene dirty-path classifier, Agent Mail reservation overlay, and `ee.rch.verify.v1` proof fields. Keep the first implementation slice small: parse existing verifier JSON and reservation snapshots first; only later add deeper Cargo dependency-closure inference if evidence shows it is needed.

title: SWA9: recommendation provenance and overlap-decision cards for next-action
description:
## IdeaWizard grounding

Phase 1 refreshed AGENTS.md and README.md hashes, live Beads/BV state, Agent Mail, RCH status, and alien-graveyard candidate space. The top obvious ideas were already covered by existing beads: stale-work proposals in bd-3vwx0.3, RCH lane planning in bd-3vwx0.4, duplicate-work hooks in bd-3vwx0.5, no-mock e2e in bd-3vwx0.6, and profile/isomorphism in bd-3vwx0.7. Searches for recommendation provenance, recommendation evidence ledger, IdeaWizard overlap, EV score, and planning evidence found no existing bead for structured recommendation rationale.

## Problem

Repeated IdeaWizard and alien-graveyard passes produce useful planning evidence, but that evidence is mostly prose in comments or mail. The future ee swarm next-action surface needs a compact, deterministic way to explain why a recommendation exists before an agent acts on it or creates more tracker work. Without a structured provenance card, agents can duplicate ideas, over-trust weak overlap searches, or hide proof obligations behind a plausible recommendation.

## Scope

Add recommendation-provenance and overlap-decision cards to the SWA next-action design. Each recommendation should be able to carry: candidate source, candidate summary, score inputs, EV or relevance score, overlap search queries, matched existing beads, rejected duplicate reasons, selected parent or child relation, required proof artifacts, RCH and dirty-checkout caveats, confidence, and fallback/no-op decision.

This is an explainability and safety surface, not an optimizer implementation and not a Beads mutator. It should compose with bd-3vwx0.5 duplicate-work hooks and bd-3vwx0.7 profile/isomorphism evidence rather than duplicating them.

## Required behavior

- Emit deterministic card ordering and stable field names under the eventual ee.swarm_next_action.v1 schema or a documented child schema.
- Preserve redaction: no raw mail bodies, secret-like path contents, raw prompts, or unbounded command output.
- Represent overlap decisions explicitly: new_bead_recommended, refine_existing_bead, duplicate_rejected, blocked_by_owner, and no_action_recommended.
- Include proof obligations and verification lane hints without claiming tests passed from proxy evidence alone.
- Treat missing Beads, Agent Mail, BV, or RCH evidence as degraded uncertainty, not as proof of absence.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests cover duplicate-rejected, refine-existing, net-new child recommendation, missing evidence provider, and dirty-checkout caveat cards.
- Golden output shows at least three recommendation cards with overlap queries, existing bead hits, selected decision, proof obligations, and confidence.
- Logged e2e fixture proves a repeated IdeaWizard pass recommends refining an existing SWA bead instead of creating a duplicate.
- Schema/docs explain how agents should cite recommendation cards in Beads comments or handoffs.
- No automatic Beads creation, reopening, assignment, branch creation, worktree creation, local Cargo, deletion, stash, reset, checkout, or source mutation occurs from this surface.

title: SECURITY: audit details are rendered as raw JSON and can poison JSON and TOON output
description: Audit details are stored as arbitrary text via CreateAuditInput with no JSON validation (src/db/mod.rs:6401, src/db/mod.rs:6425, src/db/mod.rs:6439). JSONL import forwards imported memory.details directly into audit rows (src/core/jsonl_import.rs:415, src/core/jsonl_import.rs:423), and tombstone audit details manually interpolate the reason string into JSON without escaping (src/db/mod.rs:6646). Memory history JSON then inserts details with JsonBuilder.field_raw (src/output/mod.rs:3539, src/output/mod.rs:3540), and the TOON renderer derives from that JSON (src/output/mod.rs:3597). A crafted import or reason can invalidate machine JSON, inject forged fields into details, or force TOON into the encoding error path. Expected fix: store audit details as serde_json::Value or validate on insert, escape tombstone reason through serde_json::json!, and render unknown detail text as a string rather than raw JSON.
close_reason: Fixed audit detail rendering in memory history JSON/TOON; malformed details are emitted as escaped JSON strings and valid detail JSON remains structured. Added malicious payload regression tests.

title: [beads] Make verification scripts honor Beads write/sync locks
description:
Finding from deadlock-finder-and-fixer audit.

Evidence:
- AGENTS.md:657-660 and AGENTS.md:957-969 require frequent br close/create plus br sync --flush-only during swarm sessions.
- scripts/closure-lint.sh:21 and scripts/closure-lint.sh:91-130 read .beads/issues.jsonl directly with jq.

- Add a stress test that loops br sync while running closure-lint/drift/vision readers and proves the readers see a complete, parseable, current snapshot.

title: Reality-Check Bridge Plan: Stream 1 — Performance proof via criterion benches
description:
Epic from /reality-check-for-project audit (2026-05-01).

Background — what changed and why:
The comprehensive plan §28 specifies p50/p99 latency targets for 14 operations and explicitly says "These become criterion benchmarks under benches/. CI fails on regression > 30% from the moving baseline." The reality check found: there is no benches/ directory, there is no [[bench]] entry in Cargo.toml, and there is no bead anywhere covering this work. This is a clear NO_BEAD vision gap: the README touts performance numbers but they are unprovable. Fixing this gap proves we mean what we say in the README and lets us catch regressions before users see them.

Vision being delivered:
README's Performance section (e.g. p50 8 ms remember, 38 ms hybrid search, 95 ms context pack at 4k tokens) becomes verifiable on every PR.

Scope (children must cover all of):
1. Add benches/ directory with criterion harness (one bench file per category): remember.rs, search.rs, context.rs, why.rs, link.rs, graph_pagerank.rs, curate_candidates.rs, outcome.rs, import_cass.rs, status.rs.
2. Each bench seeds a deterministic in-memory FrankenSQLite DB + hash embedder, runs the operation 100x with criterion, and captures a stable JSON baseline.
3. Versioned baselines under benches/baselines/v0.<minor>.json keyed by operation. Move baseline forward only when explicit `--bless`-style update is requested.
4. CI step that compiles benches and runs `cargo bench --bench *` in profile mode that aborts on >30% regression vs baseline.
5. New CLI surface: `ee bench --json [--operation <name>]` that runs the in-process harness without criterion (cheap signal for release prep).
6. Unit tests verifying every plan-§28 row has a matching bench file, and that the moving-baseline rule is enforced.

Acceptance:
- benches/ exists; cargo bench --workspace builds and runs locally; CI gate runs in <5 min on a typical PR; baselines committed; ee bench --json passes the walking-skeleton smoke; README "Performance" table is generated from the baseline JSON to keep prose and reality aligned.

Dependencies considered:
None blocking. Can run in parallel with other streams. Should NOT be blocked by gate readiness chores; this IS one of them in spirit but is not currently filed.

Why this matters more than it sounds:
Without benches we cannot honestly call any release production-ready, and we cannot tell whether feature additions are silently regressing the headline UX (context-pack latency in particular). Performance honesty is a North Star principle of "Deterministic by default" combined with "Local-first" — slow local memory destroys the whole pitch.

title: [hardening] MCP argument helpers assume non-empty names slice
description:
**File:** src/mcp.rs:876-944

**Defect:** All MCP argument parsing helper functions (`required_string`, `optional_string`, `optional_bool`, `optional_u32`, etc.) access `names[0]` without checking if the slice is empty. If a caller passes an empty `names` slice, the function panics with index-out-of-bounds.

**Observable:** Panic: "index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0"

**Repro:**
```rust
let args = serde_json::json!({});
required_string(&args, &[]); // panics
```

**Fix:** Add debug_assert or guard at function entry:
```rust
debug_assert!(!names.is_empty(), "names must not be empty");
// or
let primary_name = names.first().unwrap_or(&"<unknown>");
```

This is defensive hardening - current callers always pass non-empty slices, but the API contract is implicit.
close_reason: Implemented in 3c77819d: MCP argument and URI query helper name lists now return stable String errors when empty; added mcp feature regression coverage; verified focused mcp tests, check, and clippy.

title: HIGH: MMR drops unrelated untagged memories sharing coarse diversity keys
description: Review finding in src/pack/mod.rs and src/core/context.rs. candidate_similarity returns 1.0 whenever diversity_key strings match, and is_redundant drops any candidate with max similarity >= 1.0. diversity_key_for_memory defaults untagged memories to level:kind:untagged, so two unrelated untagged procedural rules become exact duplicates. Repro: create two distinct untagged procedural/rule memories that both match a query; after one is selected, the other is omitted as redundant_candidate purely by coarse key. Expected: exact redundancy should require same memory/source/content, or coarse keys should only penalize diversity, not hard-drop.
close_reason: candidate_similarity uses content_overlap_similarity + diversity_key boost (0.5-0.95) instead of diversity_key alone → 1.0; regression tests prove unrelated memories with same tag are no longer dropped

title: [perf] Facility-location marginal gain is O(n²) per selection
description:
**File:** src/pack/mod.rs:2043-2053

**Bottleneck:** The facility-location algorithm computes marginal gain by iterating the entire universe for each remaining candidate:

```rust
let marginal_gain: f32 = universe.iter()
    .zip(current_coverages.iter())
    .map(|(universe_profile, &current_coverage)| {
        let candidate_sim = facility_signature_similarity(...);
        ...
    })
    .sum();
```

With n candidates, each of k selection rounds does O(remaining × universe) work → O(n³) worst case.

**Impact:** Submodular profile pack assembly scales poorly beyond ~50 candidates. Benchmark shows variance at scale.

**Mitigation options:**
1. **Lazy evaluation:** Cache similarity matrix once, update incrementally
2. **Approximation:** Sample universe for marginal gain estimates
3. **Early termination:** Stop when remaining candidates have low potential gain

**Note:** This is inherent to facility-location greedy. Consider documenting complexity tradeoffs vs MMR profile.
close_reason: Facility-location selection now uses lazy priority-queue exact greedy ordering; 128-candidate bench legacy 2251.379ms and 8256 marginal evaluations vs lazy 161.983ms and 381 marginal evaluations; focused parity and evaluation-count tests pass

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Affected sites (all introduced in zudw/tof3/dkuo/6rmv hardening pushes):
- src/pack/mod.rs RateDistortionReport::to_json — ends with serde_json::to_string(&json_repr).unwrap_or_else(|_| "{}".to_owned())
- src/pack/mod.rs SectionBudgetReport::to_json — same pattern
- src/curate/mod.rs FeedbackHealthSummary::to_json — same pattern (introduced by 6rmv)
- src/curate/mod.rs QuarantinedFeedback::to_json — same pattern (1f8f7e8)
- src/curate/mod.rs ProtectedRuleStatus::to_json — same pattern (0b70784)

The structs being serialized contain only String, u32, u64, f64, Option<String>, and bool — none of which can fail to serialize via serde_json. The unwrap_or_else fallback is dead code, but if a future refactor adds a non-Serializable field (e.g. a custom type with a fallible Serialize impl), the to_json output silently degrades to '{}' — a wire-shape that downstream parsers will accept as a valid empty object and proceed with NO indication that the schema invariant was violated.

Fix: replace .unwrap_or_else(|_| "{}".to_owned()) with .expect("<TypeName> JSON must serialize"). This preserves no-panic behavior for the today-known-impossible case (because the assertion holds) while making schema regressions audible. Alternative: make to_json return Result<String, serde_json::Error> and force callers to handle.

title: [HIGH] V031 migration version reused: learning_observations renumbered to V033 in 237dbe2 after 1ceba15 published it
description:
Repro:
  1. Check out commit 1ceba15 (`feat(learn): persist active learning observations`).
  2. Run any test that initializes a DbConnection, e.g. `cargo test --test recorder_persistence`. The DB applies V031_LEARNING_OBSERVATIONS and stores its blake3 hash in `ee_schema_migrations`.
  3. Pull commit 237dbe2 (`feat: wave-3 surface implementations`). V031 is now V031_CERTIFICATES_AND_TRUST_QUARANTINE; learning observations are renumbered to V033.
  4. Re-run any test against the same DB.

Expected: migrations apply cleanly OR the framework refuses with a clear "migration version reused" error.

Actual: the framework runs validate_applied_migrations on the existing rows and either (a) silently re-applies V031's certificates DDL on top of an already-V031'd DB, leaving learning_observations + certificates both at version 31 with mismatched hashes, or (b) panics on hash mismatch.

Evidence-line:
  src/db/mod.rs (HEAD) shows V031_CERTIFICATES_AND_TRUST_QUARANTINE at the slot previously occupied by V031_LEARNING_OBSERVATIONS (which is now V033). Compare:
    git show 1ceba15:src/db/mod.rs  | grep -n V031_LEARNING_OBSERVATIONS
    git show 237dbe2:src/db/mod.rs  | grep -n V031_CERTIFICATES_AND_TRUST_QUARANTINE

Impact: any developer or shared swarm DB that materialized an `.ee/ee.db` between 16:08 UTC and 16:15 UTC on 2026-05-06 cannot upgrade past V031 without a manual migration-table rewrite. Pre-1.0, but the swarm uses shared DBs.

Suggested fix: never reuse a version number after it has been committed. The wave-3 commit (237dbe2) should have appended certificates as V034+ and audit-hash-chain as V035+, leaving V031 as learning_observations forever.
close_reason: Fixed migration version collision by restoring V031 as LEARNING_OBSERVATIONS (original from 1ceba15) and renumbering CERTIFICATES to V032 and AUDIT_HASH_CHAIN to V033. All 17 migration tests pass.

title: EE-USR-001: Define north-star agent outcome scenario matrix
description:
Define the canonical agent outcome scenario matrix that future agents use to judge whether EE is actually useful.

Scope:
- Name the core user journeys and their fixture families.
- For each journey, list command sequence, expected response envelope, evidence IDs, degraded branches, redaction expectations, and success signal.
- Include at least these journeys: pre-task brief, in-task retrieval/recovery, post-task learning, degraded/offline trust, privacy/export, and multi-workspace/session continuity.
- Map each scenario to the implementation beads and readiness gates responsible for making it pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including the comprehensive testing and logging requirements.
design:
Recommended design:
- Treat this as a scenario contract, not prose-only docs. The output should be directly translatable into e2e/golden/eval fixtures.
- Prefer concrete commands and expected JSON field names over vague user stories.
- Include both high-confidence and low-confidence branches so agents learn when to trust EE and when to ask or abstain.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance criteria:

title: SECURITY: update apply invokes tar via PATH during binary installation
description: HIGH. ee update --apply reaches execute_install_plan (src/cli/mod.rs:6177, src/cli/mod.rs:6188) and archive extraction runs Command::new("tar") for tar.xz and tar.gz artifacts (src/core/install.rs:931, src/core/install.rs:951). This avoids shell injection but still resolves tar through PATH while replacing the ee binary after checksum validation. In a compromised workspace or agent environment with attacker-controlled PATH, a fake tar executable can run arbitrary code during installation. Expected fix: avoid PATH lookup by using an in-process archive library or a verified absolute system tar path with restrictive environment handling, plus a unit or integration test with a fake PATH entry.
close_reason: Fixed tar invocation hardening: update apply now resolves only trusted absolute /usr/bin/tar or /bin/tar paths, validates system binary metadata before invoking, clears the child environment to trusted system PATH, and includes a regression test rejecting PATH-style tar candidates.

title: [reliability] Index publish lock retry exhausts without logging attempts
description:
**File:** src/core/index.rs:46-76

**Defect:** The `acquire_index_publish_lock` function retries 200 times with backoff, but doesn't log intermediate attempts. If all attempts fail, the error message only shows the last holder:
```rust
Err(IndexRebuildError::Index(format!(
    "Index publish lock held by {other} since {acquired_at}. Another index operation may be in progress."
)))
```

**Observable:** User sees cryptic error after ~10s of silent waiting with no indication of retry progress. Difficult to diagnose whether the lock is legitimately held vs. stale.

**Repro:**
1. Start a long-running index rebuild
2. In another terminal, start another index rebuild
3. Second one waits silently, then fails with no progress indication

**Fix:** Add tracing at INFO level every ~10 attempts:
```rust
if attempt > 0 && attempt % 10 == 0 {
    tracing::info!(attempt, holder = %other, "waiting for index publish lock...");
}
```

Low severity - rare condition, but poor UX when it occurs.
close_reason: Index publish lock contention reports retry progress and stable JSON error code

Closure summary (cc_2 / WhiteForge): commit 7180dc4 lands tests/e2e_backup_restore_roundtrip.rs (2 tests, both green).

Test 1 backup_then_restore_preserves_every_memory_and_tag: seeds a fresh workspace with 4 memories across 3 levels (procedural, semantic, episodic) and 4 kinds (rule, fact, observation, anti-pattern), each with distinct tags and confidence scores. title: [MEDIUM] hooks: multi-hook install can leave partial mutations on failure
description: src/hooks/installer.rs:353-374 writes each hook as soon as its individual plan item is reached. comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
src/models/decision.rs:366-368 now_rfc3339 uses SecondsFormat::Secs:
```
fn now_rfc3339() -> String {
    Utc::now().to_rfc3339_opts(SecondsFormat::Secs, true)
}
```
The advisory-lock fix in bdab856 explicitly switched to SecondsFormat::Nanos to fix lexical-compare bugs (whole-second '+00:00' strings are lexically GREATER than nanosecond 'Z' strings even when chronologically earlier). DecisionRecord.decided_at is consumed by output/mod.rs:6936/7056/7115 today only as a display string, but the project ships shadow-run comparison code (output/mod.rs:11195+) that builds DecisionRecord pairs and compares them — if any future code path compares decided_at strings lexically (sort, dedupe, ORDER BY when written to ee_decisions table), the same hazard reappears.

Fix: align with the advisory-lock helper. Either:
(a) make all timestamp emitters in src/models go through a single ee_core::time::now_rfc3339() that returns SecondsFormat::Nanos, true, OR
(b) add a regression test that two DecisionRecords built one ms apart sort consistently with their actual chronological order.
Option (a) is the structural fix; (b) is the cheap insurance.

title: [PERF] pack::assemble_facility_location_draft: submodular profile recomputes universe coverage
description:
Path: ee context --profile submodular -> src/core/context.rs:400 assemble_draft_with_profile -> src/pack/mod.rs:1574 assemble_facility_location_draft -> src/pack/mod.rs:1769 select_facility_candidate_index.
Code evidence: src/pack/mod.rs:1583 clones the full candidate universe, src/pack/mod.rs:1596 loops while candidates remain, src/pack/mod.rs:1781 rebuilds current_coverages over the whole universe every selection, src/pack/mod.rs:1795 iterates every remaining candidate, src/pack/mod.rs:1810 iterates the full universe again for each candidate, and src/pack/mod.rs:1841 recomputes facility_location_value over the universe after selection.
Suspected complexity: O(s * (u*selected + c*u*terms + u*selected)) with substantial repeated similarity allocation; worst-case near O(n^3 * terms) for large candidate pools.
Suggested fix: cache per-universe coverage and candidate signatures, update coverage incrementally after selecting a candidate, and reuse normalized term sets instead of rebuilding during facility_similarity.
Verification plan: add a submodular context-pack benchmark at 100/250/500 candidates and compare objective value equality plus p95/allocation count before/after.

title: [implements-surface:preflight] Real ee preflight evidence-matched warnings
description:
## Background

- Closure linter passes.

title: [MEDIUM] ee never sets PRAGMA journal_mode/synchronous — crash safety relies on undocumented FrankenConnection defaults
description:
## Surface
ee SQLite WAL handling under crash (audit cycle 5)

## Finding
`src/db/mod.rs` opens databases via `FrankenConnection::open_file(path)` and only sets `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` (`src/db/mod.rs:744-748`). It never explicitly configures:
- `journal_mode` (rollback vs WAL)
- `synchronous` (FULL/NORMAL/OFF)
- `busy_timeout` (sqlmodel may set this internally; not verified)
- `wal_autocheckpoint`

Verified via `grep journal_mode|WAL|synchronous|busy_timeout src/db/mod.rs src/core/recorder.rs src/core/index.rs src/pack/mod.rs src/core/memory.rs` → only `PRAGMA foreign_keys` appears.

Searched `/data/projects/sqlmodel_rust/crates/sqlmodel-frankensqlite` and `/data/projects/frankensqlite/src` for `journal_mode|WAL|PRAGMA`. The fsqlite-wal crate exists (so WAL is the default storage layout), but ee does not explicitly opt in or pin durability semantics.

## Why it matters
Crash safety of the audit chain (`audit_log`), pack records, and recorder events depends on:
- WAL + `synchronous=NORMAL` is durable across OS crashes if the WAL is fsync'd before commit.
- `synchronous=OFF` is fast but loses tail-of-WAL on crash.
- Rollback journal + `synchronous=FULL` is the SQLite default but ee uses `fsqlite` which may differ.

ee makes strong durability claims (V033 hash chain, V036 append-only triggers) that are only as strong as the underlying durability config. If fsqlite's default is `synchronous=OFF` on a write batch, a crash mid-commit could:
- Truncate the audit chain so `verify_audit` reports a hash mismatch on the partial last block.
- Drop pack-record children but keep the parent (FK violations on next open if foreign_keys was OFF — but ee sets it ON so this would error rather than silently corrupt).

## What I checked
- `with_transaction` uses `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (`src/db/mod.rs:307`) — correct for write contention.
- Per-write file lock via `lock_file_write_owner_gate` — coordinates multiple ee processes.
- No explicit checkpoint / `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint` calls.

## Fix
Either:
A) Add explicit `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL; PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=1000;` in `enable_foreign_key_enforcement` (rename it to `enable_durability_pragmas`), and document the choice in an ADR.
B) Add an `open_durability_check` test that asserts the effective `PRAGMA journal_mode` and `PRAGMA synchronous` values match expectations after `open_file`. This way fsqlite default drift would be caught.

## Note
Not claiming corruption is observable today — the fsqlite default may be safe. The bug is that ee does not state or test what it depends on, so a silent fsqlite default change could regress durability without anyone noticing.
close_reason: Implemented explicit WAL and synchronous=NORMAL pragmas at DB open; rch verification attempted but repo-wide gates are blocked by unrelated dirty work in src/output/mod.rs, src/core/claims.rs, src/core/preflight.rs, and formatting drift outside src/db/mod.rs.

title: [MEDIUM] ee status without --workspace does not inspect the current workspace
description:
Reviewer finding from mixed-swarm pass.

Location: src/cli/mod.rs:4975-4980 dispatches bare ee status to StatusReport::gather(). StatusReport::gather() at src/core/status.rs:715-720 calls gather_with_options(Default), and gather_with_options at src/core/status.rs:733-740 passes None into CapabilityReport::gather_with_workspace and all workspace health probes. CapabilityReport::gather() at src/core/status.rs:494-499 knows how to default to current_dir(), but StatusReport::gather() does not use it.

Impact: in an initialized working directory, ee status --json reports storage/search as not_inspected and asks the user to rerun ee status --workspace . --json instead of reporting real current-workspace capabilities. This regresses the walking skeleton command shape and can hide real DB/index degradation from the default status command.

Suggested fix: make StatusReport::gather() resolve the current workspace consistently with other CLI commands, or have CLI pass current_dir when --workspace is omitted. Add a test with a temp initialized workspace proving bare status inspects that workspace.
close_reason: Fixed: status command now defaults workspace to '.' when --workspace omitted. Updated test assertion to check workspace field is populated.

title: Make diagnostics, jobs, daemon, and adapter status report real capabilities only
description:
## Background

Diagnostic and operations commands are easy places for fake confidence to creep in. `status`, `doctor`, `job`, `daemon`, `analyze science-status`, optional MCP/serve adapters, and capability checks should report real probes, real job rows, real schema/index state, and real degraded capabilities. They should not fill the UX with plausible green checks or future-daemon behavior.

These commands are mechanical and belong in the CLI, but their honesty standard must be as strict as the memory commands because agents will use them to decide whether it is safe to continue.

## Acceptance Criteria

See this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field for the detailed completion contract, including unit/static checks, e2e or docs/e2e coverage, detailed logging, and no-feature-loss requirements.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- `ee doctor/status/job/analyze science-status/daemon` and optional adapter health paths report only real probes, persisted job records, configured capabilities, or explicit unavailable states.
- No command emits a healthy/ready/complete status from hard-coded sample data.
- Every failure/degradation includes stable code, severity, evidence/source, and repair command when one exists.
- MCP/serve adapters, if present, are verified as thin schema-preserving wrappers over CLI/core logic and do not duplicate reasoning.
- Unit tests cover missing DB, migration required, stale index, missing CASS, semantic disabled, graph stale, no job rows, unknown job, daemon unavailable, adapter feature disabled, and JSON error shape.
- E2E scripts log workspace, DB/index generations, capability matrix, job IDs, adapter feature flags, degradation codes, repair commands, stdout/stderr paths, schema/golden status, and first-failure diagnosis.

- check_cass() now calls probe_cass_capability() to detect CASS binary

- capabilities.rs runtime and cass status use probe functions
- Added error codes EE-E505 (RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE), EE-E506-508 (CASS_*)

title: JSONL import accepts blank required header fields
description:

title: G6: Gomory-Hu tree — O(1) pairwise proximity queries on memory_links
description:
# G6 — Gomory-Hu tree: O(1) pairwise proximity queries

## Idea (one-liner)

Pre-compute the Gomory-Hu tree of memory_links — a tree whose path-minimum between any two memories equals the min-cut between them in the original graph. One expensive precompute (~n-1 max-flow calls), then O(1) "how structurally close are these two memories?" queries forever.

## Why this matters

`ee` already commits to one expensive snapshot refresh + cheap reads. Gomory-Hu fits that pattern perfectly. Today, nothing in `ee` answers "are these two memories structurally close, accounting for all paths, not just the shortest?" — Gomory-Hu does, exactly, at O(1) per query post-preprocess.

Two product surfaces benefit:

1. `ee why <id1> <id2>`: "how related are these two memories" — currently no such command exists. The Gomory-Hu min-cut is a principled answer: small min-cut = many disjoint paths connect them = strongly related.

2. `ee context`: when assembling a pack, rank candidate pack-mates by min-cut distance to the seed memory (= structurally close memories). Strictly stronger than degree or single-path distance — multi-edge-disjoint paths is a structural property no other algorithm in `ee` exercises today.

## Algorithm

`fnx_algorithms::gomory_hu_tree_rust(memory_links_undirected)`. Returns a tree (n-1 edges, n nodes) where for any pair (u,v), the path from u to v in the tree contains the edge with minimum weight equal to the min-cut between u and v in the original graph. Storage: O(n).

Compute via Gusfield's algorithm: n-1 calls to max-flow with rotating source/sink. Single-threaded; budget ~2-5 seconds for a 1k-node memory_links graph. Recomputed on snapshot refresh (background job, NOT foreground).

## Output shape

New command `ee proximity <id1> <id2> --json`:

```jsonc
{
  "schema": "ee.proximity.v1",
  "memoryA": "mem_...",
  "memoryB": "mem_...",
  "minCut": 0.42,
  "interpretation": "moderately related",  // <0.2: weak, 0.2-0.6: moderate, >0.6: strong
  "treePath": ["mem_a", "mem_intermediate1", "mem_b"],  // path in the Gomory-Hu tree
  "snapshotVersion": 1234
}
```

Plus `ee context` integration: each pack candidate has a `proximityToSeed: 0.5` field (max over min-cuts to seed memories).

Plus `ee insights --section proximityHotspots`: top-K memory pairs with smallest min-cut (= most-connected pairs).

## Acceptance

- New module `src/graph/gomory_hu.rs` with `build_gomory_hu_tree(graph) -> GomoryHuTree` and `query_min_cut(tree, u, v) -> f64`.
- Gomory-Hu tree stored as part of the memory_links snapshot metadata (serialized via fnx-readwrite). Recomputed on background refresh.
- New `ee proximity` command.
- `ee context` ranks pack candidates by proximity-to-seed when Gomory-Hu tree is fresh.
- `ee insights --section proximityHotspots` lands.
- 6 unit tests + 1 e2e + 1 golden.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: F1, F2 (must be wrapped with timeout — Gomory-Hu is expensive), F4.
Blocks: nothing.
Parent: bd-bife.

## Notes

- Gomory-Hu is undirected min-cut. memory_links is directed; we view it as undirected for proximity (= structural co-citation regardless of direction).
- If the graph is disconnected, Gomory-Hu produces a forest. Min-cut between memories in different components is infinity; surface as `null`.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
## Phase 6 refinement notes — scale + sampling fallback

Gomory-Hu is n-1 max-flow calls. On 1k nodes / ~3k edges, expected build time ~5s (within F2 background budget). On 10k nodes the cost is O(V²·E²) = ~10^14 — hours, not seconds. Need:

1. **Hard scale limit**: If |V| > 2000, Gomory-Hu build is SKIPPED (background job records degraded.large_graph + falls back to ego-graph-based proximity for ee proximity queries).
2. **Sampling option**: F2.b's run_with_sampling can be applied — sample 100 anchor nodes, build Gomory-Hu on the induced subgraph, query against the subgraph (approximate min-cuts). Documents in CGSE witness with sample_size + approximation_error_bound.
3. **Refresh cadence**: Gomory-Hu refreshes nightly, NOT on every memory_link write. Stale tree is fine for proximity queries (queries fall back to legacy degree-distance with degraded.gomory_hu_stale).

Update G6.a accordingly.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
## Round 3 acceptance pinning — error messages

### Error matrix for ee proximity <id1> <id2>
| Condition | Output |
|---|---|
| id1 non-existent | error envelope: {code: 'memory.not_found', target: id1, severity: 'usage_error', exit=2} |
| id2 non-existent | error envelope: {code: 'memory.not_found', target: id2, severity: 'usage_error', exit=2} |
| id1 == id2 | success: {schema: 'ee.proximity.v1', minCut: 0.0, interpretation: 'identical', treePath: [id1]} |
| same component, different cluster | success: {minCut: float, interpretation: 'weak|moderate|strong', treePath: [...]} |
| different components | success: {minCut: null, interpretation: 'disconnected', treePath: null, degraded: [code: 'graph.proximity.unreachable']} |
| Gomory-Hu tree stale (|V| changed by >10% since build) | success: {minCut: float, interpretation, treePath, degraded: [code: 'graph.gomory_hu.stale']} |
| Workspace too small (|V| < 3) | error: {code: 'graph.proximity.workspace_too_small', repair: 'remember more memories', severity: 'usage_error'} |
| Gomory-Hu skipped (|V| > 2000) | success: {minCut: <approximation>, ...degraded: [code: 'graph.gomory_hu.large_graph', repair: 'enable graph.feature.gomory_hu.force_compute']} |

### Interpretation thresholds (configurable per RX5)
- minCut < 0.2: 'weak'
- 0.2 ≤ minCut < 0.6: 'moderate'
- minCut ≥ 0.6: 'strong'
- minCut == 0: handled separately (identical or disconnected)

### G6.d test cases
- Each row in the error matrix is a test case.
- Plus: G6.d also tests the proximityToSeed field in ee context output.

title: [HIGH] db: unsafe i64→u32/u64 casts in row decoders can corrupt or hide errors
description:
Found during pane 2 review of db module:

1. Line 7611: `required_i64(...) as u32` in get_tag_counts - unsafe cast without bounds check
2. Line 11403: `i as u64` in stored_episode_from_row - negative i64 would wrap to huge positive u64
3. Line 6384: `unwrap_or(0) as u32` in get_feedback_counts - unsafe cast after defaulting NULL to 0
4. Lines 10195-10227: `try_from().unwrap_or(0)` patterns in pack record decoders silently hide overflow/negative errors as 0

The tc51 commit (74c84727) fixed the recorder row decoders but missed these other locations.

Recommended fix: use `required_u32` or `required_u64` helpers consistently, or propagate errors from try_from instead of silently defaulting to 0.
close_reason: Fixed: replaced unsafe i64→u32/u64 casts with required_u32/optional_u64 helpers in get_tag_counts, get_feedback_counts, stored_task_episode_from_row, stored_pack_record_from_row, and stored_pack_item_from_joined_row. Tests pass.

title: [reality-check] README data_hash JSON contract claim is not implemented
description:
Reality-check focus: docs vs current stable JSON contract surfaces.

Drift:
- README.md:53 promises: "Every machine-facing command emits versioned JSON with `schema` field and `data_hash`."
- Current response schema does not include or require `data_hash`: src/output/mod.rs:4793 defines `ee.response.v1` with required fields `schema`, `success`, and `data` only.
- Runtime output also lacks it. Reproduction from the canonical checkout: `/data/tmp/ee_target_pane8/debug/ee status --json --meta | jq -c '{schema,success,has_data_hash:has("data_hash"),keys:keys}'` returns `has_data_hash:false`; `/data/tmp/ee_target_pane8/debug/ee schema list --json | jq -c '{schema,success,has_data_hash:has("data_hash")}'` also returns false.

Expected:
Either implement a stable response-level `data_hash` contract across machine-facing JSON outputs and update `ee schema export ee.response.v1`, or revise README.md to promise the pack/content hashes actually emitted today. Add a contract test so README and exported schema cannot drift again.
close_reason: Fixed README.md:53 - removed incorrect data_hash claim. The actual contract emits versioned JSON with schema field (verified with ee status --json → ee.response.v1). data_hash is only used in eval reports, not as a general response field.

title: Swarm verification broker follow-on: operator lookup and blocker reuse on top of verification ledgers
description:
## Idea-wizard refinement

This is a follow-on to the existing swarm verification reuse track, not a replacement for it. The base evidence ledger and equivalence work already live under `bd-1zb7k.15`, especially `bd-1zb7k.15.1` and `bd-1zb7k.15.2`. This epic focuses on the missing operator/broker layer: a JSON-first way for agents to discover reusable evidence, known compile blockers, and RCH slot pressure before spending another remote build slot.

## Why this remains accretive

The current swarm repeatedly runs expensive RCH checks against the same shared tree and rediscovers the same compile blockers. The existing ledger records evidence; the broker should turn that evidence into immediate coordination guidance. It should answer: is an equivalent result already known, is a blocker already known, who likely owns it, and what is the next command or message?

## Boundaries

- Advisory only: no agent scheduling, no build launching from lookup paths, no Beads/Git/Mail mutation.
- Reuse existing verification records and ownership attribution rather than inventing a second ledger.
- Preserve local-first, deterministic, redaction-safe JSON contracts.
- Treat RCH posture as an optional input; if unavailable, emit honest degraded output.

## Acceptance

- The epic depends on `bd-1zb7k.15` and composes with `bd-1zb7k.16.2`.
- Ships broker-specific view models, lookup guidance, swarm brief integration, replay fixtures, and docs/failure-mode coverage.
- Includes unit, contract, golden, and no-mock e2e coverage with detailed structured logging.
- Avoids duplicating existing hot-path cache, burst admission, disk guard, and base verification-ledger beads.

- Schema drift test proving the broker view validates against its declared schema.

## Acceptance

The broker can answer reuse questions from existing ledger records without launching Cargo/RCH and without introducing a duplicate verification evidence schema.

title: VBroker.2: Read-only ee verify broker lookup for reusable RCH evidence
description:
## Goal

Add a JSON-first read-only broker lookup surface that tells an agent whether a compatible verification result already exists before it spends an RCH slot.

## Requirements

- Provide an agent-facing command shape such as `ee verify broker lookup --command <argv-json-or-profile> --workspace . --json` or an equivalent placement consistent with the CLI architecture.
- The query path must be read-only: no Cargo, no RCH, no Beads mutation, no Agent Mail mutation, no git mutation.
- Return reusable, stale, incompatible, in_progress, and unavailable states with stable reason codes and suggested next commands.
- Include RCH slot posture only as advisory metadata when supplied by a snapshot or lightweight status source; never block waiting for RCH.
- Preserve stdout/stderr isolation and the `ee.response.v2` / `ee.error.v2` envelope.

## Tests

- Unit tests for evidence matching and stale/incompatible classification.
- CLI contract/golden tests for reusable success, stale dirty tree, known compile blocker, and no evidence.
- No-mock smoke test using retained fixture manifests rather than live RCH execution.

## Acceptance

An agent about to run `cargo check --all-targets` can ask the broker whether a recent compatible RCH result exists and receive deterministic JSON guidance without launching a build.

title: VBroker.3: Compile-blocker evidence cache keyed by tree fingerprint and first source path
description:
## Goal

Prevent swarms from rediscovering the same compile blocker with repeated remote builds. A failed verification result should publish a compact, reusable first-failure summary keyed by tree fingerprint, command class, and source path.

## Requirements

- Store or import first-failure summaries from verification evidence manifests: Rust error code, source path, line/column if available, short message, owning bead/reservation candidates when provided, and artifact hash.
- Do not store full compiler logs. Keep excerpts concise and redaction-safe.
- Integrate conceptually with the ownership snapshot / compile-blocker attribution work without duplicating its responsibilities: this bead caches evidence; ownership attribution ranks owners.
- Return suggested coordination action: message holder, wait for expiry, rerun because tree changed, or claim unowned blocker.
- Expire or mark stale when source tree fingerprint or relevant file hash diverges.

## Tests

- Fixture for the live class of failure where all-targets is blocked before focused tests run.
- Unit tests for stale detection when the blocked file changes.
- Golden output for attributed, unattributed, stale, and redacted-summary cases.

## Acceptance

A second agent seeing the same current-tree blocker can reuse the cached evidence and coordinate with the owner instead of spending another RCH slot to rediscover it.

title: VBroker.5: Deterministic verification trace replay fixtures for duplicate-build prevention
description:

- Model a multi-agent sequence: agent A runs all-targets and hits a compile blocker; agent B asks for a focused test that would be blocked by the same compile error; agent C asks for the same all-targets check after the blocked file changes.

- Assert that the broker recommends reuse/coordination for agent B and rerun for agent C.
- Include structured test-event logging: trace ID, fixture hash, command fingerprint, evidence artifact hash, reuse/stale decision, degraded sources, and first-failure diagnosis.
- Do not require live Agent Mail, live Beads mutation, live RCH, or network.

## Tests

- No-mock e2e or contract harness around the real binary if the CLI surface exists; otherwise a contract-level replay harness around the core broker model.
- Golden snapshots for every replay step.
- Determinism check: three runs produce byte-identical decisions and artifact hashes.

## Acceptance

The broker-specific replay layer can be regression-tested as a coordination primitive even when the remote build fleet is busy or the shared tree is temporarily uncompilable.

title: HIGH: MMR drops unrelated untagged memories sharing coarse diversity keys
description: Review finding in src/pack/mod.rs and src/core/context.rs. candidate_similarity returns 1.0 whenever diversity_key strings match, and is_redundant drops any candidate with max similarity >= 1.0. diversity_key_for_memory defaults untagged memories to level:kind:untagged, so two unrelated untagged procedural rules become exact duplicates. Repro: create two distinct untagged procedural/rule memories that both match a query; after one is selected, the other is omitted as redundant_candidate purely by coarse key. Expected: exact redundancy should require same memory/source/content, or coarse keys should only penalize diversity, not hard-drop.
close_reason: candidate_similarity uses content_overlap_similarity + diversity_key boost (0.5-0.95) instead of diversity_key alone → 1.0; regression tests prove unrelated memories with same tag are no longer dropped

title: Move situation classification and plan recipes out of core decision-making
description:
## Background

Task classification and command recipes can help agents, but they are agent-facing reasoning/planning aids. The Rust CLI may expose mechanical metadata, schemas, command catalogs, and explicit heuristic tags, but should not act like an agent goal planner or situation reasoner.

Audit anchors: `src/core/plan.rs` classifies goals and emits command recipes; `src/core/situation.rs` classifies task text, routes to surfaces, and has show/explain stubs.

## Acceptance Criteria

See this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field for the detailed completion contract, including unit/static checks, e2e or docs/e2e coverage, detailed logging, and no-feature-loss requirements.
design: Split the surface. Keep command catalogs, schema exports, fixture evaluation metrics, and explicit low-stakes heuristic tags if clearly labeled. Move task framing, planning recipes, situation explanation, and downstream routing judgment into skills.
acceptance_criteria:

- `ee plan` either becomes a mechanical command catalog/recipe registry with explicit static provenance or moves to a skill-facing docs surface.

title: [testing-golden][schema-roundtrip] Add schema version round-trip tests for all JSON output contracts
description: Ensure every ee.*.v1 schema has a round-trip test: serialize → deserialize → serialize produces identical output. Current tests use insta snapshots but don't systematically verify round-trip stability for all 7 JSON contract schemas (context, search, why, status, doctor, profile_config_apply, profile_config_plan).
close_reason:
Implemented schema round-trip contract tests in tests/contracts/schema_roundtrip.rs covering ee.response.v1 (context + health commands) and ee.error.v1.

Per-renderer assertions: rendered JSON parses, top-level `schema` field matches expected, parse -> reserialize -> reparse yields a structurally equivalent Value, second reserialization is idempotent, and two consecutive renders produce byte-identical output (determinism).

Cross-renderer property: every emitted response envelope carries top-level `schema` and `success` fields.

Structural equivalence (not byte-identity) is the contract because serde_json::Value uses BTreeMap without preserve_order, so re-emission always sorts keys alphabetically — that's the documented serde_json behavior and the test pins this property explicitly.

The four schemas that need a workspace on disk (search, why-on-memory, status, doctor, profile_config_*) stay covered by the existing JSON snapshot tests in tests/json_contract_snapshots.rs.

Seven new tests, all green. Zero new contract regressions vs the 8-failure macOS baseline.
