title: G7: Dominance frontiers + immediate dominators on revision DAG — impact analysis for edits
description:
# G7 — Dominance frontiers + immediate dominators on the revision DAG

## Idea (one-liner)

Treat the `logical_id`-grouped revision chains as a unified DAG and apply compiler-theory primitives: immediate dominators (the unique most-recent revision every downstream revision must pass through) and dominance frontiers (the set of revisions where impact "leaks out" of a sub-DAG). Surface as **impact analysis for memory edits**.

## Why this matters

Direct compiler-theory transfer — this is how LLVM SSA renaming works. Revision DAGs are mostly inert in `ee` today: rows pile up, get walked occasionally for `ee memory history`, but nothing tells the user "your edit to memory X invalidates the validation of these 4 downstream memories". Dominance frontiers do exactly that, with no ML.

The product question: when a memory is revised via `ee memory revise`, *which downstream concepts must be re-validated?* The answer is the dominance frontier of the revised node in the revision DAG.

A second primitive: `ee why <memory_id>` can show the **immediate dominator** as a new lineage primitive — "the most recent revision that every later iteration depends on". Strictly more informative than the parent revision alone.

## Algorithms

1. **Immediate dominators**: `fnx_algorithms::immediate_dominators(revision_dag, start=root_of_chain)`. Returns map from node → its idom. O((V+E)·α(V,E)) via Cooper-Harvey-Kennedy.

2. **Dominance frontiers**: `fnx_algorithms::dominance_frontiers(revision_dag, idoms)`. Returns map from node → its DF set. O(|DF|·V).

3. **All-pairs LCA**: `fnx_algorithms::all_pairs_lca_rust(revision_dag)`. Useful for `ee why` on contradictions — "when did this concept's lineage last agree?".

## Revision DAG construction

The revision DAG (built by F1) combines:
- **Per-logical-id chains**: For each `logical_id`, the chain of revisions ordered by `valid_from` is a linear path. Edges go from old → new (or new → old, decision below).
- **Cross-chain edges**: `memory_links.relation = 'derived_from'` edges across logical_id boundaries.
- **Edge direction**: We orient edges *from-prior-to-newer* (the prior revision is the dominator). So `dominators` and `dominance frontiers` are computed in the standard forward direction.

## Output shape

`ee memory revise <id> --json` (dry-run mode) gains an `impactAnalysis` block:

```jsonc
"impactAnalysis": {
  "schema": "ee.memory.impact_analysis.v1",
  "revisingMemoryId": "mem_...",
  "logicalId": "logical_...",
  "immediateDominator": "mem_...",
  "dominanceFrontier": [
    {
      "memoryId": "mem_...",
      "rationale": "exits the dominated region of the new revision",
      "validationStatus": "needs_revalidation"
    },
    ...
  ],
  "totalFrontierSize": 4,
  "degraded": []
}
```

`ee why <id> --json` gains an `revisionLineage` block:

```jsonc
"revisionLineage": {
  "logicalId": "logical_...",
  "immediateDominator": "mem_...",
  "ancestorsAtDepth": { "1": ["..."], "2": ["..."], ... }
}
```

`ee insights --section revisionFrontiers`: top-K recent revisions ranked by dominance-frontier size (= edits with the biggest blast radius).

## Acceptance

- New module `src/graph/dominance.rs` with `compute_immediate_dominators`, `compute_dominance_frontiers`, `compute_all_pairs_lca`.
- F1's RevisionDAG snapshot precomputes idoms + DFs.
- `ee memory revise --dry-run --json` shows the `impactAnalysis` block.
- `ee why` shows `revisionLineage`.
- 6 unit tests + 1 e2e + 1 golden.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: F1 (RevisionDAG builder), F2, F4.
Blocks: nothing.
Parent: bd-bife.

## Related code

- `src/db/mod.rs:memories.logical_id` schema.
- `src/cli/memory_revise.rs` (or wherever revise is implemented) — surface integration.
- ADR 0009 (trust class taxonomy) — revision DAG ties into trust-class transitions.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
## Phase 6 refinement notes — dominance direction + DAG violations

1. **Direction**: revision DAG edges flow from-prior-to-newer (older revision dominates newer ones in the compiler sense). Entry = oldest revision in each logical_id chain. Immediate dominator of revision N = revision N-1 in the linear case; can be older if cross-chain derived_from skips revisions.

2. **DAG violations**: derived_from cross-chain edges could create cycles (revision X is derived from revision Y, but Y was later supersedes-revised from another chain that's derived_from X's chain). G7.a must call is_directed_acyclic_graph() before computing dominators. If cycle: emit degraded.revision_cycle, fall back to immediate-parent-only (skip dominance frontier), and list the cycle members for curation.

3. **all_pairs_lca and disconnected chains**: LCA only defined for pairs in the same tree. For cross-chain LCA queries: lookup the common ancestor in the unified DAG; if no common ancestor (different roots), return None.

4. **G7.b impactAnalysis output**: When user runs ee memory revise on a memory with NO downstream descendants (leaf node), impactAnalysis.dominanceFrontier should be []. Not null. Empty array is information ('no impact'); null suggests not-computed.

Update G7.a accordingly.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text: Round 4 pinning. G7.a unit tests (6 cases): (1) Linear chain A->B->C->D: idoms {B:A,C:B,D:C}. (2) Diamond A->B,A->C,B->D,C->D: idoms {B:A,C:A,D:A}, DF(B)={D}, DF(C)={D}. (3) Multi-root DAG: components computed independently, cross-component LCA returns None. (4) Singleton (no chain): idom={self:self}, DF={}. (5) Cycle pre-flight: is_directed_acyclic_graph() check; on cycle emit degraded.revision_cycle + fall back to immediate parent. (6) all_pairs_lca: LCA(B,C)=A, LCA(B,B)=B. title: [swarm-brief][sources] Normalize coordination snapshot sources
description:
Build the internal domain model and source collection layer for `ee.swarm.brief.v1` without adding a public command yet.

Background:
The brief needs a normalized, deterministic snapshot so command rendering, support bundles, and tests do not parse external tool output ad hoc. This should reuse local project conventions for stable schemas, degraded records, redaction, workspace discovery, and command-effect honesty.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Add domain types for `SwarmBriefReport`, source snapshots, source freshness, degraded source records, advisory recommendations, file-surface risks, resource-pressure hints, and provenance for each source.
- Implement source adapters behind small interfaces for: workspace/git dirty surfaces and recent commits; Beads ready/blocked/in-progress/deferred summaries; BV robot insights/triage/plan data when available; Agent Mail reservations/threads when an explicit supported local source is available; RCH/build-pressure status when available; host profile/report evidence when available; existing agent inventory status.

- The source layer must not mutate Beads, Agent Mail, git, RCH, EE storage, support bundles, or config.
- Sorting and tie-breaking are deterministic for files, beads, agents, reservations, commits, degradations, and recommendations.
- Redaction rules prevent raw mail bodies, raw secret-like command output, absolute home-directory details when policy says to redact, and arbitrary environment dumps from leaving the process.
- Unit tests cover complete source data, missing optional tools, stale/locked Beads data, unavailable Agent Mail, missing RCH, dirty worktree file grouping, deterministic ordering, and redaction of sensitive text.

title: EE-340: Define certificate domain models for pack, curation, tail-risk, privacy-budget, and lifecycle artifacts
description:
Source plan item: EE-340 from the `Alien Artifact Math And Certificates` backlog.

Task: Define certificate domain models for pack, curation, tail-risk, privacy-budget, and lifecycle artifacts

Background and intent:
Compile advanced mathematical ideas into inspectable runtime artifacts: certificates, cards, audits, loss matrices, tail-risk gates, and lifecycle ledgers rather than opaque magic.

Why this matters:
This bead contributes to the overarching goal of making `ee` a dependable local memory substrate for coding agents: useful before work, auditable after work, and safe under degraded conditions. The work should be implemented in the smallest coherent slice that fully satisfies the public contract implied by the title.

Dependency context:
Original plan dependencies: EE-017, EE-035. These are also represented as br dependency edges where the referenced bead exists.

Non-negotiable constraints:
Global implementation invariants for this task:
- Keep the CLI local-first, deterministic, and agent-native; stdout is data, stderr is diagnostics.
- Preserve the no-Tokio and no-rusqlite constraint unless a later ADR explicitly changes the architecture.
- Use SQLModel Rust plus FrankenSQLite for durable data; do not introduce a second storage stack.
- Use Asupersync for async edges and cancellation/budget behavior; do not smuggle in a Tokio executor.
- Keep JSON as the canonical public contract. TOON, Markdown, diagrams, and MCP are renderers or adapters over the same domain data.
- Mutating commands need dry-run/idempotency/audit behavior unless the task explicitly says otherwise.
- Add focused tests proportional to risk: unit tests for domain logic, contract/golden tests for public output, and integration/evaluation tests for cross-subsystem behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including the comprehensive testing and logging requirements.
design:
Suggested design approach:
- Define versioned Rust domain/output types first; public JSON schemas and golden fixtures should derive from those types where practical.

title: [freshness] Surface stale or missing provenance in context packs
description:
Implement evidence freshness checks so context packs can honestly report when their supporting files, sessions, ADRs, or imported evidence no longer match the state that originally justified a memory. The point is to warn and explain, not to silently delete or demote memories.

Scope:
- Define freshness states for provenance: fresh, missing_source, changed_source, unreachable_source, unsupported_source, and unknown.
- For local file and workspace provenance, compare stable source hashes or metadata already stored on memory/evidence records, adding storage fields only if the ADR/contract requires them.
- For cass/session provenance, use consumed robot/json metadata or report unsupported_source if the current contract cannot verify it.
- Thread freshness into context/why explanations and degraded arrays without breaking deterministic ordering.
- Add repair hints that tell the user whether to re-import cass, refresh indexes, re-remember the rule, or inspect the source.

- Real-binary E2E mutates a fixture source file after memory capture and proves the pack reports changed_source with no stdout diagnostics.
- The implementation does not silently tombstone, delete, or rewrite memories.
- RCH cargo check/clippy/relevant tests pass.

title: [HIGH] Token budget heuristic claims tiktoken-rs but uses character ratio
description:
## Surface
ee context token budget enforcement (audit cycle 5)

## Finding
AGENTS.md "Key Dependencies" table lists `tiktoken-rs` as: 'Token budgeting for context packs'. The actual code in `src/pack/mod.rs:108` uses a deterministic character-count heuristic:
- `DEFAULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 3.5` (line 65)
- `estimate_tokens_default` divides char count by 3.5 and ceils
- No `tiktoken`, `cl100k`, or `encode_with_special` calls anywhere in src/

Cargo.toml does NOT depend on tiktoken-rs. Verified:
- `grep -n tiktoken Cargo.toml` → no match
- `grep -n tiktoken Cargo.lock` → no match
- The only mention in src/ is a doc comment at `src/core/budget.rs:267`: 'Token count (e.g. tiktoken units)'

## Why it matters
1. Budget contract drifts from real LLM context windows. CJK content tokenizes at ~1 token/char in cl100k, but the heuristic estimates ~1 token / 3.5 chars → undercounts by ~3.5x for CJK-heavy memories. JSON/code with many short tokens also miscount.
2. `pack.budget.usedTokens` field in JSON output is reported as authoritative but is actually a heuristic.
3. AGENTS.md and the comprehensive plan should not list tiktoken-rs as a key dep if the project ships a heuristic.

## Repro
```bash
grep -rn tiktoken src/ Cargo.toml Cargo.lock
# Only finds: src/core/budget.rs:267 (a comment)
```

## Fix options
A) Add real tiktoken-rs and use `cl100k_base` for counting (matches AGENTS.md claim).
B) Remove tiktoken-rs from AGENTS.md and the plan; add an explicit ADR documenting the heuristic's bias bands and rename `max_tokens` → `max_estimated_tokens` in the JSON contract for honesty.

(Option B is cheaper and consistent with the no-Tokio franken-stack ethos, but requires updating AGENTS.md and adding an ADR.)

- enum MemoryLevel { Working, Episodic, Semantic, Procedural } — Display, FromStr, all() helper
- enum MemoryKind { Rule, Fact, Decision, Failure, Command, Convention, AntiPattern, Risk, PlaybookStep, Custom(String) } — Display, FromStr, is_known() helper, KNOWN_MEMORY_KINDS const
- struct Tag(String) — parse() lowercases input, validates [a-z0-9:-], 1..=64 bytes, Ord/Hash by canonical form
- struct MemoryContent(String) — parse() trims, rejects empty, rejects > 64 KiB
- struct UnitScore(f32) — parse() rejects NaN/inf/out-of-range; type aliases Confidence, Utility, Importance; constants zero(), neutral() (0.5), one()
- enum MemoryValidationError — UnknownLevel, EmptyKind, InvalidKind, EmptyTag, TagTooLong, InvalidTag, EmptyContent, ContentTooLarge, ScoreOutOfRange (carries f32 so derives PartialEq but not Eq, by design)
- consts MAX_TAG_BYTES (64), MAX_CONTENT_BYTES (64 KiB), KNOWN_MEMORY_KINDS

Discipline:
- No new deps; std-only.
- Wire forms (level + kind strings) are part of ee.response.v1 and intentionally lowercase + stable.
- Tag inputs are lowercased on construction; emojis/spaces/underscores are rejected with InvalidTag.
- Content inputs are trimmed of ASCII whitespace before storage.
- Numeric newtypes reject NaN/infinities at the type-construction boundary so ordering downstream stays total.

16 unit tests cover round-trips per variant, custom kind acceptance, kind rejection of empty/uppercase/leading-digit/special-char/leading-dash, tag canonicalization + ordering + invalid-byte detection + size cap, content trim + empty rejection + size cap, byte_len, UnitScore at-and-outside endpoints, NaN/inf rejection, alias matching, and a constant-vs-enum consistency check.

- cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings: clean
- cargo test: 83/83 pass (74 lib + 7 forbidden_deps + 2 smoke)

title: SRR6.40: Mesh backup, restore, and disaster-recovery semantics
description:
Define backup, restore, and disaster-recovery behavior for mesh state. Backups must preserve enough peer/cache/cursor/audit/provenance state to explain a restored workspace, while avoiding accidental resurrection of revoked sharing or unsafe peer credentials.

Scope includes: which mesh tables are included in ordinary backups; how cached remote bodies are included, excluded, or revalidated; how peer credentials are redacted or marked inactive on restore; cursor/tip handling after restore; derived cache rebuild behavior; and restore diagnostics that tell the user whether mesh needs re-pairing before sync resumes.

Acceptance: backup manifest fields for mesh state; unit tests for backup serialization and credential redaction; e2e backup-restore script with two mesh nodes proving local search works after restore while mesh remains disabled until explicit reenable or re-pair; structured logs for mesh_backup_included, peer_credentials_redacted, cursor_reset_or_preserved, restore_requires_repair.

comments.text: Fourth polish finding: mesh state will live in the same workspace people back up. This bead prevents restore from silently reconnecting peers or losing provenance needed to understand cached remote memories.

title: Gate 0A: Dependency Contract Matrix
description:
Readiness gate from the comprehensive EE plan.

Gate text and intent:
Before the first product command is considered complete, freeze the dependency matrix for the default feature profile:

```text
tests/contracts/dependency_contract_matrix.rs
tests/golden/dependencies/contract_matrix.json
docs/dependency-contract-matrix.md
```

Pass criteria:

- every external project has exactly one owning `ee-*` crate
- default features exclude Tokio, Hyper, Axum, Tower, Reqwest, async-std, smol, `rusqlite`, SQLx, Diesel, SeaORM, and `petgraph`
- `cargo update --dry-run` cannot introduce a forbidden transitive dependency without the contract test catching it
- path dependencies to `/dp/...` are marked as local-development decisions and have a release pin decision recorded
- duplicate franken-stack crate families are either absent or documented in an ADR with a removal plan
- `ee diag dependencies --json` reproduces the matrix facts from the running binary
- `ee doctor --franken-health --json` returns a schema-valid response and a safe repair or ADR action for every mismatch

Why this matters:

title: [LOW] estimate_tokens silently saturates at u32::MAX for content > ~4 GB
description:
## Surface
`src/pack/mod.rs:108-128` `estimate_tokens` (audit cycle 5)

## Finding
```rust
let estimate = (char_count as f32 / DEFAULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN).ceil();
(estimate as u32).max(1)
```

Two precision/truncation issues:
1. `char_count as f32` loses precision when `char_count` exceeds 2^24 (~16.7M chars), so the f32 round-trip rounds down before division. The estimated count is no longer monotonic at scale.
2. `estimate as u32` saturates at `u32::MAX` rather than wrapping when the f32 value exceeds u32 range (~4.29e9). For inputs of that size the function silently returns u32::MAX.

## Practical impact
Memories rarely exceed even 100KB, so this is a corner case. But:
- ee imports CASS sessions / artifacts that could include large blob content.
- A pathological large memory whose `estimated_tokens` saturates would make the budget arithmetic in `assemble_mmr_draft` (`used_tokens.checked_add`) underflow into TokenBudgetExceeded for every subsequent candidate even if remaining headroom was real.

## Fix
Replace with u64 arithmetic and explicit saturation:
```rust
let chars = trimmed.chars().count() as u64;
let estimate = (chars * 10).div_ceil((DEFAULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN * 10.0) as u64); // integer math
u32::try_from(estimate.max(1)).unwrap_or(u32::MAX)
```
or reject candidates whose content len exceeds a configurable cap (e.g., 1MB) at `PackCandidate::new` with a new `OversizedContent` error variant.

## Severity
LOW because:
- Real memories are far below the threshold.
- Determinism unaffected (saturation is deterministic).
- No security or honesty impact — just silently caps very large inputs to u32::MAX.
close_reason: Fixed silent u32::MAX saturation with explicit overflow handling and regression test

title: EE-AUDIT-001: Add operation audit timeline and inspection commands
description:
Implement an agent-facing operation audit timeline and inspection command family over EE's audit records and command-effect contracts.

Background:
The plan already includes an internal audit repository and a command-effect/no-mutation contract suite. That gives implementation code somewhere to write audit records and gives tests a way to prove commands stayed inside their declared effects. What is still missing is the public agent-facing surface for answering: what did EE actually do, what changed, which command caused it, was it dry-run or applied, which tables/artifacts changed, and how can a future agent cite that evidence?

This bead turns auditability from an internal promise into a usable CLI contract. Agents should be able to inspect recent EE operations after an init/import/index/remember/curate/handoff/support run without reading the DB directly, scraping logs, or trusting prose summaries.

Intended public surface:
- `ee audit timeline --json [--since <time|operation-id>] [--limit N] [--workspace <id>]` lists recent EE operations with effect class, command path, outcome, mutated surfaces, audit IDs, redaction posture, and next inspection command.
- `ee audit show <operation-id> --json` returns a detailed operation record with command metadata, expected vs observed effect, changed tables/artifacts, idempotency key, transaction status, degradation codes, redaction summary, and linked evidence IDs.
- `ee audit diff <operation-id> --json` reports declared state deltas at the table/artifact level where available, not raw secret-bearing payloads.
- `ee audit verify --json [--since <time|operation-id>]` validates hash chains, missing records, effect-manifest conformance, and redaction invariants for the selected audit window.

This is not an undo engine, not a backup, and not a raw database browser. It is a safe, redacted, machine-readable provenance surface for EE's own operations.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including comprehensive unit tests, integration tests, e2e tests, schema/golden fixtures, redaction checks, and detailed logging requirements.
design:
Recommended design:
- Build on the audit repository, transaction helper, command-effect manifest, response envelope, and redaction policy. Do not create a second audit store or parse tracing logs as the source of truth.
- Define a versioned `operation_audit.v1` response schema with stable operation IDs, workspace ID, command path, command hash, actor/agent identity when known, started/finished timestamps, expected effect, observed effect, dry-run/apply mode, idempotency key, transaction status, changed tables, changed derived artifact classes, redaction summary, degradation codes, linked evidence IDs, and next recommended inspection commands.
- Keep raw payloads out by default. Table rows, command args, stdout/stderr snippets, and file paths that may contain secrets should be summarized, hashed, redacted, or referenced through existing safe artifacts.
- Use the effect manifest as the conformance source: `audit verify` should compare observed changes to declared command effects and report mismatch codes instead of silently tolerating drift.
- Make timeline output compact and deterministic. Use stable ordering, cursor pagination, field projection, and explicit truncation metadata so agents can use it inside context budgets.
- Treat missing or corrupted audit chains as degraded/repairable states with stable codes and doctor/support-bundle integration points. Do not mutate audit history from read-only audit commands.
- Keep the command local-first and read-only. Verification can compute derived validation results, but must not repair, compact, delete, or rewrite audit records unless a separate future repair command explicitly owns that behavior.
acceptance_criteria:

Acceptance criteria:
- `ee audit timeline --json` returns an `ee.response.v1` payload with deterministic ordering, cursor/limit metadata, operation IDs, command paths, effect classes, outcome status, dry-run/apply mode, workspace scope, redaction posture, changed-surface summaries, degradation codes, and next inspection commands.
- `ee audit show <operation-id> --json` returns a detailed redacted operation record with expected vs observed effect, idempotency key, transaction status, changed table/artifact summaries, linked evidence IDs, fixture/session/context references where available, redaction summary, and integrity/hash-chain status.
- `ee audit diff <operation-id> --json` reports declared and observed state deltas without exposing raw secret-bearing values, raw transcripts, raw DB rows, or unredacted command payloads.
- `ee audit verify --json` validates selected audit windows for hash-chain continuity, missing records, malformed entries, effect-manifest mismatch, redaction invariant failure, unsupported schema version, and out-of-order timestamps, returning stable codes and next actions.
- All audit commands are read-only by default and are covered by the command-effect manifest as read-only operations. They must not repair, compact, delete, rewrite, or backfill audit records.
- The audit timeline can be referenced by support bundles, handoff capsules, closure dossiers, failure replay artifacts, and e2e logs through stable operation IDs and manifest hashes.
- Ambiguous workspace scope returns candidate workspace IDs and next commands instead of merging unrelated workspaces silently.
- Public schemas and golden fixtures cover empty audit history, normal mutating command, dry-run command, derived-artifact write, failed transaction rollback, effect mismatch, redaction event, corrupted/missing hash-chain entry, unsupported future schema, and ambiguous workspace scope.

Testing and logging requirements:
- Add unit tests for operation ID parsing, cursor pagination, deterministic ordering, field projection, effect-conformance classification, hash-chain validation, redaction summary aggregation, changed-surface summarization, and ambiguity handling.
- Add integration tests against temporary FrankenSQLite/SQLModel databases covering empty history, init/import/remember/index-like sample operations, dry-run records, transaction rollback records, duplicate idempotency keys, malformed audit rows, and schema-version drift.
- Add real-binary e2e coverage that runs an isolated workspace through `ee init --json`, a dry-run command, a mutating memory command, `ee audit timeline --json`, `ee audit show --json`, `ee audit diff --json`, and `ee audit verify --json`, validating stdout schemas/goldens and ensuring audit commands themselves do not mutate state.
- Add privacy regression tests with synthetic secrets in command args, memory bodies, session-like text, config-like values, paths, and stdout/stderr artifacts; raw synthetic secrets must not appear in timeline, show, diff, verify, support bundles, handoff capsules, or failure summaries.
- Add adversarial/property coverage for malformed operation IDs, stale cursors, duplicate timestamps, huge audit windows, invalid UTF-8/control characters, hash collisions in fixtures, unsupported future versions, and concurrent writes happening before the read-only audit snapshot.
- E2E/logged tests must capture command, cwd/workspace, sanitized environment overrides, elapsed time, exit code, stdout/stderr artifact paths, audit operation IDs, manifest/hash-chain status, schema/golden validation status, redaction status, command-effect classification, observed state delta, and first-failure diagnosis.
- Stdout assertions must prove stdout contains only machine data; verification progress, corruption explanations, skipped payload details, redaction events, warnings, and debugging context must go to stderr or explicit artifacts.
- Closeout evidence must include fixture IDs, scenario IDs, manifest hashes, command-effect manifest entries, exact verification commands, and proof that audit commands are read-only and distinct from backup/restore/repair behavior.

title: [MEDIUM] V036 trigger lacks regression test for direct DELETE FROM recorder_events — design trade-off untested at boundary
description:
## Surface
Effect of recent swarm fixes — V036 / is96 (audit cycle 8, surface 1)

## Finding
The V036 migration (src/db/mod.rs:3141-3186) installs three triggers:
- `recorder_events_no_update` — blocks UPDATE on recorder_events ✓ tested at src/core/recorder.rs:3394
- `audit_log_no_update` — blocks UPDATE on audit_log (with workspaces SET NULL carve-out) ✓ tested at src/core/audit.rs:806
- `audit_log_no_delete` — blocks DELETE on audit_log ✓ tested at src/core/audit.rs:829

NOTABLE OMISSION: there is NO `recorder_events_no_delete` trigger. The migration comment states:
> "recorder_events: append-only at the engine. DELETE is permitted so the existing recorder_runs ON DELETE CASCADE can run; UPDATE is never legitimate."

This is a deliberate design trade-off — SQLite triggers cannot easily distinguish 'a cascade delete fires' from 'a direct DELETE statement'. The fix chose to leave DELETE on recorder_events open.

The accompanying test `deleting_recorder_run_still_cascades_to_events` (src/core/recorder.rs:3432) verifies the cascade WORKS. But there is NO test covering the OTHER half of the trade-off: a direct `DELETE FROM recorder_events WHERE event_id = X` succeeds without going through the parent run row. That's the open hole the design accepts.

The is96 bead's close_reason acknowledges this:
> "An attacker with raw-SQL access can still DROP TRIGGER first ... but the chain hash check still catches the underlying tamper."

But it doesn't address direct DELETE. A raw `DELETE FROM recorder_events WHERE event_id = 'evt_X'` succeeds silently. No DROP TRIGGER required. The chain hash catches that the chain has a gap (sequence N+1 follows N-1) but doesn't surface 'a row was deleted' — it surfaces 'the chain looks broken' which the operator might attribute to a partial import.

## Why it matters
1. The append-only contract for recorder_events is weaker than for audit_log. Documentation should make this explicit.
2. There's no test pinning the 'direct DELETE succeeds' behavior — a future migration could accidentally ADD a recorder_events_no_delete trigger that breaks the cascade, and only a runtime cascade test would notice.
3. ee's chain-verification command surface should explicitly report 'sequence gap' as a separate degradation from 'hash mismatch' so a tamper-via-DELETE is detectable.

## Fix
Either:
A) Add a test `direct_delete_on_recorder_events_succeeds` next to deleting_recorder_run_still_cascades_to_events that asserts the design intent — DELETE FROM recorder_events succeeds and cascades from the run-table delete are unaffected.
B) Replace the missing trigger with a smarter version using SQLite's `raise_when_safe` pattern: install a `recorder_events_no_direct_delete` trigger that aborts unless OLD.run_id NOT IN (SELECT run_id FROM recorder_runs). This blocks direct DELETE but lets the cascade fire because the parent row is already gone when the cascade trigger evaluates. (Verification needed — SQLite's exact trigger ordering for cascades is subtle.)
C) Surface a 'sequence gap' degradation in ee recorder verify so the chain-verifier reports tampered-via-DELETE distinctly from tampered-via-hash-mismatch.

## Severity
MEDIUM because:
- The design choice was made deliberately (per is96 close_reason).
- The trade-off is not catastrophic — chain integrity is still detectable post-hoc.
- But it is a documented gap with no test or degradation surface, which is the same pattern that landed the original is96.
close_reason: Added recorder regression coverage for the accepted direct recorder_events DELETE trade-off. The new test proves direct DELETE removes only the targeted event while preserving the parent run, then proves deleting the parent run still cascade-deletes remaining events. Also removed the adjacent recorder test's expect_err strict-clippy violation. Verification: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check src/core/recorder.rs; git diff --check -- src/core/recorder.rs; RCH cargo test --lib direct_delete_on_recorder_events_succeeds_and_cascade_still_works; RCH cargo test --lib deleting_recorder_run_still_cascades_to_events; RCH cargo test --lib append_only_trigger_blocks_recorder_events_update; RCH cargo check --all-targets; UBS src/core/recorder.rs. Repo-wide cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings were attempted and remain blocked by unrelated pre-existing dirty/baseline issues outside this bead.

title: [HIGH] pack output (ee context) does not call redact_secret_like_content — defense-in-depth gap against AGENTS.md "no secrets in context packs"
description:
Repro:
  `ee context <task> --json` emits memory content verbatim through
  `core::context::compute_pack_hash` and the JSON renderer in
  `src/output/mod.rs`. The redaction policy in `src/policy/mod.rs::
  redact_secret_like_content` is called at WRITE TIME (memory.rs:749,
  jsonl_import.rs:764, curate.rs:2408/2446, cass/import.rs:852) but
  NEVER at pack-output time.

  Construction:
    1. Bypass `ee remember` and write a memory whose content contains
       a secret directly into the SQLite store (e.g., via an
       integration test, an admin tool, or a pre-V032-redaction-rule
       backup that imported through a path predating the redaction
       upgrade).
    2. Run `ee context <query> --json` whose retrieval surfaces that
       memory.
    3. Observe the secret in the pack output.

Expected: pack output should re-apply `redact_secret_like_content` to
each item.content before emitting, as a defense-in-depth so that any
hole in the write-time redaction (or any historical write that
predated a redaction-rule update) does not leak through `ee context`.

Actual: pack output trusts the storage layer. Greppable confirmation:

      $ grep -rn 'redact_secret_like_content' src/ | grep -v test
        src/core/jsonl_import.rs:764  (write path)
        src/core/memory.rs:749        (write path)
        src/core/curate.rs:2408       (write path)
        src/core/curate.rs:2446       (write path)
        src/cass/import.rs:852        (write path)
        src/policy/mod.rs:465         (definition)

  No call site in `src/core/context.rs`, `src/pack/mod.rs`, or
  `src/output/mod.rs`.

Aggravating: AGENTS.md "Non-Goals For V1" pillar reads "No secrets in
context packs." The repo's code-level enforcement of that pillar lives
entirely on the write side, with no audit gate at the read side.
Adding a redaction pass to the pack output is cheap (the function is
already deterministic and well-tested in
`src/policy/mod.rs::tests::redact_secret_like_content_*`).

Evidence-line:
  src/policy/mod.rs:465 (redact_secret_like_content definition)
  src/core/context.rs:513-559 (compute_pack_hash — does not redact)
  src/core/context.rs (no call to redact_secret_like_content)
  src/pack/mod.rs (no call to redact_secret_like_content)

Suggested fix:
  - Apply `redact_secret_like_content` to `item.content` in the pack
    builder right before the content is hashed and emitted. Capture
    the redaction report into a per-item `redactions: Vec<...>` field
    so the JSON contract is honest.
  - Add a determinism test (`tests/pack_redacts_secrets_at_render.rs`)
    that seeds a memory with a known secret pattern via the raw DB,
    runs `ee context --json`, and asserts the secret is replaced with
    the redaction placeholder.
  - The pack hash currently includes raw content. Once redaction is
    applied at render, the hash should include the redacted content
    so that the same workspace state produces the same hash —
    redaction strings are deterministic so this is straightforward.

Severity: HIGH. The defense-in-depth gap means any future write-path
regression silently leaks secrets through the most-used surface (`ee
context` is the walking-skeleton command). Today the gap is latent
because every known write path redacts, but the architectural rule
should be enforced at every layer that crosses a trust boundary.
close_reason: Completed: context pack selected items are redacted before emission, redaction metadata is exposed in JSON output, pack hashes include redaction metadata, and focused pack/output tests pass.

title: GraphAccretion: Epic — 10 graph-theoretic features inspired by beads_viewer, backed by franken_networkx
description:
# Graph-Theoretic Accretion via franken_networkx (beads_viewer-inspired)

## Background (so future-self has full context)

This epic operationalizes a session of plan-space ideation that synthesized three independent reports:

1. **Design philosophy** drawn from `/dp/beads_viewer` — a project that pairs every graph algorithm with a *product question*. Examples: PageRank → "foundational blockers", betweenness → "bottlenecks; if cut, what unblocks most?", k-core → "tightly-coupled kernel that must ship together", topK-set (greedy submodular) → "what 5 things, done now, unblock the most?", what-if cascade → "should I prioritize this? show me the impact". The design discipline: triangulate orthogonal metrics (no single one captures the full picture); aggressively bound compute (timeouts, sampling, cycle caps) for responsive UI; precompute in phases (instant + background); visualization reflects graph theory.

2. **Capability inventory** of `/dp/franken_networkx` — 311+ public functions across connectivity, centrality, community, matching, flow, trees, paths/cycles, DAG-specific, core-decomposition, cliques, link prediction, distance metrics, mixing/assortativity, ego/local, isomorphism, planarity, approximation, generators, I/O. Critically: the project today only exercises pagerank + betweenness, leaving 99% of the toolkit unused.

3. **Substrate audit** of `ee` showing that the data model is *richer* than beads_viewer's task graph: typed edges (7 relation types on memory_links), temporal evolution (revision chains via logical_id), weighted, multi-relational, with audit/causality/lineage substrata.

## Why this epic exists

`ee` is a memory substrate for coding agents. Its core value-proposition — durable, explainable, agent-grade memory — is bottlenecked today by *flat retrieval*. Pack assembly is MMR + freshness + confidence. `ee why` returns scalar scores. `ee status` returns scalar counts. `ee curate` decays uniformly. The graph substrate exists (memory_links is a real DiGraph, PageRank + betweenness are computed and snapshotted) but it influences only a side-band features block. Its potential as a first-class explanatory and ranking primitive is unrealized.

This epic ships 10 graph-theoretic capabilities (5 top-tier features + 5 next-tier) that each map a sophisticated graph algorithm to a concrete `ee` product question. Together they constitute a coherent layer — not a grab-bag — because they triangulate orthogonal structural signals (centrality, cohesion, lineage, contradiction, causality, provenance) over the same shared substrate.

## The 10 features (in priority order)

**Top tier (highest leverage):**
- G1 — Personalized PageRank for `ee context` pack assembly (query-seeded random walk re-ranks the candidate pool)
- G2 — "Pack DNA" composite for `ee context --explain` (Voronoi + Louvain + ego graph + PPR → single readable JSON block)
- G3 — Causal explanation via transitive closure + min-cost flow on causal_evidence
- G4 — K-truss + contradiction-cluster detection for `ee health`
- G5 — Articulation points + onion layers for `ee curate` (structural decay policy)

**Next tier (deep mathematical leverage, narrower but elegant):**
- G6 — Gomory-Hu tree for O(1) pairwise proximity queries
- G7 — Dominance frontiers + immediate dominators on the revision DAG (impact analysis for edits)
- G8 — "Knowledge skyline" composite for `ee status` (onion layers × Louvain × age × trust-class)
- G9 — Bipartite eigenvector on rule ↔ source-memory provenance graph
- G10 — HITS hubs vs authorities (orientation vs grounding query profiles)

## The 4 shared foundations (prerequisites)

- F1 — Multi-graph snapshot framework: today there is exactly one snapshot type (memory_links). Add typed-subgraph support so causal_evidence, revision_dag (logical_id), rule_provenance (bipartite), and contradiction_subgraph each get their own deterministic snapshot with content-hash and refresh semantics.
- F2 — Algorithm wrapper conventions: a single pattern for calling any fnx_algorithms function with CGSE complexity witnesses, deterministic tie-breaks, sampling fallbacks for large graphs (>500 nodes), and timeout budgets. This pattern is reused by all 10 features.
- F3 — `ee insights` JSON-first command scaffold: a beads_viewer-style `--robot-insights` surface that emits structured graph-derived findings. The home for outputs that don't fit the existing `ee why` / `ee status` / `ee context` envelopes.
- F4 — Determinism + golden-snapshot harness for graph outputs: every algorithm output (PPR scores, k-truss memberships, etc.) must be byte-stable across 3 runs against the same snapshot. Same harness pattern as J7 (bd-17c65.10.7).

## Design discipline (inherited from beads_viewer)

1. **Every algorithm answers a product question.** No algorithm ships without a clear "what does this let the user do that they could not do before?".
2. **Triangulate, don't single-metric.** Composites (G2, G4, G8) combine multiple orthogonal signals — no individual metric is treated as ground truth.
3. **Aggressive bounding.** Every algorithm has a time budget (default 250ms for foreground, 2s for background-refresh), a sampling fallback when |V|>500, and a cycle/iteration cap. CGSE witnesses record the choice.
4. **Phased precompute.** Cheap metrics (degree, topo-sort) compute synchronously on snapshot refresh. Expensive ones (Gomory-Hu, k-truss, communicability) compute lazily on first request and cache. Background refresh on a 5-min ticker.
5. **Determinism is non-negotiable.** Same database, same snapshot → byte-identical output. Tie-breaks via CGSE policies. Same harness as J7.

## Non-goals

- No new graph types beyond what franken_networkx already exposes (no DGL, no PyTorch Geometric, no GraphSAGE).
- No streaming/online algorithms (franken_networkx doesn't support them and we don't need them).
- No embedding methods (DeepWalk, node2vec, etc.) — these are out of scope; if needed, separate epic.
- No graph visualization library (Mermaid output is fine for now; full graph rendering is a separate concern).

## Related ADRs / prior art

- ADR 0008 — Graph metrics are derived, rebuildable features, not authoritative state (we honor this throughout).
- `/dp/beads_viewer` — the design-philosophy source.
- `/dp/franken_networkx` — the algorithm library backing every feature.
- Existing `src/graph/mod.rs` (~6300 LOC) — already exposes memory_links via fnx_classes::DiGraph; this epic extends, never replaces, that pattern.

## Done = (when this whole epic closes)

- All 4 foundation beads (F1-F4) closed.
- All 10 feature beads (G1-G10) closed.
- Each feature has: schema/migration if needed (a), algorithm wrapper (b), CLI integration (c), unit tests (d), integration tests (e), docs (f), golden snapshot (g).
- `cargo test --workspace --all-targets` green.
- `scripts/verify.sh` green.

title: Epic.schema-governance: Register all 7 new schemas, version-evolution policy, supported_schemas() additions
description:
## Why
The graph-accretion epic introduces 7 net-new schemas:
- ee.insights.v1
- ee.context.pack_dna.v1
- ee.why.causal.v1
- ee.health.structural.v1
- ee.status.skyline.v1
- ee.memory.impact_analysis.v1

Plus 2 augmentations:
- ee.why.v1 (add bayesPosterior + loadBearing + hits + revisionLineage blocks)
- ee.context.v1 (add packDna block + proximityToSeed field)

Per AGENTS.md envelope contract: every JSON command schema is governed by a versioning policy. Today these would each ship without coordination, risking drift and rendering downstream tooling brittle.

## Tasks
1. Audit src/core/mod.rs::supported_schemas() — register every new schema constant with its version string.
2. Document evolution rules in docs/agent-ux/schema-evolution.md:
   - Schemas are frozen at .v1; new fields are additive only.

3. Add a contract test tests/contracts/graph_schemas_v1.rs that asserts every new schema in supported_schemas() actually appears in docs/schemas/*.v1.json AND has a corresponding insta snapshot under tests/snapshots/.
4. CI gate: scripts/closure-lint.sh --audit treats a missing schema-doc as a blocker.

## Acceptance
- supported_schemas() lists all 7 new schemas + the 2 augmentations.
- 9 schema JSON files under docs/schemas/.
- 1 contract test passes.
- Deliberate omission of a schema causes closure-lint to fail.

title: Epic.eval-ppr: ee eval scenarios for PPR pack-quality regression + structural recall@k
description:
## Why
Project already has a pack-quality eval harness (PACK_QUALITY_REPORT_SCHEMA_V1, tests/fixtures/golden/, ee eval). PPR re-ranking in G1 changes pack composition — this MUST be regression-tested against the existing eval, OR it could ship as a 'feature' that silently hurts quality.

## Tasks
1. Establish a baseline run of ee eval against the current corpus, save under tests/fixtures/eval/pack_quality_pre_g1_baseline.json.
2. Add 6 new eval scenarios in tests/fixtures/eval/structural_recall/:
   - 'orphan_query' — query for a memory that's textually weak but graph-central. Pre-G1: not in top-3. Post-G1: top-3.
   - 'over_grounding' — query for an authority. Pre-G1: top hit. Post-G1: still top hit (no regression).
   - 'related_concept' — query for concept A, memory tagged B is co_tag-linked. Pre-G1: not retrieved. Post-G1: in top-10.
   - 'contradicted_belief' — query has 2 candidate memories, one with high text relevance but heavily contradicted, the other moderate text + cited. Pre-G1: contradicted wins. Post-G1: cited wins.
   - 'fresh_workspace' — empty graph, PPR adds zero signal, ranking unchanged.
   - 'derived_revision' — query matches memory M; M has derived_from chain. Pre-G1: just M. Post-G1: M + 2 ancestors in top-10.
3. ee eval acceptance: NDCG@10 ≥ baseline (no regression) AND structural-recall@10 ≥ 0.75 on the new scenarios.
4. Run as CI gate: scripts/verify.sh fails if NDCG@10 drops by >2pp.

## Acceptance
- 6 new eval scenarios committed.
- Baseline + post-G1 comparison reports in tests/snapshots/.
- CI gate fires on regression.

Parent: bd-bife. Blocked by: G1 (PPR must be shipped first).

title: Epic.renderers: TOON + Markdown output renderers for all 7 new schemas
description:
## Why
The project ships JSON / Markdown / TOON formatters (src/output/). Today's renderers cover existing schemas. New graph schemas (ee.insights.v1, ee.context.pack_dna.v1, ee.why.causal.v1, ee.health.structural.v1, ee.status.skyline.v1, ee.memory.impact_analysis.v1, ee.proximity.v1) need TOON + Markdown renderers OR explicit 'json-only' tagging.

## Decision tree per schema
- ee.insights.v1: Markdown render = bulleted summary per section. TOON render = compact table per section.
- ee.context.pack_dna.v1: Markdown render = 'Pack DNA: dominator <memory>, community <id>, neighbors <list>'. TOON render = compact.
- ee.why.causal.v1: Markdown render = ASCII tree of ancestry. TOON render = nested.
- ee.health.structural.v1: Markdown render = grouped tables. TOON render = compact.
- ee.status.skyline.v1: Markdown render = ASCII heatmap (already in G8 body). TOON render = column-major table.
- ee.memory.impact_analysis.v1: Markdown render = 'Impact: <N> downstream concepts'. TOON = compact.
- ee.proximity.v1: Markdown render = 'A → B: min-cut <X>'. TOON = compact.

## Tasks
1. Add render_*_markdown and render_*_toon functions for each schema in src/output/.
2. ee why / ee status / etc. respect --format=markdown | toon | json (existing pattern).

title: Epic.audit: Audit log entries for graph snapshot refresh + algorithm result invalidation
description:
## Why
audit_log is the project's compliance trail. Every state-change should be auditable. Graph operations DO change state (snapshot rows, witness rows, result-cache rows). Today no audit entries are emitted.

## New audit_actions to add
- graph.snapshot.refreshed (target=GraphType, details={graph_type, snapshot_version, content_hash, build_time_ms, node_count, edge_count})
- graph.snapshot.archived (target=snapshot_id, details={archived_at, reason=newer_snapshot|manual})
- graph.algorithm.result_cached (target=witness_id, details={algorithm, params_hash, elapsed_ms, cache_size_after})
- graph.algorithm.result_evicted (target=witness_id, details={reason=snapshot_invalidated|ttl_expired})
- graph.algorithm.degraded (target=algorithm, details={code, severity, repair, snapshot_version})

## Tasks
1. Register the 5 new audit_actions in src/db/audit.rs (or wherever).
2. Wire into F1's snapshot lifecycle + F2's cache + F2's algorithm wrappers.
3. tests/contracts/graph_audit.rs verifies each action fires on its trigger.
4. ee audit query filter --action=graph.* surfaces the entries.

## Acceptance
- 5 audit actions register.
- Contract test verifies each fires.
- Audit log queryable via existing ee audit pattern.

Parent: bd-bife. Blocked by: F1, F2.cache.

comments.author: CalmBridge
comments.text:
CalmBridge progress note (Claude Code Opus 4.7) — bd-bife.15 partial completion:

## Shipped this session

Audit-action constants + typed payload builders for the five graph audit actions landed in commit **`adb03fc`** "feat(core): add graph audit-action payload builders (bd-bife.15)":

- New module: `src/core/graph_audit.rs` (~545 lines including tests).
- Module registration: `src/core/mod.rs` between `focus`/`graph_telemetry`/`handoff`.

## Action vocabulary (matches the bead body verbatim)

| Action constant | target_type | mutation_kind |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SNAPSHOT_REFRESHED_ACTION` (`graph.snapshot.refreshed`) | `graph_snapshot` | `state_change` |
| `SNAPSHOT_ARCHIVED_ACTION` (`graph.snapshot.archived`)   | `graph_snapshot` | `state_change` |
| `RESULT_CACHED_ACTION` (`graph.algorithm.result_cached`) | `graph_algorithm_witness` | `derived_write` |
| `RESULT_EVICTED_ACTION` (`graph.algorithm.result_evicted`) | `graph_algorithm_witness` | `derived_delete` |
| `ALGORITHM_DEGRADED_ACTION` (`graph.algorithm.degraded`) | `graph_algorithm` | `degraded_emit` |

`ALL_GRAPH_AUDIT_ACTIONS` is the canonical sweep slice — the documentation generator and the contract test both walk it, so adding a sixth action automatically gains downstream coverage with no further file-edits.

## Typed builders

Each action has a `*Inputs<'a>` struct + `build_*_payload` constructor returning `GraphAuditPayload { action, target_type, target_id, mutation_kind, details: serde_json::Value }`. The `details` body uses `BTreeMap` / `serde_json::Map` with fixed key ordering so two identical inputs always produce byte-identical JSON.

Reason enums with stable lower-snake_case `as_str` wire strings:

- `SnapshotArchivedReason::{NewerSnapshot, Manual}` → `"newer_snapshot"`, `"manual"`
- `ResultEvictedReason::{SnapshotInvalidated, TtlExpired}` → `"snapshot_invalidated"`, `"ttl_expired"`

## Inline test coverage

10 tests:

1. `all_actions_share_the_graph_namespace_prefix` — contract guard on the `graph.` namespace.
2. `all_action_names_are_unique` — contract guard against duplicate action strings.
3. `snapshot_refreshed_payload_carries_documented_keys_and_values` — full key-set verification.
4. `snapshot_archived_payload_handles_both_reasons` — both reason variants.
5. `result_cached_payload_records_cache_size_after_for_correlation` — full payload verification.
6. `result_evicted_payload_records_both_documented_reasons` — both reason variants.
7. `algorithm_degraded_payload_omits_snapshot_version_when_unresolved` — None case.
8. `algorithm_degraded_payload_includes_snapshot_version_when_known` — Some case.
9. `snapshot_archived_reason_wire_strings_are_unique_and_snake_case` — wire-string guard.
10. `result_evicted_reason_wire_strings_are_unique_and_snake_case` — wire-string guard.
11. `payloads_serialize_byte_stable_across_runs` — J7 determinism check.

(Eleven actually — the wire-string guards + determinism check are over and above the bead's explicit ask.)

## Verification

- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on both touched files: pass.
- `git diff --check` on both touched files: pass.
- RCH `cargo check --lib` on worker `trj`: exit 0 in 174s with no errors.

## Remaining work (filed as bd-28m0i)

The bead's tasks 2-4 — call-site wiring (F1 snapshot lifecycle, F2 cache, algorithm wrappers) plus the `tests/contracts/graph_audit.rs` end-to-end test driving each trigger path — are tracked in **bd-28m0i** "Wire graph_audit payload builders into F1 snapshot lifecycle + F2 cache + algorithm wrappers". That bead has been wired as a blocker for bd-bife.15 closure and contains the call-site-by-call-site action plan, builder reference, and the sweep-list-driven contract-test pattern.

Reservations on `src/core/mod.rs` and `src/core/graph_audit.rs` released.

## Why split

title: Epic.cross-feature-perf: Cross-feature interaction perf test (all 10 features enabled simultaneously)
description:
## Why
Each feature has its own perf budget (F2.bench). But what happens when ALL 10 ship together? Worst case: every ee context invocation triggers PPR + Pack DNA + HITS + Voronoi + Louvain caches. Sequential overhead is the sum (~250ms × 5 = 1.25s). Parallel via cache hits should be ~30ms total.

## Tasks
1. New bench: benches/graph_full_stack.rs.
2. Seed 1k-memory workspace, all features enabled, all snapshots fresh.
3. Run 100 ee context invocations across varied queries.
4. Assert: p50 ≤ 100ms (cache hit dominates), p99 ≤ 500ms (cold compute under load).
5. With cache disabled (graph.cache.enabled=false): p50 ≤ 350ms (sequential compute), p99 ≤ 1000ms.

## Acceptance
- Bench runs in CI under both cache=on and cache=off.
- Hard ceilings committed in benches/baselines/.
- Deliberate 100ms-per-algorithm regression triggers failure.

Parent: bd-bife. Blocked by: F2.cache, all G features.

title: Epic.scale-fixtures: Stress fixtures at 10k / 50k / 100k memories
description:
## Why
Existing fixtures top out at ~5k memories. Real workspaces will hit 10k-100k. Algorithms with quadratic or worse complexity (Gomory-Hu, communicability_betweenness, all_pairs_lca) will time out or OOM.

## Tasks
1. New fixtures (synthetic, hash-embedder seeded):
   - tests/fixtures/scale/graph_10k.jsonl
   - tests/fixtures/scale/graph_50k.jsonl
   - tests/fixtures/scale/graph_100k.jsonl
2. Per-fixture, per-algorithm benchmark. Algorithms that exceed budget at scale fall back to:
   - PPR: keep (linear in iterations).
   - HITS: keep.
   - PageRank: keep.
   - Betweenness: pivot-sample (F2.b already).
   - Communicability_betweenness: pivot-sample.
   - K-truss: stay (E^1.5 is OK).
   - Louvain: stay (N log N).
   - Onion layers: stay (V+E).
   - Articulation points: stay (V+E).
   - Gomory-Hu: SKIP for |V|>2000 (G6.refinement-note).
   - Voronoi cells: stay.
   - Ego graph: stay (local).
   - Transitive closure (causal): cap depth to 10 + emit degraded.causal_depth_capped.
   - Min-cost flow (causal): cap iterations.
   - Dominance frontiers: stay.
   - All-pairs LCA: SKIP for |V|>1000; lazy LCA on demand.
   - Simrank: SKIP for |V|>500 (very expensive); fall back to Jaccard.
3. Document scale degradations in docs/scale-degradation-policy.md.

## Acceptance
- 3 scale fixtures land.
- Per-algorithm degradation policy enforced + tested.
- 100k-memory ee insights call completes in ≤5s with appropriate degraded codes.

The project has ee backup / ee restore for disaster recovery. New tables (graph_snapshots is existing, but graph_algorithm_witnesses + graph_algorithm_results are new) accumulate state. 5. Cross-version restore: backup at schema vN, restore at schema vN+1; warn user + auto-migrate graph_* tables.

- Restore preserves cache; cache-hit path verified post-restore.

title: Epic.telemetry: Production telemetry hooks (tracing events) for graph operations
description:
## Why
beads_viewer is a research project; ee runs in production at users with real workloads. Production needs visibility: which algorithms are slow? How often does PPR cache hit? Are users hitting timeouts?

## Decision: tracing events, NOT a Prometheus client
The project uses tracing + tracing-subscriber (already in tree). Telemetry is opt-in via env vars (consistent with existing env var registry). Adding a new exporter (Prometheus, OTLP) is out of scope; we expose tracing events at well-known names + levels so a user can pipe them into anything.

## Telemetry event taxonomy
- ee.graph.snapshot.refresh — INFO level — fields: graph_type, snapshot_version, build_ms, node_count, edge_count, lock_wait_ms
- ee.graph.algorithm.compute — DEBUG — fields: algorithm, snapshot_id, params_hash, elapsed_ms, cache_hit (bool), sampling_used (bool)

title: Epic.memory-budget: Runtime enforcement of 250MB cap on graph snapshots (degrade gracefully)
description:
## Why
RX7 sets a 250MB snapshot footprint target. At 100k memories with typed edges, fnx-classes DiGraph in RAM could exceed that. Today there's no runtime check — bad allocations would just OOM the ee process.

## Enforcement strategy
1. **Pre-build estimate**: Before building a snapshot, count (workspace.memories) and (workspace.memory_links). Estimate bytes ~= 32 * |V| + 96 * |E|. If > 250MB: skip the build, emit degraded.large_graph_uncached, set snapshot.status = Skipped.
2. **In-build measurement**: F1.b/c/d builders track allocated bytes via fnx_runtime stats. If a build exceeds 1.5× the pre-estimate during construction: abort + emit degraded.unexpected_growth + roll back.
3. **In-query measurement**: Algorithm wrappers query current resident memory before invoking. If active snapshots already consume 200MB and current algorithm would need 100MB more: refuse + emit degraded.memory_pressure.

## Config keys (per RX5)
- graph.memory.snapshot_cap_mb (default 250)
- graph.memory.per_algorithm_cap_mb (default 100)
- graph.memory.degraded_below_pct (default 80%)

## Tasks
1. Pre-build estimation utility.
2. F1 wrappers respect the cap.
3. tests/graph_memory_budget.rs — synthetic large fixture exercises the path.
4. Documentation in docs/architecture/graph-memory-budget.md.

## Acceptance
- 100k-memory fixture triggers graceful degradation, NOT OOM.
- 3 unit tests + 1 e2e.
- Memory metrics emitted via telemetry events (RX22).

- `MemoryBudgetPolicy { snapshot_cap_bytes, per_algorithm_cap_bytes, degraded_below_pct, growth_multiplier_basis_points }` with documented defaults: 250 MB / 100 MB / 80% / 1.5×.
- `estimate_snapshot_bytes(node_count, edge_count) -> u64` using `saturating_mul` + `saturating_add` so a `usize::MAX` node count can't silently wrap to a small estimate that would bypass the cap.

title: Epic.witnesses-retention: Witness table retention + maintenance subcommand
description:
## Why
F2.c adds graph_algorithm_witnesses. Witnesses accumulate (every algorithm run = 1 row). On a busy workspace with 100 daily ee context calls, that's ~100 rows/day from PPR alone. After 1 year: 36k rows, plus other algorithms. Need retention + maintenance.

## Retention policy
- Default TTL: 30 days (configurable via graph.witnesses.retention_days).
- Per-algorithm overrides allowed (some witnesses more valuable: cache_results stay longer than ad-hoc PPR runs).
- Witnesses tied to active snapshots are NEVER pruned (until the snapshot is archived).

## New maintenance subcommand
- ee maintenance graph-witnesses-prune [--dry-run]: deletes witnesses older than retention_days that aren't tied to active snapshots.
- Runs nightly via the existing maintenance scheduler (if any), or on-demand.

## Tasks
1. Add retention column to graph_algorithm_witnesses (or use computed retention from recorded_at + per-algorithm TTL).

3. ee insights respects ALL non-pruned witnesses for backward-historical analysis (so pruning doesn't break a 'show me yesterday's PageRank scores' query).
4. Contract test: 30-day-old witnesses untied to snapshots are pruned; same-day witnesses preserved.

title: Epic.cli-flag-precedence: Document + enforce precedence for triple-disable / triple-enable flag combos
description:
## Why
30+ new flags ship. Users will combine them in unexpected ways. Examples:
- ee context --ppr-weight=0 --no-pack-dna --profile=balanced — what's the effective ranking?
- ee curate --no-structural-decay --allow-tombstone-load-bearing — load-bearing protection still in effect?
- ee why --causal-explain --format=toon — does TOON renderer still emit causalExplanation?

## Precedence rules (canonical)
1. **Explicit disable always wins**: --no-X disables feature X regardless of other flags.
2. **Profile flags compose with explicit weights**: --profile=grounding (sets α_hits) + --ppr-weight=0.7 (sets α_ppr); both apply.
3. **Read-only protection precedence (G9 load-bearing × G5 articulation × G7 dominance)**:
   - Explicit ee memory tombstone <id> bypasses ALL protections.
   - Otherwise: load-bearing > articulation > onion-layer-shell.
4. **Format flags**: --format applies to ALL fields uniformly (no per-field format).

## Tasks
1. Document precedence in docs/cli-reference/flag-precedence.md.
2. tests/contracts/flag_precedence.rs exercises every documented rule.
3. ee --help <command> mentions precedence interactions where non-obvious.

## Acceptance
- Documentation committed.
- 10+ precedence rule tests pass.
- Each rule has a worked example.

AGENTS.md required test categories include 'Property and fuzz tests'. Graph algorithms have well-defined mathematical invariants — perfect targets for property-based testing.

## Property tests to add (one per file in tests/property_graph_*.rs)
1. **PageRank invariants**: Σ pagerank(v) ≈ 1.0 (within 1e-6); pagerank(v) > 0 for every reachable v; idempotent under iteration cap.
2. **HITS invariants**: ||authority||_2 = 1.0; ||hub||_2 = 1.0; authority and hub scores are non-negative.
3. **K-truss monotonicity**: k_truss(graph, k+1) ⊆ k_truss(graph, k). Removing any edge from a k-truss can only decrease k (never increase).
4. **Transitive closure idempotency**: tc(tc(graph)) = tc(graph).
5. **Topological order respect**: every edge (u, v) in a DAG ⇒ topo_order[u] < topo_order[v].
6. **Articulation point definition**: removing an articulation point increases the number of connected components by ≥1.
7. **Onion layer monotonicity**: peeling a graph by removing layer 0 leaves a graph whose layer-0 was previously layer-1.
8. **Gomory-Hu tree min-cut**: for any pair (u,v), tree-path-min(u,v) ≤ graph-edge-connectivity(u,v).
9. **Dominance frontier definition**: every node in DF(n) has a predecessor dominated by n but is itself not strictly-dominated by n.

Each property test generates 100 random graphs (Erdős-Rényi via fnx_generators) and asserts the invariant.

## Acceptance
- 9 property test files; 100+ shrunken cases each.
- Deliberate insertion of a bug (e.g., off-by-one in pagerank normalization) is caught by proptest minimization.
- Total runtime ≤30s in CI.

title: Epic.cancellation: Honor asupersync Cx cancellation in every graph algorithm wrapper
description:
## Why
AGENTS.md: 'Asupersync is the runtime; no Tokio. Cx (cancellation context) governs every long-running operation.' Graph algorithms can be slow (Gomory-Hu on 10k nodes, communicability_betweenness on dense graphs). If a CLI invocation is cancelled (user Ctrl-C, agent timeout), the algorithm must stop within ~100ms — not run to completion against a stale request.

## Tasks
1. F2.a (run_with_budget) MUST accept an asupersync Cx parameter. On Cx.is_cancelled(), break out of the algorithm loop (NOT just return — actually stop fnx computation).
2. fnx_algorithms doesn't natively support cancellation. Workaround:
   - Spawn the fnx call in a worker via asupersync.
   - Poll Cx.is_cancelled() every 10ms in the main thread.
   - On cancel: drop the worker (asupersync supervision), record degraded.cancelled in CGSE witness.
3. Add tests/cancellation_graph.rs:
   - Issue a PPR query with a 250ms budget; cancel after 50ms; verify Cx-cancelled exit within 100ms.
   - Issue a Gomory-Hu build with a 2s budget; cancel after 500ms; same.
4. Document the pattern in docs/agent-ux/cancellation-contract.md.

## Acceptance
- F2.a accepts &Cx parameter.
- Every algorithm wrapper threads Cx through.
- 2 cancellation tests pass.
- A deliberate non-cancelling wrapper (busy-wait on fnx without polling) fails the test.

Parent: bd-bife. Blocks: F2.a (it must learn about Cx).

title: Epic.config: Promote heuristic thresholds to configuration keys (no hard-coded magic numbers)
description:
## Why
The 10 features ship with multiple heuristic thresholds:
- α_ppr = 0.30 (PPR blending weight, G1)
- contradiction-cluster density threshold = 0.20 (G4)
- onion-layer decay multiplier = 1×→3× (G5)
- articulation-protection multiplier = 0.5 (G5)
- HITS profile boost = 0.5 (G10)
- causal min-cost normalization (G3)
- pack-dna section budgets (G2)
- Gomory-Hu sample threshold (G6)

Hard-coded magic numbers are anti-pattern: workspace owners can't tune them, A/B testing is impossible, and rolling out new features requires code changes.

## Tasks
1. Add a new config table 'graph_config' (or extend the existing config taxonomy) with namespaced keys: graph.ppr.alpha, graph.health.contradiction_threshold, graph.curate.onion_decay_max, etc.
2. Each algorithm wrapper reads its config keys via the existing config registry; defaults are documented.
3. ee config get graph.* and ee config set graph.* surfaces work.
4. Document every config key in docs/configuration/graph.md with: name, type, default, range, description, tuning_advice.
5. Contract test: deliberately set graph.ppr.alpha=0.0 and verify pack assembly produces the legacy (no-PPR) output byte-identically.

## Acceptance
- 8+ config keys land with documented defaults.
- ee config set/get round-trips work.
- Documentation page enumerates all keys.
- 3 contract tests pin key-driven behavior shifts.

title: Epic.honesty-sentinels: Abstention sentinels for every new graph surface (per AGENTS.md taxonomy)
description:
## Why
AGENTS.md bead taxonomy is strict: every surface that can degrade MUST surface an abstention sentinel (degraded.* with code + severity + message + repair). Today's degraded code taxonomy (docs/degraded_codes.md) covers the existing surfaces. Each new G feature adds failure modes that need explicit codes.

## New degraded codes needed
| Surface | Code | When fires | Repair hint |
|---|---|---|---|
| ee context PPR (G1) | graph.ppr.snapshot_stale | snapshot >300s old | run: ee graph snapshot refresh |
| ee context PPR (G1) | graph.ppr.empty_seed_set | top-k retrieval returned 0 results | broaden query / drop relevance floor |
| ee context Pack DNA (G2) | graph.pack_dna.no_dominator | no trust anchors in workspace | seed a memory with trust_class=human_explicit |
| ee why causal (G3) | graph.causal.no_evidence | causal_evidence table has no rows for this memory | record causal evidence via ee outcome --causal-link |
| ee health (G4) | graph.health.no_contradictions | contradicts edge count is 0 | (info, not error) |
| ee curate (G5) | graph.curate.disconnected_graph | graph has >1 connected component | run: ee graph snapshot refresh, then ee health --robot-insights |
| ee proximity (G6) | graph.proximity.unreachable | nodes in different components | (information) |
| ee memory revise (G7) | graph.dominance.no_revision_chain | memory has no logical_id chain | (information) |

| ee why HITS (G10) | graph.hits.convergence_failure | iteration cap reached without convergence | run: ee graph snapshot refresh |

title: Epic.snapshot-lifecycle: Eviction, memory footprint, and refresh-cadence policy for 5 subgraphs
description:
## Why
F1 adds 4 new subgraph types alongside the existing memory_links. Each gets snapshotted independently. Naive accumulation leads to: (a) disk bloat (graph_snapshots table grows unbounded), (b) RAM pressure (background refresh job holds multiple snapshots in memory), (c) refresh-cadence conflicts (5 different cadences may collide).

## Decisions to ratify
1. **Eviction**: After a successful new snapshot lands, prior snapshot of the same graph_type goes to status=Archived. Snapshots >7 days old in Archived state are pruned by a maintenance job (ee maintenance graph-snapshot-prune).
2. **Memory footprint**: Each snapshot in memory ≤ 50MB (target). For workspaces with >10k memories, fnx-classes graph is uncached; algorithms operate on rebuild-each-time mode with degraded.large_graph code.
3. **Refresh cadence**:
   - MemoryLinks: every write (existing behavior preserved).
   - CausalEvidence: every causal_evidence INSERT.
   - RevisionDAG: every memory edit / logical_id change.
   - RuleProvenance: nightly + on-demand via ee graph snapshot refresh.
   - ContradictionSubgraph: every contradicts memory_link INSERT.
4. **Conflict resolution**: 300s advisory lock per graph_type (separate locks per type — refreshing causal and rules in parallel is fine; two refreshes of the same type are serialized).

## Tasks
1. Update F1 body to incorporate these decisions.
2. New maintenance subcommand: ee maintenance graph-snapshot-prune.
3. Add storage-footprint contract test: 5k-memory fixture stays under 250MB total snapshot disk.
4. Document in docs/architecture/graph-snapshots.md.

## Acceptance
- Eviction job runs on demand and removes Archived >7d.
- Per-type advisory lock prevents double-refresh.
- Storage footprint test green.
- Documentation page committed.

title: Epic.rollout: Phased implementation order + feature-flag rollout for 10 graph features
description:
## Why
86 beads is a lot. Big-bang release risks: (a) hidden cross-feature dependencies, (b) compounding bugs, (c) one feature stalling holds up the rest. Need explicit phases + feature flags so partial completion is shippable.

## Phase plan
- **Phase α (foundation)**: F1.a-F1.e + F2.a-F2.d + F4.a-F4.b. Ships nothing user-facing. Validates the wrapper conventions and snapshot framework on the existing pagerank surface. Closes when refactored pagerank passes byte-identical insta tests.
- **Phase β (insights scaffold)**: F3.a-F3.b + RX1 (schema gov). Lands ee insights as an empty bundle that returns valid JSON. Sections are stubs that return null with degraded.section_not_yet_implemented.
- **Phase γ (first 3 features)**: G1 (PPR), G4 (k-truss + contradictions), G5 (articulation + onion). These three deliver immediate value (better packs, health diagnostics, smarter decay) and validate the framework with diverse algorithms.
- **Phase δ (composites)**: G2 (Pack DNA — composes G1 + G4), G8 (skyline — composes G4 + G5 + G1). Demonstrates the triangulation pattern.
- **Phase ε (deep math)**: G3 (causal), G6 (Gomory-Hu), G7 (dominance), G9 (bipartite), G10 (HITS). Each independent; can ship in any order.

## Feature flags
Each G feature gates behind a config flag: graph.feature.<name>.enabled = false (default during phase α/β, default=true after phase γ).
Examples: graph.feature.ppr.enabled, graph.feature.pack_dna.enabled, graph.feature.causal_explain.enabled.

When a feature is disabled: its surface still exists but returns degraded.feature_disabled (so agents see honest output, not a missing field).

## Acceptance
- 5 phase milestones documented in docs/rollout/graph-accretion.md.
- 10 feature flags wired through config.
- Phase α can ship to production with no user-visible changes (just framework).
- Disabling a flag at runtime suppresses the feature's output and emits degraded.feature_disabled.

FILE SURFACE: src/config/file.rs, src/config/merge.rs, src/config/mod.rs, src/core/config_surface.rs, docs/rollout/**

title: Re-scope preflight to deterministic evidence matching and move advice prompts to skills
description:
## Background

Preflight is useful when it mechanically matches task text or explicit event metadata against stored rules, high-utility memories, dependency contracts, and tripwires. It crosses the boundary when it performs broad task-risk assessment or emits ask-now advice as though the CLI understood the task.

Audit anchors: `src/core/preflight.rs` uses keyword risk patterns and emits ask-now prompts/must-verify checks even when no persisted evidence exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

See this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field for the detailed completion contract, including unit/static checks, e2e or docs/e2e coverage, detailed logging, and no-feature-loss requirements.
design: Keep deterministic matching, risk categories derived from explicit rule metadata, generated tripwires with provenance, and degraded output when evidence is missing. Move human/agent questioning, rollback planning, and nuanced risk review to a project-local preflight skill.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- `ee preflight run` separates evidence-backed matches from heuristic task-text matches; heuristic-only output is clearly low-confidence or degraded.
- Ask-now prompts and broad advice are removed from CLI or replaced by skill handoff suggestions.
- Generated tripwires include stable IDs, source kind, source ID, score, trigger terms, and provenance.
- Show/close read persisted preflight runs or return honest not-found/degraded responses.
- Unit tests cover empty evidence, no task text, forbidden dependency contracts, high-risk source ordering, stable IDs, and threshold boundaries.
- E2E scripts log evidence sources, generated tripwire IDs, degradation codes, mutation posture, schema validation, and stdout/stderr isolation.
close_reason: Completed: preflight/tripwire paths now separate evidence-backed output from unavailable heuristic advice, persisted show/close behavior degrades honestly, generated tripwires include provenance, and focused degraded-honesty/status/golden checks plus cargo check/clippy passed before the later unrelated src/cli/mod.rs clippy drift.

title: Epic: Retrieval Completeness — Speed Modes, EQL, Scoring (§13)
description:
Source: COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_TO_MAKE_EE__OPUS.md §13 (Hybrid retrieval pipeline), §13.5 (EQL-inspired JSON query schema), §13.6 (answer envelope), and §27.1 unit test list.

# Epic: Retrieval Completeness — Speed Modes, Full EQL Query Schema, Scoring Formula

## Why this epic exists

ee's retrieval surface is the most user-visible and the most determinism-sensitive. The plan documents an 8-stage pipeline with a precise scoring formula, three speed modes that map onto Frankensearch's TwoTierSearcher phases, and a 15-field EQL-inspired JSON query schema. The current beads cover the lexical+semantic baseline and a partial filter wiring, but they do NOT pin down:

- The `--speed instant|default|quality` triad and its mapping onto TwoTier Phase-1 / Phase-2 budgets.
- The canonical scoring formula `final = base × quality × structure × risk`, with the per-multiplier expansion (recency τ=30 days, confidence floor 0.1, utility linear in [0.5, 1.0], maturity step table, harmful_penalty floor 0.2 with -0.1 per harmful hit), tied to the [scoring] config block.
- The full EQL JSON query document beyond simple filters: graph.center / hops / relations, tags_mode (any|all), time.since / until, confidence.min, rerank: true, return_subgraph: true, explain: true.
- The canonical short-tag vocabulary used in the answer envelope's `why[]` array (workspace_scope, tag_match:<tag>, proven_rule, graph_central, derived_from, same_error, etc.).

Without this epic, agents calling `ee context "<task>" --json` cannot rely on the same task input giving comparable JSON across versions, the eval harness cannot regress on per-component score deltas, and the §13 explainability promise is undelivered.

## Cross-cutting constraints (apply to every child bead under this epic)

- Determinism is non-negotiable: the same DB + indexes + config + query must produce byte-identical JSON output and identical pack_hash. Determinism is asserted by a golden test that runs the same call N=10 times and diffs the outputs.
- Score components are emitted as a structured `components: { recency, confidence, utility, maturity, harmful_penalty, scope_match, graph_centrality, redundancy, … }` object on every hit when `--explain` is set. Each component's range and meaning is documented in the bead's acceptance criteria.
- The scoring formula is bound to the [scoring] config block (8 keys: recency_tau_days, confidence_floor, utility_floor, harmful_penalty_per_hit, harmful_penalty_floor, scope_match_bonus, graph_centrality_weight, redundancy_lambda). Changing a key without updating the golden expansion is caught by the golden test.
- Speed modes have hard p50 / p99 targets from §28; the criterion bench gates each mode's regression at 30% of the rolling baseline.
- Each EQL field has a parser unit test (valid + adversarial), a serializer round-trip test (parse → render → parse → equal AST), and a real-binary e2e test that drives `ee context --query-file <document>` and asserts the field actually constrained the result.
- Tests log: query document, parsed AST snapshot, candidate pool size before and after each pipeline stage, top-K with score components, total elapsed_ms, and a first_failure_diagnosis on assertion failure.

## Closure criteria

- `--speed instant`, `--speed default`, `--speed quality` are wired to TwoTier Phase-1 / Phase-2 budgets with a documented mapping; each has a criterion bench tied to the §28 latency table.
- The canonical scoring formula is implemented as `crate::search::scoring::final_score(...)` and unit-tested with the §27.1 boundary cases (0×, 1×, 2×, 10× recency half-life; harmful hit count 0..6; maturity in {Working, Episodic, Semantic, Procedural-Established, Procedural-Proven}).
- Every EQL field from §13.5 has a parser, validator, executor pass, and at least one golden e2e test that asserts the field's effect on the result set.
- The `why[]` short-tag vocabulary is defined as a module-level enum + golden coverage that asserts each tag is reachable through at least one query path.
- `ee why result:<doc-id>` and `ee why <rule-id>` are first-class CLI paths, not falling through to the default memory-id branch.
- The 8-stage pipeline contract is asserted by a single integration test that captures candidates per stage and asserts monotonic narrowing + audit-row coverage.

## Verification path

- Unit tests in `src/search/scoring.rs`, `src/search/query.rs`, `src/search/pipeline.rs`.
- Golden tests in `tests/snapshots/scoring_*` and `tests/snapshots/eql_*`.
- E2E in `tests/eql_query_full_surface.rs` and `tests/retrieval_pipeline_eight_stage.rs`.
- Bench in `benches/search_speed_modes.rs`.
