title: EE-019: Add stdout/stderr stream isolation tests
description:
Source plan item: EE-019 from the `Foundation` backlog.

Task: Add stdout/stderr stream isolation tests

Background and intent:
Establish the Rust workspace, core crate boundaries, runtime shell, error model, and test harness that every later subsystem depends on. This is the delivery foundation: no feature work should bypass these invariants.

Why this matters:
This bead contributes to the overarching goal of making `ee` a dependable local memory substrate for coding agents: useful before work, auditable after work, and safe under degraded conditions. The work should be implemented in the smallest coherent slice that fully satisfies the public contract implied by the title.

Dependency context:
Original plan dependencies: EE-016, EE-017. These are also represented as br dependency edges where the referenced bead exists.

Non-negotiable constraints:
Global implementation invariants for this task:
- Keep the CLI local-first, deterministic, and agent-native; stdout is data, stderr is diagnostics.
- Preserve the no-Tokio and no-rusqlite constraint unless a later ADR explicitly changes the architecture.
- Use SQLModel Rust plus FrankenSQLite for durable data; do not introduce a second storage stack.
- Use Asupersync for async edges and cancellation/budget behavior; do not smuggle in a Tokio executor.
- Keep JSON as the canonical public contract. TOON, Markdown, diagrams, and MCP are renderers or adapters over the same domain data.
- Mutating commands need dry-run/idempotency/audit behavior unless the task explicitly says otherwise.
- Add focused tests proportional to risk: unit tests for domain logic, contract/golden tests for public output, and integration/evaluation tests for cross-subsystem behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including the comprehensive testing and logging requirements.
design:
Suggested design approach:
- Runtime boundaries must preserve `Outcome`, request budgets, capability narrowing, and cancellation semantics through Asupersync rather than Tokio.
- Tests are part of the deliverable, not a follow-up. Golden output should be deterministic with fixed IDs, timestamps, ordering, and schema versions.

title: Epic: Curation Proposers, Workspace Review, Playbook YAML Surface (§16, §17)
description:
Source: COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_TO_MAKE_EE__OPUS.md §16 (Curation, consolidation, and review), §17 (Procedural memory & playbooks), §15.2 (turn_looks_important heuristics).

# Epic: Curation Proposers, Workspace Review, Playbook YAML Surface

## Why this epic exists

§16 describes the propose → validate → apply curation flow with two named proposers (cluster-based summary EE-187 and rule-extraction EE-188 in §16.2 and §16.3) and a `ee review workspace` command that runs review across every CASS-recorded session in the workspace. §17.1 specifies a hand-editable `playbook.yaml` schema for procedural rules and the round-trip `ee playbook export/import/extract/list` family. Today the curation candidate table, validate, and apply paths exist, but:

- No bead implements the cluster-based summary proposer (single-link agglomerative on cosine, threshold 0.78, deterministic order via cgse, cluster-size ≥ 3).
- No bead implements the pattern-based rule-extraction proposer (sentence markers: "always", "never", "prefer", "avoid", "make sure to", "we found that").
- The scope-sanity sub-check inside `ee curate validate` is not bead-tracked.
- `ee review workspace` (multi-session) has no bead — only `ee review session` exists, and a STUB bead acknowledges the README/CLI mismatch.
- The complete `ee playbook *` command family with `playbook.yaml.bak` rolling-backup is missing.
- The `turn_looks_important` heuristic that gates which CASS turns become candidates has no bead either, so the import side that feeds curation is undefined.

This epic exists to close the curation pipeline end-to-end: a real session yields candidates, candidates yield rules, rules round-trip through hand-editable YAML, and every transition is audited.

## Cross-cutting constraints (apply to every child bead under this epic)

- Proposers are deterministic: same input fixtures + same fnx-cgse seed → same candidates in the same order. Assert via golden.
- Validation produces a 4-class output: `Ok`, `Warning(reason)`, `Rejected(reason)`, `Pending(blocker)`. Each child bead must say which classes it can produce and golden-cover them.
- The propose/validate/apply triad is gated; no apply without a prior validate Ok in the same audit chain.
- `ee playbook export` and `ee playbook import` are byte-stable round-trips: parse YAML → render → parse → equal. The schema string is `ee.playbook.v1` and is asserted by golden.
- `playbook.yaml.bak` is written before every apply; only the last 5 backups are kept (rolling).
- Every command has --dry-run and --json modes. The dry-run JSON contains `would_propose: N`, `would_validate: N`, `would_apply: N`, `audit_preview: [...]`.
- Tests log: input fixture path, candidate ids generated, validation outcomes per candidate, apply targets, audit row ids, total elapsed_ms.

## Closure criteria

- Cluster-based summary proposer implemented; unit + golden + e2e tests cover small/large/threshold-edge fixtures.
- Pattern-based rule-extraction proposer implemented; the 6 sentence markers each have positive + adversarial fixtures.
- `ee curate validate` includes specificity, evidence-resolves, duplication, scope-sanity, and redaction sub-checks. Each sub-check has its own bead under this epic.
- `ee review workspace` implemented; idempotent across runs (same inputs → same candidates).
- `ee playbook export/import/extract/list` implemented; YAML schema golden; rolling backup + restore tested.
- `turn_looks_important` heuristic implemented as a pure function with the four documented signals (non-zero exit code, "why did that fail" + long assistant reply, conventional markers like `# Lesson learned`, high-token thinking-mode) — fixture-driven unit tests + a CASS import e2e.
- The full curation epic gate: a single integration test (tests/curation_pipeline_e2e.rs) imports a CASS fixture session, runs `ee review session --propose`, applies an Ok candidate, exports the resulting rule into `playbook.yaml`, edits the YAML in-place, imports it back, and asserts the rule reflects the edit and the audit chain is intact.

## Verification path

- Unit tests under `src/curate/` and `src/playbook/`.
- Goldens in `tests/snapshots/curate_*` and `tests/snapshots/playbook_*`.
- E2E in `tests/curation_pipeline_e2e.rs`, `tests/playbook_round_trip.rs`.

title: EE-DIAG-001: Add redacted diagnostic support bundle command and schema
description:
Define and implement an agent-native redacted diagnostic support bundle command and schema.

Background:
The bead graph already has strong individual pieces for status, health, capabilities, doctor/fix-plan, DB integrity, redacted JSONL export, failure replay artifacts, command-effect manifests, fixture provenance, closure dossiers, and CI artifact policy. The remaining operational gap is that an agent in the middle of a failing run still has to manually assemble those pieces into a trustworthy handoff packet.

This bead adds a single support-bundle contract so agents can capture the state of an EE workspace, the relevant diagnostics, and the exact evidence needed for another agent or future self to continue without losing privacy, provenance, or stdout/stderr discipline.

Intended public surface:
- `ee support bundle --json --redacted --out <dir>` creates a redacted diagnostic bundle only at an explicit output path and prints a machine-readable manifest to stdout.
- `ee support bundle --dry-run --json` reports exactly what would be collected, why, redaction posture, size estimates, and excluded unsafe/raw sources without writing a bundle.
- `ee support bundle inspect <path> --json` validates a previously created bundle and reports schema version, content hashes, redaction status, included evidence, and replay/doctor hints.

The bundle is not a backup and is not a raw database export. It is a privacy-preserving diagnostic evidence packet optimized for agents.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including comprehensive unit tests, e2e tests, golden/schema fixtures, privacy checks, and detailed logging requirements.
design:
Recommended design:
- Define a strict `support_bundle.v1` schema with a top-level manifest and optional files under deterministic subpaths. The manifest should be the canonical stdout payload and should include every included artifact path, hash, schema version, redaction summary, source command, and degradation code.
- Include data by reference and summary where possible: status, health, capabilities, doctor/fix-plan, DB integrity summary, migration/schema versions, dependency/capability matrix excerpts, index freshness, fixture/effect/closure manifest hashes, recent redacted failure summaries, and explicit pointers to replay artifacts.
- Never include raw secrets, raw unredacted logs, raw DB files, or raw session transcripts by default. If a future explicit unsafe mode is ever added, it must require a separate bead, a distinct command flag, and scary schema fields that make the privacy downgrade machine-visible.
- Treat bundle creation as an explicit artifact write, not a durable EE state mutation. It must be idempotent with deterministic content under fixed fixtures and must support dry-run/no-write planning.
- Keep stdout as the manifest only. Progress, collection decisions, skipped items, redaction events, size warnings, and first-failure diagnostics go to stderr or bundle-local diagnostics files referenced by the manifest.
- Bundle inspection should validate hashes, schema versions, expected redaction classes/counts, missing artifacts, stale fix-plan data, and unsupported future versions without trying to mutate the bundle.
- The command should remain useful under degradation: if a subsystem is unavailable, include a stable degradation code and next action rather than failing the entire bundle unless the output path itself or manifest write fails.
- The support bundle should be usable from CLI and, later, MCP as the same core service; MCP must remain a thin adapter and not fork bundle semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance criteria:
- `ee support bundle --dry-run --json` returns an `ee.response.v1` payload listing planned artifacts, source commands, privacy posture, expected redaction classes, size estimates, excluded raw sources, degraded/unavailable subsystems, and whether a real bundle would be complete enough for handoff.
- `ee support bundle --json --redacted --out <dir>` writes a deterministic redacted diagnostic bundle only under the explicit output path and prints only the manifest response to stdout.
- `ee support bundle inspect <path> --json` validates manifest schema, content hashes, required artifacts, redaction summaries, schema/API versions, migration versions, fixture/effect/closure manifest hashes, and supported version ranges.
- The bundle manifest includes stable IDs and hashes for status, health, capabilities, doctor/fix-plan, DB integrity summary, dependency/capability matrix excerpts, index freshness, redacted failure/replay artifacts, fixture provenance, command-effect manifests, closure dossiers, and relevant degraded codes.
- The bundle never includes raw DB files, raw unredacted logs, raw session transcripts, raw secrets, user-global config secrets, or unrelated workspace files by default.
- Redaction reporting is explicit: class, count, stable evidence hash where safe, source artifact, and whether validation used raw synthetic fixtures or already-redacted data.
- Bundle creation is idempotent for fixed fixtures, timestamps, stable IDs, and deterministic ordering; repeated runs produce the same manifest content hash except for explicitly declared run metadata.
- Dry-run and inspect never mutate EE state. Bundle creation mutates only the explicit output directory and records that artifact write in command-effect expectations.
- Degraded subsystems produce partial but honest bundles with stable degradation codes and next actions; only output-path failures, manifest write failures, schema serialization failures, and redaction failures are hard errors.
- Public schemas and golden fixtures cover dry-run, successful bundle, partial degraded bundle, redaction failure, inspect success, inspect stale/unsupported version, missing artifact, and hash mismatch.

Testing and logging requirements:
- Add unit tests for artifact selection, deterministic ordering, manifest hashing, redaction summary aggregation, unsafe-source exclusion, degraded subsystem inclusion, dry-run planning, output-path validation, inspect validation, hash mismatch detection, and unsupported-version handling.
- Add contract/golden tests for every public response shape and for the bundle-local manifest schema.
- Add real-binary e2e coverage that creates a support bundle in an isolated workspace, validates stdout/stderr isolation, inspects the bundle, checks redaction, checks content hashes, and proves no hidden EE state mutation occurred beyond the explicit output artifact.
- Add a degraded/offline e2e fixture where search index, CASS/session import, or a derived analyzer is unavailable; the bundle must remain useful and include stable degraded codes with next actions.
- Add privacy regression tests with synthetic secrets in logs, config-like values, session-like text, and fixture data; raw synthetic secrets must not appear in stdout, bundle manifests, redacted artifacts, failure summaries, or inspect output.
- Add adversarial/property coverage for path traversal in `--out`, duplicate artifact IDs, huge logs, invalid UTF-8/control characters, malformed prior bundles, stale hashes, symlinked output paths, and concurrent bundle creation attempts.
- E2E/logged tests must capture command, cwd/workspace, sanitized environment overrides, elapsed time, exit code, stdout/stderr artifact paths, bundle path, manifest hash, schema/golden validation status, redaction status, command-effect classification, and first-failure diagnosis.
- Stdout assertions must prove stdout contains only machine data; collection progress, skipped-artifact explanations, redaction events, warnings, and debugging context must go to stderr or explicit bundle-local artifacts.
- Closeout evidence must include the generated fixture IDs, scenario IDs, manifest content hashes, command-effect manifest entries, and exact verification commands needed for a future agent to reproduce the checks.
notes: Added during repeated bead quality review after targeted searches for support bundles, diagnostic bundles, bug-report bundles, and redacted diagnostics returned no existing bead. This is intentionally not a backup/export replacement. It is a compact, privacy-preserving diagnostic handoff contract that makes EE easier for agents to operate under failure, degradation, handoff, and future debugging.

title: [implements-surface:eval] Real ee eval run/list with deterministic fixtures and golden reports
description:
## Background
Stub: `EVAL_UNAVAILABLE_CODE = "eval_fixtures_unavailable"` at src/cli/mod.rs:5562. Honesty closure: eidetic_engine_cli-uiy3 (built fixture corpus, did not implement runner). README §Diagnostics promises "Run or list retrieval-quality evaluation fixtures." Plan §27 (testing strategy & evaluation harness).

## What ships
1. Eval-fixture loader reading tests/fixtures/eval/*.json (registry + per-fixture queries with expected memory IDs).
2. Eval runner that opens a deterministic test workspace (LabRuntime + hash embedder), seeds the corpus, runs hybrid retrieval per query, computes Precision@k, nDCG@k, MRR, and answer-coverage.
3. Versioned JSON report `{schema:"ee.eval.report.v1", fixture, metrics, per_query[], duration_ms, data_hash}`.
4. `ee eval list` enumerates available fixtures from the registry.
5. `ee eval run <fixture-id> [--json]` executes one and reports.
6. Golden snapshot per fixture in tests/golden/eval/.

## Acceptance
- Same fixture → byte-identical JSON output (hashed in test).
- EVAL_UNAVAILABLE_CODE constant deleted from src/cli/mod.rs in same PR.
- Unit + integration + golden tests cover happy path, missing fixture, malformed query, empty result, perfect-recall result.
- README command reference no longer cites stub status.
- Closure linter passes.

title: [HIGH] tests/mcp_parity.rs is cfg(feature="mcp") and CI never enables the feature — 9 parity tests dormant
description:
Repro:
  1. `tests/mcp_parity.rs:11` opens with `#![cfg(feature = "mcp")]`.
  2. The MCP module itself in `src/lib.rs:23-24` is `#[cfg(feature = "mcp")] pub mod mcp;`.
  3. Default features in `Cargo.toml:33` are `["fts5", "json", "embed-fast", "lexical-bm25"]` — no `"mcp"`.
  4. The CI workflow `.github/workflows/ci.yml:44` runs `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`, with no `--features mcp` and no `--all-features`.
  5. Run `cargo test --workspace --all-targets` — the 9 `mcp_parity` tests are silently dropped (entire test crate is `#![cfg(feature = "mcp")]`-gated).

Expected: a bead that closes with the message "9 tests verifying JSON
output parity between CLI commands and MCP tools" should produce 9 tests
that run in the default test suite, or at minimum be exercised on every
CI build via an explicit `cargo test --features mcp` step.

Actual: in default CI / local `cargo test`, zero MCP parity assertions
fire. The tests compile only when `--features mcp` is explicitly passed,
which CI never does. So the bead's closure evidence is dormant.

Evidence-line:
  Cargo.toml:33 (default features omit `mcp`)
  Cargo.toml:41 (`mcp = []` — empty feature definition; AGENTS.md says it
                  should be `mcp = ["dep:rust-mcp-sdk"]`, so today the
                  feature gates a module that has no opt-in deps to pull)
  src/lib.rs:23-24 (cfg-gated module)
  tests/mcp_parity.rs:11 (cfg-gated whole test file)
  .github/workflows/ci.yml:44 (no --features mcp)
  Bead eidetic_engine_cli-phje closed in e4a4e43.

Suggested fix:
  - EITHER add `mcp` to the default features so CI exercises the parity
    suite. (Cleanest if the project's default story is "MCP available out
    of the box".)
  - OR add an explicit CI step:
        cargo test --workspace --features mcp tests/mcp_parity.rs
    so the 9 tests run on every build.
  - AND fix Cargo.toml:41 — the feature should pull in
    `rust-mcp-sdk` (or whatever crate the mcp module actually depends
    on) per AGENTS.md.

Severity rationale: the parity tests are real and well-designed, but
they don't gate any merge today. Any drift between the CLI output
shape and the MCP adapter goes undetected in CI.
close_reason: Added CI MCP feature-profile parity gate and workflow guard; RCH cargo test --workspace --features mcp --test mcp_parity -- --list reached remote exit 0 and listed all 9 parity tests.

title: [perf-forensics][compare] Add deterministic regression comparison core
description:
## Background

Once artifacts are normalized, `ee` needs a deterministic comparison engine that can tell agents what changed between a baseline and candidate run. The output must be useful without a profiler but honest about confidence and missing evidence.

## Scope

Implement a pure/read-only comparison core over normalized artifact summaries. It should compute metric deltas, severity bands, confidence, degraded states, profile/fixture compatibility, and likely subsystem owner hints.

## Acceptance criteria

- Baseline/candidate comparison is deterministic for identical inputs.
- Metrics compare by stable name and unit; missing metrics produce `metric_missing` degradations rather than zero deltas.
- Severity bands distinguish no regression, advisory regression, warning regression, and blocking regression using explicit profile-aware thresholds.
- Owner hints are stable and evidence-backed for at least `search`, `pack`, `db`, `cache`, `writeSpool`, `profile`, `hostPressure`, and `unknown`.
- Profile mismatch and fixture tier mismatch are visible in output and reduce confidence.
- Comparison never reads or emits raw logs, raw memory text, raw query text, raw command output, secrets, or host-specific paths.
- Unit tests cover latency regression, memory regression, cache hit regression, write queue regression, missing metrics, mismatched profile, unsupported schema, and deterministic tie ordering.

## Testing and logging

Tests should use small synthetic summaries and exact JSON snapshots for deterministic fields. RCH-backed `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are required before closure.
close_reason: compare_artifacts() with 16 tests covering latency/memory/cache/write-queue regressions, missing metrics, profile/fixture-tier mismatches, hash tampering, deterministic ordering; SubsystemOwner inference for search/pack/db/cache/write_spool/profile/host_pressure; severity bands and confidence calculation

title: [MEDIUM] db/mod.rs is_lock_held tolerates stale canonical-key rows but acquire never reaps them
close_reason: Fixed: advisory lock acquisition now queries and arbitrates by logical resource_type/resource_id, so stale canonical-key rows for the same logical resource block acquisition while active and are reaped when expired before inserting the current canonical key. release_advisory_lock now releases by logical resource identity plus holder. is_lock_held skips expired newer stale rows and can still report an older active logical row. Added regression tests for active stale rows, expired stale cleanup, logical release, and stale held lookup. UBS residuals on src/db/mod.rs are pre-existing heuristic integer-flag comparisons.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
src/db/mod.rs:8408-8430 is_lock_held does:
```
SELECT ... FROM ee_advisory_locks
WHERE resource_type = ?1 AND resource_id = ?2
ORDER BY acquired_at DESC LIMIT 1
```
The bdab856 commit message says this lookup style supports 'a stale row with a slightly different canonical key still exists (e.g. after a key-format migration)'. But acquire_advisory_lock_in_transaction (8310-8320) only consults WHERE resource_key = ?1, and release_advisory_lock (8390-8402) deletes WHERE resource_key = ? AND holder_id = ?. There is no code path that prunes stale (resource_type, resource_id) rows whose resource_key differs from the current canonical encoding.

Concrete failure: holder A acquires v1-encoded resource_key, code is upgraded to v2 encoding, holder A attempts release with v2 key — DELETE finds nothing, function returns false. Holder B then acquires v2 key successfully. is_lock_held now returns the row with the most recent acquired_at, which depends on row ordering — possibly the stale v1 row, which falsely advertises a held lock to a third party.

Fix: either (a) acquire_advisory_lock_in_transaction also clears stale rows for the same (resource_type, resource_id), or (b) cleanup_expired_locks scans by (resource_type, resource_id) and reaps duplicates. Add a regression test that multi-encoded rows for the same logical resource resolve consistently.

title: EE-452: Implement `ee causal estimate --json` with evidence tiers, assumptions, confounders, and conservative confidence states
description:
Source plan item: EE-452 from the `Causal Memory Credit And Uplift` backlog.

Task: Implement `ee causal estimate --json` with evidence tiers, assumptions, confounders, and conservative confidence states

Background and intent:
Estimate whether memory interventions actually changed agent behavior or outcomes, distinguishing useful influence from mere exposure or popularity.

Why this matters:
This bead contributes to the overarching goal of making `ee` a dependable local memory substrate for coding agents: useful before work, auditable after work, and safe under degraded conditions. The work should be implemented in the smallest coherent slice that fully satisfies the public contract implied by the title.

Dependency context:
Original plan dependencies: EE-451, EE-444. These are also represented as br dependency edges where the referenced bead exists.

Non-negotiable constraints:
Global implementation invariants for this task:
- Keep the CLI local-first, deterministic, and agent-native; stdout is data, stderr is diagnostics.
- Preserve the no-Tokio and no-rusqlite constraint unless a later ADR explicitly changes the architecture.
- Use SQLModel Rust plus FrankenSQLite for durable data; do not introduce a second storage stack.
- Use Asupersync for async edges and cancellation/budget behavior; do not smuggle in a Tokio executor.
- Keep JSON as the canonical public contract. TOON, Markdown, diagrams, and MCP are renderers or adapters over the same domain data.
- Mutating commands need dry-run/idempotency/audit behavior unless the task explicitly says otherwise.
- Add focused tests proportional to risk: unit tests for domain logic, contract/golden tests for public output, and integration/evaluation tests for cross-subsystem behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including the comprehensive testing and logging requirements.
design:
Suggested design approach:
- Command output must use the stable `ee.response.v1` envelope, preserve stdout/stderr isolation, and provide useful degraded-state metadata.
- Distinguish exposure, plausible influence, replay-backed hypotheses, and experimental evidence. Do not claim causal uplift from correlation alone.

Implementation guidance:
- Read the surrounding modules and existing project conventions before editing.
- Prefer the planned crate boundaries from the comprehensive plan: CLI wiring in `ee-cli`, reusable domain/services in `ee-core`, models in `ee-models`, persistence in `ee-db`, output rendering in `ee-output`, and adapters in their own optional crates.
- Keep public contracts stable and versioned. Any data structure that leaves the process through CLI/MCP/hook/export should have a schema and at least one golden fixture.
- If a dependency or upstream Franken project is not ready, implement the smallest honest diagnostic/degraded path rather than faking behavior.
- Document any architectural exception with an ADR-oriented note and a verification hook.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance criteria:
- The behavior described by `Implement `ee causal estimate --json` with evidence tiers, assumptions, confounders, and conservative confidence states` is implemented or, for spikes, conclusively reported with a clear go/no-go recommendation.
- The implementation preserves local-first, no-Tokio, no-rusqlite, agent-native CLI behavior.
- Public command output, if any, validates against the stable response envelope and does not pollute stdout with diagnostics.
- Relevant unit, integration, golden, contract, or evaluation tests are added and named so future agents can find them.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the relevant test subset pass after implementation.
- Any degraded or unavailable dependency state returns a stable error/degradation code with a useful next action.

title: [CONCURRENCY] cass import ledger: read-modify-write counters lose updates
description:
Files: src/cass/import.rs:766, src/cass/import.rs:814, src/db/mod.rs:4291.
Code path: ensure_running_ledger reads the existing ledger by source and writes attempt_count = existing.attempt_count + 1. complete_ledger later re-reads the row and writes imported_session_count/imported_span_count = existing counts + local delta. DbConnection::update_import_ledger overwrites absolute counter values. None of these read-modify-write sequences are enclosed in one transaction or implemented as atomic SQL increments.
Hazard: concurrent imports sharing a source_id can lose attempts and imported count increments. Interleaving: A and B both read attempt_count=1; both update to 2, so two attempts record as one. The same pattern applies to imported_session_count/imported_span_count in complete_ledger.
Repro plan: add a file-backed concurrency test with two connections and a barrier around ensure_running_ledger/complete_ledger. Expected final attempt_count and imported counts equal the sum of both callers. Fix with a single transaction using BEGIN IMMEDIATE plus UPDATE ... SET count = count + ? or route ledger writes through the write owner.

title: [MEDIUM] redaction policy missing common secret formats — Slack, Twilio, Azure, Discord, NPM, HuggingFace, OAuth access/refresh tokens
description:
## Surface
policy/redaction secret format coverage (audit cycle 7, surface 7)

## What ee covers today
src/policy/mod.rs:36-117 SECRET_KEY_PATTERNS:
- api_key / apikey / api-key
- auth_token, bearer_token, bearer (whitespace value)
- client_secret, connection_string, database_url
- password, passwd, private_key, secret, secret_key, ssh_key, token

src/policy/mod.rs:693-724 RAW_TOKEN_PATTERNS:
- Anthropic (sk-ant-api03-)
- OpenAI (sk-proj-, sk- legacy)
- GitHub (ghp_/gho_/ghs_/ghu_/ghr_)
- AWS (AKIA, ASIA)
- Stripe (sk_live_/sk_test_/rk_live_/rk_test_)
- GCP (AIza)

PEM blocks: covered by redact_pem_blocks (so SSH/TLS private keys are caught when they appear in PEM form).
JWT: covered by redact_jwt_tokens.

## Gaps
Common secrets that ee does NOT redact:

### Raw-prefix tokens missing
- Slack: `xoxb-`, `xoxp-`, `xoxa-`, `xoxr-` (bot, user, app, refresh)
- NPM: `npm_<token>`
- HuggingFace: `hf_<token>`
- PyPI: `pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc...`
- Twilio: `AC<sid>` + auth-token pair
- SendGrid: `SG.<id>.<token>`
- Discord bot tokens: `MT...` / `Nz...` (base64-ish, harder to detect by prefix alone)
- Square: `sq0idp-`, `sq0csp-`
- Mailgun: `key-...` / `pubkey-...`

### Key/value names missing
- `access_token` (very common in OAuth flows)
- `refresh_token`
- `id_token` (OIDC)
- `oauth_token` / `oauth_secret`
- `webhook_secret`
- `signing_key` / `signing_secret`
- `master_key` / `encryption_key`
- `session_token` / `session_secret`
- `aws_secret_access_key` / `aws_access_key_id` (these would be in env files alongside AKIA values)
- `personal_access_token` / `pat`
- `service_account_key` / `service_account_json`

### Format-class missing
- Azure storage account keys (88-char base64; no recognizable prefix, but always paired with `AccountKey=` in connection strings — `connection_string` pattern catches the wrapper but not bare key strings).
- 1Password / LastPass / Bitwarden vault tokens.
- Generic high-entropy base64/hex strings (length+entropy heuristic — e.g., gitleaks 'generic-api-key' rule).

## Why it matters
1. ee's pack/redaction contract claims to mask 'secret-like content'. A user who pastes a Slack bot token into a memory expects redaction; today the raw token leaks into context packs.
2. The new pack-emit redaction (gww5 from cycle 5) runs through redact_secret_like_content — every gap there is also a context-pack leak.
3. Multi-agent swarms often deal with workflow secrets (Slack notifications, Twilio SMS, NPM publishes). These are exactly the audiences ee is built for.

## Fix
1. Extend RAW_TOKEN_PATTERNS with the prefixed tokens (Slack, NPM, HuggingFace, PyPI, Twilio, SendGrid, Square, Mailgun) — prefix-based detection mirrors what's already there, low-risk diff.
2. Extend SECRET_KEY_PATTERNS with: access_token, refresh_token, id_token, oauth_token, oauth_secret, webhook_secret, signing_key, signing_secret, master_key, encryption_key, session_token, aws_secret_access_key, aws_access_key_id, service_account_key.
3. Add an entropy-based fallback redactor for high-entropy base64/hex strings >= 32 chars adjacent to a known-secret keyword.
4. Add a unit test per added pattern (the existing tests in src/policy/mod.rs already follow this pattern; mirror the structure).

## Severity rationale
MEDIUM, not HIGH, because:
- The existing SECRET_KEY_PATTERNS catches generic 'token=' / 'secret=' assignments, so most env-style leaks are already masked.
- The known prefix tokens (Anthropic/OpenAI/GitHub/AWS/Stripe/GCP) cover the most common cases.
- But the gap is real and well-bounded; the fix is small.
close_reason: Completed redaction coverage for common service tokens, OAuth/session/service-account/Azure key names, and adjacent high-entropy secret fallback with inline tests; broader verification blocked by unrelated concurrent tree changes documented in bead comment.

title: Write the mechanical-boundary ADR and product contract
description:
## Background

The README and AGENTS instructions already say `ee` is a durable memory layer, not an agent loop. The audit sharpened that into a stricter product contract: `ee` must be mechanical in execution, while agent harnesses and skills perform judgment around its outputs.

This bead turns that principle into an ADR and developer-facing contract so future roadmap work does not reintroduce fake intelligence, mock reasoning, or skill-like flows into the binary.
design: Write an ADR under `docs/adr/` and, if appropriate, a short developer contract in docs or AGENTS-linked guidance. The ADR should define allowed and disallowed CLI behavior, examples of split surfaces, and how project-local skills relate to the binary. It should also explain why determinism alone is not sufficient if deterministic code fabricates qualitative conclusions.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria

- ADR states that `ee` may compute, retrieve, index, pack, replay, validate, hash, aggregate, redact, and render, but may not invent reasoning, causal claims, procedure quality, or task plans without explicit evidence inputs.
- ADR defines project-local `skills/` as the correct home for agent reasoning workflows that consume `ee` outputs.
- ADR includes concrete examples from lab, causal, learn, preflight, procedure, and situation/plan.
- ADR documents the rule: mock/sample/stub data may exist in tests/fixtures but not production command output.
- ADR includes verification hooks: command inventory check, no-mock-output contract, dependency audit, and skill workflow e2e.
- Unit/docs tests or link checks validate required ADR anchors, command/skill references, and no stale path references if the repo has a suitable docs test mechanism; otherwise an e2e log artifact records the ADR path, required anchors, checked references, and first-failure diagnosis.
- The ADR cross-links the command matrix, fixture corpus, side-effect/idempotency contract, runtime/cancellation contract, degraded-honesty contract, and skill evidence-handoff contract so future implementers do not need the original conversation.

title: Re-scope lab commands to evidence-only capture, replay, and hypothesis export
description:
## Background

`ee lab` is valuable if it captures redacted episodes, replays frozen evidence, compares context packs, and exports hypotheses for an agent to review. It crosses the boundary when it fabricates original/counterfactual outcomes or implies a memory would have changed agent behavior.

Audit anchors: `src/core/lab.rs` includes capture/replay/counterfactual paths that currently produce simulated success/failure semantics. Gate 15 had good safety language, but implementation must be rechecked against the stricter mechanical boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

See this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field for the detailed completion contract, including unit/static checks, e2e or docs/e2e coverage, detailed logging, and no-feature-loss requirements.
design: Keep mechanical lab surfaces in Rust: episode capture, redaction, repository fingerprinting, pack hashes, frozen replay manifests, changed-pack diffs, mutation posture, and hypothesis records. Move interpretive failure analysis to a skill bead. If true replay is not yet wired, return degraded JSON rather than simulated outcomes.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- `ee lab capture` records or dry-runs only concrete episode metadata: redaction status, pack hash, policy IDs, outcome refs, repo fingerprint, and evidence IDs.
- `ee lab replay` reads frozen episode inputs or reports exactly which frozen inputs are missing; it must not access mutable current state silently.
- `ee lab counterfactual` emits pack diffs and hypothesis records only; no field may claim the agent would have succeeded, failed, learned, or changed behavior unless backed by explicit replay evidence.
- All generated curation candidates remain validate/apply-only and never mutate durable memory directly.
- Unit tests cover empty evidence, missing frozen inputs, redacted payloads, pack-hash stability, and no-mutation posture.
- E2E scripts with boundary logging cover capture, replay, degraded missing replay input, counterfactual dry run, JSON schema validation, stdout/stderr isolation, and first-failure diagnosis.

Implementation records concrete capture metadata only (redaction status/classes, pack hash, policy IDs, outcome refs, repo fingerprint, evidence IDs), replay reports missing frozen inputs without mutable current-state access, and counterfactual emits hypothesis-only pack diffs/records with no behavior-success claims or durable mutation. title: SRR6.41: Peer admission control, rate limits, and resource isolation
description:
Add per-peer admission control, rate limits, payload limits, and hostile-or-overloaded peer protection. Mesh should remain friendly on trusted Tailscale networks, but a buggy or compromised peer must not be able to exhaust disk, memory, CPU, logs, or index jobs.

Scope includes: per-peer concurrent request limits, event batch size limits, body fetch size limits, index job amplification caps, backoff after repeated malformed frames or policy denials, status/doctor reporting for throttled peers, and deterministic tests for budget exhaustion. This should compose with Asupersync budgets and cache quotas rather than inventing a second resource model.

Acceptance: unit tests for admission decisions and limit accounting; e2e script with a noisy peer sending oversized batches/bodies and repeated invalid requests; structured logs for peer_throttled, payload_rejected, budget_exhausted, backoff_until, and local_tier1_unaffected; no forbidden network/runtime dependency added.

title: [LOW] ADR-0018 references V033 plan_recipes migration but actual migration is V035 (post-renumber drift)
description:
Repro:
  1. Read docs/adr/0018-plan-recommend-ranking.md (committed in d0e0224
     2026-05-06 14:55 UTC).
  2. Search line 83: "Requires plan_recipes table migration (V033)".
  3. Read src/db/mod.rs and find:
        V031_CERTIFICATES_AND_TRUST_QUARANTINE
        V032_AUDIT_HASH_CHAIN
        V033_LEARNING_OBSERVATIONS  (NOT plan_recipes)
        V034_PROCEDURE_STORE
        V035_PLAN_RECIPES           (the actual table migration)

  The plan_recipes migration is V035, not V033. V033 is learning
  observations, which has nothing to do with plan recommendation.

Expected: ADR-0018 references the correct migration version
(V035_PLAN_RECIPES, file:src/db/mod.rs).

Actual: ADR-0018:83 says "V033", which is wrong by two versions and
points at a different feature.

Aggravating: the V031 → V033 renumber that mis-anchored the ADR is
itself a separate violation tracked in eidetic_engine_cli-4j7v
(migration-version-reuse). The ADR was probably written against the
intermediate state where V031 was learning_observations and a future
V032 would be plan_recipes; the wave-3 renumber and the subsequent
V034/V035 additions left the ADR stale.

Evidence-line:
  docs/adr/0018-plan-recommend-ranking.md:83 (says V033)
  src/db/mod.rs (V035_PLAN_RECIPES is the actual migration)

Suggested fix: edit ADR-0018 to say V035, and add a one-line
"Migration version" cross-reference at the top of the ADR so future
renumbers cannot silently invalidate the doc.

Severity: LOW. Doc-only drift, no behavioural impact, but it leads
the next agent reading the ADR to grep the wrong migration when
implementing the recommender.
close_reason: Fixed V033→V035 reference in ADR-0018. Added explicit Migration field in frontmatter to link ADR to actual migration line in code.

## Why this matters

`ee graph centrality-refresh` and the snapshot-refresh path call `compute_pagerank` then `compute_betweenness` then (after bd-1o99v) `compute_hits` then HITS-bipartite then dominance, sequentially. Each algorithm uses ~1 worker core inside fnx_algorithms. On a 64-core host this leaves 63 cores idle during the most expensive maintenance window. README perf table shows graph centrality-refresh p99 = 2.0s on 5k links; with the full G-suite landing (HITS, bipartite HITS, dominance, gomory_hu, causal betweenness) the sequential cost will balloon to 10-20s.

The fix is direct: thread these as independent cooperative tasks under one Asupersync `Cx` budget, sharing the input graph (read-only). Asupersync already provides structured concurrency, supervision, and budget accounting — this is exactly what it was designed for.

## Surface

- New `src/graph/cooperative_refresh.rs` with `refresh_centrality_cooperative(cx: &Cx, snapshot: &TypedGraphSnapshot, budget: Duration) -> GraphResult<CooperativeCentralityReport>`.
- Internally spawns N cooperative tasks (one per algorithm) via Asupersync `Scope::child`, each guarded by a per-algorithm sub-budget (default budget/N + 10% slack).
- Aggregates results into the existing CentralityRefreshReport shape so downstream consumers don't change.
- `ee graph centrality-refresh --cooperative` flag (advisory at first, default after a measured-safe migration).

## Cx-honoring discipline

Every algorithm subtask MUST: (a) poll `cx.is_cancelled()` between iterations; (b) on cancel, drop partial state and return a `degraded` signal with code `graph_centrality_cancelled`; (c) emit a witness counting iterations actually performed. The supervisor task aggregates the reports and degrades the overall CentralityRefreshReport with `partial_centrality_due_to_cancellation` when any subtask cancelled.

## Determinism

Cooperative scheduling could observe race-dependent iteration counts. The user-facing JSON output is from the *deterministic post-merge* of per-algorithm scores keyed by memory_id (BTreeMap), so byte-stable output is preserved as long as each algorithm's own determinism contract holds. Witness fields (elapsed_ms, iteration_count) ARE non-deterministic and live in a separate `witness` block already scrubbed by the determinism test harness.

## Acceptance

- src/graph/cooperative_refresh.rs lands with refresh_centrality_cooperative + 6 unit tests: empty snapshot, single-algorithm, all-algorithms-converge, one-algorithm-times-out, cancellation-mid-flight, deterministic-output-across-3-runs.
- E2E: tests/e2e_graph_centrality_cooperative.sh seeds a 5k-link workspace, runs the cooperative refresh under a 5s budget, asserts all algorithms converged within budget AND aggregate JSON byte-matches the sequential output (modulo witness fields).
- Perf bench: benches/graph_refresh_cooperative.rs criterion harness compares sequential vs cooperative on 1k/5k/25k-link fixtures; cooperative wins by ≥3x on a 64-core host (CI host class label honored).
- Tracing per bd-3usjw.58: surface=cooperative_centrality, fields { algorithm_count, max_subtask_elapsed_ms, supervisor_overhead_ms, partial_results_count, cancelled_algorithms }.

## Risk register

- fnx_algorithms internal locks: if PageRank shares state with Betweenness inside the franken-stack, parallel calls deadlock. Mitigate by cloning the input DiGraph per subtask (already the pattern used by run_with_budget).
- Memory: cloning a 25k-edge graph 6× costs ~50MB; bounded.
- Scheduler fairness under Asupersync: ensure subtasks yield often enough; add a yield_periodic() helper if needed.

## Cost of omission

Centrality refresh becomes the dominant maintenance-window cost as more graph features ship. A 20s refresh window blocks the daemon's steward loop for a non-trivial fraction of wall time.

## File surface

- src/graph/cooperative_refresh.rs (NEW)
- src/graph/mod.rs (add `pub mod cooperative_refresh;`)
- src/cli/mod.rs (--cooperative flag on `ee graph centrality-refresh`)
- benches/graph_refresh_cooperative.rs (NEW)
- tests/e2e_graph_centrality_cooperative.sh (NEW)
- benches/baselines/perf_v0_2.json (row for cooperative variant, hardware_class scoped)

title: [REVIEW][LOW] EQL time filters compare timestamps as raw strings
description: Commit 5439e5e added EQL time filters. src/models/query.rs matches_since and matches_until compare metadata createdAt/created_at strings directly against since/until strings for absolute timestamps. Lexicographic comparison is only valid for normalized timestamps with the same format and offset; RFC3339 values with offsets or equivalent instants can be misfiltered. title: [process] Re-classify the 14 dishonestly-closed follow-up beads as honesty-only
description:
## Background

The 2026-05-06 reality-check audit identified 14 closed follow-up beads (referenced by 20 `_UNAVAILABLE_CODE` constants in src/cli/mod.rs) where each closure added an abstention sentinel rather than implementing the surface. List:

| Stub surface | Closed bead | Adjusted label |
|---|---|---|
| review | eidetic_engine_cli-0hjw | honesty-only |
| daemon, support-bundle, diag-quarantine | eidetic_engine_cli-5g6d | honesty-only |
| situation, plan-decisioning | eidetic_engine_cli-6cks | honesty-only |

| audit/side-effect contracts | eidetic_engine_cli-s43e | honesty-only |
| eval | eidetic_engine_cli-uiy3 | honesty-only |
| certificate, claim | eidetic_engine_cli-v76q | honesty-only |

## What this bead does

For each ID above, run `br update <id> --add-label honesty-only`. Do NOT reopen them — they are accurate descriptions of work that DID ship (the abstention layer). They simply must not be confused with implementation. The new `implements-surface:<name>` beads created in waves 1-3 of CLOSE_THE_GAP_PLAN are the implementation work.

Append a one-line note to each via `br update --notes` if supported, citing this bead and CLOSE_THE_GAP_PLAN.md as the audit source.

## Why this is wave-0

The closure linter (sibling bead) requires the historical record to be labeled correctly so it can distinguish the existing honesty-only closures from the new implementation work. Without this, every closed bead in the tracker looks indistinguishable from real implementation — the closure linter cannot operate.

title: Re-scope causal commands to evidence ledgers and conservative computed reports
description:
## Background

Causal credit is useful only if it is visibly derived from recorder exposures, context-pack records, preflight closes, tripwire checks, procedure uses, fixture replays, shadow runs, or controlled experiments. It crosses the boundary when uplift is generated from method constants, source ID hashes, or qualitative promotion rules.

Audit anchors: `src/core/causal.rs` has sample chains, method-signal constants, deterministic uplift offsets, downstream projections, and promotion-plan wording that can sound stronger than the evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

See this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field for the detailed completion contract, including unit/static checks, e2e or docs/e2e coverage, detailed logging, and no-feature-loss requirements.
design: Keep mechanical causal surfaces: trace ledgers, exposure tables, decision/outcome joins, statistical summaries over observed data, confounder flags from explicit fields, and conservative abstain/review states. Move causal interpretation, promotion judgment, and experiment design into skills. A causal command may compute numeric estimates only from real rows or explicit fixture inputs and must expose sample size, assumptions, and evidence tier.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- `ee causal trace` reports only observed exposures, decisions, outcomes, and missing evidence from persisted or explicit fixture data.
- `ee causal estimate` refuses or degrades when sample size, baseline, or outcome data are insufficient; it does not invent uplift from method names.
- `ee causal compare` compares candidate/baseline artifacts only through supplied fixture, shadow, replay, or experiment evidence.
- `ee causal promote-plan` becomes a report-only review input; it never directly promotes/demotes/reroutes and never treats underpowered evidence as actionable.
- Unit tests cover no evidence, confounded evidence, underpowered samples, deterministic ordering, and safety-critical warnings pinned.
- E2E scripts log evidence IDs, sample sizes, assumptions, confounders, degradation codes, stdout/stderr artifacts, and schema/golden results.
close_reason: Causal trace/estimate/compare/promote-plan commands now abstain with explicit degradation codes when evidence ledgers are unavailable. Commit 0f0bacd implements all acceptance criteria.

title: [reality-check] agent docs map stale golden paths and missing docs
description:
Reality-check focus: CLAUDE.md/README.md navigation vs current repository layout.

Drift:
- CLAUDE.md:64 says `Golden snaps in tests/golden/*.snap document surface contracts`; CLAUDE.md:73 says golden tests are `tests/golden.rs` + `tests/golden/*.snap`. Current JSON contract snapshots also live under `tests/snapshots/json_contract_snapshots__*.snap`, and command/schema golden artifacts heavily live under `tests/fixtures/golden/**/*.golden` plus nested `tests/golden/**` files. Agents following CLAUDE.md miss large parts of the stable JSON contract surface.
- README.md:860-874 links a documentation map for `docs/storage.md`, `docs/context-packs.md`, `docs/cass-integration.md`, `docs/scoring.md`, `docs/graph.md`, `docs/integration.md`, `docs/privacy.md`, `docs/diagnostics.md`, `docs/evaluation.md`, `docs/dependency-contracts.md`, `docs/schema-evolution.md`, and `docs/legacy-eidetic-import.md`; none of those files exist in the current checkout.

Reproduction:
- `find tests/snapshots -maxdepth 1 -type f` shows JSON contract snapshot files outside the CLAUDE.md golden path.
- `find tests/fixtures/golden -type f | wc -l` reports 143 fixture golden files.
- `for f in storage.md context-packs.md cass-integration.md scoring.md graph.md integration.md privacy.md diagnostics.md evaluation.md dependency-contracts.md schema-evolution.md legacy-eidetic-import.md; do test -e docs/$f || echo missing:docs/$f; done` prints all listed README targets as missing.

Expected:
Refresh CLAUDE.md and README.md so agent-facing guidance points to the actual contract/golden locations and only links docs that exist, or add the missing docs with current code-backed content.
close_reason: Fixed CLAUDE.md golden paths (added tests/snapshots/, tests/fixtures/golden/); fixed README.md doc map (removed 12 stale links, kept 9 existing docs)

title: [CONCURRENCY] cass import: session check-then-insert races concurrent imports
description:
Files: src/cass/import.rs:346, src/cass/import.rs:373, src/db/mod.rs:4231, src/db/mod.rs:4242.
Code path: import_cass_sessions checks connection.get_session_by_cass_id(&workspace_id, &session.source_path) before the write transaction. Only after optional span loading does it enter connection.with_transaction to insert_session, insert_evidence_span, and insert_search_index_job.
Hazard: two imports of the same workspace/source can both observe no existing session, then both compute the same stable session_id/index_job_id. The winner inserts; the loser attempts the same insert and returns a storage/constraint error instead of reporting the session as skipped. This is a concrete TOCTOU race, not just contention.
Repro plan: use a fake CASS client or saved cass JSON fixture returning one session, start two import_cass_sessions callers against the same file DB with a barrier after the existence check, and assert both commands succeed with exactly one imported session and one skipped session.
close_reason: Resolved by transactional CASS session insert recheck and concurrent import regression coverage

title: [reality-check][determinism] RehearseRunReport.artifact_paths uses HashMap with non-deterministic serialization
description: src/core/rehearse.rs:293 uses HashMap<String, String> for artifact_paths. serde serializes HashMap in arbitrary iteration order, violating the 'deterministic by default' principle from AGENTS.md. Same report with same data could produce different JSON byte sequences, breaking content-addressed hashes. Fix: use IndexMap or BTreeMap for deterministic key ordering.
close_reason: Replaced HashMap with BTreeMap for RehearseRunReport.artifact_paths in src/core/rehearse.rs. serde now emits artifact_paths keys in alphabetical order so RehearseRunReport JSON is byte-stable for the same logical content — restoring the content-addressed hash invariant. title: SECURITY: update apply invokes tar via PATH during binary installation
description: HIGH. ee update --apply reaches execute_install_plan (src/cli/mod.rs:6177, src/cli/mod.rs:6188) and archive extraction runs Command::new("tar") for tar.xz and tar.gz artifacts (src/core/install.rs:931, src/core/install.rs:951). In a compromised workspace or agent environment with attacker-controlled PATH, a fake tar executable can run arbitrary code during installation. title: [security] Permissive profile disables secret redaction entirely
description:
**File:** src/policy/security_profile.rs:73-75

**Vulnerability:** The `SecurityProfile::Permissive` variant sets `enforce_redaction: false`, which when configured via `EE_SECURITY_PROFILE=permissive` disables all secret redaction in context pack output.

```rust
pub const fn enforce_redaction(self) -> bool {
    match self {
        Self::Permissive => false,  // All secrets pass through unredacted
        ...
    }
}
```

**Attack Scenario:** A developer sets `EE_SECURITY_PROFILE=permissive` for debugging, forgets to unset it, then generates context packs that include unredacted API keys, JWTs, and PII. These packs get shared with LLM providers or logged.

**Mitigation:**
1. Emit a warning to stderr when permissive profile is active and redaction is skipped
2. Consider requiring an additional explicit flag like `--allow-secrets-in-output` before actually passing through secrets
3. Make the permissive profile still redact high-severity secret classes (API keys, JWTs) while allowing low-entropy values
close_reason: Completed in 660d34d3: permissive security profile keeps output redaction enabled while still relaxing file-permission enforcement, with inline policy test updated.

title: EE-TST-010: Add fixture provenance and scenario traceability manifest
description:
Define a versioned fixture provenance and scenario traceability manifest for EE's test, e2e, golden, replay, and evaluation corpus.

Background:
The bead graph already has a strong scenario matrix, logged e2e scripts, golden/schema contracts, failure replay artifacts, closure dossiers, and command-effect contracts. The remaining risk is that fixtures can still become anonymous blobs: future agents may know a test passed but not which user outcome it proves, which degraded branch it exercises, whether the source is safe/redacted, which deterministic seeds and timestamps were used, or which implementation bead owns stale fixture drift.

This bead closes that gap by making fixtures and scenarios first-class, inspectable evidence. A future agent should be able to answer: which fixture proves this command behavior, what source data shaped it, what secrets were intentionally synthetic, which redaction classes are expected, which scenario and gate does it cover, what state/effect mutations are allowed, and what artifact/log paths should exist after a run.

Scope:
- Define a `fixture_manifest.v1` or equivalent schema for all tracked fixtures and generated test artifacts that need stable references.
- Define a scenario traceability report that maps scenario IDs to commands, fixture IDs, golden/schema contracts, e2e scripts, eval cases, degraded branches, command-effect expectations, implementation beads, and readiness gates.
- Require every fixture family named by the test strategy and north-star scenario matrix to have either an implemented manifest entry or an explicit staged placeholder with owner bead, planned command surface, and skip-until dependency.
- Capture provenance and safety metadata: source kind, synthetic/derived/imported status, source hash, redaction class expectations, secret-leak assertions, deterministic seed, fixed timestamps/IDs, workspace fingerprints, external I/O posture, and allowed mutation/effect class.
- Ensure logs, closure dossiers, and failure replay artifacts include fixture IDs and manifest hashes so failures are attributable instead of ad hoc.

Why this improves user outcomes:
EE is intended to be trusted by agents during real work. Trust comes from knowing not just that tests exist, but what they prove and whether their evidence is safe to reuse. This manifest gives future agents a map from user outcome to executable proof, reduces silent coverage holes, prevents unsafe fixture leakage, and makes test failures much faster to diagnose.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including comprehensive unit tests, e2e tests, contract fixtures, and logging requirements.
design:
Recommended design:
- Keep the manifest small, strict, and versioned. The initial schema can be TOML, JSON, or YAML, but it must validate deterministically and expose stable IDs that can be referenced from test logs, closure dossiers, readiness gates, and scenario reports.
- Use two linked concepts: `fixture_manifest.v1` for concrete fixture/evidence inputs and `scenario_traceability.v1` for coverage mapping from user journeys to executable proof. They may live in the same file family if implementation prefers.
- Suggested fixture fields: fixture_id, fixture_family, owning_bead_ids, owning_gate_ids, scenario_ids, command_family, command_sequence, source_kind, source_hash, synthetic_secret_policy, redaction_classes_expected, deterministic_seed, fixed_clock, stable_ids, workspace_fingerprints, external_io_posture, expected_effect_class, allowed_derived_writes, expected_degradation_codes, golden_paths, schema_paths, replay_hint, artifact_path_pattern, and stale_until_bead_ids.
- Suggested traceability report fields: scenario_id, journey name, commands, fixture IDs, expected response schemas, expected degradation branches, effect-manifest entries, e2e/golden/eval scripts, readiness gates, implementation beads, and current coverage state (`implemented`, `staged_skip`, `blocked`, `missing`).
- The report should fail closed on orphaned fixtures, missing fixture owners, missing redaction posture, missing deterministic controls, undeclared external I/O, missing effect expectation, stale manifest hashes, and scenario rows without executable coverage or an explicit staged skip.
- Do not make every generated artifact tracked. Track manifests, schemas, scripts, and intentional fixtures; keep run artifacts under ignored target paths while including their IDs/hashes in logs and closure dossiers.
- Prefer a validation command that emits compact machine-readable summaries for agents plus detailed artifact paths for investigation. Stdout remains data; progress and diagnostics go to stderr or files.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance criteria:
- A versioned fixture provenance manifest schema exists for the implemented test corpus and includes stable fixture IDs, family, owners, scenario links, command family, provenance/source hash, redaction posture, deterministic controls, expected effect class, expected degraded states, and artifact/golden/schema references.
- A scenario traceability report maps each north-star agent scenario to command sequences, fixture IDs, golden/schema contracts, e2e scripts, eval cases, degraded branches, command-effect expectations, implementation beads, and readiness gates.
- Every fixture family named by the test strategy and scenario matrix has either an implemented manifest entry or an explicit staged placeholder with owner bead, planned public surface, blocked-by dependency, and skip-until condition.
- Manifest validation fails on orphan fixtures, unowned scenarios, missing redaction posture, missing deterministic seed/timestamp/ID controls where relevant, undeclared external I/O, missing command-effect expectation, schema/golden path drift, and scenario rows with neither executable coverage nor a staged-skip rationale.
- E2E, golden/schema, replay, evaluation, and closure-dossier artifacts include fixture ID, scenario ID where applicable, manifest version, manifest content hash, artifact paths, and first failure diagnosis.
- Fixture entries involving synthetic secrets require explicit leak assertions, expected redaction classes/counts or hashes, and proof that raw synthetic secrets do not appear in stdout, public exports, or failure summaries.
- The manifest distinguishes tracked source fixtures from generated run artifacts; generated artifacts are kept out of commits unless they are intentional golden fixtures or tracked documentation.
- CI/local verification has a targetable check for manifest syntax, traceability completeness, stale fixture references, orphan fixtures, and missing user-scenario coverage.

Testing and logging requirements:
- Add or update unit tests for manifest parsing, schema validation, duplicate ID rejection, stale hash detection, redaction posture validation, deterministic-control validation, staged-skip validation, and scenario coverage classification.
- Add golden/schema contract fixtures for valid and invalid manifest/report examples with readable diffs for missing owner, missing redaction posture, undeclared external I/O, and orphan scenario cases.
- Extend real-binary e2e or verification scripts so at least the walking-skeleton and advanced-subsystem fixture families record fixture IDs, scenario IDs, manifest hashes, stdout/stderr artifact paths, redaction status, effect expectation, and first-failure diagnosis.
- Stdout assertions must prove stdout contains only machine data; fixture validation diagnostics, traceability summaries, progress, and debugging context must go to stderr or explicit artifacts.
- If a future fixture cannot yet be executable because an implementation bead is blocked, the manifest must record the staged-skip reason and the bead that will turn the placeholder into executable coverage.
notes: Added during repeated bead quality review after `br search` found no existing fixture manifest, fixture provenance, seed corpus, scenario coverage, coverage matrix, or traceability bead. This is intentionally accretive: it does not replace the scenario matrix, e2e scripts, golden/schema runner, failure replay, closure dossier, or effect manifest. It binds those pieces together so future agents can see exactly which fixture proves which user outcome and whether the evidence is deterministic, redacted, and safe.

title: EE-028: Implement first-run `ee init --json` with dry-run and idempotency
description:
Implement the first-run `ee init` command for creating or validating a local EE workspace.

Background:
The walking-skeleton test flow already expects an initialization/setup step, and the plan has strong primitives for config parsing, workspace detection, status, doctor, migrations, and the workspace repository. What is missing is the concrete product command that an agent runs first in a repository to make EE usable without guessing which directories, config files, database files, migrations, and source roots need to exist.

This bead owns the first minute of the agent experience. `ee init` must be boring, explicit, idempotent, machine-readable, and safe. It should not import histories, create memories, install hooks, scan the whole repository, or mutate unrelated project files. It establishes EE's local workspace state and gives the agent the next safe commands.

Intended public surface:
- `ee init --dry-run --json` reports the exact initialization plan, paths, detected workspace/repository identity, config sources, migration actions, optional dependency status, and next commands without writing anything.
- `ee init --json` creates or validates the minimal EE workspace state and prints only a stable response envelope to stdout.
- `ee init --repair-plan --json` reports non-destructive repair actions for partially initialized or drifted workspaces without applying them.
- `ee init --force --json` is allowed only for explicit, idempotent revalidation/recreation of EE-owned artifacts and must never overwrite user-managed files without a prior dry-run-visible reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including comprehensive unit tests, e2e tests, schema/golden fixtures, idempotency checks, and detailed logging requirements.
design:
Recommended design:
- Keep `init` as a command over existing primitives: config/path resolution, workspace detection, FrankenSQLite/SQLModel migration setup, workspace repository registration, response envelope, error registry, command-effect manifest, and doctor/status summaries.
- Make the command two-phase internally: plan first, then apply. The dry-run output and real apply output should share the same planned-action schema so tests can diff them cleanly.
- Treat initialization as a small set of named effects: create EE data directory, create/open DB, apply migrations, create or update workspace record, write EE-owned config defaults if explicitly requested, validate feature/dependency posture, and emit next commands. Each effect needs idempotency status.
- Default posture should be conservative: do not import CASS/session history, install hooks, run expensive indexing, create context packs, or capture secrets. Instead, suggest explicit next commands such as `ee import cass --dry-run --json`, `ee index rebuild --dry-run --json`, `ee doctor --fix-plan --json`, or `ee context --json` when those surfaces exist.
- Handle partial initialization honestly. Missing DB, stale migration, mismatched workspace fingerprint, moved repository, unwritable data dir, ambiguous workspace, and unsupported dependency posture should return stable codes and safe next actions.
- Preserve stdout/stderr isolation. Stdout is only `ee.response.v1`; progress, path decisions, skipped optional steps, warnings, and first-failure diagnosis go to stderr or explicit artifacts.
- The implementation should remain local-first and single-process friendly. Do not require a daemon, web service, MCP server, network access, or multiple concurrent SQLite writers.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance criteria:
- `ee init --dry-run --json` returns an `ee.response.v1` payload with detected workspace/repository identity, planned EE-owned paths, config sources and precedence, planned DB/migration actions, optional dependency posture, idempotency classification, command-effect classification, and recommended next commands.
- `ee init --json` creates or validates only EE-owned workspace artifacts, applies required migrations, creates or updates the workspace record, and returns the same stable plan/apply schema with actual effects, skipped effects, artifact paths, and next commands.
- `ee init --repair-plan --json` reports safe, non-destructive repair actions for partially initialized workspaces without writing anything.
- Re-running `ee init --json` is idempotent and reports `already_initialized` or equivalent effect statuses without duplicate workspace records, duplicate migrations, duplicate config entries, or changed output ordering.
- Ambiguous workspace roots, moved repositories, unwritable data directories, stale migrations, unsupported schema versions, and forbidden dependency posture return stable error/degradation codes with clear next actions.
- The command never imports session history, creates memories, installs hooks, performs full indexing, scans unrelated files, stores secrets, or mutates user-managed project files by default.
- All paths in output are normalized, scoped, and safe to display; sensitive home/config values are redacted or summarized according to privacy policy.
- The init response is compatible with `ee status --json`, `ee health --json`, `ee doctor --json`, `ee doctor --fix-plan --json`, and later support/handoff bundle summaries.
- Public schemas and golden fixtures cover dry-run fresh workspace, apply fresh workspace, rerun idempotency, partial workspace repair-plan, ambiguous workspace, unwritable path, stale migration, and unsupported future schema cases.

Testing and logging requirements:
- Add unit tests for init planning, path normalization, config-source precedence, workspace fingerprinting, effect classification, idempotency detection, migration plan rendering, repair-plan generation, ambiguity handling, and redaction of sensitive paths/config values.
- Add integration tests against temporary FrankenSQLite/SQLModel databases covering fresh init, rerun idempotency, partial DB state, stale migration table, moved workspace fingerprint, and rollback on failed effect.
- Add real-binary e2e coverage where an isolated workspace runs `ee init --dry-run --json`, `ee init --json`, `ee status --json`, `ee health --json`, `ee doctor --fix-plan --json`, and a second `ee init --json`, with schema/golden validation for every stdout payload.
- Add adversarial/property coverage for path traversal-like workspace names, symlinked output/data directories, invalid UTF-8/control characters in paths, extremely long paths, read-only directories, and concurrent init attempts.
- E2E/logged tests must capture command, cwd/workspace, sanitized environment overrides, elapsed time, exit code, stdout/stderr artifact paths, initialized paths, migration version, workspace ID/fingerprint, schema/golden validation status, redaction status, command-effect classification, and first-failure diagnosis.
- Stdout assertions must prove stdout contains only machine data; initialization progress, skipped optional steps, warnings, repair explanations, and debugging context must go to stderr or explicit artifacts.
- Closeout evidence must include fixture IDs, scenario IDs, manifest hashes, command-effect manifest entries, exact verification commands, and proof that init does not perform import, indexing, hook installation, or unrelated file mutation.

title: Per-workspace fsqlite shard fan-out: eliminate global write serialization (idea-wizard MagentaPanther 2026-05-18)
description: see follow-up comment with full spec

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
FULL SPEC (MagentaPanther idea-wizard + reality-check 2026-05-18)

EVIDENCE: src/db/mod.rs:278-282 defines static FILE_WRITE_OWNER_GATE: OnceLock<Mutex<()>> — a singleton write mutex acquired at :308 lock_file_write_owner_gate(location). Every write across every workspace globally serializes through this one mutex. On a 64+-agent swarm host spanning 5-20 active workspaces, this is the dominant tail-latency contributor for ee remember / ee outcome / curate apply / audit emit.

DISTINGUISHABILITY vs existing swarm-X coverage:
- bd-2caru (read pool, src/db/read_pool.rs): READS only. Orthogonal.
- bd-wp5ac (audit MPSC): batches audit-row writes off the foreground but still serializes through same global writer.
- bd-1prrl.3 (NUMA mmap snapshot): graph snapshot RAM pinning. Orthogonal.
- bd-gni47 (single-flight): coalesces duplicate READS, not parallelizes WRITES.
This bead is NET-NEW: turns global single-writer into per-workspace concurrent writers via fsqlite shard fan-out.

DESIGN:
1. ~/.local/share/ee/shards/<workspace_id>.db — one fsqlite per workspace.
2. ~/.local/share/ee/catalog.db — thin coordinator (workspace registry, alias map, global config). Low-write.
3. Per-workspace writes hit ONLY that shard. No cross-shard transactions in v1.
4. Cross-workspace reads ATTACH peer shards read-only; search across workspaces UNIONs per-shard results (composes with src/core/memory_scope.rs).
5. Audit chain per-shard (audit.prev_hash sequence local). Global ee audit timeline view UNIONs per-shard chains sorted by audit_ts.
6. ee migrate shard-fanout: one-shot deterministic migration. Emits ee.migration.shard_fanout.v1 audit per workspace. Original ee.db RENAMED .pre-shard-fanout.db (NOT deleted per AGENTS.md R-1).

FILE SURFACE:
- src/db/mod.rs (shard router; coordinate with bd-2caru owner before substantive refactor)
- src/db/shard.rs (NEW): per-workspace handle, attach-peer logic
- src/db/migrations/<NNN>_shard_fanout.sql
- src/cli/mod.rs: ee migrate shard-fanout [--dry-run]
- src/core/workspace.rs: shard-path resolution
- src/config/env_registry.rs: EE_SHARDS_DIR, EE_SHARD_FANOUT_ENABLED (feature flag for v1)
- docs/architecture/shard-fanout.md (NEW)
- docs/adr/00XX-per-workspace-shard-fanout.md (NEW)
- docs/schemas/ee.migration.shard_fanout.v1.json (NEW)
- tests/shard_fanout_{e2e,audit_chain,migration,backup}.rs (NEW)

ACCEPTANCE:
1. With EE_SHARD_FANOUT_ENABLED=1, writes against workspace A do not block writes against workspace B. Proof: tests/shard_fanout_e2e.rs runs 8 OS threads × 4 workspaces × 100 remember calls; total throughput >= 3.5× single-writer baseline; ee.test_event.v1 JSONL captures phase=enqueue|grant|commit|shard_id|workspace_id|elapsed_ms.
2. Cross-workspace search (ee search --workspace A --include-peers B,C) returns byte-identical results to single-writer baseline (golden parity test).
3. Per-shard audit chains continuous (no hash break); global ee audit timeline preserves cross-shard ts ordering.
4. ee migrate shard-fanout migrates an existing global ee.db deterministically; idempotent on second run; structured ee.migration.shard_fanout.v1 audit row per shard.
5. ee backup create includes all per-shard .db files; ee backup restore reconstructs the shard layout.
6. EE_SHARD_FANOUT_ENABLED=0 + migrate rollback returns byte-identical behavior to v0.x for same DB content.
7. All Cargo verification through RCH only.

TRACING: surface=shard_fanout; required fields workspace_id, shard_id, request_id, phase (input|attach_peer|write|chain_append|cross_shard_union|response), elapsed_ms, degraded_codes (shard_attach_failed, shard_chain_mismatch, cross_shard_skew_detected).

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES:
- cross-shard transactions in v1 (would re-introduce global lock)
- hashing memories into N fixed shards (vs per-workspace) — breaks workspace-as-truth-unit
- monolithic single-DB optimization (page-cache-pin only) — does not unblock concurrent writers

COMPOSES WITH: bd-2caru (read pool per-shard), bd-wp5ac (audit MPSC per-shard channels), bd-1zb7k.20 (QoS lanes), bd-bife (graph snapshots per-shard).

description:

title: shard-fanout.3: DbShardRouter and per-shard write ownership
description:
## Goal
Replace the global single process write-owner bottleneck for shard-enabled workspaces with a router that serializes writes per shard file, not across all workspaces. This is the core performance lever for the parent bead.

## Current evidence
`src/db/mod.rs` currently has `static FILE_WRITE_OWNER_GATE: OnceLock<Mutex<()>>`, and `lock_file_write_owner_gate(location)` takes that global process mutex before opening a file database or beginning an immediate write transaction. This means workspace A and workspace B serialize even when they target different database files.

## Scope
- Introduce a `DbShardRouter` or equivalent storage-layer type that resolves a workspace_id to a shard handle and opens `DbConnection` through the resolver from shard-fanout.2.
- Preserve the existing per-file `.write.lock` behavior for each shard.
- Replace or narrow the process-global mutex so independent shard files can write concurrently while same-shard nested writes remain safe.
- Keep all non-shard-enabled paths byte-compatible with the current single `ee.db` path.
- Thread request/workspace/shard identity through tracing: phase=input|write|response with workspace_id, shard_id, request_id, elapsed_ms, degraded_codes.

## Acceptance
- Unit tests prove same-shard writes serialize and different-shard writes do not acquire the same process-global gate.
- Existing transaction helpers still roll back on error and never leak write-owner depth.
- No Tokio, no forbidden dependencies, no local Cargo verification.
- RCH-focused tests include a concurrency unit or integration target when RCH topology allows; otherwise the bead records the exact remote-required verifier and why it was blocked.
- The implementation remains source-local and does not touch RCH topology or peer-owned read-pool work.
