title: [security] High-entropy secret detection requires keyword proximity
description:
**File:** src/policy/mod.rs:1010-1011

**Vulnerability:** The `redact_high_entropy_secret_values` function only redacts high-entropy content when `has_nearby_secret_keyword` returns true. Secrets not near keywords like "key", "secret", "token" etc. will not be redacted.

```rust
if looks_like_high_entropy_secret(candidate)
    && has_nearby_secret_keyword(input, token_start, token_end)  // <-- requires keyword
{
```

**Attack Scenario:** An agent stores a memory containing a redacted Stripe-like sample value `[REDACTED_STRIPE_KEY]` without secret/key/token in the surrounding text. While prefix-based detection catches this class when the prefix is present, a high-entropy AWS secret key without recognizable prefix (e.g. base64-encoded HMAC secret) placed in generic content could leak.

**Mitigation:**
1. Consider a standalone high-entropy pass for very long (64+ char) random-looking strings
2. Or: accept that prefix-based detection + keyword proximity covers the practical attack surface and document this as a known limitation

**Note:** The original audit text used a secret-shaped synthetic Stripe example; it was redacted to keep GitHub push protection and repository history clean.
close_reason: Added standalone high-entropy detection for 64+ char base64-like strings without requiring keyword proximity. Pure hex strings still require keywords (likely public hashes). 3 test cases added. Commit 6c1fdd5.

title: v2:serve_localhost — in-tree loopback HTTP/1.1 + SSE adapter per ADR 0033
description:
Open v2 follow-up bead per docs/adr/0033-serve-localhost-v2-design.md and the bd-3usjw.4 defer-to-v2 closure. The v1 surface ships an honest serve_unavailable_v1 error; this bead tracks the real adapter.

SCOPE (per ADR 0033)
- In-tree loopback HTTP/1.1 + SSE adapter using std::net + asupersync Scope; NO hyper/axum/tower/reqwest (AGENTS.md forbidden deps).
- Bind only 127.0.0.1 by default; refuse non-loopback unless --allow-non-loopback explicit.
- Endpoints: GET /v1/context, /v1/search, /v1/why, /v1/status, /v1/doctor, /v1/swarm/brief (POST for durable_write surfaces).
- Auth: bearer token from EE_SERVE_TOKEN env (256-bit random); refuse unauthenticated requests.
- Response envelopes: same ee.response.v2 / ee.error.v2 shapes the CLI emits; CLI remains authoritative.
- Schema: docs/schemas/ee.serve.startup.v1.json + docs/schemas/ee.serve.endpoint.v1.json.
- Tests: tests/e2e_serve_localhost.rs driving a real curl-equivalent loop via std::net::TcpStream; no mock servers.

ACCEPTANCE
- HTTP/1.1 + SSE adapter implemented in-tree without any forbidden HTTP dep entering the tree (forbidden_deps.rs continues to pass).
- All 6 endpoints route through existing core services; no business logic duplicated from cli/.
- Bearer token verification before any handler dispatch; failure returns 401 with ee.error.v2 shape.
- Same DB + indexes + config + query + bearer token -> byte-identical JSON output via HTTP as via CLI (determinism preserved across surfaces).
- Tests cover happy path, auth failure, non-loopback refusal, malformed request, cancellation via Cx, SSE stream termination, and the swarm/brief POST path.
- bd-3usjw.4 close_reason's serve_unavailable_v1 error stays in place until this beads acceptance lands.
- No local Cargo; RCH-only.

NON-GOALS
- No TLS in v2 (loopback only).
- No WebSockets; SSE only for streaming.
- No multi-process write coordination changes; the daemon write-owner (ADR 0013) still owns mutations.

FILE SURFACE: src/serve.rs (rewrite), docs/schemas/ee.serve.startup.v1.json (NEW), docs/schemas/ee.serve.endpoint.v1.json (NEW), tests/e2e_serve_localhost.rs (NEW), tests/serve_localhost_unit.rs (NEW)

TRACING: surface=serve_localhost; required fields workspace_id, request_id, bead_id, surface, endpoint, status_code, elapsed_ms, degraded_codes.

title: Epic: Configuration UX, EE_* Env-Var Matrix, Per-Section Keys (§25)
description:
Source: COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_TO_MAKE_EE__OPUS.md §25 (Configuration), §25.1 (config shape), §25.2 (env vars), §25.3 (`ee config` subcommand).

# Epic: Configuration UX, EE_* Env-Var Matrix, and Per-Section Key Coverage

## Why this epic exists

§25 specifies an 11-section config file with 40+ keys, 8 named EE_* env vars, and a 5-verb `ee config` subcommand (`show`, `get`, `set`, `edit`, `validate`). Today the parser and merge order exist, but:

- Most per-section keys are not bead-tracked individually. e.g., `[scoring]` has 8 keys, `[pack]` has 6 quotas + `mmr_lambda`/`min_mmr`/`include_explanations`, `[playbook]` has decay_half_life_days and trauma_multiplier — none have beads.
- `ee config show / get / set / edit / validate` have no beads at all. Operators currently cannot inspect or override config from the CLI.
- The 8 EE_* env vars (EE_CONFIG, EE_DB, EE_INDEX_DIR, EE_WORKSPACE, EE_NO_SEMANTIC, EE_CASS_BIN, EE_LOG, EE_HARMFUL_*) need an end-to-end precedence matrix that asserts CLI flag > env var > project config > user config > default.
- There is no canonical "config key ↔ env var ↔ CLI flag" matrix asserted in CI, so a future drift between the three is not detected.

This epic exists so an agent can `ee config show` and trust the answer, so adversarial environments (with conflicting EE_* vars set) produce sane and explainable results, and so every config knob in the plan is exercised by at least one test.

## Cross-cutting constraints (apply to every child bead under this epic)

- `ee config show` emits the merged-effective config plus per-key source attribution (`{"value": ..., "source": "user-config" | "project-config" | "env" | "cli" | "default"}`). Asserted by a golden.
- `ee config validate` returns a typed list of issues with severity + repair hint; never panics; never writes.
- `ee config set` writes only to the workspace project config, never to user config; an explicit `--user` flag is required to write user config.
- `ee config edit` opens `$EDITOR`, writes a temp file, validates on save, and refuses to overwrite a malformed result.
- The CLI flag > env > project > user > default precedence is asserted by a precedence test that sets the same key at every layer with a different value and checks the layer wins.
- Each EE_* env var has: a doc string in `ee --help`, a row in the precedence table, a logged-e2e test that exports the var to a fixture and asserts the effect.
- Tests log: which config files were merged and from which paths, env vars present (sanitized — keys only, never values when the value would be sensitive like a path), final effective config fingerprint, total elapsed_ms.

## Closure criteria

- All 5 `ee config` subcommands implemented with stable JSON contracts.
- A "config-key matrix" generated golden enumerates every key with: section, key name, type, default, range/sanity check, CLI flag (if any), EE_* env var (if any), config path note. The golden fails if a new key is added without updating it.
- Each of the 8 EE_* env vars has a logged e2e test.
- Each config section's keys have at least one effect-asserting test (e.g., setting [scoring].recency_tau_days = 1 vs. 90 changes the score component golden).
- `ee doctor` includes a "config-conflict surprise reporter" check that warns on improbable EE_* combinations.

## Verification path

- Unit tests under `src/config/`.
- Goldens in `tests/snapshots/config_*`.
- E2E in `tests/config_precedence_matrix.rs`, `tests/config_show_get_set.rs`.

title: [HIGH] Curation TTL stores invalid non-RFC3339 expiration strings
description:
Reviewer finding from mixed-swarm pass.

Location: src/curate/mod.rs:1842-1847 creates ttl_expires_at with format!("{now_rfc3339}+{secs}s"). src/core/curate.rs:2742-2748 later parses ttl_expires_at with DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339.

Impact: any candidate created through validate_candidate with ttl_seconds stores values like 2026-04-29T12:00:00Z+3600s, which are not RFC3339. Later validation/disposition paths treat that as malformed storage instead of expiring or validating the candidate. The current unit test only asserts ttl_expires_at.is_some(), so this regression is not caught.

Suggested fix: compute expires_at with chrono from a parsed now timestamp and store a real RFC3339 instant. Add unit coverage that ttl_expires_at parses and that an expired generated TTL reaches CandidateExpired rather than invalid timestamp storage errors.
close_reason: Fixed TTL to use chrono Duration + to_rfc3339() in 11377a2. Added 4 unit tests for RFC3339 round-trip, None, zero, and large TTL values.

title: EE implementation program from comprehensive plan
description:
Program-level bead for the Eidetic Engine CLI implementation. The project is a Rust CLI named `ee` that reimagines the old Eidetic Engine as a local-first, harness-agnostic memory substrate for coding agents.

Overarching goals:
- Help agents repeat fewer mistakes by retrieving, explaining, validating, and evolving memory from real work.
- Stay CLI-first and agent-native: commands must be deterministic, parseable, non-interactive by default, and useful from any agent harness.
- Use the required local stack: FrankenSQLite through SQLModel Rust, Asupersync, Frankensearch, FrankenNetworkX, CASS, and carefully gated optional Franken-family integrations.
- Never use rusqlite or Tokio in the core design.
- Treat indexes, graphs, embeddings, caches, diagrams, certificates, and metrics as derived artifacts over durable local memory.
- Prefer dry-run, audit, evidence, and explicit promotion over silent mutation.

This bead graph is intended to be self-contained. Each child bead carries enough background, design intent, and acceptance criteria that future agents should not need to consult the markdown plan to understand what to build and why.

## Success Criteria

Detailed epic closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as the epic's success contract, including cross-bead user validation, evidence, and logging requirements.

title: EE-TST-REDACT-FUZZ-001: Add deep redaction fuzz corpus, mutation generator, and coverage report
description:
Add a deep redaction fuzz/property corpus that tests the privacy pipeline against the kind of adversarial input that real codebases and chat logs actually contain.

Background:
The OPUS plan §27.6 explicitly notes redaction fuzz coverage "could be deeper" and §22 commits the system to redacting before storage. The README lists default redaction classes (api_key, jwt, password, private_key, ssh_key, aws_secret, oauth_token) and promises that the original is "never written to disk". EE-TST-011 (adversarial fuzz and property-test harness for agent-facing inputs) is the existing umbrella, but it is generic; it does not own a redaction-specific corpus or the property assertions that prove the pipeline is robust against pattern mutations and multilingual or encoded payloads.

Real coding-agent traffic carries: secrets split across multiple lines, secrets embedded in JSON or YAML, base64-encoded secrets, secrets with custom prefixes that defeat naive detectors, secrets in non-Latin scripts, secrets in code comments, secrets in file paths (e.g. ".aws/credentials"), and secrets that look like ordinary tokens until paired with a context word. F4 failure-mode and H2 adversarial review both flagged that a single false-negative in the redaction pipeline destroys the trust promise of the system.

Intended scope:
This bead adds a redaction-specific fuzz corpus, the property assertions that compose with it, and the multilingual/encoded mutation strategies. It does not replace EE-TST-011; it extends the harness with the redaction-specific test pack.

Public surface (test-only):
- A corpus directory tests/fixtures/redaction/ with categorised payloads: by class (api_key, jwt, etc.), by encoding (raw, base64, percent-encoded, json-escaped, yaml-quoted), by language (English, plus at minimum one Cyrillic and one CJK example), by structural context (code comment, JSON value, YAML block, environment-variable assignment, error message body, file path).
- A property assertion harness that for every fixture: runs the redaction pipeline, asserts no raw payload appears in the redacted output, asserts the audit log records the redaction class and a stable evidence hash but NOT the raw payload, and asserts deterministic redaction (same input -> same output).
- A pattern-mutation generator that takes a known-good detector and asserts the detector still fires after small mutations (whitespace insertion, case changes, line breaks, leading/trailing punctuation, base64 wrapping, YAML quote wrapping).
- A coverage report that lists every redaction class against every encoding and every structural context, with green/red status.

Why this matters:
Redaction is the single most visible privacy promise of EE. A fuzz corpus that codifies the realistic adversarial patterns is the only durable defense against detector regressions. Plan §27.6 explicitly named this as under-covered.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including the redaction fixture corpus, mutation generator, positive/negative corpora, coverage report, property tests, support-bundle/import/remember integration tests, and e2e logging requirements.
design:
Recommended design:
- Treat the corpus as code-adjacent fixtures, not test-only inputs. Every fixture is a small JSON file with raw, encoding, context, expected_class, expected_redacted_form. The test loader iterates the directory and builds the test matrix at runtime.
- The mutation generator is a deterministic function with seeded randomness; same seed -> same mutations. Seeds are committed alongside the corpus.
- For multilingual coverage, lean on existing locale-tagged sample tokens (e.g. UTF-8 password fixtures from public security research). Avoid bundling actual production secrets.
- Compose with EE-TST-011 (adversarial fuzz harness) by reusing its property-testing utilities; do not fork them.
- Compose with EE-DIAG-001 (support bundle) by including a redaction-coverage-aware integration test in the support-bundle path.
- The negative corpus is load-bearing: false positives erode user trust as much as false negatives. Both directions must be asserted.
- Document a quarterly review: the corpus must grow as new agent traffic patterns emerge. The notes field captures this expectation.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance criteria:
- The fixture corpus under tests/fixtures/redaction/ covers every redaction class named in the README (api_key, jwt, password, private_key, ssh_key, aws_secret, oauth_token) crossed with at minimum five encodings (raw, base64, percent-encoded, json-escaped, yaml-quoted) and at minimum five structural contexts (code comment, JSON value, YAML block, environment variable assignment, error message body, file path).
- For each fixture, the redaction pipeline produces a deterministic redacted form, audits the redaction with class and a stable evidence hash, and never writes the raw payload to any artifact (DB, audit log, stderr diagnostics, support bundle, JSONL export).
- The mutation generator takes any positive fixture and produces a documented set of mutations: whitespace insertion at every position, case mutation for case-insensitive prefixes, line-break insertion, leading/trailing punctuation, base64 wrapping, yaml quote wrapping, json-escape wrapping. Each mutation is asserted to still fire the detector.
- A negative corpus tests/fixtures/redaction/negative/ contains tokens that look like secrets but are not (e.g. example tokens from public docs, base64 of harmless strings). The pipeline asserts no false positive on these.
- A coverage report tests/contracts/redaction_coverage.json is regenerated as part of the test run and asserted byte-stable; a missing class*encoding*context cell fails CI.
- Multilingual coverage includes at minimum one Cyrillic example and one CJK example for password and api_key classes.
- All assertions go through the audit log and not through stdout, so the test produces a stable JSON contract on stdout that consumers can parse.

Testing and logging requirements:
- Unit tests cover detector correctness on the negative corpus (no false positives) and on the positive corpus (no false negatives), plus deterministic redaction output for all fixtures.
- Property tests assert: redaction is idempotent (redact(redact(x)) == redact(x)), deterministic (redact(x) == redact(x) across process restarts), and never lengthens the output beyond a documented bound.
- Adversarial: a fixture that hides a secret inside a UTF-8 BOM, a fixture that uses zero-width joiners, a fixture that splits a secret across log lines, a fixture that encodes a secret in URL-encoded form within a query string. Each must redact correctly.
- Integration tests via the real ee binary run `ee remember`, `ee import cass --dry-run`, and `ee support bundle --dry-run` against a workspace seeded with redaction fixtures and assert no raw payload appears anywhere.
- E2E logs capture the corpus run, the per-fixture verdict, the audit log diff, and a coverage summary. Logs go to stderr and a per-fixture log artifact.
- Closeout evidence cites the corpus directory, the coverage report, the negative corpus, and the integration test outcomes.
notes: Closes the §27.6 explicitly-named coverage gap. Composes with EE-TST-011 rather than duplicating it: this bead owns the redaction-specific corpus and assertions, EE-TST-011 owns the harness primitives. Multilingual coverage is required because real coding-agent traffic includes non-ASCII passwords and identifiers.

description:
Add a dedicated real-binary e2e scenario suite for the feature set introduced by the legacy Eidetic comparison and walking-skeleton repair plan.

This does not replace unit/golden tests inside each implementation bead. It is a cross-feature acceptance pack proving that durable remember, persisted context packs, query-file contracts, memory-link evidence, temporal validity, recorder follow, focus/task-frame state, rationale traces, and the narrow artifact registry work together in realistic agent workflows.

The suite should run locally without daemon/web/MCP dependencies, external services, paid LLM APIs, or non-deterministic model calls. It should reuse the existing fixture provenance, command-effect, no-mutation, golden/schema, and failure-logging harnesses.

## Acceptance Criteria

See this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field for the detailed completion contract, including unit/static checks, e2e or docs/e2e coverage, detailed logging, and no-feature-loss requirements.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- Acts as the aggregate closure bead for the five memory-composition scenario beads, not as a monolithic implementation task.
- Depends on and verifies closeout artifacts from:
  - eidetic_engine_cli-acf3: walking skeleton durable memory and pack proof
  - eidetic_engine_cli-d19r: query document/query-file contract proof
  - eidetic_engine_cli-4ypp: temporal validity and memory-link graph proof
  - eidetic_engine_cli-dc0w: recorder/focus/task-frame/rationale resume proof
  - eidetic_engine_cli-5c8d: artifact registry/search/support-bundle proof
- Adds or updates a single aggregate CI/local runner that invokes all five scenarios in deterministic order and also supports running each scenario independently.
- Confirms scenario artifacts are complete, linked, and non-overlapping: command logs, stdout/stderr paths, schema/golden status, effect deltas, redaction status, DB/state hashes, fixture IDs, and first-failure diagnoses.
- Confirms cross-scenario composition with one end-to-end workspace where feasible: memories, packs, links, temporal validity, recorder/focus/task/rationale state, artifacts, support bundles, and query files coexist without schema drift, hidden mutation, stdout pollution, or redaction leaks.
- Produces an aggregate closeout dossier with exact commands, artifact root, scenario IDs, manifest/content hashes, known limitations, and any follow-up beads.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the aggregate e2e/golden/schema suite pass before closure.

description:

title: [explain] Query and pack performance explain-plan report
description:
## Background
Agents need to understand why `ee context` is slow or memory-heavy before they can fix it. Today explainability focuses on why a memory was selected; swarm-scale operation also needs explainability for query plans, pack assembly, cache behavior, and derived-index state.

## What ships
1. `--explain-performance` or equivalent JSON report for context/search/pack commands, gated so normal stable JSON remains unchanged unless requested.
2. Breakdown of DB reads, search hits, candidate count, pack pruning stages, graph/cache usage, token budgeting, elapsed time, and degradation/fallback reasons.
3. Stable schema suitable for golden tests and support bundles.
4. Redaction-safe output: no secret-bearing memory content in the performance report.

## Implementation notes
This should instrument existing code paths and score components, not fork retrieval logic. It should complement `ee why` and support bundle diagnostics. Keep output deterministic where timings are not asserted; timing fields may be bucketed or separately marked non-deterministic if needed.

## Tests and logging
- Unit tests pin the report schema and redaction behavior.
- Golden tests cover context/search/pack examples.
- Bench tests compare report overhead and ensure explain mode does not materially change selection results.

## Closure evidence
Close only after explain reports catch at least one known hotspot or cache fallback in a deterministic fixture and after rch-offloaded verification passes.
close_reason: Explain-performance report fully implemented. CLI flags wired for context/pack/search commands. JSON output includes: dbReads, search metrics, candidate resolution, pack assembly, cache/graph status, timings, fallbacks, redaction metadata. Unit tests verify schema, redaction safety (no memory content or query text), and fallback capture (stale_index). Tests pass with RCH target dir.

title: [reality-check][acceptance] Ranking tie determinism needs explicit test
description: AGENTS.md determinism rule states 'Ranking ties must be deterministic'. While sort() calls exist in pack/focus/search code, there's no explicit test that verifies: given two items with identical relevance scores, the ordering is stable across runs. Need test with seeded identical-score items to verify secondary sort key (e.g., memory ID) provides deterministic tiebreaking.
close_reason: Completed by existing coverage: tests/search_deterministic_golden.rs includes equal_score_search_ties_order_by_memory_id_across_runs, which seeds identical-score memories in non-sorted insert order, verifies all scores are equal, expects memory-id ordering, and repeats across 10 runs for canonical JSON stability. No new test run: rch has no workers configured and rch 0.1.3 lacks exec.

title: Implement ee.query.v1 temporal query-file filters
description:
Implement `ee.query.v1` temporal query-file controls: `time.after`, `time.before`, `asOf`, and `temporalValidity`.

Current evidence:
- `docs/query-schema.md:139` marks temporal fields as not implemented.
- `src/cli/mod.rs:14588-14590` rejects `time`, `asOf`, and `temporalValidity` after timestamp validation.
- Closed bead `eidetic_engine_cli-io24` recorded the stub/reroute; closed bead `eidetic_engine_cli-9eg.1` added memory validity windows.

Acceptance criteria:
- Query-file temporal controls filter or annotate retrieval consistently with existing memory created/updated timestamps and valid_from/valid_to semantics.
- `asOf` has deterministic point-in-time behavior and does not silently expose later updates.
- `temporalValidity.posture` implements strict/relaxed/ignore with explainable output/degradation where applicable.
- Invalid timestamps keep `ERR_INVALID_TIMESTAMP`; unsupported temporal sentinel entries are removed only when the real behavior lands.
- Add unit, real-binary E2E, and golden coverage for open-ended windows, expired/future/current validity, boundary equality, as-of snapshots, and stdout/stderr isolation.
close_reason: Temporal query-file filters implemented. time.after/before filter by created_at with explainable degradation. asOf provides point-in-time snapshots. temporalValidity postures (strict/relaxed/ignore) work. Matrix tests pass: matrix_time_after_filters_created_at, matrix_time_before_accepts_open_ended_future_window, matrix_as_of_future_snapshot_succeeds, matrix_temporal_validity_strict_succeeds.

title: [implements-surface:certificate] Real ee certificate verify with manifest hashing and signatures
description:
## Background
Stub: CERTIFICATE_STORE_UNAVAILABLE_CODE = certificate_store_unavailable at src/cli/mod.rs:14763. Honesty closure: eidetic_engine_cli-v76q (manifest evidence logging only, no real verification). README backup section + plan §10. Necessary for signed-backup verification chain.

## What ships
1. certificates table: id, target_kind (backup|manifest|export), target_id, hash_algo, content_hash, signature, signer, signed_at, verified_at.
2. Hashing harness using blake3 (already a dep).
3. Signature: optional sigstore-style detached bundle, falls back to user-provided ed25519 keypair via config.
4. ee certificate verify <id> --json returns {valid: true|false, mismatches: [...], signature_ok: bool, signer: ...}.
5. ee certificate list [--target-kind X] [--json] enumerates persisted certificates.
6. Integration: ee backup create automatically generates a certificate for the backup; ee backup verify uses it.

## Acceptance
- Tampered backup detected: test mutates a backup file, verify returns valid=false with mismatch path.
- Signature verification works for both sigstore and local-key configurations.
- CERTIFICATE_STORE_UNAVAILABLE_CODE deleted in same PR.
- Unit + integration + golden tests cover valid, hash-mismatch, signature-mismatch, missing-target.
- Closure linter passes.
close_reason: Implementation complete: core/certificate.rs (2035 lines) provides verify_certificate, list_certificates, show_certificate with blake3 hashing. CLI handlers wired at mod.rs:15669+. CERTIFICATE_STORE_UNAVAILABLE_CODE deleted. Golden test at tests/golden/certificate.snap. Closure linter passes.

title: HIGH: ProcessExitCode enum values diverge from AGENTS.md exit code table
description:
The ProcessExitCode enum in src/models/mod.rs (lines 424-436) has different exit codes than documented in AGENTS.md 'Exit Codes' table.

AGENTS.md specifies:
- 5 = import error
- 6 = degraded but command could not satisfy required mode
- 7 = policy denied operation
- 8 = migration required

Actual enum:
- 5 = Graph (not documented)
- 6 = Import
- 7 = UnsatisfiedDegradedMode
- 8 = PolicyDenied
- 9 = MigrationRequired (not in docs)
- 10 = NotFound (not in docs)

Either the enum or AGENTS.md needs to be updated to match. Machine consumers depend on stable documented exit codes.
close_reason: Aligned ProcessExitCode with AGENTS.md exit code table and updated contract tests.

title: G8: Knowledge skyline composite for ee status — onion × Louvain × trust × age × k-truss × PPR
description:
# G8 — "Knowledge skyline" composite for `ee status`

## Idea (one-liner)

Render the workspace as a 4-dimensional stratification: for each Louvain community, show a histogram with rows = onion-layer (innermost → outermost) and columns = trust-class; cells show count + mean age. Plus k-truss membership and PPR percentile as overlays. The workspace's *shape* at a glance.

## Why this matters

`ee status` today shows scalar counts. Skyline reveals the *shape* of the workspace: are you knowledge-rich at the core (innermost layer dense, mostly human_explicit) but periphery-bloated (outer shells dense, mostly agent_assertion)? That's an actionable curation signal that no current command produces.

This is the second composite (after G2's Pack DNA) — paired with Pack DNA, the two form the "explain your workspace + explain this pack" diptych. Multiple algorithms triangulating into a single multi-modal output.

## Composite of:

- Onion layers (from G5)
- Louvain communities (from G4)
- Trust-class taxonomy (existing)
- Age decile (computed inline)
- K-truss membership (from G4)
- PPR percentile (from G1)

All cached on the snapshot; `ee status --skyline` is a read-only roll-up.

## Output shape

`ee status --skyline --json`:

```jsonc
"knowledgeSkyline": {
  "schema": "ee.status.skyline.v1",
  "snapshotVersion": 1234,
  "communities": [
    {
      "louvainId": 0,
      "label": "auto-derived",  // first tag majority in the cluster
      "size": 42,
      "skylineMatrix": {
        "rows": ["innermost_layer", "layer_2", "layer_3", "outermost_layer"],
        "columns": ["human_explicit", "agent_validated", "agent_assertion", "cass_evidence", "legacy_import"],
        "cells": [
          [{"count": 5, "meanAgeDays": 12.4, "kTrussRank": 5, "pprPercentile": 90}, ...],
          ...
        ]
      },
      "summary": {
        "dominantTrustClass": "agent_validated",
        "dominantLayer": "outermost_layer",
        "skylineHealth": "periphery_heavy"  // diagnostic label
      }
    },
    ...
  ],
  "workspaceSummary": {
    "totalCommunities": 7,
    "totalMemories": 312,
    "skylineHealth": "balanced",
    "concerns": ["community_0_is_periphery_heavy", "community_3_has_no_innermost_layer"]
  },
  "degraded": []
}
```

`ee status --skyline` (human render): ASCII heatmap, one block per community.

## Acceptance

- New module `src/graph/skyline.rs` with `compute_knowledge_skyline(snapshot) -> KnowledgeSkyline`.
- `ee status --skyline` cli flag and human/JSON output.
- Schema `ee.status.skyline.v1` documented.
- 6 unit tests + 1 e2e + 1 golden.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: G4 (Louvain communities + k-truss), G5 (onion layers), G1 (PPR percentile), F3 (insights surface). Plus F1, F2, F4.
Blocks: nothing.
Parent: bd-bife.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text: Round 4 pinning. G8.a unit tests (6 cases): (1) Single-community 10-memory fixture, mixed layers/classes: skylineMatrix has 1 entry. (2) 3 communities of size 10/8/5: emitted sorted size-desc. (3) 80% of memories outermost-layer+agent_assertion: skylineHealth=periphery_heavy. (4) Uniform distribution: skylineHealth=balanced. (5) Innermost empty + outer-dense: skylineHealth=core_sparse. (6) >=30% communities periphery_heavy => workspace concerns[] emits. G8.b CLI: JSON emits ee.status.skyline.v1; human emits ASCII heatmap, layers as rows (innermost->outermost) trust as columns. Skyline edge case: <3 communities emits degraded.skyline.degenerate_communities. Age computation: age_days=(now-created).days; cells emit meanAgeDays not decile.

title: [MEDIUM] graph/mod.rs:1658-1666 next_graph_snapshot_version overflow check is dead code (saturating_add(1) on u32::MAX returns u32::MAX, not 0)
close_reason: Fixed: next_graph_snapshot_version now uses checked_add and returns GraphError::SnapshotVersionOverflow when the latest snapshot is u32::MAX instead of saturating and reusing u32::MAX forever. Added regression coverage for u32::MAX. Verification: cargo fmt --check; cargo test graph_snapshot --lib; cargo check --all-targets; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; UBS src/graph/mod.rs exited 0; full cargo test; forbidden dependency audit no matches.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
src/graph/mod.rs:1658-1666:
```
fn next_graph_snapshot_version(conn: &DbConnection, workspace_id: &str) -> Result<u32, String> {
    let next = conn
        .get_latest_graph_snapshot(workspace_id, GraphSnapshotType::MemoryLinks)
        .map_err(|error| format!("Failed to inspect latest graph snapshot: {error}"))?
        .map_or(1, |snapshot| snapshot.snapshot_version.saturating_add(1));
    if next == 0 {
        return Err("Graph snapshot version overflowed".to_owned());
    }
    Ok(next)
}
```
The 'next == 0' check appears to be guarding against u32 wrap. But saturating_add does NOT wrap to 0 — it saturates at u32::MAX. Concrete: if snapshot_version reaches u32::MAX, next = u32::MAX, the 'next == 0' guard is false, function returns u32::MAX. The next call still gets u32::MAX. The system silently stops issuing new versions.

Two bugs in one:
1. The overflow guard never fires (dead code).
2. After 4.29 billion snapshots a single workspace silently re-uses u32::MAX as the snapshot_version forever.

Fix: use checked_add and surface the failure:
```
let next = conn
    .get_latest_graph_snapshot(workspace_id, GraphSnapshotType::MemoryLinks)
    .map_err(|error| format!("Failed to inspect latest graph snapshot: {error}"))?
    .map(|snapshot| snapshot.snapshot_version.checked_add(1).ok_or_else(|| "Graph snapshot version overflowed u32".to_owned()))
    .unwrap_or(Ok(1))?;
Ok(next)
```
Or migrate snapshot_version to u64 if u32 is not architecturally meaningful.

title: [CRITICAL] policy: file permission check uses numeric comparison instead of bitmask
description:
In src/policy/security_profile.rs lines 303 and 348, file permission checks use:

```rust
if mode <= max_mode {
```

This is WRONG. Permission bits are not comparable numerically for security.

Example: max_mode=0o600 (owner rw), actual=0o044 (group r, other r)
- 0o044 = 36 decimal
- 0o600 = 384 decimal  
- 36 <= 384 is TRUE, but 0o044 grants group+other read access!

The correct check is: `(mode & !max_mode) == 0`

This ensures no permission bits are set that aren't in the allowed mask.
close_reason: Fixed: replaced numeric comparison (mode <= max_mode) with bitmask check ((mode & !max_mode) == 0) in both file and directory permission checks. This correctly catches modes that grant unauthorized group/other access.

title: Epic: Graph Algorithms, Auto-Linking, and Retrieval-Feature Completeness (§14)
description:
Source: COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_TO_MAKE_EE__OPUS.md §14 (Knowledge graph layer), specifically §14.2 (algorithms), §14.4 (graph features for retrieval), §14.5 (graph jobs), §14.6 (auto-links).

# Epic: Graph Algorithms, Auto-Linking, and Retrieval-Feature Completeness

## Why this epic exists

§14 of the plan describes a complete graph layer over memories, sessions, rules, and decisions, providing centrality, community, hubs/authorities, articulation, k-core, shortest path, and link explanation. Today only PageRank-based centrality and a partial CoTag autolink dry-run are bead-tracked. Without the rest:

- The retrieval scoring multipliers in §14.4 (centrality_score, authority_score, hub_score, community_id, distance_to_query_seed, same_cluster_as_top_result, evidence_support_count, contradiction_count, orphan_penalty, stale_bridge_penalty) cannot be populated.
- The 7 named graph jobs in §14.5 (graph.refresh.workspace, .global, .compute.centrality, .compute.communities, .compute.link_candidates, .detect.orphans, .detect.contradictions) cannot be scheduled or audited.
- The CoMention auto-link rule (shared Entity neighbour), Hebbian reinforcement (`weight += 0.05`, `evidence_count += 1`, capped at 1.0), and AUTO-source garbage collection (auto-edges removed when underlying memories change) have no implementation beads.

This epic exists so retrieval scoring can use real graph features instead of zero-weight stubs, so the steward can run audited graph jobs, and so auto-linking learns from agent behavior in the bounded, deterministic way the plan specifies.

## Cross-cutting constraints (apply to every child bead under this epic)

- Graph metrics are deterministic: same DB + same fnx-cgse seed → byte-identical metrics_json + identical witness_hash. Asserted by a determinism golden that runs the metric N times and diffs.
- Graph snapshots are derived assets, never source of truth. Losing a snapshot means a rebuild, not a data loss; tests cover the rebuild path.
- All metrics use franken_networkx (fnx-runtime, fnx-classes, fnx-algorithms, fnx-cgse, fnx-convert). No petgraph, no custom hand-rolled algorithms for core metrics. Audited by the forbidden-deps gate.
- Auto-link writes flow through the same advisory-lock-protected single-write-owner path as any other memory write, and produce LinkSource=AUTO rows. Manual-edit-then-auto-rewrite must not silently overwrite human edits; tests cover the conflict.
- Each graph subcommand has a JSON contract (schema string, structured output) and a Markdown / TOON renderer. Witness hashes are emitted on every output.
- Tests log: subcommand, query parameters, snapshot generation, witness_hash, metric vector, total elapsed_ms, and a first_failure_diagnosis on assertion failure.

## Closure criteria

- Subcommands implemented and CLI-bound: `ee graph louvain`, `ee graph communities`, `ee graph k-core --k <n>`, `ee graph articulation`, `ee graph hits`, `ee graph betweenness`, `ee graph path <src> <dst>`, `ee graph explain-link <src> <dst>`. Each emits a stable JSON schema (e.g., `ee.graph.louvain.v1`) and a witness_hash.

title: Differential pack delta protocol — ee context --since <prior-pack-hash> returns JSON patch
description:
## Why this matters (agent token budget at swarm scale)

Long agent sessions repeatedly call `ee context` for slowly-evolving queries. Today every call returns the full pack JSON (often 4-8 KB rendered, 12-30 KB raw). When 10 agents run for 8 hours each at one context request per minute, that's ~5MB/agent of pack JSON moved + parsed + re-tokenized into the agent's prompt context — a non-trivial chunk of the LLM's input budget.

The RIGHT shape for a long-running agent is: 'give me the delta from the last pack you sent me'. Server-side: when an agent passes `--since <prior-pack-hash>`, ee looks up the prior pack record (already persisted per the pack-replay ledger), computes a structural JSON diff against the freshly assembled pack, and returns either:
- The full pack (when the diff is larger than the full pack — degenerate case fallback)
- A delta envelope (`ee.context.delta.v1`) that the agent can apply client-side

## Architecture

ee context --since <hash> [--max-delta-bytes N]:
- Look up prior pack record by hash. If absent (evicted, never recorded, wrong workspace), fall back to a full pack with degraded.context_delta_prior_unknown (severity=low).
- Assemble the new pack normally (canonical key includes everything except --since flag — determinism preserved).
- Compute structural diff: prior_pack.items vs new_pack.items by item.id. Categorize each item as added, removed, modified (one or more fields changed), or unchanged. For modified items, emit per-field changes.
- Build delta envelope:
  {
    'schema': 'ee.context.delta.v1',
    'success': true,
    'data': {
      'priorPackHash': '<input>',
      'newPackHash': '<computed>',
      'baseDbGeneration': <int>,
      'newDbGeneration': <int>,
      'items': {
        'added': [...full item objects...],
        'removed': ['<id1>', '<id2>'],
        'modified': [{ 'id': '<id3>', 'fieldChanges': { 'confidence': [old, new], 'utility': [old, new] } }]
      },
      'tokenSavings': { 'fullBytes': N, 'deltaBytes': M, 'savedBytes': N-M, 'savedPercent': pct }
    }
  }
- If delta envelope serialized > newPack serialized (rare, e.g. complete reshuffle): emit the full pack with degraded.context_delta_larger_than_full (severity=info, NOT a failure — just an honest report).

Determinism contract: --since changes the OUTPUT shape but the COMPUTATION is identical. The new pack's hash + content are the same whether emitted full or as delta. The delta envelope is byte-stable for the same (prior_hash, new_pack_state) pair.

Agent-side apply: documented in docs/agent-ux/context-delta-apply.md as a small TypeScript/Python pseudo-snippet (no library shipped — agents have varied harnesses; the shape is the contract).

## Hard constraints

- Per AGENTS.md determinism: same DB + indexes + config + query → identical newPackHash whether delta or full. New tests pin this.
- Privacy preserved: delta MUST honor the same redaction level as the full pack would have. No 'leak via diff' (e.g. removed field showing pre-redaction value).
- The --since flag is a HINT, not a contract. The server may always return a full pack with a clear reason (degraded code). Agents must handle both shapes.

## File surface

- src/core/context_delta.rs (NEW): compute_pack_delta(prior_pack, new_pack) -> Result<DeltaResult, DomainError>; render_delta_envelope. Inline #[cfg(test)] units.
- src/cli/mod.rs (MODIFY): add --since flag to ContextArgs; --max-delta-bytes flag (default = newPack size).
- src/core/context.rs (MODIFY): handle_context branches on args.since after assembly.
- docs/schemas/ee.context.delta.v1.json (NEW): JSON schema doc with field invariants.
- docs/agent-ux/context-delta-apply.md (NEW): client-side apply guide for agent harnesses.
- src/core/mod.rs (MODIFY): register the new schema in supported_schemas().
- docs/degraded_code_taxonomy.md (MODIFY): add context_delta_prior_unknown (low, response_time), context_delta_larger_than_full (info, response_time).
- tests/fixtures/failure_modes/context_delta_prior_unknown.json (NEW), context_delta_larger_than_full.json (NEW).

## UNIT TESTS REQUIRED

Inline #[cfg(test)] in src/core/context_delta.rs, minimum:
- happy_path__delta_between_identical_packs_is_empty_with_zero_savings
- happy_path__delta_with_one_added_one_removed_yields_correct_envelope
- happy_path__delta_with_modified_field_emits_old_new_pair
- empty_or_boundary__delta_against_empty_prior_returns_full_added_set
- empty_or_boundary__delta_against_empty_new_returns_full_removed_set
- error_or_invalid__delta_envelope_serialized_size_check_correctly_falls_back_to_full
- error_or_invalid__delta_with_redaction_level_mismatch_emits_degraded
- determinism__same_prior_and_new_pack_state_yield_byte_identical_delta_envelope_across_3_runs

## E2E TESTS REQUIRED

tests/context_delta_e2e.rs (NEW): scripts/e2e_overhaul/context_delta.sh (NEW). Sequence:
1. `ee context 'task A' --json` → capture pack hash H1
2. `ee remember --tags taskA 'new fact'` → trigger one new memory
3. `ee context 'task A' --since H1 --json` → assert delta envelope; assert exactly one item in items.added; assert tokenSavings.savedPercent > 0
4. `ee context 'task A' --since DEADBEEF --json` (bogus hash) → assert full pack returned with degraded.context_delta_prior_unknown
5. `ee context 'completely different task' --since H1 --json` → assert either delta with all-removed-all-added OR full pack with context_delta_larger_than_full

Structured logs per AGENTS.md tracing convention: surface=context_delta, phase=lookup_prior|compute_diff|render_delta|fallback_full, plus prior_hash_prefix (8 hex chars), savings_bytes, savings_percent.

## Acceptance

- src/core/context_delta.rs lands with 8+ unit tests passing.
- ee context --since flag implemented; ee context --help mentions it under 'Token efficiency for long agent sessions'.
- e2e proves all 5 scenarios above.
- Two new degraded codes documented + classified.
- ee.context.delta.v1 schema documented; CI schema-drift gate covers it.
- Determinism extended: dimensions = (with --since, without --since); both byte-identical newPackHash for same input state.
- README Performance section gets a row showing realistic delta-vs-full byte savings on a representative workspace.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: nothing. Pack-record ledger already persists the prior_pack lookup (per ADR 0025 — replayable context pack selection ledgers).

Related: bd-17c65.1 (pack format densification — orthogonal); bd-3gutc (alien-artifact swarm responsiveness umbrella).

## Tracing

surface=context_delta; phase=lookup_prior|compute_diff|render_delta|fallback_full; required fields workspace_id, request_id, bead_id=THIS, surface, phase, elapsed_ms, degraded_codes, savings_bytes, savings_percent.

comments.author: PearlPlateau
comments.text:
Phase 6 refinement pass (PearlPlateau).

Re-read AGENTS.md, particularly the "No secrets in context packs" non-goal, the "Explainable retrieval" product principle, and the "Determinism by default" contract. Found 7 gaps/refinements.

### Refined hard constraints

1. PRIOR-HASH VALIDATION (server-side): the `--since <prior-pack-hash>` lookup MUST verify that the named hash was previously emitted by ee for THIS workspace. Specifically:
   - Look up prior_pack in the pack_records ledger by content_hash AND workspace_id AND db_generation (the ledger row carries all three).
   - If not found, emit `degraded.context_delta_prior_unknown` (severity=low, response_time) and return the full pack.
   - REJECT (do not silently accept) hashes the agent computed locally by applying prior deltas — the server cannot verify those, and accepting them opens a replay-attack-style vector where an agent could ask for a "delta from H_attacker" where H_attacker was never an ee output.

2. NO SERVER-SIDE DELTA CHAINING: each `--since` call computes a fresh delta from the named base pack record to the just-assembled new pack. Deltas are NEVER chained server-side. Document this as a load-bearing simplification: the server's correctness contract is "delta is the structural difference between two pack records ee itself has emitted", not "delta layered on top of agent's local state".

3. REDACTION-CLASS-CHANGE SAFETY: if a memory's redaction class changed between the base pack and the new pack (e.g. previously visible, now flagged as containing a secret), the delta MUST emit the REDACTED form (the new pack's view), not the prior unredacted value. The delta MUST NOT include `fieldChanges.content: [old_unredacted, new_redacted]` because that would leak the pre-redaction value via the diff. Implementation: when emitting a `modified` item, the diff path checks the OLD pack's redaction_class against the NEW pack's. If they differ AND the new is more restrictive, the field shows only the new value (not a pair). Add `degraded.context_delta_redaction_drift` (severity=info, response_time) to make this observable.

4. DELTA COMPUTE BUDGET: for pathological pack sizes (e.g. 10000+ items), computing the diff could be expensive enough to dwarf the assembly itself. Add:
   - `EE_CONTEXT_DELTA_COMPUTE_BUDGET_MS` (default 50ms).
   - If delta computation exceeds budget, abandon the delta and return the full pack with `degraded.context_delta_compute_budget_exceeded` (severity=info, response_time).
   - Add unit test `compute_budget__exceeds_returns_full_pack_with_degraded`.

5. JSON PATCH STANDARD CONSIDERATION (decision record): ee.context.delta.v1 uses a custom envelope shape (`added` / `removed` / `modified` arrays) rather than RFC 6902 JSON Patch. Decision rationale (must be embedded in the schema doc):
   - Our delta is item-scoped (memory IDs), not arbitrary JSON path; RFC 6902 over-generalizes for our use case.
   - We carry `tokenSavings` metadata + per-field diffs in a single envelope; RFC 6902 has no slot for that.
   - Agents already know ee.context.v2; piggybacking on that shape minimizes integration friction.
   - JSON Patch can be added later as a separate `ee.context.delta.rfc6902.v1` if a real consumer demand emerges. Not a v1 commitment.

6. BACKWARDS COMPAT CHECK: the `--since` flag is purely additive. Agents that don't know about it MUST continue to call `ee context` normally and receive the full pack with no observable change. Required test additions:
   - tests/golden/context.snap and tests/snapshots/context_full.snap (whatever the existing context goldens are) MUST be unchanged after this bead lands. Determinism gate test asserts this explicitly: `existing_context_goldens_unchanged_when_no_since_flag`.

7. PACK RECORD RETENTION ALIGNMENT: this bead depends on the pack record ledger being present for the named prior_hash. The pack record retention contract (size cap + age cap) is owned by another subsystem. Add cross-reference:
   - If the user has retention configured aggressively (e.g., 1 day), --since requests older than 1 day will return `degraded.context_delta_prior_unknown` more often. Document this trade-off in docs/agent-ux/context-delta-apply.md.
   - Suggest defaults: keep at least the last 24 hours of pack records OR the last 100 records, whichever is larger.

### Refined unit-test obligation (extends original)

Original 8 tests stay. Add:
- prior_hash_validation__rejects_hash_not_in_pack_records_for_workspace
- prior_hash_validation__accepts_valid_hash_from_same_workspace
- prior_hash_validation__rejects_valid_hash_from_DIFFERENT_workspace
- redaction_drift__memory_newly_redacted_emits_redacted_value_only
- redaction_drift__memory_newly_redacted_emits_context_delta_redaction_drift_event
- redaction_drift__memory_redaction_class_unchanged_does_full_field_diff
- compute_budget__exceeds_returns_full_pack_with_degraded
- compute_budget__within_budget_returns_delta_normally
- backwards_compat__existing_context_goldens_unchanged_when_no_since_flag (cross-bead test)
- property_determinism__random_pack_pair_yields_byte_stable_delta_across_3_runs (proptest)

### Refined e2e obligation (extends original)

Original 5-step e2e stays. Add:
- Scenario F (NEW): cross-workspace replay — `ee context` in workspace A → capture H1. `ee context "task" --since H1 --json` in workspace B → MUST return full pack with `degraded.context_delta_prior_unknown` (NOT a delta from A's pack, even if H1 happens to collide with one B has emitted, since the workspace_id is in the ledger lookup).
- Scenario G (NEW): redaction drift — capture pack H1 where memory M has visible content; revise M to add a secret token; capture pack H2; `ee context "task" --since H1 --json`. Assert the modified item shows ONLY the redacted form, no leak of pre-redaction content.
- Scenario H (NEW): compute-budget — generate a synthetic 10k-item pack via fixture, run --since against another 10k-item pack, set `EE_CONTEXT_DELTA_COMPUTE_BUDGET_MS=1`, assert full-pack fallback with the expected degraded code.

### Refined dependency edges (must be added)

- bd-muovx `related to` bd-17c65.1 (Pack format densification) — both shape pack output bytes; coordinate field-name choices.
- bd-muovx `related to` bd-ndzfg (L2 pack cache) — delta protocol benefits from L2 cache; combined, an agent's `--since H1` lookup of H1's record hits L2 instantly.

### Refined acceptance (extends)

Original 6 items stay. Add:
- 4 new degraded codes documented + classified (context_delta_redaction_drift, context_delta_compute_budget_exceeded, plus the 2 original); all have fixtures under `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/`.
- Decision record about RFC 6902 vs custom envelope embedded in `docs/schemas/ee.context.delta.v1.json` description field.
- `EE_CONTEXT_DELTA_COMPUTE_BUDGET_MS` registered in `src/config/env_registry.rs` and documented in `docs/env_vars.md`.
- Cross-workspace replay safety verified via Scenario F e2e.
- Redaction-drift safety verified via Scenario G e2e.

### Encryption / transport note

This bead does NOT introduce a new encryption boundary. The delta envelope inherits whatever transport the agent uses to consume `ee context --json` (typically local CLI stdout, no encryption). Agents that pipe ee output across an untrusted boundary (e.g., over network without TLS) are already in a broken security posture for the full pack as well; the delta does not make this worse. Documentation note in `docs/agent-ux/context-delta-apply.md`.

### Open question (decide before implementation starts)

Should ee provide a server-side apply convenience (`ee context apply-delta --base <hash> --delta-stdin`)? Considered + rejected at refinement time:
- DEFEATS the bead's purpose (delta exists to reduce bytes on the wire; if agent sends both back, they might as well have asked for the full pack).
- Adds a confusing surface that agents would misuse.
- AGENTS CAN already re-query `ee context "<task>" --json` without --since for the canonical full pack.
- Decision: do not add. Document in the bead body and reject if requested.

comments.author: PearlPlateau
comments.text:
Phase 6 refinement pass 2 (PearlPlateau).

Second-order audit after pass 1. Found 10 schema/lifecycle/tooling issues.

### Schema lifecycle

1. SCHEMA VERSIONING POLICY: `ee.context.delta.v1` is the v1 envelope. The bead's docs/schemas/ee.context.delta.v1.json description field MUST document the upgrade-compat policy:
   - v1.x: additive fields only (e.g., new tokenSavings sub-fields, new per-field-diff types). Existing parsers must ignore unknown fields.
   - v2: breaking changes (e.g., re-shaped items.modified). Bump the major; agents pin to v1 until they explicitly upgrade.
   - Per AGENTS.md "Response envelope contract" + "Schema versions" tables: `schema` field is the version pin.
   - Schema drift CI gate (tests/contracts/schema_drift.rs) MUST cover the delta envelope.

2. SCHEMA REGISTRATION: ee.context.delta.v1 MUST be registered in src/core/mod.rs `supported_schemas()` so `ee schema list --json` returns it. Add unit test in src/core/mod.rs that asserts the schema appears in the supported list. Add golden snapshot `tests/snapshots/supported_schemas__includes_context_delta_v1.snap` (per the existing golden test pattern for schema enumeration).

### Tooling / documentation testability

3. LITERATE-PROGRAMMING APPLY TEST: pass 1 specified docs/agent-ux/context-delta-apply.md with pseudo-snippets. Pass 2 adds: `tests/context_delta_apply_roundtrip.rs` that PARSES the documented apply pseudo-code (or implements it from the doc's spec), runs it against a fresh delta envelope, and asserts the reconstructed state matches the full pack from a `--no-since` re-query. If the docs change, the test catches drift. This is the AGENTS.md "Documentation cross-reference" pattern adapted for an apply contract.

4. ee context --help DOCUMENTATION TEXT: the --since flag's --help text MUST include:
   - "Reduces token budget on long agent sessions" (the why)
   - "Pass a pack hash from a prior `ee context --json` response's data.pack.hash" (the how)
   - "Server may return a full pack with `degraded.context_delta_prior_unknown` if the hash is not recognized" (the failure mode)
   - Link to docs/agent-ux/context-delta-apply.md (the deep dive)
   The --help text is part of the user contract; add a test asserting these substrings.

### Determinism cross-checks

5. SAME-NEW-PACK INVARIANT: the new pack's content MUST be identical whether `--since` is provided or not. The delta computation happens AFTER assembly. Pin this via determinism test: `same_query_produces_same_new_pack_hash_with_or_without_since`. This guards against a future implementer accidentally letting --since influence retrieval/scoring.

6. DELTA DETERMINISM PROPERTY TEST: `tests/property_context_delta_determinism.rs` (new) using proptest. For random pairs (prior_pack_state, new_pack_state) from a fixed seeded corpus, the delta envelope MUST be byte-identical across 3 runs. ### Adjacent-surface integration

7. HANDOFF + BACKUP DO NOT CARRY DELTAS: `ee handoff create` and `ee backup create` wrap context output. Decision (must be embedded in the bead): handoff capsules and backup manifests contain FULL packs (the schema for handoff is `ee.handoff.*`, not `ee.context.delta.*`). Delta is a transport-time optimization only. Document this in `docs/agent-ux/context-delta-apply.md` to prevent confusion.

8. L2 CACHE SHORT-CIRCUIT: when bd-ndzfg L2 cache has BOTH the prior pack (by hash lookup) AND the new pack would be L2-resident (by canonical-key lookup), the delta can be computed without re-assembly. Both pack records are read from L2; diff is computed over them; delta envelope is returned. This is a perf bonus when both bd-ndzfg + bd-muovx ship. Add the optimization as an explicit acceptance item:
   - Test `delta__short_circuits_when_both_packs_l2_resident` (requires bd-ndzfg landed).
   - Tracing event `context_delta.l2_short_circuit` when this path fires.
   - Documented in docs/agent-ux/context-delta-apply.md as "fastest path".

### Failure modes

9. ENVELOPE SIZE BUDGET: pass 1 says delta envelope falls back to full pack when delta > full pack size. Pass 2 adds: even when delta < full pack, if delta envelope exceeds `EE_CONTEXT_DELTA_ENVELOPE_MAX_BYTES` (default 10 MiB), emit `degraded.context_delta_envelope_oversized` (severity=warning, response_time) and fall back to full pack. Pathological deltas (e.g. complete pack rewrite where added.len() = 1000) shouldn't ship 10MB JSON to the agent under any circumstance. Add test `envelope_oversized__falls_back_with_degraded`.

10. CANCELLATION MID-DELTA-COMPUTE: if `ee context --since H1` is cancelled mid-delta (e.g. SIGINT after assembly succeeded but before delta envelope is rendered), NO partial delta envelope is emitted. The drop semantics for the in-progress delta state are tested via `tests/cancellation_context_delta.rs` (new, mirroring `tests/cancellation_graph.rs` shape).

### Pack record retention precision

11. PASS 1 SUGGESTED "last 24h OR last 100 records, whichever is larger" as a default. Pass 2: this is a contract owned by ADR 0025 (replayable context pack selection ledgers per README). Implementer MUST:
    - Verify the current pack_records retention default in the existing config (file likely under `src/core/pack_record_retention.rs` or similar).
    - If the existing default is more aggressive than 24h/100, file a child bead `bd-muovx.1` titled "Pack record retention defaults for delta protocol viability" with proposed new default and rationale.
    - Do NOT silently change the existing retention default as part of bd-muovx — that affects an existing user contract.

- Scenario I (NEW): ee context --help asserts the documented substrings about --since.
- Scenario J (NEW): same-new-pack invariant — `ee context "X" --json` (capture hash); `ee context "X" --since DEADBEEF --json` (full pack returned with degraded code); assert the new pack hash from both calls is identical (the --since flag did not influence assembly).
- Scenario K (NEW): envelope-oversized — generate a synthetic case where delta serialized exceeds 10 MiB but is still smaller than full pack; assert `degraded.context_delta_envelope_oversized` + full-pack fallback.
- Scenario L (NEW): cancellation — start `ee context --since H1` against a slow assembly (use the asupersync LabRuntime budget), SIGINT mid-flight, assert no partial output and clean process exit.
- Scenario M (NEW, depends on bd-ndzfg landed): L2-short-circuit perf — warm L2 with both prior pack and new pack; `ee context --since H1` should complete in << assembly-time-from-cold (assert p50 ≤ 20ms when both packs are L2-resident).

### Pass 2 acceptance (extends pass 1)

- Schema lifecycle documented in docs/schemas/ee.context.delta.v1.json description.
- Schema registered in supported_schemas() with golden snapshot.
- ee context --help asserts the documented substring contract.
- Literate-programming apply roundtrip test (`tests/context_delta_apply_roundtrip.rs`).
- 5 new e2e scenarios (I-M) shipped.
- 3 new degraded codes filed: `context_delta_envelope_oversized` (and the pass-1 + pass-2 codes — full catalog: `context_delta_prior_unknown`, `context_delta_larger_than_full`, `context_delta_redaction_drift`, `context_delta_compute_budget_exceeded`, `context_delta_envelope_oversized`).
- L2 short-circuit path documented + tested when bd-ndzfg has landed.
- Cross-link bd-muovx.1 (if filed) for pack-record retention default change.

### Tracing fields extended

`surface=context_delta`; `phase=lookup_prior|compute_diff|render_delta|fallback_full|l2_short_circuit|envelope_oversized|cancelled`; fields workspace_id, request_id, bead_id=bd-muovx, surface, phase, elapsed_ms, degraded_codes, prior_hash_prefix (8 hex), new_hash_prefix (8 hex), savings_bytes, savings_percent, envelope_bytes.

### Open question (decide before implementation starts, pass 2)

Should the delta envelope support COMPRESSED bodies (gzip) for very large deltas? Considered + DEFERRED:
- Agent stdin/stdout is typically uncompressed plain text.
- Agents would need a decompression step that varies per harness.
- The envelope_oversized fallback to full-pack already prevents pathological cases.
- If swarm-scale measurements show this matters later, file a follow-up `bd-muovx.2` for "Compressed delta envelope for very large diffs".

comments.author: PearlPlateau
comments.text:
Phase 6 refinement pass 3 (PearlPlateau).

Third audit. Focus: agent-side token-accounting docs, no-op delta decision, savings telemetry, failure injection, format-matrix coverage (markdown/TOON with --since), and the dual-render parity gate. 7 items.

### Agent-side token-budget accounting

1. AGENT MUST COUNT BASE+DELTA TOKENS TOGETHER: when an agent receives a delta envelope, the agent's prompt-budget calculator MUST account for BOTH:
   - The base pack's token count (already in the agent's previous prompt), AND
   - The delta envelope's token count (the new payload).
   If the agent only counts the delta, it under-counts and risks blowing its model's context window. Document this prominently in docs/agent-ux/context-delta-apply.md:
   - First sentence of the doc must say: "Delta payloads add to your prompt; they do not replace the base pack."
   - Worked example: agent has pack P1 (3500 tokens) + delta D1 (200 tokens) → effective prompt size = 3700 tokens.
   - Also note: when the new pack's logical size SHRINKS (e.g. memory removed), the delta has a `tokenSavings.netPackTokens` field showing the NEW logical pack's token count so agents can budget on the new size.
   Add `tokenSavings.netPackTokens` to the schema. Update unit tests to pin this field.

### No-op delta decision record

2. NO-OP DELTA DOES NOT SPECIAL-CASE: when prior == new (no changes since last call), the delta envelope is `{ items: { added:[], removed:[], modified:[] }, tokenSavings: {...} }`. Should this be replaced with a tinier `{ schema, success, data:{ noChange: true, baseHash, ... } }` envelope? Considered + REJECTED:
   - Saves ~50 bytes per no-op (marginal).
   - Adds a third response shape agents must handle (now: full / delta / no-change), increasing complexity.
   - Empty arrays serialize compactly anyway.
   Decision: empty-arrays-stay. Document in the bead. Add unit test `no_op_delta__empty_arrays_returned_not_special_cased` to lock the contract.

### Server-side savings telemetry

3. SAVINGS METRIC AT TRACING LEVEL: when delta savings ≥ 50%, emit a tracing event `context_delta.high_savings` with `{ workspace_id, request_id, prior_hash_prefix, new_hash_prefix, savings_percent, savings_bytes }`. This lets operators validate at swarm scale that the delta protocol is actually paying off. Also report aggregate p50/p99 savings_percent in `ee status --json data.context_delta.savings_percentile_24h`. Add unit test `telemetry__high_savings_event_emits_when_pct_ge_50`.

### Failure injection

4. CORRUPTED PRIOR-PACK-RECORD HANDLING: pack records are persisted; their integrity is protected by the ledger's chain hash (per ADR 0025). If an operator (or an attacker, or bit rot) corrupts a row in pack_records such that the stored body's hash no longer matches the stored content_hash, the prior lookup returns an inconsistent record. The delta computation MUST detect this:
   - Verify the pack_records row's body_hash matches blake3(body) on load.
   - On mismatch: emit `degraded.context_delta_prior_corrupted` (severity=high, response_time), fall back to full pack, surface a repair hint pointing at `ee db check-integrity` (which we just shipped per bd-3usjw.1.3 — full circle).
   - Add unit test `prior_lookup__detects_body_hash_mismatch_and_falls_back`.
   - Add e2e test that corrupts a pack_records row, then runs ee context --since, asserts the degraded code + repair hint + clean assembly.

### Format-matrix coverage

5. --since IS JSON-ONLY in v1: the delta envelope is `ee.context.delta.v1` JSON. Markdown / TOON / Mermaid renderers do NOT have a delta form yet. Therefore:
   - `ee context "X" --since H1 --format markdown` → returns the FULL markdown pack with `degraded.context_delta_format_unsupported` (severity=info, response_time). Agent gets useful output + clear signal that delta wasn't applied.
   - Same for `--format toon`, `--format mermaid`.
   - JSON / JSONL / Compact / Hook renderers DO support delta.
   Add to the failure-mode catalog. Add unit test `unsupported_format__emits_degraded_and_returns_full`.
   Cross-reference bd-17c65.4 (Schema consistency: canonical content field, JSON/Markdown parity) — adding markdown-delta later is a v2 surface, not in scope for v1.

### Cross-renderer parity gate alignment

6. RENDERER PARITY MATRIX GATE (bd-17c65.4.9 / D8): when bd-17c65.4.9 (Cross-renderer parity matrix golden + CI gate) lands, the matrix MUST include a "supports_since_flag" column declaring which renderers honor --since. The pass-1+2 spec didn't address this matrix integration. Add to the bead:
   - Coordinate with bd-17c65.4.9 implementer: when both land, the parity matrix asserts that markdown/toon/mermaid renderers emit `degraded.context_delta_format_unsupported` AND a full pack (not an error).
   - File this as a child bead `bd-muovx.3` if bd-17c65.4.9 has shipped before bd-muovx, OR as an explicit acceptance item in bd-muovx if bd-muovx ships first.

### Determinism interaction with feature flags

7. FEATURE-FLAG DIMENSION IN canonical_key: bd-ndzfg's canonical_key includes feature_flag_set_hash. The delta computation uses TWO pack records (prior + new). If feature flags differed between the two assemblies (e.g. prior was built without graph-feature-A; new is built with it), the resulting items may differ for reasons unrelated to memory state. The delta should HONESTLY report this in degraded codes:
   - `degraded.context_delta_feature_flag_drift` (severity=info, response_time) emitted when prior.feature_flag_set_hash != new.feature_flag_set_hash.
   - Delta is still computed and returned; the degraded code flags the dimension difference so agents can explain unexpected modifications to users.
   - Add unit test `feature_flag_drift__emitted_when_prior_and_new_disagree`.

### Pass 3 acceptance (extends pass 1 + pass 2)

- `tokenSavings.netPackTokens` field added to ee.context.delta.v1 schema; agents have the new pack's logical token count.
- No-op delta empty-arrays-stay decision locked by test.
- `context_delta.high_savings` tracing event + p50/p99 aggregate in ee status.
- Corrupted prior pack record detected via body_hash verification; degraded code + repair hint pointing to `ee db check-integrity`; e2e test.
- `degraded.context_delta_format_unsupported` for markdown/toon/mermaid + `degraded.context_delta_feature_flag_drift` for FF dimension differences; both fixtures filed.
- Cross-bead coordination with bd-17c65.4.9 (parity matrix) recorded as explicit acceptance item OR child bead.

### Test count audit

After all 3 refinement passes, bd-muovx's accumulated unit test list:
- 8 (original) + 10 (pass 1) + 10 (pass 2) + 6 (pass 3) = 34 unit tests
- 5 (original) + 3 (pass 1) + 5 (pass 2) + 1 (pass 3) = 14 e2e scenarios
- Plus 1 property test, 1 literate-programming roundtrip test, 1 cancellation test

This is comprehensive and matches AGENTS.md "Property and fuzz tests" + "Integration tests" + inline unit obligation. Future passes should ADD only when a real gap is found; the test count is now structurally complete.

### Open question (pass 3)

Should v2 of the delta envelope use COLUMNAR encoding (e.g. one array of IDs + parallel arrays of changed fields) instead of row-based items.added/items.removed/items.modified? Considered + DEFERRED:
- Columnar saves ~30% bytes on packs with many small diffs.
- Significantly harder to parse for agent harnesses.
- v1 row-based shape is the right tradeoff for first release.
- If a v2 user emerges, file `bd-muovx.4` for columnar-delta-envelope research.
- Decision: not v1. Recorded.

title: G5: Articulation points + onion layers for ee curate — structurally-informed decay
description:
# G5 — Articulation points + onion layers for `ee curate` (structural decay)

## Idea (one-liner)

Replace `ee curate`'s uniform age-decay with structurally-informed decay: **articulation points** (bridges) get a decay multiplier ≤ 1 — they're protected because their removal disconnects clusters. **Onion layer index** determines per-memory decay rate — innermost shells are effectively permanent, outermost shells decay 3× as fast.

## Why this matters

Curate today is rule-based + age decay (uniform across memories). This is the first time graph structure informs **retention policy** rather than just retrieval scoring.

- **Articulation points** = memories that, if tombstoned, would disconnect knowledge clusters. These are structural single-points-of-failure; losing them is irreversible because the inferred relationships between the disconnected halves disappear too.
- **Onion layers** = nested k-shells from innermost (densely-interconnected core knowledge) to outermost (peripheral leaf memories). The core knowledge is what makes the workspace valuable; peripheral memories are mostly transient context that should age out.

Pragmatic, structurally-derived, lowest-risk high-payoff. Pure structure — no model dependence; no embeddings; no probabilistic priors. Lands on a surface that already exists with minimal new schema.

## Algorithms

1. **Articulation points**: `fnx_algorithms::articulation_points(memory_links_undirected_view)`. Returns the set of node IDs whose removal disconnects the graph (more precisely: increases the number of connected components). O(V+E) via Tarjan's algorithm.

2. **Onion layers / k-shell decomposition**: `fnx_algorithms::onion_layers_rust(memory_links_undirected_view)`. Returns per-node onion layer index. Layer 0 = outermost peeled first; higher layer = deeper inside. O(V+E).

3. **PageRank with negative weights on `contradicts` edges** (bonus, complements G4): A variant of G1's PPR that subtracts contribution from `contradicts` edges. Surfaces "trust net of contradiction" — a memory cited by 5 but contradicted by 3 should rank lower than one cited by 5 only. Custom implementation atop fnx_algorithms::pagerank_directed using negative edge weights (CGSE Hardened mode for non-determinism handling).

## Decay policy

Define `structural_decay_multiplier(memory)`:

```
base_multiplier = 1.0  // legacy uniform decay
onion_normalized = (max_layer - memory.onion_layer) / max_layer  // 0 (innermost) to 1 (outermost)
onion_multiplier = 1.0 + 2.0 * onion_normalized  // 1× innermost, 3× outermost
articulation_multiplier = 0.5 if memory.is_articulation_point else 1.0  // halve decay for bridges
final = onion_multiplier * articulation_multiplier
```

Multiplier applies to whatever age-based decay `ee curate` already uses (the multiplier shortens the half-life: e.g., outermost shell halves at 1/3 the timescale).

## Output shape

`ee curate dry-run --json`:

```jsonc
"curatePlan": {
  ...,  // existing fields
  "structuralAdjustments": [
    {
      "memoryId": "mem_...",
      "onionLayer": 4,
      "isArticulationPoint": true,
      "baseDecay": 0.05,
      "structuralMultiplier": 0.5,
      "adjustedDecay": 0.025,
      "rationale": "articulation_point_in_layer_4"
    },
    ...
  ]
}
```

Plus an insights section:

`ee insights --section bridges` → top articulation points with cluster-disconnection-magnitude.

## Acceptance

- New module `src/graph/decay.rs` with `compute_structural_decay_multiplier(graph, memory_id) -> f64` and `compute_articulation_points + onion_layers` exposed.
- `src/core/curate.rs` (wherever decay runs) multiplies by the structural multiplier.
- New cli flag: `ee curate --no-structural-decay` to opt out (legacy behavior).
- `ee insights --section bridges` surfaces articulation points.
- 7 unit tests + 1 e2e + 1 golden.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: F1 (memory_links snapshot already exists; this needs articulation-point/onion-layer caching on it), F2, F4.
Blocks: G8 (knowledge skyline uses onion layers from this bead).
Parent: bd-bife.

## Related code

- `src/core/curate.rs` — decay computation.
- `src/cli/curate.rs` — surface integration.

Patch 556450a6 seeds a deterministic bridge/leaf curation fixture in scripts/e2e_overhaul/g5_curate_decay.sh, asserts default structuralAdjustments including bridge articulation protection, and preserves --no-structural-decay opt-out omission/empty behavior. Static checks passed (bash -n, shellcheck -x, git diff --check), and remote-only RCH cargo test --test g5_curate_decay_e2e -- --nocapture passed on trj with command_hash 0e13fa0c364c8ce91bf57c71f6203990d5796b646ac6254fb9a073ec437e2523, exit 0, degraded_codes none. comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
## Phase 6 refinement notes — edge cases

1. **max_layer = 1**: If the entire graph is one onion shell (everything is core OR everything is periphery), structural_decay_multiplier collapses to 1.0 for every memory. Formula: when max_layer < 2, return baseline multiplier (1.0). Test: 1 case in G5.a unit suite.

2. **Disconnected graph + articulation_points**: Articulation points are computed per connected component. The 'cluster-disconnection-magnitude' insight (ee insights --section bridges) must show component-scoped magnitude, not global.

3. **Decay-multiplier interaction with bd-bife.5 config**: graph.curate.onion_decay_max (default 3.0) and graph.curate.articulation_protection (default 0.5) — both promoted to config per RX5.

4. **ADR**: bd-mvld.5 documents the decision to make decay structurally-informed. The ADR includes the 3 rejected alternatives and the math derivation.

Update G5.a + G5.b accordingly.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
## Round 3 acceptance pinning — dry-run vs execute

### Behavior matrix
| Command | --no-structural-decay | structural multiplier applied |
|---|---|---|
| ee curate dry-run --json | false (default) | YES; output shows structuralAdjustments[] |
| ee curate dry-run --json --no-structural-decay | true | NO; output omits structuralAdjustments[] (or shows it as empty) |
| ee curate execute | false (default) | YES; tombstones honor the structural multiplier |
| ee curate execute --no-structural-decay | true | NO; tombstones use legacy uniform decay |

### Articulation-point precedence
- Bridge memory + age > threshold → structural_multiplier=0.5, so half-life is 2× the threshold.
- This means the bridge memory is NOT tombstoned unless the threshold is also doubled.
- User can override via ee memory tombstone <id> --reason 'manual' (bypasses curate entirely).

### Load-bearing precedence (interaction with G9)
- Load-bearing memories (G9) get a hard 'do not tombstone' badge by default.
- Articulation points get a 'soft' 0.5× decay multiplier.
- Both protections combine: bridge + load-bearing = strongest protection = effectively immortal until explicitly tombstoned.

### G5.d e2e test cases
1. Seed: 5 memories, 1 is articulation, 1 is innermost-layer, 3 are periphery.
2. Run ee curate dry-run --json. Expected: periphery has decay > baseline; articulation has decay < baseline; innermost has decay ≈ 0.
3. Compare against --no-structural-decay run: all 5 should have decay = baseline.
4. Verify structuralAdjustments[] block emitted in default mode, absent in --no-structural-decay.

title: G5.adr: ADR — Structural decay policy (curate is no longer uniform)
description:
Write docs/adr/00XX-structural-decay-policy.md.

## Decision
ee curate's age-based decay is now multiplied by a structural-decay multiplier derived from articulation-point status and onion-layer index. Default is structurally-informed; --no-structural-decay restores legacy uniform behavior.

## Why this needs an ADR
This is a policy change affecting retention. Future curate audits will see different decay rates per memory; without ADR, the rationale is invisible.

## Rejected alternatives
1. Hand-tuned per-memory decay multipliers (rejected: not derivable from structure)
2. Per-trust-class decay rates only (rejected: doesn't capture structural importance — a low-trust memory at an articulation point is still load-bearing)
3. Probabilistic decay via Beta posterior (rejected: that's a separate axis; this ADR concerns structure, not feedback signals)

## Verification
1 contract test verifying articulation point + onion layer correctly modulate decay.

Parent: bd-mvld. Blocked by: G5.a-G5.d.
Acceptance: ADR lands, indexed in docs/adr/README.md, sections present per AGENTS.md template.

title: [idea-wizard] Epic: Differential swarm performance forensics
description:
## Background

The fcq1 and k8dp tracks established deterministic swarm-scale fixtures, benchmark/support-bundle artifacts, performance explain reports, host-adaptive profiles, and profile evidence. The next gap is not another benchmark harness or host profile. Operators and agents now need to compare two runs or support bundles and answer: what regressed, how severe is it, which subsystem likely owns it, and what evidence supports that conclusion?

This epic creates a read-only differential performance-forensics surface. It consumes existing benchmark reports, explain-performance reports, support-bundle manifests, profile evidence, cache/write queue reports, and swarm contention artifacts. It emits stable JSON with normalized artifact summaries, deltas, confidence/degradation codes, owner hints, and repair commands.

## Product boundary

- `ee` remains a CLI-first memory substrate, not a profiler daemon, scheduler, benchmark universe, or agent orchestrator.
- This epic must not duplicate Frankensearch, FrankenSQLite, FrankenNetworkX, Asupersync, fcq1 benchmark logic, or k8dp profile logic.
- All commands are read-only unless a future explicit budget-promotion bead adds dry-run mutation.
- Missing metrics, mismatched profiles, stale artifacts, and redaction gaps are honest degradations, never zeros or silent passes.

## Target user value

When a massive swarm slows down after a change, a future agent should be able to run a compare command against two redacted artifacts and get a deterministic answer that is useful before opening a flamegraph: latency/RSS/index/cache/write deltas, profile mismatch warnings, likely subsystem owners, and concrete next commands.

## Closure criteria

This epic closes only when child beads provide the ADR, normalized artifact schema, deterministic compare core, CLI surfaces, golden fixtures, logged no-mock E2E, support-bundle integration, and operator docs. Closure also requires `bv --robot-insights` to report no cycles and RCH-backed verification for the implemented slices.

title: [perf-forensics][adr] Define read-only regression compare contract

## Background
