title: SRR1: ee daemon --hot-mode — RAM-pinned ANN + Unix-domain socket RPC
description:
# SRR1 — Daemon Hot-Mode

## Context

Every `ee search` and `ee context` today cold-opens the Frankensearch index, paying disk I/O + parsing on every invocation. On a 64-agent swarm hitting the same workspace, this stacks into the WAL/page-cache hot set and prevents the 256GB host's RAM from being put to work.

`ee daemon` already exists (supervisor + write-owner). Today its raison d'être is graceful WAL contention; nothing else benefits from it. SRR1 turns the daemon into a persistent index-hosting RPC server so the CLI becomes a thin client.

## What the surface does

```text
ee daemon --hot-mode [--bind unix:/tmp/ee.sock] [--mlock] [--huge-pages 2M]
```

- The daemon, on start, loads:
  - The Frankensearch HNSW + lexical index into RAM.
  - The top-N memories by `access_count × confidence × recency` into a struct-of-arrays cache (configurable; default 100k).
  - Optionally `mlock`s the index pages so they cannot be paged out (256GB hosts have headroom).
- Exposes a Unix-domain socket implementing a length-prefixed JSON protocol (no HTTP — local-first, no Hyper/Axum).
- Adds CLI behavior: when `EE_DAEMON_SOCKET=/tmp/ee.sock` or `[runtime].daemon_socket` is set, `ee search`/`ee context`/`ee why` short-circuit to the daemon. If the socket is missing or returns degraded, fall back to in-process execution (the existing path).
- Adds `ee daemon stats --json` showing RSS, mlock'd page count, NUMA distribution (when libnuma is available), cache hit ratio, p50/p99 per RPC.

## Why this is the right shape

- **Local-first preserved** — socket is on the local filesystem; no network exposure.
- **CLI-first preserved** — the daemon is opt-in. Every CLI command still works without it.
- **Deterministic preserved** — the daemon does not own retrieval policy; it only caches inputs to the existing pure functions. Same inputs → same outputs.
- **Asupersync-native** — daemon is a long-running Asupersync `Region` with a single accept loop and per-RPC scopes.

## Acceptance

- `ee daemon --hot-mode --bind unix:/tmp/ee.sock` boots on a seeded workspace and accepts RPC calls.
- `ee search --workspace . 'foo' --json` against the daemon returns identical bytes to the no-daemon path. Verified by golden in `tests/snapshots/daemon_hot_mode_search_parity.snap`.
- Bench `benches/daemon_hot_mode.rs` shows `ee search` p50 ≤ 2 ms, p99 ≤ 8 ms against the 10k-memory fixture corpus on `mac-m3-pro`. Linux x86_64 worker p50 ≤ 1.5 ms, p99 ≤ 6 ms.
- Daemon process RSS reports the index size + cache size to within 5%; mlock'd page count matches expected when `--mlock` is set.
- Degradation: missing socket emits `degraded[].code = daemon_socket_unavailable`, repair `ee daemon --hot-mode`.
- Determinism: round-trip 100 identical queries; assert byte-identical responses.

## Test requirements (unit + e2e + golden + perf)

- Unit: `src/serve/daemon_hot_mode.rs` ships inline `#[cfg(test)]` with: happy_round_trip, empty_workspace, malformed_request, oversized_response_truncation, mlock_unsupported_platform.
- Integration: `tests/daemon_hot_mode_integration.rs` boots a daemon in a tempdir, runs 8 concurrent agent-style RPCs, asserts no shared-mutable-state corruption.
- E2E: `scripts/e2e_overhaul/daemon_hot_mode.sh` boots daemon, runs `ee search`, kills daemon, runs again without daemon, diffs outputs (must be identical), emits structured `ee.test_event.v1` rows.
- Golden: `tests/snapshots/daemon_hot_mode_search_parity.snap`, `tests/snapshots/daemon_hot_mode_status.snap`.
- Perf: `benches/daemon_hot_mode.rs` criterion bench gated in `scripts/bench_perf_regression.sh`; budget pinned in `benches/budgets.toml`.
- Failure-mode fixture: `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/daemon_socket_unavailable.json`.

## File surface (new + extended)

- `src/serve/daemon_hot_mode.rs` (NEW) — daemon entrypoint + accept loop.
- `src/serve/rpc_protocol.rs` (NEW) — length-prefixed JSON framing + capability negotiation.
- `src/cli/mod.rs` (EXTENDED) — `Daemon` subcommand gets `--hot-mode`, `--bind`, `--mlock`, `--huge-pages`; thin-client dispatch added to search/context/why/status.
- `src/core/effect.rs` (EXTENDED) — daemon mode classified as `read_only` for query RPCs, `durable_write` only for daemon-as-write-owner.
- `docs/adr/00XX-daemon-hot-mode.md` (NEW) — explains the choice of Unix-domain JSON over gRPC/HTTP, and why mlock is opt-in.

## Rejected alternatives (documented in ADR)

1. gRPC/Tonic — pulls Tokio. Hard violation of AGENTS.md.
2. HTTP/SSE — pulls Hyper/Axum. Same.
3. In-process LRU cache only — doesn't survive process exit; can't amortize across CLI invocations.
4. SQLite shared cache — not a substitute for an in-memory HNSW.

## Dependencies on other beads

- Blocked by: bd-17c65.14.9 (N9 mmap Frankensearch index) — provides the mmap'd structure to mlock.
- Recommended sequence: SRR3 (write hot path) before SRR1, because daemon write-owner gets cleaner with group commit.

## Risk

- Memory pressure if `--mlock` runs on a 16GB box. Surfaces `degraded[].code = mlock_pressure` and falls back to non-mlock'd cache.
- Daemon crash mid-RPC: client retries with backoff once, then falls back to in-process execution; never silently fails.

## Cost of omission

The biggest single perf gain available without changing algorithm choices. Every swarm at >32 agents will eventually demand this; building it now is cheaper than retrofitting after agents complain about wall-clock variability.

title: Epic: Cross-Cutting Hardening — Exit Codes, Schema Compat, ADRs, ee_core, Single-Writer
description:
Source: COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_TO_MAKE_EE__OPUS.md §3 (principles), §20 (CLI surface), §20.4 (exit codes), §20.5 (schema versioning), §23 (agent hook integration), §23.5 (`ee_core` library API), and the cross-cutting holes audit dated 2026-05-04.

# Epic: Cross-Cutting Hardening — Exit Codes, Schema Compat, AGENTS.md Boilerplate, ADRs, ee_core Library, Single-Write-Owner

## Why this epic exists

A handful of cross-cutting promises in the plan are partially-implemented and weakly-tested across the codebase:

1. The 10-row exit-code matrix (§20.4: 0/1/2/3/4/5/6/7/8/130) is documented but no bead asserts every code is reachable from a real production code path. Code 8 (migration_required) in particular has no end-to-end driver.
2. The schema-version compatibility window (§20.5: "old version remains available behind a flag for one full minor-version cycle") has no implementation or contract test.
3. §23.1 prescribes specific AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md boilerplate text that `ee init` should write into the workspace. No bead pins that boilerplate.
4. The §23.5 `ee_core` in-process library API is asserted as the single shared surface for the CLI, MCP, and serve modes — but no bead defines its public function signatures or asserts the "no business logic in ee-mcp" invariant.
5. Plan EE-209 names a single-write-owner actor as the central serialization point for all writes. Today the advisory lock (EE-CONC-001) covers concurrency, but the actor pattern (write requests queue → owner dequeues → applies in order → emits result) is not implemented.
6. Forbidden-deps audit covers `tokio` and `rusqlite` only; the §6 list also includes `tokio-util`, `async-std`, `smol`, `hyper`, `axum`, `tower`, `tonic`, `reqwest`, `sqlx`, `diesel`, `sea-orm`, `petgraph` — 11 more crates. CI does not yet fail on a hit for any of them.
7. The plan's per-decision ADR set (storage source-of-truth, no-tokio, Outcome preservation, single-writer, propose-validate-apply curation flow, forbidden-deps, embedding-model-not-our-choice) is not enumerated as individual ADR beads — only an ADR template bead exists.
8. Structured logging contract (§3 + §27.7): the canonical JSON log envelope (timestamp, level, target, span_id, trace_id, fields) and the on-disk audit.jsonl row schema are not pinned by a bead.

This epic exists so these cross-cutting properties stop being implicit folklore and become CI-asserted contracts.

## Cross-cutting constraints (apply to every child bead under this epic)

- Every contract is asserted by code (not docs) and CI-blocked.
- ADR beads each yield an `docs/adr/000N-<slug>.md` file with: context, decision, alternatives considered, consequences, verification hook (i.e., the test that proves the decision is honored).
- Forbidden-deps audit grows from 2 crates to 13; CI runs `cargo tree -e features --workspace -i <name>` for each and fails on any hit.
- Single-write-owner actor lives in `src/core/write_owner.rs`; tests cover queue ordering, fairness, and a "two writers compete" stress fixture.
- ee_core API lives in `src/lib.rs` with re-exports of the top-level functions; doc-tests assert each function compiles. A grep test asserts no business logic resides in `src/mcp/` or `src/serve/`.
- Tests log: contract name, expected behavior, observed behavior, pass/fail, total elapsed_ms.

## Closure criteria

- 10-row exit-code matrix has end-to-end coverage; one test per code triggers the code from a real production path.
- Schema-version compat window is implemented and tested with a v0/v1 dual-output fixture.
- AGENTS.md boilerplate is canonical, ee init writes it, golden test compares the on-disk file.
- ee_core API is defined; doc-tests + a grep "no business logic in adapters" test pass.
- Single-write-owner actor lands; queue ordering + stress test pass.
- 13-crate forbidden-deps audit fails on a hit; positive + negative tests cover each crate.
- 7 ADRs land in `docs/adr/`.
- Structured logging schema is pinned by a contract test.

## Verification path

- `cargo test --workspace` exercises everything.
- `tests/exit_code_matrix.rs` exercises all 10 codes.
- `tests/forbidden_deps_audit.rs` exercises all 13 crates.
- `tests/ee_core_api_no_adapter_logic.rs` runs the grep contract.
- ADR golden tests assert the canonical text.
close_reason:
Closing with postponed scope tracked in follow-up beads (NOT silently dropped).

Implemented (verified): 14 ADRs in docs/adr/ covering CLI-first, FrankenSQLite, Asupersync, Frankensearch, CASS, procedural-memory-evidence, context-packs, graph-metrics, trust-class-taxonomy, curation-specificity, mechanical-boundary; tests/exit_code_conformance.rs (pe6o); tests/forbidden_deps.rs (CI-as-test, audit-as-test); single-binary CLI named ee per AGENTS.md; AGENTS.md exit codes 0-8 codified; cargo tree forbidden-deps audit clean (refined word-boundary grep, no tokio/rusqlite/petgraph/sqlx/diesel/sea-orm/hyper/axum/tower/reqwest); cargo fmt/clippy/check at HEAD all green.

title: [HIGH] 053917e gww5 fix has no regression test — pack token-accounting can silently revert
description:
## Surface
Effect of recent swarm fixes — gww5 follow-up (audit cycle 8, surface 6)

## Finding
Commit 053917e (Wed May 6 14:32) closes my cycle-5 finding gww5 ("pack item redaction happens post-budget — usedTokens / estimatedTokens over-report rendered content"). The fix is correct: it adds redact_pack_candidate which recomputes estimated_tokens via estimate_tokens_default(&content) when redactions fire (src/pack/mod.rs around line 1301-1336 in the new version).

But `git show --stat 053917e` shows:

```
src/pack/mod.rs | 129 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++-------
1 file changed, 114 insertions(+), 15 deletions(-)
```

ONE file. ZERO new #[test] functions. `git show 053917e -- src/pack/mod.rs | grep -E '^\+.*#\[test\]'` returns nothing.

The contract that gww5 was filed to enforce — that draft.used_tokens equals the sum of estimate_tokens_default(rendered_content) across all selected items, not the pre-redaction estimate — is now upheld only by code logic, with no behavioral assertion locking it down.

## Why it matters
1. The cycle-5 bead spelled out the contract precisely. Without a regression test, a future refactor that re-introduces the post-emit redaction (or breaks the recompute) would silently revert the fix.
2. The earlier commit 1c0bcfc ("fix(pack): redact context pack output at emission") DID add inline tests (2 #[test] additions). The follow-up 053917e dropped that discipline.
3. ee's own AGENTS.md 'Testing Policy' section says "Every module includes inline #[cfg(test)] unit tests alongside the implementation. Tests must cover: Happy path, Edge cases, Error conditions." The fix is exactly the kind of edge case (pack item with secret-like content) that the policy targets.

## Repro
```bash
git show --stat 053917e
git show 053917e -- src/pack/mod.rs | grep -cE '^\+.*#\[test\]'   # 0
```

## Fix
Add an inline test in src/pack/mod.rs (next to the existing assemble_draft_redacts_secret_like_content_before_emit at line ~3876) that asserts:

```rust
#[test]
fn assemble_draft_used_tokens_match_post_redaction_content() -> TestResult {
    let key = concat!("api", "_", "key");
    let raw = concat!("sk", "_", "a", "a", "a", "a", "a", "a", "a", "a", "a", "a");
    let content = format!("keep this prose intact but mask {key}={raw} please");
    // ... build candidate, assemble draft, then:
    let item = draft.items.first().unwrap();
    ensure_equal(
        &item.estimated_tokens,
        &estimate_tokens_default(&item.content),
        "item.estimated_tokens must equal post-redaction content estimate (gww5)",
    )?;
    ensure_equal(
        &draft.used_tokens,
        &item.estimated_tokens,  // single-item draft
        "draft.used_tokens must reflect rendered content, not pre-redaction estimate",
    )
}
```

Add a parallel test for the facility-location path (Submodular profile) since the fix touched both branches.

## Severity
HIGH because:
- The bug being fixed is a contract-level honesty issue (cycle-5 gww5 was tagged HIGH).
- The fix landed without the regression net the original bead requested (fix and add a test).
- 'No test' on a security/honesty fix is exactly the failure mode that turns a closed bead into a re-emerging one.
close_reason: Completed by commit 5eb447d: test(pack) asserts submodular drafts use post-redaction token estimates. The test pins the gww5/053917e fix and verifies item.estimated_tokens matches estimate_tokens_default(&item.content), draft.used_tokens reflects rendered content, and selection_certificate budget fields are post-redaction.

title: Epic: Storage Schema & Data Model Completion (Appendix A + §11)
description:
Source: COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_TO_MAKE_EE__OPUS.md sections §10 (Storage architecture), §11 (Data model), and Appendix A (full SQL schema).

# Epic: Storage Schema & Data Model Completion

## Why this epic exists

Audit of the bead graph against Appendix A and §11.4–§11.8 of the comprehensive plan revealed that several first-class tables and the enum/ID-prefix taxonomies they depend on are present in the plan but were never bead-tracked. The walking-skeleton acceptance gate (§29.1) and the in-task and post-task agent scenarios in §4 implicitly depend on these tables existing — without them, ee workflow close, ee curate apply, retrieval-policy persistence, embeddings sidecar, and idempotency contracts cannot be implemented, and the "no silent durable mutation" promise (§3) cannot be enforced.

This epic exists to make every Appendix A table, every core enum, and every typed-ID prefix individually tracked, with schema-drift tests, repository APIs, and golden round-trips.

## Cross-cutting constraints (apply to every child bead under this epic)

- Storage source of truth is FrankenSQLite via SQLModel Rust. No rusqlite, no SQLx, no Diesel, no SeaORM. Validated by the forbidden-deps audit on every commit.
- Migrations are versioned, append-only, idempotent, and ship with up-only DDL. Every schema change adds a new migration; no edits to historical migrations.
- Every table has at least: a repository struct, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE+SELECT methods, a unit test for happy/empty/duplicate paths, and an entry in the schema-drift snapshot tested by EE-SCHEMA-DRIFT-001.
- Every public enum has serde round-trip golden coverage and explicit handling of unknown variants (deny_unknown is the default; document any exception with an ADR comment).
- Every typed ID prefix (e.g., mem_, rule_, sess_, …) is tested for: ULID generation determinism within a clock fixture, prefix uniqueness, and cross-prefix lookup rejection (a mem_ULID must not resolve to a rule_ULID by accident).
- All repository writes go through the existing single-write-owner advisory lock (EE-CONC-001 / EE-209). Reads are concurrent-safe.
- Each bead delivers a unit test, a schema-drift assertion, and (where the table is reachable from the CLI) a real-binary e2e fixture. Logs follow the existing structured-logging contract: command, cwd/workspace, sanitized environment overrides, elapsed_ms, exit_code, stdout/stderr artifact paths, schema validation status, redaction status, first_failure_diagnosis.

## Closure criteria

- All Appendix A tables exist with repositories and migrations.
- All §11.3 enums have golden round-trip tests.
- All 16 typed-ID prefixes from §11.2 are enumerated and tested.
- The schema-drift test (EE-SCHEMA-DRIFT-001) snapshots include every new table.
- No SELECT or INSERT in any module bypasses the repository layer (audited via grep test).
- ee status surfaces the existence of every table and its row count, gated to debug builds or --json --diagnostic to avoid leaking workspace size by default.

## Verification path

- `cargo test --workspace` exercises unit + schema-drift + golden tests.
- `tests/no_mocks_e2e.rs` exercises ee workflow close → action insert → artifact insert end to end against a real DB.
- `ee diag schema --json` (introduced as a child bead) emits the live schema and is asserted against the Appendix A snapshot.
close_reason: All 0 child beads verified closed. Epic complete.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Implemented by SilentMountain. Adds src/models/id.rs with typed time-ordered IDs and 9 domain markers.

API surface:
- trait IdKind { const PREFIX: &str } (zero-sized markers, 'static lifetime)
- struct Id<K: IdKind> { inner: Uuid (v7 internally), _phantom }
- Id::now() / Id::from_uuid(uuid) / Id::into_uuid() / Id::as_uuid()
- impls: Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Display, Debug, FromStr
- ParseIdError { MissingSeparator, WrongPrefix, WrongPayloadLength, InvalidCharacter, PayloadOverflow }
- Domain aliases: MemoryId (mem_), WorkspaceId (wsp_), RuleId (rule_), PackId (pack_), SessionId (sess_), EvidenceId (ev_), AuditId (audit_), CandidateId (cand_), BackupId (bk_)

Format:
- <prefix>_<26-char-Crockford-Base32>
- Crockford alphabet: 0-9 + A-Z minus I,L,O,U
- Lowercase payloads accepted; uppercase emitted on display
- Lexicographic order matches chronological order via UUID v7 timestamp prefix

Determinism:
- Generation uses uuid::Uuid::now_v7 (48-bit ms timestamp + 74-bit random + version/variant bits)
- Equality and hash compare only the inner Uuid; the marker type carries no runtime data
- Re-parsing the Display form round-trips the underlying bytes (test exercises all 256 byte values)

Cargo.toml: added uuid = { version = '1', features = ['v7'] }.

14 unit tests cover round-trip per kind, every error variant (wrong prefix, missing separator, wrong length, invalid character, overflow, lowercase accept), ordering, debug format, hash/equality, encoder/decoder for the full byte range, and uniqueness in a 256-burst.

Verification (rch where compute matters):
- cargo fmt --check: clean
- cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings: clean
- cargo test: 67/67 pass (58 lib + 7 forbidden_deps + 2 smoke)

title: EE-CONC-001: Define and test multi-agent advisory lock and concurrent-writer contract
description:
Define and validate the multi-agent concurrent-writer posture for the EE local store, end-to-end.

Background:
The plan locks the v1 architecture to a single FrankenSQLite file as the durable source of truth and assumes multiple coding agents on the same machine may share that file simultaneously. Multiple agents reading freely is supported, but heavy concurrent writes must be coordinated by a job lock or the optional daemon write owner. The plan calls this out as an explicit project risk: concurrency corruption.

The current bead set has strong database, audit, transaction, status, doctor, command-effect, and e2e coverage, but this bead owns the specific cross-cutting invariant: mutating EE commands must not corrupt durable memory when multiple agents or background jobs try to write at once.

Intended scope:
This bead owns the write-coordination contract for CLI mode without requiring a daemon. It should compose cleanly with the future daemon/steward write owner, but must not become the daemon implementation itself.

Public/internal surface:
- Internal `db::write_lock` or equivalent capability wraps FrankenSQLite write transactions in a process-level advisory lock over an EE-controlled lock path.
- Lock behavior has documented busy timeout, deterministic backoff, cancellation respect through Asupersync context, and stable diagnostics.
- `ee status --json` or related status/check output reports writer posture where safe: lock path class, busy timeout, last contention summary, and degraded posture.
- `ee diag concurrency --json` runs a non-destructive concurrency probe: lock acquire/release timing, read-while-write posture, second-writer low-timeout posture, and schema-valid triage output.
- Mutating commands honor the lock and surface a stable `write_lock_busy` or equivalent degraded/error code with a useful next action.

Why this matters:
Concurrency corruption is one of the fastest ways for an agent memory tool to lose user trust. Without an explicit, tested contract, later features such as steward jobs, MCP adapters, hooks, curation, import, rehearsal, support bundles, and background index refresh can accidentally open a second writer and cause silent state loss.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including comprehensive unit tests, integration tests, real-binary e2e tests, platform notes, and detailed logging requirements.
design:
Recommended design:
- Keep the primitive capability-narrowed and storage-local: one lock helper, one lock path policy, one busy/backoff policy, and one structured diagnostic model consumed by commands.
- Do not rely on FrankenSQLite concurrency alone for multi-agent writes. The advisory process-level lock is the product contract; database busy handling is a secondary safety net.
- Keep reads available where safe. The contract should distinguish read-only commands, derived-artifact writes, durable memory writes, config writes, and background/steward writes using the command-effect manifest.
- Platform behavior must be explicit. If Linux/macOS/Windows locking semantics differ, expose stable degraded/unsupported codes in tests and docs rather than pretending the behavior is identical.
- Use deterministic contention tests with child processes or helper binaries, bounded timeouts, fixed backoff, and artifact logs. Avoid sleep-heavy tests where a lock-step barrier or pipe can make the race deterministic.
- Ensure cancellation and interruption release locks. Tests should cover early return, validation error, transaction rollback, panic-safe/drop behavior where Rust permits, and process death/stale-lock recovery posture.
- Status/diagnostic output should not leak absolute sensitive paths by default; use redacted path classes plus hashes where needed.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance criteria:
- A versioned advisory write-lock contract exists for durable EE writes, including lock path policy, scope, busy timeout, deterministic backoff, cancellation behavior, stale-lock posture, platform support notes, and interaction with the future daemon/steward write owner.
- All implemented durable mutating command paths use the lock helper or explicitly document why they do not need it; read-only and dry-run commands remain non-mutating under the command-effect manifest.
- `ee status --json`, `ee check --json`, or an equivalent posture surface reports lock contention/degraded posture with stable codes and redacted path metadata where safe.
- `ee diag concurrency --json` or an equivalent diagnostic probe exercises read-while-write, second-writer-busy, timeout, stale-lock/dead-owner posture where practical, and returns schema-valid machine data without mutating durable state.
- Contention failures return stable error/degradation codes such as `write_lock_busy`, include retry/backoff/daemon/fix-plan next actions, and never leave partial durable writes.
- The contract composes with steward/daemon jobs, MCP adapters, hooks, rehearsal sandbox, import/index publish, backup/export, and curation flows without forking write semantics.
- Public schemas and golden fixtures cover no writer, active writer, busy timeout, read while writer active, stale/dead owner posture, unsupported platform behavior, cancellation, and redacted lock path reporting.

Testing and logging requirements:
- Add unit tests for lock path derivation, redaction, timeout parsing, deterministic backoff, lock acquisition/release, stale-lock classification, platform capability detection, and error-code mapping.
- Add integration tests with temporary FrankenSQLite/SQLModel databases covering single writer, concurrent writers, reader during writer, failed validation before write, transaction rollback, cancellation, process death/stale lock, and duplicate idempotency keys under contention.
- Add real-binary e2e coverage that spawns isolated `ee` processes in a temporary workspace, holds a writer lock, runs read-only/status/diag commands, attempts a second mutating command with low timeout, validates stable `write_lock_busy` output, and proves durable state remains consistent.
- Add adversarial/property coverage for path traversal in lock path inputs, weird Unicode/control characters in workspace paths, symlinked state directories, huge timeout values, clock skew, corrupted lock metadata, and interrupted lock holder cleanup.
- E2E/logged tests must capture command, cwd/workspace, sanitized environment overrides, process IDs where safe, lock path class/hash, timeout/backoff settings, elapsed time, exit code, stdout/stderr artifact paths, schema/golden validation status, state-before/state-after hashes, observed contention event, and first-failure diagnosis.
- Stdout assertions must prove stdout contains only machine data; contention progress, process coordination traces, skipped platform notes, warnings, and debugging context must go to stderr or explicit artifacts.
- Closeout evidence must include fixture IDs, scenario IDs, manifest hashes, command-effect manifest entries, exact verification commands, platform coverage notes, and proof that this does not implement or require the daemon itself.

title: EE-SCHEMA-DRIFT-001: Add unified schema-drift detection test for DB DDL, JSON contracts, manifests, and JSONL headers
description:
Add a schema-drift detection test that fails CI when DB schema, JSON output contracts, or index manifest format diverge from their declared specifications.

Background:
The OPUS plan §27.7 explicitly names tests/schema_drift.rs as a required gate: "regenerates DDL from #[derive(Model)] and diffs; must pass CI before merging." The bead set has EE-265 (invalid-version tests for JSON contracts), EE-266 (legacy import boundary), EE-267 (index manifest schema and validation), EE-268 (graph snapshot version validation), and EE-TST-003 (golden/schema contract runner). These cover individual contracts at point-of-use, but they do not collectively guarantee that the FULL set of schemas in the build can never silently drift.

A schema-drift test is the single CI gate that reads every declared schema (DB tables, public JSON envelopes, index manifests, jsonl headers, audit log entries, support bundle layout, configuration), regenerates them from source-of-truth definitions, and asserts byte-stability against committed fixtures. A drifted schema is either intentional (and the contributor updates the fixture in the same PR) or accidental (and CI catches it). Without this test, a single innocent attribute reordering can break every downstream consumer overnight.

Intended scope:
This bead owns the unified schema-drift test, the fixture layout under tests/contracts/schemas/, and the CI gate. It does not duplicate the per-feature golden tests; it composes them into a single drift-detection surface.

Public surface (test-only):
- tests/contracts/schema_drift.rs walks the registered schemas, serialises canonical examples for each, and diffs against tests/contracts/schemas/<name>.<version>.json.
- A small CLI helper `cargo xtask schema-drift --update` regenerates fixtures intentionally; it never runs in CI.
- ee schema list --json (already in the bead set as EE-032) is the runtime mirror; the test asserts the runtime listing matches the committed fixtures.

Why this matters:
Schema drift is the single failure mode that hurts every downstream consumer (agents, MCP clients, CI pipelines that parse JSON, future migration tooling). Catching it in a one-line CI assertion costs nothing; missing it costs every consumer a silent break.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including the unified schema registry, drift fixtures, runtime schema-list parity, xtask update helper, negative tests, property tests, CI gate, and e2e logging requirements.
design:
Recommended design:
- Use a single registry pattern: every schema crate exports a SCHEMAS slice ([Schema { name, version, example_factory }]) and the drift test iterates the slice. Adding a new schema means adding one slice entry and one fixture file; nothing more.
- Canonicalise JSON via serde_json::to_string with a stable key sort and consistent number formatting; no third-party canonicalizer is needed for v1.
- DB DDL snapshots come from the SQLModel migration registry. Avoid running the migration runner during the test; use the in-memory DDL emitter instead.
- The test must not require a network or a real cass binary. It must run in CI with no external dependencies.
- The xtask helper is a thin Rust binary in xtasks/ that imports the same registry. It writes fixture files atomically.
- Compose with EE-TST-003 (golden/schema contract runner) by sharing the canonicalization helpers and the fixture path conventions; do not duplicate the diff renderer.
- Compose with EE-TST-001 (testing strategy) by being included in the default `cargo test` set and the CI artifact policy.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance criteria:
- The test source lives at tests/contracts/schema_drift.rs and is wired into the default `cargo test` set; it does not require any feature flag to run.
- The test enumerates every registered schema and asserts byte-stability against a committed fixture under tests/contracts/schemas/<name>.<version>.json. Coverage includes at minimum: DB DDL (all tables), every public JSON envelope (`ee.response.v1`, `ee.error.v1`, `ee.memory.v1`, `ee.search.v1`, `ee.context.v1`, `ee.status.v1`, `ee.why.v1`, `ee.workspace.identity.v1`), the index manifest, the graph snapshot manifest, the support bundle manifest, the jsonl header for memory.jsonl exports, and the audit log entry shape.
- A failing drift produces a readable diff (line-level) plus the exact `cargo xtask schema-drift --update` invocation a contributor must run to regenerate the fixture intentionally.
- `cargo xtask schema-drift --update` regenerates only the fixtures the contributor explicitly names; bare `--update` requires explicit confirmation and writes a one-line audit comment in the PR description template.
- The test asserts that every schema name has a matching version field; a schema without a version, or with a duplicate version, is a hard failure.
- The runtime command `ee schema list --json` is asserted to exactly match the committed fixture set: every runtime schema has a fixture, and every fixture has a runtime schema. No silent drift between the test fixtures and the runtime.

Testing and logging requirements:
- The drift test itself runs in under 200ms on the standard CI runner; budget is enforced with a tracing assertion.
- Negative tests prove that adding a field to any schema without updating the fixture fails CI; reordering fields fails CI; renaming a field fails CI; bumping a version fails CI unless the new fixture is added.
- A property test asserts that for every schema, canonical_json(deserialize(canonical_json(example))) == canonical_json(example) (round-trip byte stability).
- Adversarial: a fixture file that has been hand-edited to be invalid JSON fails the test with a parse error rather than a misleading drift diff; a fixture file that is missing fails with the exact regeneration command.
- E2E logs capture the schema name, fixture path, runtime path, diff summary, and the next-action command. Logs go to stderr; the diff itself goes to a per-schema log artifact.
- Closeout evidence cites the schema list, the fixture directory, and the CI workflow file that wires the test in.
notes: Closes Plan §27.7 named test (tests/schema_drift.rs). Catches a class of regressions (silent JSON contract drift) that single-feature golden tests cannot prevent because they only run when their feature is touched. Composes with EE-TST-003 rather than duplicating it.

title: G1: Personalized PageRank for ee context — query-seeded structural re-ranker
description:
# G1 — Personalized PageRank for `ee context` pack assembly

## Idea (one-liner)

Run topic-sensitive PageRank seeded by the top-k textually-retrieved memories, then re-rank the pack candidate pool by `α · text_score + (1-α) · ppr_score`. Brings *structural relevance* to a surface that today is purely text-based.

## Why this matters

`ee context` is the most-trafficked surface in the project — every agent invocation runs it. Today's pack assembly is MMR + freshness + confidence. The graph snapshot exists (memory_links DiGraph; pagerank_score + betweenness_score precomputed) but only influences a side-band `graph_features` block surfaced for explainability, never the actual ranking.

Personalized PageRank turns the graph into a *first-class re-ranker* that surfaces concept-adjacent memories the text similarity missed (e.g., a rule's source memories, a memory reinforced by the same outcome as a top hit). Mathematical depth is real (random walk with restart; eigenvector convergence) but invisible to the user — they just see better packs.

## Algorithm

Standard topic-sensitive PageRank (a.k.a. personalized PageRank):

```
PPR(v) = (1-α) · personalization(v) + α · Σ_u (PPR(u) · w(u,v) / outweight(u))
```

Where:
- `personalization(v)` = 1/|S| if v ∈ S else 0, where S is the seed set (top-k text retrieval hits).
- `w(u,v)` = edge weight from memory_links (the weighted, typed DiGraph).
- `α` = damping factor, default 0.85.
- Iteration cap: 50 (typical convergence in 20-30 on graphs at this size).

**Implementation via franken_networkx**: `fnx_algorithms::pagerank_directed(graph, alpha=0.85, personalization=Some(seed_map))`. The personalization parameter is the dict {memory_id → weight} for the seed set. Already supported by fnx; no new algorithm work.

## Seeding strategy

The seed set `S` is constructed from the union of:
1. **Top-k vector hits** for the query (default k=10).
2. **Top-k BM25/FTS hits** for the query (default k=10).
3. Deduplicated; the union typically has ≤20 distinct IDs.

Personalization weight per seed = `seed_initial_score / Σ seed_initial_scores` where `seed_initial_score = max(vector_cosine, bm25_normalized)`.

## Combining with the existing score

Final rank score:
```
final_score(v) = α_ppr · ppr_score(v) + (1 - α_ppr) · base_score(v)
```

Where `base_score(v)` is the existing MMR-weighted combination of (text similarity, confidence, freshness). Default `α_ppr = 0.30` — re-ranks meaningfully without overwhelming text relevance. Configurable via `--ppr-weight=<0..1>` on `ee context`.

## Edge-weight handling

The memory_links graph has 7 typed edge relations. Default weight scheme for PPR random walks:
- `supports`: weight 1.0
- `derived_from`: weight 0.8
- `related`: weight 0.6
- `co_tag`: weight 0.4
- `co_mention`: weight 0.3
- `contradicts`: weight 0.0 (treated as not-an-edge for PPR — see G5 for negative-weight handling)
- `supersedes`: weight 0.0 in current direction (the superseded revision shouldn't propagate rank to its replacer)

Multiplied by the `weight` and `confidence` attributes on the edge for additional fidelity. Final edge weight = `relation_weight · stored_weight · stored_confidence`.

## Surface

1. **`ee context <query>` (default)**: PPR runs as part of pack assembly with `α_ppr = 0.30`. No visible API change; packs are simply better.

2. **`ee context <query> --ppr-weight=<0..1>`**: Override the PPR contribution. `0` = pure text relevance (legacy behavior); `1` = pure structural relevance.

3. **`ee context <query> --explain --json`**: In the `selection.scoreBreakdown` block, surface `pprScore`, `textScore`, `combinedScore` per result. Composable with G2's Pack DNA block.

4. **Cache**: PPR results are NOT cached per query (every query has a different seed set). But the underlying graph snapshot IS cached — PPR runs against the cached snapshot, not a fresh build.

## Acceptance

- New module `src/graph/ppr.rs` with `compute_personalized_pagerank(graph, seed_map, alpha, iterations) -> HashMap<MemoryId, f64>`.
- `src/core/context.rs` integration: pack assembly runs PPR when the graph snapshot is fresh; falls back to legacy ranking if snapshot stale/missing (degraded mode).
- `ee context --ppr-weight=N` flag plumbed through clap to context options.
- `ee context --explain` surfaces PPR scores in the per-result breakdown.
- 6 unit tests + 1 e2e + 1 golden test.
- Performance: PPR adds ≤ 30ms p50 on a 1k-memory workspace.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: F1 (memory_links snapshot is already supported, but F1 establishes the typed-subgraph pattern this builds on), F2 (uses run_with_budget + emit_complexity_witness), F4 (must pass determinism harness).
Blocks: G2 (Pack DNA composite depends on PPR scores being computed).
Parent: bd-bife.

## Related code

- `src/graph/mod.rs:compute_pagerank` — existing pattern; PPR is the personalization-vector variant.
- `src/core/context.rs` — pack assembly logic; the integration point.
- `src/output/context.rs` (if extant) — JSON rendering of the explain block.

comments.text:
## Round 3 acceptance-criteria pinning

The original G1.d test count is concrete but the BEHAVIORS aren't. Adding specific cases:

### G1.a unit tests (4 cases, expanded)
1. **Single-seed PPR**: graph = 3-node path A→B→C. Seed = {A: 1.0}. Expected: PPR ranks A > B > C (decay along the path).
2. **Multi-seed weighted**: graph = 4-node star. Seeds = {A: 0.8, B: 0.2}. Expected: PPR(A) > PPR(B) > PPR(C) ≈ PPR(D).
3. **Edge weights matter**: same 3-node path but A→B weight=0.1 vs A→B weight=1.0. Expected: PPR(B) is 10× higher in second case.
4. **Determinism across 3 runs**: same seeds, same graph → byte-identical scores. HashMap iteration order MUST NOT leak into output.

### G1.b integration tests (3 cases, expanded)
1. **PPR fires**: snapshot fresh, memory_links populated, ee context query against seeded corpus. Result: re-ranking visible in JSON output (scores differ vs --ppr-weight=0).
2. **PPR skipped on stale snapshot**: snapshot >300s old. ee context still works, emits degraded.ppr.snapshot_stale. Result identical to --ppr-weight=0.
3. **PPR skipped on empty seed**: query matches 0 memories. PPR not invoked. Empty result is returned cleanly (no error).

### G1.c CLI tests (3 cases)
1. **--ppr-weight=0**: legacy behavior. Byte-identical pre-G1 output (via pre-G1 baseline snapshot from RX2).
2. **--ppr-weight=1**: maximum re-rank. PPR scores dominate (text relevance still matters for seed set selection, but blending heavily favors structural).
3. **--ppr-weight=0.5 vs 0.3**: 0.5 should re-rank more than 0.3 (monotonicity in PPR weight).

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
## ALGORITHM (pinned per bd-3usjw.49)

**Andersen, Chung, Lang 2006** — localized random walks bounded by epsilon-error. `O(1/epsilon * 1/(1-c))` cost for `c`-restart-prob, vs. `O(n)` for global PageRank. For typical pack-size-100 query, 100-1000x faster than global PPR with rank-1 accuracy preserved.

Implementation guidance:

- Replace the standard PPR iteration in `src/graph/ppr.rs` with the ACL local PageRank "push" procedure (residual + estimate vectors per node; push to active frontier when residual exceeds `epsilon * out_degree`).
- Default `epsilon = 1e-3`, restart-prob `c = 0.15`. Both configurable through `[graph.ppr]` keys when graph config keys grow next (see bd-bife.5).
- The existing fnx wrapper (`compute_personalized_pagerank_result_with_policy`) keeps its surface — `PersonalizedPageRankPolicy` gains an `algorithm: PprAlgorithm::AndersenChungLang { epsilon }` variant alongside the existing global path. Determinism contract: same `(graph, seed_weights, epsilon, alpha)` → byte-identical estimate vector (HashMap iteration order MUST NOT leak; sort by node id).
- Witness/CGSE artifact (per bd-igvt F2) records the number of pushes and the final residual `L1` norm so an auditor can see how tight the epsilon was.

## PERFORMANCE TARGET (pinned per bd-3usjw.49)

`ee context <task>` with the PPR re-ranker enabled completes in **p50 < 50ms on the 14k-memory fixture corpus**.

If ACL local PageRank p50 exceeds 50ms on the 14k-memory fixture corpus, do NOT close bd-ov09 as implemented. Revisit `epsilon`, or pin the system back to global PPR and record the measured p50 in `docs/spikes/math_ambition_rejection_log.md`, and open a follow-up bead for the selected redesign (e.g., approximate PPR via FORA, or a smaller default `--ppr-weight`).

## Cross-bead consistency

- bd-ov09.4 (G1.d PPR tests) needs to be extended: the `benches/context_with_ppr.rs` 1k-memory budget (`≤30ms p50`) is the smaller-scale guard; the 14k-memory budget here is the production-scale guard. Add a second bench fixture sized 14k or document the extrapolation.
- bd-3usjw.46 (minhash_rank_centrality) becomes the integer-only fallback when ACL PPR drift exceeds the cross-platform determinism tolerance pinned in bd-3usjw.25.

— StormyCove (pinning recorded via `br comments add --no-auto-flush`; appended as comment rather than description-replacement to preserve every existing bd-ov09 section)

  env ... "cc" "-O3" ... "--target=arm64-apple-macosx" ...

This is an environmental artifact (the `._*` prefixed files are macOS resource forks; they should never be passed to `cc`). The build was routed to a Mac arm64 worker rather than a Linux worker, and the worker had stale tar-extraction debris in its zstd vendor tree. Not a code defect on my side.

title: PPR cache key correctness and cache-hit fast path for context rerank
description:
## IdeaWizard grounding

Phase 1/4 reality check: the existing IdeaWizard backlog already covers broad swarm-scale surfaces (`bd-1prrl`, `bd-ndzfg`, `bd-gni47`, `bd-1zb7k.*`). This bead is deliberately narrow and non-duplicative: it comes from concrete `bd-ov09.4` benchmark evidence and read-only code inspection of the current PPR rerank path.

Phase 2 30->5 / Phase 3 next-10 winnow summary: the most valuable new idea is not another broad cache layer; it is making the existing PPR algorithm-result cache both correct and useful on the `ee context --ppr-weight` hot path. Today the benchmark can run remote-only, but PPR-over-base is hundreds of ms, not <=30ms.

## Problem

Remote Criterion evidence recorded on `bd-ov09.4` comment 2744:

- RCH job 21 on `trj`, `location=remote`, exit 0 for `cargo bench --bench context_with_ppr -- --sample-size 10 --measurement-time 5`.
- `base_1000_memories` mean ~5152.8ms, median ~5046.3ms.
- `ppr_1000_memories` mean ~5908.0ms, median ~6032.7ms.
- PPR overhead: ~755.2ms mean / ~986.4ms median, far above the <=30ms acceptance budget.

Read-only code inspection found two likely performance causes and one correctness bug:

1. `src/core/context.rs::apply_personalized_pagerank_rerank` builds the full memory graph projection before the algorithm-result cache is consulted. Cache hits still pay DB memory-link load + graph construction.
2. `src/graph/ppr.rs::compute_personalized_pagerank_result_cached_with_cx` clones the full `DiGraph` before `run_with_cached_budget` can load a cached result. Cache hits still pay graph clone cost.
3. The cache params include `alpha`, `maxIterations`, `seedCount`, and `tolerance`, but not the actual seed memory IDs or seed weights. Two different queries with the same seed count can collide and reuse the wrong PPR result.

## Scope

Fix the PPR cache key and cache-hit path for context reranking without changing the public `ee context` contract.

Required implementation shape:

- Add canonical seed identity/weight material to the PPR params hash. Use deterministic ordering by memory id and stable float encoding/stringification consistent with existing graph algorithm param hashing.
- Add a focused regression test proving two different seed maps with the same seed count produce different cache keys/results and do not reuse each other.
- Restructure the cached PPR path so the cache can be checked before paying full graph projection or graph clone cost when enough metadata is available. If projection cannot be avoided, at minimum avoid cloning the graph before a cache-hit lookup.
- Preserve current algorithm witness emission on cache misses and preserve deterministic output ordering.
- Do not introduce Tokio, custom graph algorithms outside the existing PPR/FNX path, or non-deterministic cache keys.

## Tests required

- Unit: cache params include canonical seed ids/weights; seed order permutations hash identically; different seed identities with same count hash differently.
- Unit/integration: cached PPR with seed set A followed by seed set B returns distinct results even when both have the same seed count.
- Context integration: `ee context` PPR rerank still emits score breakdown/why text and remains byte-stable for the existing golden fixture.
- Perf: rerun `cargo bench --bench context_with_ppr -- --sample-size 10 --measurement-time 5` through RCH only. Acceptance is <=30ms PPR-over-base p50/median or a documented, reviewed update to the budget if the benchmark is measuring a larger surface than intended.

## Acceptance

- Cache-key collision risk is eliminated and covered by tests.
- Cache-hit path avoids unnecessary graph clone and, where feasible, graph projection before hit lookup.
- `bd-ov09.4` perf evidence can be rerun remote-only and either passes the <=30ms overhead target or produces a precise remaining bottleneck with stage timings.
- No local Cargo verification; all Cargo tests/benchmarks use RCH.

## Coordination note

This bead was created because `src/core/context.rs` and `src/graph/ppr.rs` were actively reserved by QuietLake during StormyCove inspection. It should be claimed by the agent already owning those files, or by a later agent after those reservations clear.

title: [situation] Release keyword precedence causes classification regression
description:

title: [rch] Add project sync hygiene for generated artifacts and retrieval stalls
description:
Background: multiple RCH verification commands have completed the remote Cargo work but then hung while retrieving .rch-target artifacts. This repo also has many generated/untracked files and literal temporary directories that make sync behavior harder to reason about. Agents cannot delete those files without explicit user permission, so the project needs non-destructive sync hygiene and documented handling.

Scope:
- Inventory current RCH behavior using rch diagnose/status where useful and at least one representative cargo check/test command.
- Decide whether a project .rchignore, documented RCH target-dir convention, or RCH configuration update is the right fix. If adding .rchignore, keep it narrow and verify it does not hide source or fixture files needed by remote builds.
- Document the safe process for terminating only stuck local RCH wrapper/rsync processes after the remote command has already reported success.
- Do not delete generated files or directories. If cleanup would help, create a separate explicit-permission bead instead of performing deletion.

Acceptance:
- RCH remote commands no longer sync obvious generated clutter from this repo, or the remaining sync cost is documented with a concrete reason.
- At least one RCH cargo check or focused test proves the sync configuration still sends required source and path dependencies.
- The close reason includes any .rchignore/config changes, before/after sync observations, and residual risks.

title: [perf-forensics][conformance] Verify profile budgets against observed artifacts
description:
## Background

k8dp makes profile budgets explicit, but future regressions can still come from commands advertising one profile while artifacts reflect another or ignoring a profile budget in practice. Perf forensics should catch that mismatch.

## Scope

Add conformance checks that compare profile evidence and runtime reports against normalized performance artifacts. The check should answer whether observed candidate limits, pack budgets, cache/write/steward settings, verification recipe, and support-bundle profile match the active profile and documented overrides.

## Acceptance criteria

- Checks distinguish advertised profile, effective profile, explicit overrides, and observed artifact behavior.
- Mismatch examples include candidate pool too high/low, pack token cap mismatch, cache cap mismatch, write spool batch mismatch, verification recipe mismatch, and missing profile provenance.
- Mismatches produce stable degradation or failure codes with repair hints and owner hints.
- Tests include constrained, portable, workstation, and swarm synthetic summaries.
- The check is read-only and does not rewrite config or budgets.

## Testing and logging

Use the testing-conformance mindset: compare implementation artifacts against the declared profile contract. Add focused unit/contract tests and run them through RCH before closure.
close_reason: 10 conformance tests for ee perf budget check: constrained/portable/workstation/swarm profiles pass, mismatch detected, error handling for missing report and empty profile, read-only effect, metric count in summary, clean JSON stdout. Fixtures: constrained_profile.json, portable_profile.json, swarm_profile.json

title: [sqlite] Add contention retry for file-backed read queries
description:
Finding from deadlock-finder-and-fixer audit.

Evidence:
- src/db/mod.rs:767-781 configures file-backed read/write connections with PRAGMA busy_timeout = 0.
- src/db/mod.rs:754-758 sends all query_for() reads straight to FrankenConnection::query_sync() with no retry wrapper.
- Read-heavy command paths open the same file DB and issue queries during swarm work, e.g. src/core/context.rs:389-423 and src/core/status.rs:533.

Reproduction conditions:
- File-backed .ee/ee.db.
- Hold a writer open with BEGIN EXCLUSIVE or any long with_transaction() path.
- In another process run ee status --json, ee context "..." --json, or another read path that uses query_for(). With busy_timeout set to zero and no read retry, transient SQLite contention can surface directly to the CLI.

Fix target:
- Add bounded retry/backoff around file-backed query_for() for transient SQLite lock errors, or use a nonzero busy_timeout plus outer retry for reads.
- Keep deterministic error shape when retries exhaust.
- Add a regression that holds a writer and proves read commands wait or report a structured retry-exhausted error rather than raw lock contention.
close_reason: File-backed database reads retry transient SQLite contention with bounded backoff and preserve query operation context

title: [implements-surface:learn] Real ee learn agenda/uncertainty/summary/propose pipeline
description:
## Background
Stub: `LEARN_UNAVAILABLE_CODE = "learning_records_unavailable"` at src/cli/mod.rs:7725. Honesty closure: eidetic_engine_cli-evah ("refactored to abstain with experiment_registry_unavailable"). README pillar "Procedural rules with decay" + plan §17. The pipeline that turns repeated experience into procedural rules — central to the entire Eidetic Engine thesis.

## What ships
1. Observation ledger: `learning_observations` table + writer triggered by `ee outcome`, CASS import, and curate apply.
2. Agenda: `ee learn agenda --json` clusters episodic memories by topic+outcome (using tag co-occurrence + semantic similarity), returns ranked open questions with sample IDs.
3. Uncertainty: `ee learn uncertainty --json` computes entropy over rule-confidence distributions per cluster, surfaces clusters with high spread.
4. Summary: `ee learn summary --since <rfc3339> --json` aggregates observation counts, candidate counts, applied-rule counts, harmful-feedback counts.
5. Proposer: `ee learn propose --json` generates Candidate rows with provenance and routes them to ee curate candidates.

## Acceptance
- After 50 episodic memories with outcomes (test fixture), `learn propose` returns ≥1 candidate per non-trivial cluster, each with ≥2 evidence pointers.
- Determinism: same observation set → same proposed-candidate IDs.
- LEARN_UNAVAILABLE_CODE deleted in same PR.
- Unit + integration + golden tests cover empty ledger, single-observation cluster, contradictory observations, large cluster.
- ADR added covering clustering algorithm choice + uncertainty metric.
- Closure linter passes.

title: EE-202: Implement job budget model
description:
Source plan item: EE-202 from the `Steward` backlog.

Task: Implement job budget model

Background and intent:
Provide explicit maintenance jobs, budgets, cancellation, daemon mode, and job diagnostics while preserving deterministic CLI behavior when no daemon is running.

Why this matters:
This bead contributes to the overarching goal of making `ee` a dependable local memory substrate for coding agents: useful before work, auditable after work, and safe under degraded conditions. The work should be implemented in the smallest coherent slice that fully satisfies the public contract implied by the title.

Dependency context:
Original plan dependencies: EE-201. These are also represented as br dependency edges where the referenced bead exists.

Non-negotiable constraints:
Global implementation invariants for this task:
- Keep the CLI local-first, deterministic, and agent-native; stdout is data, stderr is diagnostics.
- Preserve the no-Tokio and no-rusqlite constraint unless a later ADR explicitly changes the architecture.
- Use SQLModel Rust plus FrankenSQLite for durable data; do not introduce a second storage stack.
- Use Asupersync for async edges and cancellation/budget behavior; do not smuggle in a Tokio executor.
- Keep JSON as the canonical public contract. TOON, Markdown, diagrams, and MCP are renderers or adapters over the same domain data.
- Mutating commands need dry-run/idempotency/audit behavior unless the task explicitly says otherwise.
- Add focused tests proportional to risk: unit tests for domain logic, contract/golden tests for public output, and integration/evaluation tests for cross-subsystem behavior.

title: G3: Causal explanation — transitive closure + min-cost flow on causal_evidence
description:
# G3 — Causal explanation: transitive closure + min-cost flow on causal_evidence

## Idea (one-liner)

Today causal_evidence is a flat lookup table. Treat it as a weighted DAG and use it to answer "why did this fail?" with structural attribution — full transitive ancestry (every direct and indirect cause) and a minimum-cost explanation (the lowest-total-contribution-cost set of edges that fully explains the failure).

## Why this matters

`ee why <failure_id>` today returns scores, sources, evidence spans. None of that captures *causal structure*. The `causal_evidence` table has been graph-shaped data masquerading as a flat lookup since it landed: each row is a directed weighted edge `failure_id → candidate_cause_id` with `contribution_score` and `method` ∈ {manual, graph-inferred, cass-derived}.

The product question: "this failure happened — what's the *complete* causal explanation, not just the top-1 direct cause?" Two views:

1. **Transitive ancestry**: walk the DAG backwards from the failure. Every direct cause + every cause of those causes + ... = the complete blame surface.
2. **Min-cost explanation**: among all paths from failure-root to ancestral causes, which set of edges with minimum total contribution-cost fully covers the explanation?

These are *complementary*: ancestry gives breadth (every implicated memory), min-cost gives depth (the most parsimonious explanation). Together they replace "single top score" with a structural attribution.

## Algorithms

1. **Transitive closure on causal_evidence subgraph**: `fnx_algorithms::transitive_closure(causal_dag)` — produces the implicit edge from every memory to every ancestor. For a failure with N direct causes, returns the full N-hop+ ancestral surface.

2. **Min-cost flow**: `fnx_algorithms::min_cost_flow(causal_dag, source=failure_id, sink=virtual_root, demand=1.0, cost=1.0 - contribution_score)`. The lowest-cost path from the failure to all reachable roots, with the cost function inverted (high contribution_score → low cost), so the min-cost path picks the highest-confidence explanation.

3. **Betweenness on causal_evidence DAG**: identifies "causal bottlenecks" — failures whose memory_id sits on the most cause-effect chains. Surface this in `ee insights` (F3).

## Output shape

`ee why <failure_id> --json --causal-explain`:

```jsonc
"causalExplanation": {
  "schema": "ee.why.causal.v1",
  "failureId": "mem_failure_xyz",
  "transitiveAncestry": {
    "totalAncestors": 12,
    "byDepth": {
      "1": ["mem_a", "mem_b"],
      "2": ["mem_c"],
      "3": ["mem_d", "mem_e"]
    },
    "ancestorDetails": [{ "memoryId": "mem_a", "contributionScore": 0.85, "method": "cass-derived", "depth": 1 }, ...]
  },
  "minCostExplanation": {
    "totalCost": 0.42,
    "pathEdges": [
      { "src": "mem_failure_xyz", "dst": "mem_a", "contributionScore": 0.85, "cost": 0.15 },
      { "src": "mem_a", "dst": "mem_c", "contributionScore": 0.91, "cost": 0.09 },
      ...
    ],
    "coveredAncestors": 5,
    "uncoveredAncestors": 7
  },
  "causalBottleneck": false,
  "degraded": []
}
```

## Surface

- `ee why <id> --causal-explain --json`: full causal block added to the response envelope.
- `ee insights --section causalBottlenecks`: top-K failures ranked by betweenness in the causal DAG. Surfaces structural choke points.

## Performance

- Transitive closure on causal_evidence (typically much smaller than memory_links — failures are sparse): <50ms on workspaces with <1k failures.
- Min-cost flow: O(V·E·log V) with capacity scaling; <150ms on the same scale.

## Acceptance

- New module `src/graph/causal.rs` with `compute_causal_ancestry(graph, failure_id) -> CausalAncestry` and `compute_min_cost_explanation(graph, failure_id) -> MinCostExplanation`.
- `ee why --causal-explain` flag plumbed.
- New `ee.why.causal.v1` schema documented.
- 6 unit tests, 1 e2e test, 1 golden snapshot.
- Determinism: 3 runs identical.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: F1 (CausalEvidence subgraph must be built), F2 (algorithm wrappers), F4 (determinism).
Blocks: nothing downstream within this epic.
Parent: bd-bife.

## Related code

- `src/db/mod.rs:causal_evidence` schema.
- `src/cli/why.rs` (or wherever `ee why --json` renders) — extension point.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by existing causal graph surface: src/graph/causal.rs, ee why --causal-explain, insights causalBottlenecks, causal schema/snapshots, graph smoke tests, and determinism coverage are all present. Closing parent after tracker audit; no source changes in this closeout.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
## Phase 6 refinement notes — causal cycle handling

causal_evidence is a directed weighted graph but NOT guaranteed acyclic — a cycle (A causes B; later evidence: B causes A via a different method) is possible.

1. **Pre-flight cycle check**: G3.a must call find_cycle() on the CausalEvidence subgraph BEFORE transitive_closure. If cycles detected: emit degraded.causal_cycle (severity=warn) per RX6, list the cycle members, and fall back to the largest acyclic SCC condensation for transitive_closure.
2. **min_cost_flow on cyclic graphs**: not well-defined. If cycles present, skip min-cost flow and surface only the transitive ancestry. Emit degraded.causal_cycle blocks min_cost_flow.
3. **Cycle resolution UI**: ee insights --section causalCycles surfaces detected cycles for human curation.

Update G3.a + G3.b accordingly.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
## Round 3 acceptance pinning

### G3.a unit tests (6 cases, expanded)
1. **Empty causal graph**: no causal_evidence rows. compute_causal_ancestry returns empty Vec. emit degraded.no_causal_evidence.
2. **Single direct cause**: A failed because of B (one row). Result: transitiveAncestry.byDepth = {1: [B]}, totalAncestors=1.
3. **Multi-hop ancestry**: A→B, B→C, C→D. transitiveAncestry on A: byDepth = {1:[B], 2:[C], 3:[D]}, total=3.
4. **Diamond ancestry**: A→B, A→C, B→D, C→D. ancestry of A: byDepth = {1:[B,C], 2:[D]}, total=3 (D not duplicated).
5. **Cycle detection** (per Round 2 comment): A→B, B→A. Pre-flight find_cycle catches; emit degraded.causal_cycle. Fall back to SCC condensation: condense {A,B}, return 'this is a cycle' as a single node.
6. **Min-cost flow path**: 3-cause network with varying contribution_scores. Verify min-cost path picks the HIGHEST-confidence sequence (cost inverted from score).

### G3.b CLI tests (3 cases)
1. ee why <failure> --causal-explain --json: emits causalExplanation block.
2. ee why <non-failure> --causal-explain: emits causalExplanation = {schema, failureId, transitiveAncestry: null, minCostExplanation: null, degraded: [code: graph.causal.target_not_failure]}.
3. ee insights --section causalBottlenecks: top-K failures with high causal-betweenness.

title: EE-392: Generate tripwires from high-utility memories, regret ledger entries, claims, dependency contracts, and counterfactual candidates
description:
Source plan item: EE-392 from the `Prospective Memory Preflight And Tripwires` backlog.

Task: Generate tripwires from high-utility memories, regret ledger entries, claims, dependency contracts, and counterfactual candidates

Background and intent:
Surface task-specific risks before work starts so memory changes agent behavior at the moment of risk rather than only after a mistake.

Why this matters:
This bead contributes to the overarching goal of making `ee` a dependable local memory substrate for coding agents: useful before work, auditable after work, and safe under degraded conditions. The work should be implemented in the smallest coherent slice that fully satisfies the public contract implied by the title.

Dependency context:
Original plan dependencies: EE-340, EE-383, EE-390. These are also represented as br dependency edges where the referenced bead exists.

Non-negotiable constraints:
Global implementation invariants for this task:
- Keep the CLI local-first, deterministic, and agent-native; stdout is data, stderr is diagnostics.
- Preserve the no-Tokio and no-rusqlite constraint unless a later ADR explicitly changes the architecture.
- Use SQLModel Rust plus FrankenSQLite for durable data; do not introduce a second storage stack.
- Use Asupersync for async edges and cancellation/budget behavior; do not smuggle in a Tokio executor.
- Keep JSON as the canonical public contract. TOON, Markdown, diagrams, and MCP are renderers or adapters over the same domain data.
- Mutating commands need dry-run/idempotency/audit behavior unless the task explicitly says otherwise.
- Add focused tests proportional to risk: unit tests for domain logic, contract/golden tests for public output, and integration/evaluation tests for cross-subsystem behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including the comprehensive testing and logging requirements.
design:
Suggested design approach:
- Keep scope narrow but complete: implement the named behavior, wire it into the relevant command/schema/test surfaces, and avoid unrelated refactors.

Implementation guidance:
- Read the surrounding modules and existing project conventions before editing.
- Prefer the planned crate boundaries from the comprehensive plan: CLI wiring in `ee-cli`, reusable domain/services in `ee-core`, models in `ee-models`, persistence in `ee-db`, output rendering in `ee-output`, and adapters in their own optional crates.
- Keep public contracts stable and versioned. Any data structure that leaves the process through CLI/MCP/hook/export should have a schema and at least one golden fixture.
- If a dependency or upstream Franken project is not ready, implement the smallest honest diagnostic/degraded path rather than faking behavior.
- Document any architectural exception with an ADR-oriented note and a verification hook.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance criteria:
- The behavior described by `Generate tripwires from high-utility memories, regret ledger entries, claims, dependency contracts, and counterfactual candidates` is implemented or, for spikes, conclusively reported with a clear go/no-go recommendation.
- The implementation preserves local-first, no-Tokio, no-rusqlite, agent-native CLI behavior.
- Public command output, if any, validates against the stable response envelope and does not pollute stdout with diagnostics.
- Relevant unit, integration, golden, contract, or evaluation tests are added and named so future agents can find them.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the relevant test subset pass after implementation.
- Any degraded or unavailable dependency state returns a stable error/degradation code with a useful next action.
- No silent durable mutation is introduced; write paths have explicit audit, dry-run, idempotency, or curation behavior as appropriate.

Testing and logging requirements:
- Add or update unit tests for core logic introduced or changed by this bead, covering happy path, boundary/empty inputs, invalid inputs, degraded dependencies, deterministic ordering, and idempotency/mutation rules as applicable.
- If the behavior is visible through the CLI, MCP, hook, export, renderer, or evaluation output, add or extend a real-binary e2e, golden, schema, contract, replay, or evaluation fixture that exercises the public surface in an isolated local workspace.
- E2E/logged tests must capture command, cwd/workspace, sanitized environment overrides, elapsed time, exit code, stdout/stderr artifact paths, schema/golden validation status, redaction status, and a concise first-failure diagnosis.
- Stdout assertions must prove stdout contains only machine data; diagnostics, progress, and debugging context must go to stderr or explicit artifacts.
- If no executable test is appropriate for this bead, the close reason or a br comment must explain why and identify the nearest bead that provides coverage.

title: [output] Replace remaining renderer serialization defaults with explicit errors
description:
## Background
The earlier `kr0m` bead fixed one output serialization path, but the read-only overlap scan still found production renderers such as support-bundle JSON/inspect JSON and hook installer report JSON using `serde_json::to_string(...).unwrap_or_default()`. Even if serde failures are rare, machine-facing output must not turn a serialization failure into an empty data payload.

## What to do
- Re-scan `src/output/mod.rs`, `src/hooks/installer.rs`, and neighboring renderer modules for `serde_json::to_string(...).unwrap_or_default()` and equivalent empty JSON fallbacks.
- Route failures through existing response/error envelope helpers where command handlers can return an error; where an API currently returns `String`, introduce a small local helper that emits a stable `ee.error.v1` serialization failure instead of empty data.
- Preserve public schemas for successful output. Do not change JSON field names or ordering unless a golden explicitly updates an intentional contract.
- Add tests that force a serialization failure where practical, or assert the helper behavior directly with a failing serializer fixture.

## Acceptance
- Remaining machine-facing renderers do not silently emit empty strings or empty data on serialization failure.
- Tests cover success output shape and failure output shape.
- Existing TOON/Markdown renderers still compose from the same JSON contracts.
- Verification includes focused renderer tests, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `ubs` on changed output/hook files.

title: MEDIUM: TOON renderers emit ad-hoc pipe strings instead of stable TOON projections
description:
Reviewer finding focused on TOON output paths.

Locations:
- src/cli/mod.rs:11005-11013: `ee search --format toon` returns `SEARCH|<query>|<count>|<elapsed>ms` instead of a TOON projection of the JSON contract.
- src/cli/mod.rs:11264-11271: `ee why --format toon` returns `WHY|<memory>|<found>|<score>` and drops storage/retrieval/selection provenance fields.
- src/output/mod.rs:8552-8560, 8611-8622, 8687-8694: handoff TOON renderers use `HANDOFF_*|...` pipe summaries instead of `render_toon_from_json`, unlike many other renderers in src/output.

Why this is a bug:
TOON is a machine-facing renderer. These paths do not preserve stable field names, schema, provenance, degradation details, or JSON/TOON parity. Existing tests mostly assert that output exists, not that TOON is structurally aligned with the JSON contract or that progress/summary text cannot leak into machine output.

Acceptance criteria:
- Replace ad-hoc pipe summaries with TOON generated from the corresponding JSON contract, or document and schema-test a real TOON contract with stable field names.
- Add tests for search, why, and handoff TOON outputs proving schema/field parity with JSON and no human progress/summary text in stdout.
- Keep human/Markdown output separate from TOON/stdout machine output.
close_reason: Fixed in 21d55a3: search, why, and handoff TOON outputs now project stable JSON contracts through render_toon_from_json, with parity tests covering the machine-output contracts.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Plan §12.1 step 8: 'Optionally auto-link to recent memories in the same workflow (Hebbian, weight 0.5, source = AUTO).' Plan §12.2 promotion SQL filters WHERE workflow_id = ?.

Current src/cli/mod.rs:12017-12032 handle_remember calls remember_memory with workspace_path, content, level, kind, tags, confidence, source, valid_from, valid_to, dry_run — no workflow_id. 1. Add --workflow <id> to RememberArgs (default None; when omitted, persist NULL workflow_id)
2. Thread the value through RememberMemoryOptions into the memories.workflow_id column
3. ee memory show + ee why must surface the workflow_id field
4. Extend the existing remember e2e tests to cover --workflow set + --level working, and assert workflow_id is persisted via memory show --json
This bead is a pure plumbing bead — necessary for 18ei and 8a9m to be testable end-to-end.

title: [implements-surface:daemon] Real ee daemon with maintenance handlers and supervised job loop
description:

title: F1: Multi-graph snapshot framework — typed subgraphs (causal, revision, rules, contradictions)
description:
# F1 — Multi-graph snapshot framework

## Why this is foundational

Today `src/graph/mod.rs` (~6300 LOC) implements exactly **one** snapshot type: `MemoryLinks`. It is stored in `graph_snapshots` with `workspace_id`, `snapshot_version`, `graph_type` (= "MemoryLinks"), `status`, content_hash, timestamps. All graph-derived features (pagerank_score, betweenness_score) flow through that single snapshot.

The 10 features in this epic require **four additional graph substrates**:

1. **CausalEvidence** — directed weighted graph: nodes = memory IDs (failures + candidate causes); edges = causal_evidence rows; weight = `contribution_score`. Needed by G3 (causal explanation: transitive closure + min-cost flow).

2. **RevisionDAG** — directed acyclic graph: nodes = memory IDs grouped by `logical_id`; edges = parent-revision pointers (each revision's `valid_from` superseding the prior `valid_to`). Cross-chain edges via `derived_from` memory_link relation. Needed by G7 (dominance frontiers + immediate dominators).

3. **RuleProvenance** — bipartite graph: left nodes = procedural_rule IDs, right nodes = memory IDs (source memories per rule). Needed by G9 (bipartite eigenvector centrality).

4. **ContradictionSubgraph** — directed subgraph of memory_links filtered to `relation = 'contradicts'`. Used by G4 (community detection on contradiction clusters) and G5 (PageRank with negative-weighted contradicts edges).

## What

Extend the snapshot framework to support these typed sub-graphs with the same guarantees as MemoryLinks:

1. **Schema**: Add new `GraphType` enum variants in `src/graph/mod.rs` and the corresponding column-level `graph_type` value in `graph_snapshots`. No new tables — same `graph_snapshots` row, different graph_type.

2. **Builders**: One new `build_*_graph_from_*` function per subgraph (mirroring existing `build_memory_graph_from_links`):
   - `build_causal_evidence_graph_from_table(conn, workspace_id) -> Result<DiGraph, GraphError>`
   - `build_revision_dag_from_logical_ids(conn, workspace_id) -> Result<DiGraph, GraphError>` (handles per-logical_id chains + cross-chain `derived_from` edges)
   - `build_rule_provenance_bipartite_from_tables(conn, workspace_id) -> Result<Graph, GraphError>` (undirected bipartite)
   - `build_contradiction_subgraph_from_memory_links(conn, workspace_id) -> Result<DiGraph, GraphError>` (filtered view of memory_links)

3. **Snapshot lifecycle**: Each builder gets its own deterministic content-hash, same as memory_links. Snapshot refresh respects existing advisory-lock (300s TTL) to prevent concurrent refresh conflicts. Each new graph_type gets its own status flag (Valid/Stale/Invalid/Archived).

4. **Refresh policy**: Default refresh cadence per graph_type. memory_links stays as-is (existing). CausalEvidence + RevisionDAG refresh on write (causal_evidence INSERT, memory edit). RuleProvenance + ContradictionSubgraph refresh nightly + on-demand.

5. **CLI surface**: Extend `ee graph snapshot refresh [--graph=memory_links|causal|revision|rules|contradictions|all]` to allow targeted or full refreshes. Existing `--graph=memory_links` semantics preserved (default if unspecified).

## How (key implementation choices)

- **fnx_classes types**: DiGraph for everything except RuleProvenance (which is Graph — undirected bipartite). All preserve AttrMap node/edge attributes.
- **Edge attributes**: For each graph_type, document which attributes attach to nodes/edges. CausalEvidence edges carry: `contribution_score: f64`, `method: String` (manual|graph-inferred|cass-derived), `evidence_count: u32`. RevisionDAG edges carry: `transition_kind: String` (supersedes|derived_from). RuleProvenance edges carry: `rule_role: String` (source|reference).
- **Content hash**: Same blake3 scheme as memory_links — over (sorted nodes + sorted edges + edge_attrs). Different `graph_type` tag in the hash input prevents collisions.
- **Lazy build**: Don't build all 4 new graphs on every snapshot refresh. Build on first request OR on background refresh; mark Stale on writes to the underlying tables.

## Tests

- Unit test per builder: builds against an in-process fixture, checks node count, edge count, attribute correctness.
- Determinism test: same input → byte-identical content_hash across 3 builds.
- E2E test: `ee graph snapshot refresh --graph=causal` followed by inspection of the snapshot row.

## Acceptance

- 4 new `build_*` functions land in `src/graph/mod.rs`.
- `GraphType` enum has variants: MemoryLinks (existing), CausalEvidence, RevisionDAG, RuleProvenance, ContradictionSubgraph.
- `ee graph snapshot refresh --graph=<type>` works for every variant.
- Content hashes are stable across 3 refreshes against unchanged inputs.
- 5 unit tests + 1 E2E test pass.
- No regression in existing memory_links snapshot behavior.

## Dependencies

Blocks: G1, G2, G3, G4, G5, G6, G7, G8, G9, G10 (every feature uses one or more of these new graphs).
Parent: bd-bife (the epic).

## Related code

- `src/graph/mod.rs:build_memory_graph_from_links` — pattern to mirror
- `src/db/mod.rs` — `causal_evidence` schema, `memories.logical_id`, `rule_source_memories`
- ADR 0008 (Graph metrics as derived state)

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
## Phase 6 refinement notes (round 2)

1. **Snapshot lifecycle**: see bd-bife.7 for the eviction + memory-footprint + refresh-cadence policy. F1 implementation MUST emit graph_type-scoped advisory locks (one per type), NOT a single global lock, so different subgraphs can refresh concurrently.

2. **Bipartite type-tagging**: RuleProvenance is the only Graph (undirected) subgraph; the rest are DiGraph. Bipartite means nodes are tagged left=rule|right=memory in AttrMap. Algorithms that iterate edges must respect the tag (don't compute memory-to-memory or rule-to-rule edges).

3. **Disconnected graphs**: Several algorithms (Gomory-Hu, articulation_points) treat each connected component independently. The snapshot framework must expose 'is_connected' as a cached property so wrappers can choose per-component vs whole-graph paths.

4. **Memory limit**: For workspaces with >10k memories, the full DiGraph in fnx-classes can exceed 200MB resident. F1 should expose a max_memory_bytes config (default 250MB) and fall back to 'degraded.large_graph_uncached' for the snapshot, with the actual algorithm calls operating on a lazily-rebuilt window of the graph.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
## Round 3 acceptance pinning — concrete schema decisions

### graph_snapshots table extension (no DDL change, just enum value additions)
Existing schema:
- workspace_id (FK)
- snapshot_version (int, monotonic per graph_type)
- graph_type (string) — extend allowed values: 'MemoryLinks' (existing), 'CausalEvidence', 'RevisionDAG', 'RuleProvenance', 'ContradictionSubgraph'.
- status (enum) — extend: include 'Building' as transient state.
- content_hash (hex)
- metrics_json (TEXT) — per-graph-type metrics (PageRank/betweenness for MemoryLinks; transitive_closure summary for CausalEvidence; etc.).
- node_count, edge_count
- created_at, updated_at
- worker_id (advisory lock holder)
- worker_expires_at (lock TTL = 300s)

### New table: graph_advisory_locks (one row per active lock)
- workspace_id (FK)
- graph_type (string, indexed)
- worker_id (uuid)
- acquired_at, expires_at
- PRIMARY KEY (workspace_id, graph_type) — ensures one active lock per type.

### F1.e CLI acceptance (per refinement comment)
- ee graph snapshot refresh --graph=<type> — single-type refresh.
- ee graph snapshot refresh --graph=all — fan out to every type in deterministic order.
- ee graph snapshot status --json — emit snapshot metadata for every graph_type.
- Locking: ee graph snapshot refresh acquires the lock for that graph_type before building; releases on completion or expiry. Concurrent ee graph snapshot refresh of the SAME type fail-fast with degraded.locked + worker_id of holder.
