title: F1.adr: ADR — Multi-graph snapshot framework (typed subgraphs over fnx_classes)
description:
Write docs/adr/00XX-multi-graph-snapshot-framework.md.

## Decision
Memory-substrate metadata is partitioned into 5 typed sub-graphs (MemoryLinks, CausalEvidence, RevisionDAG, RuleProvenance, ContradictionSubgraph), each with its own deterministic content-hash and refresh cadence. ADR 0008 (Graph metrics as derived state) remains load-bearing: every subgraph is rebuildable from authoritative tables.

## Why this needs an ADR
This is a non-trivial extension of the existing single-graph model. Future contributors will ask 'why didn't you reuse memory_links with a tag for typed edges?' — answer: typed edges have heterogeneous attribute schemas (causal contribution_score vs revision transition_kind vs bipartite rule_role) that don't generalize cleanly.

## Rejected alternatives
1. **Single combined graph with typed edges**: breaks attribute homogeneity, complicates determinism witnessing.
2. **One subgraph per relation type within memory_links**: would mean 7 subgraphs vs 5 — bloats refresh cadence with low-value splits.
3. **No subgraph framework, build on demand per query**: violates ADR 0008's 'derived but cached' principle and turns every ee insights call into an O(N) graph build.

## Sections
- Context (substrate audit)
- Decision (5 subgraph types, refresh cadence per type)
- Consequences (graph_algorithm_witnesses table, content_hash with type tag)
- Rejected alternatives (with rationale)
- Verification (5 tests in tests/contracts/multi_graph_snapshots.rs)

Parent: bd-rnfh. Blocked by: F1.a-F1.e (must understand the implementation first).
Acceptance: ADR lands, sections present, validated by docs/adr/README.md listing.

## Background

The user explicitly requested comprehensive unit tests and e2e scripts with detailed logging, because this migration changes trust boundaries. description:

Task: Implement JSON-to-TOON rendering from canonical `serde_json::Value` envelopes

Background and intent:
Add optional TOON rendering as a token-saving output format while keeping JSON canonical for tests, schemas, hooks, MCP, audit, and storage. TOON must never become hidden state.

Why this matters:
This bead contributes to the overarching goal of making `ee` a dependable local memory substrate for coding agents: useful before work, auditable after work, and safe under degraded conditions. The work should be implemented in the smallest coherent slice that fully satisfies the public contract implied by the title.

Dependency context:
Original plan dependencies: EE-017, EE-331. These are also represented as br dependency edges where the referenced bead exists.

Non-negotiable constraints:
Global implementation invariants for this task:
- Keep the CLI local-first, deterministic, and agent-native; stdout is data, stderr is diagnostics.
- Preserve the no-Tokio and no-rusqlite constraint unless a later ADR explicitly changes the architecture.
- Use SQLModel Rust plus FrankenSQLite for durable data; do not introduce a second storage stack.
- Use Asupersync for async edges and cancellation/budget behavior; do not smuggle in a Tokio executor.
- Keep JSON as the canonical public contract. TOON, Markdown, diagrams, and MCP are renderers or adapters over the same domain data.
- Mutating commands need dry-run/idempotency/audit behavior unless the task explicitly says otherwise.
- Add focused tests proportional to risk: unit tests for domain logic, contract/golden tests for public output, and integration/evaluation tests for cross-subsystem behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Plan §12.5 says: 'Inverts rules with harmful_count >= 2 AND trust_score < 0.3 to anti-patterns'. Plan §18.3 (trauma guard) is the rationale.

Searched src/: no fn invert_rule, no to_anti_pattern, no harmful_count check. `AntiPattern` exists only as a MemoryKind enum variant (src/models/memory.rs:116). No transition logic ever flips a procedural_rule into an anti-pattern.

Concrete impact: when an agent reports a harmful outcome (`ee outcome <id> --harmful` writes feedback_events), the procedural rule's harmful_count grows but nothing converts the rule into an anti-pattern. Bad rules keep ranking until manually retired. North Star Scenario 5 (catastrophic mistake avoidance) leans on the trauma guard pinning prior incidents as anti-patterns; without inversion, the rule cited in the pack is the *unmodified original*.

Fix scope:
1. Add fn evaluate_trauma_guard(conn, rule_id) -> InversionDecision
2. ee maintenance (separate bead 9o18) drives the pass: SELECT rules WHERE harmful_count >= 2 AND trust_score < 0.3, call evaluate_trauma_guard, on Invert: UPDATE rules SET state='retired', kind='anti-pattern', invert_origin_id=<original> + INSERT new memory rows pointing to the original
3. Add an audit_log entry per inversion for traceability
4. Pin behavior: e2e test that two harmful outcomes plus low trust flips a rule, and that subsequent ee context renders the anti-pattern not the original

title: Wire graph_memory_budget admission checks into F1 builders + F2 algorithm wrappers (bd-bife.24 follow-up to commit c3bf406)
description:
Pure admission helpers for bd-bife.24 landed in commit `c3bf406` "feat(graph): bd-bife.24 add graph_memory_budget admission helpers" — `src/core/graph_memory_budget.rs` exposes `MemoryBudgetPolicy`, `estimate_snapshot_bytes`, and three admission-decision functions returning deterministic refusal payloads.

This child captures the remaining call-site wiring.

## Files to touch

- `src/graph/mod.rs` / `src/steward/` snapshot builders (F1.b/c/d):
  - Before building: call `estimate_snapshot_bytes(node_count, edge_count)` then `check_snapshot_admission(estimate, &policy)`. On `Refuse`, write `snapshot.status = Skipped`, push the refusal into the response's `degraded[]`, and emit a `graph_audit::build_snapshot_archived_payload` row.
  - During build: poll `fnx_runtime` allocator stats periodically, call `check_in_build_growth(pre_build_estimate, observed_bytes, &policy)`. On `Abort`, roll back and surface the refusal.
- `src/graph/algorithms.rs` / `src/graph/{pack_dna,bipartite_provenance,minhash_rank,ppr,...}.rs` algorithm wrappers (F2):
  - Before invoking each algorithm: call `check_algorithm_admission(active_resident_bytes, requested_working_set, &policy)`. On `Refuse`, return without allocating + push the refusal to `degraded[]`.
  - `active_resident_bytes` should come from a process-local counter the snapshot builder increments/decrements.
- `src/config/file.rs` + `src/config/merge.rs` + `src/config/env_registry.rs`:
  - Add `[graph.memory]` config section with `snapshot_cap_mb` (default 250), `per_algorithm_cap_mb` (default 100), `degraded_below_pct` (default 80), `growth_multiplier_basis_points` (default 15000).
  - Register `EE_GRAPH_MEMORY_SNAPSHOT_CAP_MB`, `EE_GRAPH_MEMORY_PER_ALGORITHM_CAP_MB`, `EE_GRAPH_MEMORY_DEGRADED_BELOW_PCT`.
- `docs/architecture/graph-memory-budget.md` (NEW): document the cap policy, the four refusal codes, the operator remediation actions per code, and the advisory `snapshot_approaching_cap` flag.
- `docs/configuration/graph.md`: cross-link to the new memory-budget doc.

## Tests

- `tests/graph_memory_budget.rs` (NEW): synthetic large fixture exercises each path:
  - 100k-memory dense fixture triggers `large_graph_uncached` and `snapshot.status = Skipped` without an OOM.
  - In-build growth past 1.5x triggers `unexpected_growth` and a roll-back.
  - Algorithm working-set past per-algorithm cap triggers `algorithm_memory_cap`.
  - Combined snapshot pressure triggers `memory_pressure`.
- Renderer parity matrix entry for the new degraded codes.

## Cross-refs

- Algorithm core: commit `c3bf406`
- Helpers: `src/core/graph_memory_budget.rs::{estimate_snapshot_bytes, check_snapshot_admission, check_in_build_growth, check_algorithm_admission}`
- Refusal envelope: `MemoryBudgetRefusal { code, severity, message, repair, observed_bytes, limit_bytes }`
- Wire codes: `LARGE_GRAPH_UNCACHED_CODE`, `UNEXPECTED_GROWTH_CODE`, `MEMORY_PRESSURE_CODE`, `ALGORITHM_MEMORY_CAP_CODE`, `APPROACHING_CAP_CODE`
- Composes with sibling slices: `graph_audit` for audit rows on refuse/abort, `graph_telemetry` for tracing emissions, `degraded_aggregation` for multi-source dedup if more than one algorithm refuses on the same request.

## Why filed as a separate child

`src/graph/*`, `src/config/*`, and the snapshot builders are currently hot with multiple in-flight agents (the bd-bife.* wiring beads bd-2inbn / bd-28m0i are already queued for the same modules). Keeping the algorithm core in a brand-new file means downstream wiring can pull it in once a quieter coordination window opens, without redesigning the policy types.

title: Define side-effect, idempotency, and mutation contracts for every command
description:
## Background

Mechanical does not only mean deterministic; it also means users can predict what a command may read, write, or refuse to touch. The project has strong no-deletion/no-worktree/no-silent-mutation rules. The mechanical-boundary beads mention mutation posture in many places, but there is no cross-cutting contract that forces every command to declare and test side effects.

This bead prevents a future implementation from preserving output behavior while accidentally making commands unsafe, non-idempotent, or surprising.

## Acceptance Criteria

See this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field for the detailed completion contract, including unit/static checks, e2e or docs/e2e coverage, detailed logging, and no-feature-loss requirements.
design:
Create a side-effect matrix for every public command and enforce it in tests. Each command should be classified as read-only, append-only, audited mutation, derived-asset rebuild, dry-run/report-only, side-path restore, or unavailable/degraded. For mutating commands, specify idempotency key, transaction boundary, audit entry, DB generation effect, derived index effect, rollback/recovery behavior, and whether a dry-run is required.

The matrix should explicitly forbid file deletion, worktree creation, silent overwrite, unlogged memory mutation, and background daemon requirements for core commands.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Every public `ee` command/subcommand has a documented side-effect classification and mutation contract linked from the command-boundary matrix.
- Mutating commands specify transaction scope, idempotency behavior, audit log entry, DB generation/index generation effects, dry-run support where appropriate, and recovery/degraded behavior.
- Backup/restore/export/import commands explicitly prove side-path/non-overwrite behavior and never delete files in tests.
- Tests fail if a command mutates durable state while declared read-only or report-only.
- Unit tests cover idempotent repeat calls, duplicate imports, failed transaction rollback, dry-run no-op, audit entry creation, derived-asset rebuild boundaries, and policy-denied mutation.
- E2E scripts log before/after DB generation, changed record IDs, audit IDs, filesystem artifacts created, forbidden filesystem operations checked, stdout/stderr paths, and first-failure diagnosis.

title: [implements-surface:certificate-signing] Real cryptographic signing for certificate verifier
description:
Replace the content-hash attestation in src/core/certificate.rs::verify_local_content_attestation with a real cryptographic signature path. As of eidetic_engine_cli-x68d, the verifier was honestly renamed to "attestation" framing (algorithm `ee.local-content-hash.v1`) and the misleading `sigstore.bundle-sha256.v1` algorithm was removed, but the verifier still authenticates only against publicly-derivable inputs.

Pick one (or both, gated by algorithm string):

1. ed25519 via `ring` or `ed25519-dalek`:
   - Workspace-held secret key in `~/.config/ee/keys/<workspace>.ed25519`
   - Signer name bound to public-key fingerprint (e.g. `ed25519:fp:...`)
   - New algorithm string `ee.ed25519.v1`
   - Signing path: `ee certificate sign <id>` reads payload_hash, signs, writes signature
   - Verification: load pubkey by signer fingerprint, verify against payload_hash bytes
   - Rotation/revocation policy

2. Real sigstore via `sigstore-rs`:
   - Strict OIDC binding + rekor inclusion proof + fulcio cert chain
   - New algorithm string `sigstore.bundle.v2` (different from the removed `.bundle-sha256.v1` lie)
   - Online verification path; document offline degraded mode

When this lands, the closure linter for eidetic_engine_cli-xvre and -x68d should refuse to accept evidence commits whose verifier collapses to a public-input hash.

Acceptance gates:
- A forged "signature" produced from public inputs (signer + payload_hash + algorithm tag) MUST fail verification.
- Round-trip test: sign a certificate with the workspace key, verify with only the workspace pubkey, mutate the payload, verification fails.
- Adversarial test mirroring the eidetic_engine_cli-x68d repro: an attacker who sees (signer, payload_hash) cannot mint a passing attestation.
- The `*_UNAVAILABLE_CODE` constant for any "real signing" surface is deleted in the same PR.

Until this lands, do not rely on certificate attestation_ok=true for authorization decisions or compliance evidence. Module docs in src/core/certificate.rs already say so.

Background: bug filed in eidetic_engine_cli-x68d. Module docs in src/core/certificate.rs (top-of-file "Honesty note") summarize what attestations do and do not prove.
close_reason: Implemented ed25519 signing with deterministic keys, verify, and acceptance tests. Round-trip, forged signature, mutated payload, and adversarial attacker tests all pass.

title: [idea-wizard] Epic: No-silent-fallback hardening for agent-facing data paths
description:
## Background
Recent fixes such as eidetic_engine_cli-6xkn proved that silent defaulting in storage/replay paths can turn corrupt or incompatible persisted data into plausible empty results. The overlap check found earlier related beads such as kr0m and 6xkn, but no open issue covers the remaining production-wide pattern: parse, serialization, subprocess-output, and builder failures that are converted to empty strings, empty vectors, or default records without a stable error or degradation.

## Idea-wizard rationale
Phase 2 generated a broader list of reliability and swarm-scale ideas. After overlap checking the existing 870-bead history, the strongest non-duplicate track was a class-based hardening effort for silent fallbacks. It is pragmatic, accretive, and directly user-visible because agents trust ee JSON, context packs, CASS imports, support bundles, and diagnostics to reflect real evidence rather than absence caused by hidden failures.

Phase 3 kept this as a foundation for later testing and optimization work: before adding more sophisticated memory behavior, ee should make failure impossible to confuse with empty data.

## Goals
- Inventory production data paths that use silent defaults after parse, serialization, process I/O, or row decode failures.
- Replace high-risk defaults with contextual `ee.error.v1`, `DbError::MalformedRow`, `CassError`, or explicit degradation records.
- Add a guard test or conformance matrix so future agents cannot reintroduce unreviewed silent fallbacks.
- Keep intentional defaults allowed only when documented with a clear invariant and test coverage.

## Non-goals
- Do not remove harmless defaults in tests or purely cosmetic human rendering paths unless they can affect machine data.
- Do not introduce a new serialization framework or broad refactor.
- Do not duplicate already-closed fixes; reference and extend them only where residual code evidence remains.

## Acceptance
- The child beads below close with focused code changes and tests.
- `bv --robot-insights` has no cycles after dependency creation.
- The final close reason lists the remaining allowlisted defaults, if any, and why each is safe.
close_reason: All 12 children closed: sos5.1-5.12 ship no-silent-fallback hardening across cass subprocess, output renderers, models builders, guard conformance tests, e2e validation, integrity diagnostics, core serialization, procedure verification, cli demo, repositories empty-vector handling. Verification baseline: silent-fallback patterns now either propagate explicit errors or are documented.

title: [no-silent-fallback] Inventory production defaults and define allowlist contract
description:
## Background
The repo has multiple legitimate uses of defaults, especially in tests and display helpers, but recent bugs show that production decode and render paths can hide corruption or failed I/O when they use `unwrap_or_default`, ignored reads, or ad hoc empty fallback values. Before broad edits, future agents need a precise map of which defaults are dangerous and which are intentional.

## What to do
- Search production code under `src/` for `unwrap_or_default`, ignored `Result`s around I/O, `serde_json::to_string(...).unwrap_or_default`, builder fields that default machine-facing IDs/timestamps/content to empty strings, and subprocess pipe reads that ignore errors.
- Classify every finding into: must-fix now, safe intentional default, test-only/non-production, or needs a separate follow-up.
- Add a small machine-readable allowlist or a conformance test table that records the safe intentional defaults with reason strings.
- Use the existing `kr0m` and `6xkn` fixes as examples of the policy: machine data failure must become a stable error or degradation, not empty data.

## Acceptance
- The inventory is committed as code/test data or as a self-contained test fixture, not only as a transient comment.
- Each must-fix finding has a linked child bead or is fixed in the same slice if trivial.
- The inventory explicitly covers `src/cass/process.rs`, `src/output/mod.rs`, `src/hooks/installer.rs`, `src/models/jsonl.rs`, and any additional production modules found by the scan.
- Verification includes the focused guard/inventory test and `ubs` on changed files.

title: [cass] Preserve missing session metadata in import hashes and counts
description:
## Background
The no-silent-fallback inventory found CASS import deriving content hashes from path plus optional modified/size fields defaulted to empty/zero and setting missing message_count to 0. If CASS JSON omits metadata, ee can store path-only hashes or zero counts that look real.

## What to do
- Decide the contract for missing CASS `modified`, `size_bytes`, `content_hash`, and `message_count` fields.
- Prefer explicit degraded import records or validation errors over silently generated path-only hashes and zero message counts.
- Preserve deterministic behavior for valid CASS JSON.

## Acceptance
- Missing CASS metadata is observable in import output, diagnostics, or row metadata; it is not silently collapsed to empty strings/zero counts.
- Tests cover valid metadata, missing optional-but-supported metadata, and malformed required metadata.
- Focused CASS import tests plus standard cargo gates pass through RCH.

title: [repositories] Classify empty-vector fallbacks in production data loaders
description:
## Background
The no-silent-fallback inventory found production loaders that return Ok(Vec::new()) for absent inputs, missing tables, empty filters, or storage read paths. Some are legitimate empty-result semantics, but others may hide repository failures as successful empty evidence.

## What to do
- Audit `return Ok(Vec::new())` in src/serve.rs, src/core/memory.rs, src/core/preflight_guard.rs, src/core/recorder.rs, src/core/claims.rs, src/models/query.rs, and relevant CLI helpers.
- Classify each as legitimate no-input/no-record behavior or replace it with a stable error/degradation when a storage/query failure is being suppressed.

title: [cass] Propagate subprocess pipe read and join failures
description:
## Background
`src/cass/process.rs` currently reads child stdout/stderr on helper threads, ignores `read_to_end` errors, and uses `join().unwrap_or_default()`. If a pipe reader fails or a helper thread panics, the CASS adapter can report an apparently valid command outcome with empty stdout/stderr, which is exactly the kind of silent evidence loss this track is meant to eliminate.

## What to do
- Replace the helper thread return type with a result that preserves whether stdout or stderr failed to read.
- Convert read failures and thread join panics into contextual `CassError` values or a stable degraded outcome if the surrounding CASS contract requires an outcome object.
- Preserve timeout behavior: killing the child on timeout should still wait/reap the process and report timeout truthfully, but it must not hide reader failures behind empty buffers.
- Add focused unit coverage with a testable reader helper where possible; avoid relying on nondeterministic OS pipe failures if a pure helper test can cover the join/read error mapping.

## Acceptance
- No `join().unwrap_or_default()` or ignored `read_to_end` result remains in the CASS subprocess output path.
- Tests cover normal stdout/stderr capture and at least one reader failure or join-failure mapping.
- Machine-facing import/search callers still get stable JSON errors or degradations, not raw panics.
- Verification: focused CASS process tests, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `ubs src/cass/process.rs` through RCH for cargo-heavy gates.
close_reason: Fix merged in e2a40542: join_pipe_reader returns Result and converts read errors/panics to CassError::Io; tests cover success, read error, and thread panic paths; no_silent_fallback_inventory now expects 0 occurrences

Even if serde failures are rare, machine-facing output must not turn a serialization failure into an empty data payload.

## What to do

## Acceptance

title: [models] Audit machine-facing builders that default required fields to blanks
description:
## Background
The scan found model/builders that use `unwrap_or_default()` for fields such as export IDs, timestamps, memory IDs, workspace IDs, levels, kinds, and content. Some builder defaults are intentionally ergonomic, but a required machine-facing identity or timestamp becoming an empty string can produce records that look valid until a later command fails or misranks evidence.

## What to do
- Audit builders and record constructors under `src/models/`, `src/curate/`, and JSONL/export code for required machine-facing fields defaulted to empty strings.
- Separate optional display fields from contract-required IDs, timestamps, schema names, content, source URIs, and provenance references.
- For required fields, prefer fallible builders, typed constructors, or validation errors over empty defaults.
- Keep ergonomic builder APIs only where tests prove the default is safe and documented.

## Acceptance
- Any remaining empty default for a machine-facing required field has a test-backed reason in the allowlist/inventory from `sos5.1`.
- At least one regression covers a previously empty-defaulted required field and proves malformed/incomplete output is rejected or reported.
- JSONL export/import and curation risk certificate contracts remain stable for valid records.
- Verification includes focused model/JSONL tests plus the standard cargo gates through RCH.

title: [guard] Add no-silent-fallback conformance test for production data paths
description:
## Background
One-off fixes are not enough. `6xkn`, `kr0m`, and this epic all point to a reusable contract: production paths that feed machine data must not erase failure evidence by defaulting to empty values. A conformance guard should make that policy executable without banning every harmless default.

## What to do
- Add a focused test or script-backed contract that scans production Rust files for high-risk silent-fallback patterns.
- Maintain a small allowlist with file, pattern, reason, and test evidence for intentional defaults.
- Fail when a new unallowlisted `unwrap_or_default`, ignored read, ignored rollback, or serialization fallback appears in an agent-facing data path.
- Keep the guard narrow enough to avoid noisy false positives in test modules, purely human-only formatting, or safe optional-display defaults.

## Acceptance
- The guard fails on at least one synthetic fixture containing `serde_json::to_string(...).unwrap_or_default()` in a machine JSON renderer.
- The guard passes on the final repo state and reports the allowlisted count.
- The guard is documented in its test failure message with the repair pattern: return a contextual error/degradation or add a justified allowlist entry with coverage.
- Verification includes the guard test, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --all-targets`, and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` through RCH.

description:
## Background

This bead adds an executable proof that representative malformed or failed data paths produce stable errors or degradations instead of empty success payloads.

## What to do

## Acceptance

- Golden or structural assertions freeze the error/degradation shape.

title: Epic: Plan Open Questions, Risk Mitigations, and Vendor/Pinning Recipes (§31)
description:
Source: COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_TO_MAKE_EE__OPUS.md §31.1 (Risks R1-R17) and §31.2 (Open questions Q1-Q8).

# Epic: Plan Open Questions, Risk Mitigations, and Vendor/Pinning Recipes

## Why this epic exists

§31.2 lists 8 explicit open questions that require user decisions before final design lock. §31.1 lists 17 risks; while the gate beads cover most operationally, some (R5 cargo vendor for fnx pre-publish, R12 dependency API drift compile-time contract, R15 vendored cass fixture DB versioning, R16 `ee init --download-models` UX, R7 asupersync-as-only-executor regression test) have no specific mitigation beads.

Without this epic these open questions linger as undocumented assumptions. The 8 user-decision items in particular gate concrete defaults — "what's the Stop hook default?" gates whether `ee maintenance` runs on session end; "what's the decay half-life?" gates the [playbook] config block; "do we ship LLM-consolidation in v1?" gates whether `--llm` flags appear in v1 CLI surface.

## Cross-cutting constraints (apply to every child bead under this epic)

- Each open-question bead is `type: question`, surfaces a concrete recommendation with rationale, lists the 2-3 viable answers and their tradeoffs, and identifies the bead(s) that depend on the answer.
- Each risk-mitigation bead defines: the risk, the trigger condition, the mitigation, the verification path (how do we know the mitigation works), and an audit/recovery procedure.
- Each cross-repo / cross-crate vendor bead documents the recipe (e.g., `cargo vendor --respect-source-config -- ...` plus `Cargo.toml` rewrites) and the trigger that requires running it (release tag, dependency major bump, etc.).
- Tests log: question id, current default, recommended answer, dependent beads, decision-required label state.

## Closure criteria

- 8 open-question beads created (Q1-Q8), each with status `open` and a `decision-required` label.
- Risk-mitigation beads for R5, R7, R12, R15, R16 created with implementation paths.
- A single dashboard query `br list -l decision-required` returns the canonical list of items the user must answer.

## Verification path

title: [perf] Index status check on every search adds latency
description:
**File:** src/core/search.rs:848, src/core/search.rs:900-921

**Bottleneck:** Every `run_search` call executes `search_degradations` which calls `get_index_status`:

```rust
let degraded = search_degradations(options, &index_dir);  // line 848
```

This performs file I/O to check index staleness against database generation, even when the index is known to be fresh.

**Impact:** Adds 1-5ms per search call depending on I/O. With p50 target of 38ms, this is ~5-13% overhead.

**Fix options:**
1. **Cache index status:** Store generation check result with short TTL (e.g., 1 second)
2. **Lazy check:** Only check staleness if results are empty or on explicit flag
3. **Background refresh:** Move staleness detection to a background job that updates a flag

**Benchmark baseline:** Search p50 38ms, p99 110ms per plan §28.

**Note:** The degradation info is useful for diagnostics but not critical for search correctness. Consider making it opt-in via `--check-staleness` flag.
close_reason: Implemented short-TTL process-local cache for search index status checks in fa2f708c; focused RCH regression core::search::tests::search_degradations_reuse_index_status_within_ttl passed, rustfmt --check and git diff --check passed on src/core/search.rs.

title: Epic: Agent-Native UX
description:
Epic for the `Agent-Native UX` workstream.

        Background and intent:
        Make ee discoverable and safe for coding agents by default: deterministic command metadata, stable envelopes, explicit errors, schema discovery, compact field profiles, and non-interactive behavior.

        How this serves the project:
        This workstream is one layer of the EE memory substrate. It should be implemented only through its child beads, preserving the constraints and evidence-first design of the root program bead.

        Cross-cutting constraints:

- Keep the CLI local-first, deterministic, and agent-native; stdout is data, stderr is diagnostics.
- Preserve the no-Tokio and no-rusqlite constraint unless a later ADR explicitly changes the architecture.

- Use Asupersync for async edges and cancellation/budget behavior; do not smuggle in a Tokio executor.
- Keep JSON as the canonical public contract. TOON, Markdown, diagrams, and MCP are renderers or adapters over the same domain data.
- Mutating commands need dry-run/idempotency/audit behavior unless the task explicitly says otherwise.
- Add focused tests proportional to risk: unit tests for domain logic, contract/golden tests for public output, and integration/evaluation tests for cross-subsystem behavior.

title: EE-FOCUS-001: Add passive active-memory set and `ee focus` workflow
description:

title: Epic: Privacy, Redaction Classes, Secret Scanners, Remote-Model Gating (§22)
description:
Source: COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_TO_MAKE_EE__OPUS.md §22 (Privacy, redaction, and safety) and §31.1 R10/R11 risks.

# Epic: Privacy, Redaction Classes, Secret Scanners, and Remote-Model Gating

## Why this epic exists

§22 establishes the privacy contract: 5 redaction classes (public / project / private / secret / blocked), 8+ secret-scanner families with placeholder format `[REDACTED:<scanner_name>]`, the trauma-record predicate (`affect_valence < -0.5 AND importance >= 0.9`) that pins risk memories into packs, the data-deletion verbs (`tombstone`, `retire`, `expire`, `redact`, `hide-from-packs`, `forget`) and their precedence vs. legal_hold, and remote-model gating by `[llm].allow_remote_models = false` with per-call audit fields. README.md mirrors the same promise.

Existing beads cover trust classes and a redaction enum, but the operational machinery is mostly aspirational:

- No bead enumerates the per-redaction-class export-allowed matrix.
- No bead enumerates the 8 scanner families (AWS / GCP / Anthropic / OpenAI / GitHub PAT / Stripe; PEM private keys; JWT; URL passwords; .env; cloud creds; DB URLs; high-entropy hex/base64 ≥32 chars).
- No bead pins the `[REDACTED:<scanner_name>]` placeholder format.
- The trauma-record pin rule has no bead.
- Remote-model gating is documented but unimplemented.
- Audit-log redaction (so audit rows themselves can't leak secrets in error output) has no bead.

This epic exists to make every privacy claim from README and AGENTS.md operationally true and CI-verifiable, so that "ee never writes a secret to disk in plaintext" is a tested invariant rather than a wish.

## Cross-cutting constraints (apply to every child bead under this epic)

- Redaction is applied at THREE choke points: import (`ee import cass`), remember (`ee remember`), and pack (`ee context`/`ee pack`). The same redactor is used at each; a unit test asserts the same input produces the same redacted output regardless of choke point.
- The placeholder format is `[REDACTED:<scanner_name>]` and includes only the scanner identifier, not the matched bytes. Asserted by a fuzz harness that mutates inputs and checks no original byte is ever present in the redacted output.
- A scanner cannot be skipped silently: if a scanner panics or errors, the whole write aborts with a typed error. Tests cover the panicked-scanner path with a fault-injection fixture.
- Audit-log row content is itself redacted via the same pipeline before hitting disk and before any user-visible rendering. A grep test scans audit.jsonl for `[REDACTED:` placeholders to confirm.
- Remote-model gating is enforced at the dispatch layer: `if !cfg.llm.allow_remote_models { return Err(RemoteModelDenied) }` with a `policy_denied_remote_model` degradation code. Per-call audit fields = timestamp, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, target, response_hash.
- Tests log: input plaintext fingerprint (not bytes), scanner family that fired, redacted output fingerprint, audit row id, redaction class, total elapsed_ms.

## Closure criteria

- All 5 redaction-class semantics are implemented and tested with an export-allowed matrix.
- All 8 scanner families have positive + adversarial unit tests; each has at least 5 positive fixtures and 5 adversarial fixtures (near-misses).
- The placeholder format is asserted by a property test over arbitrary byte sequences.
- The trauma-record predicate is implemented and golden-tested via a pack that includes a low-score but high-importance trauma record.
- Remote-model gating is enforced and tested with a fault-injected fake provider.
- Every redaction site has a fuzz harness target (added under cargo-fuzz crate).

## Verification path

- Unit tests under `src/policy/redact/`.
- Golden tests in `tests/snapshots/redact_*`.
- E2E in `tests/privacy_three_chokepoints.rs`, `tests/redact_audit_log.rs`, `tests/remote_model_gating.rs`.
- Fuzz target: `fuzz/fuzz_targets/redact_pipeline.rs`.
close_reason: All 0 child beads verified closed. Epic complete.

title: HIGH: JSON error envelope omits required severity/details fields
description:
Reviewer finding focused on src/output + CLI error paths.

Location:
- src/output/mod.rs:5811-5828 (`error_response_json`) serializes only `schema`, `error.code`, `error.message`, and optional `error.repair`.

Why this is a bug:
AGENTS.md documents the stable JSON error shape as `ee.error.v1` with `error.code`, `message`, `severity`, `repair`, and `details`. Machine consumers cannot classify severity or inspect structured context consistently.

Acceptance criteria:
- `error_response_json` emits a stable `ee.error.v1` shape with explicit `severity` and `details` fields for all DomainError variants.
- JSON error tests cover the complete required field set, including absent/empty details behavior.
- CLI --json error tests assert stdout-only machine errors still include the full shape.

title: F3: ee insights — JSON-first findings command (beads_viewer --robot-insights analogue)
description:
# F3 — `ee insights` JSON-first command scaffold

## Why this is foundational

beads_viewer's *killer surface* is `bv --robot-insights`: a single JSON command that emits a structured, batched bundle of graph-derived findings (PageRank top-K, betweenness top-K, k-core top-K, parallel-cut suggestions, topK set, cycles flagged, etc.). It's the surface that makes the system's intelligence legible.

`ee` has no equivalent. The closest is `ee status --json` (scalar workspace counts) and `ee graph snapshot show` (raw snapshot metadata). Neither emits *findings* — pre-computed insights about the workspace's knowledge graph.

The 10 features in this epic produce a steady stream of graph-derived findings that don't fit cleanly into existing surfaces:
- G2's Pack DNA: needs explanation surface for context
- G4's contradiction clusters: needs health surface
- G5's articulation points: needs curation surface
- G6's Gomory-Hu cuts: needs pairwise surface
- G8's knowledge skyline: needs status/insights surface
- G9's load-bearing memories: needs why/curate badge

We need a single home for these — analogous to beads_viewer's --robot-insights.

## What

Build `ee insights` command (`src/cli/insights.rs` + handlers) with the following surface:

1. **`ee insights --json`** — top-level: emits a JSON bundle with these top-level sections (any may be omitted if not applicable):
   - `topMemories`: PageRank top-10, with scores
   - `bridges`: articulation points + bridges (G5)
   - `kCore`: top k-core members (G4)
   - `kTruss`: top k-truss members (G4)
   - `contradictionClusters`: Louvain communities filtered to contradicts edges (G4)
   - `causalBottlenecks`: betweenness-on-causal-evidence top-K (G3)
   - `loadBearingMemories`: bipartite eigenvector top-K on rule provenance (G9)
   - `hubs` / `authorities`: HITS top-K (G10)
   - `revisionFrontiers`: dominance-frontier sets for recent edits (G7)
   - `proximityHotspots`: pairs with small Gomory-Hu min-cut (G6)
   - `knowledgeSkyline`: onion × Louvain × age × trust heatmap (G8)
   - `degradedSignals[]`: any algorithm that timed out or sampled
   - `snapshotVersion`, `generatedAt`, `runDurationMs`

2. **`ee insights --section <name>`** — emit a single section (cheaper, fast feedback).

3. **`ee insights --explain <memory_id>`** — emit a memory-centric bundle: its ego subgraph at radius 2, its PPR neighbors, its Voronoi cell, its onion-layer index, its k-truss membership, its dominance-frontier membership, its load-bearing badge if any.

4. **Schema versioning**: New `ee.insights.v1` schema constant. Documented in `docs/schemas/ee.insights.v1.json`.

5. **Determinism**: Same database, same snapshot → byte-identical JSON output. Tie-breaks per CGSE. Same harness as J7.

6. **Performance budgets**:
   - `ee insights --json` (full bundle): ≤ 2 seconds on a 1k-memory workspace (background-cached metrics dominate).
   - `ee insights --section <name>`: ≤ 250ms.
   - `ee insights --explain <id>`: ≤ 500ms.

## How (key implementation choices)

- **JSON-first**: Output is structured JSON by default. Human/Markdown/TOON renderers added later (the schema is the contract).
- **Background-cached metrics**: Heavy metrics (full PageRank, Gomory-Hu, communicability betweenness) are precomputed by the centrality-refresh background job and stored in snapshot metadata. `ee insights` reads from cache.
- **Section dispatch**: Each section is a function in `src/cli/insights/sections/<name>.rs` keyed by section name; `ee insights --json` iterates the full set in deterministic order.
- **Degraded section reporting**: If a section fails (timeout, snapshot stale, algorithm error), it's omitted from the bundle and an entry is added to `degradedSignals[]` with code + repair. Per F4.

## Tests

- Unit tests: each section function called against a fixture, structure verified, byte-stable.
- Integration test: full `ee insights --json` against a 100-memory fixture; size, schema validity, byte-stability across 3 runs.
- E2E test: `ee insights --section topMemories --json` returns the same top-K as `ee graph centrality list --top=10`.

## Acceptance

- `ee insights` command registered with handlers for: full bundle, --section, --explain.
- JSON schema documented at `docs/schemas/ee.insights.v1.json`.
- Help text describes every section.
- 10+ unit tests + 1 E2E test pass.
- Empty workspace returns an empty-but-well-formed bundle (degraded sections noted).

## Dependencies

Blocks: G2 (Pack DNA — uses `--explain` surface), G4 (contradiction clusters surface here), G5 (articulation points surface here), G8 (knowledge skyline surface here), G6 (proximity hotspots surface here), G7 (revision frontiers surface here), G9 (load-bearing memories surface here), G10 (hubs/authorities surface here).
Parent: bd-bife.

## Related code

- `src/cli/mod.rs` — command registry pattern; insights is a new top-level command.
- `src/cli/status.rs` (if extant) — pattern for renderable JSON status command.
- ADR 0008 (graph metrics as derived state — insights uses cached metrics, never recomputes synchronously).

FILE SURFACE: src/cli/mod.rs, src/cli/insights/mod.rs, docs/schemas/ee.insights.v1.json, tests/golden/insights.snap

Schema is documented in docs/schemas/ee.insights.v1.json; contract/smoke coverage includes graph_schemas_v1 insights shape checks and insights_section_pagination_json_is_deterministic_and_stdout_only, plus inline unit coverage in src/cli/insights/mod.rs. title: [E2E] Multi-workspace isolation: memories do not leak across workspaces
description:
Current state: No test verifies that memories are properly isolated by workspace. A bug allowing cross-workspace leakage would be severe.

Real test plan:
1. Create two tempdir workspaces: $ws_a and $ws_b
2. Init both: ee init --workspace $ws_a; ee init --workspace $ws_b
3. Add distinct memories to each:
   - ws_a: "Memory only in workspace A"
   - ws_b: "Memory only in workspace B"
4. Search ws_a for "workspace B" → assert 0 results
5. Search ws_b for "workspace A" → assert 0 results
6. Search ws_a for "workspace A" → assert 1 result
7. Search ws_b for "workspace B" → assert 1 result
8. Run ee context in ws_a referencing ws_b content → assert ws_b memory NOT included

This prevents data leakage bugs that could expose sensitive information.

title: [LOW] stored_recorder_event_from_row coerces NULL sequence/event_count to 0 silently — masks data corruption
description:
Cycle-4 reviewer audit (REVIEWER pane). Surface: integer coercion in recorder row decoding (boundary-adjacent to scoring math audit).

src/db/mod.rs:11527-11533 (stored_recorder_run_from_row) and 11542-11546 (stored_recorder_event_from_row) decode INTEGER columns with the pattern:
  row.get(N).and_then(|v| v.as_i64()).unwrap_or(0) as u64

Concrete instances:
  - sequence (events): CHECK (sequence > 0) at schema; decoder gives 0 on NULL → silently violates invariant downstream.
  - event_count, redacted_count, payload_bytes (runs): CHECK >= 0; decoder gives 0 on NULL → looks like an empty run, not a decode failure.

If the row is well-formed these branches never fire — but if a future migration reorders columns, drops a NOT NULL, or someone runs raw SQL that nulls a value, the decoder masks it as 'zero'. No degraded-honesty marker; no warning logged.

ALSO — 'as u64' on i64: if a corrupt row stored a negative number (CHECK can be bypassed with PRAGMA ignore_check_constraints=OFF flips, or older DBs from before the constraint), the cast wraps to a huge u64 (~9.2e18). All scoring/budgeting that consumes event_count/payload_bytes would silently misbehave.

INTEGER OVERFLOW SCAN (the broader audit task):
  - src/core/economy.rs scoring math is f64 throughout; saturating_add used at 700-702 for token sums; f64::from(u32) with .max(1) for divisors; no overflow risk found.
  - src/pack/mod.rs:2417 slack() uses saturating_sub correctly; utilization_percent guards quota_tokens > 0.
  - No raw arithmetic on u32/u64 found in scoring paths that could overflow.

So the only integer hazard found is this silent NULL→0 / wrapping-cast pattern in db row decoders.

FIX:
  (1) Change unwrap_or(0) as u64 → ok_or_else(... DbError::Integrity { column: 'sequence' }).
  (2) Use u64::try_from(i64) and surface the error rather than 'as u64' wrapping.
  (3) Add a test that injects a NULL into recorder_events.sequence (via PRAGMA writable_schema, or by mocking row) and asserts decode returns Err.

PRIORITY LOW: requires upstream corruption to fire. File for hardening sweep.
close_reason: Fixed silent data corruption. stored_recorder_run_from_row and stored_recorder_event_from_row now use required_u64/optional_u32 helpers that return DbError on NULL or negative values instead of silently coercing to 0 or wrapping.

title: [HIGH] recorder_events / audit_log have no append-only DB triggers — only post-hoc hash-chain detection
description:
Cycle-4 reviewer audit (REVIEWER pane). Surface: recorder append-only + audit append-only.

EVIDENCE:
  - grep 'CREATE TRIGGER' over src/db/mod.rs returns ZERO hits — the entire schema has no triggers.
  - V027_RECORDER_STORE (src/db/mod.rs:2611) defines recorder_events with chain hashes (event_hash, previous_event_hash, chain_status) but NO 'BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE … RAISE(ABORT)' guard.
  - V033_AUDIT_HASH_CHAIN similarly relies on row-level hashing without a write-side guard.
  - The Rust API exposes no update_recorder_event() or update_audit_log_row(), so legitimate code paths cannot mutate. But ANY raw SQL call (via DbConnection::execute_raw_for or a future migration script) will silently succeed.

DETECTION-ONLY POSTURE:
  - audit chain: src/core/audit.rs:281 verify_entries() recomputes blake3 over (id, workspace_id, timestamp, actor, action, target_type, target_id, details, surface, mutation_kind, before_hash, after_hash, prev_row_hash) and compares against this_row_hash. The existing tampering test (audit.rs:769 verify_detects_tampered_row) confirms detection works — but only when verify_audit() is invoked. Between mutation and the next verify run, the tampered state is treated as truth by every read path.
  - recorder chain: similar — chain_status='broken' is computed at INSERT time only (recorder.rs:728 RecorderEventChainStatus::for_event). No background re-verification job and no equivalent of verify_audit() for events surfaced via CLI.

CONSEQUENCE: a buggy migration that adds a column with UPDATE-style backfill, or an admin maintenance script, can silently rewrite history without immediately breaking anything user-visible.

FIX:
  Add a defensive migration (V036_APPEND_ONLY_TRIGGERS) with:
    CREATE TRIGGER recorder_events_no_update BEFORE UPDATE ON recorder_events
      BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'recorder_events is append-only'); END;
    CREATE TRIGGER recorder_events_no_delete BEFORE DELETE ON recorder_events
      WHEN OLD.run_id IS NOT NULL  -- still allow ON DELETE CASCADE from recorder_runs
      BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'recorder_events is append-only'); END;
    CREATE TRIGGER audit_log_no_update BEFORE UPDATE ON audit_log
      BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'audit_log is append-only'); END;
    CREATE TRIGGER audit_log_no_delete BEFORE DELETE ON audit_log
      BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'audit_log is append-only'); END;

  (Note: the recorder_events FK has ON DELETE CASCADE from recorder_runs — the BEFORE DELETE trigger needs to allow cascades or be omitted; UPDATE blocking is the high-value half.)

  Then add tests:
    - try UPDATE/DELETE on recorder_events through DbConnection — assert error.
    - regression: verify_audit + recorder chain still pass after migration applied.

PRIORITY rationale: HIGH not CRITICAL because chain hashing already provides detection. The trigger is defense in depth — closes the window where tampering is silent until next verify run.
close_reason: Implemented and evidenced by d3a6064 plus tests/golden/append-only-triggers.snap. V036_APPEND_ONLY_TRIGGERS installs recorder_events_no_update, audit_log_no_update, and audit_log_no_delete; recorder_events DELETE remains allowed by design for recorder_runs cascade and is tracked separately by eidetic_engine_cli-baap. Verified via RCH: cargo test --lib append_only_trigger passed 4/4, and cargo test --lib deleting_recorder_run_still_cascades_to_events passed 1/1. Closure linter surface snapshot exists for implements-surface:append-only-triggers.

title: [CRITICAL] certificate verify_detached_signature is not a signature: hash-of-public-inputs masquerades as ed25519/sigstore
description:
Repro:
  src/core/certificate.rs::verify_detached_signature claims to verify a
  "detached signature" using algorithms named `ee.local-sha256.v1` and
  `sigstore.bundle-sha256.v1`. The actual implementation is:

      fn local_sha256_signature(signer: &str, payload_hash: &str) -> String {
          format!(
              "sha256:{}",
              signature_digest("ee.certificate.local-sha256.v1", signer, payload_hash)
          )
      }

      fn signature_digest(domain: &str, signer: &str, payload_hash: &str) -> String {
          let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
          hasher.update(domain.as_bytes());
          hasher.update(b"\n");
          hasher.update(signer.as_bytes());
          hasher.update(b"\n");
          hasher.update(payload_hash.as_bytes());
          hex_lower(&hasher.finalize())
      }

  No key, no nonce, no secret material. The "signature" is just a public
  hash of public inputs. Any caller that knows (signer, payload_hash) for
  a certificate can recompute the same string and produce a "valid"
  signature.

  Demonstration:

      let signer = "any-name@example.com";
      let payload_hash = "blake3:abcdef...";  // visible in the certificate
      let forged = format!(
          "sha256:{}",
          signature_digest("ee.certificate.local-sha256.v1", signer, payload_hash)
      );
      // `forged` now passes verify_detached_signature for that signer
      // and payload_hash, even though no private key is involved.

Expected: `verify_detached_signature` performs cryptographic verification
against a public key (e.g. ed25519 with sodiumoxide/ring, or actual
sigstore bundle verification with rekor + fulcio). A forged signature
should fail verification regardless of whether the forger knows the
inputs.

Actual: the verifier confirms the signer recomputed the same hash they
already published. Authentication value: zero. The constant-time
comparison hides the real problem (it is comparing two public strings).

Aggravating: the algorithm name `sigstore.bundle-sha256.v1` strongly
implies sigstore-grade bundle verification (rekor inclusion proof,
fulcio cert chain, OIDC binding). The actual code does none of that —
it is the same domain-separated SHA-256 hash with a different string
prefix. Any user, auditor, or compliance review reading the algorithm
name will reasonably believe the certificates are signed.

Evidence-line:
  src/core/certificate.rs:1212-1254 (verify_detached_signature)
  src/core/certificate.rs:1256-1272 (local_sha256_signature, sigstore_bundle_signature)
  src/core/certificate.rs:1274-1282 (signature_digest — pure hash)
  Bead eidetic_engine_cli-xvre closure claims "Real ee certificate verify
  with manifest hashing and signatures" — the manifest hash is real, the
  signature verification is not.

Suggested fix:
  - Either: rename the algorithm strings to something honest like
    `ee.local-content-hash.v1` (no "signature" claim), drop the
    "detached_signature" framing in verify, and document that ee
    certificates are content-addressed but not signed in this slice.
  - Or: add a real signing path. Two reasonable options:
    1. ed25519 via the `ed25519-dalek` or `ring` crate, with a workspace-
       held secret in `~/.config/ee/keys/` and the signer name bound to
       the public key fingerprint.
    2. Real sigstore bundle verification through `sigstore-rs`. Strict
       OIDC + rekor inclusion required.
  - Until either lands, the closure linter for xvre should refuse to
    accept a closure-evidence commit whose verifier collapses to a
    public-input hash.

Severity rationale: this is exactly the "abstention dressed up as
implementation" pattern the closure linter is designed to catch. The bead
is closed, the surface is wired, the algorithm name promises sigstore,
and the CLI exits 0 on every "verification" — but a forger can mint
signatures with no secrets at all.
close_reason: Honest renaming per option 1 of the bug's suggested fix: dropped 'detached signature' framing, renamed algorithm string ee.local-sha256.v1 -> ee.local-content-hash.v1, removed the misleading sigstore.bundle-sha256.v1 algorithm (now returns honest AttestationMismatch citing implements-surface:certificate-signing), renamed signature_ok -> attestation_ok and signatureOk JSON -> attestationOk, renamed VerificationResult::SignatureMismatch -> AttestationMismatch, added module-level 'Honesty note' explaining what content-hash attestations do and do not prove. Forged-input attack from the repro is still POSSIBLE structurally - that is openly documented now and tracked for real signing under eidetic_engine_cli-s4fk (implements-surface:certificate-signing). Closure label: honesty-only.

title: EE-TST-009: Add command effect manifest and no-mutation contract suite
description:
Define a first-class command effect manifest and contract suite so every public EE command is explicit about what it can read, write, cache, mutate, or refuse to do.

Background:
The bead graph already requires read-only behavior, dry-run behavior, idempotency, audit records, and no hidden mutation in many individual places. That is good but still too distributed for a CLI whose primary users are agents. Agents need to know before invoking a command whether it is safe to call in the middle of a task, whether it can write durable memory, whether it can rebuild derived indexes, whether it can touch workspace files, and how to verify that dry-run actually did not mutate anything.

Scope:
- Define a command-effect taxonomy for all CLI, MCP, hook, export, renderer, and maintenance surfaces.
- Add a generated or hand-maintained manifest that maps each public command and subcommand to its default effect, dry-run effect, allowed write surfaces, idempotency behavior, audit behavior, and external I/O posture.
- Add a no-mutation contract suite that snapshots isolated workspace state before and after commands and fails on undeclared durable writes.
- Integrate effect metadata into public schemas, capabilities, test artifacts, and closure dossiers.
- Make derived-cache or index writes explicit rather than pretending they are the same as pure read-only operations.

Why this improves user outcomes:
EE is meant to be called by agents inside active coding sessions. The safest and most ergonomic interface is one where agents can mechanically choose safe commands, prove that read-only commands stayed read-only, and trust that mutating commands advertise dry-run, idempotency, audit, and repair behavior. This reduces accidental memory corruption, hidden cache surprises, MCP adapter divergence, and user mistrust.

## Acceptance Criteria

Detailed closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as part of this bead's implementation contract, including comprehensive unit tests, e2e tests, contract fixtures, and logging requirements.
design:
Recommended design:
- Define stable effect classes such as `read_only`, `derived_artifact_write`, `durable_memory_write`, `workspace_file_write`, `config_write`, `external_io`, and `disabled_until_safe`. The exact enum names can change during implementation, but the distinction between pure reads, declared derived writes, and durable user-visible mutation must remain.
- Each command manifest entry should include command path, schema version, default effect, dry-run effect, allowed database tables, allowed derived artifact paths, allowed workspace file paths, external I/O posture, idempotency-key requirement, audit requirement, confirmation/ask-before-acting behavior, and degraded fallback behavior.
- Read-only commands should be tested by state snapshots over the database, index/cache roots, config home, and workspace files. Derived writes are acceptable only when declared, isolated, and either disabled under strict mode or reported as derived artifacts.
- Mutating commands should be contract-tested for dry-run, idempotency replay, audit record creation, duplicate apply handling, and failure before partial durable writes where possible.
- MCP tools should use the same manifest, with read-only/idempotent annotations derived from the CLI service contract rather than handwritten adapter claims.
- Logs should include `effect.expected`, `effect.observed`, snapshot hashes, changed paths/tables, strict-mode status, and first undeclared mutation if the test fails.

title: Add no-fake-reasoning contract suite for all migrated commands
description:
## Background

This is the cross-cutting safety net for the migration. The core problem is not just code shape; it is that an agent might trust output that looks like it came from evidence when it actually came from canned samples or heuristic judgment.

This bead adds contracts that fail loudly when a migrated command claims unsupported reasoning, success, verification, uplift, procedure validity, risk assessment, or health.

## Acceptance Criteria

See this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field for the detailed completion contract, including unit/static checks, e2e or docs/e2e coverage, detailed logging, and no-feature-loss requirements.
design: Build on the command inventory, degraded-honesty contracts, and e2e logging standard. Prefer real-binary contract tests that exercise public command paths in isolated workspaces. Static scans may supplement but must not be the only protection.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Contract suite covers core retrieval/packing/explanation (`search`, `context`, `pack`, `why`, graph witness/explain paths), baseline infrastructure commands, recorder, tripwire, preflight, procedure, causal, lab, learn, review/curate/rule lifecycle, diagnostics/jobs/daemon/adapters, memory revise/status, economy, situation/plan, rehearse, and claims/certificates.
- Unit/contract tests cover forbidden-output scanners, fixture-mode detection, provenance validators, schema validators, degradation-code validators, stdout/stderr isolation checks, side-effect declaration checks, and stable repair-command rendering.
- Tests fail when normal command output contains sample/mock/stub/demo data or reports success, health, verification, replay, causal uplift, procedure validity, risk assessment, curation maturity, graph explanation, certificate validity, mutation, or pack selection without evidence.
- Tests explicitly allow deterministic fixtures only in fixture/eval/test modes and verify that fixture mode is marked in output.
- Tests validate stable JSON schemas, degradation codes, stdout/stderr isolation, provenance completeness, score-component traceability, redaction status, side-effect classification, idempotency behavior, runtime budget/cancellation behavior where applicable, and repair-command stability.
- The suite cross-checks the command-boundary matrix so every public command is either covered directly, intentionally out of scope with rationale, or marked feature-gated/degraded.
- E2E scripts run representative real-binary cases for fake-output rejection and honest degradation, not just unit-level scanners.
- Logs include command, workspace, evidence source summary, fixture hashes, parsed JSON schema, forbidden-output scan result, degradation code set, side-effect summary, runtime outcome, provenance IDs, redaction state, stdout/stderr paths, and first-failure diagnosis.
- Contract output is suitable for CI artifacts and local reproduction.

title: Preserve context/search/why as deterministic explainable retrieval, not agent reasoning
description:
## Background

The headline `ee` workflow is still `context -> search -> why -> pack`. These surfaces are allowed to compute ranking, packing, graph boosts, decay, profile quotas, provenance, and score explanations, but only as deterministic math over stored memories, indexes, graph snapshots, fixtures, and explicit query inputs.

This bead prevents an overcorrection. We should not remove context packs, score explanations, counterfactual score hints, profile behavior, or graph-aware retrieval simply because their human-facing wording can sound intelligent. The fix is to make every explanation traceable to concrete score components and evidence, not to delete the feature.

Risk to avoid: a future agent could replace rich context behavior with a dumb list of memories. That would technically be mechanical but would lose the product's primary user value.

## Acceptance Criteria

See this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field for the detailed completion contract, including unit/static checks, e2e or docs/e2e coverage, detailed logging, and no-feature-loss requirements.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- `ee search/context/pack/why` preserve rich explainable retrieval while proving every score and explanation field is computed from persisted records, Frankensearch results, FrankenNetworkX snapshots, explicit profile config, or deterministic fixtures.
- Graph explanation commands report witness nodes/edges and metric components, not qualitative relationship stories.
- Counterfactual score hints are renamed or documented as deterministic sensitivity reports unless backed by replay evidence.
- Unit tests cover empty DB, lexical-only degradation, graph-stale degradation, deterministic tie breaks, pack-hash reproducibility, score-component math, profile quotas, and provenance completeness.
- Golden tests pin stable JSON/Markdown/TOON output for representative context/search/why paths.
- E2E scripts log query, workspace, DB/index generations, candidate IDs, score components, selected pack IDs, pack hash, degraded capabilities, stdout/stderr paths, schema/golden status, and first-failure diagnosis.
- No feature is dropped: context profiles, provenance, graph boosts, decay/confidence weighting, and why explanations remain available when their mechanical inputs exist.

title: swarmx.subscribe: memory subscription push channel for swarms (kill the poll storm)
description:
IDEA-WIZARD ROUND 2026-05-18 (ScarletHare): the current pattern for an agent to discover a new procedural rule is polling ee search at the start of every task. With 64 agents polling every 30s, the DB sees 128/min wasted queries. On a 256GB+/64+-core host these polls are cheap but they trash the L2 pack cache and pin read connections.

PROPOSAL
Add ee subscribe (foreground long-running) and ee subscribe one-shot (returns matching deltas since a cursor) commands that push deltas when matching memories change.

DELTA EVENT SHAPE
{ schema: ee.memory.delta.v1, cursor: monotonic_seq, kind: created|updated|level_transitioned|expired|tombstoned, memoryId, levels, kinds, tags, workspaceId, trustClass, agentName (if known), changedFields: [content_hash, confidence, utility, level, ...] }

DELIVERY
Two modes:
1. One-shot, polled by an agent: ee subscribe poll --cursor SEQ --filter LEVEL=procedural,TAG=release --json. Returns all deltas since cursor that match the filter, plus a new cursor. The agent persists the cursor between calls and a single poll replaces N searches.
2. Streaming: ee subscribe stream --filter ... --json emits one JSON object per line (ee.memory.delta.v1) until SIGINT or Cx cancellation. Useful for an agent harness that wants live notifications.

FILTERS
Same advisory taxonomy as memory_list: level (working|episodic|semantic|procedural), kind (rule|fact|decision|failure|...), tag list (AND/OR), workspaceId, trustClass minimum, changedFields subset, sinceMs (in addition to cursor for time-based slicing).

DELIVERY BACKEND
- Local file watcher on the audit-emission log file + index manifest generation. Both already monotonic.
- No new IPC primitive; everything is local-only and uses file inotify/kqueue (a thin wrapper in src/io/watch.rs that already exists for other notifications, or add via fsqlite if missing).
- Cursor is the audit_seq from bd-wp5ac (composes); for legacy installs without that lane, fall back to (generation, last_change_ts) compound cursor.

WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT FROM EXISTING BEADS
- bd-3vwx0 (next-action) is read-only triage; this is a push channel for memory changes.
- bd-1zb7k.17.2 (delta capsules) is for compaction/handoff, not for runtime subscription.
- bd-ndzfg (L2 pack cache) is a cache, not a notification.
- bd-29ulx mesh peer policy is peer-to-peer; this is local agent-to-agent within one host.

FILE SURFACE
- src/cli/mod.rs: ee subscribe poll / stream subcommands.
- src/core/subscribe.rs (NEW): filter compiler, cursor management, delta producer, change-emitter integration.
- src/audit/mod.rs: light hook to publish memory deltas alongside existing audit rows (composes with bd-wp5ac).
- docs/schemas/ee.memory.delta.v1.json: schema.
- docs/agent-ux/subscribe-onboarding.md: agent workflow doc.
- tests/subscribe_unit.rs: filter parsing, cursor monotonicity, change classification.
- tests/subscribe_e2e.rs: real two-agent scenario; agent A inserts a procedural rule; agent B (subscribed) receives the delta within 100ms; cursor advances; filtered subscription excludes non-matching changes.
- tests/snapshots/subscribe_delta.snap: insta golden for one canonical delta shape.

ACCEPTANCE
- e2e: ee subscribe poll --cursor 0 followed by 5 ee remember calls returns 5 deltas; second poll with the new cursor returns 0 (no stale replay).
- e2e: ee subscribe stream stays alive until SIGINT; produces ordered deltas; cursor in every delta is strictly monotonic.
- Filter coverage: each filter primitive has a unit test that excludes non-matching deltas.
- Determinism: same DB + same series of mutations -> same delta sequence (byte-stable).
- Performance: poll p50 under load <=5ms for a workspace with 14k memories and 100 pending deltas.

TESTING WITH LOGGING (no mocks)
- Real ee binary, real DB, real audit table. Two agents in separate processes (one writes, one subscribes).
- ee.test_event.v1 emits per delta with cursor + kind + matched_filter_count.
- Property test: deltas are never reordered relative to audit_seq.

DEPENDENCIES
- Best composed with bd-wp5ac (audit MPSC) but works standalone with the existing audit table.
- Parent epic: bd-1prrl Swarm-X.

NON-GOALS
- Not WebSockets/HTTP. CLI stdout streaming only.
- Not a queue server. Local cursor + audit log is the source of truth; subscribers reconcile by replaying since their cursor on reconnect.
- Not for cross-host swarms in v1; that is bd-29ulx territory.

TRACING: surface=subscribe; required fields bead_id (of THIS bead), workspace_id, request_id, cursor, deltas_emitted, elapsed_ms, degraded_codes (subscribe_filter_invalid, subscribe_cursor_stale).

title: [swarm-scale] Define workload model and deterministic scale fixtures
description:
## Background
Before optimizing for massive agent swarms, the project needs a shared workload model. Existing performance beads cover README p50/p99 numbers and a specific submodular packing hotspot; this bead defines the scale corpus and traffic shapes those future measurements run against.

## What ships
1. A documented scale workload taxonomy: read-heavy context bursts, remember/outcome write bursts, CASS import spikes, index rebuilds, graph refreshes, daemon maintenance, and mixed-mode swarm traffic.
2. Deterministic fixture generators for small, medium, large, and stress corpora. The stress target should model 100k+ memories and many agent/session/provenance records without requiring paid APIs or nondeterministic embedding models.
3. A resource profile manifest recording expected CPU, RAM, disk, DB rows, index size, and command mix for each fixture.
4. Clear labels for which fixtures are suitable for normal CI, nightly CI, and local 256GB+/64-core validation.

## Implementation notes
Use existing deterministic hash embedders and local fixture conventions. Do not introduce custom search or DB code. Fixture generation must be reproducible from a seed and must not require the daemon for read-only cases.

## Tests and logging
- Unit tests pin corpus generation counts, ID determinism, and manifest schema.
- A lightweight integration test generates the smallest fixture and verifies it can feed `ee context`/`ee search` once the shared tree compiles.
- Logs must include seed, corpus size, row counts, and artifact paths.

## Closure evidence
Close only after fixture manifests and tests exist, and after `rch`-offloaded Cargo verification passes for the touched test targets.

title: [hardening] RiskReserve available_tokens can wrap on utilization > 1.0
description:
**File:** src/models/economy.rs:637-644

**Defect:** The `available_tokens()` and `available_slots()` methods compute:
```rust
((1.0 - self.utilization) * self.token_budget as f64) as u32
```

If `utilization` exceeds 1.0 (possible via floating-point accumulation in `reserve()` or deserialization of invalid data), this produces a negative f64 that wraps to ~u32::MAX when cast.

**Observable:** Suddenly massive "available" budget reported, causing over-allocation.

**Repro:**
```rust
let mut reserve = RiskReserve::new(1000, 100);
reserve.utilization = 1.01; // via bad deser or FP accumulation
assert_eq!(reserve.available_tokens(), 0); // FAILS: returns huge number
```

**Fix:** Clamp the utilization or the result:
```rust
((1.0 - self.utilization.min(1.0)) * self.token_budget as f64) as u32
// or
((1.0 - self.utilization) * self.token_budget as f64).max(0.0) as u32
```

Low severity - requires invalid state to trigger, but silent corruption is worse than panic.
close_reason: Fixed in da9687c8: RiskReserve availability now saturates invalid utilization values instead of wrapping; focused RCH test, cargo check, clippy, rustfmt, diff check, and UBS on src/models/economy.rs passed.

title: Epic: Distribution, Installation, and Update Reliability
description:
Program epic for getting trustworthy EE binaries onto agent machines and keeping them diagnosable after installation.

Background and intent:
The current bead graph is strong on memory architecture, agent-native command contracts, testing, diagnostics, support bundles, handoff, audit, rehearsal, and planning. What is still under-owned is distribution: how a future agent installs `ee`, verifies exactly which binary it is running, updates safely, proves release artifacts match source, and captures install/update diagnostics without leaking secrets.

For a Rust CLI intended exclusively for agents, distribution is part of the product. A brilliant memory engine that is hard to install, impossible to verify, or silently stale in PATH will fail in real-world practice. This epic makes install/release/update reliability explicit while preserving the local-first core design.

Scope:
- Version and build provenance surfaces for `ee` binaries.
- Release artifact manifest, checksums/signatures, and cross-platform packaging posture.
- Agent-safe installer/update/check behavior with dry-run, idempotency, and no hidden workspace mutation.
- Real-binary install/update e2e tests with detailed logs and offline/degraded coverage.
- Agent docs and planner recipes that explain install, verify, update, pin, diagnose, and support-bundle workflows.

This epic does not require publishing before the product is ready, and it does not weaken local-first behavior. It ensures release readiness has a real implementation path and test evidence instead of being a vague final step.

## Success Criteria

Detailed epic closure criteria are stored in this bead's structured acceptance_criteria field. Treat those criteria as the epic's success contract, including cross-bead user validation, evidence, and logging requirements.

title: [CRITICAL] closure-lint default mode (used by CI) misses historical violations: 33 currently undetected including LEARN/PROCEDURE/PLAN_DECISIONING_UNAVAILABLE_CODE on closed implements-surface beads
description:
Repro:
  1. `bash scripts/closure-lint.sh --audit` reports 33 violations across
     closed beads. Sample output (truncated):

       x q4av  [implements-surface] surface=learn:        LEARN_UNAVAILABLE_CODE      still exists in src/cli/mod.rs
       x q4av  [implements-surface] surface=learn:        missing tests/golden/learn.snap
       x oofg  [implements-surface] surface=situation:    SITUATION_UNAVAILABLE_CODE  still exists
       x jfd9  [implements-surface] surface=plan-decisioning: PLAN_DECISIONING_UNAVAILABLE_CODE still exists
       x ibw4  [implements-surface] surface=recorder-store:  missing tests/golden/recorder-store.snap
       x r1np  [implements-surface] surface=eval:         close_reason contains abstention language
       x xvre  [implements-surface] surface=certificate:  close_reason contains abstention language
       x zj46  [implements-surface] surface=review:       close_reason contains abstention language
       x q5vf,uiy3,v76q,jp06,qmu0  [honesty-only] no open implements-surface sibling

     `--audit` exits 1.

  2. `bash scripts/closure-lint.sh --json` (the CI invocation per
     .github/workflows/ci.yml:30 and scripts/verify.sh:89) reports
     "No recently changed closed beads with implements-surface or
     honesty-only labels found." and exits 0.

  3. CI passes because the default mode only inspects beads closed
     "recently" (where "recently" appears to be "in this commit's
     diff", not "in any unmerged commit since main was last clean").
     Once a bead closes with a violation, it ages out of the
     recently-changed window and silently stays broken.

Expected: CI fails on EVERY commit until the audit-mode violation
count is zero. The closure-linted bead taxonomy in AGENTS.md ("The
closure linter (CI) blocks any PR that closes an
`implements-surface:X` bead while the matching `*_UNAVAILABLE`
constant still exists in `src/cli/mod.rs`") only works if the linter
keeps enforcing on all closed beads, not just newly-closed ones.

Actual: the linter is a one-shot check at close time. After that, the
violation is permanent and invisible to CI. This is exactly the
"abstention dressed up as implementation" pattern the rule was
designed to catch — except the catch is gated on a temporal window
that is too narrow.

Evidence-line:
  scripts/closure-lint.sh:11-13 (usage docs differentiate default vs
                                  --audit; CI uses default)
  scripts/closure-lint.sh:198    (early exit if no recently changed)
  .github/workflows/ci.yml:30     (cargo invocation uses default mode)
  scripts/verify.sh:89            (verify.sh uses default mode)
  AGENTS.md "Bead Taxonomy"       (rule promised by the taxonomy doc)

Specific affected closed beads (from audit-mode output):
  - q4av     LEARN_UNAVAILABLE_CODE      at src/cli/mod.rs:8122
  - hssh     PROCEDURE_UNAVAILABLE_CODE  at src/cli/mod.rs:8983
  - jfd9     PLAN_DECISIONING_UNAVAILABLE_CODE at src/cli/mod.rs:8928
  - r1np     close_reason contains abstention language (already known)
  - xvre     close_reason contains abstention language (separately
             flagged in eidetic_engine_cli-x68d for the signature theater)
  - zj46     close_reason contains abstention language

Suggested fix:
  - Make CI run `./scripts/closure-lint.sh --audit --json` instead of
    the default mode, so historical violations also fail the build.
  - Drive the existing 33 violations to zero in a triage bead before
    flipping CI to --audit, so the flip doesn't immediately red-line
    main.
  - Document the operating mode in AGENTS.md so future agents know
    that "closure linter passes" actually means "audit-mode passes".

Severity rationale: every closed `implements-surface` bead with a
surviving abstention sentinel is a known-broken claim in the project.
The cost of silent passes is exactly the regression the closure
linter exists to prevent. CRITICAL because the protective gate is
running at all merges but provides only the illusion of protection.
close_reason: Fixed in 760760f: CI and scripts/verify.sh now run closure-lint in --audit --json mode, and AGENTS/script usage docs define audit-mode green as the taxonomy gate. Follow-up eidetic_engine_cli-4q03 tracks resolving the 35 now-visible audit violations.

title: CASS subprocess can hang when child leaves inherited pipes open
description:
File: src/cass/process.rs:260-275

Boundary: CASS subprocess input/execution.

Reproducer conditions:
1. Create executable /data/tmp/ee_fuzz_cass_hang_20260508/bin/cass whose behavior is: start a background sleep that inherits stdout/stderr, print {"sessions":[]} to stdout, then exit 0.
2. Run: EE_CASS_BINARY=/data/tmp/ee_fuzz_cass_hang_20260508/bin/cass timeout 5s ee import cass --workspace /data/tmp/ee_fuzz_cass_hang_20260508/work --dry-run --json

Observed: command does not return before the external timeout; exit=124.

Cause: run_with_timeout detects the parent exit at src/cass/process.rs:273, then blocks joining read_to_end pipe threads at lines 274-275 while the inherited background child still holds the pipes open.

Expected: ee should close or bound subprocess output collection under its own timeout and return a stable CASS import error instead of waiting on inherited pipe handles.

title: [process] Closure linter: forbid abstention-as-implementation closures
description:
## Background

Counterpart to the bead-taxonomy bead. The taxonomy is policy; this is enforcement. Without enforcement, `honesty-only` vs `implements-surface:<name>` is just a naming convention that the swarm can ignore.

## What this bead does

Adds a CI check (a Rust binary in `tools/` or a shell script in `scripts/`) that runs on every PR and on push to main:

1. Walks every bead closed in the last N commits (or every bead with status=closed if running in audit mode).
2. For each `implements-surface:<name>` bead:
   - Reject the closure if `close_reason` matches the regex: `(abstain|unavailable|degraded|stub|placeholder|removed simulation|honest empty|conservative abstention)`.
   - Reject the closure if a `<NAME>_UNAVAILABLE_CODE` constant still exists in src/cli/mod.rs for the named surface.
   - Reject the closure if no golden snapshot exists at `tests/golden/<surface>.snap`.
3. For each `honesty-only` bead:
   - Require a sibling `implements-surface:<same-name>` bead exists in the open queue (not closed, not deleted).
4. Report a summary table: bead ID, label, surface, blocking reason.

## Why this is wave-0 and blocks everything

This is the structural fix that prevents the dishonest-closure pattern from recurring. Every implements-surface bead in CLOSE_THE_GAP_PLAN depends on this gate being live before the bead can be claimed.

## Wiring

Add as the first stage of `scripts/verify.sh` (after forbidden-deps audit) so it runs locally before commit. Add to GitHub Actions on every PR. Failure exits non-zero with a JSON report at .closure-lint-report.json.
close_reason: Implemented closure linter enforcement for abstention closures, unavailable constants, golden snapshots, verify wiring, and PR/main CI.

title: EE-362: Implement `ee claim list/show/verify --json` as read-only verification commands
description:

Task: Implement `ee claim list/show/verify --json` as read-only verification commands

Background and intent:
Make claims, demos, policies, and replay evidence executable and verifiable so ambitious roadmap promises cannot drift away from measured behavior.

Why this matters:
This bead contributes to the overarching goal of making `ee` a dependable local memory substrate for coding agents: useful before work, auditable after work, and safe under degraded conditions. Dependency context:
Original plan dependencies: EE-360, EE-361. These are also represented as br dependency edges where the referenced bead exists.
